generated_text: Honestly, Liv, I’m still buzzing from Saturday. That night out with the girls was exactly what I needed. I can imagine! You looked so relaxed in those photos Sarah sent. It's been ages since you’ve properly let yourself go like that. It has! And Claire chose the  perfect  restaurant. That Italian place in the Jewellery Quarter. Remember when we used to go there after sixth form? Oh God, yes! We were so broke back then, we'd just share a plate of garlic bread. Now it’s all posh pasta and prosecco. Times have changed. Definitely. How’s little Leo doing? He seems to be growing like a weed. He is! He’s trying to sit up now, it’s hilarious. He looks like a little drunk sailor, wobbling all over the place. I’m thinking of getting him one of those baby activity gyms - you know, with all the dangling toys? That's a good idea. He does seem to need a bit more stimulation when he’s awake. How are Mark and him getting on with the new puppy? Chaos! Absolute chaos. He’s named him Winston. Winston the Terror. He’s chewing everything. Mark’s already had to replace two pairs of shoes. Classic! Boys and their dogs, eh? Speaking of chaos… did you hear from Auntie Maureen about Christmas? She wants us all over again this year, doesn't she? Yes! She called yesterday. It's the usual – ‘family is everything’ and ‘wouldn’t be Christmas without all the grandchildren.’ I know. It's lovely in theory, but trying to juggle Leo, Tom's football tournament, and travel is going to be a nightmare. Tom’s already stressed about it. We could suggest they come here this year? Save everyone the hassle. I’ve thought about that. But she’d never go for it. It’s the tradition, you know? Everything has to be at her place. Right, you're right! Still, we can try. Have you thought about Tom’s birthday yet? He's turning fifteen, can you believe it? I have! I was thinking maybe a gaming laser tag party. He's been talking about it for ages. That sounds brilliant! He’d love that. I can help you look at venues. I had a meeting with that place near the NEC the other day – they do birthday parties, very reasonably priced.

Honestly, I’m still buzzing from that trip to Portugal. Did you see the photos I posted? Yeah, yeah! Stunning. Algarve, right? You looked like you were having the time of your life. Sun, sea, and sangria – the trifecta. Exactly! It was just… easy, you know? So simple to get there, no hassle with visas or anything. I completely took it for granted how easy it was to just hop on a flight within the EU. It really was. I remember when I did a bit of fieldwork in Belgium a few years back – the Erasmus scheme made that brilliant. Felt like home from home in a weird way. I’m starting to realize how much we relied on that freedom of movement. The thought of having to fill out loads of paperwork just to go for a weekend getaway… it’s depressing. Tell me about it. I'm debating doing a conference in Berlin next year, but I’m already thinking about passport renewals and potential visa requirements. It’s a mental barrier, isn’t it? Definitely. It's not just the paperwork either, it’s the feeling of restriction. Remember that impromptu trip to Amsterdam we did after graduation? We just decided on a Wednesday and were there by Friday. Oh, good grief, yes! We practically lived on stroopwafels and windmills. That would be impossible now, wouldn't it? Suddenly, a spontaneous weekend break requires weeks of planning. Exactly! And the cost! Flights are already ridiculous, and having to factor in visa fees… It’ll massively impact people’s ability to travel and experience different cultures. I think so too. My research actually touches on the impact of Brexit on international collaboration, and the initial findings are pretty stark. Less mobility for students and researchers, more barriers to projects... That’s so frustrating. You'd think after all this time, there’d be some reciprocal agreements in place, but it doesn't seem to be a priority. It's not, sadly. Though, there are murmurings about trying to streamline things for certain professional sectors. But a casual tourist… it’s going to be a lot more complicated. I’m half tempted to just start learning another language, so I can potentially live and work somewhere within the EU. Just to escape the bureaucracy. That’s a bit drastic, isn’t it? Though I admire your spirit. Actually, I've been thinking of brushing up on my German.

Right, so dessert tonight. Any preferences? I was thinking maybe crumble? Apple or rhubarb? Chocolate cake! Chocolate cake, please! With lots of sprinkles! Ice cream! Big bowl! With jelly! Okay, okay, we can definitely do ice cream, maybe jelly too. But chocolate cake  and  crumble might be a bit much, don't you think? No! Double dessert! Please! No! Ice cream first! Then crumble! Alright, alright. Ice cream and jelly first, then crumble. Compromise. Now, has anyone been looking at the Monopoly board? I swear, every time we play, it ends with someone sobbing. Leo got Park Lane! He’s got Park Lane again! It's not fair! I need money! I’m broke! I landed on Mayfair! That's Monopoly for you. It's designed to make you feel poor and bitter. Remember, it's just a game. And Leo, you need to share the wealth a little bit, darling. You practically own the whole board already. He bought everything! He didn't even let me buy Old Kent Road! You had a chance, sweetheart, you just needed to save a bit. You spent all your money on that silly Baltic Avenue. Honestly. Can I have five pounds? Please? Just five pounds? Here you go, champ. But no more impulse buys, alright? Think strategically! What do you need to buy? I want to buy light blue! Please! I  need  light blue! Well, you’ll need to earn some money first, won’t you? Maybe try not landing on Leo's properties for a while. That’s a good strategy, isn’t it? It's not fair. Leo always wins. Not always, darling. Not always. Now, who wants to try and bankrupt Leo first? Let's see if we can shake things up a bit. And after dessert, maybe we can play something a little less stressful, eh? Like… I don't know… hide and seek? Hide and seek! Yes! Hide and seek! Good! Right then. Ice cream first, then Monopoly chaos, then hide and seek. Sounds like a plan. Let’s get that ice cream ready. Are you both helping? Or are you just going to supervise? Supervising! Helping! I like sprinkles! Rest assured, the sprinkles will be plentiful. Now, to the kitchen we go. Chocolate cake! Chocolate cake! Ice cream! Sprinkles! Lots of sprinkles! Honestly, these two. Never a dull moment. Never a dull moment. And then there's Leo...

Honestly, this traffic is brutal. I didn’t realise coming up the A1 was going to be like this on a Friday. Yeah, it’s a bit mental. Should have taken the smaller roads, but then we'd be crawling along single-track lanes for hours. At least the radio’s decent. Fancy listening to some Ed Sheeran? Ed Sheeran? Seriously? You’re trying to torture me. Put something on that’s vaguely… interesting. Something that doesn't sound like it was written by a committee. Alright, alright, moody. What do you want then? Something indie and obscure only you'd appreciate? Touché. Just… not Sheeran. So, about this thing you were saying earlier… about your job. You were being all cryptic, weren't you? Cryptic? I was just telling you about a new project. It’s… complicated. Big design and build for some new infrastructure. Complicated how? Like, rocket science complicated, or just "lots of paperwork" complicated? Because if it's the latter, I'm happy to help. I’m surprisingly good at bureaucratic stuff. It’s practically half my job managing this corpus. No, it’s definitely more than paperwork. It involves some pretty advanced modelling, particularly with… …sustainable materials. Trying to minimise the environmental impact, you know? It’s a big thing now. Right, that sounds...good. Important. Are you enjoying it then? You seem a bit stressed, to be honest. It’s challenging, yeah. There's a lot riding on it. And some of the clients… well, let’s just say they have very specific ideas. And not all of them are practical. Classic. People always think they know better than the experts. It’s infuriating. Sounds like you're dealing with a lot. Have you had a chance to eat anything today? You look a bit peaky. I grabbed a sandwich at my desk. It was a disaster, though. Soggy lettuce and some weird, processed chicken. Oh god, the worst. We’ll get you a proper feed when we get to his mum’s. She'll have something delicious cooked. Roast dinner, probably. Now you’re talking. I could really do with a roast dinner right now. And maybe a lie-down. Well, you’ll get both. Just try to relax a bit. And next time, bring your own lunch. Soggy lettuce is a crime against humanity. Noted. Definitely noted. Just… this thing is really getting to me, you know?

Another grey one, isn’t it? Seems like we’ve had nothing but grey for weeks. Aye, Harold. Norfolk weather, bless it. Always been a bit damp round here, haven't you, Elsie? Always, Arthur. You remember that flood back in '78? Costessey was practically an island for a week. Don't remind me, Elsie. Had to reinforce the foundations of the shed. Spent a whole weekend sinking posts in. Backbreaking work that was. Used to be able to do it, mind you. Knees aren’t what they used to be. You were always good at your shed repairs, Harold. Strong as an ox, you were. Remember when you built that lean-to for the grandchildren’s bikes? Proper job that was. Well, a civil engineer has to have  some  skills, doesn't he? Can't just be designing bridges all day. A man’s got to be practical. Though, truth be told, I probably spent more time fixing things around the house than designing anything these days. You always were practical, Harold. Me, I was just chasing toddlers and wiping noses. Still, it was a good life, mind. Lots of laughter. Aye, good life. Peaceful. These youngsters today, always rushing about, plugged into their… their whatchamacallits. Phones. Never looking up at the sky. They miss a lot, Arthur. They really do. Used to spend hours as a boy, just lying in the field, watching the clouds. Could see shapes in them. Dragons, ships, sometimes even castles. I used to do that too, as a little girl. My father would point out the constellations. I can still remember Orion. Orion. Used to follow that myself, back in the day. Haven't seen it properly in years. Too much light pollution. Shame, really. Used to be a proper canvas of stars above Norfolk. It is a shame. Used to be able to see the Milky Way, clear as day. Now… barely a glimmer. Progress, they call it. Progress isn't always a good thing, is it? Sometimes, a bit of simplicity is just what you need. A warm cup of tea, a good book, and a bit of sunshine… though that last one seems a bit unlikely at the moment. Aye, you said it, Elsie. Couldn't ask for much more than that, really. Just a bit of peace and quiet. And the company of good friends. Couldn't have said it better myself, Arthur.

So, the sample sizes for the new lavender range are all ready to go. I’ve wrapped them up nicely, little ribbons and everything. Ready for influencers. That’s brilliant, Rach! Ribbons are a  must . Makes it feel more… luxe, doesn’t it? Are you sticking with the brown kraft paper for the packaging? Yeah, for now. It aligns with the "honest" branding, you know? But I'm starting to wonder if we need a slightly more premium feel. Maybe a frosted glass jar for the larger sizes? It's just… expensive. Yeah, that’s the balance, isn’t it? Looking luxe without blowing the budget. I’ve been looking at some suppliers, the ones in Tamworth – they’re quite reasonable. I’ll send you the links. Did you ever get those dimensions for the shipping boxes sorted? I need to factor that into the postage costs. Oh, good point! I got them, yes. Largest bottle is 9cm high, 6cm diameter… the little travel sizes are around 5x3.5. I've got them all written down somewhere…  rummages through a notebook  Ah, here we are! I was trying to figure out if we could get a flat-pack box to save on space. Flat-pack would be amazing! Less storage space needed. And lighter too, for postage. Right, I’ll have a proper look at box suppliers too. Speaking of postage, how are the returns going? Have you had many? Surprisingly low! Only two so far. One was just because someone thought the rosehip oil would smell like roses - they hadn't read the description properly, bless them! The other was a slight allergic reaction. I’ve offered her a full refund and a discount on a different product. You gotta be fair, you know? Online beauty is tricky – people can’t smell or feel it before they buy. Absolutely. Customer service is everything. You’ve handled that really well. Have you thought about doing more videos showing the texture and how the products apply? I've noticed a lot of the bigger brands are doing that. I have! I’m just… hopeless at being on camera. It feels so awkward. My mum keeps offering to film them for me, but she's a disaster! Oh god, I can imagine! Maybe just short, quick demos – like, "Here's the consistency of the lavender face cream, lovely and light!" You don't need to be a presenter.

Honestly, David, the news is just dreadful, isn’t it? This heatwave… utter chaos. Did you see that story about the railway lines buckling? I did. A complete mess. Though, to be fair, who predicted this level of intensity? It's unprecedented, really. How are you coping with it here? Still in the flat? Yes, still in the flat. It’s no good. The council haven’t got back to me about the repairs, you know. That leaking roof. It’s just… frustrating. I’m sweltering, and I’m worried about mould. That’s awful, Moira. I told you to keep pushing them. Have you got those reference numbers handy? I’ll give them a call tomorrow – from my end, you know. Sometimes they respond better when it’s not someone ‘troublesome’ calling. Oh, David, you’re a dear. Really. They give me such a runaround. It's always "we’ll look into it," "we’ll get back to you," and then nothing. It's like talking to a brick wall. I know the feeling. Bureaucracy is a beast. So, are you managing alright otherwise? Are you eating properly? I’m trying, dear. Trying. The food bank has been a godsend, of course, but it’s not exactly exciting meals, is it? Though, I did get some lovely plums the other day. At least there's  something  nice. I picked up some proper sausages from the butcher's yesterday. I'll bring you some next time I come down. And a Victoria sponge, as you like. Oh, David! You spoil me. I haven't had a proper Victoria sponge in ages. It’s the little things, isn't it? It is. And how’s your sister, Margaret? Still enjoying her gardening? Oh, she’s flourishing, bless her. She's got some enormous pumpkins growing. Absolutely enormous. Says she’s entering them in the village show. Competition's fierce, apparently. Margaret and her pumpkins. Never a dull moment. You should go down and see her, you know. Fresh air would do you good. I know, I know. But it’s just… getting out. It’s getting to the bus stop, dealing with all the noise… it’s exhausting. I understand. Look, I’m coming down next weekend. We’ll go for a gentle walk along the seafront, maybe grab some fish and chips. We can even pop down to see Margaret and her pumpkins.

Right, everyone, help yourselves! I’ve gone a little overboard, haven't I? Roast chicken, veggie wellington, loads of sides…felt like a proper Christmas feast, even though it’s… well, it’s not Christmas. Overboard? Never! It looks brilliant, Sarah. This smells amazing. Newcastle weather’s been dreadful – honestly, it’s really grim. Proper damp chill. It is gorgeous, Sarah. Thank you so much! Swindon's a bit milder, surprisingly. We had a proper fog this morning, though. Like something out of a Dickens novel. Makes you want to curl up with a good book and a massive mug of tea. That's just the way I feel, honestly! Been battling the wind all day trying to get some wood cut for some commissions. Absolutely freezing out there. Not exactly retirement material, is it? Bit too much effort! Retirement? You’re barely over thirty, Rhys! Although, I get where you’re coming from. It’s hard work being self-employed. Thinking about retirement... Honestly, I'm still trying to pay off my student loans, let alone plan for it! Tell me about it! I'm a long way off retirement, thankfully. But I keep thinking about it, the prospect of not having to deal with the factory floor… the constant noise and pressure. A bit of pottering in the garden would be heavenly. What kind of commissions are you doing, Rhys? Mostly furniture, some smaller woodworking bits - boxes, bowls, that sort of thing. I've been experimenting with using foraged materials too, you know, branches and bits I find on walks. It’s all about finding the beauty in things other people discard. Got some lovely mulberries dried from the garden this year - want to try them in a chutney. Mulberries! That's brilliant. I've never actually tasted one. Are they sweet? I’ve been trying to grow some in my little patch but they're being very stubborn. They’re beautiful, aren't they? The trees, I mean. We had a huge one in our garden when I was a kid. Pulled hundreds of mulberries off it every summer. Reckon it’s why I’m obsessed with research on plant ecosystems. Keeps the childhood memories close. This chicken is excellent, Sarah. Seriously! So, has anyone been playing any good games lately? My son’s been obsessed with that new strategy game,  Age of Empires . Drives me mad! I’ve been back into board games actually.

This cutlery is lovely, Mum. Where did you get it? Oh, this old thing? Your Auntie Maureen gave it to us years ago. Said she was downsizing, didn't need it all. Auntie Maureen has so much stuff, doesn’t she? Remember that time she tried to give us that ceramic cat? Oh god, yes! The one with the googly eyes. I think Dad hid it in the garage. I think I remember that. Hideous thing, it was. Cats… always peering at you. Now, now, George. Be nice. So, Liam, how's the project going? Still all spreadsheets and meetings, is it? Pretty much, yeah. It's a bit of a slog, but we’re making progress. Trying to get a handle on the efficiency reports is, well, a  challenge.  Sounds intense. Have you managed to finish that presentation for Friday? Almost. Just need to tweak a few things. I'll probably be up late tonight wrestling with it. Want to help? Nah, you're alright. I'd just make it worse. Besides, I’m exhausted. This apartment hunting has been draining. Oh, still looking for a place then? You should come with us to that open house on Saturday - over in Chester. Really? That’d be great, Mum! Any idea what it’s like? Well, it’s a Victorian terrace, apparently. Needs a bit of work, but it’s got a lovely garden. Chester’s a nice city. Shame it’s so far out. It's a reasonable commute, I think. Anyplace is better than my current shoebox. You need a proper kitchen, love. Somewhere you can put down roots. Cook a proper roast dinner. I’d love that. Properly roast a chicken. I’ve been meaning to learn. Roast chicken… too much faff. Fish is easier. Don’t listen to him. It’s not faff, it’s a Sunday tradition. Remember all those Sundays at Grandma's, Liam? The smell of roasting chicken filling the whole house? Yeah, those were good times. Actually, I was thinking about ringing Sarah - haven’t spoken to her in ages. Oh, Sarah! How is she? Still doing pottery? Last time I spoke to her, she was. Said she was entering a competition. That’s lovely. She always had a good eye for detail, that girl. Just like her dad. You know, I was thinking about organising something for George's birthday next month.

Mmm, this is lovely, darling. You’ve really outdone yourself tonight. Thanks, Mum! It’s my favourite. Can I have some more peas? Of course, love. More peas coming right up. So, work today, anything exciting happen? Anything you want to tell me? Not really. Mrs. Davis made us do fractions again. They’re boring. Fractions can be a bit tricky, can’t they? You'll get the hang of it. Listen, I spoke to the travel agent this afternoon about the ski trip. Ooh! Really? When are we going? We’re looking at the week beginning the 15th of January. It's just after school holidays in England, but before the proper peak season starts. Should be a bit quieter and hopefully, cheaper. Will there be lots of snow? I want to build a proper snowman! Well, the resort we were looking at, Zell am See, usually has a good snow record. We’ll check the forecast closer to the time, of course. But it looks promising. I was also looking at ski schools for you. There’s a really good one right at the bottom of the slopes, practically on the hotel doorstep. Can I have lessons with someone fun? Not a really serious teacher? I’ll make sure they're fun, sweetheart. I’ll read the reviews and look for someone patient. Your dad's going to be pretty good too, you know. He's been practicing his snowboarding. Daddy falls over a lot! He does occasionally! But he’s getting better. Right, let’s talk about your gear. Do you think your ski boots still fit? You grew like a beanstalk over the summer! I don't know. I think so. Maybe… I need new ones? We can measure your feet. I've saved some money for new ones if you need them. Actually, I saw a great deal on waterproof trousers too, might be worth grabbing those while we're at it. Yes, please! My legs got really cold last time. Can we get them bright pink? Bright pink trousers it is! Now, back to work… I have a meeting first thing on Monday that I am dreading. Mr. Henderson is going on about efficiency again. It's such a buzzkill. What's a buzzkill, Mum? It means it’s really boring and annoying, love. It's like when you have to tidy your toys. Oh.

Ugh, I’m so ready for the weekend. Maths was a total disaster today. Tell me about it! Mrs. Davies just kept going on about quadratic equations. Like, when am I ever going to  use  that? Never. Seriously, what’s the point? I spent the whole lesson doodling unicorns. Typical you. I tried to pay attention, but my brain just shut off. I ended up staring at the patterns on the ceiling tiles. Distraction is key, honestly. So, did you finish the Food Tech homework? The one about the nutritional values? Almost! I got confused about how to calculate the protein content in the pasta bake, though. I think I messed up. Yeah, that bit was tricky. Did you remember to factor in the cheese? Because that adds a decent amount of protein. Oh! No, I didn’t! I’ll have to redo it. Thanks. What about English? Did you start reading ‘Macbeth’ yet? I skimmed it. It's… depressing. All that talk about witches and prophecies. Bit much, really. I know, right? But Mr. Henderson says it’s really important for our exam. He keeps going on about tragic heroes and stuff. Tragic heroes. More like dramatically boring heroes, if you ask me. Anyway, did you hear about the new music festival they’re putting on in July? No! Where? At the park just outside Cambridge, near the river. They’ve got loads of indie bands playing. I’m trying to convince my mum to let me go. Seriously? That sounds amazing! Maybe we could go together? Definitely! We'd have to camp though, I think. Which is terrifying. I’m not sure about camping. Snakes, spiders… Don't be such a scaredy-cat! It’ll be an adventure. Anyway, are you thinking about what you want to do after GCSEs? Honestly? I’m clueless. Everyone’s talking about university, but I'm not sure. What about you? I'm thinking about sixth form, probably. Maybe do A-levels in Spanish and English Lit. I really enjoy Spanish. You're good at it too! I’m struggling a bit, I'll admit. Señora Rodriguez is really fast. Yeah, she is! But if you put in the effort, it's rewarding. I'm hoping it’ll be useful for something one day. Maybe I could work abroad? That would be cool! Maybe in Spain or Argentina? Imagine ordering churros in fluent Spanish.

Honestly darling, I was absolutely gripped by that new film, ‘Saltburn’. Have you seen it? I have! Just last week. It's… a lot, isn't it? A lot is an understatement! Quite shocking at times, I must say. Though I did find it rather compelling, in a perverse sort of way. All that opulence and then… well, you know. Right. It definitely sticks with you. I’m still thinking about it, to be honest. I mean, the cinematography was stunning, but the characters were so… unlikeable. Exactly! That’s what made it so fascinating, though. They weren't likeable people, were they? Just… behaving in a very particular way. The way they moved, the language they used… very studied. Did you notice that? Totally. It felt very deliberately crafted, like a social experiment almost. Did you find it a bit pretentious though? I felt like it was trying too hard to be edgy. A little bit, perhaps. But I think it was also tapping into something… uncomfortable. That yearning for acceptance, for belonging, even if you have to manipulate and deceive to get it. Reminded me a bit of ‘The Talented Mr. Ripley’ actually. Oh, I see what you mean. True, it has that sense of escalating obsession. Though ‘Ripley’ felt much more elegantly done, I think. Less… visceral. Yes, ‘Ripley’ was superb. It did it with a sort of refined undercurrent of tension. ‘Saltburn’ is much more in your face. I suppose it’s meant to be. It's more of a reaction to things. Definitely. What did you think of Barry Keoghan's performance? He was incredible. So unsettling. Absolutely brilliant. He managed to convey so much with just a look. The quiet intensity… chilling. And Jacob Elordi, too. He played the perfect blank canvas. He did. Completely believable as someone out of his depth, even though he was supposedly the golden boy. It’s funny, my friend Sophie said she walked out halfway through. Found it all too much. Oh dear. Well, it’s not for everyone, I suppose. It's definitely not a lighthearted watch. It's quite… dark. Do you think it will be remembered as a classic in years to come? That is the million-dollar question, isn't it? I'm not sure. It's such a deliberately provocative film. It might just be a flash in the pan. Perhaps. But it certainly sparked a conversation, didn’t it?

This coffee's lovely, Mum. Thanks for having me. Don't mention it, love. Always a pleasure. Glad you made it over despite the - well, whatever this is. Dripping again, isn't it? Typical Birmingham weather. It really is. I almost didn't make it, the M6 was a complete nightmare. Someone had pranged near Rugby, apparently. Oh, no! Honestly, people. Are they even paying attention anymore? I was driving into work this morning, and this young man, glued to his phone, cut me off. Nearly gave me a fright. I gave him a right piece of my mind too, I did. You did, didn’t you? You always do. It's a good job you're not the one dealing with them in court. Well, I just have to be professional. Can't be shouting at people all day long. Though sometimes...sometimes it’s tempting. Especially when they're giving lippy to the judge. I can imagine. So, have you seen any of the cricket? England look like they’re having a bit of a shocker. A shocker is right! I caught a bit of it yesterday. Honestly, I don't know what's gone wrong. Used to be so reliable. Still, plenty of time for them to turn it around. I hope so. I’m trying to get tickets for the football next month - Arsenal against Liverpool. It’s always a good game. Ooh, fancy! Let me know if you manage to get any. Expensive, aren't they these days? Everything is. Honestly, the price of petrol alone… I’m thinking of getting a smaller car, you know. Something more economical. That's probably a good idea. Mine's used a fortune since I started driving more for work. Speaking of work, things are busy at school, as always. Year 11s are stressing about their GCSEs, and I've got a new batch of beginners to teach French. They're a handful, aren't they, teenagers? Full of hormones and drama. Still, you’re good with them. You always were. Remember when you used to put on those little plays for your class? Oh god, don’t remind me. It was so embarrassing, looking back. But the kids loved it. It kept them engaged. Actually, I've been thinking of incorporating some drama techniques into my lessons again. That’s a brilliant idea. You always did have a creative mind.

Honestly, that seminar was brutal today. I felt like I was talking to a wall. Really? How so? I thought the topic – intersectionality and digital activism – was pretty engaging. Engaging for  me , maybe. But the students… they just weren’t connecting. I tried different approaches, used case studies, even threw in a bit of pop culture, but… blank stares. That’s frustrating. Sometimes it feels like you’re speaking a different language entirely. Did you try probing them on their own experiences? I did. I asked about social media usage, about activism they’ve participated in. Mostly crickets. A few mumbled responses about liking a petition. Yeah, that’s hardly revolutionary. Maybe they’re just shy? Or maybe the topic is more complex than they realize. Maybe. I’m just worried they won’t be prepared for the essay. It's a significant chunk of their grade. You’ll guide them. You always do. They’ll pick up on it eventually. Besides, you had a great point about the performative aspect of online activism versus genuine engagement. That’s important stuff. I know, I know. It just felt… inefficient. So much energy expended for so little return. Speaking of expenditure, did you remember to pick up milk? Almost forgot! It's on the list. I was thinking we could grab some of those dumplings from that place on Elm Street too. Oh, yes, please! I’ve been craving them all day. Spicy pork, right? Naturally. And I saw they have that new aubergine and mushroom one. Want to try it? Definitely! We should get a selection, then. Variety is the spice of life, after all. Absolutely. And while we're at it, need anything from the pharmacy? I think you were mentioning something about allergy tablets. Oh, yes! Please. My eyes are itching something fierce. Pollen count must be insane. Consider it done. Anything else? Groceries? Actually, yes. That new Thai green curry paste. The one with the galangal? Right! I think I saw it in the Asian aisle. Should be easy enough to find. Wonderful. That’ll go perfectly with the rice I made last night. It's been waiting for a worthy partner. You and your culinary analogies. It’s one of the things I love about you. So, dumplings, pharmacy, Thai curry paste... anything else you're secretly plotting to add to the list? Nope. That's it.

“…and the little bear snuggled into his mummy’s fur and felt safe and warm.” Safe and warm! Like me with you, Mummy! Exactly like you, my love. Right, you two, time to think about tonight. Grandma and Grandad are still up for babysitting, yes? No! I want to stay with you! I know, sweetheart, but Mummy and Daddy need to have a little dinner with Chloe and Liam. Remember, we talked about it? It’s a grown-up dinner. Can I come too? Oh, you’re a little small for grown-up dinner parties, darling. But we’ll have a super fun night with Grandma and Grandad. Maybe you can help them bake cookies? Cookies! Yes! Chocolate chip? Definitely chocolate chip. And maybe we’ll try that new banana bread recipe I found too. You both like that, don’t you? Yes! Banana bread is yummy! Okay, so dinner with Chloe and Liam at seven. Then Grandma and Grandad are here at six? Right, I’ll give them a quick call. While I do that, let’s finish this story. “The little bear closed his eyes…” Did you book the photographer yet? For the pictures? I did! Next Saturday. I sent you a couple of outfits to try on. Do you want to have a little practice pose now? Like a princess! Absolutely, like a princess. You look beautiful! Now, let me just confirm with Grandma... "Hello, darling? Just checking you’re still on for tonight… perfect! Six o'clock then… Yes, we’re really looking forward to it. The children are excited about the cookies. Wonderful! Thanks so much, love you! Bye." Right, that’s all sorted. So, everyone happy? Chloe and Liam are excited to see you, Grandma and Grandad are excited to bake cookies, and Mummy and Daddy are excited to have a proper catch up! Can I have another story? Me too! A dinosaur story! Okay, okay. One more story then. But after that, we need to think about getting a haircut, don’t we? Yours is getting a little long, darling , and yours is all over the place . I want a superhero haircut! Like Spider-Man! We'll see about that, superhero. Let's finish this story first, and then we can discuss superhero haircuts. Now, where were we…? “Long ago, in a land far, far away…” A princess! A princess and a dragon! Alright then, a princess and a dragon it is!

Ugh, this queue is ridiculous. Seriously, you’d think they were giving away free iPhones. Tell me about it! I skipped breakfast just to avoid this. My stomach's basically eating itself. Right? And they’re moving so slow. What even  is  on the menu today? It all looks kinda… beige. I think there's that chicken thing again. You know, the one that looks like it’s been steamed into submission? Oh god, don't remind me. I tried that last week. I’m still not sure what  kind  of chicken it was. Probably laboratory-grown. It definitely didn't come from a farm. You're probably right. I’m going for a cheese toastie. At least that's vaguely edible. Good choice. I might risk the soup. It  might  be hot. Or at least lukewarm. Remember that time last term when the soup was literally ice cold? Don't! I had to throw it straight in the bin. Wasteful, I know, but I wasn’t risking a chill. Totally. Anyway, you going out Friday? Liam was saying something about a new bar opening in Richmond. Richmond? Ooh, fancy! What’s it like? Apparently, it's got a rooftop terrace and loads of fairy lights. Very Instagrammable. Okay, you've sold me. Is it expensive though? I'm skint as usual. A bit, maybe. But it’s one Friday. We can just have a couple of drinks and then grab a kebab on the way back. A kebab sounds amazing, actually. You know what? I need something to look forward to after this uni grind. How’s your essay going? Don't even ask. I'm completely stuck. I’ve written like, three paragraphs and they all make absolutely zero sense. The classic student experience. Did you manage to get any research done in the library yesterday? I tried. But this guy kept clearing his throat  constantly . It was like he was trying to communicate with dolphins. Seriously? That’s awful! You’d have been better off just moving. I did, eventually. But then I ended up next to someone who was chewing with their mouth open. It was sensory overload. Oh, the horror! You need to invest in some noise-canceling headphones, honestly. I know, right? I'm thinking about it. So, cheese toastie and Richmond, then? Cheese toastie and Richmond, definitely. And maybe a large kebab. Just to be safe.

Honestly, I’m still recovering from that Christmas chaos. Aunt Maureen’s fruitcake… I’m pretty sure it’s still radiating heat. Maureen’s fruitcake is a legend. I think it's achieved sentience by now. Did you manage to escape with only one slice? Barely. I strategically pretended to be fascinated by Uncle Barry's stamp collection for a solid fifteen minutes, just to distract myself. He goes on and on about perforation sizes, you know? It's brutal. Barry loves a good perforation. I’m still traumatised by his explanation of the historical significance of Prussian blue ink on Victorian-era stamps. On Christmas Day. Oh, bless. So, serious question – have you guys seen that new documentary on Netflix, ‘Coastal Chaos’? The one about the disappearing beaches in Norfolk? No, tell me about it. It’s brilliant and utterly depressing. Really makes you think about how fragile our coastlines are, you know? Seeing those communities just… vanish. I glanced at some of the articles about it. Apparently, accelerated erosion rates are even worse than they initially predicted. Bit bleak to kick off a New Year with, isn’t it? Tell me about it. I need something bright and cheerful. Are you still obsessed with that Korean drama, Chloe? Obsessed is an understatement. I’ve watched the entire thing twice already. The food alone is worth the subscription fee. Have you ever tried making Bibimbap? I attempted it once. It was... an experience. Let's just say I ended up with a mountain of rice and a rather sad-looking fried egg. I’ve actually made it a few times, surprisingly enough. It’s not as tricky as it looks. The key is the gochujang – you need a good quality one. See? This is why I love having you around, James. You always have the crucial cooking tips. I need a cooking lesson. Seriously. I'm living on beans on toast and despair at this point. Actually, speaking of needs… Anyone fancy a weekend away? I'm thinking somewhere vaguely sunny and palatable to my weary soul. Sunny and palatable… Sounds good. I was looking at flights to Lisbon. Nice beaches, good food, relatively inexpensive. Lisbon’s excellent! I went a few years ago. The custard tarts are to die for. Custard tarts? You've sold me. Let's look at dates. Are you guys free next month? I need to escape the fruitcake fumes for a bit.

Lovely cuppa, Marjorie. Proper brew, this. Always do my best, Arthur. You're looking well, you are. A bit peaked, maybe, but well. Did you see that match yesterday? Didn't. Can't abide that racket, all that shouting. Give me a good horse any day. Now,  that's  a sport. Remember old Bess, Marjorie? The mare we had back in… Oh Arthur, don’t start on Bess again! You’ll be telling tales about her jumping over hedges all afternoon. Alright you two? Sounds like a proper reminiscing session going on already. Did you see that news about the election? Absolute shambles, isn’t it? Shambles is right, David. Waste of time, the whole lot of 'em. Promises, promises, never delivered. Like that new roof they promised for the community centre. Still leaking like a sieve. Oh, Arthur, don’t even get me started on the council. They’re useless. Remember when we wanted to sell the little terrace house? Took them ages to even look at it, let alone sort out the paperwork. They’re all the same. Speaking of selling, have you had any luck with that old Austin, Dad? Still sitting out in the drive looking like it’s about to fall apart. Trying. Put it on eBay, I have. Started the bidding low. Not much interest, though. Seems everyone's after these fancy electric cars now. Don’t know how you drive something with no engine! Ridiculous, innit? All these newfangled things. Everything’s too complicated these days. I miss the simple times. Well, simple times didn’t pay the bills, did they? Speaking of bills, my daughter's trying to convince me to invest in some cryptocurrency. Says it's the future. Cryptocurrency! Sounds like something out of a science fiction film. Utter nonsense, if you ask me. Keep your money in the bank, where it's safe. Absolutely. Remember that chap who lost his life savings on one of those schemes? Awful business. Honestly, it's a wonder anyone's still trusting those things. She assures me it's different this time. Higher security, reputable advisors... Reputable advisors! They’re all after a slice of the pie, David. Don’t be a fool. We were thinking of going down to Cornwall, you know, sometime next year. Might try one of those youth hostels. A bit of a change of scenery. Cornwall, eh? Nice. My students went to a youth hostel last year.

Honestly, the sleep deprivation is hitting me harder than I thought it would. I feel like a zombie some days. Tell me about it! Leo was up every two hours for the first six weeks. It didn’t matter what I did, or how comfy I was. He just wanted to feed. Exactly! And everyone keeps saying, "Oh, they grow so fast, enjoy every minute!" But some minutes are…challenging, to put it mildly. Like, 3 AM, screaming, projectile vomit challenging. Oh God, the projectile vomit. Don't even get me started. Once, he… well, let’s just say I needed a full shower and Leo needed a full outfit change. It was all over the walls! Oh no! Poor you. I had a few close calls, but nothing quite that dramatic. Maisie mostly just dribbles. Constant dribbling. It's like she's got a leaky tap attached to her face. Maisie’s gorgeous though. All big eyes and little eyelashes. Leo’s got my dad's nose, apparently. Mum keeps saying it's getting stronger as he gets older. She always says that about everyone's noses! Remember when she said I had Uncle Barry's nose? I nearly cried. I’ve got a perfectly normal nose! You did dramatically storm out of the room. Mum’s just… Mum. She means well. How’s breastfeeding going, by the way? I tried it with Leo, but it was just so stressful. It's… okay. I'm mostly managing, but I've had to supplement with formula a few times. My nipples feel like they’re on fire! I’m trying everything they said, lanolin, different holds… nothing seems to completely help. Oh, I feel for you. That was awful for me too. I ended up feeling like a failure, which is ridiculous, but it really got to me. Don't let anyone make you feel bad about using formula. Leo thrived on it, and I got some sleep! That’s what I keep telling myself. It’s just… there’s so much pressure, isn't there? Everyone’s got an opinion, from your mum to random people in the supermarket. Absolutely. It's exhausting. Have you heard from Auntie Carol lately? She was asking about Maisie on Facebook. Not recently. Actually, I muted her on Facebook. She keeps posting about all the “natural” remedies she’s trying on Leo. Like putting him to sleep with lavender oil and singing him ancient Sumerian lullabies.

Right, so, who's taking the bins out tonight? They’re overflowing again. I’ll do it. Promised I would, didn't I? Though I was hoping to get the shed sorted today. Shed sorted? What needs doing? Just a good clear out, really. Years of accumulated…stuff. And maybe put up some better shelving. I keep losing the gardening gloves in there. Well, you’ve got a lot of stuff, dear. You’re a collector. Remember that box of bottle caps you kept? That was a phase. A very brief phase. Anyway, bins tonight, I’ll sort the shed tomorrow. Anyone else got any chores they’re dodging? I need to get the washing on. It's building up. And I really need to deadhead the roses – they’re looking dreadful. I can deadhead the roses. I’m free this afternoon. Should I pick up some plant feed while I’m out? That would be brilliant, thanks. Anything specific you want? I'll grab the rose one, yeah. And maybe some for the lavender. It hasn’t been flowering much this year. Lavender looks a bit peaky. Maybe it needs more sun. Have you moved it? I thought about it, but I’m nervous about disturbing it. It's been there for ages, you know. Well, gentle encouragement won't hurt. Little bit of compost around the base, maybe gently teasing the soil a bit. Be kind to it. Speaking of being kind, did you see what’s happening with the strikes? The nurses are striking again next week. Awful, isn't it? Absolutely awful. They deserve so much better. It's heartbreaking, really. Watching them struggle like that. You must be stressed, darling. I am. It’s just… the pressure. And the pay hasn’t improved enough to compensate for the workload. It's not just me either. It’s insane. It’s all over the news. My dad was saying this morning how the government is just completely ignoring it. Sadly, it's the usual, isn't it? All talk and no action. Anyway, enough doom and gloom. What are your plans for today, Darla? Anything exciting lined up? Not really. Working from home, mostly. Got a big copywriting project to finish. Deadline looming. And catching up with Liam later. Oh, Liam? How’s he getting on? He’s good, yeah. He’s got a band gig Friday night.

Ugh, I’m so stressed about the Chemistry test next week. Mrs. Davies is being  brutal  this year. Tell me about it! I spent, like, three hours last night just trying to memorise the periodic table. It’s completely pointless, isn’t it? A bit, yeah. Though, I did find this really cool stamp online the other day. It's a Bohr model of an atom. Really detailed. A stamp? Seriously? You collect stamps? Yeah, it's kinda my thing. My grandad got me started. He’s got a  massive  collection. Anyway, it made Chemistry a little less depressing. Did you see the Christmas decorations in the town centre? Just a quick look. Loads of those awful fairy lights, aren't there? I wish they'd put up something a bit more… artistic. Like, a proper sculpture or something. Exactly! Or a giant Ed Sheeran bauble. Think about it! Okay, now  that  would be amazing. But remember last year when they had that huge reindeer made of pinecones? It fell over and blocked the whole High Street! Oh god, yes! Mr. Harrison practically had a heart attack trying to move it. Still, it was a good story. Speaking of stories, did you hear about Maisie's name being pulled for the Art competition? No! Seriously? She's brilliant! What's she doing? A landscape? Apparently, it's a watercolour of the weeping willow in her garden. She’s obsessed with that tree. She’s got, like, a million pictures of it. She always has been. Remember when she tried to propagate it? Her mum nearly killed her for getting mud everywhere. Yeah! But it actually worked, didn’t it? She’s got three little willow saplings now. How's your Maths homework going? I’m completely stuck on question five. The quadratic equations are doing my head in. Ugh, Maths. I think I managed to cheat a little bit on question five. Found a solution online. Don't tell Mrs. Peterson. You wouldn't! Though… maybe you could send me a screenshot? Just a hint, though! I’m not copying. Maybe. But you owe me one. Hey, are you still going to the Christmas fair at St. Mary's? Yeah, my mum’s making gingerbread. Want to go together? Saturday afternoon? Definitely! We can look at the plants they're selling – maybe I can get a Christmas cactus. Mine died last year.

Right then, Doris, you've seen it, haven’t you? The rat puppet, Arthur? Yes, dear, it's rather… striking. Where did you get it? Little shop down in Norwich. Right near the market. Seemed a good price, though I'm not certain about it, really. Bit unsettling, isn’t it? Unsettling? Arthur, it’s a conversation starter! A bit of whimsy. Besides, it’s quite well-made, I’ll give it that. The detail in those eyes... Eyes are what bother me most. Too lifelike. Reminds me of that Hitchcock film, you know. Oh, Arthur, don't be like that. It's just a puppet. Brightens up the place, doesn't it? Better than that old chipped teapot you were going to put on the mantlepiece. Oh, now, that teapot had character. This… this is just a bit… cheeky. So, are you still planning on getting your eyes tested, Arthur? You mentioned it last week. Aye. Need to. The buses… horrible glare, you know. Can’t make out the numbers half the time. Ended up going completely the wrong way last Tuesday. Ended up in Sprowston! Oh, dear! That’s quite a detour. It was. Young lad on the bus, though, he was alright. Helped me get back on the right one. But still, my eyes aren't what they used to be. Well, book an appointment. The NHS is doing quite well, from what I hear. No waiting lists as bad as some places. And I need to get mine done too, actually. Haven't had them checked in ages. Everything's a bit blurry these days. You should be able to see the rat just fine, Doris. Very funny, Arthur. You and your rat. I was just thinking, have you two been practicing the handbells lately? The church needs them for the Harvest Festival next month. We have, yes. A bit rusty, to be honest. My memory isn't what it was. Keep forgetting the sequence. I’m doing alright, I think. Still got it, you know. Years of practice. Just need Doris to keep up. I’m keeping up just fine, thank you very much. You’re the one who keeps muttering about misplacing your finger positions. Just a little slip of the hand, that’s all. Perfectly normal. Don't you start making a fuss. Well, good luck with it then. It'll be lovely to hear them ringing out again.

Right, so, the Rialto Bridge first, yeah? Then maybe Doge’s Palace? It's just… loads to see, isn’t it? Aye, it is. And St. Mark’s Square, of course. But be prepared for a right crush of tourists there, love. It used to be, you know, quieter. I remember coming here when I was a lass - proper lovely, it was. Fewer coaches, more locals just enjoying the sunshine. Really? It’s hard to imagine now. Every picture I’ve seen looks packed solid. Still, gotta see it, right? For the pigeons alone, haha. Aye, the pigeons are something else. They'll practically land on your head! Remember that little café, just off the Campo Santo Stefano? The one with the blue awning? No, I don’t think so. I did a bit of research, but there’s  so  much. Used to be my favourite. Best  caffè macchiato  you'd ever taste. And they did these little biscotti, perfect for dunking. They’ve probably changed, of course. Venice changes, doesn’t it? Everything does. I’m starving though. What about lunch? Think we need to sample some proper Venetian food, don’t we? Forget the tourist traps. Absolutely. We can’t come all this way and not have some  cicchetti . Those little snacks they have with a glass of wine. Like a mini tapas, but Venetian. Ooh, sounds perfect! Where's a good place to try them then? I don’t want to end up somewhere overrun with selfie sticks. There's a little  bacaro  - that's what they call a Venetian wine bar - called All’Arco, near the Rialto fish market. Brilliant  cicchetti  and a buzzing atmosphere. Proper authentic. Rialto market, right. I'll make a note. Speaking of which, should we head that way first? See the market, then grab some snacks? Perfect idea. It's a sight in itself, that market. All the fresh fish and fruit and veg… makes you want to cook a feast, doesn’t it? It does! Although, I’m terrible at cooking. I’d probably just burn everything. Don't worry about cooking! We're on holiday. Let's leave that to the professionals. I'm already wishing I had a proper glass of Venetian wine. Me too! I saw a gelato place near St. Mark's, too. We can get one after the Doge's Palace. Pistachio, definitely. Always a good choice.

Seriously though, I need to get back to the gym. I’ve been slacking  hard  this past month. My jeans are feeling it. Tell me about it! Bupa's wellness scheme is tempting me to actually  use  the free personal training sessions they offer, though. I’m terrified. Vulnerable, you know? Vulnerable to… getting fit? I think that’s a good kind of vulnerable. Which class are you thinking of? They have a HIIT one on a Tuesday evening. HIIT! Sounds horrific. Like intense punishment. It is intense, but it's brilliant. You'll sweat buckets, but feel amazing afterwards. More amazing than, like, a Friday night out, honestly. Don't tempt me. Friday nights are sacred. Especially with Liam being away next weekend. You coming out on Saturday? Saturday? Oh, probably not. I’m thinking of booking a last-minute flight to Barcelona with my sister. Barcelona?! Seriously? That sounds incredible. When were you thinking? Next week, hopefully. Flights are surprisingly cheap. Just need to convince her to swap her plans around. We were supposed to do that spa day in Dorset but...Barcelona sun feels much more appealing. Dorset sounds a bit… grey. Barcelona is definitely the move. Speaking of moves, how's work been? Still coordinating projects that are probably more stressful than they need to be? You know it. This new one's a nightmare. Trying to wrangle three different departments, and they all think they're the most important. It's exhausting. How’s Bupa treating you? Are you still loving the health marketing? Yeah, most of the time. It's just… corporate, you know? All the meetings, the buzzwords, the endless reports. But the team’s good, and the free health stuff is a bonus. Although, I still shudder thinking about that time I accidentally sent a marketing email about colonoscopies to the wrong mailing list. No! You didn’t! I did! It was a disaster. My boss nearly had a heart attack. Apparently, it’s not the best thing to do on a Monday morning. Oh my god. That's… legendary. So, are you still seeing, uh, what's his name… Ben? Nope. Dumped him. Turns out, he was less ‘independent artist’ and more ‘lives in his mum’s basement and eats microwave meals.’ Ouch. That's a brutal discovery. Sorry to hear that, but good riddance! More room for someone decent. Exactly! And you?

It’s just… overwhelming, isn’t it? Little Leo. A grandchild. I still can't quite believe it. Wonderful, absolutely wonderful. And born in France, too. Quite the little cosmopolite already. Yes, it’s lovely. Though it does make things a bit complicated, logistically. Flying back and forth, sorting visas… I’m already wondering how we'll manage Christmas. France is a good place to be born these days. Better than here, in some ways. Property’s cheaper, if you know where to look. And the spirit of enterprise… there are fewer bureaucrats clobbering you at every turn. I’ve heard that. Although, from what I gather, you still have to navigate quite a maze of paperwork. And the anarchists haven't entirely disappeared, have they? Never entirely. They're part of the French character, you know. Like snails and strong cheese. We had some French visitors just last year, remember? That charming couple, Jean-Pierre and Sylvie... Of course! They adored the Tate Modern. And complained incessantly about the lack of decent bread. Precisely! All this reminds me… did you hear about the Chichester Cathedral spire? Collapsed, apparently. Terrible. Oh, how dreadful! They said it was the work of an architect named Porden, wasn't it? A rather eccentric chap. All those fanciful carvings… Yes, Porden. Rather flamboyant for a cathedral, some would say. There’s an open day at the Architectural Association later this month. Photo exhibition of his work, and a lecture. Might be worth a look. They’re also running an art competition, themed around Anglo-French architectural influences. That sounds fascinating. I’ll have a look online. Speaking of local things, this new housing management company… they're a disaster. Absolutely dreadful. No response to emails, broken promises… Story of their lives, I'm afraid. The failings of the new landlord. It's always the same. They promise the world, then deliver… nothing. Exactly! It’s infuriating. And then there’s the entire bollard situation on Elm Street. Utter madness. I nearly tripped over one the other day! Oh, yes! The bollard debate! It rages on, you know. Some people say they're necessary, others call them an impediment to pedestrian traffic. Personally, I think they're ridiculous. I’m with you on that one. Anyway, enough about local grievances. I wanted to talk to you about the book. How’s it progressing? It’s coming along.

This sweet and sour chicken is actually pretty good, yeah? Way better than last time. Yeah, it's alright. Still prefer the noodles though. These spring rolls are rock hard, though. Seriously. Nah, they’re fine. You’re just being dramatic, Liam. You always complain. I’m with Liam on this one. These are definitely tough. I think they forgot to, like, finish cooking them properly. See? Even Alex agrees! You guys are being ridiculous. They’re just a bit crispy. Anyway, did you hear about Mr. Davies? The history teacher? What now? Apparently, he’s taking early retirement. Said he's going travelling around South America. No way! Seriously? He’s been there forever. Who's going to teach us the Tudors now? Probably some fresh-faced newbie who doesn't even  like  the Tudors. Remember Ms. Harding? She hated teaching Shakespeare. Ugh, don't remind me. She used to just read the sparknotes to us. Speaking of teachers, did you guys see Chloe at the weekend? She’s going out with Ben now. Crazy, right? Chloe? No way! She always said Ben was a bit of a weirdo. Yeah, he dresses like he’s permanently stuck in Year 7. But hey, love is blind, I guess. Maybe she's just trying to annoy Sarah. You know how they've been proper competitive since primary school. True. Mom said at the weekend that Auntie Maureen’s trying to get me to spend more time at home, helping out. Apparently, she’s worried I’m not eating enough vegetables. Your mum’s always on about that. You’re practically living on energy drinks and comics. I do eat vegetables! Sometimes. Speaking of comics, did you guys see the new issue of ‘Cosmic Crusaders’? The artwork is insane! I got it yesterday! Captain Nebula finally faced his dad! It was epic. I’m more into ‘Shadow Knights’ myself. The storyline is way more complex. ‘Shadow Knights’ is alright, but it's all a bit dark, isn't it? Give me lasers and spaceships any day. My mum keeps trying to get me to go to the gym more. Says I need to build up my ‘core strength’. Whatever that means. My dad keeps going on about my exam results. Like it’s all I care about. He doesn’t get that revision is a nightmare. Tell me about it. I'm drowning in coursework for this physics project.

Right, so we need to nail down the plan for Jonathan’s birthday, don’t we? It’s next Saturday – feeling ambitious? Ambitious is my middle name, love. I’ve been thinking… a proper buffet, definitely. Something everyone can graze on. And a few of those fairy lights we bought last Christmas. Fairy lights are lovely, dear. Reminds me of Christmas when the bairns were little... used to get so excited. Yes, they do. I’m happy to sort out a cake. Yorkshire pudding cake, perhaps? Jonathan’s always loved that. Yorkshire pudding cake? Seriously? Can we at least have some proper crisps? Like those sour cream and onion ones. Progress, Liam! We’ll have the proper crisps. Right, so buffet, cake, fairy lights. What about a theme? Any thoughts? I was thinking, since he’s been saving up for that new telescope… a stargazing theme! We could print out constellations, get some dark blue and silver decorations. That’s rather clever, David. I like it. Though I’m not sure how you’d make Yorkshire pudding cake look like a constellation… We’ll figure it out, Maggie! We always do. Liam, you’re good at those sorts of things – designing posters, that sort of stuff. Could you maybe whip up something? Fine, but don't expect miracles. I'm busy. It's lovely to see you all getting organised. Makes me feel quite lively, it does. Remember when we used to have parties like this every year? Before… well, before everything changed. We’ll keep those memories alive, Nan. This is going to be great. I've been clearing out the attic, actually. Found some old photographs. We can put them out on display. That's a brilliant idea! A trip down memory lane. I was thinking about moving house myself, actually. It’s getting a bit cramped now, isn’t it? Oh really, Gill? Where are you thinking of going? Somewhere with a bit more space, maybe a garden. Somewhere a little closer to Liam’s school, too. It’s a nightmare getting him to after-school clubs at the moment. I don’t need after-school clubs. You need to learn some responsibility, Liam. And maybe improve your drawing skills. You’d be welcome to come and stay, Maggie, if you ever fancied a change of scenery. Oh, I don’t know, dear. I’ve got used to this little flat.

Ugh, I’m stressing so much about GCSE options. Like, what even  is  media studies? Is it just watching YouTube all day? Pretty much! My cousin does it. She spends half the lesson filming TikToks. Though, she says you have to learn about camera angles and stuff. It's not  just  TikToks. Camera angles? Sounds massively boring. I was thinking about maybe drama, but Miss Davies is terrifying. She’ll find out if you don't know your lines and you’re doomed. Yeah, she's intense. But drama could be fun! We could write our own plays, maybe. Remember that disastrous school play last year? Don't remind me! I had to be a tree. A  very  awkward tree. And someone tripped over my roots. It was mortifying. Oh my god, yeah! But think about it - you're amazing at clarinet. Maybe music? You could do that and, like, proper music theory stuff. Hmm, yeah, that’s true. But what will that even  get  me? Like, what jobs can you even do with music? Besides being a starving musician in a freezing cold flat. My dad says you could be a music therapist. Helping people. That sounds pretty cool, actually. That does. What about you? Have you picked anything yet? I'm still waffling, honestly. I thought about graphic design, but then I looked up how much designers earn and it's... underwhelming. Plus, all those Adobe programs look complicated. Totally. It’s all so overwhelming. And everyone’s like, “Think about your  future !” Like, I’m eleven! My future is just surviving PE on a Wednesday. Seriously! Why do they make us do dodgeball? I always get hit. And Mrs. Peterson’s whistle is the most piercing sound known to man. Tell me about it! Speaking of annoying sounds, have you seen that new YouTuber, ‘GlamGoddess12’? The one who does those ‘Get Ready With Me’ videos? Oh my god, yes! She’s so fake. Like, she spills her coffee on purpose just to show how she cleans it up with some expensive face wipe. I know! And the way she talks about her perfect life. It’s so unrelatable. I’d rather watch Mr. Birch try to assemble IKEA furniture. You’re right! He’s way more entertaining. Do you think Billie Eilish is actually as sad as she makes out? Probably not. It's all part of the image, right?

Lovely bit of sunshine we’re having, eh? Wouldn’t have believed it after that deluge last week. Saw a kingfisher down by the River Tas this morning. Glorious thing. Kingfisher, you say? Used to see them regularly when I was a lad, down by Costessey Park. Not so much now. Too much building, I reckon. Spoiling the natural habitat. Speaking of habitat, have you seen the state of the foxgloves in the garden, ANON? They're absolutely rampant this year. Might have to get the shears out. Hi everyone! Sorry I’m a bit late, lectures ran over. The students were arguing about Brexit again. You wouldn’t believe the points they were making... Brexit, eh? Still going on, is it? Makes you wonder what the future holds. I was just thinking about the old Norwich City wall, actually. Remember when they excavated bits of it during the Northern Distributor Road construction? Aye, I remember that. They found all sorts of things, didn’t they? Roman pottery, medieval coins... A right palaver for the archaeologists. Cost a fortune, all that digging. They said it was the best-preserved bit of medieval wall in the county. Which is saying something, considering how much of Norwich got flattened during the war. It’s amazing, isn't it, how much history is right under our noses? I was reading an article the other day about Boudicca and the Iceni tribe. It's so fascinating to think they were right here, battling the Romans. Boudicca… powerful woman. Should’ve put those Romans in their place. Speaking of powerful, have you managed to sort out that problem with your computer, ANON? Oh, don't remind me! It's driving me round the bend. That new software update completely messed things up. I can barely send an email. I could take a look at it if you like. I'm fairly handy with computers. Although, frankly, sometimes I think they’re deliberately designed to be complicated. Back in my day, a computer was the size of a room! And they did everything you needed them to. No fancy updates, no glitches. Reliable. That's the thing, isn't it? Everything’s become so complex. Even driving’s got more complicated. My nephew just got a new electric car. So many gadgets and gizmos. Honestly, he's a test pilot, not a driver. Electric cars... Don’t even get me started.

Right then, Doris, you were saying about young Thomas’s school… still trouble, is he? Trouble? Arthur, he's a whirlwind! Absolutely refused to do his times tables this morning. Said they were “boring, Gran.” Boring! At his age, knowing your times tables is fundamental. Fundamental, that’s right. They don't teach them like they used to, do they? Back in my day, you were held back if you couldn't recite them backwards. Held back! Now that's what I call a school. Not all this hand-holding, allowing children to get away with murder. Though, come to think of it, I probably would have been held back. Never was fond of sums. Don't be silly, Arthur. You were sharp as a tack. Remember that puzzle you built, the one of the Spitfire? Ah, that was a good one. Took me weeks. Though I'm not sure about this modern nonsense... this tweeting and all that. Can't make heads nor tails of it. All this jargon… It’s a bit much, isn’t it? I use it a bit for the school, putting out reminders and announcements. But it's mostly cats and political arguments. Honestly, I saw a documentary about someone tweeting about cleaning their bathroom. It was all very detailed. Felt like a complete invasion of privacy. Cleaning your bathroom? On the telly? Good heavens. Speaking of cleaning, I’ve got that young lad coming round tomorrow to give the windows a good scrub. Keeps trying to sell me new curtains, though. Persistent, he is. Always are the delivery fellas. Always trying to upsell something. I had one the other day, trying to convince me I needed a smart doorbell. “Think of the security, sir!” I told him my ginger cat provides sufficient security. Oh, you’re right! Ginger cats are the best security system. Though, I’m a bit worried about my cataracts, you know. Doctor says I need another check-up. Cataracts! At your age? I'm surprised you can see at all. Arthur! Don’t be like that. It's just…the NHS is stretched thin, you know. Getting appointments is a nightmare. Tell me about it. Trying to book a routine check-up for my daughter… weeks and weeks. You hear those stories, don’t you? People not getting the care they need. Terrible business. Remember that joke I told you last week?

Blimey, look at this! I didn't expect it to be so bad even for December. It's proper swirling. Told you I wasn’t exaggerating. Cambridge gets properly snowed in sometimes. Makes the garden look like something out of a Christmas card, though. Though I doubt the roses appreciate it. Roses can wait. I’m just hoping I can get back to Newcastle before it gets worse. Train delays are gonna be chaos, aren't they? Probably. Fancy staying a bit longer? We could build a snowman, have a hot chocolate… I promise to be a more enthusiastic snow-builder than last year. Enthusiastic is a strong word. You threw a snowball at the cat. It was an accident! He darted out. Anyway... Speaking of things that require planning... have you given any more thought to the stag do for Liam? I've had a proper think. Right, so I’ve narrowed it down to either a weekend in Prague or a fancy distillery tour in Scotland. Prague's obviously more…wild. Scotland’s more…slightly less wild. Prague sounds good, yeah. Liam would love it. Logistically, though - getting everyone organised… I know, it's a nightmare. But someone needs to do it. And your sister's Hen do is rapidly approaching too. I heard whispers of a spa weekend… Oh, please no. Not another spa weekend. Sarah’s going to want cucumber water and meditation sessions. I’d rather wrestle a badger. Don’t tempt me. Maybe we should suggest something a bit more…active for her? Like, white-water rafting? You trying to injure her before the wedding? Just trying to live a little. Okay, okay, maybe not rafting. But something slightly less…cucumber-y. Has she booked anything for the venue yet? She's looking, but apparently everywhere good is booked solid. You know what I reckon? We should have a Come Dine With Me night here. Get a few of our mates round. It'd be cheaper than a venue and potentially more entertaining. Ooh, I like that idea! We could have a theme. Like, “North vs. Midlands” cuisine! I’ll bring a proper parsnip cake, you bring…what, a Balti curry? Precisely! I’ll even attempt a pumpkin dessert. Though I’m warning you, my baking skills are…questionable. That's the best part. Right, Come Dine With Me it is then. Now, back to holiday plans… Remember we were looking at that villa in Crete?

This roast potatoes are absolutely spot on, Dad. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Well, practice makes perfect, doesn't it? Though I still can't get the gravy right like your Grandmother used to. None of us ever could. It’s a good attempt, though. Better than anything I make, that's for sure. I always end up with either a watery mess or cement. Don’t be silly, darling. You make lovely meals. This is just… special. It tastes like Sunday dinners of my childhood. Do you remember? Your Dad making a Yorkshire pudding so big it nearly touched the ceiling? Aye, those were the days. Though I can’t say I appreciated it as a lad, always wanting chips instead! You were always a fussy eater, Dad. Still are, aren’t you? I’m not fussy! I just have… particular tastes. These carrots are a bit too soft, though. Typical. So, Mum, how was your day? Did you finally manage to sort out that leaky tap? No, not yet. I tried, honestly. Got all the tools out, felt like a proper engineer, but it was no good. Something's rattling around inside that I can’t reach. I’ll have to call a plumber. Might as well. You’ll probably end up causing more damage than the leak itself! Oh, hush you. I'm perfectly capable. It's just a bit of bother, isn't it? What about that apple crumble you promised? Apple crumble sounds lovely. I’ll put the kettle on. Earl Grey for you, dear? Please, Dad. And Mum, maybe we could have some custard with it? Of course, darling. Wouldn't be an apple crumble without custard. Though, goodness, all this lovely food… I’m going to need a nap afterwards! I’m with you on that. This is a feast. Best meal I’ve had in ages. Glad you're enjoying it. Your mother makes a good crumble, you know. Always has. Though I still think it needs a sprinkle of cinnamon. Don’t you start, Arthur! That’s my secret ingredient. Oh, here we go. The great crumble debate. Let’s just enjoy the food while it lasts. Before the arguing begins. Alright, alright. Just saying. A little cinnamon wouldn’t hurt. It’d make it even better. Well, maybe just a teeny bit... for Dad. Mum, could you put a little cinnamon in?

This roast potatoes are incredible, Mum. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Aye, well, I’ve been doin’ it for nigh on fifty year, lass. Gotta get it right by now, haven't I? Your dad’s always on at me if they’re not crispy enough. They’re perfect, Dad. Honestly. Crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside. Textbook. Aye, they’re good. Can’t complain. Nowt's ever good enough for some folk, is it? Back in me day, a plate o’ boiled potatoes was a feast. Grandpa, you always say that. Remember last Christmas when you said you’d happily trade the entire turkey for just one of Mum’s Yorkshire puddings? And I meant it! Best Yorkshire puddings this side o' the Pennines. Oh, you’re a cheeky one. So, Lena, how's the new flat coming along? You said you were looking at getting the kitchen re-done. It’s coming along slowly, Mum. It's a nightmare actually, finding reliable builders is practically impossible. They all either don't return calls or give ridiculous quotes. You could try that firm Liam recommended, remember? They did his bathroom last year, and he was really happy with them. Liam’s firm? I’ll have to ask him. I was looking at getting something completely different, though. I want these retro tiles, like the kind my grandma used to have. All orange and brown and… questionable. Oh, Lena, don't you be doin' that! That's takin' yerself right back to the seventies. I always liked those tiles. A bit naff, mind you, but… characterful. Reminded me of the houses in Sale when I was a lad. We had a bit o’ patterned wallpaper in our front room. Horrible stuff. Thought it would never end. I remember helping Mum clear out your old house, Grandpa. We found so much stuff packed away. Remember that box of old postcards? Aye, I do. Sent 'em from all over the place when I was a young lad. Blackpool, Morecambe, even a few from Scarborough. Dreamed of seeing the world then, I did. Never quite got round to it, though. You’ve seen enough of the world, Arthur, right here with your family. Speaking of family, did you hear from Michael? Is he still sorting out that promotion at work? Yeah, he had a call yesterday. Apparently, it’s down to him and one other.

Right, so I was thinking about this whole university thing, you know – student engagement, retention rates… it's a mess, isn’t it? Absolutely. I’ve seen it firsthand. So many bright students, but they get lost, overwhelmed, or just… bored. It’s a real shame. What were you mulling over specifically? Well, it stemmed from that viral video we saw last week, the one about the tiny home movement. Students building their own sustainable little houses – the engagement was incredible. I thought, what if we could incorporate that kind of hands-on, project-based learning into a core module? I liked that video immensely. It was so inventive. A core module based on what? Problem-solving. We frame a real-world challenge – lets say, designing a solution for a local community need, and students have to work collaboratively, research, prototype… even present their ideas to local stakeholders. It’s not just about theory. That's… brilliant, actually. It moves away from the usual lecture-essay cycle. But how do you make it scalable? A few tiny homes are a great demonstration, but you can’t build a whole campus full. Exactly. That’s where the problem-solving element comes in. The ‘tiny home’ aspect is the hook, the initial buzz. Then, it's about applying those principles – design thinking, collaboration, resource management – to something else entirely. Maybe micro-enterprises? Helping local businesses with marketing strategies, or developing apps for community services. I like the micro-enterprise angle. Gives it a tangible, real-world impact. What about assessment? You can't just mark a prototype or a design pitch. Right, that's the tricky part. A blended approach, surely? Peer review – crucial for collaborative projects. And then we could incorporate a ‘design journal’ where students document their process, their setbacks, their learnings. Like a social history of the design. It forces them to reflect. It does. Reminds me of that anecdote I read about Seth Godin. He talks about teaching his kids problem-solving by giving them a pile of mismatched LEGO bricks and saying, "Build something impressive." No instructions, just a challenge. Genius. Similar principle. It’s about fostering that resourceful mindset, that “I can figure this out” attitude. I was chatting to that guy from ‘Innovate Now’ online – he uses that exact method for brainstorming with his startup teams. So, how do you see this fitting with current curriculum structure?

Right, smells promising, doesn’t it? Hopefully this lentil dahl isn't another disaster. Last time it tasted like dishwater. Everything you make tastes like dishwater, love. Just kidding! Seriously though, lentils are tricky. What’s for dessert? Thinking apple crumble. Easy peasy. So, how was your week? Anything exciting at the ward? Ugh, don't even ask. We had a really rough couple of days. One patient was… well, let's just say restraint was required. You know how it is. But hey, small victories too. Met someone who’s made huge progress. It’s rewarding, you know? What about you? Crushing it with the projects, I hope? Mostly. This one client is driving me insane. He keeps changing his mind about the colour scheme. First it was teal, then navy, now he's obsessed with…burnt orange. It’s hideous. Seriously, who chooses burnt orange for a corporate office? Oh god, no. Seriously? Some people have no taste. Speaking of which, are you still planning on going to that Halloween party in Brighton? I’ve been meaning to ask. Yeah! Thinking I'll go as a very posh Victorian ghost. Monocle and everything. Fancy dress is my jam. You coming? I wish I could, but Saturday's my sister’s hen do. It's in Cornwall – Padstow, actually. Apparently, there’s a shellfish festival happening too, that’s a bonus. Cornwall! That’s lovely. I went there as a kid, Penzance. Remember the Minack Theatre, carved into the cliffs? Absolutely stunning. I've heard of it! We're staying in a little cottage near the coast, apparently. How about we try and arrange a weekend away together, after all this madness dies down. Somewhere… quieter. Maybe the Cotswolds? The Cotswolds would be lovely! I’ve always wanted to go to Bibury. That Arlington Row is so picturesque. It’s like stepping back in time. Right, so, five-year plan time. Where do you see yourself? Still nursing? Definitely still nursing, in some capacity. Maybe with a bit more seniority, possibly specializing in trauma. What about you, Project Queen? Climbing the corporate ladder? Something like that. Hopefully heading up my own team, leading bigger and more exciting projects. And ideally, with a slightly less demanding client base! Although, honestly, in five years, I just want a little cottage, a garden, and a dog. Somewhere with a proper pub nearby. A proper pub, essential!

Honestly, darling, the traffic getting here was absolutely ghastly. Took me nearly two hours, and I usually do it in ninety minutes! Oh, Mum! That's awful. I'm so sorry. Are you alright? Did you get stressed? Stressed doesn't even begin to cover it, love. A lorry decided to break down right on the M11 - completely blocked the whole southbound carriageway! Chaos. Just endless brake lights. Ugh, that sounds dreadful. I kept thinking about you. I’m glad you made it though. How’s the flat looking? You know, since… well, everything. It’s… it’s alright. Still a bit bare, isn't it? I’m trying to sort out some pictures, but I can't seem to find anything that feels quite right. It's all a bit… melancholy, if you know what I mean. I do. Moving on from Dad’s things… it takes time. Have you thought about getting that little floral print you saw in that antique shop in Rye? I remember you saying you loved it. Oh, that's a good idea! I completely forgot about that. Yes, I think I will. It’s brighter than anything else I’ve got. I’ll pop down there next week, I think. Brilliant. Honestly, just having something cheerful on the walls will make a world of difference. Are you eating properly? You haven’t been yourself lately. I'm eating. Sort of. Trying to, anyway. I have those ready meals, you know, the ones from Marks & Spencer. They’re not dreadful, but they’re not exactly exciting. You need to let me cook for you more often. I’m happy to come round a couple of times a week. We could even experiment with some new recipes. Oh, that would be lovely, darling. Really lovely. You make such a wonderful risotto. Remember that time you made it for Harry’s birthday? Everyone raved about it. Oh gosh, that was a disaster! I nearly set the kitchen on fire trying to flambé the brandy. Well, you managed to salvage it in the end. And it tasted delicious. Anyway... How's work? Still keeping you busy? It is, yeah. We're on a huge push to get this new contract finalised. Long hours, but it's good experience. It’s really interesting, actually. I'm coordinating the whole production schedule for this medical device. Pretty niche, I know.

Honestly, this weather is baffling. Sunny one minute, threatening to pour the next. Proper Yorkshire weather, I reckon, even though we’re in France! You’re terrible. It’s lovely! Warm enough to sit outside and people-watch, isn’t it? Besides, you were moaning about the rain in Doncaster just last week. Aye, but that's  normal  rain! This is… changeable.
