Like trying to guess what the football scores will be. Speaking of which, did you see the result last night? City were robbed, absolutely robbed! Oh, don't even get me started on football. I tried to watch it with Liam’s dad, but all I understood was the shouting. Is there a secret language to football? Scientific methods to predict outcomes, perhaps? You know Liam's dad? He’s a proper character. I had a chat with him about it, he just kept saying "It's the ref, it's always the ref!”. It’s a complex area, though, yeah. I was reading something about probability models applied to sports. See? Science! I knew there had to be a logical explanation for it. So, how's uni going? Still battling the French translation modules? Don't even talk to me about it. Proper brain-melting stuff. I'm trying to translate a technical document on, get this, the migratory patterns of… snails. Snails?! Seriously? That sounds… fascinating and utterly depressing at the same time. Exactly! It's like, who even needs to know this? And more importantly, how do I accurately convey "gastropod locomotion strategies" in elegant French? Oh my god. I feel your pain. My Anthropology module is equally wild. We’re looking at cultural interpretations of dreams across different societies – basically trying to figure out why everyone has weird dreams about being naked in Tesco. I can relate! I dreamt I was giving a lecture to a room full of pigeons last night. Classic! You need a break. We should go to that little jazz bar later. Apparently, they have a decent band. Oh yeah? What kind of music? I think it’s some sort of fusion – French jazz with a bit of Latin thrown in. Liam said it was pretty good. Plus, a chance to forget about migratory snails. Sold. Though, I'm still going to be thinking about those snails. It’s a curse, really. I'm probably going to start seeing snail trails everywhere.

Honestly, I nearly screamed this morning. I went to grab the toast and there was a huge spider right on the breadboard. Honestly, a proper big one. Oh, you don’t say! Where? Right there, on the wood. I froze, I didn't know what to do. My husband, Mark, he came rushing in, thinking something was terribly wrong. Did he get rid of it? He did, luckily. He’s much better at handling those creepy crawlies than I am. Popped it outside. I’m still checking behind the toaster though, just in case. You get them this time of year, don’t you? Trying to get in before the cold really sets in. We've had a few in the house too, lately. Nothing massive, mind you. More little ones. Yes, it's awful. It's not just the spiders either. I'm worried about mice at the moment. We had one last winter, a cheeky little thing. Oh, mice are the worst. Little nibblers. I had a right problem a few years back, you know, when my daughter was little. Kept finding little droppings everywhere. Ugh, that’s the most unsettling feeling, isn't it? It is. Ended up having to get a professional in, eventually. Wasn't cheap, but it was worth it for my peace of mind. Traps didn't do a thing. I considered that, but I feel a bit bad about trapping them. I know it's my house, but… I understand that. I felt the same way at first. But they were just making a mess and I was constantly on edge. Right, well, I'll try to keep an eye out and maybe put some peppermint oil down. I’ve heard that deters them. That's a good idea. It does smell nice too. Though, the birds are causing me some bother. Oh? What's happening with the birds? They're nesting in the eaves of the house. Making an awful racket first thing in the morning. And they’re dropping things, you know. Everywhere! Oh, yes, bird mess. It's so difficult to get off. Acidic, isn't it? It is! I tried washing it down with some soapy water, but it's not really shifting. I think I’ll need to get some proper bird deterrent stuff. Not sure what to do, really. They're a nuisance, aren't they. I do like watching the robins in my garden though.

It’s lovely to finally meet you, Gwen. I’ve heard so much about you from my mum. Oh, it's wonderful to meet you too, Eleanor. Your mother has spoken of you often. Such a dedicated teacher, she said. Such a good girl. She always did have a soft spot, didn't she? It’s funny, isn't it? We’ve been chatting on the phone for ages, but it’s so different meeting in person. It is indeed. It’s funny how voices can conceal a person, isn’t it? I’m so glad you agreed to come. It’s been a bit… lonely, since… well, you know. Since Mum passed. Yes, it has. It’s still very raw, isn’t it? I find myself thinking about her constantly. Especially when I see things that reminded me of her, like a certain kind of flower or a particular song. It will always be that way, love. A piece of her will always be with you. It's a blessing, isn’t it? To have had her for so long. The disease… it was relentless, wasn’t it? Such a cruel thing. It was. It’s hard to think back to when she was… lively and full of energy and then… the decline. The memory loss, the frustration… it was so difficult to watch. Did you ever see anything like that in your teaching, Gwen? People dealing with similar illnesses? Oh, goodness yes. I taught for forty years, you know. You see a lot in that time. Dementia became increasingly common in my later years. Awful to witness, truly. So heartbreaking for the families. One of my former pupils, a lovely boy named Rhys, his mother developed Alzheimer’s. It was devastating for him. He dedicated his life to caring for her, bless him. That’s… incredible. That level of dedication. It really put things into perspective. I sometimes struggle with feeling guilty, you know? Guilty that I couldn't do more, that I wasn’t there as much as I should have been. Eleanor, don’t you go doing that to yourself. You were doing brilliantly to juggle your teaching and your visiting. It’s not easy. Besides, she knew you loved her. She told me so, many times. She was fiercely proud of you, you know. She was? Absolutely. She used to talk about you with such warmth.

Honestly, look at that sky, Dan. It's incredible. Perfect hot air balloon weather, isn't it? It is stunning, yeah. Though I can’t imagine being that high up. Makes my stomach churn just thinking about it. Remember that time we went up in that little Cessna? Don't remind me! I thought I was going to be sick. You were remarkably calm, though. Well, someone had to be the responsible one. Though I did clench the armrests a little. Did you see that fox dart across the field just now? I did! Beautiful ginger colour. We’re so lucky to have this on our doorstep, aren't we? It’s such a change from the city. Definitely. Although, I'm still trying to figure out why there are so many power lines crisscrossing the landscape. It's a bit jarring when you're trying to appreciate the view. It's just the way Norfolk is, I suppose. Agricultural land needs power. Remember when we tried camping here years ago? Oh god, don’t even go there. The midges were biblical! I was covered in bites for a week. You spent the entire time swatting at them and muttering about needing industrial-strength repellent. And the tent collapsed in the middle of the night! We ended up huddled in the car. It was miserable. We definitely need a new tent if we ever decide to try that again. Though, with the dogs, maybe it would be easier to manage. Absolutely. They’d love it. Though getting Winston to stop chasing rabbits would be a nightmare. He'd be off like a shot. Speaking of which, did you manage to pay that bill? The vet bill was ridiculous this month. I did, yeah. Just about. It’s a bit tight at the moment, isn’t it? I'm thinking I might need to pick up some extra marking. The students have been particularly slow submitting this term. Yeah, it's tricky. Maybe we should look at cutting back on eating out a bit. We’ve been splashing out a bit lately. Those lobster rolls aren't exactly budget-friendly. You're right. It's just so nice to treat ourselves sometimes, you know? This countryside air is making me feel all nostalgic and frivolous. That's my girl. Frivolous and nostalgic. Fancy a coffee when we get back to the car?

Phew! That was a good session. My legs are definitely feeling it this evening. Aye, it were a good one, lass. Gave us a right good workout, you did. Bit warmer today than it has been, mind. It really is. Feels almost… summery. For March, anyway. I’m still not quite convinced spring is  really  here though, are you? Not yet, no. Still expect a frost or two before we get decent weather. Yorkshire weather’s a fickle thing, it is. Never know what you’re gonna get. I imagine! I'm from Hertfordshire, so we're fairly predictable – grey, mostly. What are you doing here in Solihull anyway? Seems a bit far from Leeds for a gym visit. I'm an Area Manager, see? I cover gyms across the Midlands. This one’s part of my patch. Makes a change from the Yorkshire rain sometimes. Though I do miss a proper cup of tea from Betty's, I must admit. I completely understand that. Speaking of changes, I’ve been trying something new at work. I’m incorporating this communicative approach to teaching French, really focusing on practical conversation. Communicative, eh? Sounds a bit modern for me. They didn’t teach us like that when I were at school. Just grammar, grammar, grammar. Couldn't string a sentence together to save my life! That's a shame! It's really rewarding seeing students actually use the language, have those 'lightbulb' moments. I found a great article on coaching techniques for language learning that have been really useful. Encouraging them to take risks, not worry about being perfect… Sounds a bit touchy-feely for a language, doesn’t it? What kind of books do you read, then? Something to do with languages, I suppose? Actually, not really. I'm a bit of a fiction addict, to be honest. I just finished “Piranesi” by Susanna Clarke. Have you read it? Can’t say I have. Susanna who? Clarke. She wrote "Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell." "Piranesi" is quite different – a bit dreamlike, set in this labyrinthine house. It's wonderful. Makes you think about the power of stories and place. Sounds a bit… abstract for me. I prefer something more grounded. Give me a good crime novel any day. Something with a bit of grit to it. Read a David Foster Wallace book once. Couldn’t get through it. Too clever, it were.

Right then, so the Hoover's packed away, is it? And the folding chairs too. Ready for Gran and Grandad? Aye, all done. Where did you want them to sit? I cleared the two armchairs by the fire. Perfect, love. They like the fire on, even if it's a bit warm. Grandad gets chilly easy. You remember when he tried to wear his gloves inside last time? Aye, and kept complaining he was melting! Melting, were we? Don't be daft, lad. I was just giving meself a bit of warmth. This room's like an oven, it is. She’s right, lass. Too much heat. Sorry, love. I’ll turn it down a bit then. I was just trying to make it cosy for you both. So, did you manage to get that new bit for the telly fixed? Matthew was saying it was fiddly. Aye, it's working now. Took a bit of messing about with the wires, but it's alright. Gran and Grandad will be glad to see it working, they love a bit of Bargain Hunt. We do indeed! That Alison Hammond’s a right scream, she is. Funny lass, she is. Glad to hear it. Right, I just need to pop the kettle on. Are you having a brew, both? Please, love. A nice cup of Yorkshire Tea, strong as you can make it. Same for me, lass. Strong and sweet. I’ll get the biscuits out then. Chocolate digestives, are they alright? They're always alright. Anything else you want? Any particular sweets or something? Just a bit of peace and quiet, love. That's all we need. Aye, a bit of quiet and a good cup of tea. That's the ticket. You two are a pair. I’ll be back in a tick. Just need to make sure there's enough sugar. Remember last time, Grandad, with the sugar bowl disaster? Oh, don’t remind us! You had to sweep it up for ages! It were an accident! I tell thee, it were. Just got a bit enthusiastic. Enthusiastic is one word for it! Covered the whole carpet, it did. Right then, tea and biscuits! Don't go getting too enthusiastic with the sugar this time, Grandad. And Matthew, love, could you put on Bargain Hunt for them? It’s just starting. Already on it, Mum. Alison Hammond's on the telly right now.

Are you sure this is right, love? It's taken us down this ridiculously narrow lane. Feels like we’re heading for Farmer Giles’ prize-winning sheep, not the Northern Echo Arena! The satnav’s usually reliable, Moira. relax, it's just a shortcut. Besides, a bit of adventure never hurt anyone. Keeps you on your toes, doesn't it? Adventure when I’m late for a ceilidh? That’s not adventure, that’s a recipe for a disgruntled band and a lot of disappointed dancers. They'll be wanting their shepherd's pie, you know. They’ll be happy to see us, Moira. And I promise, we’ll be there in time to at least appreciate the jigs and reels. Though I hope you’re ready to unleash your inner Scottish Highland dancer. Don't you dare. My knees aren't what they used to be, thanks to that dodgy step I took on the icy pavement last week. Still throbbing something fierce. I swear, pavements are out to get me. You need to be more careful, love. You’re worse than a gazelle on those things. Speaking of which, did you see that article about the ospreys nesting near Kielder Water? Ospreys? Fancy that. Haven't seen one of them in years. Remember when we went over to Scotland and saw that huge eagle? Nearly knocked me off my feet it was so impressive! Aye, wonderful day that was. Reminds me, I've been meaning to try and finish that poem I started about the Lakeland fells. The light was particularly stunning that day. Oh, you and your poetry. Still haven't managed to rhyme ‘aardvark’ yet, have you? It’s a challenge, Moira! A philosophical challenge. But seriously, I need to find some time. This gig is taking all my energy. How’s the novel coming along, by the way? Anything exciting happening in the world of your crime-fighting librarians? Slow progress. The library’s being threatened by a developer wanting to build flats. Typical. They’d tear down history for a hideous block of concrete. I'm rallying the local community. Might need to organise a protest. Good on you! Fighting the good fight. Though, if you're protesting, promise to wear sensible shoes. No more icy pavement incidents. I'll try my best. Speaking of sensible, did you remember to pack the wool for the craft stall?

Right, so, croissants or pain au chocolat for me, please. And a flat white, extra hot. Sounds good. I'll have the full English – gotta fuel up after that site visit. And a black coffee, strong. Honestly, that Victorian terrace was a nightmare. Absolutely crammed with unexpected plumbing. Tell me about it! I spent half an hour just trying to map out where the radiators were. It felt like a historical treasure hunt. Did you see the detail on those cornices? Seriously gorgeous. Yeah, the craftsmanship was remarkable. But trying to retrofit a modern bathroom into that space… near impossible. They need to seriously rethink the brief. Absolutely. It's those clients who want contemporary minimalism in a listed building. It's a recipe for disaster. Speaking of disasters, did you hear about Liam? Liam from the firm? What's he up to now? Apparently, he’s having a bit of a crisis on the Jacobson project. Said he’s just completely lost his mojo. Oh, that's rough. Jacobson's a huge deal for him. What’s the problem? He said the design reviews have been brutal. Apparently, old Mr. Jacobson is being relentlessly critical about everything. Every single detail. Jacobson’s notorious. Expects perfection. He’s impossible to please. Liam needs to remember that he’s hired us for our expertise, not to be a rubber stamp. Exactly! I told him to just push back, be confident in his vision. Don't let him bully him around. Easier said than done, I know. Well, yeah. It's tough when you're starting out. Remember when I was working on the community centre and the local council kept changing their minds? It felt like I was designing a completely different building every week. Oh god, I remember you were pulling your hair out over that one. How did you get through it? Just kept reminding myself of the bigger picture – the people who would actually use the space. It's easy to get bogged down in the nitty-gritty when you’re being micromanaged. True. Makes you appreciate the university project, doesn't it? I finally cracked how to approach the brief - focusing on that sense of communal living, weaving the shared spaces through the individual studios. Ah, the 'interconnectedness' theme. That's smart. I saw your initial sketches – really promising. Are you incorporating the vertical circulation element yet?

Right, kettle’s on. Fancy a builder’s brew or something a bit fancier? I've got some Earl Grey, chamomile… Builder’s is good, thanks, Mum. Proper cuppa. So, anything exciting happening? You look knackered. Just work, love. The usual whirlwind. Trying to wrangle a particularly stubborn client. They seem to think "urgent" means "five minutes before the deadline." How about you? Still enjoying the civil service life? Yeah, actually, it’s pretty good. Less stressful than I thought it would be, surprisingly. Though the commute… honestly. Today was brutal. Oh, tell me about it. What was the hold up? The A1. Total standstill. Some idiot decided to pull over right in the middle of the fast lane, seemingly for no reason. People were weaving all over the place. It was like a demolition derby out there. Honestly, people have no spatial awareness these days. I saw a woman yesterday trying to merge onto the A47 from a side road… going ten miles an hour. It was terrifying. Seriously! It's like they forget the rules exist. Or think they don't apply to them. It’s a pandemic, I tell you. A pandemic of bad driving. Have you booked that new pottery class you were talking about? Not yet. I looked online - it's pretty popular. Loads of dates are already full. I was thinking of trying Saturday morning, but I’ll need to check. Let me have a look online while we're having tea. I’m pretty good at squeezing things in. Speaking of things... remember Chloe and Tom? Vaguely. From university? Yes! Chloe messaged me the other day. They’re having a little get-together at their place next Saturday. Just a few of us. Thought you might want to go. Oh, that sounds nice! I haven't seen Chloe in ages. What are they doing? Just a barbeque, apparently. Said they'd love to see you. It’ll be nice to catch up. Yeah, definitely. Can I bring anything? Just yourself, love. They've got it all covered. So, are you seeing anyone at the moment? Don’t have to answer if you don't want to. Mum! Always probing. No, not really. Just focusing on work, and the pottery, and avoiding crazy drivers. Sensible girl. Well, you looked a bitpale, are you feeling alright? Fancy some of these chocolate biscuits? They are heaven. I am a little tired, actually.

Right, so I’ve had another look at the job description for this Producer role at BBC Radio Leeds. It really is perfect for you, Maisie. It  is  isn’t it? I’ve gone over it a dozen times. Still feel a bit daft even thinking about applying though, you know? My experience is a bit scattered. Radio, then freelance, bits of TV… feels like I’ve never properly settled. Don’t be ridiculous. That’s  strength , Maisie. You’ve got a breadth of experience most people would kill for. You’ve worked in different environments, with different teams, different budgets. You're adaptable! That's hugely valuable. Easy for you to say, posh Hitchin girl with a shiny postgraduate degree. I’m from Leeds, innit? We're a bit more… gritty. Don't start. Grit is amazing. It shows resilience. And honestly, your portfolio is brilliant. That documentary you did on the community garden? That’s gold, Maisie. Shows you can tell a compelling story, connect with people, and deliver a finished product. Yeah, but does it scream “BBC Radio Producer” loud enough? That’s what I’m worried about. This thing wants someone with experience managing teams, line producing… I’ve dipped my toes in, but not really  led  anything. Okay, let’s address that. Think about your time freelancing. You managed your  own  workload, deadlines, payments… that’s project management in itself. You negotiated rates, sourced contributors – that’s leadership. Frame it like that. Hmm, that’s a good point. I was thinking of glossing over that bit, to be honest. Felt a bit… all over the place. No, highlight it! Show them you’re resourceful and capable. And for the team management stuff, remember that short stint you had at Heart Radio? You mentored that intern, didn't you? Oh yeah, Liam. He was a nightmare, but… yeah, I helped him get his act together with his sound edits. See! That’s a perfect example. You took someone with less experience and guided them. You created a positive learning environment. It's all about how you sell it. Right, okay. I’m thinking of opening the application with a short anecdote about interviewing the head gardener for that community garden doc. Just to grab their attention. Brilliant! It shows initiative, storytelling skills, and a genuine interest in people. What about the skills section? Are you highlighting your editing software proficiency?

This view is absolutely ridiculous isn't it? I mean, you can see all the way to the ocean. It’s just…blue. It is fantastic. Makes you want to just… chuck everything and spend the rest of your life watching the waves. Which, you know, is tempting. Tempting, yes. Feasible? Probably not. Although, I’ve been wondering... what's the absolute  minimum  we'd need to live comfortably somewhere like this? Just us, a little patch of land, a decent internet connection… Minimalist paradise. We've talked about wanting that, haven’t we? Less stuff, more freedom. But it’s a big leap. Not just from teaching, but from… well, everything we know. Exactly. And you’ve got your business to wind down properly. Can’t just abandon that. Though, realistically, how much time are you  really  putting into it now? Point taken. It’s idling along, mostly. Which is fine, but… it’s not  driving  me anymore. It’s more like…insurance. A source of income while we figure out what we  do  want to drive us. Right. So, the business… we could sell it? Or transition it to someone else? Sell it’s probably the smartest. Transition would take too long, and I wouldn’t want to saddle someone with a project I'm not fully invested in anymore. We’d need to get a proper valuation, though. Okay. That's a 'to-do' then. I'll start researching business valuation services. And in the meantime, we keep dreaming about blue horizons. While thinking about practicalities. The most practical thing right now, I think, is nailing down this little business idea you’ve been hinting at? The pottery? Pottery sounds utterly quaint, doesn't it? But… it really does appeal. I've been thinking more than hinting. There’s a real market for handmade things, you know? And I’d genuinely enjoy it. It’s not about making a fortune… it’s about creating  something . Something tangible. Exactly. And something you’re passionate about. We could do it online, start small. A little Etsy shop, maybe? We’d need a studio space, though. Somewhere with good light. We could look for a tiny cottage somewhere, with a separate workshop. Ideally with a view. Like this. Don't spoil it already! Let’s be realistic, it’ll cost a fortune, even a small place. But we could rent a little studio first, just to see if it takes off.

Honestly, darling, the sheer volume of Polish families moving into Cambridge is putting a terrible strain on the schools. Absolutely dreadful. We need more classrooms, more teachers… Strain? Always a strain, isn't it? When people move, there’s a strain. Remember the influx of Canadians in the fifties? Caused a right kerfuffle for places in Bristol Grammar. It’s not just Cambridge, Dad. It’s everywhere. Little Leo's nursery had to put a cap on the number of Polish-speaking children. Apparently, they can’t cope. Well, nurseries are one thing, but primary schools are vital! Little Jamie needs a good education, a solid foundation. And these schools are bursting at the seams. Three children to a desk in some places, I hear. Three children to a desk! Good heavens. That's hardly conducive to learning. Though, I suppose, it encourages cooperation. Back in my day, we were lucky to have a decent slate. Remember when I was talking about my 40s party plans, Gran? It’s getting so complicated trying to fit everyone in. The housing shortage is insane. My friend Sarah’s daughter can’t find anywhere to live near her, even though she works in Cambridge. Honestly, it's a disgrace. Entire generations being priced out of their own country. And what about young Jamie? Where will  he  live when he’s older? You’re worrying too much, Margaret. Jamie’s only two. Plenty of time for him to build his own empire. Probably with a magnificent beard. Like that fellow on the telly…what’s his name? The one who sells sausages. Matt Dawson? He's used to rugby, not building empires, Dad. And Leo has absolutely no interest in a beard. He’s terrified of anything on his face. It’s terrible, isn’t it? Jamie deserves a good school, a stable home, a future... Everything's so expensive. It makes you wonder how we ever managed. I remember when a loaf of bread cost a penny... Nostalgia, Margaret. It always paints a rosier picture. Don’t forget the rationing and the endless queues. Though, I must say, the quality of healthcare  has  improved considerably since my younger days. My claim for a new knee replacement went through surprisingly quickly. Nearly didn't believe it! I’m still fighting with them about my mum’s care package. They keep disputing it. It's just endless paperwork and phone calls.

So, good to see you, Jan! It feels like ages. How are things? Lovely to see you too, Sarah! Things are… busy, as ever. Lunchtime superviser at the school, you know how it is. The kids are a whirlwind. And the sales, of course, keeps me on my toes. How’s everything with your proofreading? Still keeping busy? Yes, thankfully! Things have been quite steady. The marketing side is a bit quieter, but the proofreading is keeping me well occupied. It’s nice having the flexibility, really. Did you ever end up using that parking pass for the hospital? Oh, thankfully not. David's managed to stabilise, the rheumatoids, so we’ve not had to go as much. It's still there though, just in case. Remember how he was struggling to get into the car? Absolutely awful to see. Yes, I do. Poor David. Is he doing any of that exercise the physio recommended? Sporadically. He’s stubborn, you know. He'll do a bit, then declare it’s too tiring, and he’ll stop for a week. I’m forever nagging him. Makes me feel right old, telling my husband what to do! We all do it, don’t we? I was thinking about the referendum the other day, can you believe it’s been so long? Still causing chaos, hasn't it? Don’t remind me! It’s all anyone talks about, isn’t it? It feels like the world's gone mad. Remember when we were at sixth form, all that optimism. We thought we’d change the world! Oh, goodness. We were so naïve! What about Mrs. Davies, your history teacher? Do you ever think about her? Mrs. Davies! Brilliant woman. So strict, but fair. She really made history come alive. I still remember that project we did on the suffragettes. Mind you, I spent most of the time chatting to Mark Henderson instead of actually researching! Mark Henderson! I think half the girls in our year were pining after him. He did have quite the charm. What ever happened to him? Last I heard, he was working in London, something to do with finance. I saw a picture of him in the paper a few years back - his daughter was getting married. Looks like he aged well. Have you heard from Emma lately? Not recently, no. I saw on Facebook she's expecting a baby!

Right, so I was thinking about that thing we were discussing last week, about using Twitter for engagement with clients. Aye, the campaign for the new sustainable packaging rollout? Still feels a bit… tentative, doesn’t it? Definitely. I've been drafting some potential tweets, but I'm worried they sound a bit… corporate. You know? Like a press release disguised as a witty observation. Ach, it's a precarious balance, isn’t it? You want to build a rapport, appear approachable, but you don't want to come across as trying  too  hard. I saw a really cringeworthy post from a law firm the other day - attempting to be relatable using a cat meme. Oh, dear God. Don’t even. I had a similar experience with a financial services company trying to use a dancing video. Abysmal. What did you end up doing to adapt your strategy? Well, at Stevenson’s, we've just been focusing on consistent, genuine stuff. Showcasing our current students’ successes, sharing insights from our teaching staff. Nothing too flashy. So, less manufactured engagement, more authentic content? Exactly. And replying to comments, actively engaging with discussions. It’s surprising how much of a difference a simple “thanks for the feedback” makes. What about you? What's the biggest hurdle you're facing with the packaging campaign? I think it’s the whole ‘greenwashing’ accusation. We need to be transparent, but we also don’t want to alienate people who might see it as virtue signalling. Ken, you're overthinking it. People can smell insincerity a mile off. Just focus on showcasing the genuine positive impact of the new packaging. Numbers, facts, visual demonstrations… Yeah, you're right. I was getting bogged down in the potential backlash. I should just concentrate on presenting the information clearly and honestly. Aye. And try not to force it. Social media’s about being  social , right? Not a giant megaphone for your marketing department. True. I saw a great stat the other day - engagement drops dramatically when brands try to shoehorn in promotions. Right enough. It’s the same at Stevenson’s. We have strict guidelines about how frequently we can promote specific services. More emphasis on community building, you know? Sharing relevant articles, asking questions... I've been thinking about trying some short videos interviewing different people within the company. Showing the faces behind the brand, so to speak. Good idea!

Honestly, I need a full body detox after this weekend. Three weddings in a row? My feet are screaming. Three?! You’re mental. That’s a lot of canapés and questionable dance moves. How are you even standing? Pure adrenaline and a lot of blister plasters. Did you have a better weekend? You were working, right? Yeah, a pretty standard one. Bit hectic at the hospital, new patient arrived on Sunday, bit of a challenge. But at least I wasn’t dressed in a bridesmaid dress feeling like a slightly sad, floral lampshade. Okay, fair point. This one was particularly bad. The colour was... offensively lilac. And the neckline! I felt like I was constantly adjusting it. Sounds dreadful. Speaking of adjusting things, fancy a plate of this? I’ve been experimenting with a new curry recipe. Ooh, sounds amazing. Smells incredible. Is it spicy? I'm not feeling my spice tolerance tonight. Not too bad. I’ve toned it down a bit. Though, Sarah from work keeps trying to convince me to make a vindaloo for her - she claims it "cleanses the soul". Sarah sounds like a menace. Seriously, who wants to cleanse their soul with chilli? Anyway, how’s Mark? Did you see him much this weekend? Not really. He was at his dad's, helping him sort out the garden. Said he feels guilty for not being around more. Usual story. Honestly, they need to just talk properly. The silent treatment routine is exhausting for everyone involved. I know, right? I tried to subtly suggest they have a chat, but he just gave me that look. You know, the one that says, "Please don't interfere with my complicated emotional drama." The classic. Well, you can only do so much. Still, I bet he misses you. He's always moaning when you're not around to organise his life. He does, I think. But he's also got a stubborn streak a mile wide. Anyway... speaking of organising things, are you free next Saturday? There’s that new Thai place everyone's been raving about, thought we could check it out. Saturday sounds perfect. I need a good meal and some serious gossip. Did you hear anything about Ben and Chloe? Apparently, they had a massive row at the wedding. No way! I hadn't heard that. What about? Something about him forgetting her birthday. Classic Ben move, honestly.

That’s a lovely casserole, love. Really is. Proper hearty. Thanks, Dad. Glad you like it. It's that slow cooker recipe I was telling you about. Less effort, more flavour, you know? It's beautiful, ANON. Really, really delicious. Takes me right back to my mum's Sunday dinners. Except, of course, she didn’t have a fancy slow cooker. Just pure elbow grease. Elbow grease and a bit of luck, probably. Your mum was a magician in the kitchen, she was. Nobody could make a roast like your mum. Speaking of family, has there been any… news about Mark? From the counsellor? Not much. Still hearing the voices, seems like. He’s getting frustrated, I think. Says they’re louder when he's trying to sleep. Poor boy. It just breaks your heart, doesn’t it? What did the counsellor suggest this time? Same old. Mindfulness, medication adjustments… Nothing seems to be really sticking. He needs something more, I reckon. But what? He needs to  want  to get better, Dad. That's the key, isn't it? Easy for you to say, love. You're not the one listening to him yelling at shadows at three in the morning. Now, now. Don't start feeling guilty, John. You're doing the best you can. It's a difficult situation, that’s all. Are we still firm on Tuesday for George’s visit? Yes, Tuesday's confirmed. I’ve called Aunt Carol and she’s bringing over that lemon drizzle cake he loves. Should be a good day, as long as... well, as long as everything goes smoothly. He's got a soft spot for lemon drizzle, hasn't he? Always did. Remember when he used to steal slices when he was a boy? Oh, definitely. He was a little rascal. And speaking of stealing, I saw you admiring ANON’s new car earlier. It’s quite a beauty! It is, isn't it? Needed a bit of an upgrade, you know? The old one was starting to look its age. And it’s so much more practical for school runs. Practical’s good. Safer, too. That’s the main thing. So, you’re keeping it grey then? Yep, silver grey. Blends in, doesn't attract too much attention. You know I don't like all that flashy business. Sensible girl. Though a little bit of colour never hurt anyone!

Honestly, David, it's just blooming hard, isn't it? Spanish. I thought I'd pick it up a bit quicker. You always said the same about French, love. Remember that? "Oh, French will be a doddle, Elsie." Three weeks later you were complaining about the genders of everything. Well, French is massively different! All those nasal sounds… this is, I dunno, worse. The verbs alone! Conjugating them...it’s a nightmare. It’s tricky, I’ll give you that. But you’re approaching it wrong, I reckon. This Duolingo thing? Utter rubbish. You need more immersion. Immersion? Where am I going to get immersion, David? We’re not exactly living in Barcelona, are we? Youtube! Podcasts! There’s tons of it. Try listening to Spanish radio while you’re doing the washing up. Tiny bits at a time. It sinks in, you see. I tried that. I just heard a lot of rapid-fire chittering and felt completely lost. I ended up scrubbing the sink a bit harder. You need to start slower. And not just listening, Elsie, actively  trying  to understand. Look up words. Write things down. Don’t be afraid to look like a eejit. Being an eejit is already part of the process, love. I spent twenty minutes trying to say "the cat sat on the mat" the other day and ended up with something that sounded like “a fluffy rodent perched on a woven fabric.” Oh, Elsie, you are a scream. Look, take it from someone who at least managed to grasp a bit of German – repetition is key. Flashcards. Little bits every day. Don’t try to learn it all at once. You had it easy, David. You’ve always had a knack for languages. I struggle to remember where I put my glasses, let alone the subjunctive mood! That's a load of codswallop. I just persevered. And I concentrated on pronunciation. It’s the little things that make a difference. You can get the grammar right, but if you sound like a robot, nobody's going to understand you. True. It's just so disheartening when you put in the effort and it feels like you're not getting anywhere. You know, I was reading about Catalonia recently. It's fascinating how they manage it, isn't it? Speaking both Catalan and Castillian Spanish. It’s incredible, really. The way they've managed to maintain their own language and culture alongside the broader Spanish language.

Right, so this pile here seems to be purely banking statements. Loads of them. Do you reckon we should scan these first? Definitely. We need to get rid of the paper, don't we? Space is at a premium here, son. And you can access them online, can't you? Yeah, but it's good to have a physical backup, just in case. Especially with all this talk about ransomware and data breaches. Fair point. Just make sure you put them in secure folders, labelled clearly. Can’t have anyone stumbling across your finances now, can we? Absolutely. Where's the scanner? Oh, you moved it, didn't you? Behind the telly, brilliant. Needed the space. And it’s easy to reach, isn't it? You know, you’re alright with computers, aren’t you? Lucky you. I still struggle sometimes. It's fine, Dad. What about these ones? They're all related to… Kelly Brook, apparently. Kelly Brook? What’s that all about? Some kind of subscription? Bit random, isn’t it? No idea. Looks like some online magazine or something. Probably signed up for it ages ago and forgot. Well, discard those then. Unless you’re feeling particularly nostalgic. Definitely discarding those. Right, these next ones look like various medical documents. Appointments, test results... Very important ones. Keep those safe. Scan them, and then put them in a ring binder, labelled clearly. ‘Medical Records’ or something. Will do. So, Mom asked me to check if we could look at flights to the south of France. Any luck? Briefly. Prices are ridiculous, aren’t they? Absolutely ridiculous. Probably best to wait a few weeks, see if they drop. Yeah, probably. Trying to do some corpus linguistics research, and it would be brilliant to spend some time down there. Lots of potential sources. Corpus linguistics, eh? Sounds complicated. What does it involve? Basically, analysing large collections of text to understand language patterns. It’s fascinating, really. You can learn so much about how people use language. Sounds like a lot of work! Speaking of work, you’re teaching now, aren’t you? How’s that going? It’s good. Challenging, but good. Got a class full of teenagers who think grammar is the worst thing in the world. Tell me about it! I nearly choked on my cereal reading through some of your reports the other day. All the jargon. It's the nature of the job, Dad.

Right then, petrol. Where are we lookin' for? There's one just up ahead, Shell, I think. According to the sat-nav anyway. Though you know how reliable those things can be. Aye, tell me about it. Last time it led us down a farm track, didn't it? Thought we were goin' to end up feedin’ sheep. I still can’t believe it. Honestly, a tiny lane, right in the middle of nowhere. You were brilliant though, handling the car on that. Had to be, didn't I? Didn’t want to scratch your fancy motor. You get a little protective over nice things, don't you? It's an investment, isn't it? Plus, I like looking after it. Anyway, Shell seems legit. You want premium? Nah, standard's fine. Don't need fancy fuel for a wee journey like this. Saves a few quid, doesn't it? True, true. Always sensible. I noticed there were quite a few bikes on the road earlier. So many Harleys, specifically. Aye, loads. Heading to one of those rallies, probably. They’re always on the go, aren’t they? Loud things. Proper noise pollution. I can appreciate the engineering though. The sheer power. I’ve always been fascinated by engines, you know. I know, you're a proper geek for that sort of thing. Always tinkering with somethin'. It's a passion! I was reading about this new electric bike the other day, it can do zero to sixty in like three seconds. Incredible. Electric, eh? Still sounds a bit… dull, doesn’t it? No rumble, no roar. That's fair, it lacks a certain character. But the acceleration... it’s something else. Wonder if they'll ever get a decent electric motorcycle that actually looks and sounds the part. Doubt it. Seems like they’re always tryin’ to make 'em look like… scooters. Not exactly appealin’. You've got a point. Makes you wonder why they bother. Though, petrol prices are gettin' ridiculous. Maybe electric will take over eventually. Maybe. But I’ll stick to my petrol car for now, thanks. Less fiddlin' about. Ah, there's the Shell. Pull in? Yep, pull in. I'll grab a coffee while you're filling up. Need to stay alert for the rest of the journey. You drive, then? Aye, I’ll drive the rest of the way. You look like you could do with a proper sit down when we get there.

Right, so, this coach reckons you need to work on your backhand slice a bit more, doesn't he? Yeah, he keeps saying it. But it’s boring. Boring, eh? Well, Roger Federer built a career on a deceptive backhand slice. It’s not just about hitting the ball back over the net, lad. It's about placement, spin, frustrating your opponent. Easy for  you  to say, Dad. You've never played competitive tennis. That's not entirely true, you know. Briefly, in school. But the point stands. It's a strategic weapon. Like a good poker face. You don’t want to telegraph what you’re doing. He's got a point, love. And your forehand is brilliant, absolutely. But a good player has all the shots in their locker, doesn't he? You can't just rely on blasting everything. I know, I know. It’s just… everyone else is hitting these huge topspin serves and I’m out here slicing. It feels a bit pathetic. Pathetic? No, no. It's clever. It’s about knowing your strengths and using them. Remember that match against Tom last month? The slice completely threw him, didn't it? He couldn't return it. Exactly. And think about Alcaraz – he uses a lot of slice now, doesn’t he? It’s become a modern tactic. Not just for the older guys. Yeah, but he’s, like, a prodigy. I’m just… me. You’re a very good player, love. Just need to sharpen up that slice. And actually  enjoy  practicing it, not see it as a chore. Speaking of enjoyment – I was reading about that new coaching clinic down at the Sutton Coldfield club. Apparently, they've got a specialist slice coach. Really? We could look into it. It doesn't have to be a huge commitment. Just a few sessions. Or failing that, just practice against me in the garden. I'll happily be your target. Though you'll probably win every time. My backhand's atrocious. You would. Right. Dinner's nearly ready. Less phone, more chat about tennis. And less complaining about the slice, please! It’s all part of becoming a better player. You know, when I was your age, we didn't have fancy coaches or clinics. Just a worn-out tennis ball and a concrete court. Still managed to have fun though. Bet it wasn’t as good as Wimbledon though.

This is good, Nan. Really good. Better than last year. Glad you think so, love. It's the stuffing, I reckon. A little extra sage this time. Oh my god, did you see these napkins? They look like little pairs of underpants! They do! Where did you even find those? Mum, you’re brilliant. Honestly. I’m taking a few home. My flatmates will love them. They're a bit much though, aren't they? A bit? They're fabulous! It’s Christmas, Liam, a bit of silliness is allowed. Speaking of which, have you started your Christmas shopping yet? Nope. Zero. I'm thinking about getting everyone vouchers. Less stress. Sensible. I’m slowly chipping away at it. Got Sarah her perfume, Mark’s sorting his own stuff. I've mostly got my shopping done. Got everyone little presents. It’s always a mad rush, isn’t it? Christmas Eve is always chaotic with my friends. Last year, we had a full-blown dance-off in the kitchen! A dance-off, you say? What sort of dancing? All sorts! Loads of cheesy 80s stuff. We ended up trying to recreate those moves from Footloose. It was epic. You and your friends! What are your university mates calling you these days? Still “Lexi”? Nah, they’ve started calling me "Lex-Lightning" because I’m always rushing around. Apparently, I'm a whirlwind. Typical Lexi. Remember when you went to Florida, Liam? How was the airport? You looked so nervous! It was massive! I felt like a tiny ant in a huge machine. But it was worth it to see the sun. I miss it. You’ll be back. You're always travelling somewhere. Do you think you'll do more travelling next year? Hopefully. Thinking about maybe going to New York. It’s just… the cost is frightening. We all need to be a bit kinder to ourselves though, don't we? Especially around Christmas. It's not about the presents or the travel, it’s about being together. Exactly! It's the little things. Like Nan’s stuffing and Liam’s slightly questionable taste in napkins. Don’t you go teasing your brother! I worked hard on that stuffing. And those napkins were a bargain! I’m just glad we're all here. Do you think we'll watch Downton Abbey again this year? Definitely. It wouldn’t be Christmas without a bit of Downton.

Right, so, I’ve made a massive lasagna. Hope you’re hungry! Oh, love, that smells divine! You always were a dab hand in the kitchen. Better than your Dad ever was, bless him. Remember that time he tried to make Yorkshire puddings? Don’t remind me! They were flatter than pancakes, more like savoury frisbees. Nearly took out the cat. Oh god, I’d completely forgotten. He was so proud of them too! Anyway, lasagna… are we going to eat or just reminisce about disastrous dinners? Eat, eat! Of course, eat! So, how’s work, pet? Still coordinating projects that are threatening to fall apart? Pretty much, yeah. This one’s particularly tricky. The budget's been slashed, and the client keeps changing their mind. It’s… stressful. I might need a proper holiday after this. Sounds familiar. Always a challenge, eh? Keeping everyone happy, keeping the money flowing. Agriculture's not much different, believe you me. Dealing with farmers is a whole other level of negotiation. Oh, don't get him started on farmers, love. He’ll go on for hours about the price of wheat. It’s important! It’s the bedrock of the entire food chain! Speaking of food, I think I saw Sarah and Mark are back from their trip to Italy. We should get them over for a barbecue soon. Oh, that’s a lovely idea! Sarah’s got some amazing recipes, hasn’t she? You could pick her brains for more culinary inspiration. Definitely. I need all the help I can get! Though, I’d be afraid she'd judge my grilling skills. Don't you worry about that, lass. A bit of char never hurt anyone. Though, maybe practice a bit first. Very funny. So, Mum, how’s everything with you? Still no sign of Mr. Right? Oh, you know. Still chasing the dream, dear. Though, I did have a rather nice chat with someone at the WI meeting last week. Oh really? And who might that be? Oh, just Geoff. He’s got a prize-winning marrow, apparently. A prize-winning marrow! That's brilliant! You’ve got to meet him! Don't tease, love. It’s just a bit of harmless companionship. It’s nice to have someone to talk to, you know? Especially someone who appreciates a good vegetable. There’s no shame in that, love. A man who cares about his garden is a man worth knowing.

Right, so I was thinking, pizzas tonight? I’ve got some lovely mushrooms. And that feta we got from Marks & Spencer, remember? Sounds brilliant, love. I'm starving. Anything else? Just pizzas seem a little… sparse. Well, I was considering a bit of a salad. Big, crunchy salad. And maybe some of that ready-made pesto from M&S? They’ve really upped their game, haven't they? Their food section is incredible now. It is, isn’t it? I must remember to grab some of their mini sausages next time. For Barney, of course. He’d adore those. Speaking of Barney… have you noticed he's been extra clingy today? Almost like he knows something. Must be hoping for some extra tuna. Perhaps. Or maybe he's just sensing the lack of any serious effort in the culinary department. Right now, you're risking a feline intervention. Very funny. Right, salad it is. Now, about that appraisal… it was a bit of a mess, wasn’t it? A bit of a circus, more like. Clive seemed more interested in discussing the latest Walking Dead episode than actually assessing your work. Tell me about it! He spent a good ten minutes dissecting the latest cliffhanger. Honestly, you'd think I was grading his script rather than reviewing his transcription skills. He’s obsessed. He absolutely  has  to know what’s going to happen to Daryl. Have you seen Trapped? That Icelandic crime series? Far superior. I’ve heard good things! It's on my list. But I’m still catching up on everything. Remember how we used to do crosswords every Sunday? We never have time anymore. Don’t remind me. Life’s just... busier. Though, I did manage to sneak one in this morning. Bloody difficult one, though. Got completely stuck on 17 across - 'Equine welfare group'. Took me ages. Oh, you're joking! What was it? RSPCA. Honestly! I felt like such a fool. Anyway, I need to open that fourteen-year-old Merlot. It’s been languishing in the cellar for far too long. Perfect. It'll go lovely with the pizza. Oh, and I need to get a new blender. This one's rattling like a washing machine full of bolts. Seriously? Mine’s on its last legs too. Think we need to invest in a decent one this time. So we don’t end up with chunks of mushroom in our smoothie.

Honestly, I'm proper skint after buying new jeans. They were a steal though, like, half price in River Island. Worth it for the fit, innit? Ooh, show us! What colour were they? I'm thinking of treating myself. I've been eyeing up a pair of flares, but they're a bit pricey. Flares are amazing! I got some from Depop the other week. So comfy and makes your legs look miles long. Though, trying to walk in heels with them is a whole new level of difficulty. Tell me about it! I wore heels to that gig last week and spent the whole time wobbling around like a newborn giraffe. My feet were killing me by the end. I’m sticking to trainers for a while. Unless we’re going somewhere super fancy. Which is rare, let's be honest. Speaking of fancy, are we still on for that cocktail bar on Saturday? The one in the city centre? Saturday's good for me! I've been checking out their menu online. They do a raspberry and prosecco cocktail that looks absolutely divine. Ooh, sounds lush! I’m in. Do you reckon we should book a table? It gets packed on Saturday nights. Definitely book. Last time we just queued for ages. Plus, I want to make sure we get somewhere near a comfy seat. These dodgy knees aren't getting any younger. What are you all wearing? I’m struggling to find something that doesn’t feel too… much. I don't want to look like I'm trying too hard. I’m thinking a simple black dress. Can’t go wrong with that, right? Gotta accessorise, though. Maybe some sparkly earrings? I'm going with my new jeans and a sparkly top. Gotta show 'em off! I’m also debating whether to wear my Doc Martens or a pair of chunky boots. Chunky boots are so in right now. Go for those! I'm probably just gonna throw on a jumpsuit. Easy and stylish. Less thinking about matching things. I'm rocking a denim skirt and a crop top. Keep it simple, keep it cool. Though I might need to layer something over it just in case it gets chilly. I might just wear my leggings, honestly. Honestly, comfy beats everything on a Saturday. Unless someone buys me a really nice dress. Then maybe.

This coffee's actually really good today. I think I might make it properly tomorrow morning, instead of just whacking it in the machine. It is nice. You know, I was thinking about something last night... about personality types. Remember that Myers-Briggs test we did ages ago? Vaguely. It was before we even had Leo, wasn’t it? I think I came out as an INFJ, the ‘Advocate’ or something. What were you? INTJ, the ‘Architect.’ Very fitting, really. Always planning, always analysing. Do you ever wonder if our types are actually reflective of something deeper? Like, a soul blueprint or something? A soul blueprint? You’re going all spiritual on me this morning, aren't you? Well, it just popped into my head. It’s funny, I was reading about past lives the other day, and it makes you wonder if we’re drawn to people we’ve known before, or situations we've experienced... maybe that's what soulmates are. I think soulmates are a nice idea, but I prefer to believe in the power of shared experiences and genuine connection in this lifetime. Speaking of connections, did you manage to book that table at the Italian place for Friday? Not yet, I’ve been meaning to. I’ll do it this afternoon. Listen, and this is a purely hypothetical… imagine we could throw a party. A  really  good party. Like, if we could invite anyone from history, dead or alive. Who would be on your guest list? Oh, that’s fun! Okay, definitely Elizabeth I, she’d be brilliant entertainment. And Oscar Wilde, for conversation, obviously. Maybe Leonardo da Vinci? Imagine the things he could tell us. Genius choices. I’d have to have Marie Curie, for sheer dedication. And Winston Churchill, just to stir things up a bit. But mostly, I’d want to go back to the 1920s. A proper roaring twenties party. Flapper dresses, live jazz… I'd love that! Actually, I saw a documentary about the Apollo Missions last night. It was amazing to see all those scientists and engineers working together, pushing the boundaries of what was possible. You know, I often think about what it must have been like to be alive during those moments of such massive scientific and technological leaps. It’s incredible, isn’t it? Makes you feel tiny. Did Leo enjoy it? He mostly just wanted to know if they went to Mars.

Honestly, Sarah, I'm starting to think running a craft stall is more stressful than my actual job. Really? I thought you were loving it! All those lovely knitted hats and scarves… The making's lovely, yes. It’s dealing with the public, the weather, competing with those awful mass-produced things from China… it’s exhausting. And people haggle! They really do. Like I’m some sort of market trader. You  are  a market trader, love! You’re providing a service, a lovely service full of handmade things. Don't let them get you down. You’re far too clever to be bullied over a fiver. It's just…some of it feels so ingrained, doesn't it? This idea that handmade is somehow worth less. Remember that documentary we watched about artisan bread? People were saying, "Why should I pay fifteen pounds for a loaf when I can get one for eighty pence?" It’s just about mindset, isn’t it? It’s like… valuing skill and time. And supporting small businesses. Exactly! And you put your heart and soul into it. Speaking of which, how's Millie getting on? Still obsessed with those tiny, bright pink blankets you knitted her? Oh, she adores them. She drags them everywhere. Little thing's already mastering the art of the blanket fort. Though, I'm trying to get her into something a little less…fluffy. I’ve enrolled her in a little pottery class. Ooh, that’s lovely! She’ll love getting messy. My cousin’s daughter’s been doing that, she’s making little animal sculptures. It's surprisingly impressive. My Liam's always covered in paint. He’s started this phase where he only wants to paint dinosaurs. Giant, bright green dinosaurs. The house looks like Jurassic Park exploded. Sounds chaotic! I remember when Jamie was like that – obsessed with trains. We had enough Thomas the Tank Engine paraphernalia to fill a small warehouse. It’s just a phase, right? Everything's a phase. Speaking of phases, I've been thinking about taking a first aid course. I feel like I know nothing beyond putting a plaster on a grazed knee. Good idea, love. Honestly, it's sensible, especially with little ones running around. The office has recently mandated it for everyone, ridiculous really, but I've signed up for one next month. They’re even covering some mental health first aid, which is interesting.

Honestly, you wouldn’t believe the state of the kitchen. Like, seriously. Someone left a mouldy pizza box festering for a week. A WEEK! Classic Uni accommodation, innit? You’d think people would have  some  respect for shared spaces. Did you see Ben's Insta story? He’s trying to build a miniature football pitch in his room. No! Seriously? That’s… ambitious. I'm struggling to keep my desk clear, let alone build a football pitch. Speaking of which, I’m still stressing about those essays. Deadlines are looming. Tell me about it! I’m convinced Professor Davies has a personal vendetta against me. He marked my last one down for using the word “utilise.” Utilise! Like, who even says that?! Sounds like you're picking up the Norfolk accent, Chloe. 'Utilise' sounds awfully posh coming from Barrow. You’re just jealous because your vocabulary’s limited to “mate” and “sorted.” Oi! There's more to it than that! Seriously though, did anyone hear back about the festival tickets? I’m practically vibrating with anticipation. I’ve got a ticket, yeah! But I'm booked on the late shift at the shop that weekend, which is just brilliant. I’m trying to swap over, but Sarah’s being stubborn. She’s got that eye roll mastered, you know? Ugh, retail. Don't remind me. I'm working at the student union bar next Saturday. Free drinks, but the queues are insane. Plus, dealing with drunken Freshers – not my idea of a good time. Right, well if you're feeling brave, you can tell me all about the drunken Freshers. I’m going to be scouting for potential… let's just say, ‘study buddies’ for my accounting module. It's brutal, man. Study buddies? You're using the festival as a networking opportunity? Hey, gotta maximize my time, right? Speaking of maximizing, has anyone figured out the whole tax thing? It's completely bamboozling. Do I even  need  to do it as a student? Apparently, it depends. I’m pretty sure Sarah from the finance office said something about earning under a certain threshold… I'll send you the link she gave me. It's a nightmare, though. Honestly, the government just wants our money. I saw a post online about how much students are predicted to be in debt after graduation. It’s scary. Don't even go there!

This place is absolutely gorgeous, isn’t it? Look at those fairy lights! Proper dreamy. It is lovely, pet. Much nicer than that place in Pula we tried last time. Remember how grim that was? Yeah, that place smelled like old socks. This is way better. Is there Wi-Fi here, Mum? Probably, son. Let me check. Yes, it's got a decent signal. Though, honestly, are you going to spend the whole meal on that thing? Nah, just gotta see if Liam’s posted anything. He got a new tattoo, apparently. A wolf howling at the moon. Seriously? Liam got a tattoo? What did his mum say? Oh, she'll have had a right go, I bet. You know she’s got opinions on everything, that Fiona. Still, a wolf is quite a nice image. Better than those barcodes some lads get. Fiona’s a force of nature, that one. Reminds me of my sister back in London. Always something to complain about. So, what are you all thinking about eating? This menu's a bit overwhelming. I fancy the sea bass. Looks delicious. What about you, Dad? I’m going for the grilled octopus, love. Always fancied trying that. Hopefully, it won't be rubbery. I’m having the pasta with truffles. Apparently, it’s amazing. I saw it on someone’s Facebook. Of course you did. See, you are on Facebook after all. Right, I’m thinking the lamb chops. Heard good things about Istrian lamb. How's work going, Dad? Still chasing down dodgy consultancy schemes? Something like that. Keeping the wheels of capitalism turning, as they say. Just finished a particularly stressful project. Thinking I might need to take up cycling to de-stress. Seen any decent bikes around here? You and exercise. Don’t make me laugh. Remember that time you tried to run a marathon? Nearly had to be resuscitated! A slight exaggeration. But it did involve a trip to the hospital. Speaking of hospitals, Mum, how's the midwife world treating you? Still delivering bundles of joy? Most of the time! Though it's been hectic lately with the staff shortages. It's something else trying to keep things running smoothly. And the paperwork…don't even get me started. You wouldn’t believe the hoops we have to jump through now. It sounds awful. You deserve a medal. You know, I was thinking about getting a flat share when I finish university.

Right then, settle in, settle in. Cup of tea anyone? I’ve made a fresh pot. Cornwall was lovely, wasn’t it? Bit blowy, mind you - bracing! It really was lovely, Arthur. Absolutely beautiful. Though my knees are aching something fierce from all that walking. The YHA, too, was a surprisingly lovely place. Didn’t think I’d enjoy volunteering so much. Thanks, Arthur. Tea would be brilliant. Knees? You were practically bouncing up and down the coastal paths, Margaret. You seemed to have the energy of a twenty-year-old. Don’t be daft, David. I’m an old woman now! Just trying to keep up with you all. The kids at the YHA were a delight, though. Such good manners, despite everything. Aye, they were. Little Emily was fascinated by the lighthouse at Pendeen. Kept asking me if it was a giant candle. Lighthouse, eh? Did you go up it? I love lighthouses. Such stoic, solitary things. We did! A bit of a climb, but the view was worth it. You could see for miles. I got some right good photographs, actually. Got one of you, Margaret, peering through the window - looked like a worried pirate! Honestly, Arthur! Being a worried pirate is my natural state. Did you manage to see any crabs, David? You were so keen on crab spotting. I did! Found a whole colony scuttling around on the rocks at Godolphin. Brilliant little chaps. They were having a proper party, they were. Saw a rather large one as well - looked like he was the king of the crabs. Should’ve tried to catch one for supper. Oh, Arthur! You wouldn’t! They’re lovely creatures. We gave them all names. There was Horace, Gertrude, and Bartholomew… You got all sentimental with the crabs, did you? They were charming! It's lovely to watch them. Anyway, David, you were saying about that cycle race you organised… last weekend, wasn't it? Yes, the Great Yorkshire Cycle Challenge. I decided to attempt riding across Yorkshire in a day. Complete madness, really. Good heavens! Yorkshire? That’s a fair stretch! It was. Actually, it was harder than I anticipated. The wind was relentless. Nearly blew me off the road on the moors. So, you managed it? Eventually. Got to the finish line just as it was getting dark. Exhausted, but triumphant. Sent a few photos to the school. They seemed quite impressed.

This bread is brilliant, isn't it? Proper crusty. Yorkshire bread’s never like this, it's always a bit… soft. It is good! Annie makes a mean loaf, doesn't she, Liam? Yeah, it's top. Better than that dodgy bakery stuff you get round here. Dodgy is the right word! I tried to get a sourdough once, near the market. Tasted like damp cardboard. Oh god, I remember that! What  were  they doing? No idea! Anyway, so, Liam, you were saying about... Sarah? Yeah, Sarah. Look, it's a bit of a mess, innit? A bit of a mess? That’s an understatement, I heard. What happened this time? She, like, accused me of flirting with Chloe from the building site. Chloe? The one with the bright pink boots? Yeah. Said I was giving her "the eye." Honestly! I was just nodding cos she was explaining how to use a spirit level! I barely know what she says half the time. Right, well, that does sound a bit ridiculous. Did you explain that to her? Yeah, I did. But she wasn't having it. Said I was always talking to her. Well, are you? Talking to her, I mean. More than you need to for work? Not really, no. I mean, yeah, I’ll say hello, have a quick chat, but nothing dodgy, honest. Right. So, what did you do? Did you just walk away? Nah, I apologised. Tried to say I wasn’t trying to lead her on or anything. She just… started crying. Oh. That’s a bit dramatic, isn’t it? Tell me about it! Now she's giving me the silent treatment. Doesn’t answer my calls or anything. That’s a classic. You've got to be firm with this sort of thing. You can't just keep apologising for something you haven’t done. Honestly, Sarah needs to chill a bit. Aye, she does. Maybe give her a bit of space. Sometimes that's all they need. I don’t know. I’m worried she’ll properly kick off. We've been together for over two years, you know? Two years and she's accusing you of flirting with the girl in the pink boots? Sounds like you deserve a decent cup of tea and a lie-down. You do. Honestly, Liam, you're too good for that kind of drama. I just wish she’d communicate properly, you know?

Oh my god, it’s so good to be back! Barcelona was… intense. Welcome home! You look knackered. How was it, really? Tell me everything. Did you relax at all, or was it just constant sightseeing? A bit of both, honestly. The Sagrada Familia was incredible, obviously. But the crowds were manic. We spent most of Saturday just battling through tourists. I swear, I nearly got elbowed into a fountain. Classic Barcelona. I’m glad you got to see it though. Pictures looked amazing. Did you try the paella? Oh my god, the paella. Best I’ve ever had. We found this tiny little place in the Gothic Quarter, away from the main drag. Seriously, I’d go back just for that. What did you get up to while I was gallivanting around Spain? Did you just chill? Pretty much. Had a really restful weekend, which was exactly what I needed. Finished binge-watching ‘Succession’ – you HAVE to watch it, it’s brilliant. And caught up with Sarah loads. Ooh, ‘Succession’ is on my list! I’ve been meaning to watch it for ages. But everything’s been so hectic at work. Speaking of, how was the weekend shift? Anything dramatic? Not particularly. Standard Saturday and Sunday, thankfully. It’s good to get a reset after having everything at once. Got invited to a wedding, actually! No way! Whose? Liam’s cousin. It’s in October. Fancy coming with me? Oh, yeah, absolutely! That sounds lovely. I’ll need a new dress though. Everything I own is either embarrassingly sparkly or incredibly boring. We can go shopping! I'm free next Saturday, we could hit up Westfield? Perfect. Actually, speaking of plans, what are you doing next weekend? I was thinking of trying that Italian place we talked about, "Bella Notte"? I'm free! That sounds amazing. I’ve been craving pasta like crazy. You know what I also thought? Maybe we could book a weekend away sometime soon? Like, not Spain again – somewhere completely different. Paris? Paris! That would be incredible. I've always wanted to go. We could do museums, pastries… the whole romantic cliché thing. Exactly! Or, equally, somewhere totally random. Like, maybe somewhere in Italy? Cinque Terre looks gorgeous. Let's start looking at prices. It would be amazing to have something to look forward to after this crazy summer with work. Are you dating anyone at the moment?

This view is rather lovely, isn’t it? Much calmer than the bustle of London, that’s for sure. It is. Absolutely gorgeous. I needed this, truthfully. Dorchester's charming, but... well, it's Dorchester. A bit quiet for a Sunday morning. Quiet’s good sometimes. You don't get that constant low hum of… everything. What do you do back in Dorchester, if you don't mind me asking? I teach English. Secondary school. It’s rewarding, mostly, but exhausting. You know how it is. Dealing with teenagers… a constant battle of wills and trying to instill a love of literature. I can imagine. I used to try and teach my younger cousins a thing or two about business. Didn’t always go well. Oh really? What sort of business are you in? I'm an entrepreneur. A bit of a catch-all, I suppose. Mostly tech startups, investing, that sort of thing. Nothing terribly glamorous, just… trying to find the next big thing. Always has been, really. Even when I was a kid, I was trying to sell something. Trading Pokémon cards, mostly. We all were! I tried selling homemade friendship bracelets. Never quite took off. I mostly just ended up tangled in yarn. See? The entrepreneurial spirit's there, even if the product wasn’t. What was your first “real” job then, before teaching? Hmm, a real job… Let me think. I spent a summer working at a farm shop. Dreadful. Seriously, the worst. Picking strawberries for hours in the blistering sun... My back still aches thinking about it. And rude customers! Absolute horrors. What about you? What was the first thing you did before leaping into the startup world? Good heavens, that sounds awful. I actually started in financial analysis, very corporate, very grey. Spent a few years crunching numbers for a bank. Mind-numbing, truly. But it taught me a lot about risk assessment. Surprisingly useful when you're assessing the potential of a new app. I can see that. It’s just… completely different from inspiring a classroom full of teenagers. Although, there’s a certain amount of risk assessment involved in that too, I suspect. Predicting teenage behaviour... it's practically a science. That’s brilliantly put. It’s all about understanding the patterns, isn't it? Though frankly, I'm better at predicting stock market fluctuations than spotting the signs of a looming teenage rebellion.

Honestly, I’m starting to think living with Liam and Finn is going to be the death of me. Dramatic much? What happened this time? Did someone leave dirty dishes in the sink again? It's not just the dishes, Ben! It's everything. Like, I came down this morning and the kitchen looked like a bomb had hit it. Flour everywhere, eggshells on the floor, and Liam was trying to make pancakes. Liam and pancakes? That's a recipe for disaster. You have no idea. They ended up stuck to the ceiling! Seriously, the ceiling. And Finn just stood there filming the whole thing, laughing. Oh, they are something else, aren't they? You should've shown me the video. I didn't even want to look at it! I just scrubbed the kitchen until my arms were aching, and they were both still in their rooms playing video games. They’ll learn eventually, yeah? It just takes time. Remember when we first moved out? We weren't exactly domestic goddesses ourselves. That’s different! We at least tried to tidy up. These two… it’s like they don’t even see the mess. I said something about cleaning rota the other day and Liam gave me this look, like I was asking him to move mountains. Men, eh? Allergic to housework. Tell me about it. And it’s not just the mess. Finn keeps leaving his dirty laundry all over the living room floor. Like, last night I tripped over a pair of his socks. It was not a good look. Maybe you need to have a proper sit-down with them, a serious chat. You can't just keep hinting. I know, I know. But I don't want to be the annoying housemate who’s always moaning. You're not being annoying, you're being reasonable! You've got to look out for yourself, you know? This is your home too. I suppose you're right. Maybe I’ll suggest we all do a chore together this weekend. A big clear-out. That's a good idea. Force them to face the consequences of their messiness. Honestly, sometimes I wish I’d just lived alone. Nah, it's more entertaining with them about. Think of the stories you’ll have to tell. And besides, you wouldn't want to miss out on Liam's ceiling pancake performances.

Right then, that’s the lot in, isn’t it? Bit heavier than I thought it'd be this time. It is a bit, dear. They do seem to charge more for everything these days, don't they? Even the biscuits. Aye, you’re telling me. Used to be able to get a nice tin of Roses for a fiver. Now you're lucky to get half a tin for that. Honestly. Shall I put the milk away then? And those apples. They look lovely, Boskoop, aren't they? They are, love. Best apples going. Remember when we used to pick our own from old Mr. Henderson's orchard? Oh, goodness yes. Always a bit of a scramble to get the best ones. You nearly knocked poor Mrs. Peterson over one year, trying to reach a particularly nice one! Well, she should have been quicker! They were good apples. Got a lovely taste to them. Still, not quite like those you used to get at Christmas market in Norwich. No, those were special. Heavens, do you remember the smell? Cinnamon and roasting chestnuts… Aye. Fresh bread too. Used to take Margaret down there, every year. She loved it. Poor Margaret. It’s getting on, isn’t it? Seems like only yesterday we were all young and… Don’t go down that road, Elsie. Let’s just enjoy having everything put away. Got the heating on, haven't you? Feels a bit chilly in here. It has. Just turned it up a notch. Fancy a cup of tea, Arthur? I'll put the kettle on. Wouldn’t say no to that, Elsie. Strong one, mind. And a couple of those ginger biscuits, if you please. Coming right up, dear. You sit down. Let me do the work. You’ve got your feet up already. Always the same with you, haven't you? Can’t help it, Elsie. These old bones need a rest. Everything's getting heavier these days. Even the shopping bags. Well, you're certainly managing to get through those biscuits! Careful now. Can’t waste a good biscuit, can I? Waste is a sin, Elsie knows that. A sin, I tell you! ” Don't you start with the sins, Arthur! Tea's nearly ready. And don’t you be moaning about the biscuits! They're good for you! Full of ginger! ” Aye, full of ginger and goodness. That’s what you always say."” That’s right!

Right then, settle in, settle in. Cup of tea anyone? I’ve made a fresh pot. Yorkshire Tea, naturally. Ooh, that smells lovely, Margaret. Thank you, love. Could do with a good cuppa, me bones are achin' somethin’ fierce today. Aye, and a biscuit or two wouldn't go amiss either. Got any of them ginger snaps, Margaret? Them’s my favourite. Gran, Grandad, please. Don’t start your biscuit demands the minute you walk in. I’m trying to revise here, you know. History’s giving me a headache. Now, now, Daniel. Be polite. Your grandparents have come a long way to see you. And a biscuit won’t hurt you. I've got shortbread, ginger snaps, chocolate digestives… take your pick. Fine, fine. Shortbread, then, please. And Mum, seriously, I need quiet. Got my mock exams next week. Mock exams, eh? Fancy that. When I was your age, we didn’t have nothin’ like that. Just straight to the real thing. Scary as anything it was. Aye. And you had to work for it too. Not like these days, all computers and fancy gadgets. Proper hard work, it was. Honestly, Dad, you go on about the “good old days” every time you visit. Things weren’t  always  better. Just different. Daniel’s got a great opportunity, and you should be proud of him. Thanks, Mum. It is a bit stressful though. I’m trying to decide if I should apply to York or Leeds. What do you reckon, Gran? York’s lovely, isn't it? Right on your doorstep. But Leeds is proper big. More opportunities, maybe. Hard choice, lad. Leeds is all hustle and bustle. Give me York any day. Pretty buildings, nice river… peaceful. He needs to think about what he wants to study, too. And the course offerings. Has he looked into that at all? Yeah, I’ve done loads of research. York’s got a good history department, but Leeds has a wider range of modules. It's a nightmare. Right. Well, don’t fret. You’ve got time. Speaking of which, I need to pop to the shops later. Need more milk, and those washing-up tablets are running low. I could pop down to the shops for you, Margaret. Bit of fresh air would do me good. Oh, Gran, don’t be silly. You’ll get lost. And you know how Bob down the road is getting, always trying to chat you up.

Right, so anyone else try that new Gutshot stuff? The probiotic powder? Gutshot? Nah, mate. Sounds like something you’d give a dodgy kebab. I did actually. Saw an ad on Insta, you know?
