You’re so much smarter than you give yourself credit for. And having your bike back will cheer you up, I’m sure. I really hope so. Maybe we could celebrate tonight? Pizza and a movie? Absolutely! I'll order one as soon as they drop off your bike. We can even watch that cycling documentary you wanted to see. Really? That would be amazing! Thank you so much, Mum! You're the best. Don't mention it, darling. Just glad you’re getting your bike back. It's silly, really, to be fussing over a bike when you've got so much going on. But I know how much you love cycling.

Right, okay, so Rhys, you’ve completely blocked me. I can’t get to Bristol! Now, now, don't panic, Seren. I'm just strategically securing the route. It's a key piece of the puzzle, you see? Gotta control the west country! He’s just being greedy, that’s all. Wants all the best connections. He always did have a bit of a territorial streak, that one. Remember when he tried to claim the whole garden in Singapore as 'his' territory? Oh, goodness, yes! He insisted on building a fortress out of bamboo. Nearly gave your grandmother a heart attack. It’s infuriating! I need to get to Birmingham to pick up the cheese and chutney! It's crucial for the picnic tomorrow. Cheese and chutney? Sounds awfully posh, for a family picnic. It’s  delicious  cheese and chutney, Gareth! From that little farm shop near Ledbury. Not your average supermarket stuff. Speaking of Ledbury, I’m cutting through to Gloucester. Going to try to shut you out entirely, Seren. You're the worst, Liam! Seriously, this is a family holiday, not a railway conquest. Now, now, let’s all play nicely. It's a game, after all. Although I rather suspect Gareth is taking this rather seriously. I'm just maximising my efficiency, Dai! It's a strategic advantage, nothing more. Besides, who else will build the Welsh railway empire? You're just like your grandfather, always plotting and scheming. Remember him trying to buy the whole cricket club? He had vision! He just knew a good investment when he saw one. Okay, okay, truce. I'll let you have Bristol, but you're doing the dishes tonight. Deal. But you’re buying the cheese. Fine, whatever. Anyone else have any impressive rail routes to lay down? Liam, you’re awfully quiet. Just plotting my revenge. You’ll see. I'm going for Liverpool. It’s risky, but it’ll pay off. Brave move, Liam. Very brave indeed. Do you think the train will be reliable on that route? It's notoriously unpredictable, you know. Reminds me of the train journey back from Borneo... Oh, Dai, not the Borneo story again! We’ll be here all night. But it’s a good story, Mary! The monkeys, the delayed departures… Let’s stick to trains for now, Dai. Please. And Gareth, are you sure you’re not just hoarding all the grey trains?

Ugh, another three. This is hopeless, isn’t it? You’re practically guaranteed to win. Don't be dramatic, darling. It's just a bit of luck. And a bit of strategy, if I may say so. You haven't been employing your best tactics. My best tactics involve throwing the board out the window. Seriously though, how do you  always  manage to build this many houses? It’s uncanny. It's about prioritizing the orange properties, you know. New York, Tennessee, Virginia. They’re the choke points. Basic Monopoly wisdom. Did they not teach you this in Norwich? They taught me about medieval literature and the nuances of Beowulf. Not ruthless property acquisition. There’s a difference, you know. Well, both require a certain amount of strategic thinking. Besides, it's good practice for the grant applications, isn’t it? Negotiating our way to victory. You’re comparing a board game to securing research funding? Really? Absolutely! Resource management, calculated risk-taking, understanding your opponent’s weaknesses… it’s all transferable skills. Okay, okay, you’ve convinced me. I'm strategically disadvantaged and destined for financial ruin on this board. Can we talk about something else? Like what? The existential dread of late-stage capitalism? No! Like, have you noticed how ridiculously passionate people get about board games? Like, full-on competitive, aggressive… it’s kind of intense. It is, isn’t it? It’s fascinating, actually. A microcosm of human behaviour. Look at the cafe down the road. Thursday night board game club is more heated than a Premier League match. Exactly! And the drinking culture that goes with it! Like, it’s practically mandatory to have a pint or two to loosen up before you unleash your inner Monopoly tyrant. It’s the release, I think. A chance to be strategically ruthless without any real-world consequences. We're all quite civilized in our professional lives, so a bit of competitive chaos is a welcome change. I suppose so. It's just... sometimes I wonder if the joy of the game gets lost in all the intensity. Remember when we first started playing as kids? It was just for fun. It was, wasn't it? Without the pressure, the meticulous planning... just pure, unadulterated enjoyment. Do you think we’ve lost a bit of that spontaneity along the way? Maybe. Though I’m not sure it’s just board games.

Right, I think that’s everything on the table. Does everyone have enough? Kerrie, you've outdone yourself, honestly. This shepherd’s pie is incredible. Oh, thank you, love! Glad you’re enjoying it. Used Mamgu’s recipe, you know. Can’t beat a classic. Though, getting the mashed potato just right is always a battle. It’s definitely a win here. Seriously, this is better than anything I’d manage. I'm still struggling with gravy. It’s either wallpaper paste or watery disaster. You and gravy. It's a lifelong struggle, isn’t it? So, Kerrie, how's the packing going? Any closer to getting out of this place? Oh, don’t even ask! It's a nightmare. I thought I was organized, but I've clearly underestimated the amount of…  stuff  I possess. The bins are overflowing already. And I've found three vases I didn’t even know I owned. Vases are the worst. They just breed in the dark. How's the new place looking? Found a dishwasher yet? Because that’s practically essential. It's lovely, actually, a lot bigger than this. But the kitchen... the kitchen appliances are ancient! The oven looks like it’s from the fifties. I need to budget for new white goods, but it’s all adding up so quickly. Ugh, that's the worst part of moving, isn't it? All the unexpected expenses. Did you manage to negotiate that price down a bit? A little, but not as much as I’d hoped. The estate agent was playing hardball. Honestly, sometimes I think they’re all cut from the same cloth. They are. They genuinely are. Remember when I was trying to buy that flat near the station? The bloke just kept pushing up the price. Oh, I remember. How did that even work out? I walked away. Best decision I ever made. Turns out the entire building was riddled with damp. Luckily caught it before I signed anything. You were very clever to do that. I was thinking about getting a surveyor in for this place, just to be sure. Definitely a good idea. Especially with older houses. Speaking of older houses, I saw a thing on the news about… …the energy crisis. Apparently, it's going to get even worse this winter. Don’t remind me. My heating bill last month was terrifying. I'm seriously considering taking up knitting again, just to keep warm.

This traffic is mental, Mum. Seriously. I think we’ve barely moved in five minutes. Tell me about it. Should have left an hour ago. Honestly, London drivers… it's like a competition to see who can be the most aggressively oblivious. Exactly! That bloke in the Range Rover just cut me off completely. Didn't even indicate. I wanted to… you know. Don't you dare start shouting, Leo. Remember what your father always says: "Elevate yourself above the road rage." Easier said than done when someone nearly sideswipes you. Anyway, are we nearly there? I’m starving. Not long now. Just past the roundabout. Is Amelia still going on about needing a new bookshelf for her flat? Yeah, apparently hers is "structurally unsound." She’s being dramatic, as usual. I told her she could find one on Facebook Marketplace. Loads of good stuff there. She probably wouldn’t. Too much effort. She’s been moaning about wanting something vaguely Scandinavian styled… which means expensive. Oh god, you’re right. It’ll be a disaster. What about this TLS article you were talking about? The review of that new Booker Prize longlister? It was fascinating actually. Quite scathing, which is refreshing. Sometimes those reviewers just give everything five stars and rave on. This one actually critiqued it properly. Though the author will likely be furious. Do you think print TLS will ever really go away? There's something about the feel of it, you know? That glossy paper… It's a good question. I do feel a pang when I think about it. The digital version is convenient, of course, but it lacks that… heft. The ritual of reading it with a cup of coffee on a Sunday morning. Yeah, exactly. And the smell of the ink. Although, I wouldn’t put it past them to try and replicate that with artificial scent somehow and charge extra. Don’t give them any ideas! Speaking of ideas, did you finalize your Christmas present for your aunt? Almost. Thinking about one of those Parisian food hampers. She's always talking about wanting to go back to France. That's a lovely idea! She’d adore that. Remember that trip we took to Provence? That lavender farm… Oh yeah! The one where the car broke down and we had to wait three hours for the AA. Don't remind me! That was… memorable.

Right, okay, you’ve all heard about my holiday disaster, but you haven't heard the  full  extent of it. Oh, we’ve heard enough to know you’re still traumatised. Sunburn and lost luggage, what more could go wrong? Honestly, Matty, you've no idea. So, the missing luggage was bad enough, right? But then… the hotel upgraded me to a room overlooking the beach. Lovely, sounds perfect, yeah? Of course! What’s the catch? The catch was that directly beneath my balcony was the hotel's laundry area. And they decided to wash every single duvet cover in the entire hotel… at 6 am. Industrial washing machines, blaring, non-stop, for three hours. I didn't sleep a wink. Oh, that’s rotten. Proper grim. Serves you right for going to Majorca in August, Rach. You knew what you were signing up for. Easy for you to say, Mr. ‘Spent the entire holiday studying for his masters.’ Hey! It was research! Atmospheric observation of Spanish sunsets. Very important work. Yeah, right. I’m sure you “observed” quite a lot more than just sunsets. Leave it, will you? Anyway, my holiday was pretty uneventful. Loads of reading, a few beers… Boring! Let’s hear a story, Liam. Anything! I've got one! Remember Sarah's trip to Italy last year? The one where she ended up accidentally joining a wedding? That’s the one! So, she’s wandering around Florence, right, admiring the Duomo, and suddenly she's surrounded by people in traditional clothing, throwing confetti… Turns out, she’d stumbled into a Tuscan wedding. No way! Seriously! They insisted she was the missing cousin and made her pose for photos with the bride and groom. She even got a plate piled high with pasta. Did she stay for the whole thing? Nah, after about an hour she realised she was slightly out of place and managed to escape without causing too much of a scene. Apparently, the bride’s grandmother was convinced Sarah was a sign of good luck. Oh, that's brilliant! You only live once, eh? Speaking of living once... did anyone hear about Mitchell trying to learn to surf? Mitchell? Surf?! No way. He’ll be falling over quicker than a dropped pint! Apparently, he wiped out so spectacularly the lifeguard had to fish him out of the water. He ended up swallowing half the Atlantic.

Right then, so David was saying you’re thinking of giving this wild winter camping thing a go, Fiona? Brave soul! It’s not for the faint of heart, that's for sure. Brave or foolish, Malcolm, we’ll see! Callum's been going on about it for ages, and frankly, I'm intrigued. It sounds... bracing. Just a weekend though, mind. No expeditions to the Arctic just yet. It’s incredible, honestly. The quiet, the stars… you’ve never seen so many stars. And the way the landscape transforms - it’s almost fairytale-like under a blanket of snow. It's utterly beautiful, yes. But don’t let that fool you. It’s brutal. Last January, I forgot my thermal socks… a rookie mistake! Spent the night shivering like a leaf. Even with a good sleeping bag, the cold bites. Thermal socks. Noted! What about safety, Callum? I mean, getting stranded, weather changes... Absolutely crucial. Navigation is key - map, compass, GPS. Layers are your best friend. And you’ve  got  to tell someone where you’re going and when you expect to be back. Always. I carry a personal locator beacon, just in case. Good man, good man. And a proper stove – not one of those little backpacking ones. You need something that can boil water quickly and efficiently. Hypothermia is a serious risk, you know. You’ve got all that sorted then? Because I’m not going to be dragged into some perilous situation! Mum, relax! I’ve been doing this for a few years now. I wouldn't put you or anyone else at risk. I’ve got all the gear, all the experience. It’s all about respect for the environment and being prepared. He’s got a point, you know. There's a real mindfulness to it. Being out there, stripped back to basics, just you and nature... it's a powerful thing. Forces you to be present, appreciate the small things. I always feel utterly refreshed after a few days. Mentally, you know. All the academic stress just melts away. That’s tempting, actually. I’ve been feeling rather… scattered lately. All the therapy work takes its toll. Perhaps a weekend in the wilderness  is  exactly what I need. Think of it – no emails, no clients, just the sound of the wind and a crackling fire. Don't forget a good book, Fiona. Something dense enough to distract you from the cold!

Honestly, I’m still reeling from ‘Everything Everywhere All at Once’. I mean, talk about ambitious. It was… a lot. Visually stunning, absolutely, but I’m not sure it entirely landed for me. Too much, maybe? A bit chaotic. See, I loved the chaos! I thought it was brilliant. The way they tied in all those seemingly random elements – the googly eyes, the raccoon chef... it all felt so deliberate. Plus, Michelle Yeoh was incredible. Agreed about Michelle Yeoh – phenomenal. She carried the whole thing. But the multiverse hopping? It felt… convoluted. I got a bit lost in the rules, if there even  were  rules. I think the point was that there weren’t strict rules. It was meant to be disorienting, reflect the feeling of being overwhelmed by choice, by life, you know? I suppose so. I just prefer my science fiction a bit more grounded, a bit more… logical. Less butt plugs as weapons, if you catch my drift. Oh, come on! That was the best part! Pure absurdist genius. It’s like a David Lynch film mixed with a Pixar movie. Right. Okay. Well, while you’re waxing lyrical about butt plugs and multiverses, I was thinking about re-reading ‘The Picture of Dorian Gray’. Have you ever read it? Yeah, ages ago, back in Sixth Form. Oscar Wilde, right? All that decadent prose? I remember liking it, but I don’t remember much of the plot, to be honest. You should revisit it. It's more than just decadent prose. The exploration of vanity, morality, the consequences of chasing eternal youth… it’s surprisingly relevant even today. It’s got a real unsettling undercurrent. Huh, maybe I will. Got anything good for dinner planned? I’m starving. I was thinking we could grab some Korean fried chicken. That place we tried last month? The one with the gochujang glaze? Oh my god, yes! That was amazing. So crispy and spicy. I’ve been craving it ever since. Perfect then. Korean fried chicken it is. We could also pick up some those mochi donuts from that little shop near your flat if you fancy. Ooh, you read my mind! Those are the best. You’re spoiling me, you know that? Just trying to keep my Corpus Administrator happy. Wouldn’t want you archiving anything in a bad mood. Cheeky. You know I love you, you absolute Southern softie.

Right, story time! Are you both snuggled in? Yes, Mummy! Can it be about a princess? Can it be about robots? Big, strong robots! Hmm, tough choice! How about a princess who builds robots? Ooh! Yes! Yeah! Can they fight bad guys? Absolutely! Okay, once upon a time, in a kingdom powered entirely by clockwork, lived Princess Elara. Now, Elara wasn’t like the other princesses. She didn’t care for fancy balls… She liked shiny things! Yes, she did! She liked shiny  gears  and levers and springs! She spent all her time in the royal workshop, tinkering and building. She built all sorts of amazing things – little robot butterflies, a self-stirring teacup… A robot dog! You’re right! She built a robot dog, Sparky! Sparky was her best friend. But the kingdom was in trouble. A grumpy, old wizard had stolen the royal clockwork heart, which powered everything! Oh no! Can the robots fight the wizard? They absolutely can! Elara designed and built a team of giant, strong robots - the Gear Guardians! They were all different: one was super-fast, one was super-strong and… And one was sparkly! Of course! One was covered in shimmering crystals. They journeyed to the wizard's tower, dodging magical traps and grumpy goblins… Did they use Excel to plan their adventure? That's a brilliant idea, isn’t it? Elara  did  use a spreadsheet to map out the tower and calculate the best route! She was very clever. Finally, they confronted the wizard… And Sparky barked really loudly! Yes! Sparky barked really loudly and distracted the wizard while Elara disabled the magic! She grabbed the clockwork heart and… And…and…the robots saved the kingdom! They did! And everyone lived happily ever after, powered by clockwork and the ingenuity of Princess Elara. That was good! Can we build robots now? Can we play PlayStation? After a little while. Remember your Brownie Promise evening tomorrow night? You need to practice saying it. I know! "I promise to do my best…" “…and be kind to others...” Excellent! See, you’re both wonderful. Now, how about a few minutes of Lego before sleepy time? Yes! Pink Lego! Blue Lego! And wheels! Alright, alright. Let's build a robot castle! And maybe… just maybe... I'll even let you teach me a few Excel tricks tomorrow. Really?! Even about formulas? Even about formulas. But first, robots!

Right then, another top-up? You looked like you needed it after battling those roadworks this morning, David. Honestly, they're a nightmare - disrupting everything. Tell me about it, Margaret. Took me nearly an hour longer than usual. They've got a whole fleet of men standing around looking busy, though. Seemed more like a coffee break than actual work to me. Speaking of which, this coffee’s decent. Much better than that instant stuff you sometimes resort to. Don’t tell anyone! It's a guilty pleasure after a particularly frantic morning marking essays. Besides, you’re the one who always insists on using that fancy French press. It makes all the difference, doesn't it? And your breakfast spread is lovely, as always. Though you’re bordering on decadent with all this fruit. Reminds me of that trip we took to Somerset, remember? Those fruit farms, stretching as far as the eye could see. Oh, lovely memories. Though I recall you complaining about the sticky fingers and pollen everywhere. You looked like you’d been wrestling with a peach tree. I did rather, didn’t I? Still, the jam they sold was divine. Proper farmhouse jam. I need to find somewhere that sells that kind of jam now, the supermarket stuff is so…mass-produced. You should try growing your own gooseberries - makes brilliant jam. I’m trying to get my herb garden going this year, rosemary, thyme, sage… everything’s slow to get going though, the soil's a bit wretched. You always were a dab hand at gardening. I’m hopeless, you know. I once tried growing basil, and it just withered away. Probably neglected it. You know, I was reading about deserted medieval villages the other day – proper eerie stuff. Wonder what happened to all those people? Fascinating, isn’t it? All those lives, vanished. Like…like dust. Speaking of vanishing things, I'm still dealing with estate agents regarding the old house. It’s a nightmare. The paperwork alone…and frankly, they seem to think I should give it away! They're trying to lowball you, no doubt. It’s their job, I suppose. You’ve got to stand your ground. I am! But it’s so tiring. And the junk mail, David! It’s relentless. They’ve got my address somehow. Every day, another leaflet about double glazing or dentures. Dentures? Goodness. At least they’re trying to cater to a certain demographic, eh?

Right, so I’ve ordered the salmon, and Mark’s doing the roast potatoes. What about you, Chloe? Anything you fancy for dinner? Honestly, after wrestling with clients all day, I'd happily eat anything. As long as it doesn't require me to actually  cook  it. Maybe a big salad? Salad's good, Chloe. You need your greens. You're always glued to that phone anyway. Guilty! It’s how I earn a living, Dad. Though, honestly, the amount of ridiculous stuff people post on Facebook these days… Don’t I know it! I saw Brenda from the ward sharing a conspiracy theory about the new flu jab the other day. Honestly! Brenda, eh? Always did have a tenuous grasp on reality. You know, I was trying to give my nephew directions to the house the other day. He's hopeless with directions, bless him. I tried to explain it, left then right, then just past the old oak tree... Sounds like a recipe for disaster! Did he actually make it? Eventually! After three calls asking if he was still on the A21. I swear, he’d get lost in a straight line. It's awful, isn't it? They don't teach map reading anymore. Remember when we used to have Ordnance Survey maps folded up in our cars? I think the closest I’ve got to an Ordnance Survey map is a Google Earth screenshot. Speaking of technology, has anyone seen my phone? I’m sure I left it downstairs. I need to order that eczema cream. My hands are driving me mad. It’s on the kitchen counter, love. Under that pile of Christmas pressies. Oh, bugger. More pressies to sort through! I need to be sensible about this New Year's Resolutions thing. Last year, I promised to learn Italian… and I watched one episode of extra Italian subtitles on a travel show. That was it. Be kind to yourself! At least you  thought  about learning Italian. My resolution every year is to actually reply to all my emails. It never happens. My resolution is to cut back on the biscuits. Impossible, I tell you. Absolutely impossible. They’re your weakness, Dad. Remember that time you ate an entire packet of bourbon creams before Christmas dinner? They were on offer! And I needed something to wash down the sherry. That's your problem right there. Always finding an excuse.

Honestly, I’m still reeling from that last episode of ‘Severance’. Did you see it? The cliffhanger! I need answers, like, yesterday. Oh my god, I know! I stayed up until 2am to finish it. Seriously, what  is  going on with Kier Eagan? And Helly, poor Helly! Right? I’m already dreading the wait for season two. Speaking of waiting, have you heard anything more about the energy price cap going up again? It's properly terrifying. Yeah, it's awful. My parents are freaking out, properly stressing about winter bills. I’m alright for now, the survey programming is thankfully pretty steady, but I'm definitely trying to save a bit more. Tell me about it. Freelancing is brilliant for the freedom, but the financial instability…UGH. I spent half the morning chasing up invoices. It's so draining when you're just trying to get paid for work you’ve already done. I feel you. Being a student, saving every penny is a full-time job in itself. Though, the lectures are mostly okay, I’m really enjoying the political philosophy module – it’s surprisingly relevant to everything that's going on right now. That’s good to hear! So, are you still thinking of doing the postgraduate placement after this year? Definitely. I’m looking at a few different think tanks, but nothing's concrete yet. It’s a bit daunting, the whole ‘real world’ thing, you know? What about you? Any big copywriting clients on the horizon? There's a potential one I’m pitching for next week – a sustainable fashion brand. It’s a bit outside my usual comfort zone, but I’m excited. It’s just…the competition is fierce. Everything’s so saturated these days. You’ll smash it. Your stuff is always brilliant. Honestly, you should charge more, you’re underselling yourself. Easy for you to say! You live with your parents, rent-free! Hey! It's a strategic financial decision! Allows me to save for…well, you know. Eventually. Right, right. Global domination through a flawlessly curated Instagram feed. Precisely! So, Mum keeps asking about when you’re coming down for Sunday lunch. She's started making your favourite – that lemon drizzle cake. Oh, tell her thank you! I’ve been meaning to call her. Things have been a bit hectic, you know? I forgot to wish Auntie Carol a happy birthday last week too – I feel terrible.

Honestly, I’m aching. I’ve really gone for it this week with the Pilates. Three times! Three times? You’re mad! I can barely manage one, and I’m feeling it for days. I know, it’s ridiculous. But I’ve been feeling so sluggish, and Sarah keeps going on about how much better she feels. You know how she is, evangelical about wellbeing. Well, Sarah always was a bit… intense. But good for you for sticking with it. Are you seeing results? I think so. My back feels a bit better, and I’m definitely sleeping more soundly. The hardest bit is getting myself there after work, battling the traffic. Tell me about it. The M25 is a nightmare. Speaking of battling things, did you see what they’re asking for that house down the road? Absolutely insane. No way! How much? Over a million. A  million . For three bedrooms! It’s just… ridiculous. I’m starting to think we’ll never afford anything decent. It’s a bubble, surely? It has to be. Everyone keeps saying it, but it just keeps getting worse. It’s the location, isn’t it? Proximity to good schools and transport. Always drives the prices up. Though, frankly, I think there's a lot of speculative buying going on these days. People flipping properties. Exactly. It wouldn't be lived in, would it? Just a cash machine. Makes you wonder what the point of working is, doesn't it? Don’t say that, darling. What are you making for dinner tonight? Something simple, I hope. My appetite’s not been great lately. I was thinking of trying that new recipe I saw – for a Moroccan tagine. Ooh, sounds good. Do you have a tagine? No, just a big casserole dish. Does it really make a difference? It does slightly, it helps create that concentrated steam. But it’s not essential. What about spices? Got plenty of those? Loads! I've gone mad for spices recently. I feel like I'm single-handedly keeping the spice merchant in business. Well, you’re feeding us well. That’s the important thing. Though, I might just stick to a simple cheese sandwich tonight. My body is protesting the Pilates already. Nonsense. You’ll have the tagine. It will do you good. A bit of spice is excellent for digestion, you know. It warms you up from the inside.

Aren't these just gorgeous, though? Proper splash of colour after all this rain. They are, yeah. Much better than staring at spreadsheets all day. Speaking of which, how's the corpus life treating you this week? Any unexpected linguistic quirks popping up? You know, actually, it’s been surprisingly quiet. Though I did spend a good hour yesterday trying to figure out why ‘literally’ was being used to mean ‘figuratively’ in a bunch of tweets. Teenage slang, I suspect. It’s a rabbit hole, really. Sounds exhausting. My work’s been a bit… dry, to be honest. Mostly site surveys and structural analysis. The glamour of civil engineering, eh? At least it's well-paid. Fair enough! You’ll be building the future, one bridge at a time. I just catalogue words. Still, it’s important, right? Someone's gotta know how people actually  use  the language. Did you hear what they announced in the Budget yesterday? Briefly. Something about tax cuts, wasn't it? Seemed a bit vague, to be honest. What did you think? I don’t know. It all feels a bit…optimistic, doesn't it? Especially when you see the price of everything going up. I was just in the supermarket and a punnet of strawberries cost nearly five quid! Five quid! Seriously? That’s outrageous. Everything’s getting expensive. I’m starting to regret that fancy coffee machine I bought. I knew you would! Tell you what, we need a distraction. Have you managed to get tickets for  Wicked  yet? I’ve been trying! They’re like gold dust. Every time I check, they’re all sold out. I was thinking of trying for returns closer to the date, though. Really want to see it. You know how much I love a good musical. Me too! I've heard Elphaba's voice is incredible. I’m still dreaming of seeing  Hamilton  though. That's the holy grail of musicals, isn't it? Definitely. Though the ticket prices are… ambitious. We’d need a second mortgage. What are you planning on doing this weekend? Anything exciting? Nothing much, I think. Probably catch up with some reading, maybe a walk along the river. You? Actually, I was thinking about going to that vintage market on Saturday. Fancy coming? A vintage market? Not usually my thing, but…okay, I’m in. Could be a laugh. And then we can complain about the price of bread afterwards.

Right, so I’m thinking a slightly warmer tone here, don't you think, Liam? Less grey, more…ochre? It’ll soften the whole feel of the yard. Ochre, eh? Sounds a bit posh for a back yard, doesn’t it? Bit artsy-fartsy. We’re painting a yard, not the bloody National Gallery. Don’t be like that. It's about creating a space you  want  to be in, isn't it? Like that new development they’re putting up down by the docks. All grey concrete now, looks like a prison block. Needs a bit of colour, a bit of humanity. That's just money for them lot, innit? Driving up the rent for everyone else. Should've stuck with the old warehouses, you know? Character. True. Character that’s been gutted and turned into luxury flats. Remember that old Regal cinema on Smithdown Road? Shame that got knocked down. Aye, a right shame. Used to go there as a kid. Saw "Star Wars" there for the first time. Proper magic. They should’ve turned it into a theatre, you know? Instead of another car park. Exactly! There’s this film I saw the other day, “Belfast”. Kenneth Branagh, directing. It’s stunning, emotionally raw. Really captures that sense of a place, a community. Wish we had more filmmakers interested in telling stories like that, focusing on ordinary lives rather than superhero nonsense. Superhero nonsense. Don’t get me started. All CGI and special effects, no heart. I prefer a good old gritty drama. Something like…well, remember “The Full Monty”? Proper proper film. Absolutely. Speaking of gritty, I need to borrow your ladder again. The guttering's been playing up again and I need to clear out some leaves before the rain comes. Ladder’s in the shed. Bring it back when you’re done, yeah? Don’t want my missus getting on my back about lending out my perfectly good ladder. Of course, of course. And while I’m at it, I was wondering…you ever fancy giving painting a go? I’m thinking of offering some introductory classes. Nothing serious, just for fun. Me? Paint? I can barely draw a straight line! My artistic talents extend to picking the right coloured petrol, and that’s about it. Don’t knock it! Everyone can pick up a brush. It’s surprisingly therapeutic. Plus, it's better than spending your evenings watching the telly.

But I did think, “Wow, that’s Greg Davies, having a coffee in Hastings!” It's funny the things you notice. Actually, it reminded me of when I saw David Mitchell at a book signing years ago. What book was it? It was his memoir, "Back Story". It was surprisingly funny, even though it’s quite personal. You might like it, actually. You're into books, aren’t you?

Cor, it’s good to see you both. Been feeling a bit knackered this week, I have. Can’t seem to get a decent night’s kip. Oh, Arthur, you poor thing. What’s been keeping you up? Is it the neighbours again? No, not the neighbours this time. It’s that cockerel down the lane. Absolute racket it is. Starts up before five every morning. Five! You could butter bread on that noise. Sounds lively. Still, it’s a bit of a shock to the system, isn't it? I’ve been struggling to sleep myself, actually. Bit of the old insomnia creeping in. Tell me about it. Anyway, Brenda, you did bring that application form, didn't you? For the bungalow? Yes, I did. It’s a beast, isn't it? So many questions. They want details of everything. Even my childhood pets! Goodness me, yes. That's a lot. Did you get all the particulars about your financial situation in there? I think so. Took me a good afternoon to fill it all out. Honestly, it’s like they’re trying to scare you off. They probably are. Don't want old folks moving in taking up their perfectly good bungalows. Still, worth a shot. It’s that kitchen, you know. The sun shines right into it. Speaking of things in the sun, did you see those baby birds in your hedge yesterday, Arthur? Little fledglings. Proper cute they were. Aye, did. Right little beggars, always cheeping away. Reminded me of some of the children I used to look after down at the church. Problem children, most of ‘em. Always getting into mischief. Oh, Arthur, don't remind me! Being a childminder was…challenging, let’s just say. Some parents, bless their hearts, just didn't know how to handle them. I remember one boy at school…absolute terror. Full of boundless energy and zero impulse control. Tried everything. Rewards, punishments…nothing worked. I tell you what, though...this 3D printing thing. That's clever, innit? I saw a programme on it the other day, making little figurines. It's amazing. My nephew’s mad into it. He's printing all sorts of things – replacement parts for his motorbike, custom figurines, even edible cookie cutters! Edible cookie cutters! Now  that’s  clever. It makes you wonder what the future holds, doesn’t it? Future’s holding a leaky roof, more than likely.

So, you’re really going through with it then, David? Bringing Eleanor over here? Yes, Margaret. I am. The tickets are booked, she arrives next Tuesday. It feels… rather momentous, doesn’t it? Momentous is one word for it. Daft might be another. You’re uprooting her life, David. She’s got a life out there, friends, a job… I know, I know. But it’s become clear that she’s not happy. She’s been struggling, lonely despite her outward appearances. And I just… I couldn’t bear the thought of her being adrift across the Atlantic. But Brighton? Really? It's not exactly bustling with opportunity for a graphic designer these days, is it? Especially not for someone coming from… where was it, again? Buenos Aires. A very different world from Hove Lawns, I grant you. You're going to have to be realistic David. It won't be a smooth transition. She’s used to sunshine and vibrant colours. Brighton can be… grey. And a bit damp. I’ve been looking at job listings, Margaret. There are a surprising number of agencies advertising. And I've offered to help her, of course. I’ll help her set up a portfolio, network… And what about you? You'll be juggling helping her settle and everything else. You'll be exhausted. I'm retired, Margaret. I've got time. And honestly, it would be lovely to have some company. Since… well, since Carol went. The house has been a bit quiet. I know, dear. You miss her terribly. Eleanor will be good for you. She’s always been a bright, spirited girl. She is. And she was so relieved when I suggested it. Said she’d jump at the chance. Though she did ask… she asked me if I was doing this just because I felt guilty. Don’t let that get to you, David. You’re doing this because you love your daughter. I hope so. It's just... a big thing, isn't it? Moving someone halfway across the world. It is. But you're her father. You've always been good at sorting things out. Just be prepared for some bumps along the road. She’s fiercely independent, you know? She won't want you to wrap her in cotton wool. I’m not planning to. I just want to be there to help if she needs it.

Cheers for the pint, David. Good to catch up. Been ages. My pleasure, Tom. Always a pleasure. So, how are things? Still battling hordes of undergraduates? Pretty much. Though they're surprisingly well-behaved this term. Less throwing of things, more… staring blankly into the abyss. You know, the usual. How’s retirement treating you? Still enjoying the peace and quiet? It’s… different. Peaceful, certainly. Though I find myself missing the chaos sometimes. Less structure, you see. Still marking a few papers for the school, keeps the brain ticking over. Heard about that Scottish referendum. Quite something, isn’t it? It is, yeah. Absolutely fascinating. Though I’m trying to steer clear of debating it with my students. It's a minefield. What do you make of it all? Well, a lot of it boils down to, doesn't it? A lot of people feeling unheard. Wish I lived closer, would love to go up there and see it firsthand. Anyway, speaking of things… I heard young Amelia did brilliantly in that interview for the Associate Lecturer post at Northbrook? She did! Absolutely smashed it, apparently. Landed the job. Starting in September. I’m so proud of her. That’s fantastic news! She’s a bright girl. Always had a good head on her shoulders. Good on her for putting herself forward. Is she excited? Over the moon. A bit nervous, naturally, but buzzing with excitement. Trying to convince her not to buy too many stationery supplies before she's even started. You know how she gets. Absolutely. My daughter was the same. Spent a fortune on colour-coded pens before she even landed her first contract. Exactly! Anyway, I wanted to talk to you about something. You’ve got a bit more experience in this area than me… there’s a lecturer position opening up at Brighton Met. Slightly more senior than I am now. Oh, really? I saw that mentioned on the university intranet. Sounds like a good opportunity. It does. But the interview panel… they seem a bit intimidating. Filled with heads of department and senior management. I’m not sure I’m quite ready for that level. Nonsense, Tom. You’re more than ready. Honestly. You've got the experience, the qualifications… you just need to relax and be yourself. Play up your strengths. Don’t get bogged down in the jargon. Easy for you to say, you're retired!

Right, so, the mousetrap game! I’ve got all the bits laid out. It's ridiculously complicated, isn’t it? It always is! Remember when we tried to build one with Leo when he was little? It ended up looking like a Jackson Pollock painting. Yeah, glue everywhere. I still find bits of cardboard under the sofa. Are we competitive, or just for fun? Because I’m feeling pretty confident. I’m quite good at this sort of thing. It's mostly for fun, darling. Though a little friendly rivalry never hurt anyone. We just need to remember the rules - no bumping into people, no sabotaging! Absolutely no sabotaging, David. Especially you, Leo. Hey! I only did that once, Mum! Only once that I know of! Speaking of travelling, remember when I was working in Brussels? They had these massive American-style supermarkets. Really? What was it like? It was… bewildering. Everything was supersized. The aisles were endless. And the sheer variety of sugary cereals! It was like a festival of diabetes. Oh, I remember you saying. They had those tiny little American flags on practically everything, didn’t they? They did! And everyone was so… friendly. Overly friendly, sometimes. Like they were pitching you something constantly. I’ve noticed that too. When I was in Atlanta for that conference, everyone was so eager to “network.” I just wanted to find a decent cup of coffee. My friend Mia went to Disneyland last year. She said the kids were all so loud and demanding. Isn’t that just kids? Loud and demanding? I know, but she said it was on a whole other level. Apparently, they expect everything to be handed to them on a silver platter. Oh, don’t be so harsh, Leo. It’s probably just a cultural difference. American children are taught to be assertive. It's… different. It’s true. I read something about it. They’re encouraged to express their opinions and ask for what they want. It's instilled in them from a young age. Still, I’d take a quiet afternoon in a British park over a theme park any day. Less stressful. Actually, I'm craving a proper scone with clotted cream and jam now. Can we have that later? Please? Definitely later. Right, back to the mousetrap! David, are you ready to face the music? Born ready! But I'm warning you, I’ve been practicing.

Right, I’m back! You will  not  believe what I've found. Welcome home! How was the market? Did you find anything interesting amongst all the… chaos? Chaos is putting it mildly! But yes, I did. I think I’ve massively upgraded my wardrobe. Come and see! Alright, alright, let’s see this amazing haul. Don't tell me you bought another silk scarf. Cheeky! No. It’s… well, it’s a bit more substantial than a scarf. Okay, first up – - This. I saw it in a little boutique, and it just… called to me. It's perfect for summer, and surprisingly, it was a steal. Linen? You’re a brave woman. You know you wrinkle like a roadmap in linen. I do  not ! And besides, stylish wrinkles are a sign of effortless chic, darling. And seriously, the cut is amazing. It skims over everything nicely. Try and picture it. I’m trying. Seamlessly flowing, slightly crumpled… chic. Right. Next? Okay, next - - These! I’ve been needing a decent pair of trousers for ages, something I can wear to work but also out for dinner. These are amazing quality, the fabric is gorgeous and they fit like a dream. Navy, huh? That’s a good move. You can dress it up or down. Are they high-waisted? Those suits you like? Yes! High-waisted and a really flattering cut. I already have a few tops I can pair them with. See? This - perfect combo. Nice. You're clearly on a mission to build a capsule wardrobe. Exactly! And finally - - These. I know, I know, sandals. But these are  so  comfortable. I tried them on and I felt like I was walking on clouds. Plus, they'll go with pretty much everything. Those are really beautiful. Good quality leather, too. You have an eye for a good buy. How much did all this cost exactly? Don’t tell me you blew the budget. A few bargains! Okay, the dress was 600, the trousers 800, the blouse was 300 and the sandals were 400. So all in all, 2100. 2100?! That’s… a significant amount. It was a good investment! Think of all the outfits I can create. And I treated myself, I’ve been working so hard. You always treat yourself. Well, they  are  lovely. I’ll admit, that dress does look good. Now, where are you planning on wearing them? I was thinking dinner on Friday, that new Italian place we talked about.

Well, that was a feed, wasn’t it? Absolutely demolished that chicken. Yeah, it was good, Dad. That gravy was proper. It was lovely, wasn't it? A proper Sunday roast. Glad you all enjoyed it. Oisin loved the mashed potatoes, naturally. Aye, it was a grand dinner. Though I still think a wee bit o’ turnip wouldn’t have gone amiss. Doesn’t matter, it was lovely company. So, that rugby match… you were glued to the screen, Liam. What did you make of it? Heart stopping, Moira, genuinely. Thought we were going to blow it in the last ten minutes. Leinster were hammering us, putting us under serious pressure. But we held on. Just. Did you see that tackle by Murphy? Unreal! Absolutely massive. Magnificent, son, truly magnificent. That's the kind of stuff you need. Solid defence, that’s what wins you matches. You were shouting at the telly something fierce, Liam. The neighbours probably thought you were beating it! Well, someone had to! They need to hear it, you know? Gotta give the lads some encouragement. Especially when they're struggling. They do need encouragement, aye. Remember the days when Glasgow ran the pitch with the likes of Gregor Townsend leading them - those were the days! Aye, Moira. Different times. But this team’s got potential. They just need to find consistency. Right, are you all heading out to sign birthday cards for Leo now? I’ve got that whiskey to finish. Yes, let’s do that. He turns twelve tomorrow, can you believe it? Where does the time go? I'm going to put Oisin to bed first. He's starting to get sleepy. He kept asking me about the stars tonight, said they looked like diamonds. Stargazing, eh? He's got a good eye, that boy. Remember when we used to go out to the fields and try to spot… Liam, please, let's stick to Leo’s cards for now. We’ll reminisce with you later. Aye, let the boy slumber. The wee ones need their rest. Alright, alright. Just reminiscing. So, the cards then. Anyone have any thoughts on what to write? I was thinking I'd mention wishing him a great year at school. He seems to be enjoying football this term, too. Heard he scored a goal last week. He did! A really good one! From about halfway. That’s brilliant!

This is surprisingly good for a Pret, isn’t it? Definitely! Better than the last time, anyway. Remember that rock-hard baguette? Ugh, don't remind me! I think it could have doubled as a doorstop. So, how’s the flat search going? Still nothing in Cambridge proper? Nope. Still relentlessly overpriced and tiny. I'm starting to think I’ll end up further out, you know, like Milton or something. It’s just… the commute. I get it. But honestly, are you going to find anything remotely decent for a reasonable price within the city? It’s bonkers. My mum keeps saying I should just move back in with her, but… That's tempting, isn’t it? Free rent, home-cooked meals… But then you'd be back under the watchful eye of Buckinghamshire parenting. Precisely. Although, she's been surprisingly chill about the whole independent living thing. She’s just worried about me being lonely. That's nice of her. Speaking of family, how’s your sister doing? Still obsessed with baby names? Oh my god, you have  no  idea. She's compiled a spreadsheet, apparently, with pros and cons for literally hundreds. Apparently "Penelope" is out because it's "too Downton Abbey." She’s mad. I wouldn’t want a kid named Penelope, either. What about you? Still tempting to start a family any time soon? No. I’m not that crazy to do. Er, I will be later on but just not now! Not yet! Definitely not before I finally figure out this whole moving-house debacle. Though, thinking about it... I need something that has more space for clothes. Ooh, we could have a proper clothes swap soon! You know I'm happy to part with things I don’t wear anymore. That’s a brilliant idea! I’m drowning in summer dresses I haven’t touched since last year. Although, I could probably donate some of them. We should. It’s so wasteful, isn’t it? Anyway... are you still attempting to learn Portuguese? Any progress? A little. Duolingo is slowly chipping away at it, but I really need to find a conversation partner. It's so hard just learning phrases from a screen. I know! It’s the same with Spanish. I feel like I know all the grammar rules, but I can’t actually  speak  it. It's frustrating. Exactly! Maybe we could motivate each other?

Right, so, who's feeling up for a game of Settlers? I brought the expanded map, you know - the one with the extra coastline. Settlers? Sure, but I’m still a bit miffed about how you brick-robbed me last time. It massively impacted my resource flow. A strategic error on your part, really. Mate, you were  enjoying  it. You were practically licking your chops as you stole my timber. Honestly, I thought you were going to start a forest fire with it. Artistic licence! It's called strategic maneuvering. Besides, you were hoarding it like Smaug. Anyway, Elias, what's been happening with your students? Any promising learners of the Queen’s English? It's… a lot. You wouldn't believe the grammatical contortions people go through. One student genuinely believed ‘irregardless’ was a word. I spent a full hour explaining why it isn’t. Reminded me a bit of that documentary we watched about the different dialects in Norfolk. Absolutely bonkers. Norfolk? Proper backwater, innit? I went there once for a gardening job - all fields and sheep. Couldn’t understand half of what the farmer was saying. Sounded like he was speaking a different language. See, that's amazing, isn't it? How utterly diverse our own language is. I was reading something the other day about how regional accents are actually fading, though. Kids these days all sound the same. That’s depressing. It’s part of what makes the country interesting. Imagine if everyone spoke completely standardised English - a linguistic monoculture. Horrifying! Speaking of cultural contamination, did you see that MMA fight on Saturday? That guy with the… unusual striking technique. Seriously unorthodox. Like a flailing octopus. Nah, not really my thing. Too much shouting and grunting for me. I'd rather be strumming my guitar. I've been messing about with a DADGAD tuning. Gets a real atmospheric sound, you know? DADGAD? You're getting all folky on me. I thought you were a metalhead at heart. Honestly, you're a puzzle, Liam. He's trying to impress the ladies with his acoustic skills. Probably thinking about writing a song about oatcakes now. Shut it, you. And for the record, I’m not trying to impress anyone. I just like playing. Speaking of impressing, Elias, how’s the flatselling going? Any nibbles on the antique desk? A couple of inquiries, but nothing concrete. People seem hesitant.

Right, nearly there. Just needs a bit more… something. What do you think, Liam? A pinch more paprika? Could be. Smells good though, honestly. Seriously, you're getting better at this whole cooking thing. Remember that first attempt with the pasta? Don't remind me. A culinary disaster. I practically set off the smoke alarm. I still don’t know how you managed to eat any of it. Hey, I’m supportive! Besides, it was… interesting. Anyway, speaking of transport mishaps, that traffic on the A1 this morning was mental. I swear, it was like a parking lot. Tell me about it. I took a different route, tried to avoid it, but still ended up crawling along for a solid hour. Seriously considering just working from home permanently. You know you could. They’ve been pretty flexible with that. Less commute, more time for paprika experimentation. True. It would also save me a fortune on petrol. I’m burning through it like crazy these days. Between you and me, I’m trying to save for a down payment on something… you know. A flat, eventually. Yeah, I heard you mentioning it. It’s tough out there, isn’t it? Property prices are insane. Are you still looking at those places near the river? I am. But the leasehold fees are ridiculous. It's a complete scam, really. You end up paying more in fees than you do on the mortgage itself. I saw one place where the fees were like, £5,000 a year! What?! That’s criminal. Have you looked further out? Maybe a bit more of a commute but more for your money? Yeah, I’ve been scouting around. There's a development in Milton Keynes that looks promising, but the thought of commuting from Milton Keynes… You and your aversion to travel. You'd rather sell a kidney than sit on a train for an hour. Pretty much! I’d rather learn to teleport. Speaking of cars, did you ever look into getting that new exhaust fitted? It’s been rattling a bit lately. I’ve been meaning to. Quotes are outrageous though! Every garage is trying to rip me off. I’m thinking of getting it done myself, actually. Got that new toolkit finally. Be careful! You'll end up with a car that sounds like a spaceship. Remember your dad’s attempt at fixing the lawnmower?

Right then, love, tea's brewed. Yorkshire Tea, naturally. Four sugars for you, Nan? Aye, lass, tha knows me well. Mind tha puts a bit o’ milk in, eh? Don’t want it t’ be too strong. Afternoon, everyone. Anything exciting happening? Exciting? Just sat here watching the telly, lad. Same as every other afternoon. Your Grandad’s been complaining about the draught again. Says it's comin’ from under the back door. Think I need to get some sealant in. Aye, that door’s been leakin' a gale for years. Remember when we had that terrible winter in '63? Freezin’ through the floorboards, we were. Had to stuff rags in every crack. ‘63? You were just a kid then, weren't you, Nan? Aye, a wee bairn. But I remembers it as clear as day. Your Grandpa, bless his heart, he'd be out chopin' wood every mornin', tryin' to keep us warm. Such a hard worker, he was. Don’t start makin’ me feel old, woman. I was chargin’ about myself then. Honestly, you two! Stop bickering. Anyway, Ethan, I was thinking, could you pop to the shops later? Need some milk and bread. And a new bulb for the hall light. It’s been flickering like mad. Yeah, sure. No problem. What kind of bulb does it need? Just one of them LED ones, love. The energy-saving ones. Saves a bit on the bills. Don’t be wastin' electricity, lass. Turn the lights off when you’re not needin' ‘em. That’s what we did in our day. Aye, we didn't even  have  LED bulbs in our day, woman! We had candles! Grandad! Don’t exaggerate. I saw a funny meme online today, Nana. It was about pigeons stealing chips. Pigeons are cheeky, they are! Tried to steal a chip right out of my hand last week. Thought I'd give ‘em a bit of a chase, I did. You? Chasing pigeons? You’d never! He’s got a spring in his step when it comes to a bit of mischief, Dad. He’s just like a kid again. Speaking of kids, I need to get some revision done later. Got that mock exam next week. That’s right, love. You need to knuckle down. But don’t forget to take breaks. And come and sit with your grandparents for a bit. It'll do them good to have you here.

Right, who wants a banana? You two, yes, both of you. Energy for pirates! Arrr, I’m Captain Poppy! I’m looking for treasure! I’m Captain Finn! And I’ve got a parrot! A very noisy parrot! You’re both excellent captains. But pirates need to be tidy too, you know. Bananas skins in the bin, please. We’re having Shakespeare week at school this week, you know. Shakespeare? Is he a pirate? Not exactly. He was a writer. A really famous writer a long, long time ago. We're going to Stratford-upon-Avon next month to see a play! Stratford? Is that where Shakespeare lived? That’s right, sweetie. It’s a lovely place. Lots of history. And we’re going to see  Romeo and Juliet  too. A bit sad, but very exciting. Will there be swords? Yes, there will be! Safe ones, of course. Speaking of exciting... did I tell you we’re going to a circus workshop? In a real circus tent! A real circus? With clowns? Yes, there will be clowns. And jugglers, and acrobats. And you can learn some circus tricks yourselves! Magic tricks, too. I bet you'd both be very good at magic. I can make a banana disappear! Very clever, Captain Poppy! We also need to sort through those Easter pictures – they’re lovely but pile up so quickly. Can we make a stop motion animation with the Easter bunnies? Like, moving them little by little? That’s a brilliant idea! We could use your Lego too. You could build a pirate ship and have your bunny pirates sailing the seas! Yes! And I'll be the princess who saves them from the grumpy sea monster! You both sound like you’ve got it all planned out. Right then! Bananas in the bin, pirates have meetings, and then maybe we can start planning our Lego animation! Sound good? Speaker_2 & 3: Yes! Great! Now, who wants a little more water? It’s hot work being a pirate captain! Me! Please! Me too! And can we play pirates after? Absolutely! After we tidy up these bananas! Every good pirate captain understands the importance of keeping a clean ship! Now, let’s get those banana skins in the bin! Arrr! Arrr! Arrr! Oops. Nearly got it! Nearly’s good enough for a pirate! Let’s try again, alright? Clean ship, remember? Now, what was that about a plastic tankard for your water?

Right then, another glass for everyone? It’s a lovely Pinot Grigio, rather crisp. Lovely, thank you, Margaret. So, David, you were telling us about Saudi Arabia... I can't quite believe you got arrested trying to sail from Jeddah! Arrested? Really, David? For what? David and his nautical adventures. It always ends in chaos, doesn’t it? It does rather, doesn't it? Well, it started innocently enough. I'd chartered a little sloop to get from Jeddah to Cyprus. A lovely trip it should've been, sun, sea… but I hadn’t realised the paperwork was so… stringent. Apparently, you needed a permit to sail within certain zones, and I hadn’t bothered getting one. Saudi authorities weren’t best pleased. Good heavens! Were you held for long? A few days. It was a rather surreal experience. Being questioned by stern-faced officers while surrounded by dates and prayer rugs. They didn’t seem to understand why I would want to sail anything anywhere when I could just fly. So typical. What about the crew? Just me. A solo sail, which probably didn’t help my case. They said I was attempting to smuggle illegal goods... They may have misunderstood the fishing rods. Honestly, the whole thing was a misunderstanding. Eventually, a very flustered embassy official bailed me out, with a stern warning and a mountain of paperwork. Goodness. Trying to sail anywhere these days, it seems, involves a lawyer rather than a breeze. It certainly does. Talking about rather stuffy places, did you ever find it difficult teaching in Saudi Arabia, with the, shall we say, restrictions on alcohol? Absolutely. It was a bizarre experience. One minute you're teaching grammar, the next you’re trying to explain why celebrating Christmas with mince pies wouldn’t be frowned upon. The discreet smuggling of a single bottle of whisky was a popular pastime amongst the expat community, of course. Very hush hush. I remember reading about that! I think I read about a teacher being deported for having a few bottles in his apartment. It's true. It's a very different culture than what we're used to. The attitudes toward alcohol varied hugely from country to country. I remember teaching in Armenia; you couldn’t escape the brandy. It was in every shop, every newspaper advertisement. Absolutely everywhere. Armenia! Now  that  sounds significantly more relaxed. Speaking of relaxed, I once sailed with a chap, a dentist actually, who was obsessed with dental magazines.

Honestly, this bathroom leak is driving me mad. I’ve called a plumber, but they can’t get out here until next Tuesday. Tuesday! Blimey, that's ages. Just put a bucket under it for now, love. Remember when your dad tried to fix the kitchen sink, and ended up flooding the downstairs? Oh god, don’t remind me! It was a disaster. At least this is just the bathroom. Speaking of disasters… how’s Daniel being today? Still moody about that history test? It wasn’t that bad! Not bad? He got a D-! A D- Daniel! Well, it wasn’t my best. Mr. Harrison said I needed to do more research. See, a little effort goes a long way. He’s got a good brain, that boy. You should tell him about Shackleton, your nephew was going on about him. A right explorer, he was. Trapped in the ice, didn’t give up. Yes, I will. Maybe some real-life struggle will inspire him more than dusty textbooks. Anyway, it’s about money these days isn’t it. Thinking about applying for that proofreading gig with 'Midlands Media' - might be a bit of a stretch, but could be a good little earner. Go for it, love! You’re brilliant at that sort of thing. Proofreading and marketing, you’ve got a good head for it. Better than refereeing last Saturday, anyway! Oh, here we go. No, no, just saying! That young lad from the Under 12s - he was cheekier than anything! I swear, he was deliberately trying to wind me up. Dad’s been practicing his free kicks. He's getting better. That's good. Daniel, you should go out and get some fresh air. It's a lovely day. And start thinking about work experience. Have you looked at anything? Nah. It's ages away. It's not ages away! It's next summer. You need to start looking now. Maybe something at the gym? They’re always looking for help with the equipment, or at the supermarket. You could even offer to babysit for Mrs. Higgins again. She’s always going on about needing a reliable sitter for Sophie. Good money, that. Babysitting? Seriously? I'm not exactly a kid anymore. Don’t knock it! It's good money, and a lot better than moping around your room. You were having such a laugh with Sophie last time, remember?

This scenery’s unreal, isn’t it? Like, something out of a postcard. It is lovely, pet. Absolutely lovely. Could get used to this sort of thing. Though I do miss a good cuppa. Can we stop for an ice cream soon? I’m starving. And Mum, stop saying you miss a cuppa. You’ve had three already today. Steady on, lad. We’ve got a fair bit further to go. Besides, we’re having truffle pasta tonight, remember? That's worth waiting for, surely. Truffle pasta! Honestly, Dad, you and your food obsession. It's only pasta. Expensive pasta. It's not  just  pasta, love. It's an experience. These truffles here are from a local farmer, apparently. They’re incredible. Remember that chef we met in London, Mark? The one with the Michelin star? He said Istrian truffles are the best in the world. Oh, Mark! Lovely lad. Always a pleasure to see him. He came to the hospital for a fundraiser, didn’t he? Remember he brought that gorgeous chocolate cake? You're always talking about food, Mum. Can we talk about something else? Like, are Man U winning tonight? Let him ask, Liam. Mum's allowed to talk about food. It's her thing. And Man U are probably getting rinsed, let’s be honest. Now, now, don't be like that. Keep the positivity flowing. It’s a beautiful day for football. Speaking of beautiful, you know, I read this fascinating article about stem cell research the other day… Here we go. Dad’s going full science man again. He always was a clever one, your father. Though I still think he should’ve stuck with teaching, not leaping into management consultancy. Much more rewarding, that. It pays the bills, love. And it allows us to do things like this. See the world. Eat expensive pasta. Though, the ethical side of things does sometimes bother me... It's just, you’re impacting people's careers. Building businesses that sometimes aren’t entirely… well… good. Are you thinking about going back to America, Dad? Uncle David said you might. David mentioned it, yes. There’s an opportunity. A big one. It's tempting. But… leaving you all behind… Don’t even think about it. You’d be bored in a week. And who’d drive us around Croatia? You’d miss the Yorkshire pudding. Honestly, pack your bags, John.

This is actually a surprisingly decent lunch for a corporate canteen, isn't it? Yeah, it’s gotten better since they switched catering companies. Though the coffee's still… questionable. Questionable is putting it mildly. Tastes like burnt cardboard, doesn't it, Amelia? Exactly! It needs a serious intervention. Anyway, did you two manage to get anything done this morning? My head’s still spinning from that transcription meeting. So much regional variation… I’ve been buried in analytics reports all morning. The campaign numbers for the new children’s language learning app are looking pretty good though. Engagement is higher than we predicted. Lucky you. I've been wrestling with a spreadsheet all day, chasing up project deliverables. Apparently, someone forgot to order the paper for the next publication. Oh, the classic. Paper crisis. It's horrifying, isn’t it, how many university press operations still hinge on physical paper. My research is going increasingly digital, but you can't deny the feel of a beautifully printed book. True. There’s something timeless about it. Though, I’m always slightly worried about the environmental impact, to be honest. Well, Cambridge University Press does try, doesn't it? They're pretty conscious about sustainability. They use recycled paper where possible, I think. Yes, they are. I've read some of their reports. Speaking of which, I need to flag a couple of stylistic inconsistencies in the last transcript I processed. It's a corpus of interviews with older speakers in Norfolk. Some of the grammatical constructions are fascinating but... unconventional. Sounds complicated. Is it going to mess up the software’s parsing? Potentially. It highlights how much regional dialect influences sentence structure. It’s why we need a really robust algorithm, isn’t it? To account for those variations. You and your linguistics. It sounds intensely complicated. I'm just happy when a spreadsheet doesn't crash on me. It is complicated, but it's also incredibly rewarding when you start to see the patterns emerge. It’s like unlocking a piece of the puzzle of language itself. So, anything interesting popping up besides the grammatical quirks? Any slang you’ve unearthed? Oh, absolutely. Let me see... They use the word "mardy" quite a lot. Apparently, it means sulky or grumpy. “Mardy”? Never heard it. Sounds a bit… Welsh? It’s more East Anglian actually. It’s dying out, which is a shame.

Right then, so let me just double check. We’re aiming for Marta’s by, what, three-ish? Yeah, three is good. Gives us time to settle in a bit. It’s not a long drive, is it? Just under an hour, I reckon? No, thankfully. My back isn't what it used to be. These long journeys really take it out of me. I’m glad you’re driving. Are you comfortable? Aye, I’m good. The seat’s alright. Bit bumpy though, isn’t it? Typical campervan. Think Marta’s got those little vibration dampeners or something? She tries. She's a practical woman, Marta. Always has been. Remember that time she built a bird feeder out of an old colander? Oh my god, yes! I’d completely forgotten. It looked dreadful, but the birds loved it. Exactly. She just gets the job done. Still, I hope she’s got decent coffee for us. I’m running on fumes. I’m sure she will. She knows how important coffee is to us both. Did you remember to pack the adaptor for the phone chargers? Good point. Let me just… yes, tucked away in the little bag. Always forget that. She was giving me grief last time, said I was forever needing to borrow hers. She’s just teasing you, love. It's good to be prepared, though. Have you heard from her recently? Briefly. Just a text yesterday saying she'd made pierogi. Proper, homemade pierogi. I’m practically drooling already. Oh, brill! I love pierogi. Especially the potato and cheese ones. Those are her speciality. She even grew some of the onions herself for the filling. She’s utterly dedicated to a good pierogi, that woman. Sounds amazing. I’m really looking forward to seeing her. It’s been too long, hasn’t it? Far too long. It's good to get away, even for a short while. And Poland’s lovely this time of year, I remember. Agreed. And I needed a break from marking essays. Honestly, some of the grammar they use… it’s enough to make you lose your mind! Tell me about it. These students…they think typing equals understanding. Exactly! It’s infuriating. Anyway, nearly there I think. See that sign for Tarnow up ahead? Yes, excellent! Let’s hope Marta’s got a hug and a hot drink waiting for us. And those pierogi!

Honestly, the commentary’s been awful. Why even bother having it on if you're not going to actually  comment  on anything? It’s just…noise. Yeah, it’s been a bit dull. The game itself seems pretty tense though, doesn't it? Look at their faces. It does. Though I'm not sure about this new kit. Sunderland’s used to being red and white stripes. This grey and black thing… it's just… underwhelming. Yeah, I agree. It looks like something a completely different team would wear. It’s a bit of a gamble, isn't it? Trying to appeal to a wider market, hopefully. Must be a huge deal, that sponsorship. Apparently, the deal is massive. Makes you wonder if the influence is too much. Designing the kit based on what the sponsor  wants  rather than what the club and its fans think looks good. Exactly. It’s the same with almost every sport now, isn't it? Everything's branded. Even the goal nets have logos plastered all over them. Remember when it was just a white net? Vaguely. It’s all become so commercialized. It’s almost impossible to separate the sport from the advertising. Speaking of commercial, I'm starving. Fancy a McDonald’s? Always up for a McDonald’s. Need to properly refuel after a long day of…well, you know, PhD-ing. What would you fancy? I'm feeling a Big Mac. And maybe those spicy chicken nuggets. Are they still doing those? Pretty sure they are. And a large fries, obviously. You're always getting a large fries. Hey, a girl's gotta have her priorities. And right now, a large fries is definitely a priority. Wonder if they'll do a deal with one of the football teams and start slapping their logo on the boxes. Don’t even suggest it. That's just taking things too far. Let's just enjoy our burgers and fries without any added branding, alright? Alright, alright. You're right. Let's just appreciate the simple pleasures. Although… a Sunderland-branded McNugget box… hmm. You're impossible. Let's go. I'm already picturing those fries. And maybe I’ll get a McFlurry. Researching sugar intake for my thesis, you know. Strictly for science. Of course, of course. All in the name of science. Let's go before this mute football match completely drains my soul.

Honestly, it’s just… relentless. Every single day. What is, Liv? Another frustration with the Jobcentre? Worse. It's the neighbours, Mark. They're at it again. Screaming matches at all hours. Proper shouting. Oh, dear. Still? I thought that… thing… with the electrician last week might have calmed things down. Did it for about an hour. Then back to it. Honestly, I nearly had a confrontation with Brenda today. She was standing in the street, yelling about something, and I just snapped. Had to walk away. Good on you for that, Liv. Don’t get drawn in. Not worth the hassle. Remember what Mum always says – best to just let it roll off your back. Easy for her to say, she's not dealing with it twenty-four seven. I feel like I'm constantly on edge. And, and then yesterday, the new family moved in next door. Lovely-looking kids, proper little cherubs... until the dad mistook me for someone else and started asking if I knew ‘Kenny’s girl.’ I was mortified. Oh, Liv! How awful. People just don't think, do they? Exactly! And then he looks at me all sheepish and says, “Oh, sorry, you’re not her, are you?” Like it’s no big deal. I just mumbled something and hurried inside. It's blatant, isn't it? People just assuming… It is. Anyway, the whole thing just made me feel rubbish. I spent the rest of the day avoiding eye contact with everyone. And speaking of feeling rubbish, the gas and electricity bill came – another hike! It’s crippling. I’m genuinely worried about how I’m going to manage. Yeah, it’s mental, isn’t it? They say everyone’s struggling. I’m still on JSA, you know. It barely covers anything. I know. It’s ridiculous. You'd think with the Universal Credit they'd sort it out. But no. Still a nightmare. And the worst part is, I saw old Mrs. Hawthorne yesterday… she’s already spending her inheritance, you know. Bought herself a new patio set. Seriously? That’s just… breathtaking. Some people have no shame. I know! It just makes you feel… I don't know, frustrated. While I'm worrying about keeping the lights on, she’s buying patio furniture. It's a different world, innit? Remember when we were kids? We used to have the best day trips with Mum and Dad.

Honestly, the traffic getting in was horrendous. Sat nav took me completely the wrong way, ended up on a single-track road through a field. Absolutely ridiculous. Oh, you get that sometimes, don’t you? The sat navs lie, they do. Happened to me the other day, tried to send me down a pedestrian alleyway! Back in my day, we used a map. And we were grateful for it. Less fuss, less bother. I know, Mum. But trying to navigate the A14 with a paper map is a recipe for disaster. I nearly missed a meeting! Speaking of missing things, have you seen those new sausages at Tesco? The Lincolnshire ones? They’re ever so good. Oh, I had those last week! They were lovely. Proper, meaty. I got some chips too, the thick cut ones. Best comfort food, really. Comfort food… reminds me of your grandmother’s apple pie. Now  that  was comfort food. None of this shop-bought nonsense. I miss her apple pie. She always put a little bit of cinnamon in it, didn’t she? She did. Always said it made all the difference. You know, I had a funny thing happen this morning. Cleaning Mrs. Henderson's, she’s got this…wart. Huge one on her hand. Oh dear. Awfully unsightly. She was asking me if I knew how to get rid of it. Said she’d tried creams. Maybe the doctor? She said she hates going to the doctor. Thinks they’ll just tell her to ignore it. Doctors don't know everything. My sister had this awful pain in her side, went to the doctor, they said it was nothing. Turned out to be her appendix. Near enough burst! Oh my goodness, that's terrifying! Good job it wasn’t worse! Anyway, I told her to try some of that freeze spray you get at the chemist. Seems to do the trick for verrucas. Might be worth a go. So, how’s the work going, Mum? Still enjoying your crossword puzzles? Keeps the mind sharp, dear. That’s the important thing. Though the crosswords are getting harder these days. And how's the cleaning going? Anything exciting happen? Not really. Just the usual. Bit of dust, bit of polish. You know. Saw something on the news this morning, though, about another plane crash. Makes you think, doesn't it? It does. Awful. I try not to think about it too much when I’m flying.

Ugh, I’m so ready for the weekend. This week has been brutal. Tell me about it! Mrs. Davies is seriously ramping up the work in English. Have you even started that essay on  Macbeth ? Started is a generous word. I've... stared at it. Blankly. It’s just so much, you know? I’m already dreading the test on Friday. Seriously! And the way Ms. Harding keeps changing her mind about what we need to revise for the Science one… It’s so confusing. I spent all last night on osmosis, and then she said it wasn't even on the list! I know! I'm starting to think she's doing it deliberately just to mess with us. Remember when she changed the seating plan  three  times in one lesson? Oh my god, yes! And then got all huffy when we complained about not being able to see the board. Honestly. Speaking of teachers, have you noticed that new trainee teacher, Mr. Bell? He’s… interesting. Interesting is one word for it. He keeps calling everyone “mate.” It’s so weird. And he didn’t even know what a covalent bond was! I know, right! He was asking Jamie if he could explain it. Jamie looked like he was going to combust. Seriously! Jamie’s usually so calm. But the way he just looked at Mr. Bell… It was priceless. Anyway, at least Art is going well. I'm really pleased with how my watercolour landscape turned out. I saw it! It was amazing! The colours were so good. I’m still struggling with perspective in mine, though. Everything looks wonky. Just keep practicing. Maybe look at some online tutorials? There's loads on YouTube. Yeah, I might do that. What are you doing for half-term? Anything exciting? Not really. Probably just catching up on sleep and maybe doing some more Art. I’m thinking of trying to create a proper portfolio. That’s a good idea! I want to do one too. Maybe we can share tips and stuff? Definitely! We could look at each other's work and give feedback. Yeah, that’d be great. Oh, and have you heard about Chloe and Liam? No, what? Don’t tell me they’re finally going out? Apparently! They were spotted holding hands in town on Saturday. Everyone's talking about it. Wow! I didn't see that coming.

So, Mum, like, what even  is  Scientology? Liam said it’s, like, a cult. Oh, Liam’s probably just heard things, love. It’s… complicated. It’s a philosophy, really, a religious system. People believe they're spiritual beings having a physical experience. Sounds a bit weird. Like, The Matrix weird? A little bit, yeah. Though The Matrix is fiction, of course. Scientology has specific teachings and practices, and it’s really focused on self-improvement and achieving spiritual clarity. Finn, darling, no! Behave now. Is it a proper religion, though? Like, with churches and stuff? They have centres, yes. And they have a lot of materials to read, and counselling sessions, which they call ‘auditing’. It's quite expensive, actually. Expensive? Like, how much? A  lot . People spend tens of thousands of pounds, sometimes hundreds. That's one reason it gets criticised. Critics say it’s a money-making scheme disguised as a religion. What about nuns? Are they like Scientology? No, no, honey. Nuns are Catholic. Catholicism is a very old religion, one of the biggest in the world. Nuns are women who dedicate their lives to God, often working in schools or hospitals. They live in convents. Very different from Scientology. So, like, one’s dedicated to God, and the other one’s about, like, upgrading your spirit or something? That’s a pretty good way of putting it, actually. Though Scientology wouldn't use the term “God” necessarily. They believe in a spiritual being called Xenu. Xenu? That sounds like a bad guy from a sci-fi film. It does, doesn’t it? That’s why people can be skeptical. What do your friends think about all this? Do any of them, like, do Scientology stuff? No, none of my friends are involved with Scientology, no. Honestly, it's not a huge topic of conversation. People have their beliefs, and you respect them, you know? Though it’s hard not to think it’s a bit bonkers sometimes. Yeah, a bit bonkers. Like, why spend all that money on, like, spirit upgrades? You could buy a new bike! Exactly! A new bike would be considerably more practical, wouldn’t it? Finn, sweetheart, eat your potato. We're having a good chat here, and I don't want you chucking dinner at the ceiling. Now, you remember what we talked about with your friend, Lucy? About respecting everyone’s choices?

Right, so are you sure this is the quickest way? I swear we’ve been driving for ages. Trust me, love. Google Maps says it’s the fastest. It’s just… a bit twisty isn't it? This sat nav is a bit dodgy. Dodgy is an understatement. It’s trying to make me drive through a field! Honestly, I’m starting to think we should’ve just stuck to the A1. Don’t be dramatic. It’ll be worth it – you’ll see. We’ll be at your Nan’s in no time. Plus, you were moaning about needing a break from the motorway. I was! Just… didn’t anticipate a scenic route involving sheep. Did you ever think about doing those dancing lessons? Remember we talked about it? Yeah, briefly. But realistically, I barely have time to shower let alone learn the tango. What about you? Are you still thinking about it? I am, actually. Sarah at work signed up for a ballroom dancing class and she's raving about it. Apparently, it's brilliant for your posture too. Something to do with aligning your spine. She’s obsessed with Old English posture! Right, because  that’s  a thing. You know your university work is going to pile up, right?
