You're barely getting through it as it is. I know, I know. But it’d be nice to do something fun and a bit ridiculous. Remember that time we tried to recreate that TikTok dance? Don't remind me! It looked like we were having a seizure rather than dancing. And my back hurt for days. What are you watching on LoveFilm at the moment? “The Crown,” obviously. I'm obsessed. It’s proper good. What about you? Still hooked on that crime documentary series? Guilty as charged. It’s fascinating, actually. All that forensic stuff. Makes you think. You know, I was reading about ageism in the medical profession the other day – apparently they're more likely to dismiss elderly people's symptoms. Seriously? That’s awful. Makes you wonder. Did you see what happened with Kanye West? Absolutely bonkers. Utter chaos. Though, to be fair, his fashion week shows are always… interesting. Remember when we used to spend hours on Myspace, designing our profiles? Please don't. The absolute cringe! I had a flaming heart on my profile picture. Oh my god. You did! And you had that song "Butterfly" by Crazy Town as your auto-playing song.

Honestly, this scenery is just breathtaking, isn’t it? Reminds me a bit of some of those landscape paintings I saw at the Tate. All moody greens and blues. It is lovely, pet. Much better than the M6, that's for sure. Still think you’re driving me mad with all that talking though! Dad, are we nearly there? Can I put my music on now? Nearly, son. Just a few more kilometres. And no, not until we’ve decided where we’re eating tonight. We need to find somewhere good. I’ve been looking at these reviews… Ooh, a proper Croatian restaurant. With proper seafood. I saw a place back in that little village we drove through earlier – looked amazing. Tiny place, all fairy lights. We went past a market just now, didn’t we? We should’ve stopped for some olive oil. Apparently, Istrian olive oil is the best in the world. Is there Wi-Fi at the campsite? Need to check Sons of Anarchy. Just got to episode four. Sons of Anarchy, are we? Sometimes I wonder what your childhood was like, lad. There’s a bit more to life than motorbike gangs, you know. We've got wine tasting experiences, amazing art galleries… Don’t be such a snob, Richard! It's good entertainment. And anyway, this trip is about more than just art and wine. It’s about relaxing. Remember last year’s Center Parcs debacle? That was a disaster. Don't remind me! The queue for the swimming pool… it was like something out of a zombie film. This is a much better idea, honestly. Getting out in nature. Can we go camping again next year? Or get a caravan? A caravan? Oh, please no! Those things are awful. Cramped and stuffy. That’s debatable. My auntie Brenda has a beautiful caravan. Full of chintz and doilies, but very cosy. It's just a question of finding a good campsite. Somewhere with decent facilities, you know. Not just a field and a portalo toilet. Well, wherever we go, I want to find some interesting plants. I've been reading about the local flora. Apparently, there are some incredible orchids growing wild here. You and your plants! You’d be happy just wandering around in fields, wouldn’t you? Pretty much, yeah. It’s peaceful. Better than arguing about where to park the car. You’ve been gripping the wheel like it’s going to explode, love.

Right, so you’re  definitely  saying you recorded it? Like, the whole thing? Yeah, I did. I know, it’s a bit mad, isn't it? But Lucy was being so ridiculous, trying to convince everyone she could beat Alex at Mario Kart with one hand tied behind her back, I just… I had to. You absolute legend! Can I see? Please? Honestly, you lot are mental. Recording arguments about Mario Kart? What is the world coming to? Don't be such a killjoy, Chloe! It’s hilarious. Especially the bit where Lucy's face went all red after she crashed into a wall for the tenth time. It was golden. Absolutely golden. I've sent it to a few people already, but I haven't let Alex see it yet, because he'd kill me. Should we leak it to the group chat? Imagine the carnage! No! Absolutely not. You'll get yourself in so much trouble. Chloe, tell her not to! Relax, I'm not going to leak it. I just thought you’d all appreciate a laugh. Well, I appreciate it. Where is it then? Show us. Hang on, let me find it... it’s buried somewhere amongst all my cat videos. Cat videos? Seriously? You are a menace. It's just so weird to think that someone would record something like that. What if someone had seen you? No one was around. It was just us in the living room. And anyway, it's not like it's  that  scandalous. Scandalous?! It’s peak entertainment, that’s what it is. And Lucy’s got a face like a slapped trout when she's losing. Okay, okay, you’re twisting my arm here. I’m mildly intrigued. But if Alex finds out, I’m blaming you. Right, here we go… Brace yourselves. It starts with Lucy proclaiming her Mario Kart supremacy... Oh god, here we go! I can already hear her whining. Oh, stop it! She's already got that determined look on her face. This is brilliant. She does look a bit intense for a kart racing game, doesn’t she? And then, disaster strikes...  crash sound  Told you she’d crash! Oh, that's priceless! Look at her face! Okay, I have to admit, it  is  quite funny. You’ve got a talent for capturing these moments, Chloe. You should think about becoming a filmmaker. Maybe I should.

Right, I'm absolutely starving. This morning's training session went on forever. Anyone fancy grabbing a sandwich from the cafe? Ooh, yes please! I skipped breakfast rushing in. They do a decent tuna melt, don't they? Tuna melt sounds good, but I'm craving something a bit… heartier. I saw they had those sausage and bean baguettes today. Sausage and bean? That's a bit…much for eleven o'clock, isn't it, Gaz? Nah, I need the fuel! Long afternoon of Powerpoint presentations ahead. Besides, I’m starving too, Kev. You’d think being an IT trainer would involve more moving around. Seriously! We spend most of our time sat staring at screens. I’ve got a dodgy back from it. Might have to invest in one of those ergonomic chairs. You and me both, love. Back's killing me. Alright, Gaz, go for the sausage and bean, you rebel. I’ll stick with the tuna. What about you, Maisie? Anything catch your eye? Hmm, maybe a salad. Trying to be good, you know. Although, that tuna melt  is  calling to me… it’s got that lovely melted cheese… Don’t fight it, Maisie. Life’s too short for boring salads when there's melted cheese involved. He's right. Treat yourself. We’re all going to be fuelled by caffeine and questionable lunch choices to get through this afternoon. Okay, okay, you've convinced me. Tuna melt it is! Though I’m blaming you two when I’m feeling sluggish after lunch. Fair enough. But you won't regret it. You know they put proper mature cheddar on them now. Right, let’s go then. Before the queue gets too long. And Gaz, don't hog all the sausage and bean baguettes! Leave one for the rest of us. No promises! Gotta get my energy levels up. This Excel course is going to be brutal. I'm dreading the attendees who think Excel is witchcraft. Tell me about it. Last time I had someone ask me how to get the computer to "think for them." You try explaining pivot tables to  that ! Haha, classic! You’d think it's rocket science, not spreadsheets. Okay, let's move, or we truly  will  be queuing for an eternity. Lunch awaits! "

Right, so I was reading this article the other day, proper deep dive into how libraries are using TikTok. Honestly, it’s a rabbit hole. TikTok, eh? I’ve seen a bit of it. Mostly people dancing, isn't it? Doesn't seem terribly relevant to Dewey Decimals. Oh, it’s far more than dancing, Mark! Though, admittedly, there's a lot of that. The clever libraries are using it to build community, highlight collections. I saw one doing a delightful series on Victorian mourning jewellery – absolutely fascinating. That’s exactly it! They’re doing short videos, quick looks at interesting items. Not the whole catalogue, just the intriguing bits. Got a first edition of something? Bam, a 15-second clip. Keeps it engaging. So, it’s like… teasers for the real thing? Luring people in with, dare I say it, 'viral content'? Precisely! We need to think about reach, you know? Younger generations aren't exactly flocking to the physical building. Hard to get them interested in interlibrary loans. Absolutely. Traditional marketing is dead, isn't it? Though, I do miss a well-designed leaflet. There's something comforting about holding information in your hand. Tell me about it. I still use a notepad and pencil. Drives the IT department mad. You’re a legend, Dave. But seriously, have you looked at Instagram? Loads of libraries doing the clever "shelfie" thing, showcasing their architecture, the atmosphere. Instagram is a favourite of mine. So many gorgeous library interiors showcased! I follow a few in Scandinavia – the design is just stunning. Very minimalist, very calming. Sounds a bit sterile for my tastes. Give me a chaotic, overflowing history section any day. Brings character. True, but you can capture that character in a photo. Think about it - a short video of someone pulling out a dusty, leather-bound book… that’s gold. Just as long as you’re not inadvertently promoting a damp patch or a rogue spider. One library got some serious stick for showing a web in a corner. Oh, brilliant! So, you’re saying social media’s a minefield? Potentially. You need to be mindful of copyright, accessibility. And you definitely need a good sense of humour. I saw one library trying to be ‘quirky’ and posting a picture of a pigeon on the windowsill with the caption ‘Our resident scholar.’ It didn't exactly land well. Oh, that's awful!

Right, so let’s run through this Business Case again. I’ve had a chance to look at the initial draft, and while it's solid, I think we need to really hammer home the rationale for Tunbridge Wells specifically. Aye, fair enough, Fiona. It’s easy to get bogged down in the details, forget the 'why' of it all. The Commissioning Board are already questioning the location. Something about needing better coverage of the eastern Kent area. Exactly. And the current provision, or lack thereof, for palliative care in this part of the county is frankly appalling. We really need to spell that out. The consultation process needs to demonstrate a clear and pressing need. Have we finalised the data from the local GP surgeries? Nearly there. Got a couple of hold-ups with Rotherham, surprisingly, getting numbers transcribed, but should be with you by Monday. Gives us decent figures on projected end-of-life care needs over the next five years, and the current facility gaps. They’ll see the stark figures. Good. Because just saying there's a need isn't enough. We need to be able to quantify it with precision. And we need to address the arguments about accessibility – the M25 is a nightmare, and the impact of that on family travel. Aye, we need to position it as a central hub, accessible from different directions. And that the existing estate agents are already reporting a deficit in specialist accommodation for elderly patients and those needing respite - demonstrates need. I’ve even been looking at a few potential sites around here – a couple of farms just outside town, surprisingly amenable to redevelopment. Good, good. I was thinking something modern, light. Not the traditional, rather gloomy hospice aesthetic. Lots of natural light, gardens, courtyard spaces. Something that feels…welcoming, rather than institutional. Imagine a retreat, almost. Absolutely. Somewhere families can feel comfortable spending time. We need to consider the design from a psychological perspective, too. Minimal corridors, views of green space, that kind of thing. Thinking about the layout helps me visualize the structure and also the needs. Precisely. And the staffing. We need to attract and retain the best nurses. That means competitive salaries, of course, but also a supportive environment, professional development opportunities… We need to factor that cost in, of course. And the relationship with the local hospice organisations is vital. We don’t want to be seen as rivals.

Right, who wants to tackle the washing up while we reminisce? Oh my god, look at Auntie Sheila’s hair! It's… an event. That was 1988, wasn’t it? She was convinced crimped hair was all the rage. Your mum was mortified. Absolutely mortified. She spent weeks trying to get it flat. Remember that travel hairdryer she bought? It only blew hot air directly behind you, so you'd end up even more frizzy. You’re making me miss Mum! How’s she doing? She's well, still bossing Geoff around at the garden centre. She sent me a picture of the rhododendrons – they're absolutely stunning this year. Good. Geoff needs a woman like her keeping him in line. Speaking of stunning, remember Ascot last year? Your mum pulled out all the stops. Oh, don't remind me! The hat! It nearly knocked over poor Mrs. Henderson. Speaking of Ascot, I saw Chloe posted a picture from Royal Ascot today. Looks amazing. She was worried about getting in, said the security was tighter than ever. Chloe’s doing well, isn’t she? Still loving that copywriting job? Yeah, she's really thriving! Got a big pitch next week, apparently. A national stationery company. Pretty stressful. Oh, well, tell her to breathe! It’s just a job interview disguised as a potentially lucrative deal. She's brilliant, she’ll smash it. Did she mention needing any help with her presentation? Not yet, but she might. She was moaning about her phone case, though. Said she dropped it again and the camera lens cracked. You can get those tempered glass screen protectors and cases now. Practically indestructible. I got one for my phone last month – worth every penny. Definitely. And I’ve got a couple of spares if she needs them. Right, dinner’s nearly ready. What about this family history project? Have you looked into those branches from Southport yet, David? Still sifting through birth certificates and census records. Found a fascinating snippet about a distant relative who apparently ran away to join the circus. A trapeze artist, no less! Wow! That's incredible! Suddenly my life feels very mundane. Oh, this one! Is that Grandma Elsie wearing that ridiculously big jumper? That was her signature style. She swore it kept her warm. She used to say it made her feel like a snug little badger. She was a character, that one.

Right, so, are we actually doing this then? You’re not going to chicken out, are you? No, no. I'm here, aren’t I? But honestly, I'm already regretting suggesting this. You know I'm a lightweight. Aye, well, that's why I picked it. Something proper then, not just jump scares. Something properly creepy. I’ve got ‘The Babadook’ queued up. ‘The Babadook’? Oh God. I’ve heard about that. People say it's genuinely disturbing, psychologically. Not just… things popping out. Exactly! That’s what I’m after. Proper unsettling. Like a slow creep. None of this chainsaw massacre nonsense. Right. Okay. But if I start crying, you're fetching me a hot chocolate and a massive blanket. Deal? Deal. But you’re not allowed to hide behind the sofa. That’s cheating. I didn’t say I  would  hide! Just… asserting my right to potentially need comfort. So, what's it about? Just to mentally prepare. Okay, right. So it’s about this single mum, right, and her son. He’s… a bit of a handful. And he’s convinced there’s a monster in his bedroom. A Babadook. A Babadook? Is that even a word? It sounds made up. That’s the point! It’s a clever, creepy children's book that keeps appearing in their house. And the more they read it, the more real the monster seems to become. Oh… okay. That sounds… heavy. Like, not just scary, but sad too? Aye, it’s got a really strong undercurrent of grief and depression, actually. It’s brilliant though, honestly. It really gets under your skin. Right. Well, I'm bracing myself. Should I, like, eat a whole bag of popcorn or something to build up defenses? Nah, save some for me. Just get ready to be properly freaked out. And, you know, if you need to scream, scream. Don't bottle it up. Gets the tension out. Easy for you to say, you're made of Yorkshire steel! Alright, hit play then. But if I have nightmares, you’re sleeping on the couch. Sorted. Let's do this. Get ready for the Babadook!      Oh gosh. Already feeling the dread. You were right, this looks proper creepy. Told ya. Enjoy! Or maybe not. ;) Don’t you dare laugh at me when I’m practically under the covers! I'll try not to. But no promises!

Right, just popping in to say goodnight, Grandad. Are you comfy? Comfy enough, dear. A bit chilly though. Did you remember to close the window in the spare room? I did, yes. Found a little spider crawling across it, though! Gave me a fright. Spiders, eh? Always sneaking about. I’ve never been keen on them myself. You know, back in my day, we didn’t have these fancy gadgets to scare them away. A rolled-up newspaper was the thing. Times have changed, haven't they? I was just trying to order a new pizza online earlier tonight - total disaster. The app kept crashing. Online ordering! Can’t imagine. I used to just give Fred’s down the road a ring. Simpler times, simpler ways. Did you see that Airbnb advert on the telly the other day? Fancy going on holiday and staying in someone’s spare room. I did! It's a bit odd, isn't it? Though, it  can  be cheaper. Remember Auntie Maggie wanted us to look at one for her visit next summer? Maggie, yes. She’s a busy one, always planning something. Tell you what, this new iPad I’ve got... it’s quite something. They showed me how to video call the other day. I spoke to your cousin Emily. That’s lovely! You’re getting quite the tech whiz. I showed you a few things, remember? How you can look up the news and everything? I can zoom in on the headlines, yes. Though I still prefer the paper. And all those emails… Honestly, they’re a constant nuisance. Spam, most of them. Tell me about it. I get so many. I'm trying to sort through them all tomorrow. I’ve put a few old pieces of furniture up for sale online, too, you know, since we're reorganising the house. Hoping someone will take them off our hands. Reorganising… Always changing things around. It’s tiring, isn't it? I like things just as they are. Everything in its place. That’s the key, you see. You're absolutely right. Well, I should let you get some sleep, shouldn't I? It’s getting late. Yes, dear. Don’t stay up too late yourself. These modern families, always burning the candle at both ends. Routine is important, you know. Bedtime is bedtime. I’ll try! Goodnight, Grandad. Sleep well. I’ll pop back to check on you in the morning.

This is glorious, isn’t it? Brucefield Farm at its finest. Proper escape from the city hustle. Absolutely. Fresh air, good company, decent whisky… you can’t ask for much more than that. Feels a world away from trying to wrangle postgraduate dissertations. Tell me about it. My work’s been manic. The new sustainability campaign is eating my life. But at least it’s… something. What’s got you so swamped at the Uni just now? Funding applications, mostly. Trying to secure grants for the new modern literature module. It's a tough ask. Though, I did manage to snag a few new titles for the library – had to fight for them, mind you. Got a first edition Calvino, actually. No way! A first edition? You're spoiling me! I’ll need to sneak a look. Speaking of books, I’ve been devouring Murakami again. Started  Kafka on the Shore  for the… fifth time, I think? Murakami’s a genius, isn’t he? The way he blends the mundane with the surreal... that unsettling feeling of dislocation. Reminds me a bit of Borges, in a way. Definitely. But then, I’ve been craving something completely different too. Finished a travelogue about Patagonia last week. Absolutely stunning photography. Made me itch to just… disappear. Patagonia, eh? Always wanted to go. The Andes, the glaciers... it’s on the list. I've been obsessing over Japan lately. I’ve got that Kodansha Japan guidebook, the one with all the local secrets. Japan! That’s been top of  my  list for years. The culture, the food, the history... I was looking at some itineraries for the cherry blossom season. Imagine, walking through a tunnel of blossoms… Sounds idyllic. I’ve been reading about the Shinkansen. The sheer efficiency of the bullet train system! It’s almost poetic. One of these days I'll have to head out there. It's a dream. Speaking of dreams, remember that disastrous backpacking trip we took through Southeast Asia after graduation? How could I forget? The questionable street food, the relentless humidity… and your insistence on haggling for everything! Hey, I was saving money! And those temples in Cambodia were incredible. Truly awe-inspiring. Almost makes you forget the food poisoning. Almost. You know, I was just thinking about that trip. It really broadened my horizons, didn’t it? Made me realise how much there is to see and experience beyond Edinburgh.

So, have you sent off the application then, love? For that architectural assistant role at Foster & Partners? Not yet, Mum. I'm just… staring at it. Feeling a bit overwhelmed, actually. Overwhelmed? Why? You’re brilliant! You’ve got a fantastic portfolio, a brilliant degree… You practically built half of the university’s exhibition space yourself! I know, I know. It’s just… Foster & Partners. It's  Foster & Partners . It feels almost… intimidating. All those incredible projects, all those amazing architects... Darling, they wouldn’t be advertising if they didn’t think there were people out there capable. And you are one of those people. Remember what you used to say when you were little, building those Lego castles? "Anything's possible if you put your mind to it." Oh God, I remember that. I was such a drama queen. You were a creative child! And that creativity hasn't gone anywhere. What specifically is making you hesitate? Is it the personal statement? Partly. I’ve written and rewritten it about five times. I don’t know if it sounds arrogant, or not enthusiastic enough... I just want to convey how genuinely excited I am about the opportunity and how much I admire their work, but without sounding like a groupie. Right, I can see that. Let’s have a look then. Read it aloud to me, and I’ll just listen. No interruptions, just read it as you would if you were sending it. Okay. “To the recruitment team at Foster & Partners... I am writing to express my keen interest in the Architectural Assistant position advertised on….” Ugh, does that sound too formal? A little, perhaps. Try something a bit more approachable. Maybe, “I was so excited to see the advert for the Architectural Assistant position…” See, a bit friendlier, a bit more genuine. Yeah, that’s better. Okay, continuing… “My postgraduate studies at the Bartlett….” Stop there. You don't need to recite your entire academic history. Briefly mention the major focuses of your study – sustainable design, parametric modelling – and then move on to  why  that’s relevant to them. So, instead of saying "I extensively studied…” I’d say something like "My focus on sustainable design during my postgraduate studies aligns with Foster & Partners' commitment to environmentally responsible architecture…" Exactly! See? You’ve got it. And don't forget to mention your practical experience – the university projects, the internship with Anderson & Stone.

Lovely to see you, Patricia. It's been far too long. How's your back today, Arthur? Not bad, not bad. A little stiff, you know. Rain’s always sets it off. Dreadful weather we've been having, wouldn't you agree, David? It certainly has. Though I always say, a bit of rain is good for the garden. David, dear, help yourself to a biscuit. Ginger? Chocolate? Ginger for me, thanks, Patricia. You know, I was just thinking about the price of petrol. Absolutely scandalous, isn't it? Used to be you could fill a tank for a few bob. Remember those days, Arthur? Aye, I do. And a decent car too. Not like these new ones. All plastic and electronics. Give me a good old Ford Anglia any day. Solid, that was. Reliable. Oh, Arthur, you’re stuck in the past! Though I will admit, these modern cars are a bit much. All those gadgets… I barely know how to adjust the radio! They don’t make them like they used to, that's for sure. Though I must say, this government isn’t helping the situation either. All this talk about green energy... driving up prices for everyone. Exactly! And what about the housing situation? My granddaughter can't afford to buy a flat in London. It’s ridiculous. They’re all renting, aren’t they? Trapped. It’s heartbreaking, isn’t it? When I was bringing up the children, a deposit was a struggle, but it was  possible  to buy a small house. Now… it’s a pipe dream for so many young people. And the council houses... gone, practically. They sold them all off. What were they thinking? Destroying the safety net for generations to come. They were thinking about lining their own pockets, I reckon. Politicians… they're all the same. Promises, promises, and then nothing. Remember Maggie Thatcher? People thought she was the answer… Oh, let's not start on that, Arthur. We’ve argued it to death over the years. It’s all a bit depressing, isn’t it? Let’s talk about something happier. How’s your daughter, David? Still enjoying her job? She is, yes. Thriving, actually. Just got a promotion, in fact. Manager now. Very proud of her. Though she worries about me, you know. Says I need to be more active. Tell her to worry about the state of the country instead!

Right, so I was thinking about the old pottery studio space… you know, the one we've been trying to figure out what to do with? Yeah, the one with the terrible lighting and dodgy ventilation? Still not a fan. Exactly. But I had a thought. Remember Sarah from the community choir mentioned they needed a larger rehearsal space? Vaguely. They’re always having a bit of a squeeze, aren’t they? Exactly! I reckon if we offered it to them, on a reasonably priced rental basis, it could be a really good source of income and a valuable community asset too. On paper, it sounds good. But the state of the place... We'd need to get the builders in to sort out that lighting, at the very least. And the damp patch is still there. I know, I know. It's a project, definitely. But we're trying to generate income, aren't we? And the choir’s a lovely bunch; good tenants. We’d need to factor in some initial investment for renovations though. What do you think a realistic estimate would be, just ballpark? Hmmm... re-wiring, plastering, new floor covering… easily six to eight grand, I’d say. And then we’d need to market it, create some flyers, put something on the charity website. Right. We could ask Mark from marketing to knock something up; he's been quiet lately. Speaking of Mark, have you spoken to Mrs. Henderson about the fire escape issue? She was complaining the other day that children were playing on it. I had a quick word, yeah. She’s understandably concerned. I’ve put a request in to maintenance for a gate, a basic one, just to stop the easy access. It’s a priority, I think. Any chance you saw those new chairs for the reception area? They arrived yesterday. Oh, are they in storage then? I didn’t notice. Are they the eco-friendly ones we ordered? Yeah, the recycled plastic ones. They look… surprisingly stylish actually. Though getting them up the stairs was a nightmare! Nearly lost a back in the process. I swear, the stairwell in this place is designed to defeat humanity! Tell me about it! We really need to look at improving the storage solutions too – this place is bursting at the seams, especially with all the summer bookings. The yoga class are using more and more space now.

This bread is incredible, honestly. Where did you get it from, Rhys? From that little bakery in town, remember? "The Loaf & Ladle," it's called. They do a proper bara brith too, though I didn’t get any this time. It’s amazing. I'm properly full, but I could still eat another slice of that apple pie. Gareth, you’ve outdone yourself. It's absolutely spot on! Best pie I’ve had in ages. You've got a real talent, Gareth. Thanks, lads! It's a family recipe, you know. My Nan used to make it. Secret ingredient is a pinch of cinnamon and a decent amount of butter. Can't skimp on the butter. That’s the way to do it, boy! Butter is king! You’re just like your grandmother. It IS lovely, Gareth. Reminds me of when the boys were little and we used to bake together on Saturdays. Pure chaos. Flour everywhere! Oh, I remember those days! Covered in flour, arguing about who got the most icing. Good times. You’re awfully quiet over there. Did you not enjoy the lamb stew I made? No, no, it was brilliant, honestly. Just… a lot to take in, all this delicious food. I’m not used to being waited on hand and foot like this. Don't be daft, Rhys! Everyone has to eat. Besides, you're family. Yeah! And you used to make me shepherd’s pie when I was little. Remember? With the mashed potato swirl on top? Of course, I do! It was your favourite. Took me ages to do those swirls perfectly. He always was a good cook. Even when he was a boy. Always experimenting. Remember that time he tried to make a cake using beetroot? Oh, don't remind me! It was bright purple and tasted like dirt! The poor thing was so proud of himself. Alright, alright! Let's not dig up embarrassing childhood memories. I've evolved since then, I swear! Slightly! Though I bet you still sneak a bit of chocolate in your cooking when no one's looking. A chef's secret. Can't reveal all my tricks, now can I? So, anyone for coffee and maybe some of that bara brith Rhys mentioned? Definitely! Coffee would be brilliant. Aye, I'll join you. A good cup of coffee and a bit of Welsh cake would set me up nicely for the rest of the afternoon.

Right so, I was thinking, you know, about that thing you said about Bristol. And I was just remembering... it’s a proper proper city, isn't it? Like, properly  vibrant . Yeah, it is. Really liked it when I was there for that conference last year. Lots of interesting architecture too, right? Loads! And all those murals. Remember showing you those pictures of Stokes Croft? The street art's mad. Proper good. Vaguely. Too many photos of cats fighting on your Instagram feed, to be honest. Difficult to filter through. Rude! They’re cute cats! Anyway, I was thinking… maybe we should actually  go  sometime. Not just for a conference. Like, a proper holiday. Bristol? Instead of Port Leslie? Bit of a jump, isn’t it? Well yeah, but think about it! Loads to do. Harbourside, Clifton Suspension Bridge… loads of independent shops and cafes. And you’d like the engineering bits too, wouldn’t you? Brunel and all that. Hmm, fair point. Access to decent coffee shops is always a plus. But what about everyone else? What do they think? Well, I’ve mentioned it to Mum and Dad. Dad was practically drooling about the SS Great Britain, naturally. Mum just said something about needing a good brunch. Typical. And what about Anya and Tom? Are they up for it? I haven't actually asked them yet. I was waiting to gauge your reaction first. I don't want to organise something and then nobody ends up wanting to come. Don’t be daft. They’d probably love it. Anya’s been moaning about needing a proper girls' weekend. And Tom’s always up for a bit of urban exploring. True, true. Right, I'll text them tonight then. Wonder if they've seen that advert for that Caribbean cruise. You know, the one with the cheesy music and the turquoise water? Oh God, the one that makes you feel instantly guilty for even considering going anywhere  but  the Caribbean? Exactly! It’s relentless. You feel like you  should  be sipping cocktails on a white sand beach. It's advertising done brilliantly. Creates a totally unattainable ideal. Keeps you wanting more. It does! Makes you feel rubbish. Maybe Bristol isn't so bad after all. Less pressure to look like you're having the best holiday ever. Exactly. Less tan lines to worry about. And think of the cider! It’s supposed to be really good in Bristol.

It’s lovely to properly catch up, Sarah. It feels like ages since we last had a proper chat. It has, hasn’t it? Life’s just been… a lot, lately. Glad you could pop over for a coffee. Of course. I was in the area, and I knew you’d be here. How are things with Mum? Still getting the appointments sorted? Slowly. The neurologist finally managed to squeeze her in last week. He’s talking about… well, more tests. More scans. It’s exhausting, keeping on top of it all. She's getting quite anxious now, bless her. Oh, I'm so sorry. It’s just relentless, isn’t it? The waiting and the worrying. I remember with my dad, the endless appointments… Exactly. And then poor Aunt Maggie passed away last month. Completely out of the blue. Oh, Sarah, I’m so sorry to hear that. Maggie was such a character. My heart goes out to your family. Thank you. It’s been… a whirlwind, to be honest. The funeral was last week. My brother David hasn’t stopped crying, poor thing. He was so close to her. It’s awful when they grieve so openly. Some people try to bottle it up, but he's at least letting himself feel it. Yes, completely. It's almost unsettling seeing him like that. Normally, he's so stoic. My sister, Claire, she's putting on a brave face, as always, fussing over everyone else while falling apart herself. It’s classic Claire. That’s so often how families are, isn't it? One person’s crumbling, and another’s trying to hold everything together. I used to be like that with my mum, always trying to be the strong one. It’s a terrible habit. Do you know what, after all this, I’m just craving some peace. And a decent slice of cake. I've been so stressed I've put on… well, it's noticeable. We all do, don’t we? Comfort eating is a national sport! I've been trying this new intermittent fasting thing, but it's such a juggle with the kids and work. Keeps me on my toes, that's for sure. Intermittent fasting? Really? Is it working? I've tried so many diets, you wouldn’t believe. Keto, paleo, juices… Nothing sticks. I just end up feeling deprived and then I give up completely.

Right, that was absolutely brilliant, wasn’t it? Honestly, best roast I’ve had in ages. Yeah, that was really good, Mum. Thanks. That gravy was spot on, Dad. Seriously. Proper flavour. Glad you both enjoyed it. I experimented a bit with a new wine pairing, too. What do you think? The Malbec with the beef? Actually, it was a really good combination, love. Didn't think I’d like it that much, but it worked well. Yeah, Dad, you’ve got taste. Unlike some people. Hey! I liked it. I just… I’m more of a Pepsi kind of guy. Fair enough. So, what’s everyone up to this week? Ben, any progress on that work experience application? Almost finished it. Just need to write the personal statement. It’s so boring, though. Describing why I want to work at a garage fixing cars. Like, it’s obvious, isn’t it? Well, you need to articulate why  you’re  the right person, love. What you bring to the table. Enthusiasm, a good attitude… Enthusiasm for engines! There. Done it. Very persuasive. And you, Tom? Still thinking about the ski trip with your mates? Yeah, we’re trying to sort it out. Switzerland’s looking pretty good, but it's expensive. It always is. Remember when we went to Austria? Sarah ended up breaking her arm skiing! Oh my god, Mum, do we  have  to relive that trauma every time skiing is mentioned? It's a classic! She was showing off, trying to do a jump she wasn’t ready for. I was! I was feeling confident! It was icy, though. Terribly icy. Bet you were showing off to a girl. Oh, hush you! Honestly, these young people. Speaking of work, I had that crazy situation at the warehouse today. One of the delivery trucks broke down right in the middle of the rush hour. Total chaos. Oh no, that's awful! What did you do? Had to reroute everything, contact emergency repairs… it was a nightmare. But we managed to sort it in the end, thankfully. The team really pulled together. Sounds stressful, Dad. Do you ever just… switch off? Try to! It's hard sometimes. Especially when you’re trying to control a whole operation. But I took a long walk this evening. That helped a bit. Thinking about swapping the car for an electric one, actually. Starting to feel guilty about all the emissions.

Right, so I was sorting through these old boxes – you know, the ones from when we moved – and I unearthed this entire folder of photos from that trip to Japan. Remember? Vaguely! It feels like a lifetime ago. The heat, the crowds… and those vending machines! Exactly! Look at this one, though. You, trying to pose with a vending machine that was dispensing weird, bright-green drinks. The look on your face is priceless. Oh god, don't remind me. I think I bought some melon-flavoured… something. It was awful. But look, you got a great shot of it! Your photography definitely improved over those two weeks, didn’t it? It did, I think. I was still fiddling with settings mostly, trying to figure out the light. But I’m actually kind of proud of a few of these. Check out this one of the bamboo forest in Arashiyama. Wow, that is beautiful. The way the light filters through… you really captured the stillness. You should seriously consider doing a proper exhibition someday. Maybe. It’s just... a lot of work. What do you think of this one though? I tried to get a picture of a badger, unsuccessfully, in Nara Park. You were after a badger?! In Nara Park? With all those deer running around? I know, it’s ridiculous! I was reading about them and thought, ‘I’ll have a go at getting a shot of a badger in a tourist hotspot.’ I spent ages crouched behind a bush. The deer kept giving me weird looks. Oh my god, you are unbelievable. Did you ever see one? Nope. Just deer. Lots and lots of deer. One tried to steal my sandwich, actually. That’s brilliant. Seriously, you try to photograph a badger, and a deer steals your lunch. Classic you. It’s my life story. But look, here’s a decent one. I managed to get a shot of the woman pouring the tea, you can almost feel the ceremony in the photograph. Yeah, that's lovely. You always had an eye for the details in those quiet moments. I remember you being so fascinated by the precision of everything. Did you ever try to recreate those Zen gardens back here? I did briefly! It lasted about a week before the weeds took over and the cats started using it as a litter tray. Of course they did.

This cholent is genuinely amazing, Anon. Seriously. You’ve outdone yourself. Thanks, Liam! It’s Claudia Roden’s recipe, you know. I’ve been tweaking it for ages. It's so good. Like, actually really comforting. I needed this after dealing with that absolute nightmare of a customer today. Wanted a decaf latte with oat milk  and  almond milk. Honestly, Joanie. You got that? The audacity. That’s classic. Reminds me of some of the requests I’d get back in Sydney. "Could I have a flat white, extra hot, but not  too  hot, and a sprinkle of cinnamon, but from a specific brand…” Tell me about it. I had a guy yesterday trying to convince me existentialism was basically a Jewish joke. No way! Oh, my god, Liam. That's incredible. What was his reasoning? Something about questioning everything being inherently funny, and the absurdity of it all being… well, Jewish. I didn’t even bother correcting him. You gotta love those guys. Living in their own little world. Speaking of absurd, remember that time we went to Ireland and tried to skinny dip? Don't remind me. The seaweed was  everywhere . And that freezing water! We barely lasted five minutes. Five minutes that resulted in frostbite and a close encounter with a very grumpy fisherman. Classic. It was a vibe though, wasn't it? Raw. I’ve got that photo on that new app, Memora. It catalogues photos with prompts – so you can remember the details, or what you were thinking. It captured the moment perfectly. Oh, Memora? I’ve seen ads for that. Is it any good? Pretty decent. It’s helping me keep track of… things. Exams are looming. Ugh, exams. The bane of our existence. I’m trying to avoid thinking about it. Hence, delicious cholent. Speaking of avoiding thinking about things… I was watching this zombie apocalypse show the other night. Pretty intense stuff! Oh God, please don't start. We don't need any more doom and gloom. Nah, nah, just thinking. If it were to happen, though, what's your strategy? I'm surprisingly resourceful. I'd gather books. Researching survival techniques. I’d be the one managing a community. Rationing food, setting up defenses. I’m good at logistics. I'd bake. Loads and loads of bread and pies. Morale booster, you know? Keeps the zombies distracted by sugar. Fair enough.

Right, so then the data clearly showed a significant increase in anxiety levels amongst… oh, look, they’ve refilled the peanuts! Excellent. Gotta fuel the brain, eh? I'm battling a particularly frustrating level on  Horizon Chase  at the moment. Absolutely unrelenting.  Horizon Chase ? Still? You've been playing that for weeks! It's a simple arcade racer. Simple, yes. But fiendishly difficult on the hardest setting. It’s about precision, not just speed. Like, nailing those drifts perfectly… it’s a skill. You’re talking about a game where you drive a 1980s car around a neon-lit track. Don't tell me you're getting competitive about drifting. It’s more than that! It's a zen-like experience. Though, I might be projecting. I need a break. Fancy talking about something completely different? Like, what were we just discussing before I got distracted by pixelated driving? Border security protocols. The findings were pretty surprising, actually. The reliance on facial recognition software... it's more flawed than people think. Yeah, I read something on that. Seems like biases can creep in easily, doesn’t it? They use it at the airport here, you know. I always feel a bit… scrutinized. Exactly. And the ethical implications are massive. What happens when it misidentifies someone? Or worse, targets certain demographics? It makes you think. Speaking of thinking... have you seen any good films recently? I’ve got that feeling where I really want to go to the cinema, but I can't decide what to see.  Dune: Part Two  was incredible. Absolutely stunning visuals, proper epic scope. Though, it's quite long. I keep hearing about that one. Is it worth the commitment? I'm not a huge sci-fi person normally. I'm more of a theme park kind of guy, really. Theme park? Seriously? You? Don’t knock it! I went to Alton Towers last month. The Wicker Man ride was terrifying. Brilliant. Felt like a proper cinematic experience, honestly. So, you prefer a manufactured thrill to, you know, actual intellectual stimulation? Hey! I appreciate intellectual stimulation. Just… sometimes it’s nice to scream your lungs out on a rollercoaster. It’s a good release. Also, the food's always terrible, so it’s a guaranteed diet day afterwards. You are incorrigible. I am inclined to agree with you however. Screaming on a ride, excellent for the soul.

These are absolutely brilliant, aren’t they? Best chips I’ve had in ages. They are good, yes. Much better than the ones we had that time in… oh, where was it, near the station? Dreadful they were. All soggy. Don't remind me! Right, so, you’re actually enjoying rowing lessons? You seemed a bit hesitant about it initially. I am! Surprisingly so. My arms ache terribly, of course, but it’s… bracing. Really bracing! And the scenery on the river is lovely. Bit choppy today, though. Nearly lost my hat. Oh dear! Not the good one, I hope? The tweed one? No, thankfully just the old baseball cap. Though I was thinking, I really need some proper waterproof trousers. You know, for when it  really  comes down. Do you have any recommendations? Absolutely. I got some from that outdoor shop on Mill Road last year - Rohan. They’re fantastic. A bit pricey, but totally worth it. You'll need them with this weather. Speaking of being out on the water, how was your kayaking trip to the Norfolk broads last summer? Oh, glorious! Absolutely glorious. Such peace and quiet. Though I did manage to capsize once. Completely unexpected. Just a sudden gust of wind. Went straight in! Oh, no! Yes, well, luckily it was shallow. And I was wearing my swimsuit underneath. Still, rather a shock to the system! It did remind me rather of meeting your Aunt Margaret for the first time though, didn’t it. Oh, don't remind me! That was a truly bizarre experience. You arranging that whole thing - thinking we'd strike up some instant family connection... Well, it did take a while, didn’t it? Her insisting on wearing that leopard print scarf… and constantly correcting my grammar. It was utterly surreal. Though, looking back, it’s rather lovely we made an effort. It's just a shame about Mum... I still can’t quite believe she's gone. No, me neither. It's been... a difficult few months. The funeral was lovely, of course, as much as such a thing can be, but... it's just left a huge hole. It really has. And poor Uncle David... he's not been himself at all since. No, he hasn’t. He’s trying to be strong for everyone, but it’s taking its toll. They think it’s the early stages of dementia, apparently.

Dad, did you ever learn Morse code? Like, properly? Aye, lass. Back in the day, Brownies made you learn a bit. Dot-dash, dot-dash, that was 'S', wasn't it? Can't remember much else now, though. All that texting these days, nobody needs it, do they? I know, right? It's so weird. Like, my friend Chloe was trying to teach her nan Morse code last week. Nan just kept saying “Why bother? I’ve got emojis!” Emojis! Aye, they’re a replacement for proper language, they are. Still, handy for a quick laugh, I suppose. How’s it going with A-Levels? Results day looming, eh? Stressing you out? A bit. I keep checking UCAS like every five minutes. Useless, really. And I’m still worried about the Maths one. I swear, I drew a diagram in the exam with a pen that ran out just as I was about to finish! Oh, brilliant! Just brilliant. Right, well, let's not dwell on it. We’ll get you to uni whatever happens. Speaking of which, did you see that email about the Freshers’ Week events? They’re selling reusable glass water bottles. Fancy getting one? Yeah, I saw. They’re a bit pricey, though. I was thinking about ordering one from eBay. Probably cheaper. Or maybe Amazon… Amazon’s alright but they'll hit you with delivery fees. Speaking of which, I ordered some new trainers the other day, ended up paying more for postage than the shoes themselves. Ridiculous, that is. Tell me about it! I need new shoes anyway. These ones are falling apart. Mum keeps saying I should go to Schuh. Good shout. Always a good selection there. But first, dinner! I’m starving. You forgetting to eat again, lass? You need to put some meat on those bones. Dad! I’m perfectly fine. I just haven't had time. We’re meeting at that new Thai place, aren't we? I hope they’ve got loads of vegetables. I want to make some proper healthy meals once I’m at uni. Aye, healthy meals. And who's paying for all this healthy eating, then? Student finance, is it? Don’t go splurging all your loan on avocado toast, eh? I won't! I’m trying to be sensible. I was looking on that website, Martin Lewis thing, about budgeting. It's scary how much everything costs.

Mate! Seriously, this place is a haven. Thanks for letting us crash here, Liam. Nah, no worries man, good to see you both. Long time, yeah? Feels like ages since we properly linked up. How was the journey? Mad. Tube was rammed, as usual. You’d think people would learn to spread out. Are you having a cuppa? Yeah, just put the kettle on. Tea, coffee, what you fancy? And proper biscuits? Got some Hobnobs and Digestive. Hobnobs, definitely. I’m dying for a biscuit. So, how’s life been? Still drowning in essays? You have no idea. Finals are basically consuming my entire existence. I swear, my computer is starting to judge me. Keeps crashing whenever I try to run any serious simulations. Tell me about it. Mine just decided to update at the worst possible moment, right in the middle of writing my dissertation. Nearly lost a whole section. Oh man, that’s rough. You’re finished now though, right? Dissertation done? Yeah, submitted it last week. Feels surreal, actually. Like I’ve been working towards this one thing for years, and now it’s just...over. Big up! That’s massive, man. What are you doing now then? Straight into the job hunt? Trying to, yeah. Got a few interviews lined up, but nothing concrete yet. Thinking about heading to Japan for a bit, actually. Japan?! Seriously? That’s insane! When? What are you thinking of doing? Hoping to go in September, maybe stay for a couple of months. Just wanna experience it, you know? Tokyo especially. Always been fascinated by the culture. Tokyo's unreal, man. My auntie went last year and sent back loads of pictures. Apparently, the food is incredible. And the robots. You gotta check out the robots. Definitely robots. And ramen. So much ramen. What about you? Still grinding through computer science? Got any big plans after you finish your exams? Yeah, still here, still slightly insane. Thinking of maybe doing a masters, maybe not. I don’t know, man, feeling pretty burnt out at the moment. I just want to lie on a beach somewhere and do absolutely nothing. Maybe Bali? Bali sounds amazing. You deserve it. We should go together sometime. Yeah, that would be wicked. We could stuff our faces with Pad Thai and learn to surf. It’d be sick. Exactly! Speaking of food, have you been to that new Korean place in Shoreditch? '

Look at this, Mum! Found another one from the trip to Buckfast. Remember that funny monk with the enormous smile? Oh, bless him! Yes, a proper happy chappie. He looked like he was hiding a secret, didn't he? Did you put it on Facebook, love? I did! Got loads of comments already. Auntie Carol said she thought he looked like a startled meerkat. Meerkat? What's a meerkat? Sounds like something you get in that newfangled supermarket. It's a type of animal, Grandad. Little furry thing. He's got a point, though. You youngsters and your internet… all these gadgets. Remember when a photograph was something special? You had to wait for it to be developed! I know, Mum, but it's so easy to share with everyone. Speaking of which, did you manage to sort out the insurance for the cruise? Nearly. Been wrestling with this online form all afternoon. Honestly! It's more complicated than doing my tax returns. And you know how tedious  that  is. Tax returns... Don't even get me started. David Cameron and all that offshore nonsense. Scandalous, I tell you. The cheek of it! Used to be, people paid their fair share. It's a mess, Grandad. Anyway, about the cruise… I was thinking, the Mediterranean next year? We could do Italy, Greece… Italy, that sounds lovely. But dear, remember what Dr. Ellis said about overheating? We'll need to be careful. And all that walking around those ancient ruins... We’ll take it easy, Mum. Plenty of shade, lots of ice cream. And we could look at one of those ones where they do all the excursions for you. Cruises. Waste of money, if you ask me. Being stuck on a boat with a load of strangers. Give me Devon any day. Oh, don’t be such a grumpy old man. You secretly enjoyed that trip to Buckfast. Admired their gardens, didn't you? The lavender was rather nice, I’ll admit. Though I still think they could do with a bit more topiary. Topiary! You’re incorrigible. Look, I found this article about a medical breakthrough. Apparently, they’ve found a new way to… Oh, leave it, love. It’ll just give me something else to worry about. Speaking of worries, have you heard anything about Clive’s car? Still stuck down the lane, is it? Yes, apparently there’s a problem with the alternator.

So, tell me everything! Belgium sounded amazing in your texts. Did you have a good time? Oh, love, it was lovely. Really lovely. Just what we needed. Needed to get away. Absolutely. Brighton was getting a bit much. The seagulls, the crowds… you needed a relax, didn't you, Michael? That’s right. A real chill out. Though driving over... that was a bit of a trial. Driving? Tell me about it! I remember Dad panicking about the ferry. The ferry was fine! Smooth as you like. It was the driving on the other side of the road that nearly gave me a heart attack. And the sat nav… the sat nav was a menace. Oh, don't even get me started on that thing. It kept wanting to take us down these tiny little lanes! I was shouting at it half the time. "No, not that way! Turn back!" Seriously? Did it get you lost? Lost? We were lost for a good half hour near Bruges! Ended up on a farm track. A muddy farm track! And then a farmer came out looking at us like we were mad tourists. He didn’t even speak English! I said ‘Sorry, sorry, we’re lost!’ and he just shrugged. Michael was practically white. Oh my god, Dad! Did you manage to cycle? I know you were looking forward to that. Oh yes, cycling was brilliant. Hired bikes in Ghent. Lovely city. All those canals. It was beautiful. And the waffles! Don't even get me started on the waffles! Best I’ve ever tasted. And the chocolate, of course. Every other shop was a chocolatier. I bet! Were the markets good? I saw some pictures online. Wonderful! We went to one in Antwerp. Loads of antiques, clothes, food… got a lovely little ceramic dish. It'll look perfect on the windowsill. And the frites! Thick-cut chips… dipped in mayonnaise. Heaven! Wow, you guys sound like you really embraced the Belgian life. I’m so glad you enjoyed it. I need a holiday! Work's been manic. Oh, you’re always working. You need to slow down, love. You’ll burn yourself out. Actually, speaking of phones… Michael’s finally got a new one! Oh, brilliant! About time. What did you get? Got myself a Samsung Galaxy. Big screen, good camera. It’s a bit fiddly still, mind you. Finding my way around all the menus.

Right, so I’m thinking chicken and chorizo fajitas tonight. Got everything? Pretty sure. Peppers – check. Onions – check. Chicken… yeah, chicken’s defrosting. Did you get those lovely little corn tortillas? I did! Thought they’d be a bit nicer than the flour ones. Though, remembering last time, we need to watch the burning situation. Those tortillas go up  fast . You’re right. Remember that plume of smoke billowing out the window? The neighbour did look a bit concerned. Honestly! It was just a rogue tortilla. Anyway, I’m going to get the marinade sorted. Did you see Brenda posted that video of her niece doing a Scottish accent? Ridiculous. Oh, I did! It was dreadful, wasn't it? Like she was trying to impersonate Sean Connery after swallowing a bag of gravel. Exactly! And Brenda’s commenting 'So cute!' Like it's a skill. Honestly, Facebook... A breeding ground for misguided enthusiasm and questionable accents. Still, it's a good source of distraction, isn’t it? Want me to start chopping the peppers? I’m quite good at that, you know. Speed chopping. Please do. I’ll just check if I have any of that lime and coriander perfume spray I was making. Need a little spritz while the kitchen’s smelling of chorizo. Adds a bit of… zing. Zing indeed. You and your homemade perfumes. What’s the latest concoction? Is it floral this week? It’s actually got a hint of sandalwood. Trying to get that sophisticated, mysterious vibe. Like a secret garden. Right, a secret garden filled with spicy chicken and burning tortillas. Sounds… vibrant. Exactly! More vibrant than anything you’ll find on Facebook, that’s for sure. Oh, and I picked up some lilies on the way back from the shops. Thought they’d brighten the place up. Lilies are lovely. Put them in the fireplace, will you? It'll look nice once we get the fire going tonight. It’s getting a bit chilly. Good idea. I’ll do that after the chopping. Do you think we should invite Sarah and Ben over? It's been ages since we properly chatted. I’d love that. Give Sarah a ring, she’s always up for fajitas. Just warn her about the potential tortilla fire hazard. Will do. Right, peppers it is then? And I'll start on the chicken marinade. Feeling pretty organised tonight. You always are.

It’s lovely to finally meet you both, really. ANON tells me such wonderful things. The pleasure's all ours, dear. We'd been looking forward to this. Your accent is… quite refined. I can't quite place it. Almondsbury, Gloucestershire, actually. Rather tucked away. It’s… subtle. And you? You sound like you hail from up North, don't you? Aye, that's right. Sheffield lass through and through. You can’t lose that. Manchester boy myself. Spent my working life in and around the city. A bit of a whirlwind, the business world. I was a company director, you know, dealing in… well, all sorts, really. A lot of travel involved. Oh, fascinating! I was an EFL teacher for many years. Though, mostly abroad. Never really stayed put. Did a stint in Australia, actually. Queensland. Australia! Lovely. I fancy going myself one day. What was it like teaching out there? Wonderful, really. The climate, the people… vibrant. Though teaching business English to a group of men who thought a suit was a formal shirt and jeans… that took some getting used to. They all looked like they’d stepped out of a 1970s catalogue! Businessmen's fashion can be a perplexing thing. Even here. All those dark grey suits! It's a uniform, isn’t it? Aye, it is. Everything's a bit… bland, isn't it? Back home, even in the city, you’d see a bit of colour. A good Yorkshire tweed, maybe. Not just navy and grey. It’s true. You realize how… Southern everything gets. Everything’s a bit proper and restrained. Even the way people speak. Well, down here, we consider ourselves rather sophisticated, you know. Sophisticated doesn’t always equal genuine, love. I’ve met plenty of Southern types who couldn’t tell a proper pasty from a pancake. Oh, I quite agree. Speaking of genuine, you wouldn't believe the amount of people I met over there asking for bank loans. Apparently, if you hold a degree you can get just about anything, you know. Really? That's quite something. Were they academic degrees or...? I’m wishing I had kept track of all the words my Gran used to say. Had she been down here she'd have been a champion at teaching blokes to don’t be daft. How lovely! Aye! It’s just grand, isn’t it, the way words fitted together back then.

This is lovely, isn’t it? So much better than I expected from a vegan place. Poland surprised me, honestly. Yeah, it’s brilliant. I wasn’t sure what to expect either, to be honest. Everything’s really accessible, even for us fussy eaters. So, you were saying something about TikTok earlier? Oh yes, the absolute abyss. I finally caved and downloaded it. I feel like I’ve wasted three hours of my life already. It’s just… relentless. Tell me about it! I’m trying to limit myself, I really am. It’s so addictive, the algorithm knows exactly what you want to see before  you  do. I did fall down a rabbit hole of miniature schnauzer grooming tips the other day. Seriously. Miniature schnauzer grooming! Oh, that's wonderful. See, that’s the horrifying thing – you start innocently enough, maybe looking for a decent recipe, and suddenly you’re watching ten videos on dog haircuts. Precisely! It's designed that way. What did you find yourself sucked into? Besides the endless dance challenges, obviously. Actually, oddly enough, it was people restoring old furniture. Very satisfying, very calming after the initial barrage of… everything. But then, after that, I ended up watching a woman detailing every single item in her pantry. Oh, the pantry people! Those are intense. I saw one the other day, the woman had  colour-coded  her spices. Colour-coded! I’m just shoving everything in a jar and hoping for the best. Exactly! It’s a level of organisation I can’t even comprehend. Are you still listening to that true crime podcast you were raving about? ‘Darknet Diaries’? Absolutely! It’s brilliant, isn’t it? The latest one was about a hacking group targeting hospitals. Properly chilling. Have you found anything good to listen to lately? Anything that isn't about miniature schnauzers or spice racks? Not quite. I downloaded a couple of those history podcasts – the ones about Roman Britain. Surprisingly engaging. It’s nice to learn something, even if it’s while wiping down the kitchen counter. Have you seen anything decent on TV recently? Apart from documentaries on schnauzer grooming, of course. No, not much. I tried to get into that new series everyone’s talking about on BBC, ‘Rain Dogs’, but it's a bit… niche for me, I think. Too much shouting. I prefer something a bit more slice-of-life.

Right, Pippy, Leo, swimming bags are packed, aren’t they? We're going to the pool this afternoon – excited? Yes! Splish splash! Will there be noodles? Yes, darling, there will be noodles. And floats! Pippy, make sure Leo doesn’t try and swallow the noodles again, okay? Remember what happened last time? He tried to eat it! It was funny! It tasted like rubber! Exactly! Rubber. Anyway, after swimming, ANON’s coming over. You’re both really looking forward to that, aren’t you? She’s bringing her toys! ANON! She's got that sparkly unicorn! And the dinosaur! The big one! Yes, you love the dinosaur. And guess what, Pippy? ANON’s mum said we might be able to go and see her Travelling Circus next month! A circus?! Really?! Really! We need to check ticket prices, but isn't that exciting? Although, we should probably finish your Blue Peter badges first. Blue Peter? Yes! You need to send in your drawing, Pippy, to get your badge. Remember we talked about it? We need a really good one. Do you want help thinking of what to draw? A rainbow! With a unicorn! That’s wonderful, sweetheart! Maybe we can take a photo for it, too? And maybe Leo can be in it! Although... have you remembered your passport, darling? What's a passport? Well, if we ever go on holiday abroad, we need a passport to prove who we are. It has your photo on it, see? Like a very official picture. We'll get there eventually, won't we? When will I be old enough for a passport? Oh, you're old enough already, darling! But it's more fun when you're a bit older, to go travelling. You are getting so big though. How old are you again? Five! Almost six! You are! My clever boy. So, you know, while we’re on the subject of silly things… did you hear what Mrs. Davies was saying at school yesterday? About families in China? No… Apparently, they eat… well, some people do… very old eggs! Ewwww! Old eggs? Like, really old? Apparently they are prepared very specifically, so they don’t taste too bad, and they’re very nutritious, but it’s still quite a strange thought, isn't it? We’ll stick to sandwiches, thank you very much! Right, come on you two, let’s get those swimming costumes on!

Speaker_1 :   Right, honestly, I need to ask you something. And promise you won’t laugh?   Speaker_2 :   Course not, love. What is it? You look a bit stressed.      It’s just… I’ve never properly talked to anyone about this, and I’m feeling a bit silly. It's about… well, my boyfriend, Liam.      Okay… and? Don't be nervous, you know you can tell me anything.      It’s just... things haven't been right, you know? Sexually. He’s not, like,  not  into me or anything. We still cuddle and stuff. But the actual… you know… doing it... it’s just changed. It's been a few months, and it feels wrong. Or just… off. Like he’s not really  there .      I’m sorry to hear that, Chloe. That must be confusing and upsetting. Has he said anything about it?      Nothing! That's the thing. He just… doesn’t seem to have as much… enthusiasm. And sometimes… it’s difficult for him, you know? He’s said he gets tired easily. And it's not always comfortable, which is weird because he’s always been… pretty good at all that.      It sounds like there might be something going on. Physically, maybe. Or… emotionally, too, I suppose.      That’s what I keep thinking. I googled it – which I know is dumb, but I did – and some of the stuff came up about, like… erectile dysfunction.      Yeah, it can be a symptom of a lot of things, actually. Stress, anxiety, physical health issues… sometimes even just underlying relationship stuff. It doesn't necessarily mean anything drastic.      I know, I know. But it's just… awkward to talk about. I don't want to upset him, or make him feel bad, but I also can't keep pretending everything’s alright. I feel like I'm walking on eggshells.      You're right to feel that way. Silence is always worse. Maybe you could try and bring it up gently? Say you’ve noticed things feel different, and you’re concerned. Maybe ask him if he's been feeling alright, not specifically about sex at first, just generally.      Easier said than done! I’m rubbish at being assertive. I always worry about overreacting.      Just be honest. You can say something like, "Hey, Liam, I’ve noticed lately that things have felt a bit… different between us. I just want to make sure you're okay, and that we're both happy."

Right, so I’m thinking cauliflower cheese with a roast. Proper Sunday dinner vibes. Ooh, that sounds amazing! Are we doing Quorn or…? I was thinking Quorn. They've really upped their game at Sainsbury's, haven't they? The sausages are actually decent now. Seriously! I was just thinking that. I tried their burgers last week and they weren’t bad at all. It feels like they’ve actually listened to the feedback. Definitely. Much better than that weird grey stuff they used to do. Okay, cauliflower cheese… how are we being Slimming World with that? Loads of cauliflower is a Healthy Extra, obviously. We can use a low-fat cheese or something… and maybe a tiny bit of Frylight? Frylight is a lifesaver, isn't it? Though I swear it lets off a weird smell sometimes. It does! Like melted plastic. But it's worth it just to avoid using proper oil. Speaking of which, did you get those double peas out the freezer yet? Nearly! Oh, and I need to check my Syns allowance. I had a digestive biscuit earlier and didn’t record it! Disaster. Don’t worry about one biscuit. It's not going to derail your entire week. What are you having with your tea? Thinking about a little pot of custard, with zero calorie syrup. I know, artificial, but… it’s a treat, isn’t it? I'm tempted by a hot chocolate later. But I need to be good. It’s treat day Saturday, remember? We need to stock up on the decent stuff. True, true. We should check Lidl for some nice chocolate. They’ve got some good bargains. Always. Should we look at that veg box thing again? I keep forgetting to do it. It's supposed to save money, right? Apparently. But it ends up being just loads of kale and butternut squash. Okay, fair point. Actually, I saw a recipe for a spiced butternut squash soup the other day… could be good with some chilli flakes. Speaking of spice, did you get that new spice mix I showed you? The one with the smoked paprika? Oh yeah! It’s brilliant. I put it on everything now. Even on the Quorn. See? You're embracing the healthy life. How’s work going? Still hitting those targets? Trying! It's always hectic. Mrs. Peterson keeps complaining about the pharmacist being "unfriendly."

Right, so I was looking at flights to Greece again. Santorini still seems dreamy, doesn't it? Those white houses cascading down… It does. Though remember last time we said Santorini? It was rammed full of stag dos and Instagram influencers. Maybe somewhere a little… quieter? You're probably right. Maybe Crete? I saw a beautiful villa inland, near Chania. Olive groves and all that. Away from the crowds. Crete sounds excellent. We could actually  relax  there. No need to fight for a sunbed. Think about it – morning coffee on the terrace, a swim, wandering into the local town… Exactly! And learning a few Greek phrases. I’ve been downloading Duolingo again. Though, honestly, I’m terrible at languages. You're not terrible! You picked up enough Italian to order gelato without needing a phrasebook last year. That was desperate measures, driven by a profound love of gelato. But seriously, imagine – just the two of us, a long table laden with local food, the sun setting over the Aegean… What would be your perfect day on Crete? Hmm… Well, waking up without an alarm is essential. Then a proper, slow breakfast. No rushing. And a hike. Something with a view. Somewhere we can feel truly away from everything. No emails, no deadlines… See, you're getting romantic now. I’d want a pottery class - I've always fancied having a go at making a bowl. It wouldn't be pretty, but it would be  mine . It'd probably look like something a toddler made. But that’s the charm! Right. Hypothetical time. Let’s say... we win the lottery. A proper, life-changing amount. What do you do? Oh, don't even. I’d quit my job immediately, obviously. And pay off the mortgage. Then... I’d finally finish that novel I’ve been outlining for years. No pressure, just pure writing time. See, there's the sensible side coming out. I'd buy a small vineyard in Tuscany. Just me, the grapes, and a very grumpy Italian winemaker. You and a vineyard. Classic. You'd also be perpetually covered in mud and complaining about the weather. Precisely! And you’d be visiting from your Tuscan writing retreat, complaining that I haven’t made you enough wine. Fair point. Okay, new hypothetical. You can get any tattoo, anywhere on your body. No regrets. What are you choosing? Oh, easy. A tiny, stylized owl on my wrist.

So, the weather’s finally taking a turn for the better, isn’t it? Absolutely glorious out today. Aye, it is, isn't it? Though I still wouldn't trust it entirely. Could be back to frost by Tuesday. Typical April. Did you see that postcard from you and Sarah? The Isle of Skye looked stunning. Ah, yes. Glad you liked it. The scenery was just breathtaking, really. We took so many photos, it’s a wonder we could carry them all back. I bet. Mountains and lochs… it’s a proper showstopper, that place. I’ve always wanted to go. Might have to put it on the list for next year. You absolutely should. We’d happily go again. Sarah’s already looking at dates. Anyway, speaking of schedules, have you given any thought to Michael’s birthday? It’s coming up fast. Aye, I have. I was thinking of taking him out for a proper pub lunch this Saturday. Somewhere with a good Sunday roast, you know, the works. Sounds lovely. He’d appreciate that. So, what about the arrangements for the following weekend? Is Olivia still keen on that pottery class? She is. Booked her in, actually. It's Saturday morning, ten o'clock. I booked a table at that Italian place she likes for lunch after, as a little treat. Good thinking. Olivia deserves a treat, she’s been working incredibly hard lately. Though, goodness knows what she’ll come up with from that pottery class – probably something abstract and vaguely unsettling. Likely. She does have rather…  unique  artistic vision. But that’s what makes it fun, isn’t it? It’s not about perfection, it's about letting loose. Absolutely. Though, I must confess, I’m still utterly baffled by that vase she made last year. It looked like a melted snowman. I know! But she was ever so proud of it. Said it represented “the ephemeral nature of existence.” Right. Well, I’ll stick to admiring her enthusiasm rather than questioning the artistry. Did you catch that interview with Sturgeon last night? About the independence vote? Aye, I did. Gets right up your nose, doesn’t it? All that talk of another referendum. It’s disruptive, to say the least. The country's got enough issues as it is. I quite agree. I think it's a divisive issue and frankly, stirring up trouble when we have so much else to deal with is a bit irresponsible, wouldn’t you say?

Okay, so we're going to draw a chair today, right? A really, really sturdy chair. A sparkly one! A sparkly chair is lovely, darling. But these chairs are for people who don't have anywhere to sit, remember? They're for the refugees from Syria. We need to make them strong so they can sit properly and feel safe. Chair. Yes, a chair! See, you're getting it. Now, what kind of chair do you think is best? What chairs do you have at school, Leo? The ones with lots of legs. And you can wiggle! You can wiggle! Good point. So, a four-legged chair then? Or maybe a five-legged chair, like a starfish! . See? Stable! My chair at home is swivelly! And has arms! A swivelly chair with arms – that's a really good idea! It's comfy, isn't it? But maybe too fancy for our refugee chairs. We want something simple and strong. Like a wooden one. Like your Grandpa’s old armchair. Grandpa's chair is big. I can hide in it! It  is  big! And it’s very safe. This chair can be safe too. Safe and strong. . Now, what colour are we going to make it? Brown! Like wood! Good thinking! Brown it is. Now, Leo, can you help me draw the legs? Lots of strong, straight legs. Legs! Wonderful! See, you’re brilliant at drawing legs. . Oh my goodness, I need to remember to mark those spelling tests this weekend. Mr. Davies is really cracking down on them this term, isn't he? Are you going to test me today? Not today, sweetie. Today we're helping people! This is a more important test. A test of kindness. It's about thinking of people who need help, and trying to do something, even if it’s just drawing a chair. Chair! It is a chair! A very colourful chair! You know, sometimes I wish school lessons could be like drawing. Creative and fun, and don’t involve writing loads of tests! Can we draw a sparkly chair  after  the brown chairs? Absolutely. Once we've finished the chairs for Syria, we can make a whole room full of sparkly, swivelly, comfy chairs just for us. Deal? Now, back to the legs, Leo. We need to make this chair really, really solid. Imagine someone who’s travelled a long way, needing a place to rest.

Right, so I was chatting to Chloe after my seminar today. She’s still completely frazzled by little Leo. Apparently, he’s decided sleep is optional. Poor Chloe. Leo was always a spirited one, wasn't he? Remember when he used to fling pureed carrots at everyone? Vividly. And she was trying to explain, mid-sentence, how she’d fallen asleep upright in the supermarket aisle with a basket full of nappies. It was classic Chloe. Sounds about right. Being a mum is exhausting. How's teaching going, anyway? Apart from the Leo anecdotes? It’s alright, busy as ever. The second years are really struggling with the postmodernism module, though. I think they're just completely overwhelmed by it all. It is a beast. I remember nearly weeping trying to get my head around it. Did you manage to get through to any of them? I tried. I did that little activity with the deconstructed novels, but... I don't think it landed. I might need to rethink my approach. Maybe try showing them some examples of its influence in popular culture? Like, the meta-humour in Deadpool? That’s actually a brilliant idea! I’ll definitely give that a go. Right, speaking of popular culture, have you heard anything from Liam and Sarah? Not recently. I saw on Instagram that Sarah’s been doing yoga retreats in the Cotswolds. Looks amazing, but probably obscenely expensive. Exactly! I wonder if they're actually enjoying it, or if they're just posting for the 'gram. Probably a bit of both, to be honest. I hope they're okay. They seemed a bit stressed before they left. Anything work-related? Probably. Liam’s always under pressure at the firm. He mentioned something about a big promotion he was hoping for. Oh yeah, the senior partner position? That's a lot of responsibility. Exactly. I told him to remember to breathe. Honestly, sometimes it feels like we’re all just running on empty. Tell me about it. Right, I'm making tea. Do you want Earl Grey or something stronger? You look like you need something stronger. Definitely stronger. Maybe a generous dash of something Scottish? Then I can face those postmodernism essays with renewed vigour. Coming right up. And maybe we should call Chloe later? See if she needs any emergency chocolate delivered. Or childcare. Just saying. That’s a really good idea!

Did you see that scarecrow? Honestly, it looked like it was trying to do a stand-up routine. All awkward limbs and a vacant stare. It really did! It was almost… funny, in a tragically British sort of way. Like a very low-budget, rural David Baddiel. Exactly! You know, it reminded me of that time I tried to tell a joke at Professor Davies’ retirement dinner. Complete disaster. The silence was deafening. Oh, the one about the quantum physicist and the pigeon? I’d almost forgotten about that. You looked like you wanted the floor to swallow you whole. I did! I genuinely did. It was mortifying. I’m still convinced some of the junior lecturers are secretly plotting my downfall because of it. Superstition, you know. They probably think it jinxed my chances for promotion. Don’t be ridiculous. People are just… people. Though, speaking of superstition, did Mrs. Hawthorne actually leave a horseshoe above her door because she thought it would ward off University inspectors? Absolutely. Apparently, she’d overheard one of the cleaners talking about how vital it was to keep a ‘good vibe’ when they came around for the accreditation. She honestly believed it would make the paperwork disappear! Bless her. She was always a bit… imaginative, wasn't she? Though I do wonder why she never worried about policemen seeing it. Inviting bad luck, that's what it is. You’re turning into your mother! Suddenly obsessed with warding off police officers and bad omens. Hey, my mother was sensible! Besides, have you seen the local press lately? They’re running stories about every minor incident - a dropped bin, a slightly overgrown hedge… They’re desperate for content. It's ridiculous, isn’t it? All that publicity over nothing. It’s like they’re actively trying to make the village look like a crumbling relic. Exactly. Which is ironic, considering they're also pushing for it to be a “boutique heritage destination.” Makes no sense. So, no holiday to the Greek Islands then? You looked pretty keen on that brochure the other day. I was! But the thought of spending a week arguing with travel agents, battling for sunbeds, and enduring overpriced tavernas… no, thank you. This is lovely. Fresh air, peace and quiet. Plus, I've got that chapter on Victorian comedic theatre to finish. Right, back to work then. The glamorous life of an academic.

Dad, have you seen my phone anywhere? I swear I had it a minute ago. Nope, haven't touched it, love. Probably left it in your room, like always. You know you need to get a charger that actually works, by the way. That one you’ve got is practically useless. I know, I know! I’m going to get a new one soon. It’s just… everything’s so much simpler when you don’t have a phone to worry about, isn't it? Remember when we used to just rely on landlines and calling cards? Simpler, yes. But also a bit slower. I can't imagine how you'd organise anything without all that modern tech. Though I still don’t get this TikTok business. Seems a waste of time to me. It can be, yeah. But it’s good for keeping up with friends. Speaking of which, have you thought any more about helping me move? Well, I've been thinking. That new flat is a bit of a trek, isn't it? I'm not as sprightly as I used to be. We’ll definitely need a van. Have you looked at hiring one? I’ve had a quick look online. Loads of options, but they're all quite pricey.
