I was thinking maybe we could persuade Uncle George to lend us his. George’s van? That old thing? Last time I saw that, it was making a noise like a dying walrus. Are you sure it’s roadworthy? Fine, you're right. We'll need to hire one then. I was looking at some with a tail lift. That would make moving the furniture much easier. A tail lift, eh? Fancy. Reminds me of when I went to the Great Dorset Steam Fair a few years back. Amazing things they had there, all those old engines and machinery with lifts. It was really something. I’ve always wanted to go! We should try and make it next year. Could be nice. Though it's a bit far. I’d rather just go fishing down at the coast. Been meaning to get out there more, you know? The weather's been alright lately. You have been quiet. You still playing those computer games? Well, you know me, have to have a hobby! I was just playing that old version of SimCity. It's pretty good. SimCity? Really?

Honestly, I’m fuming about the library. Did you see the notice? They want to demolish it and put up luxury flats. Saw it online, yeah. Ridiculous, isn't it? That building's got character. It’s one of the few remaining examples of decent architecture in this area. Exactly! And it’s always been such a hub for the community. Kids’ story time, author talks, my mum used to take me there… it’s more than just books. The council’s clearly lost the plot. Land value’s all they care about, isn’t it? Don’t seem to value anything else. And the flats they're proposing… all glass and steel. Utterly soulless. They never bother to maintain the facade of anything. Remember that beautiful Victorian shop on Elm Street? Gone, within a month. Don't remind me. Razed to the ground for yet another chain coffee shop. It's horrifying, really. I was thinking about signing the petition online. Have you seen it? Yeah, signed it. Not sure how much good it will do, though. The council’s already made up their mind, I reckon. Still, worth a shot. I’ve also been looking at some upholstery fabrics online. For the armchair, remember? The one we've been putting off. Oh, right. Still undecided then? I thought you’d narrowed it down. I have, but everything’s either too beige or too flashy. I want something that's durable, comfortable, and… well, doesn’t scream “look at me.” Sensible. I was thinking a dark blue might be nice, or even a dark green. Something classic. I’ve seen a few in a muted teal that I quite like, but I need to see them in person. Online colours are so deceptive. True. You should order some samples. I was reading in the paper this morning about some local fabric shops. Apparently, 'The Cloth House' on Albion Road has a good selection. Really? I didn't know that. I'll have a look online. Do you think they deliver? Saves me trekking across town. Let me see.  taps on his tablet  Yep, they do. Free delivery over £50. Perfect. Speaking of newspapers, have you seen anything about the planning application for that new office block near the river? Vaguely. Something about it blocking the view, wasn’t it? Exactly. It’s an ugly, modern design. Doesn’t fit in with the surrounding area at all.

Right, so, Chloe, are you still obsessed with that Arctic Monkeys album? Oh my god, Dad! It's not an obsession, it's a  lifestyle . It's, like, the soundtrack to my entire life right now. Seriously, I've listened to it like seventy times this week. Seventy times? You'll wear it out! It’s digital, El! It doesn't wear out! Remember when we all argued over music in the car like this? When you were a teenager, Chloe? Everything was either Avril Lavigne or gut-wrenching emo stuff. Oh, shut up, Uncle Dave. Things have evolved. This is  sophisticated  music. Sophisticated enough to warrant a gift certificate for new headphones? I noticed you were a bit… exasperated with yours yesterday. Seriously?! Dad, you’re the best! So, like, what budget are we talking? Don't get too carried away, Chloe. Remember you already have three pairs. One’s broken, one’s at the gym, and one's… decorative. They're versatile. Decorative headphones. That’s a new one. So, El, what are you editing these days? Still book reviews? Yeah, mostly. Just finished a pretty brutal review of a fantasy novel – way too much world-building, not enough plot. It was painful. Honestly, sometimes I wonder why I do it. Well, someone has to tell the truth. Don’t burn yourself out, though. Any hobbies outside of inflicting literary judgement? I’ve been trying to get back into painting, actually. Remember those watercolour landscapes I used to do? Oh yeah! The ones that looked like slightly muddy versions of the Cotswolds. Very funny. It’s a work in progress. I need to find some time. What about you, Uncle Dave? Still building miniature railway sets? Absolutely. Just finished a new section, actually. A little village station. It’s surprisingly therapeutic. Keeps me out of trouble, you know? Keeps the wife happy too. Glad to hear it. Speaking of keeping things calm, I was thinking of finally subscribing to that nature documentary channel. BBC Earth, I think it's called? Ooh, good idea! We could all watch it together. Agreement. Less scrolling, more David Attenborough. Sounds like a plan. Chloe, any particular shows you’re obsessed with at the moment? Besides, you know… the Arctic Monkeys. Okay, so  Severance  on Apple TV is mind-blowing. Seriously, you have to watch it. It’s got a really weird… vibe. But in a good way.

Right then, so let's have a proper look at these insurance quotes for the Fiesta. It’s getting on a bit now, isn't it? Yeah, but it’s a good little car, isn't it, Mum? Still gets me everywhere. Aye, it does, love. Reliable as anything. But you're 17 now, and insurance is... well, it's a beast of a thing. Did you have a look at the comparison websites like I asked? Yeah, I did. There's loads of ‘em. Confused.com, GoCompare… loads. Some of them were really cheap. Cheap isn’t always best, though, is it? We need to look at the excess, the cover... does it include breakdown assistance? That's important, especially in winter. I saw one that was like, £60 a month. Sounded good, but then when I read the small print, it was only third party, fire and theft. Exactly. That’s not enough. You need third party, fire, theft, and at least basic protection for your own vehicle as well, don’t you? Especially with the state of some of the roads around here. True. So, what about this one here? Admiral. It’s £95 a month, fully comp, zero excess. Zero excess? That’s… that’s a bit eyebrow-raising, isn’t it? Let’s have a good look at the reviews for Admiral. What do other people say about their claims process? Seems pretty good, actually. Mostly fives and fours. People say they’re quick to pay out, but a bit strict on the paperwork. Strict paperwork, eh? Right, that's something to bear in mind. We’ll need to make sure you keep everything organised. And how many miles a week do you reckon you’ll be doing? Probably around 60, Mum. School, football, seeing my mates... you know. 60 miles a week. Okay. And are you driving home every day? No, some days I get a lift with Liam or Jamie. Good. Because artificially inflating the mileage can get you into trouble. The insurance companies are clever, you know. They’ll spot it. So, this is the best one then? £95 a month. Not necessarily. Let's just double-check this one from Direct Line. It’s £105, fully comp with a £300 excess. £300 excess? That’s a lot. Aye, it is. But Direct Line’s reputation is solid.

Jaysus, this week has been something else. The project deadline’s looming and Gareth from accounts is driving me up the wall. Keeps coming in with these… well, let's just say ‘novel’ interpretations of the data. Sounds stressful, Dad. Like, really stressful. It is, love. He’s putting a lot of pressure on. I’ve been tracking my stress levels – used one of those apps on my phone, you know? The one that asks how you're feeling and analyses your sleep patterns. Apparently, I'm chronically stressed. Chronically stressed is putting it mildly. I think my windpipe's permanently constricted. Your what? He means he’s tense, darling. Remember what we talked about? How words can mean different things? Exactly. Right, so, shifting gears… did yous see the news about the vote? About the marriage equality thing? Absolutely incredible, wasn't it? Such a landmark decision for Ireland. So heartening. Yeah, it’s great. My history teacher said it was really important for equality. It is. Shows we're finally catching up with the rest of the world. Though, I’ll admit, there was an awkward silence at work yesterday after the results came in. Everyone just… avoiding eye contact, you know? That’s so typical. People are afraid of saying the wrong thing. Dad, are we being recorded? What? No, why would we be? I just… saw a light flicker. It's probably just the dodgy wiring, love. This house is older than Methuselah. Remember that podcast I was telling you about, Liam? The one on non-verbal communication? The one where they talk about facial expressions conveying more than words? Yeah, I remember. Made me think about Gareth. His facial expressions… questionable. You are a card. Speaking of questionable, anyone fancy a Chinese takeaway tonight? I'm craving something spicy. Yes! Can we get the chicken curry? The chicken in that curry from Golden Dragon is always a bit… chewy, isn't it? Never quite right. Should’ve gone for the beef. You always complain about the chicken, Liam. Just eat it and be grateful. Alright, alright. Just saying. It’s a pet peeve. You know, something else that stresses me out. Speaking of stress, did you guys see  Suicide Squad ? No. Is it good? It was… okay. A bit all over the place. Lot of yelling, lots of explosions. I think I’m getting desensitized to that sort of thing.

Look at that hawk, Mum! Proper big it is. Wonder where it's heading. Aye, lovely to see them out and about. Could be heading down to the reservoirs, they're always about there. You’d think they’d be bothered by the planes going over though, wouldn't you? Planes are way louder, Mum. Hawks are pretty quiet. Quite right. Though I do find the noise pollution from aircraft disturbing. Seems to get worse every year, doesn’t it? Reminds me of when I was working in Guildford – non-stop flights. Not the same as a lovely, quiet hilltop village like we’re heading towards. Speaking of quiet, Dad, are you ever going to tell me what you thought about my Law Conversion course application? Been ages. Oh, yes. Very good, very good. Solid choice, Fiona. Challenging, but good. You've always been a sharp one. He’s been reading up on it, love. All about contract law and torts. He was going on about liability and negligence last night. Please don't, Mum. Sounds awful. It’s interesting, Liam, trust me! So, I’m thinking… grams versus kilograms, miles versus kilometres…it's all a bit confusing when you're used to one system and suddenly having to work with another. It's like the whole EU referendum debate all over again! A classic case of unnecessary complication, wouldn’t you say? We should’ve stuck with what we knew. Simple as that. Don't start that again, David. We’ve had that argument a thousand times. Can we talk about something else?! Like, did you see Man City last night? Proper good game. Liam, this is a family road trip! Manners, please. Mum, did you hear about that new supermarket opening near Chorley? Apparently, it’s got a  massive  car park. Oh, I read about that. They're building it on what used to be farmland. Shame, really. Remember how Terry Wogan used to talk about protecting the countryside? A bygone era. Progress, as they say. Though I have to say, I'm not fond of the way parking fees are soaring. Absolute rip-off. Tell me about it! Last time I was in London, I paid more for parking than a night in a decent hotel. It’s ridiculous. It makes you wonder about the current state of society. Can we listen to music now? Please? Anything but another debate about supermarkets or parking fees.

Honestly, I’m having a bit of a crisis about dinner. It’s lovely, but… I’m still wrestling with this whole vegetarian thing. Crisis? What kind of crisis? The lentil shepherd's pie is objectively delicious. I know, I know, it is! It’s just… I was reading about cultured meat, you know, ‘shmeat’ or whatever they’re calling it. And it’s weirdly tempting. Like, if we could just  grow  meat without harming animals… It’s still a really strange concept, isn't it? Like, giving up the farm entirely. The whole ecosystem of agriculture. But isn't the ecosystem of intensive farming arguably  worse ? The animal suffering alone… Exactly! That’s what I’m struggling with. Abattoirs are horrific. Hunting is awful. But the idea of… like, a giant vat of cells creating a steak? It feels… dystopian. It’s Curb Your Enthusiasm territory. Larry would be convinced it's inherently unclean. Oh, absolutely. He'd be finding some obscure kashrut issue with it. "It’s not  derived  from an animal, therefore it's not kosher!" But if it solves the problem of animal cruelty, surely it's worth exploring? Even if it feels a little… unnatural. What about the environmental impact of it though? It wouldn't just be sunshine and rainbows, would it? Growing all that protein needs a lot of energy. True. It’s not a magic bullet, that’s for sure. But the greenhouse gas emissions from livestock are insane. Maybe, eventually, cultured meat could be a more sustainable option. Still, it feels a long way off. I’m taking a Vitamin B12 supplement now, obviously. Just to be safe. But sometimes I just miss a really good burger. You could try Beyond Meat or Impossible Burger. They’re not perfect, but they’re a step in the right direction. Honestly, I think the ethical issues go beyond just eating meat. It’s about oppression, in all its forms. How we treat animals, how we treat each other... It's all connected, isn’t it? Like, the way we’re destroying the environment is linked to our consumption habits, and that’s linked to… well, everything. It’s a depressing thought sometimes. It is. But that’s why we need to keep talking about it, trying to find solutions. And eating ridiculously good lentil shepherd’s pie, of course. You are right! This is fantastic.

This film's mental, isn’t it? Absolutely bonkers. It's alright. Bit predictable though, isn't it? You can see where it's going. Predictable is good sometimes, ya know? You want a bit of comfort watching a film. Not everything needs to be some mind-bending sci-fi epic. True, true. Just wish the special effects were a bit better. Look at that CGI dragon! It looks like it’s made of cardboard. It really does! Remember that time Dad tried to build a dragon for the Christmas play? Oh, God, yes! It was mostly tinfoil and hope. And it collapsed halfway through the performance. Classic Dad. Speaking of Christmas, have you lot started thinking about presents yet? Nah, not really. Too early, innit? I’ll probably just order something off Amazon closer to the time. Amazon’s got everything, doesn’t it? I spent three hours on there last night looking for a new phone case. Ended up spending £25 on one with a sparkly unicorn on it. A sparkly unicorn? Seriously? Hey, I like unicorns! Don’t judge. Anyway, what are  you  getting up to? Still searching for jobs? Nah, not today. Got a bit bored, to be honest. Been looking at flights to Barcelona. Barcelona! That’s brilliant. When were you thinking? Sometime next year, maybe summer. Just browsing for now. Need to save up a bit first. It’s pricey, isn’t it? Everything is these days. I’m trying to budget better. University’s draining all my money. Tell me about it! Student loans are a nightmare. I'm considering a part-time job at Christmas. Good shout. Maybe at that new cafe in town? Looks busy. Yeah, that's not a bad idea. You'd do well there, Beth. You're good with people. Thanks, Liam. You should probably get yourself a job too. Keeps you out of trouble, doesn't it? Alright, alright. I'll add it to the list. After Barcelona, naturally. Always with the Barcelona! You're obsessed! It’s got good tapas! And the architecture. You know I like architecture. You like  pictures  of architecture. You’d get bored after five minutes of actually looking at buildings. Don't be ridiculous. Anyway, have you seen that new game, 'Echo Bloom'? Everyone's talking about it. I’ve heard of it! Beth’s been telling me all about it.

Honestly, this alumni thing is exhausting. Four days of small talk about departmental funding… I need a holiday. Tell me about it! I swear, Professor Davies cornered me for fifteen minutes about the new phonology paper I’m helping with. Like, I appreciate his enthusiasm, but I'm just taking notes, not revolutionizing the field! You’re so diplomatic. I would have just mumbled something about needing to find the coffee and made a rapid exit. So, any exciting holiday plans to escape all this? I’m hoping to go to Iceland! I’ve been saving up for ages. Seeing the Northern Lights has been a lifelong dream. What about you? Anywhere you're eyeing up? Iceland sounds incredible! I'm thinking of a road trip through Italy, actually. Been wanting to explore Tuscany for years. Proper pasta and sunshine. Though my mum is already pinging me with recommendations for tiny, obscure medieval villages I "have to" visit. Oh, mums. Always the best travel agents, aren't they? Mine’s obsessed with Bruges. Says it's like stepping back in time. I swear, she's trying to convince me to elope there. Bruges is lovely, though. A bit…chocolate-box, maybe? Does your family get much opportunity to travel, anyway? Your dad works so hard. He does. It’s tough. He tries to take us somewhere every other year, mainly to Scotland. He’s a massive history buff, you know. Castles and battlefields are our forte. Last year it was Culloden. Depressing, but fascinating. My family’s a bit more scattered. My sister’s living in Australia, remember? It’s been brilliant for her, she seems genuinely happy, but it’s a long flight to visit. I miss her. I bet! It must be strange, having such a big distance between you all. It’s nice having everyone relatively close, even with my dad dragging us to Hadrian's Wall. Speaking of family, how’s your grandma doing? I saw a picture of her on Facebook the other day, looking very sprightly. She’s fantastic, actually! She's taken up pottery! Can you believe it? She's making these really quirky little sculptures. Says it keeps her mind busy. She’s surprisingly good. Keeps threatening to open her own shop. That’s wonderful! Maybe she needs you to manage her marketing. You're the expert, after all. Tempting, but I think I'll stick with phonology for now!

Honestly, I’m absolutely beat. This essay on Wuthering Heights is killing me. You’re moaning about Wuthering Heights? I’m wading through Kant’s Critique of Pure Reason! Try deciphering  that  after a night out. Okay, fair point. Kant sounds properly draining. But Cathy's obsession is just… so much. It’s exhausting just  reading  about it. You’re a softie, you are. It’s classic gothic melodrama. Embrace the angst. Easy for you to say, Mr. Postgraduate. You’re probably got a well-oiled academic brain that thrives on torment. Is that all I am to you? A well-oiled, angst-thriving academic? Shut up! Seriously though, I feel like I’m going to be staring at that blasted moor for another week. How’s your lecture prep going? Still feeling confident about that seminar on post-structuralism? Yeah, pretty good actually. I think the students will like it. I’ve got some interesting visuals this time – some old album covers, a bit of Deleuze and Guattari… trying to make it relatable, you know? Sounds intense. You need a massage after all that brain-bending. You reckon? My shoulders are a bit tight. You’d be willing to inflict your amateur massage skills on me again? Amateur? I’ll have you know I’ve been practicing! And yes, I would be  delighted  to. You’ve got that stressed-out student look about you. Only if you promise not to use the elbow technique again. That nearly sent me into early retirement. I thought it was quite effective! It released all the tension right out of your neck. It released a scream out of my throat, more like. Okay, okay, no elbows. Deal. When are you free? Later, after I’ve wrestled with Heathcliff and his brooding. Maybe around seven? I need to at least make a start on the conclusion. Sounds good. And maybe after the massage, we can order something proper. All this Kant and Wuthering Heights makes a girl hungry. Definitely. Pizza? With extra cheese? You read my mind. Right, academic struggles aside, priorities: pizza and a much-needed shoulder rub. Exactly. Come on, lemme get back to Cathy. Wish me luck. Good luck. Just don't let her consume you entirely. And don’t forget, Kant awaits… just kidding! Go get 'em. You're terrible. Bye. Bye, love. Don't let Heathcliff get you! Don't let Heathcliff get me...

This lentil soup is amazing, Mum. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Oh, stop it, love. It's just a simple recipe - my mum’s actually. Always made a big pot of it on cold days. Simple, yes, but delicious. You've got a gift, Margaret, you really do. I’ve never been much of a cook, as you know. Dad, you could boil an egg and somehow manage to set off the smoke alarm. I resent that! I’ve mastered… toast. That's your peak culinary achievement. So, has anyone seen the news today? Dreadful stuff coming out of Calais again. It’s heartbreaking, isn't it? These families… desperate to reach safety. I just don’t see how we can turn our backs. It's a terrible situation. These poor people. But the government’s got to control the borders, you know. Can’t just let anyone in. But Dad, they’re fleeing war, persecution… isn't there some humanity we can extend? Of course there is, love. But where do you draw the line? Resources are finite, you know. We have our own problems here. Honestly, it's all so overwhelming. I’m trying to focus on my class tomorrow. Little Toby keeps asking about it, bless him. He's a sensitive soul. He is. Has he been alright since his football injury? Mostly. Still a bit grumpy about not being able to play. But he's a trooper. Your sister called, by the way. She said the house viewing went well. Really? That's brilliant news! Where are we with the move then? She’s hoping to put in an offer next week. It’s all moving so fast. Good for her and Mark. A fresh start. That's what they need. I'm going to miss her terribly, though. It’ll be quiet around here without her. We’ll visit often, darling. And you’ll be over here every Sunday for lunch, naturally. Absolutely. And I’ll finally learn to make something other than toast. Maybe. Don't tempt fate, Dad. So, Mum, what’s on the agenda for next weekend? We need to sort out a date for that family get-together. Let me check my diary… How about Saturday the 27th? Everyone should be free then. That works perfectly. Shall we book the pub? The Red Lion’s always good. Red Lion’s fine. Anything with a decent pint of bitter is fine by me.

Right, David. You wouldn’t  believe  the trouble I’m having with the bathroom. Absolute nightmare. Oh aye? What’s the bother then, Idris? Another leaky pipe? You always were a dab hand at fixing those in your Cairo days, weren't you? Before all this academic nonsense took over. Cairo was different. Simple plumbing. This is… Victorian. The pipes are ancient, the walls are crumbling, and frankly, the entire layout is just ridiculous. I’m thinking of completely redoing it. A full reno, is it? That’ll cost you a pretty penny. My daughter, Sarah, just finished her kitchen. Spent a fortune, she did. But it looks lovely, all modern and sleek. Used a firm in Cardiff – recommended them highly. I've been getting quotes, and you're right. Eye-watering. It's horrifying, really. Problem is, finding a decent tradesperson is like finding a unicorn. Everyone’s either booked solid for six months, or wants to charge you the earth, or doesn’t seem to know what they're doing. Tell me about it! Tried to get someone in to fix a bit of wobbly skirting board last year, and they quoted me three hundred quid! Three hundred quid for half an hour’s work. I ended up doing it myself. Barely finished it though, I must confess. My hands aren’t what they used to be. Trust me, I understand. I'm leaning towards just patching it up for now. Though my wife, Eleanor, she’s envisioning marble floors and a rainfall shower head. The woman has  ideas . Women do, don’t they? My wife, Gwen, she’s convinced that grey is the only colour to paint the house. Everything’s grey now. Grey walls, grey carpets, grey curtains… it feels like living in a cloud. I can imagine. Eleanor’s leaning towards a very pale green. "Sage," she calls it. It’ll be lovely, apparently. I just hope it doesn't clash with the tiles. You know, I saw old Gwyneth Pritchard the other day. Remember her, from the Classics department? Distinctly. A formidable woman. Still lecturing, I heard. Aye, still going strong. She’s redoing her entire home – Edwardian farmhouse, she has now. Massive project. Apparently, she's having a bespoke kitchen made. Hand-painted cabinetry and a marble island. The works. Gwyneth, eh? Always had expensive taste. Must be living comfortably. She always did. Says she inherited a small fortune from a distant uncle.

That was a brilliant curry, wasn’t it? Proper vindaloo. Bit of a kick, even for me. It was lovely, Liam. Really hit the spot. Though, I’m still not sure why you had to add  quite  so much chili. My mouth is practically on fire. It was alright. A bit spicy. I don't think I’ve ever tasted anything that hot before. Goo! He seems to approve. See? Even the experts agree. It’s gotta have a bit of bite, you know? Keeps you awake. Speaking of which, anyone fancy a wee dram? Liam! It’s barely 7:30! And you just had a glass of wine with dinner. Just a small one, Sarah. To aid digestion. And just to chat, really. It’s been dreary today, needs a bit of warmth. Can I have a sip? Pleeease? Absolutely not, Finn. You're 14, not 40. Besides, you’d probably develop superpowers from it. Super-sensitivity to spice. Imagine melting enemies with a single burp. Honestly, Liam. You and your superpowers. Remember when Finn swallowed a paperclip last year and you convinced him he was attracting metal? Yeah! I thought I could feel it moving around! I was worried I was going to explode! It was a classic. Doc said it would pass. Said you had a remarkably strong digestive system, all things considered. He just said it was a freak occurrence. And to keep an eye on you. I wish I  could  swallow metal. That would be a cool superpower. Right. What about…we were talking about the park event tomorrow? Midsummer festivities, they're calling it. I'm still not convinced it's a good idea. Little ones everywhere, loads of people... plus, I’m still feeling a bit overwhelmed by everything. It'll be fun, love. There's face-painting, games, maybe a little music. Finn would love it, wouldn’t you? Yeah! Can we go on the bouncy castle? Please? The bouncy castle. Of course. And then you’ll whine about your legs aching for a week. He’ll be fine. We’ll take it easy. I was thinking maybe pop down the night deposit box before we go. Just to be safe with a few notes. Why do you need a night deposit box? You have online banking. Old habits die hard, Sarah. Some things are just more…reassuring. Plus, I had a thought about putting some pictures of Finn in there from when he was a little baby.

Right then, Halloween’s coming up, isn't it? Always a bit of a kerfuffle with the youngsters. It is, Arthur. Though I must say, these days it’s not like it used to be. Less trick or treating, more elaborate costumes and parties. Aye, it's changed a fair bit. Back in my day, it was just knocking on doors for sweets and hoping you got a Mars Bar. Now it’s professionally made outfits and scary houses. Keeps the parents busy, mind. Mum! Did you see that TikTok? There’s this haunted maze someone built in their garden! It looks amazing! A haunted maze in a garden? Goodness me. It sounds like a lot of work. Effort, that’s what it is. All this…effort. Remember when we just had a pumpkin or two carved on the doorstep? Simple times. Those brownies were delicious, David. Seriously, you need to get her recipe. I've asked her a hundred times, Carol! She just smiles mysteriously and says, "A woman's secret." Classic Janice. Right, so, Christmas plans… any brilliant ideas yet? Or are we just going to repeat last year’s chaos? Last year was a  moment . Aunt Maureen and Uncle Barry arguing over the stuffing… the turkey nearly burned. Maureen’s always been particular about the stuffing. Has to be sage and onion, nothing else. And Barry will argue that sausage meat is essential. Remember when he nearly had a shouting match with poor little Lily over it? Oh god, yes. We need a Christmas mediator this year. Maybe we should just go somewhere. Somewhere warm. Like… Spain? Spain? In December? It'll be teeming with other tourists. I was thinking more somewhere a bit… quieter. Cornwall, maybe? We could rent a cottage. Cornwall does sound nice. Somewhere we can walk the dogs without fighting over parking spaces. What do you think, Chloe? Cornwall sounds good. But I'd still love Spain. I want sunshine! Actually, I was looking at flights to Barcelona the other day… ridiculously cheap. Cheap flights sound tempting, but what about the dogs? They wouldn’t be happy caged up in an apartment. That’s a good point. We always feel guilty leaving them. Perhaps Cornwall and we can take them to the beach. I’d like that. Fresh air, a nice walk… and I’m in desperate need of a proper break. This trainee nurse practitioner course is  exhausting . It is, Carol. You're juggling so much. And you're still doing extra shifts at the hospital. Someone has to pick up the slack. It's stressful, but I'm enjoying the extra responsibility. Although, the pay isn’t exactly fantastic… Don’t even mention money! I’m trying to save for that new camera lens. It's ridiculously expensive. Which lens is it? The one you were drooling over at that photography shop last week?

This coffee is lovely, isn't it? Much better than I expected from an instant. ANON does put a lot of effort into things - she’s a proper hostess. Been here long? Just a few weeks, actually. Needed a break from the Dorset rain. Bit of sunshine, you know? Though, I must say, even the sun here feels different – somehow softer. It's a different light altogether. Been coming here for... goodness, must be fifteen years now. First time was on a whim, honestly. Really? What drew you in? Well, I’d heard about the prices, naturally. But it wasn't just that. There was something… peaceful about the photos I saw. A quiet kind of beauty. Tired of the grey of England, if you know what I mean. I completely understand. I was starting to feel like a damp dog myself, back home. So, what are your favourite things to do here? Besides enjoying excellent coffee, of course. Always happy to enjoy excellent coffee. I like to walk along the coast, mostly. There are some lovely little villages tucked away up in the Kyrenia Mountains too. Been exploring a bit each year, discovering new corners. Found a delightful little bakery in Lapta last summer. Their simit is to die for. Simit? I'll have to look for it. I’ve been trying to acclimatize to the food. It’s a bit different. It is! A bit heavier, in general. But fresh, and mostly very good. Have you tried the kleftiko? Slow-roasted lamb… divine. I haven’t! I’ll add that to my list. Anything you  don’t  recommend? Any tourist traps to avoid? Well, there's that casino in Girne. Don’t go in there unless you fancy losing your shirt. And the harbour front… can be a bit overpriced. You get better restaurants a few streets back. Good to know. I've been trying to find somewhere authentic to eat… somewhere the locals go. Ask ANON. She's got all the inside tips. She's lived here for years, hasn't she? Though she'll probably try to convince you to eat only her cooking! I'm willing to risk it. Have you ever been up to Bellapais Abbey? The views are incredible. Oh, yes. Went there last week, actually. Beautiful spot. Bit windy, though. Nearly blew my hat off! You know, you must see the Salamis ruins near Famagusta – incredible history there.

Honestly, you’d think they’d do something about this smog. It’s thicker than pea soup today. Feels like it too. My throat’s a bit scratchy already. Did you manage to finish marking those essays? Almost. Just the last three, and they were… surprisingly insightful. One student actually made a really interesting point about the influence of classical Chinese poetry on modern protest songs. Seriously? That’s brilliant. Maybe you should mention that in your next lecture. I struggled to get any engagement on that topic last week. I will. It’s things like that which remind me why I bother, you know? The little sparks of originality. Did you hear back from Amelia about the conference in Shanghai? Not yet, but she said she'd let me know. I’m really hoping she can make it. It would be a shame to miss that keynote speaker. It would. And it’s good practice opportunity for the students too. They need to start thinking about presenting their research. Absolutely. Speaking of students, David was asking about your feedback on his dissertation proposal. He seemed a little anxious. Oh, yes. I gave him some pretty detailed suggestions. He needs to tighten up his methodology, I think. But I told him it had potential, definitely. He just needs to put in the work. He’s a bright lad. He just needs a bit of… nudging, perhaps. Are we seeing Fiona and Mark this weekend? We are. Fiona said they’re having that barbeque they mentioned last month. I told her to brace herself for my questionable grilling skills. You’ll be fine! Just don’t burn the burgers again. Remember last time? The fire alarm went off. Don’t remind me! It was embarrassing. But the kids loved it. Screaming and running around… a proper chaotic barbeque. It was memorable, that’s for sure. I’m glad we have friends like them, though. It’s good to have some normalcy, you know? Especially here. Sometimes it just feels… overwhelming. I know what you mean. The scale of everything is just… breathtaking. And the pollution doesn’t help. I wonder if they'll ever get a proper handle on it. I hope so. For the kids’ sake, if nothing else. It's got to be better for them. Here, let me get the door. Nearly home. Just wishing every day on the train was less like breathing through fog.

Right, nearly there. Just need to get these peppers done. What do you think, Mark? Enough chillies? I’ve been a bit heavy-handed, haven't I? Hmm, a few. But good. Bit of a kick is always welcome. How was your day, love? Busy on the ward again? You have no idea. Absolute chaos. Mrs. Henderson kept wandering off, and young Liam decided to stage a protest about his mashed potatoes. Honestly, some days… Sounds…intense. Did you hear back from that agency, Mum? The one for the copywriting gig? Not yet, darling. They said they'd be in touch this week. Don't get your hopes up too much though, you know how these things are. Don’t listen to your mum, Chloe. You’re brilliant. They’ll be lucky to have you. Right, this chicken needs a good marinade. Chloe, can you grab the soy sauce from the cupboard? Sure. Oh, look! Another picture from the beach last summer. Remember how sandy everyone got? Oh, absolutely. Mark looked like a walking sandcastle. Nearly lost a shoe! Hey! I was strategically placing myself for optimal sunbathing. And besides, that picture made it into your slideshow, didn’t it? It did, yes. And it was a good one. Speaking of pictures, did you manage to sort those photos from Dad’s birthday? The ones on your phone? Almost. I’ve got them backed up, just need to put them into an album. I was thinking of printing a few and getting them framed. What do you think? That’s a lovely idea, darling. Really nice. We could put them in the hallway, next to the others. Sounds good to me. So, Chloe, anything exciting happening with your writing? Working on anything interesting? Actually, yeah. I’m doing a campaign for a new sustainable coffee brand. Lots of research, which I enjoy. It's got to resonate, you know? Connect with people. That sounds fascinating. You always were good at making things sound appealing. Remember that school project you did on Egyptian hieroglyphs? You convinced everyone they were modern art! Oh gosh, don’t remind me! I’m pretty sure the teacher was baffled. Right, this is looking promising. So, lunch tomorrow… did you want to go back to that Italian place in town, Sarah? Yes, please. I’m craving pasta. And that lovely tiramisu. Ooh, count me in! But can we watch something good afterwards?

Honestly, this new bus route is a joke, isn’t it? I’ve been trying to get to the station this week after work and it's just a complete shambles. They’ve changed the timings and the route seems to loop around unnecessarily. Aye, I’ve heard that. Sarah from work was moaning about it too. She lives near Chesterton Road and says it’s added an extra twenty minutes to her journey. It's worse than the old route, definitely. Twenty minutes! That’s ridiculous. And the buses are always packed. I ended up standing the whole way last night, felt like a sardine. Tell me about it. You’d think Cambridge University Press would have a decent bus route to their bookshop, wouldn’t you? I went in yesterday looking for a new dictionary and ended up trekking for ages. You went to the bookshop? Did you get the dictionary? I did! Eventually. They had a good sale on. But the journey was proper exhausting. It just feels like they haven’t thought things through properly. No, completely. It's just… frustrating, especially living here. You’d expect better planning. Speaking of frustrating, did you see that student protester on the news about the tuition fees? Vaguely. Something about a sit-in at the Old Divinity School, wasn't it? Aye, he was proper passionate. Clambered onto a statue and was shouting about the rise in fees and everything. Brave lad. Brave, or reckless? I mean, I sympathise with the cause, absolutely. But getting arrested isn’t exactly the most effective way to change things, is it? Maybe not, but it got people talking. It’s about raising awareness, isn’t it? What do you think about all this university comparison stuff, anyway? People keep asking me about Durham versus Cambridge. Oh, right. What are you saying? People always assume Cambridge is just automatically superior, you know? Like, 'Oh, you went to Durham? That's nice… but… Cambridge!' It's a bit silly, isn't it? I can see why you'd feel that way. Durham's a fantastic university. The collegiate system, the beautiful architecture… it's got a lot going for it. It does, aye. It’s got a really strong sense of community. Cambridge is… well, it’s Cambridge. Grand buildings, brilliant academics, but it can feel a bit impersonal sometimes. That’s a fair point.

Honestly, the scallops were divine. Absolutely divine. I haven't tasted scallops like that since… well, since my mother used to make them back in Dublin, I suppose. They did look gorgeous, didn't they? I'm so glad we finally managed to get out. It feels like ages since we've had a proper girls' lunch. Agreed. Work has been absolutely manic. The new redundancy packages are proving… complicated, to say the least. Oh, dear. That sounds stressful, love. You always were the strong one, dealing with all that paperwork. Speaking of complicated, how’s Liam coping with the move to Cumbria? Still missing Manchester, I imagine? He is, a bit. He complains about the lack of decent curry houses, you know. But he’s starting to appreciate the peace and quiet. And the walks. He’s been doing a bit of bird watching, of all things. Bird watching? Liam? That's a new one. Is he actually enjoying it? He says it's surprisingly relaxing. And he insists he spotted a rare goldcrest the other day. I’m not entirely convinced, mind you. He’s always had a theatrical flair. Sounds like him. So, any news from Ben? Is the visit still on for next weekend? He’s confirmed it! He’s booked a train up on Saturday morning. I’m actually quite nervous, to be honest. It’s been a while. Oh, darling, don't be silly. It'll be lovely. It's so good he’s making the effort. He’s a good lad, Ben. You’ve done a wonderful job raising him. Thanks, love. I'm just worried about… well, everything. Work, the flat, and suddenly having him around again. It’s a big change. You'll be grand. Remember what I always told you about language? It’s a tool, a bridge. Use it to connect. Talk to him. Really listen. That’s good advice, Mom. You always were a brilliant communicator. Even with those tricky quadratic equations. Don't remind me. I still get a shiver down my spine thinking about coordinates. Oh, you were a whiz at it! You should have become a mathematician. Or a linguist! That’s what you should have done, Mom. You always had such a knack for languages. You used to teach me Irish phrases when I was little. I did, didn’t I? "Dia dhuit" and "Go raibh maith agat."

Honestly, it’s quite lovely here today, isn’t it? Much better than last week’s deluge. You could barely see the river. It is. Though I still think it looks a bit grey. I prefer the Thames when the sun’s reflecting off the water, really sparkling. True, true. Still, better than grey, I suppose. Look, there's the O2 again. It always looks so impressive, even from this distance. It does. Though I can’t fathom why they put that giant inflatable bubble right on the river. Seems a bit… showy, doesn’t it? A bit? It's practically screaming for attention. Not that I mind, it’s a landmark now. Can you imagine what it must have cost to build? Don't even go there. Makes me shudder. You know, I was thinking about how absurd it is that we don't own a car. Absurd? I think it's rather brilliant, actually. Think of the money saved. And the parking! Don’t even get me started on trying to find a space around here. I know, I know. It’s just… logistically tricky sometimes. Especially when we’re trying to get the kids to… well, anywhere. We manage. Public transport works. Mostly. Sometimes. Mostly not, I’d say. Planning our holiday is going to be a nightmare without one. Have you looked at the train fares to Cornwall? Don’t remind me. It’s extortionate! We'll have to look at driving options for others I think. Perhaps hire a car for that leg. That’s a thought. Though the thought of navigating Cornish roads in August fills me with dread. People driving like maniacs. Ah, the joys of holidaying with the family. Speaking of which, did you remember to order those new swimming costumes for the kids? Nearly forgot! I ordered them last night. The little one wanted something with a sparkly unicorn on it. Of course she did. Honestly, I’m trying to get my head around this American cup measurement thing. Someone said a cup is eight fluid ounces. Is that right? I think so. It's all so confusing. We’re still stubbornly clinging to millilitres and grams in this country. It's ridiculous! I was trying to follow a recipe the other day, and it was all cups and tablespoons. I ended up with a completely inedible mess. So, you’re thinking… is free

Honestly, this rain is never ending. I’ve been meaning to go for a swim, but it's just not happening today. Tell me about it! It’s been chucking it down all week. I had to cancel my visit to Mrs. Peterson. She'd been looking forward to me coming round, poor thing. The kids are cooped up too. Leo was bouncing off the walls this morning. I tried to get them both to build something with the Lego, but it ended in a massive argument. Classic. Leo's always got to be the loudest, doesn’t he? Remember when he was little and he'd scream if he didn't get the blue crayon? Oh god, don't remind me! Or the whole 'Build a Bear' phase. He insisted on having, like, ten. Each one meticulously named and with a backstory. My granddaughter, Maisie, is obsessed with hers too. She’s got a whole army of them. I keep thinking I should suggest she donates a few to charity. Maybe. I'm finding sorting through my stuff a nightmare. I need to clear out some old clothes, but I keep getting distracted. My phone keeps buzzing with notifications! You and me both. I’m constantly battling the urge to check Instagram. Though Leo has been asking for a new game, so mum guilt is setting in. Speaking of kids, how did Lily's sports day go? Did you manage to go? I did! It was hilarious. She tripped during the egg and spoon race – completely face-planted. But she laughed it off and carried on. Proper little trooper. Bless her. Leo would have cried for hours. He's so dramatic sometimes. Remember when he was potty training? A single drop of water on the floor and the whole house went into lockdown. Potty training is a trial, isn’t it? My grandson gave me a run for my money. Refused to use anything but the big toilet and insisted on climbing up the step stool himself. It’s like they're determined to make our lives difficult sometimes! I’m thinking about getting a new slow cooker. Mine's on its last legs. Do you have one? I do! It's a lifesaver. Especially on days like this when you just want something warm and comforting with minimal effort. I've got one too. Makes a lovely soup. I've been trying to get Maisie to eat more vegetables, so I sneak them into the soup.

Right, so let’s actually nail down some goals for the next six months, while we're out here. Feels a bit ridiculous setting goals while we’re house-sitting in paradise, but… you know. Gotta keep the engine ticking over. I agree. Paradise can be a bit of a distraction. More of a gentle inertia than a productive environment. What were you thinking? Business-wise, I mean. Well, the obvious one is launching the new online course. I need to get that finalized and marketed. I was thinking a phased release, starting with the introductory modules. Aim for, let’s say, 50 sign-ups in the first month. Is that achievable? Fifty? I think so, assuming the marketing is solid. We’ll need to monitor the conversion rates closely. Have you done any pre-launch engagement, built up an email list or anything? A little. I’ve got a landing page going, collecting emails. Not a huge response yet, but… slow and steady, eh? What about you? Any professional development you're keen to pursue? Still thinking about that reflective practice course? Yeah, definitely. It feels really necessary at the moment. I’m feeling a bit…stuck creatively, to be honest. The course could give me some new frameworks to work with, help me re-energise my teaching. I may delay that slightly though. Why delay? Well, I was thinking… what if we combined it with that teachers’ retreat in Bali we were talking about? It would be a bit of a splurge, but we both need to recharge. And Bali's rather beautiful, as I recall. Bali… now you’re talking. That’s a brilliant idea! Combining professional development with a proper holiday. Okay, let's put that on the pile - revised timescale for Bali. What about friends? Any plans to connect with Sarah and Mark whilst we're here? I’ve messaged Sarah, she said they're heading up to the Whitsundays next week. We could maybe fly up and meet them? A few days on Hamilton Island? That sounds fantastic! I’ll reach out to Mark and coordinate. It could be a good opportunity to brainstorm some ideas too, catch up properly. It’s been too long. It has. And what about the family planning conversation? Are we any closer to, you know, actually having that conversation with Mum and Dad? Not really. They're still on that "wait and see" phase, aren't they?

Honestly, I can’t beat a Poacher on a Friday, can I? Proper classic. Aye, it is decent. Best chips in Warrington, no arguments. Though I still reckon that service station near Preston does a better bacon butty. You always say that, Liam! Every single time. It’s just… predictable. Like, we  know  you’re gonna bring up the Preston service station. It's true though. Their bacon’s thick. Right, let’s not start a service station debate. Anyone fancy another round? Yeah, I’m good. So, did you hear about Sarah? Sarah from uni? What’s she been up to? Last I heard she was trying to catch 'em all in Japan. Still at it with the Pokémon? Apparently, she got into a proper scrap in a café in Kyoto. Over a Pikachu figurine! No way! What happened? Apparently, some bloke tried to snatch it from her. She went full fight-or-flight, apparently. Apparently, she launched a cup of matcha latte at him. A matcha latte? That's a very polite fight. Proper Yorkshire lass response. Gentle aggression. Classic Sarah. Always the most dramatic one. Remember when she tried to camp in the park for Glasto tickets and got chased off by the police? Oh my god, yes! That was a disaster. She was so convinced she was going to get in. She’s got a lot of faith, that Sarah. Good on her, though, for standing up for her Pikachu. Right, but her mum's fuming. Apparently, she’s had to send a formal apology to the café. She’s convinced it’s ruined Sarah’s chances of a job in Japan. A formal apology? Foot and ankle! Who apologises for standing up for a Pikachu? She’s just following her mum's orders I bet. My mum would’ve made me write a five-page essay about the importance of good manners. My Grandma would’ve said, "Just give 'em a good thump if they try and steal your Pokémon!” Typical. Anyone else getting that craving for After Eights? It’s ridiculous how much I want one. I do! My nan always had a box. Proper posh Christmas treat. My Fitbit’s going ballistic, I’ve barely moved all day. It’s telling me I need to go for a run. Tell your Fitbit to shut up and order another pint. Speaking of, anyone need anything from the shop?

This bread's lovely, isn’t it? Proper crusty. Reminds me of Mrs. Pettigrew’s bakery down the road when I were a boy. Used to get a pennyworth of crusts, you know. Good value. It is good. Mum really outdid herself with this roast, didn't she, Dad? I’m glad you think so, dear. It’s got to be something special after all the effort. Though I do wish Colin hadn’t insisted on that blasted football on the telly during the gravy making. Gave me a right fright, nearly dropped the whole lot! It was a good game, though! Absolutely brilliant last-minute goal. You missed it, love! Football. Hmph. Can’t stand the noise. All that shouting and running about. Give me a nice game of cricket any day. Proper sport. Dad, you haven't watched cricket since 1987! Times have changed. Don’t you start, pet. Times were better then, you know. Solid values. Proper trousers. Not these ripped things the youngsters wear now. Shocking. He’s cracking on again, isn't he? Always. Dad, we were talking about the roast. Speaking of which, what about that party, dear? Have you finalised the decorations? I’ve ordered the balloons, but are we doing banners? I’ve got the banners sorted, Mum. They'll be here tomorrow. And I've booked that DJ you like. Good! It's going to be a great party. Any thoughts on the playlist yet? Don’t want anything too…avant-garde. I’ve put together a list of stuff that everyone will enjoy. A bit of 80s, some classic 90s... 80s? Awful decade for music. All that synthesized rubbish. Give me Vera Lynn any day. Oh, Arthur. You're incorrigible. You’ll be dancing with Vera Lynn on the floor, I bet. You know, there’s a documentary on this week about the political landscape of the 1980s. Might be up your street, Dad. Lots of talk about the miners' strikes. Miners’ strikes. That’s all they ever talked about back then, wasn’t it? Causing trouble. Dad, please. Not politics over dinner. We’re supposed to be relaxing. She's right, dear. Let’s talk about something pleasant. Did you read that article about the new nature reserve they're planning out near Wroxham? I did! It sounds fantastic. A real boost for the local area. It’s good to see some investment in the countryside.

Honestly, I don’t know what to do, Liv. I keep thinking about just… leaving. Leaving? Like, dropping out? Seriously, Elsie? What's brought this on? You were buzzing last week about that seminar. I know, I know! It  was  good, but then I just… started thinking. Thinking about, like, everything. All the money, the pressure, the lectures…it’s just a lot, innit? It is a lot. Uni’s a massive jump. But you’ve only been here a few months. Everyone has moments of doubt. Remember when I nearly packed it in after the first week? Just because I couldn’t find the library. Yeah, you were lost for hours! But this feels different. It's not just being lost. It's a… a fundamental question of whether I even  want  this. Alright, deep breaths. Tell me properly. What’s making you feel this way? Is it the course itself? Are you struggling? No, the course is fine. I’m alright with the work, I think. It's just… feeling so far from home. Everything. And remembering… remember how Mum always said I’d be happy selling seashells on the beach? I’ve always secretly thought she might be right. Your mum's a dreamer, Elsie. But you’re not! You're smart, you're capable… you’ve always been good at things. Remember when you built that amazing sandcastle at Polzeath? It was like a fortress! It did collapse pretty quickly though, didn’t it? The tide just… swamped it. Doesn't mean it wasn’t brilliant while it lasted. Look, about being far from home... it’s proper tough. I miss Scouse accents and chippies something awful. But you can’t let that dictate your future. But my name… it's a bit odd, isn't it? Elsie May. My Gran's name. Everyone here just stares. They think it's some sort of joke. Elsie May's a  lovely  name. It's classic. Reminds me of those old Hollywood actresses! My nan had a slightly bonkers name too. Remember I told you about Doreen Bernadette? Briefly. You said your dad almost had a heart attack when he told her to do the washing up. Exactly! And she'd just give him this look and say, "Bernadette doesn't do washing up, love." It's about embracing it. Own your Elsie May-ness! It’s unique. Easier said than done when you’re covered in mud from walking back from the library in the rain, and your shoes are practically falling apart.

Honestly, this risotto is  divine . I’m so glad we finally made it here. It's been ages! Tell me about it! Life's been absolutely manic, hasn't it? But so worth it to finally catch up. This is gorgeous, though. Seriously, I could eat a mountain of this. Right? I kept seeing pictures on Instagram and just  had  to try it. So, marketing exec life - how’s Pearson treating you? Still battling endless spreadsheets? You have no idea. Spreadsheets are my nemesis. But it’s been…interesting. We’re doing a huge campaign launch next month for their education resources, which is pretty stressful, but also a decent opportunity. Lots of late nights fuelled by copious amounts of coffee. Sounds intense. I remember you saying you wanted to get into that sort of strategic stuff. Is it what you expected? Kind of, yeah. The strategy side is brilliant, I love that. It’s the internal politics that’s a bit of a headache. You know how it is. Oh God, tell me about it. Project management – everyone thinks they're a project manager. It’s infuriating! I swear, half the meetings I’m in are just people arguing about things I’ve already documented. You too, huh? Honestly, sometimes I feel like I’m just a glorified fire-fighter. Exactly! So, speaking of life and stress…anything happening in the romance department? Still seeing Liam? No, actually. We broke up a couple of months ago. It was amicable, thankfully. Just... not working. We wanted different things. Oh, no! I’m so sorry to hear that. You seemed really into him. We were. But you know, sometimes it just doesn’t last. I’m actually kind of relieved, to be honest. It was starting to feel a bit…stale. I’m focusing on work and seeing friends. Dating apps are a  nightmare  though. Absolutely. I swore off them after one particularly disastrous date involving a man who brought his mother. Oh. My. God. That’s…wow. I know! So, what are you thinking long-term? Like, beyond spreadsheets and disastrous dates. Any travel plans? I've actually started looking into doing some volunteering abroad next year. Maybe Southeast Asia or South America. Something totally different. Wow, that’s amazing! Seriously, you should do it. You deserve a break. I'm thinking of booking a trip to Italy next Spring, just to recharge.

Right then, love, have a look at this. I’ve been having a proper nosey on eBay. What is it, Gran? More antique teacups? Not this time, lad. Found a proper bargain. A vintage Star Wars action figure. Luke Skywalker, mint condition, still in the box. Seriously? How much? Those go for loads! Seventeen quid! Seventeen pounds, can you believe it? I nearly fell off my chair. Seventeen quid? Wow. That’s a good deal. Amazon would be double that, easy. Exactly! That’s why I prefer eBay, sometimes. You just have to snoop about a bit. Amazon’s all sleek and convenient, but you’re paying for that convenience, aren't ya? Yeah, it’s like they know you’re in a hurry and they hike the prices up. They do, don’t they? It's proper cynical, it is. Remember when you wanted those new trainers last year? Nearly broke the bank on Amazon. Oh god, yeah. I ended up waiting ages for them too. Then someone posted the exact same ones on eBay for half the price. Told you! I said have a look on eBay first. I know, I know. You were right, as always. I just liked the look of Amazon's website. It’s all fancy and… organised. Organised, aye. But is it worth paying double for? You can find nearly anything on eBay these days, can’t you? Even things I’d never think to look for. Like what? Oh, I don’t know. Last week I saw a bloke selling a collection of rusty bottle caps. Seriously! Really? Who buys that? Don’t ask me! Someone did. It had loads of bids on it. People are daft, aren’t they? Some are. But there are good deals to be had if you know where to look. I got that guitar pedal I wanted for a steal on eBay. See? You’re getting the hang of it. You just need patience. Can’t rush it. It's like a treasure hunt. A digital treasure hunt. What are you looking for now? Thought I'd have a look for a replacement handle for this old suitcase. The leather’s split on it right down the middle. Let me see… "Vintage Suitcase Handle, Leather, Replacement…" Loads of them. Aye, loads. Now, which one looks the most sturdy… and the best value for money, of course. Can't be throwing money about.

This coffee's rather nice, actually. Strong, just how I like it. Glad you think so, Dad. I tried a new blend. Ethiopian, apparently. Bit of a gamble, but seems to have paid off. Ethiopian, eh? Sounds a bit fancy for me, usually stick to a builder's brew. But this is… agreeable. Lovely to be out of London for a bit, too. Cambridge is rather charming. It is, isn’t it? Better than sitting in the office, that’s for sure. How was the walk from the station? Did you manage to find that little bakery I mentioned? Oh, the walk was pleasant enough. Bit chilly, though. And the bakery…yes, found it! Lovely little place. Bought a couple of those Eccles cakes you like. Were still warm. Oh, brilliant! You remembered! Thank you. I was hoping you'd find them. I just replaced it two years ago. It  should  still be working. Besides, a new one is the last thing we need right now with all these removal costs piling up. Mum's right. The estimate came in a lot higher than we thought. Those storage units aren’t cheap, especially not the secure ones. Well, you did insist on the secure ones. Can't risk a rogue badger getting into your prize-winning marmalade collection. It's not just the marmalade, Michael! It’s the books too. My first editions. And the antique tea set. Okay, okay. So, about the removals… I’ve been looking at different companies. They all seem to charge an arm and a leg for the packing alone. It's awful, isn't it? They’re all exploiting the situation. Honestly, the way prices have gone up... it’s outrageous. Speaks volumes about the current state of affairs, doesn't it? This whole cost-of-living crisis... Don't even get me started. I was reading about the Labour leadership contest. Seems like they’re all promising the moon, as usual. Well, somebody has to try, doesn’t they? There’s got to be a glimmer of hope. I still cling to that idealism, you know? After all these years of teaching, you can’t lose sight of the possibility of a better world. Idealism? In today's climate? You're a woman of remarkable optimism, Deirdre. Remember when we both believed Blair was going to change everything? Don’t remind me. He promised no more wars and ended up sending us into Iraq. Still, that doesn’t mean we shouldn’t have hope. We have to, don't we? Otherwise, what’s the point? Fair point. I just… I don't know. They all seem so… focused on winning, rather than actually  solving  anything. It's the nature of politics, love. You have to be cynical, or you'll be chewed up and spat out.

This is lovely, Mum. Really needed this catch-up. It feels like ages since we properly talked. It has, darling. Life's been a whirl, hasn't it? Though a pleasant whirl, most of the time. How's teaching going? Still managing to wrangle those youngsters? Wrangling is definitely the word. It's rewarding mostly, but some days…you know. Little Thomas kept trying to eat his own glue stick today. Glue. Stick. Oh, bless him! They are little terrors, aren't they? Still, you're doing such a wonderful job. Giving them a good foundation, that’s important. More important than a fancy degree, I always say. Thanks, Mum. Means a lot coming from you. So, Christmas... any thoughts yet? I'm dreading the shopping. Oh, I've already started! Got a few bits for you and your lovely boy, Leo. And of course, loads for the grandchildren. It’s becoming more and more expensive every year, isn’t it? Tell me about it! I’m trying to be sensible, but Leo’s got his beady little eyes on that remote-control dinosaur. Oh, the dinosaur. He’ll be roaring around the house like a little T-Rex, won't he? Still, that's what Christmas is for, isn't it? A little bit of chaos and joy. Absolutely. We were thinking of heading to Devon for a few days after Boxing Day. Just escape the madness for a bit. Are you doing anything exciting for the holidays? Just the usual, darling. Family coming and going, a lot of eating, a lot of laughing. I might do a bit of consultancy work over the New Year – a training session for some nurses in Bristol. Pays the bills, doesn’t it? But I'm hoping to carve out some time for reading. I’ve got a pile of books taller than you! You always do! Are you still planning that trip to Italy? You mentioned it a while ago. Oh, yes! That's still on the cards. Thinking of going in April. Rome and Florence. Just a little something for myself, you know? A bit of culture and sunshine. Keeps me young. That sounds amazing! You deserve it. I'm trying to think about career moves myself. I've been thinking about taking on some online teaching. More flexibility, you know, with Leo getting older. That's a good idea, darling.

Honestly, I can’t believe Liam’s still sleeping with his mouth open like that. It’s genuinely offensive. Offensive? That's a bit strong, Rach. But yeah, it's loud. Like a freight train rattling through. I've got earplugs, you know. Gotta. Remember when he tried to deny it? Said it was just the wind! Ellie and I were practically howling with laughter. Wind, my foot! Sounded like a walrus. I’m glad I didn’t stay over at his place last week. I’d have been up all night. I've adapted, honestly. I don't even hear it anymore. It’s just…background noise. Like the hum of the fridge. Adapted? You’re practically living with him! You must be traumatised. Anyway, speaking of ridiculous noises, did you lot try Waterfields’ Eccles cakes yesterday? Did we?! I thought you were taking them home, Rach. I was! Forgot all about them. They were gorgeous though. Proper crusty, not like the soggy ones you get in the supermarkets. Oh my god, Waterfields are the best. I’m having a Richmond sausage roll later, definitely. They do the best sausage rolls, don't they? Waterfields… remind me, do they still do those little iced biscuits? The ones shaped like flowers? My grandma used to get them all the time. They do! Little floral ones, yeah. Proper old-fashioned. They've barely changed in twenty years. My mum’s always going on about Waterfields. Says they’re the only proper bakeries left. Don’t get me started on proper bakeries. Remember Mrs. Higgins' shop in Latchford? Oh god, yes. Greyest bread imaginable. But she made a fantastic Victoria sponge. That was ages ago. Everything's gone all fancy now. Artisan this, handcrafted that… It's true. You can’t even find a decent handkerchief anymore. Everything’s tissues now. My gran used to carry a linen handkerchief, folded perfectly. My nan always had a lace one. Always tucked in her sleeve. Proper posh. Mum's still got a box full of them, from her mum and her grandma. Says she keeps them “just in case.” Just in case what? You're not going to spontaneously need a linen handkerchief, Rach. I don’t know! That’s what she says! She’s got enough to outfit an entire orchestra. It’s just… another thing she cherishes, I suppose. Like those ridiculously tiny teacups.

That was a brilliant weekend, wasn’t it? Honestly, feeling so refreshed. Aye, it were good lass. Proper good. Bit breezy out on the Black Country canals though, weren't it? Thought I was gonna lose me hat a few times. It was! I kept worrying about your cardigan blowing away. Glad you brought that thicker one though, it was chilly later on. Did you manage to get any decent photos of the narrowboats? Oh aye, a few crackers. Got a lovely one of that little blue one with the roses painted on the side. Reminded me of me nan’s garden, that did. Used to have roses just like those. That’s lovely. It's always nice to hear those memories. So, other than nearly losing your hat and reminiscing about your Nan, what was the highlight for you? Well, the fish 'n' chips at the pub by the canal was spot on. Proper thick chips, not those skinny things you get now. And the beer, a decent pint of Banks’s. Can't beat a Banks’s after a walk, can you? Can't argue with that! I really enjoyed the vintage market. Found such a cute little ceramic bird. It's going straight on the windowsill. Did you now? Always got an eye for a bargain, you have. I nearly bought a ridiculous hat, a proper bowler, but thought better of it. What would I have done with a bowler? You’d have rocked it! Seriously. I was thinking about that little craft fair in Shrewsbury next month...fancy going? It’s on a Sunday. Shrewsbury, eh? Aye, I’d fancy that. We could make a day of it. Have a look around the castle and grab a pasty. Should be alright, should. Perfect. I'll check the details and send you a link. Did you hear anything more from the council about that drainage issue at the farm? That was stressing me out a bit. Aye, they said they're bringing a team out next week. Looks like they’re blaming the recent heavy rain for it all. Should sort it out, fingers crossed. Don't want those fields flooded again. Me neither! That would be awful for the crops. Well, all in all, it was a really good weekend. Thank you for bringing me. Don't mention it, love. Always good to get out and about.

Honestly, the marking pile is just… relentless this term. I swear, every time I finish one batch, another three appear. Tell me about it! Year 11 mocks are looming, so the pressure’s really on. It's a constant battle against existential dread and piles of essays. You've summed it up perfectly. At least you’re teaching them, though. I’m just correcting their interpretations of Baudelaire. It’s a bit beyond me sometimes, to be honest. Baudelaire! You're brave. I'm sticking to GCSE Shakespeare. At least I vaguely remember that from my school days. How's your French coming along? You were saying you were trying to brush up. It's… a work in progress. I've been using Duolingo, which is a bit pathetic, I know. But I’m determined to be able to hold a basic conversation before we go to Paris next year. Duolingo's brilliant for vocabulary! I used it to jog my memory for Spanish before that trip to Barcelona. But you need to supplement it with something, don’t you? Maybe a language exchange? There are loads online. That’s a good idea, actually. I’ve been putting it off, thinking it'll be too awkward. Don't be silly! Everyone's nervous. Just pick someone who seems friendly. Have you seen Sarah's Instagram lately? She’s basically a walking, talking baby encyclopedia. Oh goodness, no! I deliberately avoid baby-related content on social media. It just makes me feel… inadequate. Don’t feel that way! It’s amazing, isn’t it? Little Leo is just the cutest. He's started saying 'dada' and 'mama' and driving them mad repeating everything they say. That sounds utterly exhausting. I'm glad I'm not there yet. Although… teaching teenagers can be pretty challenging in its own way. True. They've got opinions on everything, don't they? Although, I do love seeing them making progress. It’s the small victories, isn’t it? Like when someone finally understands a really tricky concept. Absolutely. That little spark of understanding... it's the best part of the job. Are you thinking of doing any CPD this year? I saw a really interesting course on differentiation. Actually, I was. I'm feeling a bit stale with my current teaching strategies. Differentiation is definitely something I need to focus on. Do you know if it’s good value?

Blimey, look at that. Right full of 'em. Chaps are practically queuing. Aye, they are. Cheeky little beggars, aren't they? Always after a bit of seed. Remember that winter of '78, eh? Barely a bird to be seen. Oh, look! A new one. Right snug it looks. Wonder who built it? Sparrows, I expect. Could be robins. They're getting bolder, you know. Used to be shy as mice, but now they'll practically land on your hand. Not that I'm encouraging it, of course. Got to keep a bit of distance. Aye, distance is key. You don’t want a bird getting too comfortable. Then they start expecting tea and biscuits! You're a pair, you two. Speaking of tea, is that Victoria sponge ready then, Margaret? I'm starting to feel a bit peckish. Nearly, dear. Just putting the finishing touches on it. Dash of icing sugar, bit of lemon zest… makes all the difference. Victoria sponge. Proper cake that is. Nothing like those dreadful sponge things you get in the shops. All air and no substance. Your mother used to make a cracking Victoria sponge, didn't she, Arthur? Light as a feather. And that raspberry jam… She did. Best in Norfolk, I reckon. Although I think this one's rather good myself. Well, it’s not your mother’s, is it? Nothing ever is. Oh, stop being grumpy, Arthur. You’re like an old man already! Speak for yourself, Margaret! I feel as spry as a spring chicken… most days. You need to watch your sugar, you know. With your diabetes… I know, I know. Just a small slice. Doctor says a little bit of cake now and then won't do any harm. As long as I'm keeping an eye on it. And remember what he said about the walking. A bit of gentle exercise every day. It's good for the circulation. Aye, I'm trying. These old legs aren't what they used to be. Remember when young David used to chase me around the garden playing pirates? He was a little terror, that boy. Always causing mischief. He was a sweet boy though. Always brought me little wildflowers. Remember when he used to put on puppet shows for me in the living room? Aye, he did. Used to make 'em out of socks and tea towels. Silly things. But he loved it.

Oh goodness, everything looks delicious. I’m struggling to choose. What are you thinking of, Peter? Hmm. Could be anything really. The kleftiko looks tempting, but I think I’ll go for the grilled octopus. Bit adventurous, you know. You? I think I’ll have the sea bass. It’s always a winner. And some of those grilled vegetables. The waiter seems to smile at me when I compliment the vegetables. Possibly thinks I’m easy. Well, you are a delight, Sarah. Though I’m sure that's not why he smiles. Reminds me of old Mrs. Henderson who used to come in here every Tuesday. Always flirted with the waiters, poor things. Had a chihuahua draped over her shoulder the entire time. Oh, goodness! A chihuahua draped over her shoulder? What a sight! Reminds me of Aunt Margaret and her fluffy white cat, Snowball. That cat truly thought it was a lion. Used to attack Peter’s ankles every Christmas. Don’t remind me. Still have the scars, you know. And speaking of family... did you hear from David about his latest blood test results? He seemed rather vague on the phone. Sadly, yes. He said something about "elevated markers" which, as a teacher, I’m ironically rather well-equipped to interpret as ‘not good’. I’m worried about him, really worried. He never takes anything seriously. Men, eh? Always putting things off. Still, he’s got a good woman in Fiona. She’ll keep him on the straight and narrow. Though I hear he’s been seeing someone else, a yoga instructor. No! Really? I hadn’t heard that. He seemed so content with Fiona. People are so fickle. It’s all a bit bewildering, isn’t it? Like…like destiny or something playing out. Destiny? Hmm. I’m not sure about that, Sarah. I lean more toward… well, I’ve been reading a bit about shamanism lately. Fascinating stuff, you know? About connecting with the earth's energy and all that. Shamanism? Really, Peter? The environmental policy officer? Don't look so surprised! It's all about finding harmony with nature, Sarah. And I’ve got to admit, dowsing has been surprisingly accurate with finding water pipes around the house. Dowsing! You’re pulling my leg! Not at all! My cousin, Brenda, she’s a proper dowsing expert. Found a lost ring for someone just last week. It's all about… well, it’s complicated to explain.

Right, that commute was a nightmare. Seriously, should have left earlier. Oh, you poor thing! Were the trains awful again? You know, I told you to check National Rail before you left. Mum! I did, and it said perfectly fine. Then there was a signal failure near Stevenage. The whole train just… stopped. Everyone was moaning. Signal failure, eh? That's the Midlands way of doing things, love. Always something going wrong. Dad, don't start. So, what have you both been up to? Anything exciting? Just catching up on the school reports, mostly. Examinations season is looming, you know. A right frenzy it gets. Mrs. Davies is having a crisis about the Year 11 maths papers. Oh, bless her! Is she still stressing over those kids? I've been sorting out the accounts for the farm. Tedious, as ever, but important. They’re talking about re-seeding the fields next spring. Costs a fortune though. Sounds it. So, are you still watching the rugby, Dad? Of course! England had a bit of a rough patch, but they’ll pull through. You should come down to the club with me sometime. It's good fun. Maybe. I’m pretty busy at the moment, trying to get this project finished before Christmas. It’s a real beast of a thing. Project Coordinator, is it? That sounds terribly important. Doing anything interesting? It’s… mostly spreadsheets. But there's a big presentation next week. Wish me luck! Spreadsheets, eh? Brings back memories of my university days. Dreadful things. You went to university and you're telling me about spreadsheets? Well, there were plenty of spreadsheets back then too! Though we didn't call them that. We just called them… numbers. He’s terrible with technology, you know. I had to explain to him how to use video calls last month. Poor Dad. Speaking of technology, have you had a chance to look at those quotes for the kitchen renovation yet? I've got a couple. They're not cheap, are they? I think we need to prioritise – new worktops and a decent oven are a must. Well, you deserve it after all these years with that old kitchen. It’s practically falling apart! Definitely. I'm really excited about it, actually. It will make a huge difference to the house. Just imagine having a dishwasher! No more arguments about washing up. True! Speaking of arguments, have you heard from Auntie Carol recently?

Honestly, I can’t believe people fall for it still. Like, a catfish. In 2024. Tell me about it! I saw that documentary, right? The one about those American girls getting catfished by Nigerian princes. Seriously, who falls for that anymore? It’s the desperation, innit? Like, they’re lonely and they’re grasping at anything. A bit of attention, a bit of feeling wanted. Aye, but surely you can spot something’s up. Like, the pictures are always a bit… off. And the stories? They’re wild! "Oh, I'm a doctor but I can't access my money because of government corruption." Right. Exactly! And they’re always asking for money, aren't they? Starts small, like "Can you send me £20 to fix my phone so I can video call?" Then it's "My mum's sick, I need £500 for an operation." My nan got nearly scammed, you know. Some bloke online pretending to be a soldier stationed in Afghanistan. Kept sending her love letters and asking for postage money to send her important documents. Oh no! Did she send him any? Thankfully, my dad clocked it. He said, “Mum, you’re talking to a man you’ve never met, who’s asking you for money for paper? That’s a bit daft, isn’t it?” Good shout from your dad! My mate Liam, he was proper obsessed with this girl he met online. Thought she was a model, living in Italy. Turns out she was a bloke from Wigan. Wow. Wigan? What even…? Yeah! He was gutted. Spent ages sending her money for “photoshop expenses” apparently. Oh, bless him! You know, it always reminds me of Jeremy Kyle. Remember that one, with the woman who was pretending to be pregnant just to get a council house? Oh god, yeah! That was awful. The way she tried to deny it when the DNA test came back. Honestly, the lengths people will go to for a bit of money. It's mental. Do you think they feel bad afterwards? Like, the catfish, I mean. Maybe some do. But I reckon most just move on to the next victim. They get a kick out of messing with people, don't they? Aye, it's gotta be a power thing, right? Controlling someone, pretending to be someone you’re not. Yeah, it's sad really. People are so desperate for connection.

This pasta's really good, Grandma. Thanks! You’re welcome, darling. It’s a simple recipe, but the tomatoes are bursting with flavour - straight from the Italian place down the road. You know I can't resist good tomatoes. Reminds me of Vienna, actually. We used to get such beautiful ones at the market. Vienna? I’ve never been. I'm thinking about going to Paris next year though, if I can save up enough. Paris! Wonderful. You must go. Such a beautiful city. You know, I went there once, ages ago, with your grandfather. We barely spoke a word of French, but we managed somehow. Mostly pointing and smiling, I think. Sounds like a good strategy. I'm trying to learn French, actually. University has a free language course, but it’s a bit…slow. Well, you always were better with languages than I was. I had to learn English, and German of course, but French…always struggled. Still, I picked up enough to order a croissant, which is the most important thing when you're in Paris! Do you know any German? A little. Enough to embarrass myself, mostly. Classics at uni means you pick up bits and pieces, you know? Latin, Greek, bits of German… Classics! How interesting. Your mother always wanted to do Classics, but she said it was too difficult.
