She went into publishing instead. Are you enjoying it? Are you finding it useful? Yeah, it’s brilliant. Challenging, definitely, but brilliant. I'm actually thinking of specialising in Roman history. It's so fascinating. And it helps with understanding the roots of…well, everything, really. That's lovely. Family’s always been a comfort for me. Though I miss your grandfather terribly still. He would have loved to hear about your studies. He was always a champion of learning, even though he didn’t have much formal education himself. Always reading, always asking questions. I miss him too. Hey, I was trying to send you some photos of the bees I saw in Regent’s Park the other day, but my computer is being a nightmare. It keeps freezing. Oh dear. Those modern gadgets! I tell you, they have no sense. I still prefer a good notebook and pen. Much more reliable. I had a problem with my scanner last week, nearly drove me mad. Luckily, Angelo next door helped. He's a whiz with computers.

Honestly, Dad, you were tailgating that lorry! It was terrifying! Relax, love. I keep a good distance. He was driving too slow, that's all. Needed a bit of encouragement. Encouragement? That was bordering on aggressive, Arthur! There's a reason they have following distances, you know. Don’t start, Maggie. I’ve been driving longer than you’ve been alive. I know what I’m doing. And this Sat Nav isn't helping, is it? Keeps trying to send us down single-track lanes. It did that earlier! It wanted us to go through that tiny village with all those speed bumps. I said, “Dad, no way!” Well, it's programmed to find the ‘most scenic route.’ Apparently, scenic means barely passable. Scenic for sheep, maybe. Not for a family in a saloon car. Are you eating something, Elodie? You’re awfully quiet. Just a biscuit, Aunt Maggie. Still a bit stressed about those lorries. And I'm trying to revise, actually. Need to get through this chapter on Victorian literature. It’s so dry. Victorian literature! At a time like this? Shouldn’t you be focusing on, I don't know, defensive driving? Very funny, Dad. Honestly, I'm trying to keep on top of everything. Uni's relentless. And I have that solicitor’s bill to worry about. Oh, dear. How’s that progressing? Has he managed to get anything sorted with your grandmother's estate? It's slow going. Costs are piling up. They keep asking for more information. It's just a headache, really. Should've just got rid of all that stuff years ago. Your grandmother was a hoarder, darling, we all knew that. Still, it’s good to check on insurance, MOT’s. Speaking of, Arthur, when's yours up? You've been putting that off again, haven’t you? Don't nag, Maggie. It’s fine. It’ll pass. Besides, no time. I’ve been trying to get that hideous table fixed. You know, from Aunt Hilda? The one that looks like a shipwreck? Oh, the Mantiques table? You’re still trying to fix that? Trying being the operative word. The wood’s warped, the legs are wonky… It’s a disaster. Needs a craftsman, not me. I’ve got a friend who's quite good with furniture. He builds bespoke shelves, actually. I could ask him. That’d be amazing, Aunt Maggie!

The telly's been full of that chap, you know. The one with the hair. Oh, you mean Piers Morgan? What's he been up to now? Causing a ruckus, I expect. That’s the one. Seems to be saying everyone’s gone soft, hasn't he? Well, he’s always been one for stirring things up, hasn’t he? Never could understand why people bothered with him. Such a fuss over nothing. I did catch a bit of it. Blasted loud, though. Had to turn it down. My ears aren't what they used to be. I’m glad you're taking it easy on them, dear. Remember what the doctor said about the noise levels. I remember. Though sometimes it's hard to avoid it. Especially when the telly voices are shouting at each other. That's the way of it these days, isn't it? Everything's so... aggressive. Remember when the news used to be calm and measured? Aye, I do. A lot more sense to it too. Now it's just a shouting match. All those accents too. Hard to make out what anyone's on about. You always did have a good ear for an accent, didn't you? Remember when we went to Cornwall and you could tell exactly where everyone was from just by listening to them? I’ve always liked listening to people talk. You can learn a lot about a person from the way they speak. That’s true. It’s like a window into their world. Speaking of windows, the cat's been staring out at the robin again. Little blighter's got a real obsession with that bird. He does, doesn't he? Always has. Probably thinks he’s a hunter, the silly thing. More like a furry comedian, if you ask me. Sitting there, twitching his tail… It’s a good laugh, watching him. He keeps us amused, doesn't he? Wouldn’t know what we’d do without him. No, we wouldn't. Where have I put my glasses? Can’t see a thing without them. They're on your head, dear. Always are. Oh, you're right. Silly me. Getting old, you know. Don't you start with that now. You're doing just fine. And besides, a bit of silliness keeps things interesting. Wouldn't want things to get too serious, would we? No, no. Wouldn't want that at all.

This risotto is absolutely gorgeous, you’ve outdone yourself. Seriously, I might have to nick the recipe. Glad you like it! It's a bit fiddly, but worth it. Been listening to anything good lately? I've been obsessed with Fontaines D.C. again. Oh, they're brilliant. I saw them live last year, proper energy. I’ve been on a real indie-folk kick at the moment - Big Thief mostly. Have you heard of them? Big Thief? Ring a bell… vaguely. I'll have to have a listen. Things have been pretty hectic with the thesis. Trying to pull it all together is stressing me out a bit. Tell me about it. Research projects are a beast. Still, at least the weather's finally perked up a bit. You managed to get some more in the garden then? Yeah, a little. Managed to get the tomatoes planted. Though I’m a bit worried about blight, still early days. Did you manage to see Sarah and Mark last weekend? We did! It was lovely. We had a right laugh, mainly spent time moaning about work, as one does. Sarah's still struggling with the new systems at the hospital, it's chaos apparently. Poor her. Sounds awful. They need to sort that out. Mark's training for that marathon, wasn't he? Is he still on track? He is! He's been logging his runs on that fancy app and apparently he's exceeding expectations. He’s completely fanatical about it, honestly. He was telling me all about his carb loading strategy… it was a bit much. Sounds about right for Mark. Dedicated to a fault! I need to be more like that with my studying, less procrastinating on Twitter. Easier said than done! I was thinking, maybe we should try and get together with Sarah and Mark again soon. A proper pub night, not just a quick catch-up. What do you reckon? Definitely. It's been too long. We could try that new place in the city centre, The Golden Lion? Heard good things. Ooh, yes! Good shout. It's getting properly posh around here, isn't it? Still, a bit of treating ourselves now and then is good. The rain’s starting again though, isn’t it? Typical. Yeah, just a bit of drizzle. Nothing like the downpour we had on Monday. Glad we got the tomatoes in before this started.

Honestly, it’s grim, isn’t it? Seeing so many people struggling. My mum’s friend’s son – he’s got a first-class degree, brilliant lad, and he’s been unemployed for nearly six months. That’s awful. The job market's brutal, especially for graduates. I mean, I'm feeling the pressure myself, trying to juggle the PhD and somehow find consultancy work to keep afloat. Tell me about it. The debt's piling up, isn't it? University fees… it’s ridiculous. You're basically paying a fortune to be saddled with debt for the rest of your life. It is. I sometimes wonder if it was all worth it, the stress and the expense. Though, I mean, I  am  doing something I enjoy, which is a definite plus. What about your job? Still enjoying the research? Yeah, the project's good, actually. Really interesting stuff. It’s just knowing that loads of people back home aren’t having that opportunity. My cousin, Sarah, she wanted to do radiography, but she couldn't afford the training. Had to get a job at the call centre instead. That’s heartbreaking. It shouldn’t be like that, should it? People shouldn’t be held back by their financial situation. Exactly! Anyway, enough depressing conversation. You need a distraction, right? Have you seen anything good lately? Not really. Been buried in books, mostly. You? We went to see  Wicked  last week! Absolutely brilliant. Elphaba's voice was incredible.  Wicked ! I’ve heard good things. Is it as good as everyone says? Better! Seriously, if you ever get a chance, go. The costumes, the music, the story... it’s just spectacular. I was practically weeping at the end. You always are a sucker for a good musical. Hey! There’s nothing wrong with a bit of emotional release. It’s good for the soul. Plus, it's a good laugh. I was having a right giggle with ANON throughout. Sounds great. I could definitely use some emotional release. This research is draining me. I swear, some days I feel like I’m just staring at a screen and making absolutely no progress. I know the feeling, honestly. It’s frustrating. You just need to remember why you started, I suppose. And maybe a really good musical. Maybe you’re right. So, are you thinking about going to another show soon? Perhaps something a bit… lighter?

So, what do you reckon, Nan? Is it too…babyish? Oh, it’s lovely, darling. Really lovely. A bit… simplistic, perhaps? For older children. But you know, for, say, three or four? Perfect. Aye, it’s bonny. Very bonny. The wee animals are a delight. Though… Do you mind? Foxes are… are a bit unsettling, don’t you think? Not unsettling, Nan! They’re clever! And all the kids at school love foxes. I wanted to show that they're not all bad, you know? Like in that one story about the fox who helps the farmer. Exactly. It’s about showing different sides. And the illustrations are gorgeous. Liam absolutely loves them. He keeps asking me to read it again and again. That’s good! That’s what I want! I thought maybe if I did a series, like, “Adventures of Finley Fox.” Each book could be about a different problem he solves. Hmm. A series. That’s a commitment, dear. But if you’re passionate about it… it's worth pursuing. You've always had a knack for storytelling, remember those stories you used to tell about your grandad and the croft? Oh yeah! About him rescuing the sheep from the river! I could add a character like that, maybe a brave rescue. I’ve got an idea about a scarecrow who comes to life. What do you think of a scarecrow? A scarecrow is brilliant! Liam would adore a scarecrow. Maybe the scarecrow and Finley could be friends? But you need to think about the story arc, darling. What's the core message? I don’t know…about friendship? Or kindness? Kindness is always a good message, dearie. Always. Especially these days. Tell me… does it involve any family dramas? Because  that's  where the real action is. Well… there's this stepson character who's always getting into trouble… Oh, now you’re talking! Liam has a stepbrother. They have their moments. It’s relatable, isn't it? Kids understand sibling rivalry. Aye, I do. My brother and I… we were like cats and dogs when we were wee. Though, he ended up being a right good fellow, eventually. Though don’t mention the time he tried to sell the family silver… Seriously? Oh, it was a long time ago. Just a wee boy trying to earn some pocket money. Your Dad will tell you all about it, you know.

Honestly, this shift at the bakery is killing me. Like, my feet are permanently aching. Seriously? Still doing those early mornings? You told me you were trying to get shifts later on. I am, but it's tough, y'know? Everyone wants the later shifts, and I’m stuck lugging flour sacks at six am. At least the smell’s nice, I suppose. A bit like a giant, warm hug. A flour-y hug. Still, gotta earn that dosh. How’s the essay going, by the way? The one on Bronte? Don't even  mention  Bronte. I’m staring at the page and the words are just… mocking me. I swear, Heathcliff is personally conspiring to ruin my grade. Oh, you dramatic thing! It’s just a book. Easy for you to say, you're practically living in a library. You seem to absorb information just by breathing! Don't be silly. Anyway, speaking of things you’re breathing in… you've been looking a bit… prickly lately. Prickly? What do you mean? Well, you know... down there. Leg hair. It's... noticeable. Oh, here we go. Is this some kind of Cambridge etiquette lecture now? No! Seriously, I'm not trying to judge. It's just… you usually shave, don’t you? Yeah, but I haven't had time, alright? Between the bakery and the essay, shaving is pretty low on my priority list. And honestly, at this point, I'm thinking of just embracing it. Let it grow wild and free! Wild and free is a look. But you used to be so meticulous! Remember that time you spent an hour trying to get rid of that tiny little patch below your knee? Don’t remind me. It was traumatic. I nearly had a breakdown. It’s just… seems so pointless now. All that effort… for what? It did make your legs look amazing though. Right, you’re just teasing me now. Honestly, I might have to invest in some really good, dark trousers. Or just become a hermit. Don't be ridiculous! But I get it. It's all a bit much when you're stressed. Maybe a relaxing bath and a new razor would do the trick? Maybe. Or maybe I’ll just rock the prickly legs and intimidate Heathcliff. See who  really  wins. You're terrible! But… you know what? Embrace your inner wilderness. I’m with you.

Right, so, you’re  still  obsessed with listing things alphabetically, then? It’s been three weeks since you tried to alphabetize the peanuts at the last pub. It’s a system, Evie, a system! It brings order to chaos, you know? And besides, it's a surprisingly entertaining way to pass the time. I was just thinking about it earlier – alphabetizing boxing moves. Jab, left hook, overhand right... You’re really deep down a rabbit hole, aren’t you? Boxing moves? Seriously? That's a niche pastime even for you. It’s fascinating! The precision of the names, the violence behind them… plus, it's surprisingly hard to remember them all. I got stuck on a few the other day. Likely. Though, you know, I'm still slightly scarred from you trying to alphabetize my spice rack. I nearly had a nervous breakdown. It was lacking structure! Honestly, paprika before pepper? An insult to culinary organisation. Okay, okay, you win. But speaking of things that make me nervous... did you see what happened in the Newcastle-Sheffield United game on Saturday? Yeah. Disgraceful. Honestly, the behaviour… the chants… I’m glad they’re investigating those fans. It's just so disheartening, isn’t it? It’s not a new thing, obviously, but to see it happening so openly... it’s just… why? It's 2024. It’s frustrating because it reflects a much wider problem, doesn’t it? It’s not just about football. It’s about ingrained prejudices. You hear people try to argue it's 'banter' or 'just a bit of a laugh'… 'Banter'? Seriously? There’s nothing funny or lighthearted about racial abuse. And the fact that some people still try to defend it… Exactly. It’s just… lazy thinking. It’s easier to dismiss it than to confront it. Reminds me of some of the discussions I've had during my seminars. People trying to justify systemic issues with the most flimsy logic. It's exhausting. You'd think, with education and everything… but some people choose ignorance. Speaking of exhausting… you look like you need another pint. Absolutely. Researching this bloody dissertation is draining. I swear, I'm going to alphabetize my notes out of sheer frustration. Please don't. And hey, just a thought… alphabetizing  cocktails ? That could be a bit more fun. Now  that’s  an idea. Manhattan, Mojito… it’s got potential. Don't even get me started on the liquors...

Right, so the Parish Council are really keen on getting the funding for St. Michael’s roof sorted. They’ve made a bit of noise about the historical significance, of course - you know how they are – but it really  is  crucial to preserve it. But the Heritage Lottery Fund... they’re notoriously picky. Absolutely. They’ve become far more stringent in recent years. It’s not just about the fabric of the building anymore; they want to see a clear community engagement plan, a sustainable maintenance strategy… the whole shebang. Exactly! That’s where I’m getting bogged down. I’ve got the conservation plan, the structural report, all the technical bits ready to go. But demonstrating that it will benefit the community beyond just having a dry roof… that’s proving tricky. They suggested a heritage skills workshop, but there's not much enthusiasm for that, realistically. Oh, the enthusiasm for craft skills these days. It’s a lost art, isn’t it? But you're right, you need to think laterally. Have you considered something linked to the local school? Perhaps a research project, where the children explore the history of the church and its role in the village? They could present their findings – a little exhibition, a booklet... That’s actually… a really good idea! Something tangible for them to take away, and it demonstrates that the building has ongoing relevance. I hadn't thought about the school specifically. I was mulling over a historical guided walk, but likely that will only attract a few older participants and not quite the engagement HLF is looking for. Exactly. It needs to have a broader appeal. And, crucially, you need to factor in that community engagement directly into your budget. Don’t underestimate the cost of materials, advertising, volunteer coordination… the things that often get overlooked. You’re absolutely right. I tend to get so focused on the conservation costs – the leadwork, the slate replacement – that I end up short-changing the engagement side. What about the building plans themselves? Do you think the architect’s design is workable, given the budget constraints? I’ve had a quick look. It's certainly… ambitious. The proposed internal mezzanine level seems unnecessarily complex, doesn’t it? Adds to the structural engineering cost considerably, I suspect. And that stained-glass window restoration... Have they factored in the cost of specialist cleaning and protection measures long-term?

Right, Earl Grey then? Or do you fancy a switch to your usual builder’s brew after all this linguistics chat? Earl Grey’s perfect, thanks. My brain's a bit scrambled after trying to explain the complexities of grammatical gender to my flatmates. They just looked at me like I'd grown a second head. Well, explaining something like that to people who aren’t immersed in it is always a challenge. It’s like trying to explain the nuances of the Geordie accent to someone who's only ever heard Received Pronunciation. Completely different world. Exactly! It's not just about the sounds, it's the entire structure, the ingrained assumptions about language. And the way language shapes thought, you know? It's fascinating. Are you making any headway with your research into regional dialect shifts? Yeah, actually, it's getting really interesting. I’m seeing a surprising amount of code-switching happening, even amongst younger people in Sunderland. They're consciously blending traditional dialect with more standardised English, particularly online. It's not just about fitting in, though; it’s almost like they’re reclaiming the dialect, giving it a modern edge. That’s brilliant! It's a testament to the resilience of language, isn’t it? It doesn't just passively change, it's actively shaped by the community. I wonder if it's because of social media – the constant exposure to different dialects and accents. My research is starting to show similar things with online gaming communities. People adopt these hybrid linguistic forms to create a sense of belonging. It's definitely linked. And it’s not just about belonging. It’s about identity. People are forging new identities online, and language is a huge part of that. Speaking of forging new things... are you still thinking about that trip to Iceland? Absolutely. I've been looking at some amazing hiking trails. Imagine the linguistic possibilities! Icelandic is such a relatively isolated and well-preserved language. I'd love to just sit in a cafe somewhere and listen to people chatting – it would be like stepping back in time. That does sound incredible. Although I’m picturing icy winds and frozen toes. We’d need a serious stockpile of thermal socks. We'll be bundled up like polar explorers! But think of the Northern Lights! We could try to learn a few basic phrases… “Where's the nearest hot spring?” is probably top of the list.

Right, so let’s sort out this school stuff. William, are you excited about the tennis tournament next week? Yeah! Are you practicing? A little bit. I’m getting better. He's really good! He beat Leo yesterday. Did he? That’s fantastic! I’ll need to send a note to school about the tournament, won't I? And Beatrice, are you enjoying your school dinners? Sometimes. What do you mean “sometimes?” Do you like them a lot? Not at all? Umm, pizza day is good. And chips. Right, the usual favorites. What about the rest of the week? The shepherd's pie was yucky. Oh dear. Well, you know we can pack you a lunch some days if you really don't fancy it. Can I have pizza? Every day? No, William, you can't have pizza every day. That wouldn't be very healthy. Do you remember what Granny makes for lunch when you visit? Pancakes! With jam and cream! And strawberries! Exactly! Granny makes the best lunch. Though, that does cost a bit, doesn't it? We need to factor that into our budget. We’ve got the tennis tournament fees, and I need to get you both some new tennis balls, haven't we? Yes, the ones are all squishy. They are indeed. I’ll have to check how much that all adds up to. Are you both still wanting to go to the circus next month? Yes! With the clowns! Clowns? Some people don’t like clowns, you know. I do! They’re funny! They do silly things. Do they have acrobats and trapeze artists too? Yes, they do! It's a proper full-blown circus. We might even be able to get a family discount. I'll look into it. We need to save a little bit each week. Can I be a clown when I grow up? You certainly could! You’d have to learn some really good jokes, though. And maybe juggle. Maybe I could be a trapeze artist! You absolutely could, darling. You're very good at climbing. Just promise you won’t try any trapeze moves at home, okay? It’s not safe. Right, let's write a list of things we need to sort out. Tennis, circus, school dinners... and new squishy tennis balls! William, promise me you’ll wear your hat at tennis – the sun’s been strong. Okay, Mum!

Honestly, that film was dreadful, wasn’t it? Such a waste of two hours. Dreadful is a polite word, dear. I thought it was utterly absurd. The plot made no sense whatsoever. I have to agree. The visuals were stunning, I’ll give them that, but the story… well, it was all style and no substance. They clearly spent the whole budget on special effects. Exactly! And the acting was so wooden. I kept waiting for something to happen, and then nothing did. It was frustrating. Reminds me of that… oh, what was it called? That terribly pretentious film my daughter dragged me to see years ago. All black and white, and the characters spoke in riddles… You mean “Eraserhead”? That’s the one! Utter nonsense. I spent the whole time wondering what on earth they were going on about. Well, at least  this  one had explosions! Though, I suppose that doesn't elevate it much. Going back to something a bit more worthwhile, did you manage to get to that debate at Cambridge about teaching history, David? I did, yes. Quite a lively discussion. There were some passionate opinions about the national curriculum, particularly regarding the depth of coverage and the focus on specific periods. I was reading an article about it the other day. There’s a real push to embed more critical thinking skills – to get students questioning sources and challenging established narratives, rather than just rote memorization. It's about time, isn't it? When I was at school, it was all dates and battles. We never really questioned  why  things happened. Just  what  happened. And that’s the problem, isn’t it? We need to equip students with the tools to analyse and interpret history, not just regurgitate it. Though, I confess, weeding out the biases from various sources is a challenge in itself. Absolutely. And the structure of degrees is something else entirely. I was talking to a former student the other day, struggling to get his degree recognised with his advertising experience… it’s just not practical. It's a massive disconnect, isn't it? Universities are churning out graduates with impressive theoretical knowledge, but often lacking the practical skills employers are looking for. That's why I’ve always championed internships and industry placements during degrees. Building a bridge between academia and the real world. When I left school, you just got a job!

Dreadful weather we’re having, isn't it? Proper gloom. Reminds me of the rationing years, it does. Everything grey, just like that. It's not  that  bad, Arthur. Just a bit drizzly. Still, could do with a bit of sunshine, couldn't we? Remember when we went to Cornwall? The sun just shone non-stop. Cornwall was lovely. Though I’m still trying to track down where exactly we were when we took that photo of you with the pasties. It’s quite something, actually. You looked like a queen with that pasty perched on your head. You always were observant, Charles. Remember when the police came around about the stolen garden gnome in Harrow? You noticed the mud on the pavement and pointed them in the direction of young Timmy next door. Clever lad. Police. Now there’s another thing. They didn’t seem to bother much with us in Costessey. Simple life, back then. Working on the farm, mending fences. Didn’t need much policing. Though I remember the war... Oh, don’t start, Arthur. You'll go on for hours about the air raid sirens. Can't help it, Elsie. It’s etched in my memory. Hiding in the Anderson shelter, that cold damp smell...but we were lucky, weren't we? Nothing really happened in Costessey like some places. Your grandfather, I believe, was involved in the Home Guard, wasn't he? I've been looking through some family records – quite fascinating stuff. Turns out, your great-uncle on your mother’s side was a coal miner. A tough life, that. And mine, the Smiths, were always in London. My grandfather worked at the docks, down by the Thames. Pretty rough area, apparently. Always stories of dodgy characters and… well, you know. Well, we’re not all from rough areas! My family, the Wilkinsons, were always a bit…well, more respectable. My grandmother taught needlepoint, you know. Very proper. Respectable doesn't always mean happy, Elsie. We had a bit of hardship, but we had our own way. A bit of freedom. Speaking of freedom, I've been trying to convince Margaret to get rid of that awful floral sofa. It’s a monstrosity! Charles, you always did have an eye for design. Though Margaret seems quite attached to it. Says her Aunt Mildred gave it to her. It’s a perfectly good sofa! And it's comfortable.

Right, so just to be clear – you’ve got the keys to Dad’s, you’ll let me in on Saturday after I'm done at the uni? Yep, all sorted. Got them yesterday. Saturday's perfect. Give me a call when you're close, I’ll be about, probably watching the football. Good, good. It feels pretty surreal, doesn’t it? Driving from Mum’s to Dad’s for the  last  time before I move. Like, properly moving. It does. Bit emotional, isn’t it? Your mum was a bit teary, I noticed. Yeah, she was. Kept going on about how I was the last one leaving nest. Said she’d miss me rattling around the house, which is… reassuring, in a way. She’s a mum, innit? Always going to miss you even when you're a grown man. Did she harp on about the mortgage again? Briefly. Just a little, you know. "Are you sure you can afford it? Have you factored in the council tax?" The usual. Remind me again, how much did we end up paying for this place originally? Crikey, must be pushing fifty grand back in… nineteen eighty-something, I reckon. Proper bargain now, wouldn’t you say? Though the roof needs doing, doesn’t it? Yeah, definitely. Might have to look at that fairly quickly. Speaking of which, have you spoken to Uncle Barry about having a look at it? He knows a good roofer, right? I haven’t. I’ll give him a bell later. He’s been a bit under the weather lately, though. That chest thing’s been playing up. Oh dear. Hope he’s alright. Send him my best, will you? And tell Auntie Carol I said hello. Will do. It’s just… all these family members, moving house. It’s a lot to coordinate. Your cousin Sarah hasn’t even confirmed if she can help me clear out my bits yet. I’ll chase her up. She’s probably just busy. I feel a bit guilty, you know? Leaving you with everything. You've done a lot to look after Mum. Don't you worry about it, son. That’s what families are for. Besides, I’m enjoying sorting things out. Actually, remember that awful Christmas when the turkey was burnt to a crisp? Oh god, yes! Mum blamed it on the dodgy gas oven. We ended up ordering a takeaway.

Right, so let’s nail down this seating plan. Nan’s coming, obviously, and she really needs to be close to the bathroom, doesn't she? Absolutely. Remember last Christmas? The whole saga with her needing to go every ten minutes. It wasn’t pretty. No, it absolutely wasn't. So, Nan, front right, by the loo. That leaves… Uncle George and Auntie Maureen. They always bicker, so let’s keep them well separated. Agreed. George usually gravitates towards the dessert table anyway, so maybe opposite Maureen? That way she can keep an eye on him. Good thinking. And then we have the cousins. Emily and Tom are a couple, naturally. And Mark – he’s still bringing that new girlfriend, isn't he? Apparently. Said she's a "big fan of afternoon tea." Hope she appreciates a proper spread then, not just dainty sandwiches. Oh, she’d better! Speaking of which, what are we thinking for the menu? I was leaning towards roast chicken, definitely, with all the trimmings. Roast chicken is always a winner. But Nan always complains if there’s too much gravy. Should we do a lighter sauce instead? Maybe a lemon and herb one? That’s a good point. And for the vegetables… Brussels sprouts are always divisive, aren’t they? Absolutely. I'll roast some carrots and parsnips, and definitely do some steamed broccoli. Can't go wrong with that. Right, clever. And dessert? I saw this amazing lemon posset recipe. It’s quite light, which Nan will appreciate. That sounds gorgeous! Though, knowing the family, we’ll need something chocolatey too, won't we? Always. A chocolate fudge cake, then? I think I need to get some candles too. Tealights mostly, for the table. How many do you reckon? Probably about fifteen should do it. And some nice ones, not just the basic ones from the supermarket. Something with a bit of scent. I was thinking vanilla or cinnamon. Something warm and festive. I really need to sort out the cupboards before people arrive. They're a disaster zone at the moment. Tell me about it! I saw you trying to find the Yorkshire puddings the other day, and you nearly pulled the whole shelf down. It was a near miss! And I found that box of old photographs yesterday, the ones from Nan’s wedding. So lovely. Oh, show me those! I think she would love to see them again.

Honestly, I’m proper beat. This holiday's been lovely, don’t get me wrong, but I’m ready to be back home. I know, right? I miss my own bed. And I'm starting to crave a proper cuppa. Everything here is just…different. Different and mostly weird chips. I swear, they put something in 'em. Not real potatoes. You’re being dramatic. They’re just…thinner. And crisper. Anyway, did you book your dentist yet? About those wisdom teeth. No! I keep meaning to. Mum's been on at me, mind. Thinks I should get them out before uni starts again. Says it’ll be easier then. She's probably right. It'll be a faff trying to arrange it mid-term. Especially with the move. Don't even  mention  moving. I'm stressing about that loads. Finding a flat with proper space... and that doesn't cost the earth... it's impossible. I keep looking at these tiny little rooms with holes in the walls bigger than my hand! Tell me about it! My student house search has been equally depressing. Found one with a kitchen that’s basically just a cupboard. And the landlord was a bit…weird. Oh god. What was he like? Just…intense. Kept going on about how much he loved begonias. And wouldn't stop talking about his prize-winning pigeons. Crikey! You’re having a laugh, aren't you? I wish I was! Honestly, this searching is awful. What about you? Any promising leads? A few, but nothing solid. My mum keeps sending me links to places in like, the middle of nowhere. "It’s affordable, love!" she keeps saying. Your mum's always got a plan. Mine's emailing me pictures of cats she's seen online. Apparently, I need a “furry companion” to combat the loneliness of uni. Parents, eh? They mean well. Speaking of parents, how's your dad? Still going on about cricket? Oh, constantly. He’s convinced England are going to win the next series. Honestly, it's a full-time job just listening to him analyse every shot. My dad’s the same. He’ll be glued to the telly. Keeps asking if I'm coming home for the matches. You should. It would be nice to see them both. I’m definitely coming home for Christmas. Need a proper roast dinner to recover from this holiday, honestly.

Right, so we were talking about things we could do for acts of kindness, weren’t we? Brainstorming a bit. Anyone got any brilliant ideas? I could give my toys to charity! That’s a lovely idea, sweetheart! Really generous. See, that’s exactly the kind of thing we’re looking for. I could share my Lego with [Speaker_2's name]! That's super thoughtful, [Speaker_3's name]! Sharing is caring. You know what? Maybe we could each pick one little thing this week and do it. No big deal. Like… like giving someone a flower? Absolutely! Or telling someone you like their shoes. Little things that make someone smile. What about you, [Speaker_3's name]? Any ideas? Could we… could we leave a little bag of cookies on Mrs. Peterson’s doorstep? She always waves to me. That’s brilliant, darling! A bag of cookies. Especially since I’m making lactose-free ones this weekend, so everyone can enjoy them. Bit of a challenge, baking without lactose, but it's worth it. Can I help decorate them? With sprinkles? Of course you can! Loads of sprinkles. And maybe we can draw some Chinese New Year pictures to go with them, since it’s coming up soon. What’s Chinese New Year? It’s a really big celebration in China, and lots of other places too. It's like a new year party, but it happens based on the moon calendar. This year it’s the year of the Dragon! A dragon! Like a fire-breathing dragon? Exactly! They’re very powerful and lucky dragons. We can get some red envelopes– Can we get red envelopes with dragons on them? We can definitely look for ones with dragons on them. And put some small treats inside. Like… do you know what we used to do when we were short on pocket money when I was little? We'd use the Chess and Draughts pieces as money! Chess and Draughts? Money? Just for playing games with friends! A Draughts piece would be worth, like, ten pennies! It was a fun way to pretend. Anyway, back to Chinese New Year. Maybe we could make some paper lanterns too. Can I paint mine blue? Absolutely. Or purple, or orange… whatever colour you like! You could even dye your hair a different colour! It’s very traditional in some places during Chinese New Year, you know.

Mum, did you ever finish “Alice in Wonderland”? I’m halfway through it for English, but it’s a bit weird. Oh, yes, ages ago! I loved it as a kid. All those silly characters and the nonsensical rules… it's brilliant, isn't it? The Mad Hatter’s tea party is iconic. Yeah, but it’s kind of unsettling too. Like, the Queen of Hearts is terrifying. And there are so many illustrations. It's a lot. It  is  a lot. You get used to the quirkiness. Did you see that production of it in London last year? The costumes were amazing. All glitter and velvet. No, I didn’t. I wanted to go, but Dad said it was too expensive. I saw pictures online though - they were wild. Did you ever dress up for Alice in Wonderland? Like, for a party? Actually, yes! Years ago, at uni. I was the Dormouse. I made this really ridiculous, fluffy brown costume, complete with a sleeping mask sewn on. It was terribly homemade but everyone laughed. Oh my god, that's hilarious! Did you keep it? No! It’s probably in a landfill somewhere. Speaking of things I’ve gotten rid of, I found a box of old photos the other day. Remember that time you fell off your bike and scraped your knee? Ugh, don't remind me! I cried for hours. It was a massive scar for ages! I still have a tiny one, if you look really closely. I do remember. And you were convinced it would look like a lightning bolt when you got older. I know! Silly kid. Anyway, what are you listening to lately? Any good music? I'm getting really bored of the same playlists. I’ve been into a lot of acoustic stuff lately. Found this amazing singer-songwriter online - you should check her out. What about you? Still obsessed with that Korean pop band? Pretty much. They’ve released a new album, it’s amazing! I'm trying to learn the dance for their latest single though - it’s so complicated. Bless you. It’s good you’re keeping busy. Have you been on the internet much today? Anything interesting happening? Not really. Just scrolling through TikTok, mostly. Found a really weird video of seagulls stealing chips from a beach. It was hilarious. Seagulls are the worst. They’re like feathered pirates. So, have you been doing much reading apart from Alice?

Honestly, it’s exhausting, isn’t it? These people, relentless. Last night, I was practically giving them the strategy playbook for fighting those solar farms. They’re lovely people, but… so ill-informed. It’s always the same, isn't it? Good intentions, lacking in the… specifics. You tried to explain the complexities of development control, the committee’s make-up? I did! Repeatedly. I told them about the appeal process, the burden of proof. You need evidence, concrete evidence, to stand a chance against those chaps from Energetic Solutions. They’ve got the lawyers and the funding. And the council… well, let's just say they aren’t exactly impartial. Aye, that's the way of it. Seen it all my working life, dealing with boards and committees. It's about power, not planning. Those wind turbines… a bloody eyesore on the Cotswolds hills, that's what they are. And for what? A few token megawatts? The planning appeal is going to be crucial. They'll need to focus on the visual impact assessment, the noise pollution… and the impact on the local wildlife, of course. Precisely. I suggested they get a qualified ecologist to do an independent survey. Spending a bit now could save them a lot of heartache later. The trouble is, getting people to see beyond the immediate outrage… to understand that research is key. It's not just about shouting “No wind turbines!” It’s about demonstrating  why  they are an inappropriate solution. They need to dig into who's financing it all. Those energy companies, they’re masters of manipulating public opinion. Follow the money, you’ll find the strings. And the local planners - are they getting sweeteners, do you think? Sadly, it wouldn't surprise me. It’s a complicated web, isn’t it? Local planners, energy companies, protest groups… all playing different games and chasing different agendas. And the politics! This isn’t just about turbines, it's about the future of energy. We're pouring billions into subsidies for wind and solar, but no real investment in developing storage solutions. What's the point of generating clean energy if you can't actually use it when you need it? That's the crux of it, isn't it? Batteries are fiddly and unreliable. We need something more… robust. Geothermal, perhaps? Tapping into the Earth’s natural heat? There’s some fascinating research going on with hydrogen storage.

Right then, so you've had your first driving lesson, have you, love? How’d it go? Don’t tell me you stalled the car five times again. Okay, okay, it was only three stalls, Dad. And it wasn’t  that  bad, honestly. The instructor seemed alright, a bit… intense, maybe. But she says I've got potential. Potential to cause an accident, more like! Don’t you worry, love, it’s a learning curve. Remember when I was learning? I put a dent in the Morris Minor the size of a football. Mum! Not helping. Your mother always was a whirlwind behind the wheel. Though, come to think of it, she did pass first time. You’ve got a good chance too, just need to keep at it. The key is a gentle hand on the wheel and looking  well  ahead. Not at the dashboard. I’m trying! It’s just… everything’s moving so fast. And the pedals are weird. They are a bit. Want a biscuit, dear? Digestive? Yes, please, Mum. Thanks. So, Dad, have you looked into insurance yet? It's terrifying how much it is. They want nearly a thousand pounds for a year! Yes, I've had a look. It's outrageous, it really is. Being a new driver is crippling. I’m trying to shop around, see if I can get a better deal. Maybe adding you to my policy temporarily? Though that’ll bump up my premium a bit, naturally. I didn't want to put you out, Dad. Nonsense, dear. Family helps family. Though, you might want to think about a black box – one of those devices that monitors your driving. Could bring the cost down a bit, if you prove to be a safe driver. Your Uncle Barry had one of those. Said it was a nightmare. Kept getting points deducted for braking too hard when a pigeon flew out. That’s brilliant. Don’t listen to your mother. She exaggerates everything. So, holiday plans… have you managed to book anything yet? Still looking, actually. Ben and I were thinking of maybe going to Cornwall. Been ages since we’ve been down there. Cornwall’s lovely. Remember that little cafe we went to on Polperro beach? Beautiful spot. Exactly! I need a break, something a bit relaxing after all this driving madness. It’s just…everything’s so expensive. Well, we’re chipping in for your flights to see your cousins in Canada next month, aren't we?

Honestly, Dad, this is lovely, but I’m completely stressed about moving to Brighton. Brighton, eh? Bit far for visits, isn't it? But I understand why you're going. Good prospects for you there, I suppose? Yeah, the uni’s great. And I’m hoping I’ll be able to find some decent freelance work once I’m settled. Graphic design, mostly. Freelance, that's a precarious living, isn’t it? Remember your Uncle George trying that? Selling those hand-whittled wooden toys… barely made enough for a pint of bitter, let alone rent. Yeah, I know. But I’m hopefully a bit more marketable than hand-whittled toys. The parking is what’s killing me though. Have you looked at the prices? It's outrageous. Parking? Always has been a problem. Remember trying to find a space near the Streatham Baths back in the fifties? Absolute nightmare. We used to circle for ages. Sometimes we'd just give up and walk. Walk miles. I can’t be doing that every day after lectures. Speaking of things stressing me out, my phone’s already going mental with notifications about the Facebook app update. I'm worried it'll drain my battery. Facebook, eh? All those youngsters staring at their phones… back in my day, we talked to people face to face. Had proper conversations. Okay, Grandpa. I do talk to people, sometimes. Anyway, I'm attempting to eat healthier, you know. Less ready meals, more fresh produce. Costs a fortune though. Fresh produce! Used to be a luxury, you know. During the war… we were lucky to get a potato a week. My mum, God bless her, she could make a stew out of anything. And she’d stretch it out to feed a family of six. Survival, that's what it was. Pure survival. It's crazy, isn't it? People relying on food banks now… I mean, it shouldn't be like that. All those politicians promising the world and then… nothing. Politicians… don't even get me started. A bunch of chancers, the lot of them. Always promising, never delivering. It’s the same song, different verse. You've got a point. This tea's lovely, by the way. And these digestives... Always been my weakness, digestives. Had a little wager with a mate the other day. Horse racing, you know. He insisted 'Silent Storm' would win.

Honestly, the way Professor Davies was explaining Hamlet’s soliloquies… it was like he was reading a phone book. Utterly devoid of passion. Davies, eh? Always had a bit of a monotone, didn't he? Proper textbook delivery. You'd think after all these years he'd pick up a bit of… flair. Flair? He described Ophelia's madness as "a consequence of societal pressures." Societal pressures! Like she wasn’t being manipulated by everyone around her. I nearly burst out laughing. See, that's where the sarcasm comes in, doesn’t it? You gotta learn to appreciate the dry wit of the academic. Appreciate? I’m trying to  survive  it. I’m starting to think I’d rather learn Shakespeare from YouTube. Have you seen that guy, the one who does the characters as Muppets? Oh god, yes! He’s brilliant! Way more insightful than Davies. Remember trying to learn to juggle when we were kids? I was convinced I was going to be a street performer. You and your ambitions! You lasted about five minutes before dropping all three balls and blaming the cat. It wasn’t my fault! Mittens kept getting in the way! Besides, it’s the principle. You either master something or you don't. There’s no in-between. Like winning at golf – you either sink the putt or you don’t. No half-sinking. Right, because life is entirely black and white. Remember when your Aunt Maureen gave you that nickname "Sparky"? And you insisted on being called that for like, a week? Don’t remind me. Embarrassing. My grandma thought it was hilarious. "Sparky! My little Sparky!" It suited you, actually. Always a bit… energetic. What are you doing after this? Back to that soul-crushing internship at Footwear Emporium? You know it. At least it’s paying the bills. Although, I did overhear Mr. Henderson, the manager, trying to explain the difference between a loafer and a slip-on to a customer. It was… spectacular. Oh, Henderson. He’s a legend. Still clinging to the idea that he was a rugby player in his youth, isn’t he? Absolutely. Last week he was trying to demonstrate a particularly aggressive heel-turn on a display shoe. Nearly took out a small child. You’re telling me! He’s a liability! What about you, what are you up to after this? Still working at the library?

Honestly, another team-building exercise. I swear, if I have to do one more escape room, I’m going to scream. Escape rooms? Sounds…intense. I'm just stacking bricks all day, mate. Not much room for team-building. More like ‘avoid the foreman’ building. That sounds…peaceful, actually. My job is mostly spreadsheets and making sure everything arrives on time. Stressful, but at least there aren’t any spiders lurking in the dark waiting to jump out. Exactly! Last time, Emma nearly had a heart attack. Huge, hairy thing dangling right above her head. Right nightmare. You lot do posh jobs though don’t you? Fancy conferences and production plans. I’m covered in dust all day. Don't be like that, Liam. It's a proper skill, building. Someone’s gotta do it. And honestly, my spreadsheets are dull as dishwater. True, true. It’s just sometimes I feel like I'm organising fun for other people while I’m not even having any. Want to come to that new Italian place in town on Saturday? I managed to snag a booking. Saturday? Yeah, I think I can swing that. Been meaning to try Italian. What about you, Chloe? Fancy a night out? Ooh, yes please! Sounds lovely. I’m absolutely starving, actually. I’ve been trying this ridiculous new diet… Oh no, not another one! What is it this time? Kale smoothies and air? Don’t remind me. It’s the 'Intermittent Fasting with Activated Charcoal'. Apparently, it cleanses your system. All it’s cleansed is my appetite. I’m proper grumpy. Activated charcoal? Sounds grim. Can't beat a good bacon sandwich though, can you? Absolutely not. I’m rebelling against all healthy eating. I bought a giant box of chocolates. You’re terrible! But I'm slightly jealous. I’m thinking about moving out of my flat soon, too. It's just…tiny. And the landlord is awful. Really? Where have you been thinking about? I saw a place online, just outside the city centre. Two bedrooms, garden... a bit pricey, though. Two bedrooms eh? Need that garden space. Where do you live now? Just off Mill Road. It's convenient, but the walls are paper thin, and I can hear my neighbour's telly all the time. It drives me nuts. That’s the worst. I’m lucky, my flat’s pretty quiet, but it’s just ridiculously small.

Right then, come and have a look at this bamboo. Didn’t think it’d take off quite so quickly, did you, Arthur? No, no I didn't. You’ve got a right jungle going on here, Margaret. Reminds me of that documentary we watched on Japan, all those beautifully manicured bamboo forests. It’s lovely, isn't it? But it IS spreading. Are you sure you don’t need to put some kind of barrier down? Don’t want it invading the neighbour’s garden. Well, I’ve been keeping an eye on it. I’ve got a few pots to contain it, and I’m being fairly diligent about trimming it back. Though, I am wondering about that owl box. Seems a bit high, doesn’t it? Perfectly good height for an owl. They like to survey the territory. Remember old Farmer Giles saying they were good for keeping down the voles? He did. Though I’m not sure there are many voles about these days. Still, it’s nice to offer a bit of habitat. Did you manage to have a proper chat with David on Skype yesterday? We did. Bit patchy, the connection, but we managed. He’s showing them all the pictures of the eclipse. Rather spectacular, apparently. Eclipse, eh? Didn't catch that on the telly. Shame. Though, I'm glad it wasn’t completely dark for long. Always a bit unsettling, isn’t it? Makes you think about things. Black holes, the beginning of the universe… Arthur, you and your astrophysics! It’s a lovely garden, let’s focus on the roses! Speaking of which, are you eating well, Arthur? You’ve looked a bit pale lately. I’m eating fine, dear. Just a bit tired, that’s all. Been weeding a bit too much, I suspect. Need to take it easy. You know, they’re saying on the news that even eating certain vegetables can affect your brain. Oh, here we go… another health scare. Honestly, the news is full of it. Political correctness gone mad, if you ask me. Everything's an outrage these days. Now, now, George. Don’t start on that. It’s good to be mindful. Keeps us informed. And, speaking of mindful, have you been watching that painting programme? The one with the chap who does landscapes? Oh, that one. A bit predictable, isn’t it? Same techniques every week.

Right, so, are we definitely going to that new Italian place in Sheffield? 'Bella Notte' or something? Yeah, I looked at the menu online. Seems pretty good. They do a decent carbonara, apparently. Better than that place we tried last month, remember? The one with the, like, weird sausage? Oh god, don't remind me. I'm still having nightmares about those sausages. They tasted like they’d been swimming in dishwater. Seriously, what  was  that restaurant called again? 'The Rustic Hearth'? I think. Honestly, Yorkshire can be hit or miss, can’t it? It’s a big place. Not always the best. Tell me about it. It's like, one minute you're driving through some gorgeous countryside, the next you're surrounded by industrial estates named after accountants. True. Though I did like that little village we passed a few miles back – what was it called? Nether...something? Nether Poppleton! Honestly, some of these place names are unbelievable. Sounds like something out of a children’s book. It’s proper Northern, innit? It is! I tried to pronounce it the first time and felt like a right idiot. I'm worried I'm butchering everything. Don't worry about it. I’m used to explaining where I’m from to people. “Sunderland, yeah, it’s near Newcastle, but not  in  Newcastle.” It’s a constant conversation starter, or ender, depending on their reaction. I’m glad you have a car. The bus journeys around here are horrific at the best of times. Remember that time we tried to get from Leeds to York using public transport? Don't even. That was an experience. Missed connections, delayed coaches, and a man eating a pickled egg on the seat next to me. Never again. Definitely not. I’m looking at some places online, you know, for when we’re actually settled somewhere properly. Saw a cottage in… somewhere near Lincoln. Lincoln? What’s Lincoln like? It's apparently quite nice! Lots of history, got a massive cathedral... impressive-looking one if the photos are anything to go by. And not too far from Nottingham, either. A cathedral, eh? I do like a good cathedral. Though, it's gotta be more than just a building. Got to have proper shops, decent cafes... you know, the essentials. Absolutely. We wouldn’t want to end up someplace completely cut off, would we? It needs to be somewhere practical, too.

That’s a grand robin, that is. I’ve never heard him so early. Usually it's a proper dawn chorus, but this cheeky little fellow's just started on his own. He is a cheerful chappie, isn’t he? Reminds me of Edward, always chirping away, even when he wasn’t feeling his best. Edward! Goodness, it’s ages since I saw him and Margaret. How are they doing? Oh, Edward's alright, a bit slower, you know? Margaret’s not so good, bless her. Her memory’s going, poor love. Keeps asking if her mother is still alive. She’d be nearly ninety if she was! That's awful, isn't it? It’s heartbreaking to see that happen. You know, I woke up to my alarm this morning – a dreadful, jarring thing – and for a moment I thought my own mother was calling me. Such a strange feeling. Alarms are the worst! I finally threw mine out years ago. Now I just rely on the light. Not always ideal, though, when you need to be up at a specific time. Speaking of things that aren't ideal, I had to go to the dentist yesterday. Oh no, not good! What happened? Just a check-up, thankfully. But I got a nosebleed halfway through! Right there in the chair. Mortifying, it was. Dr. Peterson was a bit flustered, poor man. Oh dear! A dramatic dentist appointment. Well, at least it’ll give him something to talk about. I’ve been trying to get more into the garden, you know, feed the birds properly. That robin seems to appreciate it. Good for you! I put out seed every morning. The blue tits are greedy little blighters, they are. Scramble over each other to get at it. It’s quite entertaining. I’m trying to attract more goldfinches. They’re such lovely colours. Have you seen any? Not recently, no. Used to have a good few. Do you remember Mrs. Higginbottom down the lane? The one with the prize-winning roses? Vaguely. Little old lady, always in a floral dress. That's her. She swore by hanging out fat balls, said it brought them all in. She was a character, that one. Sadly, I heard she had some trouble with her throat a few years back. Dreadful business, throat cancer. Oh, really? I didn’t know. That’s so sad. It's just...

Honestly, it’s so lovely to see you, Sarah! It feels like ages. Last time was… what, Amelia’s graduation? It does! Goodness, where does the time go? Amelia’s off at university now, can you believe it? Proper adulting. Absolutely flown by. Little Leo's practically a teenager, isn't he? You’re keeping busy, I can see! He is! A whirlwind. It’s...well, it’s a lot. Single parenting has its challenges, you know. But we’re getting there. How’s Thomas? Still teaching History? Yes, bless him. Still passionate about the Tudors, utterly obsessed. The kids are starting to groan about all the historical anecdotes at dinner. It’s… charming, but exhausting sometimes. I know the feeling! My work is just… relentless. So much paperwork, so much need. It can be emotionally draining. I’ve been trying to get back into yoga, actually. Helps to ground me. Oh, brilliant! I've been meaning to try that. I'm so stiff these days. So much sitting. I'm considering trying to write something, a children’s book maybe. Something escapist, you know? A little bit of magic to counteract all the realities of teaching. That’s wonderful, Eleanor! You should! You're such a creative person. I’d read it! I've been thinking about a change myself, actually. After all these years in social work…I don’t know. Something completely different. Really? What were you thinking? I’m not entirely sure yet. Maybe something with plants. I’ve become obsessed with my garden. It’s a lot less stressful than dealing with families in crisis, that's for sure. A little plant shop? A pottery class? Just anything that allows me to be creative and outside. That sounds idyllic, honestly. How exciting. What about… all the social media stuff? You and I used to laugh about how utterly absurd it all was. Now everyone’s glued to their screens, showing off their perfect lives. Don’t even get me started! It's exhausting trying to keep up with it, and I hate the pressure! I deleted Instagram last month. Felt instantly lighter. Good for you! I’m seriously contemplating doing the same. Keepsakes are meant to be kept, to be treasurer, to be sung about, to be collected and eaten or scrapped. Not uploaded to some social media page. Exactly! It’s all performative, isn’t it?

It’s lovely to properly chat, David. It feels like ages since we really had a natter. Aye, it does, doesn't it? Life gets away with you, doesn’t it? Good to see you, Sarah. Still teaching, I presume? Still teaching, yes. French and Spanish, mostly. The kids are...well, they're a challenge, as ever. Though I do have a few bright sparks this year. One’s got a real talent for languages, you wouldn’t believe it. That’s grand. Always good to see ‘em taken to it. I spent my whole career teaching history, you know. Lots of battles and kings. Not quite as exciting as a foreign language, perhaps. Oh, I don’t know. History’s fascinating! I was always terrible at it myself, much to my mother’s dismay. She was a real stickler for dates. Aye, parents are like that, aren’t they? My daughter, she's a solicitor now, convinced my history lessons were all about memorizing meaningless facts. She couldn’t be more wrong, of course. It’s about understanding connections. Absolutely. I try and tell my students that too, but they just want to know the verb conjugations. Honestly, sometimes I feel like a walking dictionary. I saw on the news last night, they’re talking about cutting funding for some schools again. Terrible, isn't it? Dreadful. It’s always the schools and hospitals that suffer, isn’t it? My sister's a nurse, she’s constantly battling understaffing and long hours. Aye, it’s a right mess. Politicians, eh? Always promising the world and then forgetting all about it once they’re in. You reading much about that nonsense with the new planning laws? A bit. It's all so complicated! They want to build some enormous housing estate just on the edge of town. Apparently, it’ll create jobs… Jobs that’ll disappear as soon as they’ve built it no doubt. And the traffic! Imagine the congestion. They never think of the people who already live here. Exactly! Speaking of living here…have you noticed how much more crime there seems to be lately? I heard Mrs. Henderson got her handbag snatched just last week. Aye, it’s getting worse, isn’t it? Used to be able to leave your door unlocked. Not anymore, sadly. It’s the youngsters, mostly. No respect for anything. I hate saying it, but it’s true.

Speaker_1 : Right, so you’ve got the Bolognese sorted then, Chlo? I'm starvin'. Been a proper day lugging around those spreadsheets. Speaker_2 : Aye, it's on, Liam. Just simmering away nicely. Got some crusty bread from that bakery down the road, too. You reckon anyone wants a side of garlic bread? Speaker_3 : Garlic bread always goes down well. I’m in, definitely. Though, if I’m honest, I’m still recovering from that curry we had last week. Still dreaming of poppadoms, I am. Speaker_4 : Oh, the curry was sublime! You’re always moaning, Finn, honestly. But yes, garlic bread sounds brilliant. So, what’s the plan for tonight? Anyone seen anything good at the Arts Picturehouse? Speaker_1 : Nah, not really. I saw a trailer for that new Tarantino film, though. Sounds mental, like all his stuff. Think I’ll give it a miss, too violent for me, to be honest. Speaker_2 : I’m with Liam on that one. Too much blood and guts for me. I was thinking something a bit lighter. Maybe that rom-com everyone's talking about? "Sunshine on a Cloudy Day," is it? Speaker_3 : Rom-coms? Really, Chloe? You? I thought you were all about gritty documentaries. Speaker_2 : Hey! Don't judge my cinematic preferences, Finn! Sometimes I just want to watch something where people fall in love and things work out. It’s nice, innit? Speaker_4 : I’m up for either, to be fair. Anything’s better than another night spent staring at blueprints. This week's been brutal. Massive infrastructure project kicking off, and the client is… demanding, to put it mildly. Speaker_1 : Blimey. You’re posh, you'll be alright. They’ll bring you biscuits and fancy coffee. Speaker_4 : It’s not about the biscuits, Liam. It's about the sheer volume of revisions they're requesting. It's like they have no idea what they actually want. Speaker_3 : Tell me about it. The planning permission for that new bridge I’m working on is a nightmare. Parish council's being a right pain. Saying it’ll disrupt the views. As if anyone  really  cares about the view of a bridge. Speaker_2 : You’d think they'd be grateful for the modern infrastructure! Speaking of gratitude, I just put on some Arctic Monkeys. Fancy a listen while we eat? Speaker_1 : Arctic Monkeys? Dead good choice, Chlo! Proper tunes. Speaker_4 : Good shout. Always good to have some decent music on.

Right, so, who's actually going to use the gym membership when we get back? Because I'm not promising anything. Work's already ramping up. I’m hoping to! I really need to get back into a routine. This whole Cambridge trip has been lovely, but my fitness has gone completely out the window. Same, honestly. I’ve eaten far too many pastries. I’m definitely signing up, but actually  going … that’s the tricky part. I’ll probably use it the most, to be fair. Got some serious strength goals to hit for that new game project. Need to be able to pull all-nighters without feeling like I’m going to collapse. All-nighters? Seriously, Ben? You’re going to burn yourself out again. Gotta be done, mate. Deadline’s looming. And the gameplay needs to be  perfect . Speaking of deadlines, how was dropping off Leo at camp? Did he settle okay? He did, surprisingly. Cried for about five minutes, then ran off to join a game of tag. He’s already made three new friends. Bit worried about the sun though, didn’t pack enough factor 50. Oh, poor little guy. That's always tough, isn't it? Leaving them. It is. But he looks like he’s having a blast from the pictures his mum sent. And apparently, they've got a DJ playing every night. A DJ? At kids' camp? What kind of music? Apparently, a mix of everything. He mentioned something about “rave anthems.” I think he’s heard me listening to old stuff. Rave anthems? Blimey! He’s going to be a proper little raver. Don't encourage him! Though, I bet it’s all very tame. Probably just some cheesy 90s stuff. Still, could be worse. Could be death metal. This weather’s been amazing though, hasn't it? So much better than Birmingham lately. Gloomy as ever back home. It really has. Perfect for Cambridge. All those beautiful colleges shining in the sunlight. Yeah, it made walking around so much nicer. Although, my feet are killing me. All that cobblestone. Tell me about it. My trainers are ruined. Should've worn something more sensible. Did you guys listen to that new Arctic Monkeys track? The one they dropped last week? Oh yeah! It’s great. Proper throwback sound. Reminds me of their early stuff. I’m not the biggest fan, to be honest.

Oh, come  on ! Seriously?! Another penalty shout turned down. They’re bottling it, aren't they? Completely bottling it. Just can't seem to hold onto the ball in the midfield. Bottle it is an understatement! They’re practically handing them the win on a silver platter. I can't believe we’re still watching this. I mean, it's Easter Sunday. I know, right? Should be out enjoying the sunshine, scoffing chocolate eggs… instead we’re witnessing this absolute carnage. And I promised me mam I'd call her. She's got all the grandkids round, doing egg hunts. She’ll be furious I'm watching footie instead. Tell her you’re doing research. Essential research into the deteriorating state of modern football. That'll shut her up. You’re terrible. What did you think of  Dune  though? I finally got round to watching it last week.  Dune ? Brilliant! Seriously. The visuals were stunning. Did you think they did a good job with the sandworms? I thought they were incredible! A little long, maybe, but visually… wow. I kept thinking about how much effort went into the special effects. Probably cost a fortune. Definitely. Villeneuve knows how to make a proper sci-fi film. Better than anything Hollywood’s churned out in years, I reckon. Absolutely. Thinking about film… did you see that announcement about that remake of  Kes ? No! Seriously? Oh, man. That’s… ambitious. Blasphemous, even. Don’t mess with  Kes . I know! I’m terrified they’ll ruin it. It's a classic. It's practically untouchable. Like… messing with  Alien . Exactly. Why would you even  try ? Some things shouldn’t be tampered with. Although... a fresh perspective… it  could  be interesting. Maybe. But no. I’m already imagining some American director completely misunderstanding the bleak beauty of it all. Oh, here we go again. Don’t look now, but they’re breaking through again. I'm going to make a cup of tea. And then I'm turning this off. Happy Easter, lads. Happy Easter to you too. Just…one more minute? Please? For the sake of research, of course. And to witness this impending disaster. You’ve got to see this. Fine. Fine, one more minute. Then I'm done. Absolutely done. If they concede, I’m hiding under the duvet. Fair enough. You’ll be fine. We've seen worse. That’s not saying much.

Look at this one, Liam when he was about five. Covered head to toe in face paint at that fair in Weston-super-Mare. Oh, bless him. He looks terrified! Remember how he refused to go on anything higher than the carousel? Aye, he was a cautious one. Didn’t get the thrill-seeking gene from me, that’s for sure. You were a different story, weren’t you? Jumping on every rickety ride going. Yeah, I was fearless! I went on the Booster, remember? The one that spun you around upside down? You didn’t! I thought you made that up. Your dad nearly fainted watching you. It was brilliant! I loved it. Liam would have just clung to my legs and cried. You were always a wee whirlwind, dear. Full of energy. Still are, I imagine. Sometimes I wish I had a bit more of that whirlwind back, Nana. Just to get things done. You’re doing brilliantly, love. Juggling everything you are. Speaking of juggling, did you see that woman who ran the London Marathon last weekend? No, I missed that. Was it a good time? Apparently, it was fantastic. She was raising money for the hospice, a local girl. Really inspiring story. Reminded me of when we took Liam and Finn to Iceland a few years ago. Iceland! I want to go to Iceland. Can we go to Iceland? We’ll see, love. It’s not exactly a cheap holiday, is it? Maybe when you’re a bit older and can help save for it. He’s got his eye on a new games console though. That's always a priority. It's cool, though! It has all the new stuff. Like, they're coming out with a new version of Super Smash Bros. Super Smash Bros…what a world it is. When I was teaching, we had a little globe in the classroom. Thinking about all the places in the world and such like. Never imagined children would spend their time looking at little screens, fighting on them. Times change, Nana. Though, there's a film coming out next month I thought you might like. A historical drama, set in the Scottish Highlands. Is it any good? Do you think Finn would enjoy it. It’s been getting great reviews. Lots of history, a bit of romance, a lot of grand scenery. I want to go to a cinema.

Right, I hope you like this lentil shepherd's pie. It’s a bit healthier than the usual version. It looks lovely, Sarah. Everything does. And you know what, it smells absolutely delicious. You always did make a cracking good dinner. Remember when we were kids, Mum always burnt the Yorkshire puddings? Oh, don’t remind me! Solid as bricks they were. You couldn’t fold ‘em over, you couldn’t do anything with ‘em. Good for propping doors open though! And Dad would always say, "Well, at least they're filling!" I wonder if we ever managed to get a proper Yorkshire pudding out of her. I don’t think so! We mostly had to make do with chips then. Do you remember those little plastic horses we used to play with, Sarah? The ones with the brushable manes? Oh my goodness, yes! I had a whole stable of them. And I named them all ridiculous things. Princess Sparklehoof was a favourite. You always were a fanciful one. Always making up stories. It kept me occupied! I’ve just finished “The Nightingale” - have you two read that? I've heard so much about it. Is it as good as everyone says? I mostly stick to eBooks these days, you know. Easier on the eyes. It’s wonderful, heartbreaking even. Definitely worth a read. I'm thinking of starting "Hamnet" next. Oh, that’s Shakespeare’s son’s name, isn’t it? I’m intrigued. I’ve been trying to get back into crochet, but my fingers just aren’t what they used to be. Tell me about it! It’s all stiff joints and dropped stitches these days. I used to make blankets for the whole family. Remember that awful orange one I made for you, Sarah? I’m trying very hard  not  to remember that orange blanket! It clashed with everything. It was hideous! But it was made with love, darling. And speaking of love, have you seen that new series on ITV, “Nolly”? No, what's it about? It's about Noele Gordon, the actress from "Crossroads". Apparently, it's fascinating. Ruth Madoc is brilliant in it. Crossroads! Oh, I used to love Crossroads! We’d sit down every evening, rain or shine, and watch Crossroads. It was the highlight of the week. It’s amazing how those little things become such big memories, isn’t it? It’s a small world, really.

Cor, these are lovely, Marjorie. Really lovely. Best cheese and pickle I’ve had in… well, a good while, I reckon. Glad you think so, Arthur. Found a proper mature cheddar at the market this morning. Worth the trip, wasn’t it? Worth every step. My legs aren’t what they used to be, you know. Bit stiff this morning. Damp air, I expect. Gets into your bones, this Norfolk damp. Yes, it does. You’ve been sitting down a lot lately, haven’t you? Don't want you getting too creaky. Just catching up on the telly, mostly. Can’t manage as much walking as I used to. Remember when we used to walk all the way to Wroxham and back? Just for a bit of fish and chips. Oh, I do. You were always complaining about your feet, but you’d still go. Stubborn as an old mule, you were. Had to be, didn't I? So many good things to see. Remember that little church at Salhouse? The one with the Roman tiles in the roof? Of course. We sketched it, didn’t we? You tried, anyway. Your sketches were… abstract, shall we say? They were an interpretation! An artist’s impression of the church’s soul, you might say. Right you are. Well, are you having another sandwich, or are you full up? I made a rather large batch. I could always manage another. These pickles are rather tasty. Reminds me of my mum’s. She always used to make her own. Everything was homemade in those days, wasn't it? Seems like a different world now. All these ready-made things… Don’t miss it, though. Less fuss. Less bother. Just simpler, really. Simpler indeed. Although, sometimes I do miss having little ones around. It gets quiet, doesn't it? Aye, it does. Though quiet's not always a bad thing. Gives a man time to think, you know. That's true. Though I'm not sure you think much, Arthur. Oh, I think plenty. Just don't always let on, do I? Now, pass me that pickle, would you? It’s ever so good. Here you go. Enjoy. You’ll be needing a nap after all this good food, I reckon. Maybe I will. A bit of telly and then a nice long snooze. Best way to spend the afternoon. . . . Well now… what are you looking at on the telly?

So, you wouldn't BELIEVE the phonics assessment results I got back today. Honestly, some of them are mangling words so badly, it's heartbreaking. Like, “cat” became “gat.” Oh gosh, really? That’s… creative, I guess? It highlights how crucial those early stages are, doesn’t it? My niece is just starting school; I’m dreading the day I have to quiz her on digraphs. It’s tough, isn’t it? Seeing those little minds grapple with something as fundamental as language. I had a kid in my class last year who genuinely thought ‘there’ and ‘their’ were the same thing. Exactly! And the parents get so stressed. It’s like, ‘You need to be sounding out every word!’ When they’re just trying to enjoy being little. I was thinking about getting a little phonics rhyme book printed, something fun for the classroom. That’s a brilliant idea! You’re so thoughtful, Liv. I’m still trying to get my head around the campaign I’m writing for – it’s for some high-end pet food, and the language needs to be… aspirational. Like, ‘elevated dining experience’ for kibble. It’s ridiculous. Elevated dining experience! Oh, I can picture it. Sounds like something out of a satire. Anyway, speaking of ridiculous, Mark's car finally gave up the ghost yesterday. No! Seriously? What happened? It just… stopped. In the middle of the A3. Luckily, he wasn't on the motorway, but still. Triple-A had to tow it. He reckons it’s a blown head gasket. Oh, that's awful! Expensive, too, I bet. He should have listened to me and got a new one three years ago. He knows! He says he’s been put off by the whole electric car thing. But honestly, at this point, even a slightly dodgy petrol car would be an improvement. I get it. Those transition anxieties are real. Remember when Mum was freaking out about getting a new phone? Same sort of feeling. Completely. My dad’s the same. He refuses to upgrade his laptop, even though it practically runs on coal. He’s convinced it’s more reliable this way. Men and their outdated technology. Actually, talking about family… Have you guys heard from Sarah recently? Not for ages! I messaged her a couple of weeks ago about Christmas presents - she said she was thinking of a pottery class for Ben.

So, you’ve all been seeing the changes, haven't you? Bit by bit, it’s coming together. Feels more like a home now, doesn't it? Aye, it does, love. Proper homely. Though I still think you need a few more pictures on the walls. It's a bit bare, innit? Well, that's the ongoing project, isn’t it? I've got a few ideas, but finding the right pieces… you know how it is. It's difficult to find things that feel… right. I like it, honestly. It’s really modern. Reminds me of those houses in the magazines. Is this all your style, Anon? A bit of me, a bit of what I can afford, a lot of what I find at car boot sales. It's a mix, really. Being on a lecturer's salary isn’t exactly rolling in it, you know. Did you see that thing about ISIS, Dad? Briefly, yes. It's… troubling, isn’t it? We don't need to dwell on it, though, especially not tonight. Let’s try and keep things positive. Your mum would be going on about it, though, wouldn’t she? Always worried about something. Still, she was right about a lot of things. She was. I miss her, you know. It’s still hard, sometimes. Even after all these years. I know. Grandma was the best. Remember when she used to read us Harry Potter? How could I forget? You three were completely obsessed. Always wanting to know what happened next. She used to do all the voices, didn’t she? Snape sounded just like Mr. Peterson from my school. Aye, she did. She was a natural storyteller. This area’s changed a lot since she lived here, though. Used to be a lot safer, you know? That’s true. The neighbourhood’s… evolving. There are good things and bad things, as always. The new community centre is a plus, I think. More support for the families, you know? It's good to have somewhere to go, though. They're doing yoga classes now, which is alright. Good on you for trying it! Keeps you fit. Speaking of health, how are you feeling, love? You looked a bitpale last week. It's just been the weather, dear. Bit of a cough. Nothing to worry about. Just the usual Liverpool damp. I’m taking extra Vitamin C, though.

Honestly, Nepal sounds like an adventure. I’ve never been anywhere quite so…remote, have you, Margaret? No, dear, never. Though I did go to Kenya when I was quite young – 1968 it was. With my family, of course. Beautiful country, terribly hot, but unforgettable. We saw the giraffes… Kenya! Oh, that's lovely. I never managed to get abroad until much later. Did you go on safari, Margaret? We did! A little one, in a Land Rover. Not like the big ones you see now. It was all so different then. And the food! I remember having sausages that tasted… well, a bit gamey, I suppose. Not like the ones from the Farm Shop now. Such a difference. Oh, the Farm Shop's sausages are delicious. I got some last week. Though I did have to check they were gluten-free for David. He’s being very strict with his diet at the moment. He’s experimenting with quinoa, apparently. Quinoa! My grandson, Leo, is obsessed with it. Says it's the future. Though he refuses to eat anything else! It’s a nightmare for his mother. And the free school meals…don’t even get me started. It’s all so processed now. When I was a school administrator, we used to make everything from scratch. Proper gravy, mashed potatoes… Oh, I remember those days. My mother-in-law, you know, she had the most incredible story. Fled Siberia during the war. Can you imagine? Ended up in Africa. Lived on foraged food and whatever the army could spare. She used to tell us stories about eating dandelion and burdock root soup. Said it was delicious! Goodness! That’s incredible. My own mother’s stories during the war were mundane by comparison, really. Ration books and powdered eggs mainly. Though she did manage to get a whole chicken once, from a friend’s market garden. That was a feast! My mother always made the best wartime pudding. Used to be made with semolina and apple peel. Didn't taste bad at all. And she’d make the most incredible gravy out of nothing. Honestly, hardship brings out the best in people, doesn’t it? It certainly does. Though sometimes I wish I hadn't spent so much time travelling when I was younger. It was all very exciting then, but now, I'd quite like to have been more settled.
