Honestly, this weather is doing my head in. Proper gloomy again today. I thought summer was supposed to be… summery. Tell me about it! I was hoping to finally get some decent sunshine. Could do with it for the garden, honestly. Everything's looking a bit peaky. It’s just… damp. Everything feels damp, even when it’s not raining. I swear my clothes are perpetually slightly damp. Seriously! It’s a Yorkshire thing, I reckon. We’re used to dreary skies, but this is something else. So, you two still hating work then? Don't even get me started. This new system they’ve implemented is a complete disaster. The production line’s slowed down by at least twenty percent. And nobody seems to know how to actually  use  it properly. Ugh, sounds familiar. My boss is convinced he's the next Steve Jobs, but he can barely turn on a computer. He keeps asking me how to attach documents to emails! Oh, bless him. My job’s been a bit stressful too, actually. We’ve got this massive conference coming up in October – apparently the biggest we’ve ever hosted – and the venue is giving us nothing but grief. Oh, no! What’s wrong with them? Everything! The catering’s overpriced, the AV equipment is ancient, and they keep trying to charge us for things that are  already  included in the package. It’s a nightmare. That sounds utterly draining. Are you getting any support from your manager? He’s… well, he’s lovely, but not exactly a fire-fighter. He’s more of a… let’s say, a comfort blanket. He just pats me on the back and tells me to 'stay positive'. Which is all very nice, but doesn’t actually solve anything. Sounds like you need to be a bit assertive. Have you tried just flat-out refusing the extra charges and calmly explaining why they’re not acceptable? I’ve tried, but they just keep sending emails and bringing it up at meetings. It’s exhausting arguing about tablecloths. Maybe you need to print out the contract and highlight the relevant clauses? Sometimes putting it in black and white helps. Good shout. I might do that. Right, who's free next Saturday? I'm thinking we could have a little girls' night in. Pizza, films, lots of wine. A serious de-stressing session. I’m in!

Ugh, this is good, isn’t it? Sometimes I worry I’ll get bored of noodles, but then I remember how much effort cooking anything else is. It is good. Nice heat. So, about the library… I’ve started drafting the petition. Oh, brilliant! Have you got a good title? Something snappy? “Save Our Stories”? Too cliché? I was thinking something more direct. “Protect Plumstead Library: A Community Asset.” Bit more official. Yeah, that’s good. Solid. I was chatting to Mrs. Peterson from down the road, she's furious. Apparently, the Borough council are saying the cost of repairs is prohibitive. Ridiculous. They’ve let everything else fall into disrepair. Remember that paving on High Street? A trip hazard waiting to happen. It's always the library, isn’t it? Always the things that matter to people. Exactly! They’re prioritizing that dreary new office block. Honestly, who needs another office block in Plumstead? It'll just sit empty. Want to add a line about the benefits to local children? Research shows access to libraries directly impacts literacy rates... Absolutely. And the senior citizens, too. They rely on it for computer access, group activities… It’s a lifeline for some. Right, I’ll draft a paragraph detailing all those points. Good. I’m trying to remember the name of that memory technique… you know, the one where you create a story to help you remember a list? You mean a mnemonic? Like, “Every Good Boy Deserves Fudge” for the notes on the treble clef? That’s it! Mnemonic! My brain's gone a bit fuzzy lately. All these admin tasks at work… it's relentless. I’m on the late shift again next week, which is just not fair. Oh, that’s awful. Shouldn't they rotate those? You're always getting the short straw. Seems so. I'm thinking I should put in a formal complaint. Although, honestly, what’s the point? It’ll just end up in a digital black hole. Don't give up. You have to try. And maybe you can use it as brain training – actively remembering all the dates and details when you write it. It's ironic, isn't it? Trying to improve your memory while being drowned in paperwork that  prevents  you from improving it. So true. Reminds me of that study about multitasking… how it actually reduces efficiency. Precisely! They should be forcing us  away  from multitasking, not encouraging it!

Right, well that’s settled then. Another plate of that lovely sausage roll, Brenda? It’s surprisingly good for a village pub. It is, Arthur. They’ve really upped their game. Remember old Mrs. Pringle’s cooked lunches? Dreadful, they were. Oh, don’t remind me, George. Dry as a bone and always lukewarm. Though, she did try. Bless her heart. Remember when she tried to make that jellied eel? Nobody touched it. Let’s not. I’m still having nightmares. So, George, did you see those Jehovah's Witnesses knocking on doors the other day? Persistent bunch, weren't they? They were. Rang the bell three times! I just looked through the window and shook my head. No point, they know I’m not interested. Likely got a list of the 'vulnerable' don’t they? I had them at my door last week. Very polite, of course. Explained their beliefs and offered me some pamphlets. Told them I was busy with the grandchildren, which I was, sort of. Grandchildren keeping you busy, eh? How’s young Emily doing now? Still chasing after that footballer, is she? Sadly, yes. She’s convinced he's going to propose. Her mother’s beside herself, wanting grandchildren too. It’s all a bit much, really. Marriage these days, isn’t it? A whole different kettle of fish. You're telling me. All these divorce rates… It's a proper lottery, isn’t it. My nephew's going through it at the moment. Awful business. Terrible. Though, you know, I do wonder about taxes sometimes. All this money going into things nobody needs. Should be more for the NHS, shouldn't it? Getting harder and harder to see a decent doctor. Absolutely. And what about parking at Cromer? An absolute disgrace! Charged us a fortune last summer just to walk down to the beach. Don't even get me started. Remember old Mr. Higgins used to park outside the chip shop for free? Those were the days. Nowadays, everyone's charging a premium. Speaking of things that cost money, I need to book a dentist appointment. That ache in my molar is getting worse. Don't fancy that drill, do you? Dreadful. I’ve got Mrs. Hawthorne, you know. She's very good but a bit… chatty. Won’t stop going on about her cat. Hawthorne’s always had a soft spot for animals. You know, I saw a flock of those waxwings in the garden the other day.

Right, Mum, Dad, please, have some fudge. Freshly made this morning – hoping it's up to your standards! Very kind, dear. It smells promising. Hmm, yes, quite good, actually. A bit sweet for my taste, but perfectly acceptable. You’re always a tough audience, Margaret. It’s delicious, Anne. Really is. Though I do prefer a little more salt. Sorry, that was me going through the budget again. Seems we’re still tighter than we thought. Did you see the electricity bill, Anne? I did! It's outrageous. Log burners are looking increasingly appealing, aren't they? Though the cost of logs is… well, that’s another story. We had a log burner at our cottage in Scotland. Wonderful for cosy winter nights. But the upkeep! All that soot and ash. You needed a good sweep every six weeks, you did. Hard work, but worth it for the atmosphere. Speaking of hard work, Mum, Dad, how was your journey? Coming all the way from Tokyo must have been a bit of a slog. Tedious, dear. The flight was interminable. Honestly, these airlines… the food isn't what it used to be. And the entertainment system was dreadful. The turbulence was the worst. Nearly spilled my tea. Though at my age, I'm not as bothered by a bit of shaking. Well, I’m glad you made it safely. We were worried. Sarah next door has been keeping an eye out for you. She said she saw the taxi pull up this morning. Yes, she's lovely. Always so helpful. We should invite her over for dinner soon. Have you heard about that new Italian restaurant that’s opened up on the high street? Apparently, it’s fantastic. Italian? I'm not sure about that. It’s all so…ordinary these days. Nothing like the good old days of the Savoy Grill. Quite right, Margaret. Standards have declined dramatically. Oh, come on! We can't live on nostalgia alone. Plus, you both love a good mashed potato. I think they do a decent one there. And I've been looking at getting the armchair reupholstered. It's looking a bit threadbare. I was thinking a nice tweed? Tweed? No, no. Something a bit more elegant, dear. Perhaps a silk? Silk would be rather impractical, Margaret. With the grandchildren visiting, it’d be ruined in a week. You were telling me last time about that antique shop you visited?

Honestly, the state of it all. Taxes going up again. Don’t know how anyone's managing. Always has been, always will be, Arthur. Just part of life, innit? Though I do miss the days when a man could earn a decent living without being squeezed dry. It’s not just the taxes, George. It’s the council tax too. They keep putting it up and up. I swear, they’re trying to force us all out of our homes. Exactly, Margaret. And then they tell us we have to recycle everything. I’m all for doing our bit, mind you, but some of these new rules are just ridiculous. Sorting plastics into seven different bins? Who’s got time for that? You remember when you just threw everything in one bin, Margaret? Simpler times, eh? Though I suppose we were all a bit daft then. We were just living, George. Not worrying about microplastics and carbon footprints. Still, I do try. Though my Sat Nav insists the recycling centre is down a badger sett these days! Nearly drove into a ditch this morning. A badger sett! Those things are everywhere now. My nephew, he’s got one of those fancy electric cars, you know. Keeps going on about how green it is. Electric cars, eh? They’re likely to run out of power halfway up the A11, if you ask me. Give me a good old petrol engine any day. Reliable. Speaking of journeys, has anyone seen that documentary about the Faroe Islands? Absolutely stunning scenery. Remote as anything. I was thinking, perhaps a holiday there… The Faroe Islands? Isn’t that terribly bleak? All windswept and rocky? Well, it  is  remote, Arthur. That's the appeal! It'd be nice to get away from all this… ...from the news and the bills and everything. Wouldn’t want to go somewhere without a decent cup of tea, though. Can’t imagine them having Earl Grey up there. You’re right, George. You need your comforts. I tell you what, I've been thinking about buying a new TV. The picture on this one is fading. Keeps going all blurry on the news. Can barely make out what they’re saying. Oh, Arthur, that's a luxury! Think of all the energy it will use. A small price to pay for clear news, Margaret. It’s important to keep up with the current state of affairs.

Right, so the laptop's definitely gone, hasn’t it? No sparks or anything, just…blank. Yeah, Dad. Completely dead. I tried everything, honestly. Unplugging it, holding the power button down…nothing. Poor thing. It's a shame. Was it the one with the warranty still? That’s what I’m trying to figure out, love. I think it was, but I’ll need to dig out the paperwork. This is a disaster. I need that for the presentations next week. Well, it was a bit slow anyway. I was trying to load a game and it took like five minutes. Games are fine, Ben. Work is crucial! Right, so, hopefully, the warranty kicks in. Otherwise, it's a hefty repair bill. Liam, are you nearly done with your dinner? He’s making a right racket. He’s just happy to be here. You know, I was thinking, maybe you could take him swimming tomorrow? Get him used to the water. Swimming sounds lovely, but I've got that report to finish. Maybe on Sunday. We could go to the community pool. Are we watching the rugby on Saturday then? Of course, son! Ireland versus… who are we playing? Scotland, I think. Right. Scotland. We should probably get tickets sorted. Ben, will you check online? Yeah, okay. I’ll have a look. Ticketmaster, right? Probably. It will be bedlam getting them, though, won't it? You’ll be fine. Just get in quick. Anything else for dinner? Any requests? Fajita night tomorrow? Sounds brilliant! You fancy doing the shopping for that, darling? I can sort the shopping. Are you sure you don't want me to look at the laptop as well, Liam? I remember you fixed my uncle's old one once. Thanks, Mum, but no. I already messed around with it enough. It’s probably a hardware fault anyway. True. It's probably beyond our capabilities. Still, I’ll have a poke around later when Liam’s asleep. You know I enjoy a good fiddling. Just be careful you don't hurt yourself. And don't swear in front of Liam! I'll try my best. He's already picking up a few choice phrases, the little scamp. He gets it from you, Dad! Hey! And speaking of the little scamp, does he still have that really sticky-out ear thing going on? Oh, it’s worse than ever!

Right, pizza’s ready! Everyone wash your hands, please. Rosie, Leo, especially – those fingers have been covered in mud! But I was building a fairy garden, Mummy! It needed mud for the houses. I was helping Rosie. I know, sweethearts. Fairies need proper homes. But pizza grease and fairy mud don’t mix, do they? So, scrubbing time. Are you two excited about the party tomorrow? Yes! I’m wearing my sparkly dress! Me too! But I want to do a handstand. Can I do a handstand at the party? Well, maybe a little one, Leo. We’ll see. Don't want to knock over any cakes! It's important to communicate what you're doing, though, isn’t it? If you're doing a handstand, shout "Handstand!" so people don't bump into you! Handstand! Handstand! Mummy, help! Steady now. See? Communication! Now, who wants pepperoni or veggie? And before you answer, let’s do some quick maths. If I have three slices and you both have two each, how many slices do we need in total? Let me see… Three plus two… and two more… Five! Five? You're doing great, Rosie! Leo, let's count together. One, two, three… four, five! Excellent. Now, about that party food. If we had our dream party menu, what would it be? Rosie, you go first. Pizza, obviously! And ice cream! And those tiny sausages that come in rolls! Fish fingers! And chips! LOTS of chips! Good choices! My dream menu would have a big salad… just to balance out all the lovely treats. Speaking of things that are a bit mysterious… Did you know there's a story about a monster that lives in a big lake in Scotland? A monster? Like a dinosaur? Not quite a dinosaur. People have seen something swimming in Loch Ness, a very big, long thing. They call it the Loch Ness Monster! No one’s ever  really  proved it’s there though. Is it green? Maybe! Or dark, and slithery. No one knows for sure. Isn’t it amazing how some things stay mysterious? Now, eat your pizza before it gets cold! And Leo, maybe we can practice your handstands later, after dinner. But be careful! We need to communicate where you’re going, okay? And don't spill the pizza. That's very important. Okay, Mummy! Lots of pizza! And sparkly dress tomorrow! Handstand!

This is gorgeous, isn’t it? I mean, the light… it’s perfect for photos. Yeah, it's alright. Is the Wi-Fi any good here, Mum? I need to upload this reel. Absolutely lovely, love. Lovely setting. And the smell of the food… oh, it’s divine. Reminds me of when your Grandma used to make that Istrian truffle pasta. Remember? Quite stylish. They’ve done a good job with the interior. A bit rustic-chic, wouldn’t you say? Reminds me of a project I did in Tuscany, actually… Tuscany, wow! You’ve been? Years ago now. Wonderful place. Although, a bit… overdone, perhaps. Too many tourists. Istria seems more authentic. It is. Much quieter. We should have booked that villa closer to Rovinj, though. It was recommended online, but the pictures weren't quite accurate. The pool was tiny! Tiny pools are rubbish. Seriously. I need a proper sized pool to do a dive bomb. Always the drama, eh, Jamie? Dad, did you manage to order the Istrian ham? I’m dying to try it. Yes, it's on its way. And the Malvazija? Excellent choice. Crisp and dry. Suits the weather perfectly. Speaking of weather, it's been glorious. Although I do miss a proper rainy day. Gets you settled in, doesn’t it? I love thunderstorms! Though, thinking about health, did you hear they’re doing genetic engineering in school now? Liam’s class is looking at it. Apparently, they can modify fruit to last longer. Bit weird, innit? It’s cool. But what about Ebola? Should we be worried about that and also genetically modified bananas or what? Oh Jamie, don’t go starting on that! Everything's fine. It’s just…technology moving on. It's all a bit much sometimes. Remember when Steve Jobs brought out the first iPhone? You wouldn’t believe how excited everyone was. Now look at us, glued to our phones everywhere. That’s the price of progress, I suppose. Although, his management style was… controversial, to say the least. I read a fascinating article about it recently. Right then, forget innovation for a minute. So, you guys reckon we should try and get to Pula? I want to see the Roman amphitheatre. Oh, aye. Definately. We could go on a boat trip too. Heard the coastline is stunning. Can we go swimming though? Like really swimming? Pool or sea, I don't mind.

Right then, more sprouts? They’re ever so nice this year. Costessey soil, you know. Nothing like it. Please, Arthur. I’ve had my fill. Though the roast was lovely, dear. Really lovely. Did you see that article in ‘Country Life’ about the singing in that Abbey? Singing in an Abbey, eh? Sounds a bit… theatrical for me, Penelope. Are they doing Handel? I used to know quite a bit about Handel, you know. When I had the antiques shop, people would bring in really interesting things related to him. Handel's a bit much for a Sunday lunch, David. It was more choral stuff, lovely harmonies. Very uplifting. Reminded me a bit of the choir at St. Jude’s back in Harrow, actually. Harrow, eh? Always thought Harrow was a bit posh. All those grand houses. Not like our little Costessey. Or Middlesex, for that matter. Though I did like Middlesex. Arthur, don’t start reminiscing about Middlesex again. We've been through this. You were always complaining about the traffic. Well, it was different then! Less… aggressive. You’d wave to people. Now it’s all horns and shouting. Speaking of which, that debt collector called again today. Nasty piece of work. Oh dear, still? That’s outrageous, Arthur. Are you sure you can’t get some legal advice? I know a good solicitor in London… Don’t know, Nigel. Don't want to get into another palaver. It’s just… a bit of a worry. They’re getting quite insistent. These debt collectors, they’re all the same. Scare tactics. Ignore ‘em. They'll go away eventually. I had a similar issue years ago with a supplier for the shop. Just turned a blind eye and they vanished. It’s all so stressful, Arthur. You need to relax. Have you been watching that new detective series on TV? The one with the vicar? Yes, yes! Rather clever, that. Though the vicar’s a bit too… optimistic, if you ask me. Real life isn’t like that. People are much more… difficult. Like that debt collector. He’s got a point, Penelope. The storylines in those shows are always so neatly wrapped up. Reality is much messier. Remember that PPI scandal? Absolute chaos. The PPI. It was a right racket. Made some people very wealthy, I imagine. Although I never bothered with any of it. Too much paperwork for an old man.

That was a particularly busy day, wasn't it? Felt like every case was dragging on forever. You're telling me! I've seen busier, mind, but it was a lot of, shall we say,  spirited  defendants today. Takes it out of you, doesn't it? Just standing there, making sure everything runs smoothly. It does. It’s fascinating, though, isn’t it? Seeing the whole system in action. Sometimes I wonder if people really understand how it all works, or how much goes on behind the scenes. Not many do, love. They just see the headlines, don’t they? The sensational stuff. Don't appreciate the quiet work of keeping things ticking over. You lot, teaching languages, that’s important work too, opening doors. Essential in this day and age. Thank you. It feels good to hear that. Sometimes, you know, teaching grammar rules feels a bit removed from the ‘real world’. But communication is everything, isn't it? Absolutely. Keeps the world turning. Speaking of which… did you see the price of petrol today? Robbery, it is. And the trains! Don’t even get me started. I'm worried about my granddaughter, she works in London, commuting is bleeding her dry. I know! It’s ridiculous. I’m lucky I can cycle most of the way to work. Thinking about climate change, it feels like everything is getting more and more difficult, eh? The price of everything rising. It is. I try to do my bit, recycling and all that, but sometimes you wonder if it makes any difference at all. My son, he’s getting into solar panels for the house. Says it's the way to go, long term. That's good, that's really good. I’ve been looking into it for my flat, but… well, money’s tight, isn’t it? Everything's so expensive. Tell me about it! Pensions don't stretch as far as they used to. But you have to keep plugging along, don't you? Still, I'm hoping to get away on holiday next year. Been saving up. Maybe Scotland... haven't been back in ages. Oh, that's wonderful! Where in Scotland? Near Insch, where I was born. Small village, beautiful countryside. Not much to do, but peaceful. My sister still lives there. Keeps me grounded, she does. You know, reminds me where I came from. That’s lovely.

You know what, guys? I'm feeling really happy today. Like, properly happy. Happy like a butterfly, Mummy? Yes, darling! Exactly like a butterfly, flitting and fluttering! Happy like a… like a sunbeam! Happy like a big tower! That’s brilliant, Leo! Happy like a big, strong tower. You're so clever. Happy, happy, happy! I’m glad you're all so happy. Sometimes, when I’m at work, things can be a bit… stressful, you know? But coming home to you two, it all just melts away. Uh oh! Careful, buddy! See? Even towers need a little bit of help sometimes. Just like us. Mummy, what makes grownups happy? That’s a big question, sweetheart. Lots of things make grownups happy. Playing with you two, for one! Reading stories... and sometimes... having lots and lots of money! Lots and lots?! Like a giant pile?! A really, really giant pile! Enough to buy all the toys you could ever want! And ice cream! All the ice cream! All the ice cream in the world! But you know what makes me  really  happy? It’s not just about having lots of money. What is it then? It’s about being kind. And loving each other. And laughing together. Like we’re doing right now. Can you think of a rhyme for happy? Uh… Trappy! That’s close! It’s tricky! Try this one: “Happy as can be, buzzing like a bee!” Happy as can be, buzzing like a bee! You got it! See? That's what being happy is all about! Buzzing like a bee, with the people you love. Now, who wants to build an even bigger tower? Speaker_2 & Me! Me! Okay, let’s do it! This time, let’s make it color-coordinated. Red blocks on the bottom, blue in the middle… and maybe a little yellow on top, like a happy sun! What do you think? Pink for the top! Okay, pink it is! Pink for the top, like a very happy, bouncy castle. Restocking your imagination station right now... Bounce, bounce, bounce! I'm a happy bouncy castle. Wonderful Kiddo! That's it! We are a happy bouncy castle of a family! Now, fetch me the pink blocks! I got it! Fantastic! Teamwork makes the dream work!. Just like happiness! So you see – a happy, bouncy castle, with pink on top is the very best! That is the real gold, kids.

So, what are you thinking about for uni, then? Still robotics? Yeah, pretty much. It's just… it feels a bit saturated, doesn't it? Everyone’s going for AI or robotics now. True, but you’re actually good at it. Like, properly good. Remember that robot arm you built for the science fair last year? That was insane. Yeah, but what's the actual career path? Just building robots? It feels limited. My dad keeps saying I should look at something broader, like engineering. My mum’s pushing me into law. Says it's 'stable'. As if I want to spend my life arguing in court. I've been looking into inventing stuff, actually. Like, patent stuff? Yeah! It seems interesting. Designing something cool, getting a patent, and then seeing it actually  used . It's way more creative, I think. I was reading about this guy who invented a self-watering plant pot. Simple, right? But it’s been a massive success. That's actually pretty clever. I was watching a thing on YouTube about China, you know? They’re patenting everything now. It’s crazy how quickly they’re developing. I know! It's kinda scary, isn’t it? Like, the whole balance of the world is shifting. My history teacher was saying it’s the biggest shift since… well, ever, really. It is. And the sheer scale of their economy... you think, how are they even  doing  it? It's like they're 30 years ahead in some areas. My uncle’s into investing. He keeps going on about Chinese tech stocks. Apparently, loads of people are putting money in. Is it risky though? My dad says you need to be super careful with investments. He’s always going on about compound interest and diversification. It’s all a bit beyond me. Yeah, he's right. My uncle's lost a bit of money before on some dodgy scheme. But he says if you do your research… it can be rewarding. What about you? Any thoughts on investing? Nah, not yet. I’m more interested in the inventing side of things. Imagine inventing something that helps solve a real-world problem, you know? Like, sustainable energy or something. Exactly! That would be amazing. Maybe we should brainstorm some ideas together. We could even try and patent something. That’s a good idea! We could start with something small, just to learn the process.

Honestly, I’m absolutely beat. My legs feel like jelly. I think I spent too much time attempting to look graceful on those blue runs. Graceful isn’t quite the word I’d use. More like…determinedly wobbly. But you managed to stay upright, which is the main thing! That's what Dave kept saying, bless him. Though he did offer to carry me back to the hotel at one point. Oh, did he? Typical Dave. Always the knight in shining…ski suit. So, how was it overall? Was it worth the effort? Definitely. The scenery is breathtaking, isn't it? And the food here has been surprisingly good, hasn’t it? This goulash is lovely. It is. Much better than I expected. Though I’m still trying to work out what half the ingredients  are . Remind me to ask the waiter, I'm fascinated. Let's just not ask too many questions. It’ll probably involve something pickled and something I can't pronounce. True enough. Speaking of questions, have you heard from Mum and Dad? They were supposed to call this morning. No, nothing yet. I wonder if the Wi-Fi is patchy at the apartment. They’re probably just enjoying being away from the madness. Hope so. They needed a break. Remember how stressed Dad was before we left? He was constantly checking the weather forecast and complaining about the price of ski passes. Oh, the eternal Dad routine. I miss him already, though. It feels weird not having him badgering us to wear hats and gloves. I know. And little Tom - he sent a video of himself building a snow fort! He’s absolutely beaming. Aww, send me that! I need to see that. He's going to be a mini-engineer, isn't he? Building snow empires. Absolutely. He's showing off to all his friends, I bet. Okay, I’ll send it over when I get a bit of signal. Fancy another glass of wine? My legs could do with relaxing too. Absolutely. And maybe we should look at booking this again next year? It's been so good to just…disconnect, you know? Definitely. A week of fresh air, skiing, and hearty meals is exactly what we all needed. Though, next time, I'm sticking to the green runs. My knees can barely manage another blue! Good plan. I might join you on the green runs, actually.

Right, John, this is the bane of my existence. Another one snapped. Honestly, I’m spending more time mending these things than I am actually playing. Tell me about it, dear. The sheer number of strings breaking seems… excessive. We need a solution, and a good one. Not just slapping on another cheap set that’ll go in a week. Precisely! I was thinking… cable ties. Little black ones. Strong ones, obviously. Could we reinforce the existing strings with them? Discreetly, of course. Cable ties... hmm. It's an interesting thought. But where would you put them? Too many and it looks a mess. We need to think about positioning – not interfering with the hitting surface. And weight, of course. Can't make it too heavy. Perhaps diagonally across the frame? That's what I was picturing. Maybe four or five strategically placed. We'd need to test it, naturally. What sort of cable ties are we talking about? Size-wise? Well, they can’t be enormous. Maybe 2mm wide? And short – no trailing ends. That’d be unsightly and dangerous. I wonder what the cost would be per racket? We’d need to do the sums. Don’t want to be losing money. Right calculations - I'll have a look online, work out a rough cost. We wouldn’t be using loads of cable ties per racket, would we? No, no. A few judiciously placed ones. It's more about reinforcement than replacing the string entirely. It's clever, actually. What do you think about calling the product 'FleetFix'? It sounds snappy, a bit like a ‘fleet’ of rackets you can repair. FleetFix? Bit much, isn’t it? A bit… over the top for badminton rackets. It sounds like something for ships! Although, I do like the idea of ‘Fleet,’ referencing a whole lot of rackets being fixed. Perhaps just ‘FixFleet’? It’s still a working title! But how could we market it? Primary school kids? Secondary school? It's probably more practical for older players, isn't it? The ones who really put the rackets through their paces. Definitely secondary school. Possibly even university level. We could target clubs, schools... even sell them online. Maybe even try for Dragons’ Den! Imagine – us, pitching our racket repair solution to those stern-faced entrepreneurs! Don’t be ridiculous! Although… it would be a  very  interesting experience. Oh dear… Oh, heavens!

Lovely room, ANON. Always did like your taste. Simple, but nice. Much nicer than my little place. It’s lovely to have you, Arthur. And you too, darling, Bethany. Good to see you both relax a bit, you've been working so hard, haven't you, Mark? We have, Mum. End-of-term assessments are brutal. But it’s good to be home, honestly. Feels like a proper break. Absolutely. Needed this. It’s been a non-stop sprint. That's a rather pretty picture, that is. Did you paint that, ANON? Yes, I did. It's a little scene from the Broads. I've been trying to capture the light on the reeds, you know? It’s so elusive. It's beautiful, Mum. Really. The colours are lovely. You’ve done a great job. Seriously, it is. You’ve got a real talent, ANON. It’s far better than anything I’ve ever attempted. Oh, you’re just being kind, darling. It's a hobby really. Nothing more. Bethany, you're the artistic one, you know. All that clever art history you do. Well, I appreciate art, but creating it is a whole different ballgame. I can analyse a Van Gogh until I’m blue in the face, but I couldn't paint one to save my life. Well, I couldn't paint a stick man, let alone a Van Gogh. Always admired folk who could, though. My Uncle George used to dabble a bit. Mostly landscapes, mostly fields. Not as fancy as that there. He sounds lovely. It’s all about capturing a feeling, isn’t it? That’s what I try to do. Convey how it  feels  to be here, by the Broad. I think you succeed really well, ANON. It's a feeling I recognise. There's peace in that scene. The way you've rendered the water... it’s almost shimmering. Oh, you're being very generous. I've been trying different techniques. I've read about layering washes to get that effect. It's a lot of trial and error, though. You should consider entering it into a competition. There are local art shows all the time. Oh, I couldn't! It’s just a hobby, love. I’d be embarrassed. Nonsense! You ought to. You’d probably win. Seriously. Don't be shy, ANON! Give it a go! What have you got to lose?

Honestly, Chloe from accounts is  still  going on about her Pilates certification. Like, bless her, but no one cares, do they? Pilates? Seriously? That’s a new level of excruciating small talk. At least when people talk about, like, their travel plans, there's potential for some vaguely exciting anecdotes. Pilates just screams “I need to be able to wear white leggings and not spill anything on them.” Exactly! And the way she goes on about it, like she’s just cured cancer. "Oh, it's completely transformed my core!" Like, we all get cores, Chloe. It's a basic human feature. Speaking of features... have you seen Sarah's Instagram lately? The filters... the  filters ! She looks like a cartoon version of herself. Oh god, don't even. It's unsettling. Like she’s actively trying to avoid resembling a human being. I’m starting to think she’s building a new persona. “Unfiltered Sarah” will be a surprise launch in six months. You’re probably right. Right, I need a proper sit-down. My shift was chaotic. Loads of patients feeling really low after the bank holiday. Proper draining. Ugh, sorry to hear that. Being a mental health nurse must be exhausting. Do you ever just… feel like the English language is working against you? Like trying to explain nuanced feelings when all you have are these clunky, inadequate words? All the time. I spent half an hour today trying to articulate to someone how they felt when their cat died. How do you even  begin  to describe that? “Sad”? That’s like saying the Mona Lisa is “nice.” Seriously! It’s absurd. I used it at work today, trying to explain a simple query to my manager. I ended up rambling for like ten minutes. He just looked at me with that vacant expression. The classic manager stare. You know the one. "Just send me an email." Precisely. Okay, change of topic before I start another rant about corporate jargon. I really need to clean the bathroom. It's bordering on biohazard territory. Please don't. My brain is still recovering from dealing with actual biohazards today. Fair point. Procrastination level: expert. Let’s just… watch Netflix and pretend the grime monsters aren’t slowly taking over. Now  that's  a plan I can get behind. What are we watching? And please, no documentaries. I need fluff, not more existential dread.

Honestly, another day, another crisis averted at the office. Apparently, someone accidentally sent a company-wide email with a rather… unflattering meme about the CEO. Oh dear. Sounds like someone needs to brush up on their professional etiquette. Did you manage to smooth things over? Eventually. Had to pretend I hadn't seen it, subtly redirect the conversation, and then blame it on a “technical glitch.” The IT department are my saviours, truly. Though I did have to resist the urge to light a cigarette while dealing with it. You’re still sneaking those, aren't you? You promised. I know, I know. It’s just… stressful days require comfort blankets. And sometimes that comfort blanket is a Marlboro Light. Don't judge. I’m not judging, just observing. It’s a silly vice, really. Much healthier to have a glass of wine, wouldn't you say? Now you’re talking. A large glass of Sauvignon Blanc sounds  perfect  right now. It’s funny though, isn't it? How we justify these little failings. Wanting a cigarette versus wanting a wine. It’s about feeling in control, I think. A fleeting moment where you feel like you're reclaiming a tiny piece of yourself. Exactly. It got me thinking, though, about the whole common sense versus intelligence thing. I mean, I’m surrounded by incredibly intelligent people at work. PhDs and everything. But sometimes their common sense is… lacking. It's like the cleverer you get, the less you consider the obvious. I’ve noticed that. My brother's the same. Brilliant with spreadsheets and algorithms, but can’t work out why the washing machine is overflowing. It’s bizarre! You’d think years of education would equip you with the basics. Speaking of which, I was reading an article earlier about this feminist activist in Sweden. Apparently, she was saying that women shouldn't feel pressured to have kids just because society expects it. Right. I’ve heard that argument. It's… complicated. Isn’t it always? I get it. The pressure is real. But, I also think there's something incredibly special about motherhood. And the freedom of choice shouldn't negate the joy some women find in it. It's like, different cultures have such wildly different expectations. In some parts of the world, a woman's entire purpose is defined by her role as a mother. Absolutely.

Right, so farm day debrief! What was everyone’s favourite part? Isla, you seem particularly animated. The pigs! They were so muddy and they oinked and oinked and made really funny noises! And the little piglet was pink! I liked the tractors. The big ones. I sat in one! You did, didn’t you? You were very proud of yourself, perched up there. Did you learn anything about tractors, Finn? They go really fast. But you need a grown-up to drive. Good point. And Isla, did you get to feed the lambs? Yes! I gave them bottles of milk. They were very fluffy and they licked my hand! It tickled! That's lovely. It sounds like you both had a really good time. Though, I have to say, the ice cream queue was a  bit  long. I dropped mine. Oh, sweetheart, I’m sorry. It happens. We’ll get you another one next time. I got strawberry! So yummy! Right, let's move on to something a little less sugary. How was school today, both of you? Isla, Mrs. Davies said you were a little… distracted in the afternoon. I was thinking about the pigs! And the mud. And the pink piglet! I understand, darling. It was a wonderful day, but sometimes we have to concentrate. Finn, how about you? Mr. Jones mentioned you were chatting a bit too much during maths. I was helping Olly. He didn’t know what 7x3 was. That's kind of you, helping your friends. But you need to ask Mr. Jones if it’s okay first, okay? Don't just start explaining things without asking. Okay. Right. Now, for tonight… are we thinking Horrid Henry or Moody Margaret? Moody Margaret! She’s funny! Henry! He does silly things! Oh, this is a tough one. I wonder if we could do a DVD and then some baking. How does a little cake sound? Yes! Can we make chocolate ones? With sprinkles! Lots of sprinkles! Sprinkles it is. Let's get Moody Margaret on and then we'll raid the cupboards. You two are exhausting, but in the best possible way. So, Moody Margaret it is. Let's go! Do you want me to put it on? It’s in the living room. Yes! Come on! Sprinkles! Sprinkles are coming, I promise. First, Moody Margaret! Now, let me just switch this off... right, let's go.

Right, Earl Grey then? Or do you fancy a switch to something a bit…stronger after that Olympic closing ceremony? Earl Grey's good. Needed something calming, to be honest. That women’s gymnastics was intense. Absolutely intense. Did you see that beam routine? See it? I was on the edge of my seat! Honestly, some of those moves…you’d need a NASA-level computer to calculate the physics. And the pressure! Imagine, competing on that stage. Exactly! It’s mental. I was trying to picture myself doing anything remotely athletic, and I ended up just picturing myself dropping my knitting needles. You and your knitting! You're going to be churning out jumpers at the rate you’re going. Have you started that cable knit thing you were talking about? I've wound the wool, at least. Haven’t actually picked up the needles yet. It looks a little…complicated. I’m slightly intimidated by cables. I keep thinking I'm going to end up with a very tangled mess. Don't be daft! You're brilliant at this. Remember that scarf you made me last Christmas? It's still going strong, even if it  does  clash horribly with everything. A bold choice, I’ll admit. Though I thought those mustard yellows would work well with your…erm…collection of grey sweaters. Very thoughtful! So, what are you thinking for Easter? Anything planned? Not really. Mum's trying to wrangle us all down to Birmingham, which always feels like a military operation. And my sister's threatening to make a seven-layer carrot cake. Oh dear. Seven layers? That sounds ambitious. Seven layers of potential disaster. Exactly. But I do love a good chocolate Easter egg. You and I could buy one and have a proper, adult Easter egg hunt. Like, pretend we’re children again. That’s a brilliant idea! No hiding eggs in awkward places though, alright? Last time, I nearly broke my ankle retrieving one from behind the radiator. Fair enough. We’ll stick to strategically placed cushions. Did you see what happened with that celebrity artist, the one doing all the flower portraits? Oh, the one that turned out to be using AI? Yeah, the scandal! It’s fascinating, isn’t it? The line between genuine artistry and something…manufactured… blurs even more. It makes you think about what creativity  really  is. It does. It’s unsettling.

Right then, love, settle yourself. My feet are killing me! Honestly, all that walking about in London… it’s a right trek, isn't it? It was lovely, though, wasn’t it? The Science Museum was brilliant. Such fascinating things. I didn’t realise they had so much on space exploration. It was, it was. But honestly, Arthur, navigating the Tube to get there felt like an Olympic sport. Packed like sardines, we were. I nearly got crushed! Well, it was a Sunday. Everyone’s out and about, enjoying themselves. And that IMAX… spectacular. The dinosaurs felt like they were right there with us! Spectacular? Hmph. Gave me the willies, that did. The 3D was a bit much, I thought. Everything jumping out at ya. My eyes felt strained by the end of it. You just need to let your eyes adjust, Betty. It’s the way they do it. It's just the illusion, really. Illusion or not, it rattled me a bit. I prefer a nice, traditional film, I do. Where you can actually  see  the screen without feeling like a T-Rex is about to land on your lap. You’re always moaning about something, Betty. I thought you enjoyed it. I did enjoy parts of it, I did. But the transport, Arthur! Truly dreadful. All those stairs! I swear my knees are gonna give way. Did you see that poor bloke struggling with the pram? It is a bit challenging sometimes, I must admit. Perhaps we should have got a taxi. A taxi? And spend a fortune? Don’t be daft. Besides, the buses were even worse. All stuck in traffic. Ended up walking more than we travelled, practically. Well, at least we got some exercise. Doctor says I need to move around a bit more. Aye, well, you get plenty moving around the flat, don’t you? Always tinkering with somethin’. Though, honestly, I’d rather have moved about in a slightly less hectic fashion. I liked the bit when we were looking at the collections in the museum and I learned a lot about space travel. See! You enjoyed it! And we got a cup of tea at the end, didn't we? That always makes everything better. It did, it did. A good cuppa and a sit-down. That’s all I needed after all that faffing about. Think I’ll put my feet up for a few hours now, you can do what you like.

Right, so Christmas dinner. We need a plan, don't we? Last year was… chaotic, to say the least. Chaotic is putting it mildly, Liam. Remember Carol trying to carve the turkey whilst simultaneously on a video call with her mother? And the Brussels sprouts launching across the table! It was a festive disaster. This year, we’re aiming for slightly more organized chaos, perhaps? Definitely. I’m volunteering myself to handle the bird. Last time I offered, you said I’d set it on fire. You almost did! There was a worrying amount of smoke. Let’s just say, my fire alarm has a nervous twitch now. Alright, alright. Bird is mine. What about the sides? I was thinking a proper roast potatoes, plenty of gravy... Sounds good. I could do the Yorkshire puddings? Those are always a hit - if I can manage to get them right this year. Last time they were flatter than pancakes. Bit of a Yorkshire pudding crisis last year too then, eh? Speaking of crises, did you see  Oppenheimer ? Absolutely phenomenal. Oh, absolutely. Proper cinematic experience. Three hours well spent, though I need a nap just thinking about it. Margot Robbie in that tiny role, incredible. She was, wasn't she? It's amazing how much they could convey with so little screen time. It makes you think, doesn't it? About the responsibility of storytelling… It does. Right, back to Christmas. How are Sarah and Mark doing? Still in Sydney? Yep, still down under. They’re sending a video message, apparently. Might have to position the TV so we can all see it properly – don’t want another Carol situation. Good thinking. How's their little one, Leo? Is he still obsessed with dinosaurs? Utterly. He's convinced he’s going to be a paleontologist. Apparently, he’s built a full-scale T-Rex skeleton out of Lego. It’s quite something. Only Leo! I bet. And have you heard from Ben? He was supposed to be coming back from Japan. He texted earlier. Apparently, a last-minute work project sprung up. Gutted, but he's sending a massive care package. Says it contains 'sufficient sake to fuel a small nation'. Classic Ben. Good to hear he's doing well. We'll miss him though. Should we start coordinating who's bringing what? I can handle dessert - maybe a proper Christmas pudding this year, not just the shop-bought one.

Honestly, I’m still reeling from that Twitter thread. Did you see the one about the restaurant in Soho? People were  brutal . Oh, the one where they clearly used frozen fish but insisted it was line-caught? Yeah, I saw it. Absolutely savage. People love to pile in, don't they? They do. I’ve had a few incidents with reviews myself. Not as bad as frozen fish, thankfully. More like… nitpicking about the placement of the sugar sachets. Seriously? People do that? Apparently! One person gave me two stars because the latte art wasn’t “Instagrammable enough.” I nearly lost it. I'm running a café, not an art gallery. Oh my god, that’s ridiculous. You're a café owner – people should be focusing on the coffee and the cake, not whether it looks good on their feed. Exactly! It's like, appreciate the effort, at least! I had a nightmare customer earlier today, too. This guy kept complaining that his toast was too… crispy. Like, what do you want, soggy toast? Some people are just determined to be miserable. I had a woman yesterday practically accusing me of sabotaging her buttercream. Said it was “too fluffy.” Too fluffy? How is buttercream  too fluffy ? That’s the entire point! I know! I just stared at her. Honestly, I considered telling her to bake her own cake. You should have! Although, thinking about cake… I saw this amazing design inspiration online for tiered wedding cakes. All pastel colours and edible flowers. Ooh, send me that! I’m trying to branch out from my usual stuff. I’m thinking of doing a workshop, you know, teaching people basic baking skills. That’s a brilliant idea! You're so talented, people would love it. I just need to find a space. Somewhere central. Maybe you could collaborate with someone? Someone who’s got a studio or a shop they could let you use? Speaking of shops, I'm finally getting around to redesigning the café. It's been a disaster zone for months. Too cluttered, not enough light. It needs a total overhaul. What are you thinking? I'm leaning towards a more minimalist vibe. Lots of wood, some greenery… less chintz. I found this amazing artist online who does these incredible murals. So cool! Are you thinking of a seaside theme? You know, given the current  thing  with Margate… Oh my god, everyone’s obsessed with Margate!

Right, everyone, dinner's ready! Let's all pile on. Oisin, darling, come and get it. Smells good, Mum. Is that broccoli again? It is, yes. You know you need your greens, Leo. It’ll help you concentrate for your exams next month. Exams already? Where does the time go? Feels like yesterday we were celebrating your birthday. It's only mocks. Still, I’m nervous. Well, eat your dinner, that’s the first step. And less complaining. There’s raspberries tonight too, Oisin. Look! Raspberries! Careful, sweetheart! Not everywhere! Nana's trying to take a photo. Nana lets you have one on your chin. She is adorable. You know, I was thinking about getting a little hamster or gerbil. Something to keep her entertained while I'm sorting things. Oh, that's a lovely idea, actually. Just make sure you research them properly first. They need a lot of care. Remember when we had that guinea pig, Percy? A complete disaster. Percy ate my Lego. He did. And shredded all the cushions. But he was cute, wasn't he? Anyway, everyone, vegetables first! Leo, dig in, you've got a big bike ride tomorrow, haven't you? Yeah, with Mark and Ethan. We're going to the new trail by the river. Dad’s got us all new helmets. That sounds brilliant. Be careful, though. The weather's been a bit dodgy lately. Did you see about those bird eggs someone found abandoned in the park? Poor little things. It's awful, isn’t it? People shouldn’t be messing with wildlife. Oisin, try a pea. Just one. Right, no peas today. Anyone want some chocolate ice cream after? Yes! Definitely. Oh, you're tempting me. I'm trying to be good. It's Sunday! A little indulgence is allowed. Plus, you’ve been working so hard looking after Oisin. You deserve it. Remember that amazing tomato plant you got going in the garden? It’s really taking off. It is! I think I might get a proper bumper crop this year. I'm thinking of making a big batch of chutney. You should make tomato soup too. And add a bit of cream. Good idea. We should have a picnic in the garden soon, when it’s a bit warmer. Leo, eat your broccoli. Honestly, you’re like a teenager again sometimes. It tastes like trees, Mum. That’s because it’s good for you!

Right, so I've been thinking about Nana’s meals for next week. I was thinking two soups, a cottage pie and then maybe a chicken and leek bake? What do you reckon, Sarah? Sounds lovely, love. Proper comfort food. She loves a good cottage pie, doesn’t she? You've been a star sorting that all out, honestly. I wouldn't know where to start. Cottage pie does sound mighty fine, dear. Makes a change from tinned soup, eh? Though I do appreciate it, you know. Bless you both. Don’t be silly, Nana. It’s nothing. And I've managed to grab those special biscuits she likes too – the ones with the little chocolate chips. Oh, you're spoiling her! I'm trying to get a proper grocery order sorted for myself. Everything's gone up again, hasn't it? I was shocked at the price of butter the other day. Tell me about it. I practically choked when I saw the price of asparagus. Remember when we used to get a huge bunch for practically nothing? Oh, I remember! And the butcher's was so much friendlier. Always had a chat and a wee discount if you were lucky. Everything costs too much now, doesn't it? When I was a girl, a shilling went a long way! And a cigarette cost a ha'penny! Right, Nana, we know! Though I'm rather glad you gave that up, to be honest. For your health. Nonsense. Keeps you going, a little puff now and then. Settles the nerves, you know. Don't you start, Mum! The doctor would have a fit. Now, speaking of looking after ourselves, are you still seeing that lovely woman for your eyebrows, Lucy? Yes, I am! She’s brilliant. I’ve got an appointment next Tuesday, actually. I booked a quick haircut for me afterwards too. Just a trim, nothing fancy. Oh, good. You look much better with a bit off the ends. I need to look into getting mine done. It's just a faff finding the time, you know with work and everything. I know, it's tricky. Actually, I was thinking… maybe we could all go out for a meal next Saturday? Just a little treat. Italian, perhaps? Ooh, that sounds lovely! Nana would like that, wouldn't she? I'd love that, dear. Somewhere with a bit of a buzz. And a nice cup of tea afterwards, of course.

He's settling really well this afternoon, isn’t he? Much better than yesterday. Yeah, definitely. I think he just needed a bit more time to adjust to being away from you. He kept looking around, all wide-eyed. Poor darling. It’s a big change for him, isn’t it? Weening him off the milk is proving a bit tricky, though. He gets so upset sometimes. I’m trying to offer him more fruits and veggies, but he just turns his nose up. I know, babies are notoriously fussy! Have you tried those little teething rusks? They seem to distract him sometimes. I have, but he just smashes them against the highchair tray. It’s a mess! I'm debating trying one of those mesh feeders with pureed fruit. Oh, those are good! Rosie loved hers. It kept her entertained, and she got some yummy fruit in. I’ll have a look online then. So, about next week… what are your plans? Auntie Carol said she wanted to take you out for lunch on Tuesday. Oh, yes! That would be lovely. I need to get out of the house. I’ve been feeling a bit cooped up, looking after everyone. Where did she suggest? She mentioned that Italian place in Four Oaks. You know, the one with the garden. Said you could sit outside if the weather’s nice. That sounds perfect. I’ll text her and confirm. And what about Grandma and Grandad? Are they coming on Saturday? Yes, they’re definitely coming. Grandma’s already planning a special afternoon tea. She’s been baking all day, apparently! That’s classic Grandma! She always goes overboard. It’ll be lovely to see them all. It will. And don't forget you've got your sign language class on Wednesday evening. Oh, I almost forgot! It’s the halfway point of the course. I'm actually starting to pick up quite a bit. It’s so useful in the classroom, especially with some of the quieter children. Gets them engaged. That’s brilliant, darling. I'm really impressed with you. Have you been practicing with me at all? A little bit! I tried to teach you 'hello' the other day, but you kept getting the hand shapes wrong . Well, it  is  harder than it looks! You’re a natural. How's that student you’ve been worried about, Liam? Is he making any progress?

Honestly, I didn’t realise Norfolk had  hills . I mean, I know it's not entirely flat, but this is… surprising. It’s gentle, isn’t it? Not like the Cotswolds. More of a… rise. A pleasing undulation. Undulation is definitely the word. It’s lovely. It’s just… not what I expect when I think of Norfolk. All flat fields and windmills. That’s the coastal strip. Inland, it’s a bit more varied. We’re lucky to be walking here today, the light's gorgeous. It is. Look at how the sun’s hitting the fields. All those shades of gold and green. I should take a photo. Go for it. You're the photographer. I’m just the… scenic backdrop. You’re being modest. You chose this route, you insisted we explore. Because I wanted to show you a different side of Norfolk. We spend so much time in the city, it's good to get out here and breathe. Definitely. It's so quiet too. I can hear the birdsong, and... is that a pheasant? Yep, right there, disappearing into the hedge. See, countryside life. It’s charming. Those little villages we passed through earlier... all the thatched roofs, the stone walls… it's like stepping back in time. They are pretty special, aren't they? Each village has its own character. I wonder what the history’s like in some of them. Centuries of stories layered on top of each other. It makes you think about all the people who walked these same paths before us. Farmers, shepherds, travellers… Their lives were so different, yet they were connected to this landscape in a way we can barely imagine now. It feels grounding, doesn't it? Being out here. Away from emails, lectures, deadlines… just… being. Exactly. A bit of perspective. A reminder of what’s important. Do you think we should loop back around that way, past the church? Good idea. I want to see if the yew tree is still in bloom; it was looking particularly lovely last time we were out. Alright. Let's go then. Enjoying the undulation. I am. Very much so. This is what a break is for, isn't it? A bit of countryside, a bit of quiet, a bit of each other. Absolutely. Couldn’t ask for more. No, you really couldn’t. Unless you were asking for a pub lunch at the end of it.

Honestly, I’m still buzzing from seeing Oppenheimer. Didn’t realise it was going to be quite so… intense. Three hours! But brilliant. Yeah, it was pretty weighty, wasn’t it? I mean, I knew the basics of the story, but seeing it all unfold like that… proper thought-provoking. Right? And Cillian Murphy was incredible. Proper lost in the role. I’ve not seen him do anything like that before. Did you spot Emily Blunt? She was amazing too. Definitely. She held her own, even with him dominating the screen. Did you see that little documentary about cycling in Amsterdam beforehand? Oh God, no! I just went straight in. Is it good? I’m considering watching it actually, been thinking about getting a bike again. It’s brilliant. Really makes you think about how much space we dedicate to cars and how a city could be so much better designed around cycling. Makes you feel a bit guilty about driving everywhere, doesn't it? It does a bit. Especially when you're stuck in traffic. Speaking of, how's work been? Still battling with spreadsheets and bridges? Pretty much! We’re working on a new design for a pedestrian bridge over the Thames. It’s surprisingly complex, trying to get the structural integrity and the aesthetic right. And the budget, naturally. Sounds stressful. I’m glad my life is just… words. Still, that promotion seems to have settled you down a bit, hasn’t it? Less complaining about deadlines. Less to complain about, yes. Though I’m having to mentor this new graduate now. A bit like being back at university, honestly. Oh, really? What’s he like? Pretty bright, actually. A bit… eager though. Constantly asking questions, needing everything spelled out for him. It’s like having a younger, more energetic version of me, circa 2010. Haha! You and spreadsheets, of course. Remember when you thought you were going to be an architect? Don’t remind me! That was a dark time. Thankfully, I figured out I preferred numbers to blueprints. What about you? Still happy being surrounded by dictionaries? Absolutely. Though sometimes I wish I could just  delete  a phrase. Like, why do people still say ‘at the end of the day’? It's so… unnecessary. Tell me about it. It’s the linguistic equivalent of a beige wall. Exactly! Oh, and did you hear about Liam? He got promoted at the brewery!

Honestly, this air is incredible. Much better than battling the tube, isn’t it? Absolutely. It’s… revitalising. I forgot what blue skies actually looked like. London’s permanently grey, you know? Tell me about it. Though, speaking of grey, I was reading an article on the impact of inflation on rural economies… pretty bleak, actually. Oh really? What were they saying? Mostly about the rising cost of living hitting smaller farms hard. Land prices are ridiculous, and these cash crops… are they even viable anymore? It's a vicious cycle. Less profit, less investment in sustainable practices... It's a shame, isn’t it? You’d think with the emphasis on local produce, they’d be able to charge a premium, but the supermarkets have such a stranglehold. Reminds me of that lecture I gave last week – about the neo-liberal principles underpinning global food distribution... Always bringing it back to economics, don't you? But you've got a point. It’s all so interconnected. Look at these wildflowers – they’re beautiful, but their existence depends on farming practices that are increasingly under pressure. Precisely. Ecosystem services versus economic viability. A classic conflict. Look! There’s a field of poppies! Gorgeous. And those are foxgloves, aren’t they? I’m rubbish at identifying flowers. Yeah, foxgloves. My grandmother used to grow them in her garden. Said they were good for… something. Probably a folk remedy. Of course. Everything was a folk remedy with your grandmother. Remember when you tried to convince me that nettle tea would cure my cold? It might have! Probably just placebo, though. Anyway, speaking of remedies, I’ve been making some progress on that Basque language project. Oh, wonderful! How’s the phonology analysis going? It’s… challenging. Their ergative-absolutive alignment is giving me a headache. It’s so different from anything in Indo-European languages. I was reading about a fascinating paper comparing Basque and Georgian speech patterns—the isolationist nature of both cultures... Fascinating! It sounds wonderfully complex. Though, you know, sometimes I wonder if all this intense linguistic research is actually practical. Does it change anything real in the world? It sheds light on the cognitive processes underlying language, the history of human migration… It's about understanding ourselves, really. And it's something a bit different from the usual academic grind. It’s relaxing, in a weird way. How's your student feedback report going?

Right, so just to be clear – you’re picking me up at half past four then, not four? Because Mum’s getting a bit muddled with the times. Yeah, half past. Four-thirty sharp. Got it. Don't want to be chasing you about. Where are you heading after, anyway? Probably back to mine, I reckon. Need to chuck my stuff down before heading to Liam’s later. He’s having a little get-together. Football on, you know. Oh, the derby? Don’t tell me you’re supporting ‘em. Don’t be daft! Newcastle all the way. Always have been, always will be. Even though my Dad’s a Sunderland man. It’s a constant battle. Classic. Can’t win with that. Makes my family squabbles seem pretty tame. How's your tennis going, by the way? Heard you were smashing it last week. Aye, feeling pretty good about it, to be honest. Got a new racket, which helps. Still got miles to go before I'm Wimbledon material, though. What about you? Still battling it out on the court? Trying to. Work’s been mental lately. Loads of deadlines. I’ve barely had time to breathe, let alone hit a ball. Thinking I might need a new car though, to help with the stress. Oh yeah? What are you looking at? I'm not sure, something a bit more…reliable, I think. This one's been chugging along but it’s starting to show its age. Thinking about an electric one maybe. Costs are going up everywhere. Smart move, all the rage now, innit? Parking’s a nightmare with those charging points though, when you live in London. Tell me about it! Another reason I need to sort this out. Speaking of which, are you still having trouble finding parking near your flat? Don't even get me started! It’s a joke. I swear, they're deliberately making it difficult. I spent twenty minutes circling the other day just trying to find a space. Ended up walking three blocks. Ridiculous. Should petition the council. I saw some photos of the Angel of the North the other day – they've done a really good job with the lighting around it now, haven’t they? Always makes me think of home. Absolutely stunning. Reckon it’s the best thing in the North East, bar none. Makes you miss it something fierce when you're down here.

Honestly, this trial is gripping. You wouldn’t believe the things they’re bringing up about Rebekah Vardy. It's just… extraordinary. Aye, I’ve been hearing about it on the radio. All that legal jargon, seems a right kerfuffle, doesn't it? More fuss than a flock of geese over a fallen apple, I reckon. Aye, a right kerfuffle. All that shouting and pointing. You know, I remember a time when a disagreement meant a cup of tea and a sit down, not a courtroom. Quite. It's all so dramatic, though. Did you see the photos of her shopping habits they produced as evidence? Well, we all like a bit of retail therapy, don’t we? Though I wouldn't broadcast it like that. Still, fancy dragging it all out like this. Got to wonder who's really winning. I agree. Anyway, speaking of wildlife… have you seen the geese this year? They’re absolutely massive. A whole gaggle came down to the pond this morning. Oh aye, they’ve been about. A proper racket they make, honking and squawking. They’re getting ready for their migration, aren’t they? Aye, the migration’s a wonder. All those miles they fly, just following the instinct. Nature’s clever, she is. Reminds me of my Harold. Always knew where he wanted to go, clever man he was. It’s amazing, isn’t it? They seem to just  know  where to go. I was reading an article about how they use the stars to navigate. Stars, eh? Fancy that. Never thought about it. I just used to watch them go overhead, heading south. Always makes you think a bit, doesn’t it? Wondering where they're going and what they’re leaving behind. Leaving behind the cold, I expect. They’re sensible birds, geese are. Don't want to freeze their little tails off. Used to have a goose loose in our garden when I was a girl. Nipped me right on the bottom! Oh dear! That sounds like quite the experience. Aye, they can be nippy! But they’re beautiful to watch, all circling and swooping. Makes you appreciate the simple things. Absolutely. It's a lovely distraction from all the trial nonsense, anyway. Although I do confess, I'm a bit addicted to the drama now. Drama’s been around a long time, love. Don’t you worry about a bit of drama.

This quiche is genuinely amazing, Chloe. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Oh, stop it! It's just a recipe I found online - a bit fiddly, but worth it. You know I always loved a good bake. Still miss getting into the kitchen at school sometimes, you know? More rewarding than marking essays, that's for sure. Absolutely. Teaching’s brilliant, don’t get me wrong, but the creativity sometimes feels a bit… stifled. How’s everything going with you, though? Heard you were interviewing for that head of department position? Oh, the interview. Don't even get me started. Utter disaster. No! Really? What happened? I just… froze. Total brain blank. They asked me about my vision for the department, and all I could think was, "Vision? I need a nap!" It was mortifying. Oh, Chloe, I’m so sorry. But honestly, these interview panels can be so intimidating. It’s not really a reflection of your abilities. Remember how I butchered that interview for the senior language post back in… what, 2018? Vaguely. You tripped over a chair, didn’t you? And then proceeded to call the headmistress ‘Brenda’ when her name was Penelope. It was a masterclass in awkward. But I got the job eventually, didn’t I? You did! See? It just takes perseverance. Try not to dwell on it too much. Maybe the panel weren't right for you anyway. Exactly. It's probably a blessing in disguise. So, Sarah’s little one, Alfie, how’s he doing? Still obsessed with throwing food? Oh my goodness, you have no idea. He’s reached a new level of projectile vomiting. Apparently, mashed sweet potato is now his weapon of choice. Covered the entire highchair in it the other day. And me! Oh, the joys of parenthood! Millie’s just starting to experiment with solids herself. She’s mostly just making faces at the food, though. No actual eating. Give it time. It’s a phase. Though I do worry sometimes. He's so...loud. Sometimes I wonder if I'm just not cut out for this. Don't be silly! You're a fantastic mum. It's hard work, no denying it. And some days it feels like you're just surviving. So true. I think I need a serious spa day. Do you ever get a chance to do anything for yourself these days? Barely! Millie’s keeping me pretty occupied.

Honestly, I’m starting to freak out a little bit about the future. Like, properly. Tell me about it! It's overwhelming, isn’t it? I was just having a mini existential crisis earlier while alphabetising invoices. Invoices! Such a profound task summing up the anxieties of modern life. Right? I was trying to think, what do I  actually  want to be doing in five years? It felt impossible to picture. Right now, I'm just…doing this. Production Controller. It’s fine, it’s steady, it’s…beige. Beige is a perfectly good colour! And steady is vital, especially these days. But I get it. It's the feeling of being on a conveyer belt, isn't it? Just…moving along. Exactly! And everyone else seems to have it figured out. Like, Sarah from uni just bought a flat, and Mark’s off to Australia to 'find himself'. Sarah's always been good at manifesting. Remember that time she willed herself a free pint at that pub crawl? And Mark's probably just running from his student debt. No shade, though – Australia sounds lovely. But it's easy to look at other people’s highlight reels and think you’re lagging behind. It’s so true. I keep thinking about the training course I did, the one on sustainable supply chains. I really enjoyed it, felt…passionate about it, almost. But that's hardly a blazing career path, is it? It sounds really interesting actually! Maybe you could look for something that incorporates that? There's tonnes of companies now focusing on ethical sourcing. You could become a sustainability consultant or something. I've looked a bit, but it all seems so…competitive. And I'd need more experience. It's a whole cycle of needing experience to get experience, isn't it? That’s the game, unfortunately. What about volunteering? You could volunteer with a charity focused on fair trade or something. It would look good on a CV and you’d be doing something good. That's a good point. Actually, I saw something about a volunteer position at the local community garden, focused on reducing food waste. It’s not exactly supply chains, but it’s connected. See! Baby steps. And it's nice to do something that’s tangible, right? Something you can actually  see  the impact of. I've been thinking about doing some open courses myself.

Honestly, I can’t believe Liam’s still going on about Chloe. Like, we broke up months ago! Aye, tell me about it. He's proper clingy, isn't he? Keeps messaging you, doesn’t he? He really does, doesn't he? It’s kind of pathetic, actually. It's been ages. You should just block him. I’ve considered it, I really have. But I don’t want to look dramatic, you know? Like, a bitter ex. Bitter ex? Lass, you're not bitter, you’re just moving on! He's the one being dramatic clinging to the last shred of hope. Don't let him drag you down. Exactly. And honestly, it’s just annoying. I keep seeing him liking my Instagram posts, even though, like, he hasn’t spoken to me in years. Same! It’s just creepy. I’m tempted to unfollow him, but then he'll probably notice and start messaging me about that too. It's a vicious cycle! Just block him! Seriously! What's the worst that can happen? He’ll moan about it on Facebook? Who cares? She’s right, you know. It's getting tiresome, isn't it? Anyway, speaking of lads… Did you hear about Tom and that girl from the bakery? No way! Tom? He was like, head-over-heels for Sophie! What happened to Sophie? Apparently, she’s moved on to someone else. Some American tourist, apparently, who was only in town for a week. Isn’t that awful? He was devastated, proper gutted. I felt a bit sorry for him, to be honest. I feel a bit sorry for Sophie too though. Running off with an American tourist? That's a recipe for disaster. Aye, it is! It’ll be all sunshine and roses for a few weeks and then… poof! Gone. Just like that. I wonder if it’s a rebound thing, you know? Like, she’s trying to get over something. Or maybe she just likes the whole ‘American’ thing – the accents, the money, the… well, you know. Don't be like that! Although… he did have a really nice car. Mine's been playing up again - makes me want to give Joe a kicking. Last week, he was moaning about my breadcrumbs in his car, but  his  radio was playing terrible music all the way from Bristol! Oh, God, Joe. He's just… Joe. You love him really, don’t you?

This chicken is lovely, isn’t it? Really tender. Yeah, it's good. Though I still think having chips with chicken is weird. What’s weird about it, love? It’s a classic combination. You youngsters have some strange ideas sometimes. It's alright, I like it. More chips, please, Mum. Always with the chips. You’ll be bouncing off the walls later! Did you two manage to finish your homework? Nearly. Got Maths to do after this. Not looking forward to it, honestly. Don't complain. Maths is important. You'll need it for… well, for everything. So, did you see the highlights of the hockey match last night? Yeah! It was mental! Loads of goals! It was pretty good. That slap shot from Ben was insane. Absolutely. They played really well as a team. Such a shame about Carl's ankle though. Poor Carl. Hopefully it’s not too bad. He's always been such a key player. They said it looked quite nasty. Yeah, he was limping really badly when he came off. Thinking about a trip somewhere warm… having a really stressful week. Somewhere tropical maybe? Ooh, that sounds lovely. Where were you thinking? Well, I was browsing flights to the Maldives last night. Crystal clear water, white sand beaches… total relaxation. Maldives?! Cool! Can we go???? Probably more expensive than a trip to Skegness. Don't be ridiculous. But it would be wonderful. We could really use a break. When were you considering? I was thinking maybe Easter? Although it would be pricey then… perhaps later in the summer? Let’s have a look at the finances first. We need to be sensible. But a little daydreaming won't hurt. Did you hear from Liam today? Nah, not yet. He was saying he was going on a mountain bike ride with his mates. Probably out all day. Liam’s got a new bike! He showed it to me last week. It's got suspension and everything. That's brilliant for him. He seems to be really enjoying cycling. I hope he's being careful though. Those trails can be tricky. Speaking of tricky, did you ever resolve that issue with the Henderson account? Still working on it. They’re proving to be quite difficult. I’ve got a meeting with them next week, hopefully we can come to some sort of agreement. It’s frustrating, though.

Wow. Just…wow. I feel like an ant in a cathedral. It's incredible, isn’t it? Photos just don't do it justice. You can feel how old they are, you know? Like, breathing ancient history. Absolutely. It’s… humbling. I was just thinking about Sarah and Mark, you know, back home. They’d be  livid  if they missed this. Oh, they would be, wouldn't they? Sarah would be on Instagram the whole time, tagging everyone and everything. Poor Mark would be forced to pose in front of every tree. Precisely. He pretends he’s not interested in nature, but deep down… I bet he'd be secretly loving it. Did you hear back from him about the dog-sitting? Yeah, he said they’re all sorted. Aunt Carol is doing it, luckily. Much more reliable than poor Mrs. Higgins next door. Remember last Christmas when she let Buster eat an entire box of chocolates? Oh god, don't remind me! The vet bill was astronomical. And Buster didn’t look very happy either, just a very guilty-looking, chocolate-covered mess. He practically glowed green! Anyway, Carol’s confirmed. Apparently, Buster loves her and follows her around like a shadow. That’s good, that's really good. I wouldn’t trust him with a goldfish, let alone a bouncy, chocolate-loving Labrador. Speaking of goldfish…did you hear anything from Liam about his new apartment? I know he was struggling to find somewhere. Actually, yes! He texted me yesterday. Said he finally found a place in Shoreditch, a tiny studio but apparently, it's got "amazing vibes." Typical Liam. Amazing vibes. That’s his go-to phrase for everything. Does it have a kitchen? I remember him complaining about having to eat takeaways every night. Apparently, it does, though it's “a compact culinary zone,” according to him. I think he’s trying to sound all trendy. He always does. You know, I saw Emily the other day... at that farmer's market in Santa Monica. She looked really well. Really? That’s fantastic. She seemed so down when she left, remember? Struggling with the breakup. She did. But she seemed really happy, really grounded. Said she's been doing yoga and painting - cliché, I know, but it seems to be working for her. That’s brilliant. I’m so glad to hear it. It’s good to see people finding their way.

Right, that was decent. Bit greasy though, wasn’t it? It was alright. Could've been hotter. And there's loads of garlic! Loads of garlic? You’re moaning about garlic, you’re the one who asked for extra! I did, but I didn’t realise it would be  this  much. My breath’s gonna smell like a vampire's armpit. Honestly, you two. Complaint after complaint. At least there’s food on the table. I’m starving. Not complaining, just observing, love. Observing. Did you catch any of the rugby earlier? Nah, I was playing FIFA. Ireland did alright, though, right, Dad? Aye, they did. Tough match. Needed a bit more bite in the second half, but we’ll take the win. Speaking of bite, I need a biscuit. Don't you start on the biscuits! You’ve already had half the tin! Sharing is caring, Sarah. Sharing is caring. And Granny wants a visit next week, doesn't she? Yeah, she was asking about me on the phone yesterday. Said she’d made her famous apple crumble. Right. We need to sort that out then. I need to book the train. And think about taking some photos for her, she'd love that. I’ll put them on Flickr, she can have a look. Good idea. I'll upload a few to Dropbox too, so you can download them easily if Flicker's being a wallie again. Always acting up, that website. Wallie? Is that even a word? It is now. Means unreliable. Like Flicker sometimes. Or that new app you downloaded. It’s fine! It’s just… I’m getting a bit of a headache now, could be all the garlic. Oh, poor love! Maybe lie down for a bit. And definitely stay away from the biscuits! Don’t be ridiculous, Sarah. Biscuits are medicine. Especially ginger ones. Dad! Just saying. There was a hedgehog in the garden this morning, you know. Had a little wander. A hedgehog! Oh, how lovely! I didn't see it. He was rooting around in the flower beds. Little blighter probably causing chaos. Same as you two. Hey! I’m not causing chaos. Maybe not. But you're certainly making a lot of noise. Now, who wants another chicken kiev? Absolutely not! I'm having a biscuit. And a cup of tea. And then I'm going to lie down. This conversation is exhausting.

Right, so I think I’ve got enough onions for the soup. Do you want me to chop these or shall we tackle this buckwheat bread first? Let's do the bread. It's a bit fiddly, isn't it? And you're faster at it than I am. Plus, I’m still trying to get the hang of this new electric whisk. I’m terrified of splattering the kitchen. You and your electric whisk anxieties! It’s perfectly safe. It’s more likely to be the buckwheat flour flying everywhere. That stuff’s like volcanic dust. True, true. Right, shall I get the bowl out then? Did you remember the molasses? Yep, right here. Alongside the weirdest collection of vintage cups and saucers eBay has ever seen. Seriously, look at this one. Oh wow, that  is  something. Where did you even find that? Some woman in Dorset clearing out her grandmother’s attic. Said it was "passed down through generations." I'm not sure about that, but it’s got character, doesn’t it? And it was only £3! Three quid!
