You are a bargain hunter. So, are you going to display them, or just…add them to the ever-growing pile? I'm thinking a small display. Maybe on that little shelf in the hallway. It needs  something  that isn’t just bills and takeaway menus. Good idea. Alright, mixing bowl out, molasses measured… this bread's going to be dark, isn't it? It will be lovely and hearty. Much better than that supermarket stuff. By the way, have you had any more word on the leaving do for Mark? Not really. Still seems like a bit of a shambles, to be honest. Apparently, half the team wants something formal, the other half is all for a pub crawl. I suggested we compromise with a nice curry house. That sounds good. Somewhere with a decent atmosphere. I’ll chase up Sarah tomorrow, she's head of HR, she  should  know something. Poor Mark deserves a proper send off, he's been there ages. He has. And look, remember that lovely chap, Thomas, from accounts? He’s organising a charity stall at the local market next weekend. Selling homemade jams and things. Oh, really? That’s nice. I might pop down and have a look. We need some proper honey, the supermarket stuff is all rubbish. Exactly! And maybe some of those miniature pumpkins everyone’s obsessed with.

So, Dad, you were saying about… about how your business has been affected by these new regulations? Affected is putting it mildly, love. Seriously affected. It’s a nightmare, trying to navigate all this new paperwork, the extra scrutiny… it's like they're actively trying to shut down small businesses. Are they really? I thought things seemed a bit… layered, with your accounts lately, Rob. It seemed a lot of movement. Well, it’s all above board, of course. Perfectly legal. Just… complex. There are a lot of international transactions, you see, with the imports and exports. Things changed drastically after that EU directive on anti-money laundering. You have to prove the source of every single penny. Seems like a right pain. Makes you wish you could just deal in cash, eh? Don't even  say  that, Liam. That's… not the point. Dad, are you sure you’re not getting any kind of… unfair attention? Because of what you do? Unfair attention? Of course, I am. It’s practically a witch hunt. They are auditing me every other month. The other day they tried to fine me for something ridiculous, a technicality about reporting a transfer from Switzerland. It was a perfectly legitimate deal. I’ve been doing it for years! Switzerland? What exactly were you transferring? I mean, no judgement, just… curious. Honestly, it’s not something I want to get into, right here. It’s… contract work. Confidential. Let's just say it involves moving funds for some overseas companies. It’s always been done, always been legal. Until now, apparently. But moving funds for  overseas companies … Dad, don't you see? That looks suspicious. It’s practically textbook money laundering! Now, hold on a minute! I am not laundering anything. I’m providing a service. Perfectly legal accounting! I’m a middleman. I don't ask questions. So you’re saying you don’t know where the money comes from? That’s not what I’m saying. I just… focus on facilitating the transactions. I don't need to know the details. Ignorance is bliss. Blissful ignorance can land you in a lot of trouble, Rob. Remember Uncle Mark? All that hassle with the offshore accounts? Don’t bring up Mark. That was completely different circumstances. He was reckless, took unnecessary risks. I’m meticulous, I follow the rules… mostly. Dad, have you talked to a lawyer about this?

Honestly, this weather is just relentless, isn’t it? One minute sunshine, next minute you're battling a gale. Aye, typical British weather then. Can’t trust it for anything. At least it’s good for the garden, though. Everything’s growing like mad. It  is  good for the garden. Little Timmy’s been absolutely fascinated watching the snails munching on the lettuce. I’ve been trying to teach him a bit about the lifecycle – it’s a bit tricky at this age, though! Snails in lettuce? Sounds like a nightmare when you’re trying to make a salad! Everything's grown so fast at my nan’s, she's had to give away loads of courgettes. Oh, courgettes! Everyone’s got courgettes! I’ve got a mountain of them. I might have to whip up a massive batch of courgette bread. Anyone fancy some? Definitely! Timmy loves bread. He's starting to try all sorts of new things, actually. Such a fussy eater at first, but now he’s gobbling down broccoli and sweet potatoes. I’m envious. My Liam barely touches anything green. He lives on chicken nuggets and chips. It's exhausting trying to get him to eat properly. Tell me about it. Remember when Emily was like that? Nearly drove your mother mad. Don't remind me! I thought I'd never see her eat anything other than bread and jam. Right, so, Lydia, how’s the sign language class going? You were so excited about it. It’s brilliant, actually! Really enjoyed the first few lessons. It’s harder than I thought, but so rewarding. We’re learning a lot of basic greetings and introductions. It’s lovely to see how expressive it can be. That sounds amazing! I always thought sign language was really beautiful and graceful. Should we all go to a class together? That’s a lovely idea! We could all get involved. Might be good for a bit of family bonding. Though I might struggle to keep up with you young’uns. Don’t you worry, love. We'll all be signing like natives in no time. Though I'll probably just end up looking like I’m having a fit. Speaking of natives, have you booked the tickets for the Lichfield Festival yet? I really want to take Timmy to a children’s theatre show. He’s been asking about it non-stop.

…and then the methodology section just completely collapsed. Like, it contradicted everything in the introduction! It was a mess, honestly. Oh god, those are the worst. At least when there’s a blank page, you know where you stand. Seriously! I’m still wading through a manuscript that’s twenty thousand words over the allocated length. It’s brutal. Tell me about it. My brief was “tidy up this chapter on medieval embroidery”. Medieval embroidery! Who  writes  that much about medieval embroidery? Well, academics, apparently. But still, twenty thousand over? That’s…ambitious, to say the least. I had a professor submit a piece arguing for the revival of Old English grammar. It was delivered entirely in Old English, of course. You’re kidding! It’s lovely to see you, Arthur! Please, sit down, I’ve just put the kettle on. Thank you, dear. Always a pleasure to pop in and see you, Anne. Your garden’s looking rather splendid, by the way. The roses are a riot of colour. Oh, thank you! They're a bit of a passion of mine, you know. Keeps me occupied. So, how have you been? Still enjoying your model boats? Absolutely! Had a lovely day down at the boating lake last Sunday. Bit windy, but the little ‘Lady Penelope’ handled it beautifully. Tried a new propulsion system actually, a slightly more powerful motor. Made quite a difference. That's fascinating! You always were a dab hand at engineering, weren’t you? I remember your stories about your time at the company – managing a whole department, wasn’t it? That's right. Quite a responsibility, looking after the logistics. All those numbers… I used to dream in spreadsheets! But now, peace and quiet with a cup of tea and a model boat is bliss. What about you, Anne? Keeping busy with the teaching? It’s good, thank you. The kids are… well, they’re kids! Full of energy and asking the most wonderfully odd questions. I'm teaching a new group of GCSE students this year. They’re determined to learn French, which is a definite plus. French, eh? Always fancied learning French myself, but never quite got around to it. My wife, bless her, tried. She got as far as ordering a croissant and asking where the toilet was, and then she declared victory! That’s a classic! It’s amazing how far a little bit of French can get you on holiday, isn’t it? Are you thinking of getting away anywhere this year? We are, actually. Thinking of a trip to Italy. Always wanted to see Florence, see the David and all that. Bit of a cliché, I suppose, but… Not at all! Italy is wonderful. Have you been before? Never. It's something we’ve discussed many times but never actually did. Said we'd do it when we retired, and now, well, time seems to be slipping away! What are your weekend plans? Anything exciting? Nothing too wild! My niece, Emily, is coming down with her children, so a bit of chaos, I imagine. They're all obsessed with dinosaurs at the moment. I'll be trying to distract them with biscuits and a trip to the park.

Honestly, Valentine’s Day was a bit of a letdown, wasn’t it? Felt so manufactured. Tell me about it! Everyone was all loved-up, posting these Insta stories of roses and candles. I felt like hiding under a duvet. Exactly! Like, you’ve gotta work harder to feel romantic than just buying a bunch of overpriced red flowers. It felt…contrived. Did anything exciting happen with you, though? Not really. Mum made a huge roast, which was lovely, classic. My Nan insisted on sending me a box of chocolates - the ones with the really cheap caramel filling. You know, the ones that stick to your teeth? Oh god, yes! Those are a menace. She’s sweet, though. My mum just kept commenting on how single I still was. You know the routine. Oh, the routine is  always  reliable. My dad just winked, and said, “Plenty of time, love!” Like I’m going to suddenly sprout a partner next week. Haha! Right? It's like they think we’re formulaic. “Just add a romantic weekend and  bam , sorted!” Seriously though, what are you doing this weekend? Anything exciting planned now it’s all over? I’m heading to Birmingham actually, with my sister. Big shopping trip. She's been wanting to hit up Selfridges. Need a new winter coat, I reckon. This one’s absolutely seen better days. Ooh, sounds good! Birmingham’s got some decent stuff. I was thinking of catching a film. Have you seen  Oppenheimer  yet? Everyone’s raving about it. No! It’s on my list, though. A bit long, innit? I’m not the best for long films. Gets a bit…much. Yeah, it’s a commitment. We could go to that new Italian place on Elm Street, then the cinema. What do you think? That sounds perfect! That pasta place, Bella Notte? Their carbonara’s amazing. I’ve been craving it all week. Bella Notte it is then! You know, I was thinking, you’ve got such a good accent when you're excited. I always forget you grew up in Brum. Oh, you’re just teasing. It’s barely noticeable, yeah? I still sound pretty London, most people tell me. Being around Mum all the time helps keeps it going. No, it’s lovely! It's just… you get all enthusiastic and the Midland tones come out. It’s endearing! Aw, you’re being nice.

This broth is absolutely divine, isn’t it? Seriously, I could drink this all day. It’s pretty good. Bit salty for my taste, but good. You got the extra chilli oil? Yeah, loaded it up. Gotta have the burn, you know? So, what did you think of that article I sent you? About the new housing developments in Hackney? Ugh, don't even get me started. It’s just… blatant gentrification, isn’t it? Kicking out the existing community to build overpriced flats for City types. Exactly! And the council is just rolling over. Saying it's 'necessary for economic growth'. As if displacing people is somehow growth. It’s infuriating. It’s just the same story everywhere, isn’t it? Capitalism at its finest. Squeezing out the people who actually built the neighbourhoods. Totally. I was just looking at some plans for a new development down near Canary Wharf. This massive skyscraper, and they're claiming it will provide 'affordable housing'. Affordable for whom? A banker’s au pair? Pretty much. They’re playing with the numbers, you know? Defining affordable as something no one actually working in the area can realistically afford. It's disgusting. It makes you wonder… do they even see us? Do they notice there are actual people living here, with histories and families? I don’t think so. It’s like we’re just… obstacles to be cleared. It feels bigger than just housing, doesn’t it? It’s part of this wider conversation about immigration and… well, racism, really. You're right. It's all intertwined. The way they position immigrants as the problem, as taking 'our' jobs and housing, conveniently distracts from the fact that it's the system – capitalism – that's creating the scarcity. It’s just… exhausting. You know? Trying to navigate this world as someone who actually cares about equality and social justice. Tell me about it. I had a real awkward conversation with my dad the other day about it. He was saying how much house prices have gone up in Kensal Rise and how he's glad he bought when he did. Oh, god. Yeah. It's like… he's completely oblivious to the impact it has on the people who can’t afford to buy. He just sees it as a good investment. It’s that generational thing, isn’t it? They benefited from a different system, and they can’t see why it’s not working anymore.

So, the nursery thing is really happening next week, isn't it? Feels a bit surreal. Yeah, it does. Bittersweet, honestly. I'm excited for you to get back to work, though. You've been so… you know. Dedicated to Elsie. I have, haven't I? And I've loved it, don’t get me wrong. But I miss having a bit of independence, a bit of… something that’s just for me. And honestly, Elsie needs to mix with other kids, doesn't she? Definitely. She’s got a few friends in the park, but it’s not the same as being in a proper setting. Are you nervous about going back to work, though? A bit. It's been so long. I'm worried about remembering everything, about fitting in again. And just… the pressure. You’ll be brilliant. You always were. You just need to ease yourself back in. Don't try and do everything at once. And you’ve got a good job lined up, apparently. It is, thankfully. So, about Elsie… how’s the weaning going? Seems like a constant battle of wills! Tell me about it! She’s decided mushy peas are the enemy. Proper dramatic spitting and screaming. And she throws sweet potato like a projectile. Oh, Elsie! She's a character, isn’t she? I’m trying to be patient, but it's exhausting. I feel like I'm spending the whole day cleaning pureed food off the furniture. It's a phase. They all go through it. Maybe try something different? I read somewhere that sometimes they reject things because they're concentrating on other things, like teeth coming through. Possibly. I was thinking of trying those baby-led weaning things, letting her feed herself a bit more. Less mess, apparently. Yeah, I’ve seen bits about that. Might be worth a shot. So, future plans… besides surviving weaning, obviously. Any thoughts on a holiday? I’ve started looking at Spain actually. Somewhere with a beach. Elsie needs to feel sand between her toes, you know? And I need to feel some sunshine on my face. Just need to figure out the logistics. Spain’s good. Easy to get to. We could look at all-inclusive resorts, to make things easier. Less cooking, less cleaning... That’s tempting. Or maybe a cottage somewhere in the country. Somewhere quiet, with a garden for Elsie to run around in.

Right, so, updates. Anyone actually  enjoyed  their day? It was…a day. Fundraising is never glamorous, you know? Just relentless badgering for a good cause. At least the cause is worthwhile. Mine was pretty good! We had a staff competition at the shop, best window display. We won! Yeah, massive win. Best window display in Burton – we’re officially the reigning champs. That’s brilliant, Elara! Well done. George, what about you? Did you wrestle any particularly stubborn donors today? You could say that. Had one insist I had to promise him a signed photo of the CEO. It's ridiculous, the demands people make. Honestly! Well, my day, as you know, has been a bit… intense. What happened? You seemed a little stressed earlier. Remember that incident at the warehouse last week, the break-in? They finally got around to interviewing me. Had to give a full statement to the police this afternoon. Seriously? That must have been awful. It wasn’t… awful, just tedious. Lots of repeating the same things. Honestly, I'd forgotten half the details. They kept pressing me about security protocols, which, you know, aren’t  my  responsibility. Did they suspect anyone? They didn't say. Just said it's standard procedure to interview everyone who works there. I hope they catch whoever did it. It was a real blow to morale. Awful, I can imagine. Any luck sorting out that EE phone bill? You were fuming about it earlier. Don’t even get me started. They’ve added another £30! It’s outrageous. I spent ages on the phone with them, got passed from person to person. It's like a maze. Have you checked your data usage? Sometimes it's just a phantom spike. I have! It's no higher than usual. I’m pretty sure they’ve messed up the billing again. I’m going to escalate it to their complaints department tomorrow. It’s just such a waste of time. You really should consider switching provider. There are loads of better deals out there. I know, I know. It’s just such a hassle. But you’re probably right. So, plans for the week? Anything exciting? We’re heading up to the Lake District on Friday. Camping. Ooh, lovely! Weather permitting, of course. Camping? In November? Brave souls. It’ll be fine! We've got all the gear. It's booked, we’re doing it.

So, how’s married life treating you? Settling in okay with Sarah? Yeah, it’s… good. Really good, actually. Feels a bit weird, you know? Like a part of me is still single-guy-hanging-out-in-the-garden-all-day, but then another part's… settled. I can imagine. It's a big change. You’ve got the wedding photos still up, haven’t you? Sarah looked stunning. Thanks, man. She did. We've got loads. I’m still sorting through them, trying to make an album. I found a really weird photo of my uncle trying to wrestle the ring bearer pillow. Classic Uncle George! He'd do anything for attention, wouldn’t he? So, what have you been up to lately, besides adjusting to domestic bliss? Mainly gardening, obviously. Sarah’s really into herbs and spices now, so I’ve been expanding the herb garden. Got a proper mortar and pestle for her – she’s been wanting one for ages. Oh, nice! What’s she experimenting with? Something exotic? She’s trying to recreate this chickpea and bread thing she had in a Chinese restaurant. Apparently, it's a northern dish, and they use all these amazing spices. She was mumbling something about cumin, coriander, and… I don’t know, twenty other things. Sounds intense. I’m more of a plain bread and butter man myself. Speaking of, I made a fresh loaf this morning. You want a slice? I’ve got some homemade apricot jam. Don’t mind if I do! So, have you been watching anything good on telly? I’ve been re-watching Spartacus - the original, not the… the other one. Ah, Kirk Douglas! Proper classic. I always feel a bit sad watching it, though, knowing how many people died so young back then. Incredible acting, though. Yeah, it's a bit bleak. But the battles are fantastic. Have you read any good books recently? I’m trying to get into Roman history, but it’s a bit… dry. Mostly lists of emperors and dates. I get that. I tried something similar. I was thinking of diving into Plutarch’s  Lives  - more focus on character than just dates. It’s quite engaging. Actually, that sounds perfect. I’ll look it up. I'm already wishing I had some proper Roman snacks. Did you know they ate roasted nuts with everything? And figs? I did! We wouldn’t be able to handle the lack of proper tea, though.

Ugh, I’m so ready for the weekend. This week has been brutal. Tell me about it! Mrs. Davies was drilling us on all those nouns and adjectives for ages in English today. I swear my brain is going to explode. Seriously! And the English test is next week, right? I need to start revising, but… motivation is low. I’m still trying to recover from last Friday’s test. Oh god, me too. I completely blanked on that Shakespeare quote. I knew it! I  knew  it! It just vanished. I know the feeling! At least art was good today. Mr. Finch let us do free sketching. I think mine turned out alright. Did you finish yours? Sort of. I got distracted trying to draw Emily’s hair. It’s so shiny! I kept adding highlights and then I just gave up. It looked like a bird's nest. Emily  does  have amazing hair. Still, free sketching is always better than analyzing poems, right? Totally. What about French? Did you manage to remember all those prepositions? Nope. Monsieur Dubois just kept looking at me with that disappointed face. It’s terrifying. I’m thinking of asking my mum to get me a French tutor. That’s a good idea. I might do the same. I’m really struggling with the subjunctive. It’s so confusing! It is! Okay, random question: Did you hear about Liam and Chloe? No! What happened? Apparently, they were arguing in the cafeteria today. Something about Liam borrowing Chloe’s gel pens without asking. The gel pens! Those are like, sacred relics! Chloe’s devastated, isn’t she? Seriously! I heard her crying in the toilets. Poor Chloe. Liam is such a pain sometimes. He really is. And remember when he tripped over Miss Peterson's foot in assembly last month? Oh my gosh, yes! She was furious! Honestly, he's a walking disaster. Speaking of disasters, how's wind band going? Still torturing people with your trombone playing? Hey! I'm getting better! Mr. Harrison says I’m improving. Plus, the concert's next month, so we have to be. Are you practicing your flute? Barely. I’m way behind. I keep forgetting my fingering charts. I need to make a note of it somewhere. We  have  to practice more, otherwise, Mr. Harrison's going to have a meltdown. Remember last year when the clarinet section was completely off-key?

Lovely day for it, isn’t it? A bit breezy, mind you, but better than the rain we were having last week. Aye, it is that. Though I'm fair knackered after getting up early to get here. Darlington’s traffic is a nightmare, ya know. Traffic’s never  that  bad, Nan. Just exaggerating. Don’t you start, lad. Your Nan’s earned the right to exaggerate. I’ve been dealing with teenagers for thirty years, I’m allowed a bit of dramatic license. How’s school going, anyway? Exams looming? Yeah, mocks next month. History's brutal, to be honest. All those dates… History always was a struggle for young lads. More interested in the football scores, I bet. Well, City played brilliantly on Saturday! Proper thrashing. I saw bits of it on the telly. Good to see. Though, honestly, all this talk about player transfers these days… it's just commercialised entertainment, isn’t it? All branding and sponsorship. Tell me about it. Remember when football was just about the game, love? Not about who’s got the biggest shirt sponsor. And the accents! All these foreign players, barely attempting a Yorkshire accent - it's a disgrace. Oh, come on, Maggie. It’s the modern world. It's a global game now. Though I do miss the days when you could understand everything everyone said on the pitch. Nan’s always moaning about the accents. She says they all sound like they're trying to be American. Because they are, lad! Everyone wants to sound American these days. Even on the telly. It's all a bit depressing, really. Makes you proud to be from Yorkshire, though. Foot and mouth, the floods, the grit… we've weathered it all! Aye, we have indeed. Remember when the hospital had to close down for a bit? That was a worryin’ time, that. I only heard bits about that, Grandma. Why did it close? Budget cuts, lad. Always budget cuts. They’re closin' things down left, right, and centre. They say it’s for efficiency, but it just reduces access for people. It’s a disgrace. And they want you to eat healthily and exercise, don’t they? Tell me, is there a healthy cake? There’s always a compromise, Maggie. A smaller slice, perhaps? And less cream. Speaking of, did you see that article about the rising cost of living? Absolutely scandalous.

Right, everyone piled up? Plenty of roasties, I think. Can’t get enough of these, eh? Proper roast potatoes. Not those oven-baked things people try to pass off. Your potatoes always are lovely, darling. Secret ingredient, I reckon. It’s amazing how much we rely on potatoes, isn’t it? Such a staple. Though, perhaps a bit much given… the current climate, shall we say? You meaning what, David? Well, just… obesity rates are climbing, aren't they? And it's not all bad food, it's the sheer volume of carbs. It’s genetic too, you know. My dad always put on weight easily. Genetics, pah! It’s about willpower, son. I’ve been wrestling engines all my life, keeps you trim. You lot with your lectures… sitting down all day. Not exactly a fair comparison, Dad. And genetics do play a role, undeniably. My mum struggled with her weight too, despite eating healthy. Don’t start with that, dear. We're having a nice dinner, aren't we? Remember your Great Aunt Mildred - never touched a biscuit in her life, and she was practically disappearing! Speaking of disappearing, did you manage to finish the jigsaw, Mum? The one with the lighthouse? Nearly! Just the corner pieces. Those are always tricky. It’s just like life, really - often the last bits are the hardest. Though, not as hard as that time your father tried building a birdhouse. Hey! That birds house was a masterpiece! Just needed a bit more… reinforcement. More like structural integrity. Speaking of things needing reinforcement, how are your allergies doing, Mum? Did you need to take anything today? A bit scratchy this morning. The pollen’s been awful. Dr. Harris says I should be careful. He’s a good man, Dr. Harris – a bit rushed, but a good man. Said my operation was a success, mind you. Quite a shock, being laid up for a while. Glad to hear it, Mum. It's been tough on everyone. Have you been able to manage the gardening much? Not as much as I’d like, but your sister's been a darling, helping out. Though, she does over-fertilize the roses… I just like to be thorough, Mum. Anyway, did anyone catch that documentary on the BBC last night? About the connection between faith and… engineering? Faith and engineering? What nonsense. All that’s needed is a good spanner and a bit of common sense.

Right, so I was wrestling with Moodle again today. Honestly, it feels like a sentient being actively trying to make my life difficult. Tell me about it. What's it doing now? The discussion forums. I tried to embed a Padlet – you know, for collaborative brainstorming – and it completely messed up the formatting. Everything's all skewed and unreadable. I've spent an hour trying to fix it. Oh, the Padlet integration. That's always a tricky one. Did you try using the LTI link instead of embedding? Sometimes that works a little better. I did, but then it just opens up a new tab and people get confused. It's the seamlessness, isn’t it? It's supposed to be easy, integrated, accessible…and it just isn’t. Yeah, that's the frustrating thing. It looks so good in theory. I had a similar issue with the H5P thing last week – the interactive videos wouldn't load on some students' devices. Seriously? Which ones? Because I'm thinking about using those for the upcoming module on post-structuralism. The branching scenarios. They seemed fine on my machine and on the uni computers, but a couple of students reported issues on their phones. I ended up having to provide an alternative activity. That's so annoying! It's always the ones who have the oldest phones, isn’t it? Or the ones with the most obscure operating systems. Absolutely. It’s the digital divide in action. I'm starting to think I need to build a spreadsheet of known issues and workarounds for different devices. You're joking, but that's not a bad idea actually. A Moodle troubleshooting bible. We could share it with the department. We should. Seriously, I spent half my prep time yesterday just trying to figure out why the quiz submissions weren't registering for one student. Turned out the time limit was set to zero. Zero? Who sets the time limit to zero?! Apparently, me. Must have fat-fingered it. It’s easy to do. It's just… exhausting sometimes, isn't it? You spend so much time fighting with the technology that you don’t have time for the actual teaching. Totally. Honestly, I sometimes dream of just handing out printed handouts and having a proper discussion. Simpler times. Remember when we used to just use Blackboard? It wasn't exactly brilliant but at least it was… predictable.

Ugh, I feel like I'm wading through treacle. This jetlag is brutal. How are you holding up? Slightly better, I think. Still operating on Greenwich Mean Time, which is about three hours behind our actual time. Little one kept me up for a good chunk of last night. Tell me about it. Leo was having a monumental meltdown around 4 AM. Something about a missing teddy bear, apparently. It took twenty minutes and a rendition of ‘Twinkle Twinkle’ to appease him. Classic Leo. He’s a drama king, that one. Did you manage to get any sleep at all? A couple of broken hours, punctuated by baby noises. I’m running on caffeine and sheer willpower. So, about Saturday... Did you manage to sort out the tickets for ‘A Midsummer Night's Dream’ at the community theatre? Yep, got them. Front row seats, too. Figured we deserved a good view after the week we’ve had. Should be a nice distraction. Oh, brilliant! I’m really looking forward to that. It sounds lovely. I’m glad we made the effort to book it. It’s easy to let things slip with everything else going on, isn't it? Absolutely. Speaking of slipping… Need to ring Sarah about picking up the kids from playgroup on Monday. I completely forgot to arrange that. Oh dear. Let me know when you’ve done it. I can chase her up if you have no luck. Thanks. I will. It's just, balancing everything is a constant juggle, isn't it? Work, the kids, trying to remember to eat, let alone have a social life… Exactly! It’s exhausting. Are we thinking nursery for Leo next term? I feel like we’re at that point where we need a little bit of breathing room. I think we should seriously consider it. I've been looking at Bright Horizons - they seem to have good reviews. It's just… sending him somewhere new feels a bit strange. I know, but we can't keep running ourselves into the ground. And he'll benefit from socializing with other children. Plus, a little peace and quiet would do us both the world of good. True. We'll have to go and visit a few places and see what we think. I'll put it on the list – right after sorting out Sarah and reminding myself to actually sleep sometime this week.

So, have you heard from your sister’s family in Erbil lately? Last I heard, they were still wrestling with the paperwork for her kids’ visas. Not recently. It’s a nightmare, honestly. The bureaucratic hoops you have to jump through… It's disheartening. Her husband’s trying to get them all tourist visas, just to get them out of Iraq for a bit, give them some breathing room. But it's temporary, of course. The long-term stuff… it's just stalled. They’re relying on a private immigration lawyer now. Costs a fortune, but what choice do they have? It’s scandalous, isn’t it? The disparity. My cousin in Berlin, she got her niece from Ukraine a visa practically overnight. And here, a family fleeing instability... it's a different story. Exactly. It’s not about merit, is it? It's about who has the connections and the money. Speaking of connections, did you ever hear back from the embassy about that specialist visa for your colleague, Dr. Hassan? Nothing yet. I had a slightly awkward meeting with someone there last week. They seemed… preoccupied with certain geopolitical issues. Kept bringing up oil prices and the instability in Libya. Of course they were. Everything always comes back to oil, doesn’t it? And the influence of… well, you know. The Wahabis? It's terrifying the way their narrative is shaping global policy. It's like a slow-motion disaster. It is. And the young people… they're growing up in this atmosphere of constant conflict and uncertainty. My nephew, Omar, he’s 18. Brilliant student, wanted to study engineering. Now he's just… withdrawn. He says he sees no future for himself there. That’s heartbreaking. It's the same here, you know. My students… they're disillusioned, angry. They feel powerless. Trying to teach Shakespeare when the world feels like it’s actively crumbling… it’s difficult. I understand. It's hard to feel optimistic. But we have to keep striving, right? Keep fighting for those visas, keep supporting those who need it. Speaking of moving, how's the house search going? You mentioned something about viewing a place in Woolton last week? It’s… progressing, slowly. Honestly, the housing market here is insane. That place in Woolton was lovely, a real character cottage, but the price was astronomical. And the estate agent kept going on about “potential,” which translated to “needs a complete renovation.”

That lamb was absolutely divine, wasn’t it? Honestly, the best I’ve had in ages. It was brilliant, love. Really hit the spot. You’ve outdone yourself. Don't you flatter her, David. It was a perfectly acceptable roast, nothing spectacular. Though the potatoes were lovely. Oh, Mum, you always say that! You’ve been saying that about my roasts since I was ten. Well, it’s true. You were always a bit… experimental in the kitchen. Remember that time you tried to make a cake using beetroot? Don’t remind me! It was a disaster. The dog wouldn’t even touch it. Speaking of, how’s Buster doing? Still terrorising the neighbourhood? He’s grand. He’s got a new nemesis – Mrs. Henderson’s poodle. They have stand-offs in the park every morning. It’s hilarious. These modern dogs... so much energy. In my day, dogs were sensible. They stayed by the fire and didn't chase small, fluffy creatures. Times change, Mum. But at least we have him for company. It’s a bit lonely here otherwise. I’m still not loving this rented place, though, are you? The landlord keeps threatening to ‘inspect’ the garden. He’s just trying to assert his authority. Don’t worry about it. Have you looked at those cruise brochures I left on the coffee table? I have! A Mediterranean cruise? Sounds wonderful. Though I’m not sure my fitness level is up to it. I need to get back into some sort of workout routine. Nonsense! Keep walking, dear. That’s all you need. And a bit of Scottish tablet afterwards – that’s essential for strength. I brought some, actually. From that little shop on Victoria Street. It’s the real stuff, not that cheap imitation. Oh, you shouldn't have! Though I probably  shouldn’t … my waistband is already protesting against the lamb. A little bit of indulgence is important. Living a long life requires it. Although, you know, they do have that new TV in the dining room now. It's quite distracting if you’re trying to have a conversation. Oh, Mum, not the TV again! It’s supposed to be a dining room, not a cinema. She's got a point, love. We were barely talking during the news earlier. Distraction city. Exactly! It encourages dreadful habits. Everyone glued to a screen. Remember when families actually  talked  at dinner?

Honestly, I'm starving. Anyone fancy ordering something? I’m proper skint though, so it’d have to be cheap. Yeah, I'm starving too. Remember that terrible Chinese place down the road? Could get a load of spring rolls for a fiver. Absolutely not, Liam. Remember last time? I swear, I could still taste the… well, I don't  want  to remember. She’s got a point, Liam. Let's not repeat that experience. I’m up for cooking something though, if people are in. Got pasta and some sauce. Pasta's good, mate. Proper good. Beats spring rolls that taste like old socks. Okay, pasta it is then. What about uni plans though? Any news? Still nothing. Keep getting rejection letters. Feels like I’m shouting into a void. Don’t let it get you down, Liam. You’ve got a good degree, it'll happen. University's not the be-all and end-all anyway. Yeah, true. Loads of people do amazing things without a degree these days. Besides, more time for this pasta feast! Easy for you to say, Danny. You’ve got your TA job and you’re actually  doing  something. It's alright. The kids are a handful sometimes, but it's good to be around them. Helps you remember why you’re doing it, you know? You’ll be a brilliant teacher, Danny. Always were good at explaining things. Speaking of which, how's your grandma doing? Saw she was poorly last time I spoke to Mum. She’s a bit better, thankfully. Still slow, but she’s got her sparkle back. Mum's driving her mad though, constantly fussing over her. My mum’s the same with my nan. It’s like a competition to see who can be the most worried and overprotective. Sounds familiar. My mum’s constantly asking if I've eaten enough. Like she thinks I’m going to starve to death out here. It's just love, really. They worry because they care. True. Anyway, speaking of love… How’s things with you and Finn, Chloe? Oh, shut up, Maya. It's going well. We went for a walk along the coast yesterday. It was freezing, but really nice. Proper romantic. You spoil them, do you? Hey! He bought me a  hot chocolate . It was freezing – see? It all comes back. You're all hopeless, you know that?

Right, so I need to get these fairy cakes baked for tomorrow’s lesson. Do you reckon twelve is enough, or should I do a batch of eighteen? Eighteen! So everyone gets two! Two! Two is good! Can I lick the spoon again, Mummy? You already licked the spoon, darling. And you got frosting everywhere! Let’s see… twelve or eighteen. Well, Ms. Davies said to focus on measuring, so each child only needs one to practice with. Twelve it is then. Poppy, can you help me sprinkle the sugar? Yes! Pink sugar! You’re a star. So, right, what are we actually  doing  in the lesson tomorrow? Remind me. We're doing maths! And singing! That’s right. We're measuring the sprinkles and comparing how many each cup contains. And then we'll sing 'Five Little Ducks'. It's always a winner. Quack, quack, quack! Exactly! Oh, and we need to remember to talk about fractions. Bit tricky for this age, but we can do a simple demonstration with the cakes. Half a cake, quarter of a cake… Daddy got us a special half-birthday cake yesterday! You did! A little chocolate one, with candles and everything. Did you see how big the candles were? Really big! I turned five and a half! You did indeed! And Oliver is four and a half. Speaking of which, have you two been playing Tomodachi Life on Daddy’s tablet? Yes! My Mii got married to a penguin! A penguin, did she? Well, that’s a bit different! Oliver, what’s your Mii doing? His is building a house! Out of cheese! A cheese house? You and your penguin friend. Right, focus, Mummy, focus on the fairy cakes. I need to check if I have enough icing sugar. I think I picked up a book in Morrisons yesterday, actually. Remember? It was all about baking… Did it have a picture of a cake? It did! A very colourful one. I thought it might have some good ideas for the lesson. It was hidden behind a pile of gardening books, can you believe it? Did you find any other good books? Well, I found a really old copy of 'Where the Wild Things Are'! It was a bit battered, but the pictures are still amazing. I might need to read that to them as well. It's a good one to talk about emotions with, you know?

It’s lovely to finally get out of the house, isn't it? The weather has been awful all week. Absolutely. Needed this. Work’s been… well, you know work. Endless marking. Tell me about it. I’m wading through essays on Victorian literature. Honestly, some of them read like they’ve been written by a robot. No spark, no personality. Sounds brutal. I’m dealing with undergraduate film analyses – a whole other level of… creativity. Some of it’s genuinely insightful, though. That’s nice to hear! Anyway, did you see that post Sarah made on Facebook? About her new car? Oh, the SUV. Yes, I did. A giant, metallic… thing. Exactly! I don't understand the obsession. All that petrol, the parking struggles, the sheer size of them! It’s a status symbol, isn’t it? Like, “Look at me, I can afford to drive a tank.” Ridiculous. I'm still clinging onto my little hatchback. Reliable, economical, and easy to park. Sensible man. I'm worried about buying a new car too. Everything’s so expensive now. And the internet – the sheer volume of advertising when you're even thinking about buying something… It’s terrifying, isn’t it? You just mention you’re considering a new model, and suddenly your entire online life is flooded with targeted ads. It feels a bit… invasive. It is! And the prices they advertise... it's all designed to lure you in. I saw one for a very nice Volvo - looked amazing online, but the added extras and delivery charges... it was extortionate. They always get you in the end. It’s the same with everything online. You start searching for one thing, and suddenly you’re three hours later, down a rabbit hole of obscure products you never knew existed. Oh, definitely. I was looking for a new tea kettle last week, and ended up watching seventeen videos about artisanal ceramic tea cups. See? The internet. A wonderful, terrible thing. So, back to Sarah’s SUV… Do you think she’s secretly regretting it already? Probably. Give her a month when she’s struggling to parallel park in Tesco’s car park. Then she’ll be wishing for a little hatchback like yours. Let's hope so. Another cider? It's a beautiful evening. Absolutely. Let’s. You’re right, it is. Should be a bit windy though, right? Probably.

Right, so, the day at work was absolutely mental today. Seriously. Had to deal with three returns in a row, all for different reasons. One lady swore the toaster she bought five minutes ago was already broken. That’s silly, surely? Tell me about it. Five minutes! Honestly, people. Anyway, what do you reckon of this film? It’s a bit weird, innit? It’s good. I like the food falling. It’s funny. Yeah, it’s bonkers. But like, do you think it's  just  about food falling? Bit of a message about consumerism maybe? No, it's just about food. Falling. Fair enough. You've got a much simpler view of things than me. Right, can you pass me the remote? I just fancy a quick drink. It’s… there. I think. Seriously? How does it always end up there? Okay, right, lemme just... Blimey, this remote's a nightmare. Just press the red one. The red one? What red one? All these buttons! See, that's what I mean about how things have changed - technology is just needlessly complicated. It's easy! The red one! Right, there we go. Blimey, I’m starving though. Did you eat anything before we came over? Just a biscuit. Just a biscuit? You're tiny! You should eat more. Maybe we should get some chips later. Or pizza? Pizza. Definitely pizza. Right. Back to the film. The guy's pretty hopeless, isn’t he? Flint. Just inventing stuff that goes wrong. He’s trying! I know he's trying. But he's making the situation massively worse. You know, I read an article the other day about how women are always portrayed as the responsible ones in these stories, and the men are just... chaotic. What? Never mind! Just forget I said that. It's a film about food falling from the sky. No need for a deep dive into gender roles. It’s just silly fun. He should’ve made vegetables fall. Why vegetables? Because vegetables are good for you. That’s a very sensible point, actually. Restricting it to just meat and desserts was pretty damaging to the world, wasn't it? Look, honestly, the artistic license they took… It’s wild. Do you think they thought about the ecological impact of giant meatballs? I want a strawberry. You and me both. Look, I’m going to sneak off and see if your mum’s got any biscuits.

So, you're saying things are really tight back home then? Even for a taxi driver? Tight? Mate, it’s bordering on ridiculous. Petrol prices are through the roof, insurance, congestion charge…you name it, it's gobbling up my earnings. And don’t even get me started on parking. It sounds…familiar. Though I imagine the landscape is a little different than the autobahn. I’m hearing a lot of the same stories back in Liverpool from people I know. The cost of living is just relentless. Aye, relentless is the word. And all this talk about the economy…it’s all just words, innit? Politicians spouting nonsense while the rest of us scrape by. Well, politics has always been a bit of a performance. Even in Germany, though the scale, thankfully, feels somewhat less…chaotic at times. What do you make of this current government, then? Don't get me started on 'em. Another load of posh blokes who’ve never driven a taxi in their lives, let alone worried about filling up the tank. Remember New Labour? Tony Blair? Seems a long time ago. A significant shift, certainly. Blair had a certain…charm. A manufactured charm, perhaps, but effective. I recall a lot of hope attached to those early years. Charm won't pay the bills, though, will it? And everything’s been going downhill since then, to be honest. It's like nobody's listening to working people. They’re all stuck in their bubbles, don't they? Talking about some economic models and things I can’t even understand. I understand the frustration. It's a disconnect, isn’t it? Between those who shape policy and those who are affected by it. It’s something I address in my teaching, trying to show my students how language constructs and perpetuates these divisions. That's a clever thing to do, that. I bet you can get a good debate going in your classes. You know, football's another good way to stir things up around here. Liverpool’s having a storming season. Indeed! Klopp's done a remarkable job. The energy in the team... it's palpable, even across the Baltic Sea. Though, I'll admit, I'm more of a Dortmund man at heart. Roots, you know? Dortmund? Alright then. So, you’re a German who supports a German team. Typical. Loyalty's a wonderful thing, I suppose.

Right, so I’ve been wading through these BNC recordings all morning. Honestly, the variety of phrasing people use to say the most mundane things is just…fascinating. Like, twenty different ways to describe having a cup of tea. Sounds like you’ve got a proper rabbit hole there! You always did love a good linguistic deep dive. So, how’s LinkedIn treating you this week? Any exciting job offers lurking? LinkedIn is… a landscape. A relentless, slightly overwhelming landscape of people being  very  impressive. I’m mostly avoiding it at the moment, to be honest. It's making me feel slightly inadequate. LinkedIn's a waste of time! Just put your head down and do good work! Thanks, Mum. Always the voice of wisdom. Mum's right, you know. But I get it. It’s good for networking, but the performative aspects are exhausting. I’m mostly on Instagram these days, just scrolling through pictures of Pugs. Pugs are adorable. Do you ever think about… I don’t know… moving somewhere completely different? Like, escaping the London hustle? Loads. I miss Wales, obviously. I'm thinking of booking a long weekend back. Maybe try and squeeze in a whale watching trip if the weather's decent. Remember Pembrokeshire? The sunsets were unreal. Oh my god, amazing. I'd love to come. I haven't been back since uni. It feels like a lifetime ago. Thinking about escaping… I was looking at flights to the Maldives the other day. Just as a hypothetical. The Maldives! Fancy! That’s seriously escaping. You’re brave, you know, flying. Brave? I’m terrified! Honestly, the thought of being that high up in the air makes my palms sweat. It’s ridiculous. But the water… the pictures are just breathtaking. Just book the flights! What’s the worst that could happen? Mum, please don't encourage me! I'd probably faint halfway through. Although, maybe a little hypnotherapy… You should have a go! I was thinking about Spain as well actually. Just wandering around Seville, soaking up the sun… No flying involved, just a train. That sounds heavenly. Honestly, just the idea of being somewhere warm… I’m so over grey skies and drizzle. What about you? Any travel plans besides Wales? Not really concrete. Work’s been a bit mad, deadlines everywhere. It's funny, isn't it? How much we romanticize escaping, when really, it’s just about finding little pockets of peace wherever you are.

Right, so I’m thinking chicken tagine tonight. Got all the spices, apricots… should be good. What do you reckon, Auntie Carol? Sounds lovely, darling. Much better than that frozen pizza you attempted last week. Remember the smoke alarm? Don't remind me. A learning experience. Speaking of experiences, I was thinking about getting a tattoo. Oh really? What on earth for? And where? Not sure yet. Maybe on my forearm. Something small, meaningful. I don’t want a massive dragon or anything. Just… a little something. Well, think long and hard about it, love. Tattoos are permanent. And that’s coming from someone who has a rather regrettable one herself, I might add. You and your rose bush, Auntie Carol. It was the eighties! Everyone had a rose bush. Anyway, are you still living at uni for Christmas? Yeah, mostly. I’m coming back for a few days, obviously, but most of my mates are staying put. All this student debt means Christmas is a very low-key affair. Sensible. Less expense. Listen, I’ve got an intern starting on Monday. From UCL. Apparently, very bright. Oh, that's good. Is she going to be any help or another one who just makes endless cups of tea and asks where the stapler is? Let's hope not. She seems enthusiastic, at least. It's so hard to find good ones these days. Honestly, they just want Instagram opportunities, not to learn about the craft of editing. That’ll be Liam. Right on time! Liam, darling, come in, come in! We’re just making dinner. Liam: Hey! Sorry I'm late, got held up at the garden centre. Couldn’t resist getting a little tree early. Oh, you shouldn’t have! It's adorable. Bless you. It’s so early though! Liam: Well, the festive spirit called! So, Carol, how’s the editing going? Any juicy projects? Terribly busy, as always. Just finished proofing a rather lengthy biography about… well, it’s not really important who. It was a beast, honestly. So many footnotes. Liam: Sounds intense! You deserve a huge glass of wine tonight. Speaking of wine, I was thinking maybe we could go into town on Saturday, do a bit of Christmas shopping? It’ll be rammed, but… Liam: I’m in! Need to get a present sorted for my mum. She’s impossible to buy for. Honestly, all these deadlines at work are making me want to bury myself under a blanket and not come out until January.

Right, nearly ready! What do you reckon, is this enough chilli? I’m always nervous of not having enough. I think it smells amazing, honestly. And yes, probably a bit more kick wouldn’t hurt. Remember that time we went to that Thai place in Soho and I practically cried from the spice? Oh god, yes! You were a mess. I kept offering you milk, and you just glared. This isn’t  that  hot though, promise. It’s more of a warming flavour. I added a bit of ginger too, to lift it. Good thinking. I'm starving, by the way. How was your pilates this morning? Did your hip give you any bother? It was okay, surprisingly. Progressing, I think! Definitely felt it afterwards, though. Still stiff. I’m thinking of trying that reformer Pilates class Sarah was raving about. Apparently, it's amazing for core strength. Ooh, yes, Sarah did say that. I might look into that too. I need to actually  do  something, rather than just talk about it. I’ve been so busy with work lately, I barely have time to breathe, let alone exercise. I know the feeling! This article I’m working on is a beast. Apparently, I need to interview this expert in… obscure Irish folklore. Honestly, where do they find these people? Sounds fascinating, though! You always end up with the weirdest assignments. Reminds me, did you ever manage to look at flights to Morocco? I was thinking Marrakech in the spring. I did! Prices are insane at the moment, sadly. I was looking at flights in April, and they’re already pushing £400. Maybe we should push it back to May or June? Yeah, that’s probably sensible. I just need a break, you know? Somewhere hot and sunny with lots of colourful spices and… tagine. Definitely lots of tagine. Perfect! Tagine is mandatory. Okay, I think this is good. Let’s set the table. Oh, and I found this amazing new recipe for lemon and cardamom cake. Thought I'd try making it tomorrow. Ooh, you are spoiling us! That’s so lovely. You know, I’ve been meaning to try making more sourdough. Actually, I bought that proving basket Sarah recommended. It’s really cute, woven. Oh, nice! I'm hopeless at sourdough, I keep killing the starter. It’s like a tiny, bread-based pet that I can’t keep alive.

Honestly, that seminar on post-structuralism today was a disaster. Half the students were actively disengaged, and the other half just seemed confused. I felt like I was talking to a wall. Oh, that’s rough. Was it the usual suspects, or did you have some new faces in the apathy brigade? A bit of both, actually. Liam was, predictably, scrolling through Instagram the whole time, but even some of the ones who usually seem interested were just… blank. I tried to steer it towards Derrida’s concept of  différance , but it just seemed to glaze over.  Différance . Right. Always a crowd-pleaser. You need to start throwing in some memes, I reckon. A Derrida cat. You’re terrible. Seriously though, I'm starting to wonder if I’m just not connecting with them. Maybe I need to rethink my approach. You're a brilliant lecturer, you know that. It's just… students these days, right? Short attention spans, constantly plugged in... Exactly! It's exhausting. Speaking of exhausting, my toes are killing me. I really need to book myself in for a pedicure. They're a disgrace. You’re always complaining about your toes. They were perfectly acceptable last week, weren’t they? Don’t be cheeky. They're never  perfectly  acceptable. And all this walking around campus doesn't help. Did you hear back from Sarah and Tom about the weekend? Not yet. Sent them a message this morning. I was rather hoping they'd be up for it. It would be nice to actually see them, you know? It feels like ages since we all got together. I know, right? We’re always saying we should make more of an effort. Then life just gets in the way – marking, seminars, lectures… and toe maintenance. True. I think it’s important to prioritize. Friendships are vital. We need to schedule something, a proper date in the diary. Maybe that new Italian place they opened? That sounds lovely. Let's definitely chase them up. I'm craving pasta already. Although, knowing Sarah, she'll probably want to talk about her new succulents for three hours. That’s Sarah. We wouldn’t have it any other way, would we? These lights are really pretty tonight though, aren't they? They give everything such a warm glow. They do. It’s nice to just walk and talk sometimes, without any pressure. It is, isn't it?

Honestly, I’m still reeling from that new Scorsese film. Did you see it?  Killers of the Flower Moon ? Yeah, I managed to catch it last week. Three and a half hours, though! A commitment. Tell me about it! I felt like I needed a lie down afterwards, but it was… incredible. The performances, the cinematography. It was just brutal. Absolutely. DiCaprio's acting was phenomenal, wasn’t it? Though, you know, he's wearing those almost cartoonish prosthetics now. You can tell it's him really struggling to look older… I noticed that! A bit distracting, actually. But I think it worked ultimately. More distracting was the sheer bleakness of it all. Real history, of course, but still…gut-wrenching. It is. Speaking of bleak, did you see that article about Johnny Depp? Apparently he's doing some bizarre, experimental art exhibition in Venice. Oh, horrifying! I try to avoid celebrity stuff, but it just pops up everywhere, doesn't it? I saw something about him and Amber Heard too, back in the news, somehow. It's just…a mess. A complete mess. It’s hard to know what’s real anymore, isn’t it? Everything's so manufactured and sensationalized. Makes you think there's something bigger going on, doesn't it? You’re going down the rabbit hole again, aren’t you? Maybe. I was reading about the QAnon stuff the other day. I know, I know! It’s ridiculous but the reach of that stuff is genuinely concerning. I avoid anything that even hints at conspiracy theories. It gives me a headache. I’d rather just watch a nice, simple baking show. More your speed, I suppose! How's the teaching going? Still a whirlwind of teenage French? It is! They’re fascinated by reality TV at the moment. Every conversation somehow circles back to  Love Island . It’s exhausting. Trying to get them to discuss Proust is like… pulling teeth. I can imagine. My niece is obsessed with that show. I don’t get it. I watch  Strictly  every week though. It's so comforting. Oh, you’re a  Strictly  fan! I always intend to watch it, but I never quite get around to it. You should! It’s a palate cleanser after all the doom and gloom. How are the kids? Last I heard, Leo was having a phase where he only wanted to eat beige food.

Dad, are we nearly there yet? This journey is taking forever! Nowt ever feels like it’s 'nearly' when you’re 16, love. It always feels miles off. We’ve still got a good chunk to go before we get to Cornwall. I know, I know, but I’m bored. And my phone’s nearly dead. Did you charge my charger? Aye, it’s in the glove box. Though I reckon you should put it away for a bit. Look out the window, love. See that field? All those poppies? Looks like a Jackson Pollock painting, doesn't it? It’s nice, I guess. Bit red though, isn't it? Everything’s so…brown. It’d be nice if the roads were painted some other colour. Like yellow. Like in The Wizard of Oz. Right you are. Yellow roads and green skies. That’d give people something to talk about. Reminds me of a Sherlock Holmes story, you know, the one where the landscape was all wrong… Oh yeah, the one where he had to figure out what happened because the scenery didn’t match what people had said? That’s the one. It’s about observing, isn't it? Paying attention to detail. Like Lewis Carroll. Did you know he was a mathematician? All those riddles in Alice in Wonderland… Yeah, they’re confusing! I prefer fairy tales. Cinderella, Sleeping Beauty… proper stories. There's a logic to fairy tales, lass. A moral. Even if it's just don’t talk to strangers. Right. Are you sure you’ve got your map downloaded? Signal's a bit patchy around here. Yeah, I've got Google Maps. Don't worry. Should we stick to the A30 or take the scenic route? Scenic route could add a couple hours. But… look at that wind farm! Amazing, innit? Remember when those were just a pipe dream? Yeah. They’re quite pretty actually. Like giant white… um…things. Flowers in the sky, I reckon. See that hedgerow? Full of wildflowers. And listen—fieldfare! Hear them? I think so. Are we getting close to that place Jamaica Inn? I read about it. Apparently, it’s really spooky. Aye, it is. Used to be smugglers' haunt, you know. Real history there. Though I reckon it's probably full of tourists now. Heard a fascinating thing the other day – did you know back in the day, before phones, people used to send messages using telegraphs?

Right, so Grandad, did you see the new petrol prices? Absolutely ridiculous, aren't they? Aye, scandalous, lass. Used to get a full tank for a couple of quid back in the day. Now you're lucky to get a quarter for that. Bleedin' rip-off, that's what it is. It's supply and demand, really. Geopolitical factors... inflation… Oh, here we go with the engineering explanations again, Jack. Can’t just let a good rant happen, can you? It's just an observation, Elodie. Doesn't mean I don't empathise with the outrage. Fancy a walk, though? The light's lovely out there. Walk? At my age? I'll be lucky to make it to the loo, lad. Remember when I tried to climb that hill in Cornwall? Nearly broke a hip. You tried to climb a  slightly  sloping field, Grandad. Still, it’s a hill to me! And I had to be helped down by a nice young lady whose name I've completely forgotten now. Such is life. Speaking of life, Elodie, how's the corpus work going? Still wrestling with those tagging schemes? They’re a nightmare, honestly. Trying to categorize colloquialisms is like trying to herd cats. I swear, some phrases just refuse to be pinned down. It's like that game we used to play when I was little, remember? Spot the difference, but with words? Aye, I remember! You were always cheating. Swapping the jam for the marmalade and claiming no one noticed. I was a strategic thinker, Grandad! You were just easily distracted. Like when Auntie Maureen tried to hide her sweets during Christmas. Auntie Maureen was legendary. Remember that time she tried to smuggle a whole box of chocolates through airport security? And claimed they were medicinal. Said they helped with her nerves. Bless her heart. She used to tell me stories about the war, you know. Ration books and air raid shelters and all that. Terrible times. I was looking at old primary school photos the other day. Remember those awful yellow jumpers we all had to wear? It's a wonder anyone survived. Distinctly remember those jumpers. Utterly hideous. What year were you in, Elodie? Year three, I think. Mrs. Hawthorne was our teacher. Strict, but fair. Did you go to primary school near Timperley, Grandad? Aye, St. Bartholomew’s. Fancy that – they still have inter-house swimming galas!

Right, that’s the last of the boxes from the flat. Feeling utterly wrecked, Mum. Jet lag is  real . Oh, darling, you look it. Come, sit down. I've made you a proper cuppa, strong, just how you like it. And I did a roast chicken, your favourite. Roast chicken? You absolute legend. I was mentally preparing myself for builder’s tea and digestive biscuits. Nonsense. You’ve travelled halfway around the world to see your old Mum, you deserve a feast. So, tell me, how’s the new flat coming along? Did you get all the flatpack furniture sorted? Mostly. The bookcase was a nightmare. I think I put it together backwards at one point. Had to dismantle it and start again. Progress is… slow. I’ve got a monstrous list still to do. Let me see. You said you needed new curtains, a rug, that lamp you were eyeing up... Oh, and you mentioned a new kettle. Don’t want you drinking lukewarm tea, do we? Exactly. And I need to sort out a proper shelving unit for the study. Space is… compact. Thinking about getting one of those tall, narrow ones. Well, your Auntie Maureen is clearing out her shed. She's got a lovely oak one. Strong and sturdy, you know. I can ask her. Seriously? That would be amazing, Mum! You're a lifesaver. It would be so much better than fighting with flatpack instructions again. Speaking of lifesavers, I need to remember to book a dentist appointment. It’s been ages. Oh yes, your teeth. You always were a worrier about your teeth. Remember when you were little and you swore you saw a weaver fish lurking in the paddling pool at Butlin’s? Oh, God. Yes! I was convinced it was going to bite my toes. Dad had to practically drag me out of the water. I was terrified. Silly boy. It was just a bit of seaweed. But you were so dramatic. You inherited that from your grandfather. He once swore he saw a ghost in the garden! It's nice to be back. Even just for a few days. Feels good to be home. Are you getting on alright on your own? Still seeing David? Yes, darling. David's wonderful. We went to that new Italian place in town last week. Delicious. He's been a great help with the garden, you know.

Honestly, look at that fella's clematis. Proper jungle, isn't it? It is a bit much, yeah. Needs a trim, definitely. You reckon our roses will be alright after that storm last week? Aye, I gave ‘em a good watering yesterday. They seemed okay. I’m thinking of trying some of that liquid feed this year, see if it gives ‘em a boost. Good idea. Did you see that thing about the A-Level reforms? Apparently, they are dropping practical assessments. Typical, isn’t it? More emphasis on just the exam. What about all the skills they should be learning? It's all about numbers and league tables, isn't it? No real focus on actually  doing  anything. Exactly! It’s like, “Memorise this, regurgitate it on the day, and you’re sorted.” Doesn’t prepare anyone for the real world. My mate's daughter is doing art, and she’s gutted about it. Poor lass. Art needs to be practical. You can’t paint a masterpiece in an exam hall. So, what are you thinking about doing with your hair after it’s grown a bit? Honestly, I’m just going for the “relaxed, I’m-a-PhD-student” look. It’s likely to remain a chaotic mess. You thinking of a new style? I was, actually. Maybe a bob? Something a bit shorter, easier to manage. I've been staring at pictures all week. But I keep thinking, will it suit me? You’d look brilliant. Seriously. You’ve got great cheekbones, a shorter style would show them off. You're just saying that to be nice. No, I’m serious! And besides, you always look amazing. Speaking of looking amazing and also worrying… Did you see petrol prices are going up again? Don’t even start. It’s ridiculous! I filled up last week, and I'm already dreading the next time. How are people supposed to afford that? Especially those who have to drive for work. It's awful. And it's all interconnected, isn't it? The supply chain issues, the war... Aye. It's all mad. Makes you think about the NHS too, doesn't it? All these fuel costs for ambulances and doctors... Absolutely. They're already stretched so thin. It’s just…a lot. It is. Mind you, at least the garden’s looking lovely. True. That’s something to be grateful for.

Honestly, I’m proper skint this month. Between rent and lectures, it’s brutal. Tell me about it. I’m rationing my oat milk like it’s liquid gold. Cambridge prices, eh? They'll bankrupt you before you even finish a degree. You're lucky if you even  get  a degree, like, with all the strikes and stuff. I swear, I'm starting to think I should just get a job in Greggs and be done with it. Don't say that, Chloe! You’re brilliant! Besides, Greggs is a decent shout. Sausage rolls are life. True, but I’m trying to quit the fags, and those things don’t exactly help. It's proper stressful trying to stop, innit? It is. Have you tried the patches? My mum swears by them. Though she also thinks essential oils can cure everything, so… take that with a pinch of salt. Patches are rubbish. Give me nicotine gum any day. At least you can hide it. I got caught chewing one in a lecture the other day, the professor gave me the look of death. Oh my god, I remember that. You looked so guilty. Reminded me of when I tried to sneak a vape in the library. Got told off by a librarian with a permanent frown. Right nightmare. Anyway, speaking of stressful…did you see that article about how the gender pay gap is even  worse  for young women? Oh, don’t even start me. It's absolutely infuriating. All this talk about feminism and progress and we’re still being paid less for doing the same job. It's depressing, isn't it? Like, what’s the point in even trying? Though, I suppose trying to do nothing is equally pointless. I saw this TikTok about it, actually. It was explaining how, like, historically, women were literally just… forgotten in official records. Footnotes in history. It was mad. Proper mad. Makes you think, doesn’t it? Like, how much stuff are we missing out on because society’s been designed by and for men for centuries? Loads. Absolutely loads. My history tutor was talking about the Black Death the other day, y’know. Apparently, afterwards, women ended up inheriting land and businesses because so many men had died. Suddenly, they had power! Woah, really? That’s actually kinda cool. So, like, a pandemic actually gave women more rights for a bit?

It’s just… vast, isn’t it? Sometimes I think that’s how I feel about friendships lately. Vast, endless expanse, but with so much wave crashing around that you can’t actually see anything clearly. You’re being dramatic, Liv. But I get it. You've been quieter than usual, even for you. Is it about Chloe and Mark? Partly. It’s more than that, though. It's just... I've realized I don't really  want  to see them anymore. Properly want to. Not out of obligation, or because we’ve known each other since we were kids. And that's the messy part, isn’t it? Letting go of history. Definitely. It feels almost… disrespectful, doesn’t it? Like you’re invalidating all those years. Exactly! Everyone keeps saying, 'Oh, you've been friends since forever!' Like that somehow makes the feeling mutual. But it doesn’t. And I’m tired of pretending it does. I'm tired of the effort. So, what are you planning to do? Just… ghost them? Because that feels brutal. Absolutely not. I’m not a monster. I’ve thought about it, obviously, but that's not me. I was wondering about… phasing out, I think. A slow fade. A slow fade. That's a good way to put it. My grandma used to call it "letting the threads unravel." It's less jarring. See? Even your grandma has wisdom to impart. It's just... how do you  do  that without causing a scene? Chloe, especially, will be on the phone demanding a heart-to-heart. Classic Chloe. Honesty used to be her superpower, remember? Now, it’s just a weapon. Look, I think you just have to be subtle. Less availability. Shorter replies. Vague excuses. Vague excuses. Right. "Oh, I'm terribly busy…" “Something came up…” I feel like a teenager trying to get out of a family dinner. Well, you’re basically trying to do the same thing, just with slightly more complicated emotional baggage. Remember how Dad used to handle Aunt Margaret’s endless phone calls? Oh God, yes. He'd answer, say "Yes, dear," and then just trail off muttering about needing to check the washing machine. Then hang up. Exactly! Master that level of non-committal mumbling. It works wonders. Okay, "Yes, dear… the washing machine…” I like it. But what about Mark? He’s always trying to organise things – weekend hikes, pub quizzes… With Mark, you just need to be… busy.

This lentil soup is amazing, Gran. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Oh, you’re just saying that because you're starving, darling. University life does that to a young man, doesn't it? It really does. I swear I live on instant noodles and whatever the college canteen throws at me. It’s… sustaining. Not exactly enriching the soul, though. Enriching the soul requires more than lentils and canteen food, my dear. It requires museums and galleries, conversation, travel… Have you been to any good exhibitions lately? Not really, no. Been too busy with lectures and the dissertation looming. I’m trying to focus on that, you know? It’s all about post-war abstract expressionism. Daunting stuff. Abstract expressionism… Jackson Pollock, Rothko? It’s not my favourite, to be honest. A bit too much splattering, not enough soul. I prefer a good Klimt. All that gold, that intricate detail… now there’s something to look at. You should come and look at some of my newer pieces, actually. I've been experimenting with encaustic again. I'd love to, Gran. When are you free? And are you still planning that trip to Italy in the autumn? Oh yes! Trying to finalise the details now. Florence, Venice, maybe a little excursion to the Dolomites. I’m thinking of taking a sketching course while I'm there. Need to keep the creative juices flowing, you know. Your cousin, Leo, is supposed to be in Florence around then too, isn't he? Yeah, he’s doing his internship at that architecture firm. He mentioned wanting to meet up, but I haven’t heard anything definite yet. Should I chase him up? Perhaps. It would be lovely if you all could be together. It’s been far too long since we’ve all been in the same place. Your brother’s grown so tall, hasn't he? Last time I saw him, he was still wearing short trousers. Yeah, he's a proper teenager now. Moody and obsessed with football. But he’s good, you know? Doing really well at school. Good! That’s what matters. Though sometimes I wish he’d develop a little artistic inclination. He has your grandfather’s hands, you know – perfect for sculpting. He says sculpting is “messy” and “boring.” Typical boy. What are you reading at the moment? Anything good? I just finished “The Labyrinth of Secrets” by Kate Mosse.

Right then, nearly halfway through this leg, I think. Feels like forever though, doesn't it? Yeah, a bit. Poland’s… a lot of fields. Beautiful, though, honest. Just a bit…monotonous to look at while concentrating, you know? I know exactly what you mean. I was just thinking about when I used to go to the gym back in Cambridge. I always had to eat something substantial beforehand, otherwise I’d just collapse. Proper protein and carbs. Yeah, I’m the same. A banana and a yogurt barely cuts it. Need a full-on breakfast, especially after a long drive like this. Speaking of which, how much longer do you reckon? Google Maps is being annoyingly vague. It said about an hour and fifteen. But those things are never accurate, are they? Depends on the traffic. Or if we get caught behind one of these massive Polish lorries. True. It's just, I’m starting to feel a bit wired. Need to get back to a routine, properly. Want to hit the gym tomorrow morning, really get a good session in. Good for you. Getting back into it. It’s good for the mind, too, isn’t it? All the endorphins. Definitely. It's better than… well, better than thinking about how frustrating it is trying to find a decent teaching job. Especially when you’re female. Oh, don’t start me on that. I’ve seen so much nonsense. Honestly, the recruitment processes. So often just full of… subtle biases. Tell me about it. I’ve had a couple of interviews where the questions were just… weird. Like, “Do you think you’d be able to manage a class full of rambunctious boys?” It’s always phrased as a genuine question, too. Not even sarcastic. It’s that assumption, isn’t it? That women are naturally better suited to primary school or childcare. Anything that isn’t… assertive enough for the 'proper' leadership roles. Exactly. It’s so infuriating. You have to be twice as good to get half the recognition. And even then… It used to be… different, you know. When I left university, it felt like things were changing. More opportunity. More fairness. It's a backwards spiral sometimes, isn't it? Feels like we're constantly fighting to maintain what we’ve already won. Exactly. Beautiful light, isn't it? It is. Peaceful. Do you think it’s alright if I have a little nap?

It’s a lovely morning, isn’t it, Mum? The sun’s finally decided to show its face. Though I do worry what the rain’s done to the seedlings. Aye, it's a grand morning. Though a bit breezy, mind. Give the washing a good whirl, that does. Did you remember to bring the milk in from the doorstep? That fella, young Tom, leaves it there regular as clockwork. Already done, Mum. Brought it in straight away. I was admiring your new mugs, by the way. These hand-thrown ones are gorgeous. Who made them? Oh, Elsie from Saltaire. She's a lovely lass, Elsie. Got a little stall down at the festival next month. You should pop along. There's always good stuff. I’d like that. I do enjoy the Handmade in Bradford festival. Though last year, remember, that awful power cut? Right in the middle of the Morris dancing! Aye, that was a mess. Nearly tripped over half the dancers, I did. And my poor ears! All that shouting when the lights went out... Speaking of tripping… I’m still a bit shaken up after my little mishap yesterday. Knocked over a whole pot of petunias while trying to deadhead them. Oh dear, love! Are you alright? Did you hurt yourself? Just my pride, really. And a few muddy knees. Honestly, I felt like such a clumsy fool. There was a spider lurking amongst the fallen petals too. Gave me a right fright. Spiders! Don't like 'em, not one bit. Used to have a little phobia when I were a girl. My dad used to catch ‘em in a jam jar and take 'em outside. Always thought they were watching me. Sounds like my dad. Always had a soft spot for the wildlife. Did you manage to get your decorating done, Mum? That little bedroom… Nearly there. Just needs a final coat of magnolia. It’s a tricky colour to get right, you know. Not quite white, but not cream either. Awful colour, magnolia, really. Gets everywhere. Reminds me of that Doris Featherstone - always dressed in magnolia. You and Doris Featherstone! You always had your opinions about her. Remember when she fell and broke her wrist delivering those raffle tickets for the WI? Aye, that I remember. Poor lass. Though, she did always argue about the price of rhubarb at the market. You remember Harold and Betty, don’t you?

So, are we  actually  going to France then? Or is Dad going to chicken out again? Don't be silly, sweetheart. Your grandad's booked everything. Flights, the little cottage… the works. We’re definitely going. Aye, lass. Booked and paid for. Wouldn't miss it for the world. Needed a break from this damp weather anyway. Lancashire's been dreary. Okay, good. I was worried. Last time we tried to go, he got all stressed about passport photos and ended up cancelling the whole thing. That was a few years ago, darling. He’s much better now. Besides, I've organised everything, taken the stress out of it all. Passport photos done weeks ago. She's a good woman, your mum. Organised as anything. Keeps me on the straight and narrow. Are Chloe and Liam coming too? They said they would, but Chloe's got that big exam next week, so she’s a bit nervous about being away. Liam's definitely coming though. He's buzzing about seeing all the castles. He will be! All he cares about is history. Do you think we’ll actually get to see Mont Saint-Michel? I really want to. Aye, lass, we'll get you to Mont Saint-Michel. I’ll play a bit of Breton folk music for you there too, set the mood. Oh, grandad, don’t start planning concerts! Just enjoy the holiday. I've packed your accordion, haven't I? Aye, wife, you have. Can’t have a holiday without a bit of music, can we? Keeps the spirits up. What about Sam and Jess? Are they going? Sam’s sadly stuck with that overtime at the warehouse. But Jess said she confirmed she is coming. She's been looking at all the French restaurants online and sending me recipes. Ooh, maybe we can try and make some of them when we get back. French crêpes sound amazing. Crêpes! Now you're talking. Reminds me of a little place I played in Paris, back in the day… Grandad! Let’s stick to this holiday for now, shall we? Don't start telling stories about your younger days again. Please don’t! I'll fall asleep. Alright, alright. Just saying, lass. Paris is a lovely city. You'll enjoy it. Just be careful of pickpockets. Exactly! That’s my lecture for the holiday, everyone – keep your valuables safe. Okay, Mum.

Ugh, that film was  amazing  though, right? Heath Ledger! Totally! I literally screamed when he did that poem for her. It was so cringe but so…romantic. I know! Kat Stratford is my hero. Such a proper icon. Though I wish I was as cool as her when I was fifteen. Yeah, I’d love to just say exactly what I thought, without caring what everyone else thought. School’s making it hard to do that right now. Tell me about it. Mr. Davies is being  so  unfair in history. He keeps marking me down on my essays because I don’t ‘conform to his expectations’. What does that even mean? Seriously! It’s like he wants us to all write the same boring thing. Mrs. Peterson in English is way better – she actually encourages us to be creative. Definitely.
