I think I’m going to ask her about my personal statement. I have absolutely no idea what to write about. Me neither! I mean, I like art, but is that enough? Should I talk about my pottery? Maybe? It’s gotta be something different, right? Everyone’s gonna be talking about their sports or volunteering. I’ve been thinking about trying out for the school orchestra next year. Really? That’s cool! Which instrument? I was thinking cello. It just seems…vibey. Plus, it wouldn’t be something everyone else is doing. That's a great idea! Remember when we were little and we both wanted to learn the harp?  Laughs  Oh my god, yes! We were convinced we’d be professional harpists touring the world. Exactly! Anyway, back to the serious stuff...London! Are you excited for next month? So excited! But also stressed. We have to figure out what we want to do. The British Museum is a must, obviously. Definitely. And maybe the Tate Modern? I read about this amazing exhibit… plus, we need to go shopping in Camden. Camden! Yes! I need a new jacket. Do you think we should try and see that musical everyone's talking about? Wicked? We should! Mum said she might be able to grab us some tickets, but it depends on the price. Let’s hope so. It would be the perfect way to end the trip. Although I’m mostly excited about the food. Me too! All those cute cafes and shops... We have to find a bookstore too.

Right then. This chamomile's quite pleasant, Patricia. Not like that peppermint stuff you tried to foist on me last week. Tasted like mouthwash. Oh, come on, Arthur, it's good for digestion! You need something for your digestion. And relax, for goodness sake. You've been frowning like a thundercloud all afternoon. Is it the Facebook again, Grandad? Are you having another row with someone about politics? It's that Sarah Miller! Posting about… about that religion business again. Telling everyone she's 'found her path' and sending prayers up to… well, I won't repeat what she said. Blasphemy, I tell you. Sarah's always been a bit… intense, hasn't she? Remember when she tried to convert Auntie Maggie to Wicca? Oh, good heavens, yes! Maggie nearly fainted. Thankfully, she just put it down to the heat from the oven. Didn’t like it one bit. Not even a bit. Want to talk about something else. Is your little Lewis still having bother? He’s much better now, thankfully. He had a truly awful patch of chicken pox last week. Covered head to toe. It was heartbreaking. Poor little darling, he was so miserable. All those little itchy spots! It must have been awful watching him discomfort. It is a dreadful thing. Thank goodness it's mostly gone now. Just a few little scars, nothing to worry about. Remember when Elsie had it. Back in 58. Oh, don’t bring that up! Elsie screamed for three days straight. Grandad, you always tell that story. It's a bit morbid, isn’t it? Well, it’s a story. And I remember it. And it shows you how things were back then. No fancy creams or anything. Just calamine lotion and a lot of patience. It's funny, isn’t it? How much we obsess about things now. I was reading an article the other day about OCD. Compulsive behaviours that people develop... Arthur used to worry about that, about germs, you know when we used to go away camping. You did used to wash your hands a lot, didn't you? Well, one must be clean! There’s no point in getting ill, is there? And it's something a man must do, to prepare. You were practically sterilizing the campsite, Grandad! Don't you start, Sarah. A clean campsite is a happy campsite. Anything's better than germs, I tell you.

Right, so dinner’s nearly ready. Who’s feeling hungry? I’ve gone for a proper Sunday roast this week – beef, all the trimmings. Sounds amazing, Mum! Definitely hungry. Been glued to my screen all day, deadlines are a killer. I'm starving! Can I set the table? Which wine are we having? Red, I hope. You know I prefer it with the beef. And someone get me a cushion, these chairs are murder on my back. Still complaining about the chairs, are you, David? They’ve been like that for twenty years! Remember when we got these? Oh, goodness yes! David insisted they were “mid-century modern”, didn’t he? We were so young and thought we knew everything. Mid-century modern, my foot! They're uncomfortable! Something smells heavenly though, Sarah. Thanks, Tom! Just trying to recreate my mum's roast dinner. It always felt so special. Remember those holidays in Germany, everyone squeezed around the table? Oh, yeah! Grandma’s dodgy German. "Wo ist die Toilette?" forever. And Grandpa trying to haggle for souvenirs in broken German. He’d end up paying double, wouldn’t he? I rather liked trying! It’s good to make an effort, even if you’re butchering the language. Besides, some of those stallholders spoke brilliant English, they just enjoyed watching us stumble. Don’t forget the time your dad tried to order a beer and asked for a “rolling stone”. They looked utterly bewildered. He did! And then he insisted he’d said it perfectly. Classic David. Speaking of classic, did anyone ever figure out what happened to Uncle Barry's old Jaguar? The one he used to drive around in? Vaguely remember it. Wasn't it that awful shade of green? Like pea soup. It was terrible! But he loved it. Said it was a “statement piece”. I heard it ended up in a salvage yard somewhere. Shame, really. It was a beautiful car in its day. Oh, I remember. So did you all enjoy your holidays this year, it’s nearly the same time next year. Yes, absolutely. France again. It was great to escape to somewhere warm. I went to Italy with some friends from university, it was great to breathe some new air. I couldn't get out, so it was just me keeping the workshop going. Don't worry, the whole family will hopefully get out next year.

Hey, good to see you, Liam! Been ages. Your mum’s cooking smells amazing, as always. Mate! Good to see you too, Tom! Yeah, she’s on form today. Proper Sunday roast vibes. So, what have you been up to? Still drowning in uni work? Pretty much! End of term madness, you know. Essays, projects… the usual. But it’s almost over, which is a relief. How’s the chef life treating you? Still at The Pheasant? Yep, still there. It's hectic, absolutely mental on a Saturday night, but I’m learning loads. They’re letting me get involved in more menu development now, which is brilliant. That’s awesome! Always fancied giving cooking a proper go, but I’m just not coordinated enough. Did you ever hear back about that internship at the Wildflower restaurant in London? Yeah, actually, I did! Didn’t get it, unfortunately. They went with someone who had a bit more fine dining experience, apparently. Bit gutted, but it's alright, got to keep trying, right? Yeah, totally. Those things can be brutal. Still, more experience for the CV. What are you listening to at the moment? Anything good? Loads! Been properly into Dry Cleaning at the moment. Their new album is sick. The guitars are just…  chef's kiss . Have you heard it? Yeah, yeah, they're brilliant! Saw them live a couple of months ago. The energy was insane. Florence Shaw is just magnetic, isn't she? 100%! Proper stage presence. I'm trying to get back into drumming too, you know, dust off the sticks. Been a while. Seriously? That’s amazing! You were always a wicked drummer. Any gigs coming up? Should I come along? Potentially. I'm jamming with a few mates, nothing solid yet. But yeah, if we get something organised and you're free, definitely let you know. What about you? Still playing guitar? Occasionally. Mostly just noodling around in my room when I'm stressed. Nothing serious. I’ve been going to a few gigs though. Saw The Static Echoes last week - they were surprisingly good live. Heard of them. Are they any good on record? Yeah, their first album is great. Bit indie, bit post-punk. Give it a listen. What about Mark and Sarah? Still together? Yeah, they’re good. Just bought a flat together down by the docks, actually. Apparently, the view is amazing.

Right, this is lovely. Needed that. All this rushing about! It’s really busy in here, isn't it? Can you hear what they're playing on the radio? It's a bit loud. I can, a bit. It's alright though, adds to the atmosphere, don't you think? More lively than a quiet cafe. So, we got everything on the shopping list? Milk, bread, teabags… Yeah, pretty much. Forgot the Yorkshire Tea though. Oh, bother! Right, I’ll add it to the list. We’ll get it tomorrow. Speaking of tomorrow, are you free to come to that domino drive on Saturday? The community centre’s having one. Dominoes? Nah, not really my thing. I'd rather watch the Newcastle game. Is it on? Always football. Yes, I think it is. But your Uncle Barry will be there, and your Auntie Maureen makes her famous gingerbread. Alright, maybe. Depends what time it starts. And if I can sneak out early to see the lads after. We’ll see. Let’s not get ahead of ourselves. Listen, have you thought any more about what you want to do after your A-Levels? University? Apprenticeship? Not really. Everyone’s talking about Durham, innit? Loads of people from school are looking there. Durham's lovely. It’s a beautiful city. Maybe something to consider. But you could look at apprenticeships too, you know? There’s a software engineering place, right near Newcastle, that seems decent. Remember I showed you that article? Yeah, yeah. It’s alright. But it’s all coding and stuff. Well, you’re good at computers. And they're always looking for people. This country needs more entrepreneurs, you know? People with good ideas. Like Elon Musk? Something like that, but maybe less…explosive. You'd get a good wage too. And think of all the holidays! Still reckon I’d rather play FIFA. You and your FIFA. Right, tell me, what did you think of that documentary about obesity they had on the news last night? It was quite shocking, really. It was a bit grim, yeah. All those people struggling to move. Precisely. It’s a real problem, isn’t it? Anyway, let’s not get all doom and gloom. Are you thinking about that summer holiday yet? We could go camping again this year. Camping? Seriously? Yes! Fresh air, stars… we could get new sleeping bags, ones that are really comfy.

So, what do you reckon? Not bad for a first attempt at decorating, eh? Still a bit… sparse, maybe. Nah, it’s brilliant, man. Honestly. Really nice space. Proper calming. Sussex suits you, I reckon. More… chilled out than Bedford ever was. Definitely. It’s a breath of fresh air. Been meaning to ask, how's things back in Bromsgrove? Still battling the traffic on the M5? Don't even get me started! It’s a nightmare. Though… things are going pretty well actually. Work’s good, the missus is… well, she's got some news, in fact. Oh? Do tell! Don't leave me hanging. She’s pregnant. Blimey! That's massive! Congratulations, mate! Seriously, that’s fantastic. When are they due? Early January. It’s a bit mad, isn’t it? Suddenly, spreadsheets and assurance become significantly less important than, you know, tiny human survival. Absolutely. Speaking of things getting more important, I’ve been trying to get this linguistics recording finished. It's awful, though, practically a monologue. Need to get the ‘proper’ conversation happening. I was thinking, maybe focusing on colloquialisms… you've still got that proper Midlands twang, you know. Gold dust for research. You’re trying to exploit my accent for your academic purposes, are you? Typical! It's for science! And it’s fascinating. Did you hear about that study on how regional accents are disappearing? It’s heartbreaking. Yeah, awful, innit? My mum’s always going on about it. 'Don't you dare sound like you’re moving down south, lad!' She’s obsessed. My nan's the same. It’s like they're terrified of losing a piece of their identity. Anyway, about that recording… could you maybe drop a few Midlands gems for me? Like, any phrases you only ever heard back home? Right, let me think... there's "Now then" of course... can't escape that. And "Our kid" when referring to anyone, not just your own children. Utterly universal. Brilliant! Actually, I was trying to explain 'Now then' to a Korean student the other day – complete blank faces! Koreans, eh? Still planning on heading out there again, then? Thinking about it. It’s just… the cost of living over there is getting ridiculous. And the hassle of all the visa stuff... and trying to understand those application forms. It’s enough to make you want to just stay here and garden.

Honestly, Sarah, I'm just…exhausted. It’s been a week, hasn’t it? Since we heard about Auntie Carol. It has, hasn't it? Feels like a lifetime already. Still can't quite believe it, can you? Such a shock. A complete shock. She seemed…robust, you know? Always pottering about, gardening, visiting the grandkids. Cancer just…took her. So quickly. It does, doesn't it? It’s brutal. And the way it's affected Mum… I’m really worried about her. Me too. She’s trying to be strong for everyone, but I saw her yesterday, and she was just…blank. Staring out the window, not really saying anything. That's exactly what she was doing when I spoke to her this morning. Just kind of… distant. She keeps saying she’s fine, but you know Mum. 'Fine' means she’s on the verge of a proper meltdown. Absolutely. We need to keep an eye on her. Maybe suggest she see Dr. Evans? He’s always been good with her. I’ve already mentioned it. She brushed it off, said she’s just tired. Typical Mum. I feel like I'm walking on eggshells half the time. And the kids… Leo’s been quiet, which is worrying. Usually, he’s bouncing off the walls. He’s probably processing it. Kids internalise things, don’t they? My Mia’s been sketching a lot, mostly flowers. It's rather beautiful, actually, but feels a little…sad, you know? Yes. Grief manifests in different ways. Have you spoken to Daniel about it? He's always been close to Carol. Briefly. He’s busy with the move, naturally. But I think he’s taking it harder than he’s letting on. He just said, “She was a good woman.” Very stoic. You know Daniel. Yes, Mr. Strong and Silent. He’ll probably bury it all and it'll surface later. I’ve started going to that yoga class in Lichfield, you know. The Wednesday evenings? It’s actually helping with the anxiety a bit. That's good! You should. I haven’t really been looking after myself lately, with all the proofreading deadlines and Mum's…well, everything. I've been living on coffee and biscuits. You need to prioritize yourself, love. You can’t pour from an empty cup. Seriously, book a slot. It's really quite relaxing. And they do a lovely herbal tea afterwards.

Right, so, football scores this weekend? Anyone have any particularly good or bad ones to report? Villa lost, Mum! 2-1. It was awful. Honestly, they didn't even try. Harsh, Liam. Every team has a bad day. Did you watch the whole game? Yeah, all of it. It was painful. Man U won. Good for you, Ethan! See, it’s not all doom and gloom. So, Liam, anything exciting happening at school this week? Not really. Exams are looming. The history teacher’s being particularly evil. History’s never easy. What are you studying at the moment? Tudors. Henry VIII mostly. Right, plenty to moan about there then! Ethan, how’s the tennis coaching going? Did you have a session this week? Yeah, it was good. Coach says my serve’s improving. That’s brilliant! You’ve been putting in the hours. Dad, you remember how you were saying you were thinking about investing in that new vegan bakery down the road? I am, yes. Had a proper chat with the owner yesterday. Seems like a really smart, driven young woman. The business plan’s solid. And it’s growing, isn’t it? I saw a queue out the door the other day. It is. Which is encouraging. It’s a bit of a risk, obviously, but early signs are good. Sarah, what do you think? I think it sounds promising, honestly. Just do your due diligence, make sure you’re comfortable with the potential downsides. And think about the legal stuff, right? Contracts and all that. Already on it. I've got a friend who's a solicitor, I’m running it past him next week. Liam, what about you? Got any ideas what you want to do after school? Anyone mentioning apprenticeships yet? Not really. I mean, everyone's just stressing about GCSEs at the moment. I was thinking about maybe doing a sports science apprenticeship. That’s great, Ethan! A fantastic option to combine your passion for tennis with gaining some real-world experience. Have you looked at any local providers? Yeah, a few. There’s one in Birmingham, seems pretty good. Good. Do your research, Ethan. It’s a really valuable route. It's a shame the whole apprenticeship scheme got messed up with the referendum, lot of uncertainty around funding for some areas. It’s a shame, definitely. It knocked back a lot of opportunities, didn't it?

Right, so Lancaster then. It feels ages since I’ve been up north. It does! And I’m really looking forward to seeing your Auntie Maureen. She’ll be so chuffed you're visiting. She will, won't she? I feel a bit guilty, I haven’t seen her properly in… well, it’s been too long. She always sends the best Christmas cards, you know? Detailed little watercolour paintings. She’s lovely. Are you planning on heading to the coast while you're there? Maybe Morecambe? I was thinking about it. Although, I remember one time, years ago, we went to Morecambe, and there was this…cockle disaster. Oh god, don’t remind me! I think we bought a huge bag from one of those stalls, and they were all gritty and tasted of seawater. It was awful. Absolutely revolting. My stomach was churning for hours! We'll definitely have to get fish and chips instead then, won’t we? Proper chippy, not that pre-cooked stuff. Agreed. Fresh cod, loads of salt and vinegar. Perfect seaside food. Are you still thinking about applying for that Masters in Linguistics at Lancaster Uni? I am, yeah. I had a look at their modules and it actually looks really interesting. A bit daunting though, the dissertation… I know, right? Mine feels like a monumental task. I think I’ve written like, three opening paragraphs and then just stared at a blank page for a week. That sounds about right. Procrastination at its finest. Have you had any luck with the job research? You said you were looking into more specialist roles? A little. There’s a couple that look promising, but they’re both asking for a significant amount of experience in corpus linguistics, which, let's be honest, I’m still developing. That's a tricky one. But your experience as a Research Administrator is super valuable. Don't undersell yourself. It’s all about transferable skills, right? I try to tell myself that. It’s just a bit unsettling seeing everyone else seemingly have their careers all sorted. Especially with what's been happening at your dad’s company. Has he heard anything more about the potential redundancies? Not much more. They're still 'exploring options', apparently. Which is corporate speak for 'massive job cuts are coming'. It’s making Mum really anxious, obviously. That must be awful for her.

Honestly, I'm still buzzing from that Arctic Monkeys gig last night. Liam was mental, wasn’t he? Mental doesn't even cover it! Crowd was insane. Nearly got knocked over like three times. Worth it though, right? Absolutely! Best night out in ages. Did you manage to get near the stage at all? Not really, no. Ended up pretty much at the back, but the sound was still pretty good. You? I was a bit further forward, managed to snag a spot near the barrier for a couple of songs. Alex Turner was actually looking right at me at one point! No way! You’re kidding. Which song was it? "Do I Wanna Know?". Honestly, I froze completely. Just stared back like a lemon. Probably looked like a right idiot. Nah, he probably thought you were a dedicated fan, soaking it all in. You always do. I just felt proper awkward. What about you, did you film anything? I wish I’d have got more on my phone. Tried to, yeah. But kept dropping it! Seriously, I’m a liability in a crowded space. Got some shaky footage of "Fluorescent Adolescent" though, it's mostly people’s heads, to be fair. We need to share our videos, then.
