She used to say, "a pinch of this and a handful of that,” you know? Women of that generation were all like that. No precise measurements. It was all about gut feeling and instinct. Much better than these complicated recipes you see now. True. I was reading about it the other day – apparently, there’s a whole science to baking now, explaining why certain ingredients react better with others. I downloaded this app, "Bake Smarter," that analyses your recipe and suggests tweaks to improve the outcome. Oh really? How does it work? Sounds a bit complicated. It’s surprisingly intuitive. You input the ingredients and measurements, and it tells you things like whether you’re overmixing, or if your oven temperature is too high. Apparently, even altitude affects baking! Altitude? Good heavens! I never thought of that. Me neither until I started reading about it! Apparently, you need to adjust leavening agents at higher altitudes to prevent flat cakes. Well, that’s all very interesting, but I’m more interested in how we’re all moving! Look at you two, practically bursting after all that food! We really need to get back to regular walks. You’re right, Brenda. I've been a bit lax with my fitness this week, I must admit. All this delicious food hasn't helped! I've been trying to be good. I’ve been using that fitness tracker you got me last Christmas, Mum. It's pretty motivating seeing how many steps I've done each day. I walked over 10,000 yesterday exploring the coast path. Wonderful, dear! Honestly, it's made such a difference to my energy levels too. I've been trying to fit in a brisk walk most mornings. Speaking of things that are making a difference... did you hear they’re finally opening the new train station in Totnes?

Right, so, you saw “The Lie” then, didn’t you? Yeah, last night. Absolutely brutal, wasn't it? I mean, I knew the basics of the story, obviously, but… wow. Proper gut punch. Absolutely. The cinematography was amazing too, wasn't it? Bleak and beautiful, all at the same time. Felt properly claustrophobic. Definitely. Did you spot the little Shakespeare reference? The guy quoting Hamlet at the end? No way! I missed that. Where? Just before he…well, you know. It was subtle, but there. Thought it was a nice touch. A bit on the nose, maybe, but I appreciated it. Clever. Right, speaking of bleak... Premier League looking dodgy this year, isn’t it? Tell me about it. Spurs are actually looking decent though. Didn’t see  that  coming. They're on a good run, I’ll give you that. Man City’s relentless though, isn't it? Like watching a machine. Yeah, it’s almost boring now, isn’t it? No real competition. So, how’s the seminar going for your Shakespeare module? Ugh, don’t even get me started. Professor Davies is… intense. He's really pushing us on textual analysis, which is fine, I guess, but he’s got this habit of just staring at you when you answer a question. Sounds terrifying. Remember old Mr. Peterson in sixth form? Had a similar stare. Could wither a plant with his gaze. Exactly! It's like he's trying to drill the answer into your brain. And some of the course mates… honestly, they’re all so keen to show off. I know the feeling. Uni's full of those sorts of people. Trying to out-intellectual each other. It is, isn't it? Anyway, speaking of out-doing each other... Marco's already planning his stag do. Has got the spreadsheets  and  the PowerPoint presentation. Oh god, no. Marco and organised fun… those two words rarely go together. What's he thinking this time? Something involving paintballing, an inflatable maze, and a trip to a brewery. It's going to be horrific. Classic Marco. I'm not looking forward to the photos. You going to Cardiff for the weekend soon? Yeah, meeting up with Liam and a few others from the rugby club. Should be a laugh. Trying to avoid pubs this time. Last time involved a questionable karaoke performance of "Bohemian Rhapsody." Oh heavens. That’s a memory I’d rather forget.

Oh my gosh, it’s  so  good to see you, Liv! It feels like ages. Honestly, Oxford felt like a different planet. You too, Chloe! Honestly, seeing your face is a massive mood boost. It  has  been ages, hasn't it? How's everything been? You look well! Yeah, pretty good, all things considered. Work’s been… well, work. Project deadlines are a constant source of stress, as you can imagine. But I'm managing. How's the marketing life? Still knee-deep in campaigns? Oh, you have no  idea . It’s a whirlwind. We’ve got this massive launch coming up next month, so I’m basically living on coffee and adrenaline. Pearson's been good to me, though. The team’s brilliant. That's good to hear. Are you still seeing anyone? Nope. Officially single. Turns out, dating apps are a minefield. Had one date where the guy spent the entire time talking about his collection of vintage bottle openers. Seriously. No! That is absolutely insane! You deserve better than a bottle opener enthusiast. I’m still single too, by the way. Turns out, that uni ‘researcher’ was more interested in his precious fungi than, well, anything else. Oh, Chloe, you deserve a king, not a mushroom hunter! Seriously, what was that about? You seemed really into him at one point. I know, right? I was blinded by the… the intellectualism, I guess? He kept quoting obscure poetry at me. At breakfast! It got exhausting. Anyway, enough about our disastrous love lives. How’s your family? Still battling it out over Sunday dinners? Oh, you know it. My mum's been on my case about settling down. Apparently, being nearly thirty and single is a national crisis. Tell me about it. Mine's subtly hinting that I should start thinking about…you know… “biological time” and all that. Don't even. Do you want to order? I'm starving. I saw they have those amazing lemon and poppy seed scones. Yes! Absolutely. Scone sounds perfect. And maybe a latte. I'm flagging. Are you thinking about that trip to Morocco we talked about? I really am! I was looking at flights the other day. Maybe next spring? Somewhere warm and sunny where I don’t have to answer questions about my relationship status. I'm so in! We need a serious escape. Although, I’m terrified of the food.

Right, tea’s on! Fancy a biscuit with yours? Got some gingers left from Nan’s visit. Cheers, love. Ginger sounds perfect. How are things with your mam? I haven't heard much lately. She’s good, yeah. Bit moany, as always, about the cost of heating, but otherwise alright. She sent me a load of photos of the garden, actually. Apparently, the roses are coming out early this year. That’s lovely. She always had a green thumb, your mam. I’m still battling with this spider plant. It’s got like, fifteen little plantlets hanging off it, but the main plant looks utterly miserable. Oh, the drama. Spider plants are notorious for being dramatic. Have you tried repotting it? Sometimes they just need a bit more space. I was thinking about it, but I’m terrified I’ll kill it in the process. I have a terrible track record with houseplants, honestly. My flat looks like a botanical graveyard sometimes. Nah, you’ll be fine. It’s just a plant. Want me to show you how to repot it? We could do it later. It’d be a nice bit of downtime. That's really kind of you, thanks. I might take you up on that. Actually, speaking of downtime, Nan was telling me about this amazing chicken and chorizo bake she made the other day. It sounds ridiculously simple, but apparently, it’s incredible. Ooh, tell me more! I'm always looking for easy dinner ideas. Research has been absolutely manic lately, I barely have time to boil an egg, let alone make something fancy. Apparently, you just chuck chicken chunks, chorizo, peppers, onion - whatever you fancy, really – in a tray, drizzle with some olive oil, season it, and bake it. And then she put a layer of chopped tomatoes on top for the last half hour. That  is  brilliantly simple! I might have to give that a go. I've been trying to cut down on takeaway, you know? It's murder on my bank balance. Totally. I've been attempting to channel my inner Jamie Oliver, but with considerably less success. I once tried to make a risotto. Ended up looking like congealed wallpaper paste. Oh, bless you. Don't we all have those cooking disasters? My attempt at macarons last Christmas was... unforgettable. Ended up looking like misshapen pebbles. Macarons! Brave move. Those are notoriously tricky.

Morning, Rhys. Dreadful weather we’re having, isn’t it? Though, I suppose it’s a change from the heatwave. Morning, David. Aye, it is that. Could do with a bit more sunshine, mind. Managed to get a bit of gardening done on Saturday though, before it properly rained. Good man! I always admire those who manage to keep their gardens looking shipshape. Mine is a jungle at the moment. The weeds are having a field day. Did you see that young lad, Messi's son, playing football on the telly the other day? I did! A bit too flashy for my liking. Reminds me of that young Gareth Bale when he was starting out. All tricks and no grit, you know? The modern game. It’s changed so much. It has. Though, there's still talent out there. Speaking of talent, have you been watching the snooker? That Ronnie O'Sullivan is still incredible. Aye, the Rocket! Still got it, hasn’t he? Though he’s a bit…eccentric, isn't he? Mind you, most of the top players are. Gets you thinking about discipline and focus, doesn’t it? Absolutely. Which brings me to something I was thinking about. I’ve got a few students worried about their future. They’re looking at jobs like the police and the armed forces – seems a sensible prospect these days, with everything going on. It is, isn’t it? A good, stable career. But very competitive. Entry standards are incredibly high, as they should be. I know a few young men who’ve tried and haven’t made it. Brutal stuff. Exactly. One of them was asking about the fitness tests. Apparently, they’re not just about running. It’s all about strength, endurance, and technical skills. It's a right slog, I hear. You’ve got to be dedicated. My nephew tried for the army a few years back. He didn't make it through the medical. Apparently, a minor knee injury from playing rugby years ago held him back. A real shame. That’s awful. Life can be so unfair. Speaking of setbacks, I'm completely drowning in marking. This batch of essays... some of them are truly... challenging. Tell me about it! I’ve got a stack of dissertations to plough through, too. Political Science, of all things. Some of the arguments are… well, let’s just say they require a  lot  of red ink.

Right, so let’s run through it all again. Lizzie’s birthday is the 18th, isn’t it? Yep, 18th of October. Three weeks away. Feels like it's creeping up fast. Cake! Cake! Yes, darling, cake. We’ll definitely have cake. Now, about the venue… are we still thinking The Swan? I rang them today, Mum. They’re booked solid that Saturday. Apparently, there’s a wedding reception on. Oh, really? That’s annoying. Where else could we do it? The community hall is always a bit… clinical, isn't it? We could look at The Railway Inn, maybe? They've got that little function room at the back. It’s got a bit more character. Train! Cho-choo! Yes, sweetheart. A train. Well, let’s investigate The Railway Inn, then. Can you give them a ring, love? See if they’ve got availability? Sure, I can do that tonight. What about the Christening? We haven’t really touched on that much. Good point. That’s after Lizzie’s birthday, isn’t it? Mid-November? Yeah, the 11th. I was thinking we could do something a bit smaller, just family and close friends. Less stress. I agree. A big, lavish affair feels a bit much, doesn't it? Maybe at our place? We’ve got space in the garden, weather permitting. That would be lovely, Mum. Less to organise for me too, which is a bonus. Bubbles? Christening bubbles! Yes, darling, we can have bubbles. Just imagine all the little ones chasing them. It’ll be delightful. Now, invitations… I can start on those. Do you want something formal or more relaxed? More relaxed, definitely. Something with a picture of her, maybe? I’ve got loads on my phone. Perfect. And we need to think about a gift, don’t we? Something she can keep. I was thinking of putting money towards her university fund. Practical, but useful. That’s a lovely idea, love. Very sensible. Actually, speaking of money… Have you managed to sort out that bill for the garage yet? Not yet, Mum. I keep meaning to, but it’s just slipped my mind. I’ll do it first thing tomorrow, I promise. Please do, love. They’re starting to send some rather aggressive letters. And have you started considering your dissertation topic properly? I’m getting there. I’ve narrowed it down to two possibilities, but I’m still not entirely sure.

Right, so, has anyone heard anything more about flights to New York? It's just ridiculous prices at the moment. I’ve been having a look, yeah. It's mental! I reckon we're gonna have to be super flexible with dates if we want to get a decent deal. Maybe going mid-week? New York! Can I go on a big wheel? Absolutely, sweetheart. A giant Ferris wheel is definitely on the agenda. We’ll go on loads of them. Yeah, and the Statue of Liberty, Central Park… Loads of things! It’s going to be amazing. Mum, have you started looking at hotels yet? I’ve glanced, but haven't committed to anything. Everything seems so expensive. Remember that awful hotel we ended up in in Spain, years ago? Oh god, the one with the dodgy plumbing and the stained carpets? Don't remind me. I still have nightmares about that breakfast buffet. Exactly! We don't want a repeat of that, do we? Speaking of awful experiences, how's work been, love? You sound stressed every time you mention it. Ugh, don’t even get me started. It's been manic. We’ve got a huge promotion on this weekend, and the stock levels are… well, let's just say it's a miracle we haven't run out of everything already. Can I have a lollipop? In a little bit, darling, after we've finished chatting. You deserve a proper holiday after that. Maybe New York will do the trick. I hope so. What are your plans for the weekend, Mum? Anything exciting? Not really, just relaxing, I think. Maybe a potter around in the garden if the weather holds up. It’s been lovely these past couple of days, hasn't it? A welcome change from all that rain we had last month. It really has. Although, I'm not convinced it’s going to last. Knowing our luck, we’ll get a downpour on Saturday. Don't say that! I'm making a proper Sunday roast. It would be lovely if we could eat it in the garden, you know? That would be nice. Remember when we went to Cornwall for your birthday? That was such a good holiday. Oh, that was brilliant! We found that little cove, and the kids spent the whole day digging in the sand. And the pasties! I’ve not tasted pasties like that since.

Right, so basically, this is the outline of my dissertation proposal. I’ve been wrestling with it for weeks. Salford, yeah? Seems intense. Let me see. Okay, "The Impact of Post-Industrial Landscapes on Northern Identity." Sounds… weighty. It is. That’s what I’m finding. I've got the core argument, I think, but fleshing it out feels never-ending. See, I'm proposing to look at how the decline of industries like cotton mills and coal mining has shaped the sense of identity – both positive pride and, well, a kind of melancholic resignation - in towns like Lancaster and Burnley. Right, interesting. So, less about architectural decline and more about how people  feel  about it? Exactly. I’m trying to avoid just another lament about decaying buildings. I want to explore the cultural narrative, the folklore even, that grows up around these places. The stories people tell themselves, and each other, to make sense of it. Yeah, that's clever. So, you've got sections on historical context, obviously… and then what? Methodology? Yep. That’s the bit I’m really struggling with. I initially wanted to do a lot of oral history work, interviews with people who remember the heyday of these industries and then how things changed. Proper in-depth stuff. Makes sense. But? But it’s proving difficult to get access. University ethical guidelines are a nightmare, and frankly, finding people willing to commit to lengthy interviews on top of their lives is… tricky. Yeah, I can see that. Universities and ethics… a classic. So, I’m considering supplementing that with textual analysis - local newspapers, community websites, even social media groups dedicated to remembering old mills. Like, digitally archiving memories, if that makes sense. Definitely. It’s a good compromise, right? Brings in a different perspective too, a more contemporary one. What about the theoretical framework? What are you leaning towards? I'm playing with a bit of Benedict Anderson’s “Imagined Communities,” obviously, but trying to ground it in some sociological work too, particularly around concepts of place attachment and collective memory. I’ve got a paragraph here about how industrial heritage becomes a form of symbolic capital… Symbolic capital… yeah, I get it. It’s about creating a sense of belonging and value through association with a particular past, even if that past isn't entirely rosy. Precisely. It’s a coping mechanism, in a way.

Right, so, weirdest dream ever last night. I was presenting a pitch… to a room full of penguins. Penguins? Seriously? What was the pitch about? Prospect Research, obviously. But they kept interrupting to squawk about fish. I’m pretty sure one of them threw a herring at me. Fish! Penguin! See, even they're getting in on the penguin action. Anyway, that’s ridiculous. My dream was much more… grounded. I was wandering through a massive garden, full of roses, and there was this little cottage at the end. Completely overgrown with ivy, but utterly charming. Sounds lovely. Like something out of a fairytale. It was. And then I woke up, and I realised it was exactly how I want our garden to look, eventually. When we actually have time to do it, of course. A garden is a distant dream at the moment. Speaking of dreams... did you ever think we’d actually be here? In Comberton? I mean, remember those tiny bedsits in London? Don’t remind me! Though, to be fair, they were full of character. Still, this is… nice. Spacious. And we’re finally starting to feel settled. Definitely. I think my biggest dream, at the moment, is a rather more immediate one… Let me guess. A pay rise? Tempting, but no. I want a dog. A big, fluffy one. Golden Retriever, maybe? Doggy! Ball! A dog is a big commitment though, isn't it? Walking, feeding, vet bills… I know, I know. But I’d love the company. And the kids would adore it. I’ve been looking at rescue shelters online... That’s sweet. Just… let’s get the garden sorted first, alright? Before we’re chasing a golden retriever around a jungle of weeds. Fair enough. Although, on the subject of dreams coming true… have you bought a lottery ticket this week? No. Waste of money, I always say. Well, you never know. A few million quid would  really  speed up the garden project. And maybe buy us a very large, very fluffy dog. More! Play! Alright, alright. One more cup for you, and then it’s time to build more towers... Maybe your dreams will be about castles, eh? And I'll dream about that garden again. Perhaps with a dog chasing butterflies… That sounds perfect. A very sensible, very achievable dream. Unlike presenting to a room full of fish-throwing penguins… I still can’t get over that.

Right, you’re sure you’re driving okay? My head's still doing a little dance. Yeah, I'm fine. Just concentrate on the road, love. You look like you're about to faint. Do you want me to pull over? No, no, I’m alright. Just… everything happened so fast. Honestly, A&E was chaos. Absolute chaos. Tell me about it. The waiting room was rammed. I thought we’d be there all night. What did the doctor say, exactly? Said it was a pretty nasty concussion. Apparently, I’m lucky I didn’t break anything. And a sprained wrist. The wrist is throbbing, actually. Right, let me have a look. Ouch, yeah, that’s definitely swollen. Did they give you anything for the pain? Just paracetamol. Said to take it regularly, but it’s barely touching it. And they kept asking me loads of questions about what I remember… which wasn't much, to be honest. They have to, don’t they? Just making sure everything’s connected. Do you remember how it happened? Vaguely. One minute I was reaching for the ball, the next… the ground rushed up to meet me. Honestly, I forgot I was even playing netball. All those years ago, and I still manage to injure myself. You always did have a knack for it, eh? You were always a bit clumsy, even as a kid. Remember when you fell out of that tree trying to rescue that cat? Don't remind me! That was mortifying. And this is just as bad, if not worse. I feel proper silly. Don’t feel silly. It was an accident. And you were being a good sport, trying to get involved in the game. Besides, it could have been so much worse. The doctor said you were lucky. Yeah, I know, I know. Still… my head feels like it’s full of cotton wool. Everything's a bit blurry. You need to rest. Absolutely no screens for the rest of the day. And definitely no netball anytime soon. Promise me. Promise. I’m not rushing back to that court any time soon. Actually, I think I’ll stick to knitting from now on. Less chance of concussion with a pair of socks. That’s the spirit! Look, I'll take you home, get you settled on the sofa, and make you a cup of tea. Strong one. You need it.

Dreadful business, isn't it? This situation in Ukraine. Absolutely dreadful. Read another article this morning, even more concerning than the last. Aye, it is. Hard to make heads or tails of it all with so many different reports flying about. Feels like we’re back in the Cold War, doesn’t it? In some ways, yes. Though, of course, the complexities are far greater now. Makes you wonder what the world’s coming to. Speaking of worrying things, how’s the shop doing, David? Been quiet these past few weeks? Not terrible, actually. A bit of a lull, as always in the autumn. But I’ve been thinking... I’ve got an idea, a slightly mad one, really. Oh? Do tell. You know I'm always happy to listen to a bit of madness. Well, I was thinking about expanding the online side of things. Beyond just selling what's in store. I reckon I could curate little boxes – themed gift boxes, you know? Say, a "Gardener’s Delight" box, with seeds, gloves, little tools... or a "Coastal Escape" box with scented candles, shells, little notebooks… That’s… actually quite clever, David. A clever way to tap into the gifting market. People always need gifts, and themed boxes are so popular. Much more appealing than just browsing through endless shelves. Exactly! I’ve even got some contacts who could supply the individual items at decent prices. The biggest hurdle is the photography and the website updates. It’s all a bit beyond me, truth be told. Well, my grandson, Tom, is rather handy with a camera and websites. He’s studying graphic design, you know. He might be willing to help out. I’ll have a word with him. That would be fantastic, Arthur! Really would. I’d be happy to pay him, of course. Don’t want to put him out too much. Don't worry about that. He'd enjoy it, I'm sure. Keeps him off the PlayStation, anyway. Although, I'm not sure it’s the best sort of influence, these video games. Tell me about it! My granddaughter is addicted to that Fortnite. I can’t get her to put it down. Gets right cross if I suggest she do something else. Kids these days. We used to be happy with a simple game of cricket in the garden. Though, thinking about it, old Bernard from down the road was always a bit dodgy at bowling.

This pub's got a really odd vibe, doesn’t it? Bit… fortress-y. Like being inside a giant guardhouse, which, I suppose, it is. It is. I mean, Woolwich always had that feel, didn’t it? Military presence everywhere. But yeah, the décor is… interesting. All that dark wood and those brass fittings. It's trying to be Victorian, I think, but mostly it just feels a bit gloomy. Gloomy, exactly! But in a strangely comforting way, you know? It’s got character. So, what are we thinking food-wise? I'm starving. I saw they have a burger on the menu. A decent-looking one. Or fish and chips, the classic. Fish and chips would be good. It’s a bit chilly out. Though, I should have grabbed a thicker coat. I'm regretting that now. You’ll warm up with a few more pints, I’m sure. Speaking of which, another half? Please. I was thinking about Happy Valley the other night. Absolutely brilliant, wasn't it? That ending... wow. Absolutely. Sarah Lancashire is phenomenal. She just carries the whole show. It’s so gritty and realistic. Reminds me a little of some of the stuff I studied at uni. Criminology, remember? Oh, right! Of course. You always were the clever one, analysing everything. Makes me wish I'd picked something slightly more… intense than English Literature. Don't knock English Lit! You’re a transcriber. You’re surrounded by words all day. Anyway, did you hear what they’re doing with the campus at Edinburgh? Apparently, they’re building a new arts centre right on the Meadows? No! That's amazing! But also, a bit tragic for the old charm of the place. I loved wandering through the Meadows when I visited. What's Willow doing? Still playing with that feather toy relentlessly? Relentlessly is the perfect word. She hasn't left it alone since we got home. Actually, I think she’s probably more obsessed with it than she ever was with that laser pointer. Cats, eh? Simple pleasures. It reminds me, I saw this article online about how music can affect cats’ moods – apparently, certain frequencies are really calming. Wonder if Willow would like classical music? Give it a try! Though, knowing Willow, she’ll probably just stare blankly at the speaker and then proceed to knock over a vase. You know her too well.

Aye, that’s a belter of a pint. Needed that after luggin’ pallets all day. You always do look like you've wrestled a grizzly bear after work, pal. So, show me these photos then. You were saying you got some cracking ones up north, weren't you? Aye, I was. Went up to Skye last weekend. Proper batterin’ it was, mind you. Rained near constant. Skye? Brave man. I’ve heard the weather there can be… fickle. Fickle’s an understatement! On Saturday, I swear I saw the four seasons in an hour. Hail, sunshine, drizzle, then a proper downpour. But it did somethin' for the light, eh? Gave it a real moody feel. Right, let’s see. You said you got some of the Old Man of Storr? Aye, got a few. Had to battle through a herd of Japanese tourists for a decent angle though. Honestly, they were like wee buzzing bees around the place. But managed to snag one where the mist’s rollin' in around the peaks. Looks right atmospheric. Here. Wow. That's… that's stunning. The light is incredible. All those shades of grey and green... you’ve captured it perfectly. Glad you think so. Trying to get better with the landscape stuff, know what I mean? Used to just snap away, but now I'm actually trying to think about composition. Rule of thirds and all that. It shows. You've got a good eye, Liam. Really. Better than my attempts, anyway. My photos always look like someone sneezed on them. Don't be daft, you take fine photos. Just… different. More… spontaneous, maybe? Spontaneous is a nice way of saying chaotic. Still, I admire your dedication, going up there in that weather. It must have been brutal. Brutal, aye. But worth it. Found this wee lochan hidden away too – hardly a soul around. Got some reflections of the hills. Proper peaceful, that was. Sounds idyllic. You should print those, frame 'em. Aye, maybe I will. Been thinking about gettin' one of those fancy printers for photos. Something that does proper canvas prints. That’s a good shout. The paper ones never quite do it justice. And then you could hang ‘em up, impress everyone with your photography skills. Exactly! Then you’ll be jealous. Fancy a another one? Weather's still lookin’ grim out there though. Aye, let's. Just one more.

Right then, love. Tea's brewed, biscuits are out. So, what’s the plan for this week? Anything exciting happening? Not hugely exciting, Mum. Just the usual school madness really. Year two are being particularly clingy this week, you know how they get. Oh, bless ‘em. They’re all little Velcro, aren't they? So, Arthur...is he being a little terror, or mostly an angel? A bit of both, honestly. Had a real meltdown yesterday because I wouldn’t let him paint the cat. You know he really wanted to. Oh, that’s classic Arthur. You’ve got to be firm with that one, he’ll walk all over you if you let him. Have you sorted the nursery place properly? Did you hear back from Little Acorns? Yeah, they offered me a place. Starting the 15th of next month. I'm a bit nervous, to be honest. Three days a week feels like a long time. It  does  feel long at first, pet. But you’ll get used to it. And it's brilliant for him, giving him that socialisation. And you’ll get some time to yourself, which you deserve. Remember, you're still young! I know, I know. It’s just...it feels like a big step, you know? Suddenly he’s not all mine all the time. I understand that. But it’s a good thing, love. Don’t feel guilty about it. Listen, are you coming for Sunday lunch? I'm making that roast pork you like, with all the trimmings. That sounds lovely, Mum. Yes, definitely. Dad’s coming too, isn’t he? Of course. He’s been asking about Arthur all week. He wants to take him to the park. Though he’ll probably end up trying to teach him how to fly a kite. He will, won’t he? Oh, and I was wondering… could you possibly have a look at this… it’s the school’s reading scheme. They want parents to contribute ideas. I’m a bit stuck. Of course, love. Let me have a look. I was always good at spotting a good story when I was a kid – used to spend hours in the library, didn't I? What have you been watching on telly lately? Anything good? “Happy Valley” is brilliant, Mum! Have you seen it? It's so gripping. Oh, I've heard good things! I don’t get Sky though, you know I am a bit behind the times.

This is absolutely brilliant, Anon. Honestly, best pasta I've had in ages. Seriously! You've outdone yourself. Though, I’m feeling slightly carb-logged already. You always say that, Liv. You say that after, like, three mouthfuls. Shut up, Ben. I just appreciate a good carb load. Speaking of things I appreciate, this pesto is amazing. Where did you get it? Anon, you secretly are a gourmet chef, aren't you? It's from that little Italian deli down the road. Remember? We went in there last week. Oh, right! Yeah, that’s good. Everything tastes proper. So, Liv, how’s the conference planning going? Still battling the catering companies? Don’t even  start  on the catering companies. Honestly, I swear they’re actively trying to sabotage me. I sent them the allergen list  three  times, and they’re still suggesting dishes with nuts. Nuts, Ben! For a room full of people with potentially life-threatening allergies. That’s wild! You should take screenshots of everything. Evidence. I already have a document dedicated to their incompetence. It's getting pretty thick. You should share it with us. Like, a ‘Catering Company Horror Stories’ blog. It wouldn't be funny for me! It’s stressful. I think my boss thinks I'm being pedantic. You're being responsible! They’re being negligent. Anyway, back to less stressful topics… Ben, how’s the building site treating you? Still dodging falling bricks? Don’t remind me. Leg’s hurting today, actually. Twanged it a bit yesterday lifting some concrete blocks. Ouch! Get it checked out. Seriously. You can't mess around with that sort of thing. Nah, it’s fine. Just a bit stiff. It'll be gone by tomorrow. Typical me, though, always hurting myself. You really need to be careful. You’re not getting any younger! I'm nineteen, Maisie. Feels like you’re forty with the way you talk about your aches and pains. So, Maisie, anything happening in your life? Still seeing Liam? No. Liam and I… we’re not together anymore. Oh Liv, I’m so sorry. What happened? It’s complicated. Long distance just wasn’t working, I think. He’s really focused on his music, which is great, but it meant he was never really  here . You know? Sorry to hear that, Liv. Don't be. It just felt like it was time to move on.

Right then, who wants tea? I’ve just put the kettle on. Oh lovely, Arthur. I’m ready for a cuppa. Feels like ages since I had a proper sit down. Don't mind if I do, Elsie. Needed something to warm me up, a bit chilly in here today, isn't it? Yes please, Arthur. My knees are playing up something awful this afternoon. A nice warm tea will do them good. Kettle's boiled. Anyone got a preference? Earl Grey, English Breakfast, I’ve still got that Darjeeling… English Breakfast for me, please. Always been a traditionalist. Darjeeling, if you've got it. Bit more sophisticated, you know. Reminds me of my holidays in India, back in the day. English Breakfast is fine for me, dear. Can't go wrong with a good cup of English Breakfast. Right you are. Elsie, you want a biscuit with that? I’ve got digestives, shortbread, ginger snaps… Oh, shortbread, please Arthur. Those are lovely. A little bit of sweetness with the tea. Digestives for me, thank you. Sturdy biscuit, you need something to hold the tea properly. Don’t want it going everywhere. Ginger snaps, please dear. Bit of a kick to them, good for my aches and pains. Now then, settle in everyone. Lovely to have you all. It's been a busy week, hasn't it? It has indeed. The garden needs a lot of attention, the weeds are taking over something awful. Aye, the weather’s been doing funny things, isn’t it? Sunny one minute, raining the next. Hard to keep on top of things. My daughter called yesterday. Said her grandson is getting a bit rebellious. Typical teenage behaviour, I suppose. That's life, isn't it? Always something to keep you busy. At least we've got a bit of sunshine for a change. Makes a good cup of tea even better. You're right Arthur! This is just what I needed. Quite right, Arthur. A good brew and good company. Can't ask for much more. Agreed. Thank you, Arthur. You're a dear. Arthur: You're very welcome! Anything else needed? No THANK you. No thanks. No thank you dear. Arthur: Well enjoy your tea! We will! We Are! Thank you! Arthur: You're very welcome! Hope this fits the prompt well! Let me know if you'd like any adjustments. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .H...

Right, everyone dig in! I've made far too much, as usual. Fantastic! You always do, Anon. Never a complaint from me. Proper Sunday roast, this. Beats anything I could whip up. It smells heavenly. You’ve really outdone yourself. Though, honestly, I’m still reeling from that protest we saw earlier. That was… intense. Quite a lot of shouting. Not sure what they were even protesting about, to be honest. Just a general air of discontent. It was about the new development in the village, apparently. The one that’ll block out all the sunlight for Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning roses. Roses eh? Bet she’s not happy. You know, my Nana was obsessed with roses. Had a whole garden dedicated to 'em. Could tell you the Latin name of every single one. Sounds lovely. Speaking of Nana, I was thinking about her the other day… remember when she nearly drove into a ditch trying to parallel park in London? Oh god, yes! We were all crammed in the car, terrified. And she just kept saying, “Oh, I’m just having a little wobble!” A little wobble! That’s putting it mildly. I think that’s why she stuck to the bus after that. And it’s why I wouldn’t let her drive me anywhere in London. London, eh? Fancy a trip soon? I’ve heard there's a proper art scene going on now. Not just stuffy museums. I’d be up for that. We could check out the Tate Modern, maybe see a play? Though, the hotel prices are ridiculous. They are, aren't they? We might be better off looking at something a bit further out, then hopping on the tube. Definitely. I was looking at some places in Hackney the other day. Seems like a good vibe. Anyway, back to slightly less stressful topics… Anyone been thinking about the little one and crèche options? Still early days, isn’t it? Though with Rhys's growing, it brings up things like... well, you know. Circumcision? Honestly, it's a minefield. So much conflicting information. It's a deeply personal decision, isn't it? No right or wrong answer. Just need to do your research. Exactly. And make sure any place you send him has proper CRB checks. Can't be too careful. It's exhausting trying to keep on top of everything. Tell me about it.

God, it’s good to be back. Everything smells… normal. Not like sunscreen and chlorine. Welcome back! I missed you. Honestly, the flat felt so empty without you. How was Greece? Seriously, give me all the details. Amazing! Seriously, I’m already planning to go back. The beaches were incredible, the food… oh my god, the food. I need to recreate that souvlaki I had. Ooh, you have to! I’ve been surviving on cereal and instant noodles while you were off living the dream. I’m ready for some decent grub. Did you see loads of sun? You’re looking tanned! Loads of sun! Definitely got a bit of a burn on day one, learned my lesson quick. Stupidly wore a factor 15. Should have gone straight for 50 like you always say. Did you do anything exciting while I was gone besides just, you know, existing? Pretty much existing, yeah. Work's been… work. The usual drama. Liam and Chloe are still going strong, apparently they went to that new Italian place we wanted to try. Oh really? Good for them. He looks so happy when he’s with her. Remember when we thought he’d never get over… you know. Don't remind me. Honestly, looking back, what was I even thinking? He was a mess! Glad I dodged that bullet. Anyway, my mum sent me like, ten kilos of homemade marmalade while you were away. It's taking over the kitchen. Oh god, your mum and her marmalade. Is there any chance of sharing? I’m starving. And did you catch any of the football? England were playing, weren't they? Yeah, they lost. Predictable. It was on in the background when I was marking essays. Speaking of which, I'm drowning in them. I need a serious weekend of marking. Ugh, the worst. Want to order some pizza tonight? Comfort food to combat the marmalade overload and your essay pile. That sounds amazing. Pepperoni and pineapple? I'm feeling adventurous. Always. Hey, while I’m unpacking, do you want me to grab the milk? We’re completely out. Yes, please! You’re a lifesaver. I was thinking of venturing out later, but honestly, I just want to collapse on the sofa and binge-watch something rubbish. I am exactly the same. I’m thinking trashy reality TV. You in? Absolutely. Come on, let’s just forget this week ever happened and embrace the comfy chaos of being back home.

Did you hear back from Sarah about the Macmillan nurse? Did she manage to get one sorted? Not yet, no. She left a message, said she’d call back today, but nothing as of yet. I know she's been pushing hard, poor thing. The chemo’s really knocked her about this last cycle. It's awful, isn’t it? That documentary we watched last week… it just felt so relentlessly bleak. I keep thinking about her having to navigate all of this alone. She’s not entirely alone. Mark’s doing his best, but you can hear the strain in his voice. It’s a lot for anyone to shoulder. Did you get a chance to email the hospital about that referral for her? Yes, sent it this morning. Fingers crossed it goes through quickly. It's just frustrating – bureaucracy seems to slow everything down at the worst possible times. Tell me about it. Speaking of slow, have you been looking at those houses in Little Puddleton again? The one with the garden backing onto the woods? I have! I had another look on Rightmove this morning. It’s still on, ridiculously overpriced if you ask me, but… the garden  is  lovely. And it’s actually got planning permission for that extension they were talking about. Planning permission? Really? That's a huge hurdle cleared. I thought getting anything through the Parish Council would be a nightmare. Apparently, the previous owners had a very good relationship with them and a well-argued case for the extension. They even got them to agree on the garden design. Well, that’s definitely more promising. Still wouldn’t pay their asking price, though. But if we could negotiate… what do you think about the styling? It’s very… traditional. A bit dated, definitely. But the bones of the house are good, aren’t they? High ceilings, big windows… we could strip it back and modernise it. Imagine a minimalist kitchen overlooking that garden… It's a nice thought. We'd have to be careful though; that conservation area designation means we'd be jumping through hoops for  everything . I know, I know. I did some digging into the articles on the Parish Council website. They're incredibly pedantic about those houses. The roof tiles have to be  exactly  the right shade of grey. Exactly! That's why I'm hesitant. Little Puddleton is charming, but it's also got a serious reputation for being… difficult.

Honestly, Sarah, the bins. They’re a nightmare. Absolute nightmare. Tell me about it, Liam. It's like a weekly battleground out there. Battleground is right. People just chuck everything, doesn't matter if it's recycling or not. Pizza boxes, overflowing, nappies…you name it. And the smell! Don’t even get me started on the smell on a hot day. The smell is something else. I swear, sometimes I can smell it through my flat window. And the seagulls! They’re loving it. Perched on the lids, scavenging…it's disgusting. Don’t remind me about the seagulls. They're bolder than ever, aren’t they? Last week one actually tried to grab a bit of paper from my hand. Nearly gave me a heart attack. Oh my god! They’re getting fearless. And the noise they make first thing in the morning... it’s a proper wake-up call, just not the kind anyone wants. It is. And then there's the students who leave their bikes chained to literally anything. Lamp posts, fences, even each other sometimes. Haha, yeah, I’ve seen that. It’s a right tangle out there. It's a proper obstacle course just getting to the bike storage. They don't think about anyone else, do they? Nope. Selfish. And don't even get me started on that one group who always leave their dishes in the communal kitchen for days. Like, seriously, who doesn't know to wash up? Oh god, the dishes. I found a mouldy mug the other day. A  mouldy  mug! I nearly chucked up. It's like they're cultivating bacteria in there. Absolutely. And then they complain when the kitchen gets a bit grimy. It's their mess! It’s infuriating. You know what else really gets on my nerves? What? Tell me, I need to vent too. The fire alarms. They go off at least twice a month for absolutely no reason. False alarms. People cooking toast, someone steaming vegetables… Oh, the burnt toast alarms! I hate those. You spend ten minutes evacuating everyone, shivering in the rain, just to find out someone burnt a piece of bread. Exactly! It’s such a waste of time and energy. And then everyone's moaning, but nobody ever takes responsibility. No, they just pretend it never happened. I wish they'd install some sort of system to fine people for false alarms.

Honestly, it’s mad, isn’t it? Running into so many Brits everywhere we go. Like, we were in Antwerp last week and at least four people we overheard were speaking with the same accent as my Nan. It’s the package tour effect, love. They follow each other like pigeons. Brighton seems to be filled with them too, doesn't it, Susan? It does, doesn’t it, Arthur? Though I reckon a lot of it's just people escaping London. This area's always been a draw. Remember when we used to go caravanning in Dorset? Absolute mayhem! Oh my god, I can't even imagine. I’m just trying to figure out when I’m going to find time to actually do some Christmas shopping. University's already consuming every waking moment. It’s just the cohort is so… intense. Everyone’s already planning their careers. They always are at that age. Bright young things. I used to feel that way, thinking I’d be a rocket scientist or something. Life has a way of… rearranging things, doesn't it? Oh, tell me about it! My youngest, Liam, he's turning ten next month. Can you believe it? Seems like only yesterday I was bringing him home from hospital. Raising boys, eh? A constant trial and tribulation. Speaking of trials, I ran into Chloe from school. You remember, the one who barely spoke? She’s apparently marrying that guy from Year 8 we all used to tease! Well, people change. Good for her. Though I still can’t fathom why anyone would want to live in Herne Bay. All those charity shops. Nothing to do there. Don't knock it, Arthur. I got a lovely scarf there last week. And you know, it’s a nice little trip for a potter around. Besides, I’d rather a poke around a charity shop than wrestle with the traffic trying to get back to Harlow. Dreadful. The seafront's so busy today. Brighton's always buzzing. Reminds me, I said I'd meet Ben for coffee later. He’s starting to get a bit… clingy, you know? These relationships. Always a bit of a puzzle, aren't they? Remember Maggie? The girl from down the road? Always chasing after fellas with silly names. Don't start on Maggie, Arthur! She ended up perfectly happy with old Derek from the bakery. And he treated her right.

Honestly, Mum, the whole Equality Vote thing is mental. Didn’t even bother. Mental how, love? Did you not get a postal vote? Yeah, I did. But like, what’s the point? Everyone’s saying it’s rigged anyway. And it’s just, like, arguing all the time. I saw Liam’s Dad shouting at someone in the supermarket today about it. It was so awkward. Well, democracy isn’t always pretty, is it? It’s important to have your say, even if you think it's a bit of a shambles. Think of your grandparents, fighting for the right to vote. Yeah, but it feels like nothing actually changes. Politicians say one thing and do another. It's infuriating. And all that online stuff… so much fake news. Makes you wonder what to believe. I agree. It's disheartening, isn't it? Though, I do think it’s good to see these issues being talked about, even if the conversation is a bit… heated. At least people are engaged, in their own ways. Engaged and arguing. Remember when you tried to explain Parliament to me when I was like, seven? You spent an hour drawing diagrams and I just wanted to play Minecraft. Oh, goodness, yes! You were completely uninterested. Said it was “boring history stuff”. Suddenly you’re a political expert because it’s on TikTok, are you? Well, it's different when it’s, like, relevant, isn't it? Like, it actually affects  us . It always affects us, darling. Whether you're paying attention or not. Still, it's good you're thinking about these things. You'll be surprised how quickly you'll be dragging  me  into political debates. Just wait until you’re getting married, I’ll be a nightmare. Don’t even go there! I'm not getting married anytime soon. And even if I did, you’d probably embarrass me at the wedding. Like wearing one of those “Bride’s Mum – Making Memories” sashes. Oh, I would not! Perhaps. I might. It's tradition! It's mortifying! You’d be posting baby photos of me on Facebook with captions like, "My little prince, all grown up!" Maybe. Little prince or little princess, depending on the dress code. Look, I’m just saying, you’ll need me to keep things lively at the reception. Someone has to keep a watchful eye on the dance floor.

This bread's a bit dry, isn’t it, Margaret? Not quite as nice as that sourdough you got last week. It is a bit, isn't it? I had to use what was left. Didn't want to waste it. I thought we could have soup tomorrow, that would soften it up a bit. Soup sounds good. Though I still think you overdo the nutmeg in your butternut squash soup. Overdo it? Don't be silly, Bernard. It just gives it a bit of warmth. Reminds me of when I was a lad. My uncle had a lathe, you know. A proper one, made of cast iron. He’d turn out little bowls and things. Had all sorts of fancy tools for it. Oh, I remember. You used to go round to his workshop, didn't you, Arthur? All covered in sawdust. Aye, I did. He tried to teach me once, but I wasn’t very good. Kept getting the chisel stuck. He said I didn't have the knack. You always were better with your hands when it came to fixing things though. Remember that time the washing machine broke and you managed to get it going again? That was a tricky one, that was. Parts flying everywhere. Still, got it working in the end. Not like these modern things, eh? All plastic and complicated. Speaking of complicated, did you see that story online the other day? Dreadful, absolutely dreadful. About the hamster? Yes. Unbelievable. I nearly dropped my cup of tea! Putting a hamster in a microwave! Who would do such a thing? It's barbaric. Some people, eh? No sense at all. Used to get into a right state over animals. Remember when old Mrs. Higgins’ cat went missing? Blamed the foxes. She was convinced the foxes were conspiring against her. Absolutely convinced. Poor Mrs. Higgins. She was a lovely woman, in her own way. It's just… some people lack empathy. It’s so upsetting. I can’t imagine being a child and witnessing something like that. Well, there’s plenty of upsetting things in the world, that's for sure. Still, gotta eat, eh? This sandwich, dry as it is, is keeping me going. Right, I need to get going. Got that meeting with the headteacher this afternoon. About the revised curriculum. It’s a nightmare, frankly. Good luck, darling. Don’t let them wear you down.

Honestly, I was reading about this mirror-writing thing online. Apparently, it’s not as rare as people think. Someone managed to write an entire novel backwards, and then read it in a mirror! Really? That’s quite something. I struggle to read a cryptic crossword, let alone write one backwards. My brain just refuses. Oh, you young people and your technology. When I was a girl, we were happy with a pencil and a bit of paper. And a good book, of course. It’s fascinating though, isn't it? Apparently, some people with dyslexia use it as a workaround. They find it easier to process things that way. That's interesting. Reminds me of all the different ways people navigate the world. Speaking of navigating, have you seen the house prices around here lately? Absolutely ridiculous! Don’t even mention it! We were looking at a place, just a small cottage really, and it was over a million. A million pounds! My goodness. When I was starting out, you could buy a perfectly decent house for a fraction of that. And pay off your mortgage in a reasonable timeframe. Now, people are saddled with debt for decades. It’s disheartening. Especially when you see the banks… I was trying to sort out some online banking the other day. Honestly, it’s like they're deliberately trying to make it difficult. Tell me about it! I spent an hour on hold just to change my address. And then they tried to sell me a new credit card. The world's gone mad. And all this talk about charging for plastic bags... Honestly! As if that’s going to solve the climate crisis. It's a start, I suppose. Though I did hear a story on the news about a cat stealing a whole bag of plastic bags from a shop. It was dragging them along the street. Oh, that's brilliant! A cat with a penchant for plastic. Cats are always getting up to mischief. They’re like little furry anarchists. I remember one of my headmistresses had a Siamese that used to unravel all the students' scarves… That’s terrible! Though I do enjoy a good cat story. Have you been following what’s happening in American politics? It’s just… relentless. I try not to. It drains all the energy. All that shouting and arguing. Give me a quiet evening and a cryptic crossword any day.

Honestly, you two. It's a beautiful day outside. The sun is shining. But Mum, I’m building a whole new village in Minecraft! It needs a marketplace, and a blacksmith, and a stable for the horses. And I’m about to defeat the Stone Ninja! He’s got a really powerful sword. Stone Ninja? What even  is  a Stone Ninja? It's Ninjago, Mum! You know. Lego Ninjago. Kai has to defeat him to get the Golden Scroll. He's got a shield too, that’s really annoying. It deflects all the shurikens. Shurikens? Right. So, instead of, you know, actually  playing  with your Lego, you’re just...fighting them on a screen. It’s different! We're building stuff too! Digital building. It's like...architecture, but with pixels. Architecture with pixels. Okay. And what about reading? Remember that book about the girl who went to space? You both loved the pictures. Too boring. There's no explosions. Yeah, and no dragons! Minecraft has way more dragons. And creepers. Creepers? Seriously? You’re being controlled by digital monsters. Don't you miss building a real fort out of blankets and cushions? We  did  that last week. And Mom, this is more exciting! I built a secret underground tunnel system in my world. You wouldn’t believe it. I won! I defeated the Stone Ninja! Now I can go to the Emerald Temple. Emerald Temple? This is getting out of hand. I just… I worry you're missing out on things. On real things. But Mum, this  is  real to me! It's my world. I get to design everything. Can I start a new Minecraft world now? One with a volcano? A volcano, huh? Alright, alright. But when you’re done with your volcano… maybe, just maybe, we can dust off those picture books about space? Please? Maybe. But can I build a spaceship in Minecraft first? A really big one? With lasers! And a rocket booster! Lasers and a rocket booster it is. Just… please put the tablets down for five minutes and tell me about your volcano. I’m genuinely curious. Okay! So, you need to find obsidian… and then… …and you have to be really careful because if you get too close, it explodes! Boom! Boom indeed. Tell me more... and maybe later we'll try building a  real  volcano out of Play-Doh. Sound good?

Right, so, coffee's ready. Cream and sugar for both of you? Please, Mum. Sugar, yeah. Thanks. It's lovely to be back, honestly. This house feels so… calm. Yeah, it’s a nice change from student halls. Bit of peace and quiet is exactly what I needed after that essay deadline. Glad you think so, love. So, tell me everything about the holiday. How were the beaches in Cornwall? Amazing! Honestly, the weather was ridiculously good. We got some proper sunshine. Spent most of the time just… being. You know? No pressure, no rushing around. Cornwall was gorgeous. We did loads of walking, which my legs are still regretting, haha. Found this amazing little cove, practically deserted. Ooh, a secret cove? You must tell me where it was. I love a good hidden beach. It’s a bit tricky to find, to be honest. Lots of scrambling over rocks. But worth it. The sea was crystal clear. Absolutely. We had a little picnic down there one day too. Proper idyllic. Sounds wonderful. Did you manage to get away from technology completely? I’m trying to encourage you both to disconnect a bit more. I tried! Managed a whole day without Instagram, which is a personal record. Chloe, I don’t think you moved from your phone. Hey! I took pictures! For memories! Plus, posting about it kept my mum updated, didn't want her to worry. Fair enough. It’s just… sometimes it’s nice to truly  be  in the moment, without feeling the need to document it for everyone else. You’re preaching to the choir, Mum. I’m trying to be better about it. So, what’s the plan for today? Anything exciting happening? Nothing massive. I was thinking we could wander into Lichfield, have a look around the shops. Maybe try that new bakery everyone’s been raving about? That sounds good! I’m starving, to be honest. That walk in Cornwall really worked up an appetite. Definitely. And maybe a coffee in one of those little cafes? Just need to recharge my brain after all that essay writing. We could. Or, I thought, seeing as you’re both here, I'd start sorting through those old photos I found in the attic. Remember that holiday to Spain? The one where Chloe got stung by a jellyfish? Oh god, don’t remind me! I was so dramatic.

Right, who’s got the ham and cheese? I’m starving. Relax, Liam, it's here. See? Massive one. Mum went overboard again. Seriously, Ethan, you’re going to explode. I've got tuna mayo, if you want to swap, but it’s a bit…fishy. Nah, I'm sticking with the ham. Fishy tuna is not a vibe today. Anyone else got snacks? I’ve got a bag of those weird prawn crackers. Want some? Oh god, no. Those taste like old socks. Remember when my little brother ate a whole bag of those? He was sick everywhere. Gross. Anyway, did you guys see Mr. Davies' face when Taylor tried to argue with him about the history essay? Oh my god! It was priceless. He looked like he was about to explode. Taylor’s always pushing it, isn't he? He just wants to be a prefect, doesn’t he? Trying to show off. It’s so cringe. So, are Chloe and Maya coming to watch that new show tonight? ‘Cos if not, I’m not even bothering. Chloe said she might be busy, something about a family thing. Maya hasn’t replied to my message. Honestly, these people. Typical. What about Ben? Is he still going on about joining the army? Yeah, he was posting loads of stuff about tanks and stuff on Insta yesterday. Bit intense, isn't it? All he talks about is war and stuff. It is. My dad was saying something last week about how there's loads more conflict in the world right now. It’s a bit scary if you think about it. Yeah, but Ben's just trying to be edgy, you know? He probably doesn't even know what he's talking about. Probably. Speaking of edgy, did you hear about what happened with Patel and Mr. Jones last week? Oh, the shouting match in the corridor? Yeah! Apparently, Patel said Mr. Jones was being biased in the rankings. Ridiculous. Mr. Jones is the fairest teacher in the whole school. Yeah. Though, remember when Sharma was calling someone names? Honestly, it's just so tiring sometimes. Tell me about it. It's ridiculous how some people act. I overheard someone saying something really racist on the bus the other day. I couldn't believe it. Ugh, that’s awful. People need to just… think, you know? Exactly. Alright, enough heavy stuff.

Honestly, Mr. Davies is just… baffling. He keeps talking about quantum entanglement like we're all theoretical physicists. Tell me about it! I spent the whole lesson drawing diagrams of cats in boxes. He didn’t even notice. I tried to ask a question about projectile motion, and he just launched into a five-minute explanation of the history of Newtonian physics. It was so irrelevant. Ugh, yeah. He does that. Remember Ms. Harding in Year 7? She'd just go off on tangents about her cats. Oh my god, yes! And she'd expect us to take notes on it. Did you finish the English reading? The one on, like, Victorian poetry? Almost. It’s so boring, though. All about sunsets and lost loves. I’m struggling to find anything interesting to write about. Right? I’m just going to skim it and try to pull out a few keywords. Mr. Jacobson is so intense about annotations though; he'll mark you down for  not  writing enough. Seriously! He's like a hawk, watching for any sign of laziness. Remember when Chloe tried to get away with just one word in each line? Oh, he ripped her apart! He made her write out the entire poem again, line by line, with detailed explanations. Brutal. Have you seen  17 Again ? The Zac Efron one? Yeah! It was so cheesy but really good. I wish I could go back and redo Year 11, honestly. Me too! I’d actually pay attention in Physics. And I’d be nicer to Sophie Peterson. Sophie Peterson? Why would you be nicer to her? She’s a nightmare. I know, but I’d still regret being so mean. You know, when I’m, like, really old. True. What about Liam? He's being really weird in form. Weird how? I don’t know. Just, like, staring out the window a lot, not talking. He usually makes fun of Mrs. Finch’s cardigan. Maybe he finally realised how harsh he is. Maybe. Or maybe he just lost his phone. That’s more likely. You think his parents would ground him for a week? Easily. They're super strict. Speaking of Mrs. Finch, did you hear about what happened in her lesson yesterday? No! What? Apparently, someone replaced her whiteboard pens with felt tip pens. The whole board is covered in bright pink doodles. No way! Whose idea was that?

Right, Sunday night done and dusted. Feeling like I need a week just to recover from the weekend. Tell me about it! Flour everywhere, sugar coating every surface… my flat looks like a bakery exploded. Seriously considering just living in the cooling rack from now on. You always make it sound so dramatic, Liv. It’s just baking! You’re brilliant at it, though. The croissants this morning were incredible. Cor blimey, croissants? I haven't had a decent croissant since I left Sydney. Everything here's a bit… dense, isn't it? Mate, you've got no idea. Anyway, I was actually thinking about Transylvania. Transylvania? Seriously? You’re not planning a vampire hunt, are you? No! Well, maybe a  slightly  themed one. But I found this tour group offering cycling holidays through the mountains, exploring castles and stuff. It looks amazing. That does sound pretty cool. When were you thinking? September, apparently. Bit of a last-minute thing. I’m just poking around the idea. Anyone fancy joining? September sounds lovely, actually. I could definitely use a break from buttercream and proving. What sort of budget are we looking at? September… bit chilly for cycling around Europe, isn’t it? Reckon I’d need a good jumper. But yeah, sounds interesting. Got any photos of the castles? Loads! I'll send you the link. It's seriously breathtaking. And speaking of journeys, Sarah’s going to Bali – did you guys hear? No way! Okay, here's a conversation based on the provided context, aiming for a natural flow and incorporating the diverse speaker personalities. Right, your move, Dad. Honestly, you’re playing incredibly aggressively today. Are you feeling alright? Just…focused, love. Need to sharpen my skills. This place is rammed, isn't it? Glad we got here before it got even busier. Yeah, Westfield always is. Good choice though, I’ve heard the burgers here are decent. You want anything to drink yet? So, Dad, you were saying you didn’t agree with this new windfall tax? Not particularly, no. It's a short-sighted solution, really. They're trying to appear as though they're doing something about the energy price rises, but it's just kicking the can down the road. How so? I mean, isn't it fair to tax companies who are making record profits when people are struggling to heat their homes? Fair, perhaps, in principle. But it disincentivises investment. Companies are less likely to invest in new projects, in exploration, if they know a chunk of the profits is just going to be taken away by the government. Where does that leave us in the long run? Still reliant on foreign imports, still vulnerable to price shocks. But surely there's a balance. They could invest in renewable energy alongside. They  should  be. And there are incentives already in place for that. But the oil and gas companies, they’ve got expertise, infrastructure. You can't just wave a magic wand and suddenly have a functional renewable energy system. It takes time and capital, and this tax actively discourages the capital investment. Right. So it’s more about the bigger picture than about the immediate relief people need. Precisely. And the money they're raising…it's a drop in the ocean really. It’ll be swallowed up by bureaucracy and inefficiencies. Look, I’ve been doing taxes for over fifty years, and I’ve seen governments come and go, promising the world. It’s always the same story. You’re very cynical. Experience, my dear, not cynicism. Experience teaches you to expect less. And don’t get me started on corporation tax - reducing it was a mistake. It encouraged companies to shuffle profits around overseas, avoiding paying their fair share here. So what would  you  do then, if you were in charge? Oh, don’t go putting that pressure on me! But seriously, a more stable regulatory framework, incentives for investment in energy security, both traditional and renewable, and a fairer tax system that doesn't penalise success. And a serious look at government spending. It's bloated, wasteful… You always say that. Because it’s true! Look at the HS2 project. A colossal waste of money. That money could have been used to actually help people. Okay, okay, I get it. You think the government’s got its priorities wrong.

Honestly, Mum, the meeting this morning was absolutely mental. You won’t believe it. Oh really? What happened? Tell me everything. You know I love a good bit of office drama. Right then, sorted the tea, has it? Got a nice brew steamin’ here. Fancy a biccie wi’ it? I got them ginger nuts yer mam likes. Cheers, Dad. Ginger nuts sound brilliant! How's your back today? Not exactly glamorous, but a foot in the door is a foot in the door. The library? I don't know if... It's just not what I was hoping for. Don't knock it til you've tried it. Plus, you've got a good eye for detail – perfect for cataloguing! Speaking of details, did you remember to take the empties out earlier, lass? I nearly tripped over them this morning. Oh! Blast. Totally forgot. I was running around like a headless chicken trying to finish that application.

Honestly, I’m still recovering from that conference. Three days of listening to people drone on about communicative approaches to teaching… my brain feels like mush. Tell me about it! Don’t even get me started on the parents. One of them emailed me last week with a five-page rant about how I was “stifling” her son’s creativity by making him write essays. Oh my goodness. Honestly, this landscape is… uniform. Fields and fields. It’s a bit monotonous, isn’t it? Tarnów was prettier, I thought. It gets a bit more interesting after Krosno, apparently. Little bit of a valley. Right, about another hour and fifteen, according to Google. And we need to sort the parking situation in Rzeszów. It’s notoriously tricky. Parking? Really? I was thinking about that book I started. 'Hamnet'. Do you fancy giving it a go after this? I’m only about a quarter of the way through. ‘Hamnet’? Oh, Maggie O’Farrell, right? I’ve heard good things. Proper rewarding. Absolutely. Sometimes feeling useful is more important than anything else. I’ve been thinking about volunteering myself, actually. Maybe the library? They’re apparently desperate for help. That would be brilliant! You’d be amazing at it, honestly. You always did have a head for organisation. Better than me, definitely. I’d probably end up alphabetising the cushions. You’d probably do a good job of it too! How about that bloke you were seeing, though? What was his name... David? David. Yeah. That fizzled out, didn’t it? Turns out he was more interested in showing me his extensive vinyl collection than, well, anything else. Vinyl collections are a tricky thing. Good indicator of priorities, I suppose. Exactly! I'm not against a bit of music appreciation, but when it's a three-hour lecture on the merits of obscure 70s funk… it's a bit much, isn’t it? A bit much. You deserve someone who's interested in you, not just their record player. Are you hitting the gym much, by the way? You look good. Trying to! It's the only thing keeping me sane, really. Three times a week. Keeps the stress at bay, you know? What about you? Are you still doing your walks? Sporadically. My knees aren’t what they used to be, sadly.

So, I was reading about the Vikings the other night, you know, for a bit of a change. That’s amazing. I always thought Columbus was the big breakthrough. Though, I suppose, history is filled with those kinds of reassessments, isn't it? It's all about who finds the records, really. You’ve got the potential for huge breakthroughs, but also the ethical considerations are huge, aren’t they? Wanting to live forever... what does that do to society? And the strain on resources! We’re struggling already with global warming and energy. Don’t even get me started on global warming. It's terrifying, isn't it? All the predictions... and it feels like no one's doing nearly enough. Though, I did read something about harnessing energy from comets… pretty futuristic. Right? Like sci-fi! Speaking of futuristic, I was actually thinking… we need to book that weekend away. Somewhere to escape. Oh, yes! Please. I'm desperate for a break. Where were you thinking? Still leaning towards the kayaking in Donegal? Yeah, I think so. The scenery is incredible, and it’s good exercise. We could stay in that little cottage near Bundoran. Remember? The one with the view of the cliffs? Yes! That was lovely. Just… I’m still a bit anxious about leaving [Toddler's name] for that long. He’s starting to string a few more phrases together though. He said "juice gone" the other day. It was the clearest he's ever been. That’s brilliant! It’s so lovely to hear him communicating. Has the speech therapist made any progress with him? Actually, yes. She suggested we try incorporating more icons into his routine – visual cues to help him express himself.

Honestly, the neighbours are driving me mad. Mr. Henderson’s put up  another  set of fairy lights. They’re flashing, you know? Flashing red and green! Mum! Seriously?
