It wasn't pretty. Don't remind me! Speaking of things to buy, I really need a proper set of kitchen knives. The one I brought is… pathetic. Definitely a priority. And a decent vacuum cleaner. This place is going to get dusty fast. What about curtains? Those windows let in a  lot  of light. True. I was thinking blackout blinds for the bedroom, at least. Brighton can get surprisingly sunny. Speaking of sunny… I need to quit smoking. This move is a good excuse, right? It absolutely is. Baby steps. Maybe just one less a day? Easy for you to say, non-smoker. Right, so, what are we going to do tomorrow? Need to visit the bank, sort out the utilities… Tomorrow, we explore! There’s a fantastic farmer’s market in Lewes, apparently. They have the best seasonal produce. Asparagus is coming into season, you know. Oh, I love asparagus! This already feels better than unpacking boxes. And… ...did you hear anything last night?

Rach! So good to see you! Sorry I'm a little late – the traffic was insane coming from London. Liv! No worries at all, I was just getting a drink. So good to see you too! Peterborough’s surprisingly busy tonight. Tell me about it! So, what did you order? I’m thinking the halloumi fries - they smelled amazing when I walked past. I went for the calamari – you know me, always predictable! I’m really craving seafood. How's everything going? Last time we spoke, you were drowning in project reports, right? Don't even remind me! It's calmed down a bit now, thankfully. We launched the new campaign last week, which was a massive relief. Lots of late nights, but worth it. How's your placement going? Is it what you expected? It's... interesting. It’s at that marketing agency, yeah? It’s a steep learning curve, but I'm getting some really valuable experience. The people are lovely, but it’s a lot different to Uni lectures, let me tell you! I bet! All that theory put into practice, huh? So are your parents happy with it? Yeah, they love it. They're always asking if I'm learning loads. Mum keeps wanting to know if I can use my skills to promote her saree shop! Classic Mum move! My Mum's been on at me to come home for Sunday roast. Apparently, Dad's made a particularly good Yorkshire pudding. Oh, send me a picture! Speaking of home, are you still living in that tiny flat in London? Sadly, yes. Rent is extortionate. I’m seriously considering moving back to the suburbs when my lease is up. Maybe somewhere a little quieter. What about you? Still at your parents’ in Birmingham? Yeah, for now. It's convenient, you know? Saves on bills! Thinking about it, I actually miss my little sister loads. It’s nice being independent, but… It is. Remember that crazy holiday we had in Spain after second year? When we got completely lost trying to find that hidden beach? Oh my god! Don’t even! We walked for like, three hours! And then we found it, and it was beautiful, but we were so exhausted. I still have that ridiculous photo of us covered in sand. I do too! We should print them out, frame them. A proper throwback. We need to make more memories like that.

Honestly, this is a bit… posh, isn’t it? Not a patch on The Dun Cow back home. Cambridge is Cambridge, love. You can’t expect a proper Sunderland vibe. Though, I agree, it’s missing a certain… grit. Grit’s an understatement. It's missing the smell of the sea, the sound of the seagulls, and the slightly alarming amount of seagulls. I miss the seagulls. You and your seagulls. So, how’s the research going? Still wrestling with those elusive statistical anomalies? You have no idea. It feels like I’m spending my life chasing a decimal point. We had a proper meltdown in the team yesterday. Data set just… vanished. Poof. Gone. Blimey. That’s a nightmare. Did you manage to track it down? Eventually. Turns out someone accidentally saved it over with a previous version. Of course. After a three-hour panicked search and several strongly worded emails. Sounds stressful. You need a holiday. Something involving sand and, you know… not spreadsheets. You’re preaching to the choir. I was thinking of going back up to Northumberland. Hike along the coast, see if I can spot a puffin. Now you’re talking. Northumberland’s beautiful, isn't it? Proper wild. It is. Completely different from this… well, everything here. What about your PhD? Are you finally cracking the secrets of Victorian plumbing? Not quite, no. I’m getting there, though. Lots of tedious archive work, a surprising amount of muck smell, and a distinct lack of breakthroughs recently. My supervisor's starting to give me the ‘concerned’ look. The dreaded concerned look. Familiar territory. You know, I saw a really cute vintage coat in a charity shop the other day. A proper 60s shift dress thing. It made me think of you, actually. You’d look brilliant in it. Me? In a shift dress? That’s a dangerous combination. I’d probably trip over it and spill beer down it within five minutes. You'd rock it. You always have a good eye for style. Remember that band you used to go on about? The, uh… what were they called? The Northern Sparks? They're supporting Interpol next month. The Northern Sparks! Blimey, they are. Nearly forgot about them. They were brilliant, weren't they? Raw, energetic. Seriously good. I thought you’d be all over that. You’re right. I should definitely try to get tickets.

Alright, Grandma, you still watching the news? Seems like there’s always something going on. Aye, lad. Can’t escape it, can ya? Though, truth be told, it’s all a bit much these days, innit? Such a lot of shouting about nothing. It feels that way sometimes. Did you see what they’re saying about… well, about that new policy on… on renewable energy? Renewable energy, you say? Fancy name for wind turbines, eh? Making a right racket, those things do. Remember old Mr. Henderson down the street? He used to complain about the noise something awful. Said it kept him awake at night. Yeah, I read that a lot of people are worried about the noise. But isn't it important to try and be greener? Like, less pollution and stuff? Course it is, lad. Nobody wants a dirty world. But at what cost, eh? They’re chopping down trees to put 'em up, these turbines. And the birds...poor birds. Used to see flocks of them flying over Darlington, now… not so much. Hmm, fair point. But surely there are ways around that? Like, different locations or… bird-friendly turbine designs? Well, that’s what they always say, isn’t it? “We’ll find a way!” But do they? Seems like they just go and do what’s easiest for them, regardless of what it does to the rest of us. My teacher was saying that the government’s trying to meet these targets, like, to reduce carbon emissions or something. It’s complicated, though, isn't it? Complicated is one word for it. Deceitful's another. They promise you the world, and then… nothing changes. Remember Margaret Thatcher? Everyone said she'd fix everything. Grandma, I don’t even know who that is. Oh, lad. A long time ago. A very strong woman, or so they said. But she upset a lot of folks, she did. Made life hard for a lot of mining communities… it’s changed this country, it has. It’s just… a lot to take in, isn't it? I read some articles online, and it's all so divided. People shouting at each other. Aye, that's the trouble with this modern world. Everyone's got an opinion, and nobody's listening. Used to be, you could have a sensible conversation, even if you didn’t agree. Now it’s just… shouting match.

Right, now, that was a lovely bit of cod, wasn't it? Keep your elbows off the table, Jamie, please. Manners maketh the man, as they say. Sorry, Dad. He’s a growing boy, Liam. He needs the space. And honestly, it’s a fairly relaxed atmosphere here, isn’t it, Nana? Relaxed is a good word, Maggie. Though your grandfather would have had a fit if he saw any elbows on the table. Proper posture, he’d say. Aye, well, thankfully we’re not dealing with your Grandad tonight. Though, he’d have appreciated this weather, I reckon. Did you see the blood moon last night? Yeah! It was mental! All red. It was beautiful, wasn't it? I managed to snap a few photos. I'll show you later, Nana. A blood moon, you say? Always felt a wee bit ominous, those. Old wives' tales, of course, but still. Gave me a shiver up the spine. Nonsense, Agnes. It’s just science. Refraction and all that. Though I do admire a bit of superstitious blarney now and again. Speaking of blarney, Liam, have you booked that picnic at Fitzgerald's Park for next weekend? The kids are buzzing about it. Aye, sorted it. Saturday, right? Jamie’s been going on about it for a week now. Wants to take his new kite. It’s gonna be epic! Big loops and everything! Fitzgerald’s Park is lovely this time of year. Remember taking your father there when he was a wee lad, Maggie? He’d chase the pigeons for hours. Oh, I remember. He was a menace! A little terror, bless him. That reminds me, Agnes, I was wondering… could you possibly look after the kids next Saturday afternoon? I’ve got that project deadline looming, and Mary needs to be in Dublin for a conference. Oh, do I! Of course I can, dear. I love having those wee ones around. Keeps this old bird lively! Though, you’ll need to warn me if Jamie’s planning on chasing any pigeons. Don't worry, Nana. I’ll be too busy flying my kite. That’s wonderful, Nana, thank you so much. You're a lifesaver. Liam, are you going to finish your vegetables? Jamie! Eat your greens. They’re good for you. And no phones at the table, please. Family meals are important. Fine, Dad. Aye, meals like this.

So, you’ve seen the news about the Scottish referendum? Quite something, isn’t it? Indeed. It’s been dominating the papers. I can't say I'm surprised, though. Seems inevitable really, after all these years of simmering. I know, but it still feels quite… momentous. What do you make of it all? Difficult to say. There’s a lot at stake. My nephew in Edinburgh is quite fervent about it – wants them to go for it. Says it’s time for Scotland to chart its own course. My daughter’s taken a similar view. She’s got a lot of friends up there. Said they all genuinely believe they can build a fairer society. Good for them if they do. Though, I worry about the economic implications. Especially for the smaller businesses. Uncertainty doesn't do anyone any good. Quite right. Anyway, enough about politics! How’s the shop going? Still busy with the tourists? Surprisingly so, yes. Even with the rumblings of all this political upheaval, people still want a souvenir of Brighton. Though, I did have a bit of a saga this week. Interviewed a lad for the summer job. Seemed promising, good references... Oh? What happened? Well, he got halfway through the interview, and then casually mentioned he was expecting a significant inheritance. Said he was just "keeping his options open" until he knew exactly how much he’d be getting. Good heavens! The cheek of it! I know! I had to politely but firmly let him know that wasn’t quite the attitude we were looking for. Needed someone reliable, eager to work, not someone expecting a handout. You were right to. It's all about work ethic, isn’t it? Speaking of which, how’s Sarah doing with her job search? Last I heard she was feeling a bit disheartened. She is, a bit. Had a couple of interviews that didn't go her way. Apparently, one headteacher thought she was "too passionate" about teaching special needs kids. Can you believe it? Too passionate? What a ridiculous thing to say! Where have they been all their lives if enthusiasm for children is a problem? Exactly! Keeps her bouncing. Says she'll find the right place eventually. She's been trying not to take it all to heart. That’s good. She’s a determined girl. You know, sometimes I think I’m trying too hard to keep busy.

Right, next stop, Aaron's place, then we’ll swing by Ann’s. Feeling alright back there? Yeah, Dad, fine. Just a bit… crowded, I guess. Cramped in the back with all the boxes. Tell me about it. I’m practically sitting on a bag of frozen peas. Well, I’ve tried to pack as lightly as possible! Honestly, having to move all this stuff again is a bit of a nightmare. It is a bit, isn’t it? But it'll be worth it once you’re settled in. Less travel time to work for you, Ann. That's a win. That's true. Though I'll miss my garden terribly. And the village shop – those sausages were to die for. Did you manage to grab any of those sausages for the journey? I'm starving. I did! There’s a couple in the cooler. We’ll have them at lunchtime. Excellent news. Anything else edible in the car, Dad? Just some apples and a few biscuits. Bit of a bare bones selection, I'm afraid. Didn't want to overload the car. Speaking of which, you two keeping an eye on the Sat Nav? I'm worried about these narrow lanes. Yeah, got it on my phone, Dad. Seems alright so far, aside from those crazy winds we just hit. The wind was ferocious! Honestly, sounded like it was trying to rip the car door off. I hope it hasn't done any damage to the fence at my old house. I’ll have to check when I get there. You thinking of getting a new fence? That one was looking a bit worse for wear. Possibly. Depends on the damage and what I can afford, really. You know how it is, always something to fix. I'm trying to save for a decent pension, but… Pensions. Don’t even get me started. They've messed everything up haven’t they. Should’ve just stuck with the old system. Honestly, Dad, pensions are a bit dry for lunchtime conversation. Sorry, sorry. Just thinking aloud. You two ever thought about investing in anything? Tried a bit of Bitcoin once. Lost a small fortune. Stick to apples, thanks. Bitcoin? Good heavens! No, I’m much too cautious for that. I've got a couple of savings accounts, and that’s about it. Sensible. Sensible. Speaking of caution… did you see that article about that man who tried to break the world record for stacking coins on his forehead?

Right, you’re sure this is the quickest way, Grandad? Feels like we’re going miles around. Quickest? Lass, the quickest way is usually the most boring. This way’s scenic. Besides, you relax, let your old grandad navigate. I used to navigate lorries all over the country, you know. Didn't get lost once. Lorries were different then, weren’t they? Sat Navs and all that. I’m just a bit worried about being late. Relax, Elara. It’s only a meeting, not the end of the world. And, honestly, a bit of countryside is a nice change. Easy for you to say, Marcus. You don’t have a presentation to run. And speaking of nice changes, did you see that cow back there? Proper big one. Aye, good Yorkshire. Solid cow, that one. They’re bred for milk, you know. Big frames, good udders… You know a lot about cows, Grandad. Lived near farms all my life, didn’t I? Learned a thing or two. Used to sneak in and watch them calve when I was a lad, I did. Nearly got chased by the farmer once. Sneaking into farms. You were a bit of a rascal, weren’t you? Just curious, lad. Just curious. Were those sheep, the ones we saw a bit earlier? Looked like a right flock. They were. And some goats as well. Honestly, this is like driving through Farmer Giles’ adventure park. Should’ve stopped and got some ice cream. We’ve got time. Should we pull over? No, no. We’re almost there, I think. Unless… are you sure you know where we're going, Grandad? You’ve been awfully quiet. Course I know where we’re going. I’m just… thinking about the cows. Good cows are a dying breed, you know. All these fancy breeds, not as hardy as the old Yorkshires. Right. Hardy cows. That’s good to know. Marcus, have a look on the map, will you? Just to make sure we're actually heading in the right direction. Yeah, you’re fine. Grandad's got you on the right track. It's just a slightly… unconventional route. "Slightly unconventional." That’s what they said about the last route you navigated, Grandad, and we ended up on a single-track road for three miles. It was a scenic single-track road! You should appreciate the scenery, lass. I appreciate getting to my meeting on time, Grandad.

This is lovely, isn’t it? So much better than our usual Tuesday night fish fingers! Thanks for having us, Michael. And you, Sarah, the roast is smelling divine. It's no problem at all, Mum. Glad you could make it. Michael’s been complaining about eating beans on toast every night. Needed a change. How was the choir practice? Oh, it was…eventful. Mrs. Higgins, bless her heart, decided to introduce a Bulgarian folk song. Completely threw everyone. The harmonies were… challenging, to say the least. Bulgarian folk music? Sounds like a recipe for chaos. I remember trying to learn the ukulele. Gave up after a week. My fingers just wouldn't cooperate. You and the ukulele, Dad! That’s a story for another time. Mum, did you ever manage to get that email to Mr. Davies about the school fundraiser? Not yet, dear. I've been meaning to, but between the choir and sorting through old photographs, my brain has been completely full. It’s for the new library wing, isn't it? They really need the money. The children deserve a proper library. A good library is essential. It was the one place I found some peace at school, really. Escaping the football fanatics. Always preferred a good book and a bit of quiet over a muddy pitch. You wouldn’t think it, looking at you now. Always out walking the dogs, keeping fit! Speaking of exercise, have you thought about joining the walking group in town, Mum? They do a lovely circuit around Derwentwater. I have, Sarah, but the thought of all that fresh air… I’m a creature of habit, you know. A cup of tea and a crossword is my exercise for the day. Don't let her fool you, Sarah. She used to be a formidable netball player back in the day. Remember the St. Michael's team? She was the star player. Oh, stop it, Michael. That was a lifetime ago. My knees wouldn't thank me now. Although, a bit of gentle stretching wouldn't hurt... Right. Well, while you’re contemplating stretching, I’m going to grab some more gravy. Sarah, have you heard anything more from Aunt Eleanor? Is she still considering coming to visit for Christmas? No, not yet. I’ll give her a ring next week. She seemed keen, but you know how she is, always dithering about.

Right, so Mrs. Davies at parent’s evening said… well, she said Thomas is struggling a little with his maths. Specifically, times tables. But I know my two times table! You do, darling, you’re brilliant at your two times table. It’s the six, sevens, eights, nines that are proving tricky. And Eliza, you were really well-behaved, apparently. Ms. Peterson said you were a delight. I helped her find her lost pencil! And I told her a story about a dragon and a princess. That's wonderful, sweetheart. See, Thomas? Be like Eliza, help others. But dragons are cool! Maths isn't cool. Maths  is  cool! It's like a puzzle. And we can practice together, can't we? We’ll do fifteen minutes every evening. How does that sound? Fifteen minutes... Can I watch superheroes after? Possibly. Let’s see how well you’re doing. Speaking of stories, World Book Day is next week, isn’t it? Have you both thought about what characters you want to dress up as? I’m going to be Hermione Granger! I’ve already got the wand. Excellent choice! A very clever witch. And Thomas? What are you thinking? I don't know. Maybe Harry Potter. But that’s boring. It’s a classic, though. And if you don’t want to be Harry, there are loads of other characters. Remember that book we read about the little boy who went to the circus? The one with the lion? Yes! You loved that one. Maybe you could dress up as a lion tamer! Lions are scary. Daddy said lions smell like cooked human flesh! Eliza! Don’t say things like that! Where did you even… Daddy said! He was joking! Right, okay. Well, that's... a slightly morbid thing to say. Let’s just stick to the dragons and witches, shall we? So, after school on Tuesday, you’ve got swimming, Thomas, right? And Eliza, you've got your ballet class. And homework. And homework. Yes. I'll pack your swimming bag tonight, darling. And maybe we can find a book about maths to read. Something fun. Do you want to pop outside after dinner and pick a couple of books to look at? Can I choose a dragon book? Of course you can, sweetie. And Thomas, you can pick out a superhero comic, if that makes you feel better about learning your times tables.

Right, so Oisin's birthday’s next month. We need to start thinking about something. What do you reckon? Well, he keeps going on about bouncy castles. It’s all he talks about. Bounce! Bounce! Aye, youngsters and their bouncy castles. Reminds me of the fairground in Glasgow when I was a wee lass. Though it was more about the candy floss than the bouncing back then. A bouncy castle might be a bit extravagant, though, wouldn’t it? Maybe a smaller party, at home? Invite a few of the lads from school? I think he’d be happy with that, honestly. We could do a treasure hunt in the garden, maybe a little cake… Treasure hunt sounds good. Liam’s been saying he wants to help organise something. Could give him a bit of responsibility, you know, keep him entertained. That’s a lovely idea. He’s been moaning about being bored lately. Is he still wanting to work at that curtain shop down the road? Aye, he’s keen on it. Says he’s learning a lot about fabrics and things. A bit of pocket money wouldn’t go amiss either. He’s going through a phase of wanting everything practically immediately. Teenagers, eh? Always needing. Always wanting. When I was his age, we were grateful for a wee bar of chocolate and a shiny penny. Times have changed, haven't they? Speaking of money, did you ever sort out that treasurer nonsense with the garage committee? Oh, don’t remind me. Honestly, it’s a nightmare. People thinking they know better, questioning every penny. It's a thankless job, isn’t it? You're forever chasing up payments. I keep thinking about putting my foot down and making them all pay upfront. You can't be doing with that sort of hassle. It’s all too stressful. Just steer clear of it, dear. Let someone else worry about the finances. Easier said than done! It’s important someone does it though. And it’s not like there's exactly a queue of volunteers. True. Thinking about things that are stressful…did you see anything about that new tax on rented houses? Seems like they’re squeezing us from all sides. They are. Absolutely bonkers. It’s just going to make it harder to keep on top of bills. So, back to Oisin. Have you had any calls from those charities again?

Right, I’ve got a right belter of a word game for you lot. You'll love this, Liam, you’re always moaning about how boring things are. Oh, here we go. What is it this time, Tilly? Something involving obscure Latin roots, I presume? Nah, nothing like that, posh boy. It’s called “Chain Reaction Words.” You have to say a word, and the next person has to say a word that starts with the last letter of the previous word. Simple as that. Sounds alright, actually. A bit like Scattergories, but less pressure. Less pressure? Scattergories is the zenith of pressured wordplay! Fine, I’ll play. Let's start. Apple. Alright, alright. Easy peasy. Elephant! Terrific. Right, terrific. Hmm, that's a bit tricky. Cat. Brilliant! Dog! And I’m sticking with the animals theme. Zebra. Keeping it going nicely. Okay, that’s… that's a bit clever, I’ll give you that. Alright, Zebra. Alright, alright… Tea. I’m drawing a blank. Proper brain freeze. Tea! Excellent! Alright, er… sun. Nice one! Now, that's a good one. Squirrel. Oh, for goodness sake. Squirrel? Seriously? I'm struggling here. Let me think… last letter's ‘l’… that’s tough. Lovely. Lovely! Aye, good choice. Alright, yeah… eel. Easy now. Lobster. Lobster...Right, this is getting ridiculous. I'm starting to sweat. Okay, last letter's 'r'...Right...Radio! Please don’t let me fail. Radio! Brilliant! See, I knew you could do it! Alright… Owl! Wow, you're really sticking with the animals. Okay, then… alright… Umm… Unicorn. You are winding me up! Unicorn! Of all the words! Oh, that’s just brilliant! Okay, right, ‘n’… hmm… Now, this is properly hard. Nightingale. Nightingale! Good on ya! Alright, er...Excellent. Fantastic. That's it, I’m calling it! We don’t need to play anymore. It's too brilliant. Agreed. My brain’s officially melted. That unicorn did it in. Let’s get some biscuits. You owe us both a victory cuppa, Tilly. Rest assured, it’s all on me. And next time, we’re playing something even harder! You’ll be begging for mercy. Bring it on! I'm ready for the challenge. Oh, lord… let's just enjoy the biscuits first. Please. Alright, alright… Biscuits it is then. But don't think you've escaped just yet. I've got loads more games lined up! Here we go again...

Oh my god, look at this! Remember that holiday to Skegness? Blimey! Is that… is that really you in that inflatable donut thing? You look terrified! I  was  terrified! The sea was freezing, and I kept thinking I was going to get swept out to sea. But Mum insisted we had to get the picture. Classic Mum move. She's always got to document everything. Remember that time she tried to film me falling off the climbing frame? Oh god, yes! That was brutal. You were so embarrassed. I think you hid in the shed for a week after that. I totally did. I was convinced the whole world had seen it. Anyway, what have you been up to? Besides reliving traumatic childhood memories. Not much, honestly. Been buried in coursework. I swear, I'm just going to nap my way through the rest of the semester. I slept for like, twelve hours straight yesterday. Yeah, I get it. I've been mainlining coffee just to stay awake in lectures. Did you hear about the band ‘Cosmic Bloom’ though? They’re playing at The Live Lounge next month. No way! Seriously? I love ‘em. Remember we used to blast them out in the car on the way to sixth form? How could I forget? Every single Saturday morning. Nearly got us pulled over for noise pollution. Worth it. We should try and get tickets. It'd be good to actually  do  something other than study. Definitely. Are Chloe and Josh free? We should all go. I’ll text them. Josh has been a bit quiet lately, I wonder what he’s up to. He probably just has loads on. He's always been a bit of a workaholic. Speaking of… Did you see that post Sarah put up on Instagram? About her and Mark having a massive row? Oh no! What happened? I saw something, but I didn't really want to pry. Apparently, it was over him forgetting their anniversary. Can you believe it? After all that fuss she made about planning it! That’s awful! Poor Sarah. She's always been so madly in love with him. Honestly, people can be so clueless sometimes. Totally. It's just... shakes head ... So, you free for a cheeky pint before the lecture tomorrow. Need to de-stress after this conversation! Definitely. Sounds perfect. You are a lifesaver. Coming here and having a good laugh is exactly what I needed.

Right, so let’s run through this planning application one last time before tomorrow. I want to be absolutely certain we’ve covered everything. Absolutely. It's a tricky one, isn't it? The community pushback is significant. It is. And justified, to a degree. The increased traffic alone… but we need to make a strong case for the affordable housing component. That's the key selling point, really. Agreed. I’ve been tweaking the presentation slides. I think I’ve managed to make the traffic impact assessment look a little less… alarming. Added some mitigation strategies, you know, cycle lanes, bus stop improvements. Good. Did you include the updated figures from Sustrans? Showing the potential for increased cycling uptake if the area is properly connected? Yes, right at the end. I thought a positive spin, rather than dwelling on the negative. How are you feeling about your opening statement? I’m fairly happy with it. I just need to ensure I'm not overly apologetic. We’re not  sorry  for providing much-needed housing. We're presenting a viable, albeit imperfect, solution. Want to hear it? Please do. I’m always happy to offer a fresh perspective. Okay, here goes. “Members of the committee, we understand and appreciate the concerns raised by local residents regarding this application. However, the urgent need for affordable housing within our district cannot be ignored. This proposal, while requiring careful consideration of potential impacts, represents a significant opportunity to address a critical social need..." Strong start. A little bit formal maybe, but appropriate for the setting. Perhaps soften the “critical social need” a tad? Sounds a little… heightened. You’re right. Perhaps “an important social need.” Much better. Okay, revised. What about the structure of the presentation overall? I was thinking a brief overview, the need for housing, the proposal itself, the potential impacts, mitigation strategies, and then a summary emphasizing the benefits. That sounds solid. I think the order is crucial. We need to establish the ‘why’ before diving into the ‘what’. If they don't understand why we  need  this, they won’t be receptive to anything else. Agreed. And I'm planning on referencing the council's own housing needs assessment early on. Using their data, not ours. Smart move. Demonstrates we’re aligned with council policy. And did you manage to get the updated visualisations of the proposed landscaping? Yes, those landed this morning.

Honestly, this day. I need wine. And a giant slab of chocolate. Rough one then? What's set you off? Where do I even start? The meeting went on forever, Mark from accounts keeps using Comic Sans in all his reports -  Comic Sans , honestly! - and then the printer jammed, and I spent twenty minutes wrestling with it. It’s just… relentless. Ugh, I feel you. Mondays are brutal. Did you manage to grab anything for dinner? I'm thinking pasta. Nah, didn't have time. Work ate my entire lunch break. Is there anything in the fridge? I'm too exhausted to go out. There's some leftover chicken stir-fry. And I picked up some pesto. We could do that and a salad? You’re a lifesaver. Seriously. Pesto is  exactly  what I need. So, what have  you  been up to? Anything exciting? Not particularly. Work was… work. Had a really challenging session with a patient this afternoon, but that’s par for the course, I suppose. Though, you won’t believe what I heard about Sarah Miller… Oh yes? Spill! Is it true she's engaged to Liam from the gym? Apparently! Saw her the other day, and she was practically glowing. He's a bit vanilla, isn’t he? A bit? He's the human equivalent of a beige cardigan. But she seems happy, so that’s what counts, I guess. Remember when we used to gossip about her and Tom back in school? Oh my god, yes! We thought they were the ultimate power couple. He was captain of the rugby team, and she was head girl. Look at us now, both stressed and fuelled by pesto. Exactly! And remember Chloe Davies? The girl who always wore those ridiculously oversized sunglasses? The one who dated Aaron for like, five minutes? What about her? Apparently, she’s living in Dubai now and running a really successful travel agency. Can you believe it? I saw her on Instagram. Living the high life! Wow! That’s amazing. This is quite a turnout for Alumni Day, isn't it? I’m Eleanor – Eleanor Davies. Language Research Co-ordinator here. Hi Eleanor! I'm Clara Hayes. Language Research Administrator. Lovely to meet you. Wonderful city, though sadly… It's a difficult time for the region, isn't it? Indeed. It's heartbreaking to see what's happening.

Right, nearly ready! Smells amazing, doesn't it? Bit heavy on the garlic, maybe, but who cares? Honestly, it smells incredible. Proper comfort food. Much needed after that day. Like, what's the connection? Oh my god, no! Seriously? That’s wild. They’re probably just trying to be fancy. Fancy and wildly inappropriate! Speaking of rom-coms, Mum's been on one lately. She’s obsessed with that new one, "Anyone But You". Oh yeah, I've seen ads for that! Is it any good? Apparently amazing. Right then, so you've been lookin' at that poll this week, haven't you, lad? The one about the Scottish referendum? Aye, Mum. It's close, isn't it? It's not like choosin' between a packet of crisps, is it? This changes things. No, it’s massive. I was talkin’ to Tom at sixth form the other day, and he was saying he’s leaning towards independence. Oh, really? What’s his reasoning? He says it's about gettin' more control over things, you know? Like healthcare, education... and he thinks the Westminster government ignores Scotland. He's got a point, that. Been happenin' for years, hasn’t it? But then, lookin' at the bigger picture, there’s the economy, isn't there? Being part of the UK gives Scotland a bigger market, more investment. Yeah, but is that worth losin’ control over your own laws? It’s a tricky one. Aye, it is. My dad, bless ‘im, he always said, “Yorkshire lad, Yorkshire lad, stick with England, lad!” A proper unionist he was. Never wavered. Did he ever think about Scotland at all? Hmm, not really. He was more concerned with whether Hull were gonna win their next match, that’s what. But he did say once, “What’s good for England is good for Yorkshire, and what’s good for Yorkshire is good for me.” Simple as that. Sounds a bit narrow-minded, doesn't it? So, what do you reckon, Mum? What way are you leaning? Honestly? I’m still on the fence. I can see the arguments on both sides. Scotland’s got a right to choose its own destiny, that’s undeniable. But the potential upheaval… the economic uncertainty… it's worryin'. Do you think they’ll actually go for it? Hard to say, isn’t it? It's a wee bit closer than I thought it’d be, that's for sure. The polls are all over the place, aren’t they?

Okay, here's a conversation based on your provided context. I've tried to capture the distinct regional dialects and dynamics of a group of close friends watching a reality show.   Setting:   A cluttered student flat in Chester. Four girls – Grace , Maisie , Chloe , and Tilly & Freya – are sprawled on a sofa, cushions scattered, watching Jeremy Kyle. Empty takeaway containers litter the coffee table.   Conversation:   Grace: Honestly, look at ‘im. He’s well proper dramatic, innit? “My missus says I’ve been seeing Jezebel!” Jezebel! Who names someone Jezebel? Maisie: Yeah, bruv! It's a right laugh, though, isn' say? The way 'e’s shakin' 'is 'ead like 'e’s just found out the earth is round. Chloe: I just feel a bit sorry for the poor girl, really. Gets dragged into all this shouting and mess. It’s relentless. Tilly: Reckon she’s enjoyin’ it a bit, though! Look at 'er smirkin’. Proper theatrical, she is. Freya: Aye, she’s puttin’ on. Everyone on that show’s puttin’ on, aren't they? It’s all for the cameras. Maisie: Nah, some of 'em are genuine, love. You can tell. Like, the ones wi' the dodgy tattoos and the look in their eyes… real sadness, that is. Grace: Dodgy tattoos! You’re right! What is it with that show and dodgy tattoos? You’d think folk would learn. Chloe: It’s proper bizarre. I was listening to a podcast about accents the other day, and they were talking about elision. You know, like how people drop sounds when they speak. Tilly: El…what now? Chloe: Elision! Like…you know, how you might say "gonna" instead of "going to”. It’s a thing loads of accents do. Like, you girls over here, you’re dropping ‘h’ sounds! Grace: We're not! It's just… natural. Sounds better without the 'h' sometimes. Maisie: You sound like you're shoutin' when you keep your 'h's, Grace! It's dead funny. Freya: She sounds like she’s lecturing everyone! Grace: Alright, alright! I don’t need you lot to teach me how to speak. You sound like you're swallowing your words, Maisie! Maisie: That’s just how we do it, pet. Proper scouse, innit? Chloe: It’s fascinating though, isn't it? How accents change depending on where you're from and even social class. Tilly: So Jeremy Kyle’s got a posh accent 'cos he's on the telly?

Oh, come on! That was a definite foul! Robbed, honestly. You always say that, Liv. Every time someone breathes on a player, it's a foul in your book. No, but seriously! Look at the replay. He clipped his ankle! It's blatant. They’re letting them get away with murder today. Right, murder. It’s a game of football, not a heist movie. Though, I suppose the stakes feel pretty high for some people. They are! My dad would be having a meltdown right now if he was here. He'd be shouting at the telly and making all sorts of noises. Picture that. Definitely entertaining. So, did you finish that scarf you were working on? The one for your niece? Almost! Just the sleeves left. I’m trying to find a decent pattern for them, something a bit…cozy. Winter’s coming, you know. Need to keep little Maisie warm. You’re a knitting wizard. Honestly. I tried to make a hat once. It looked like a potato. A potato hat? Oh, bless. You’re better at, you know, complicated scientific stuff. Leave the knitting to those of us whose fingers are slightly less… clumsy. True. Speaking of complicated, have you been following the Olympics at all? I caught a bit of the diving last night. Absolutely incredible. A bit! I'm trying to, but it’s hard to focus with this game on. The diving was amazing though, wasn't it? The precision... mind-blowing. Seriously. And the pressure! Imagine performing like that in front of millions. Makes my research presentations seem like a walk in the park. Although, defending my thesis  did  feel a bit like being judged by a panel of very stern Olympians. I can relate. It’s the same sort of feeling, isn't it? That no matter how much you prepare, you're always worried they'll find something wrong. Exactly. So, speaking of Maisie… any progress on names? You and Sarah still bouncing ideas around? Oh, yes! We’ve got a shortlist. It's actually surprisingly hard. We want something that feels… right, you know? Something that suits her. Definitely. I remember when my mum and dad were trying to decide on a name for me. They argued for weeks! Ended up with a very classic, very sensible name. Classic and sensible is good. Unless it’s one of those names that everyone calls you ironically for the rest of your life.

Right, so Barry the Bee is  still  obsessed with The Bee Movie. Has watched it approximately 7 times this week. He says Barry needs to get honey! And make the human bees pay! King Arthur did it better. He had knights. Yes, darling, King Arthur had knights. Far more impressive than a tiny bee demanding money, isn't he? What’s that you’ve got there? A sword? Are you going to be a knight? Maybe a king. A king! And what would you do as a king? I’d make everyone eat Royal fruits! Royal fruits? What are those? These! They're Royal. We're going to the Olympic Stadium on Saturday, remember? The diving competition? Yes! We have to be silent! Extremely silent. Like little ninjas. It’ll be good. It's just... I do wish we could take you lovely children to nice restaurants more often. It’s just such a palaver, isn't it? Sticky fingers, spilled drinks… Can we go to Granny’s old house? Granny's old house. Always the answer with you two, isn’t it? That garden  was  amazing. Remember the wisteria? It was the most incredible purple. And the swings! Yes, the swings. Maybe we should book a weekend there soon. It's been far too long. Honestly, sometimes, a simple garden and some swings are better than any Royal palace. Don't you think, darling? Now, who wants another satsuma? They’re Royal, you know. Me! I'm a king! I need Royal fruit! You certainly do, your Majesty.

Honestly, that tip was quite the ordeal wasn’t it? I swear, half the things I took there I could have used! Aye, tell me about it. My back is absolutely killing me. Thought I was going to throw it out wrestling with that old sideboard. Absolutely ludicrous, some of the stuff people just chuck. Grandad, you should have got the sideboard! Let your grandma finish telling us about her mother's auction prowess. It’s apparently the most riveting topic in the world. Oh, hush, David. It was a different time, you know. People valued things more. They made things to last. It wasn’t all this throwaway culture we have now. Speaking of culture, has anyone been watching that new detective series on BBC? The one set in York? Nah, too slow. I'm watching space stuff. They found another planet that might have water! See, there's a difference in interests. Your grandma’s interested in porcelain dolls and your cousin wants to find aliens. I’d like to find a decent NHS dentist, that’s what I’d like to find. It’s absolutely ridiculous trying to get an appointment. You're not alone there, love. It's a joke. We’re lucky to have a good practice in Darlington – though even they’re struggling. Grandad, can I have some cake? They’ve got chocolate cake. Of course, love. You deserve it after lugging all those boxes to the tip with your mum. Speaking of, Mary, have you made any decisions about moving house? It’s been dragging on forever.

Right, so I’ve been thinking about the Tate Modern. Fancy a trip next weekend? We haven't been in ages. Oh, yeah! That would be brilliant. It’s been way too long. But…how are we going to park? She’s notoriously hard to buy for. I know! I’ve been racking my brain. I was thinking maybe a hamper? Like a posh one from M&S? That's a good shout! She loves those. Invitation to interview next month. I'm actually buzzing! Honestly, that's amazing, Liam! I knew you'd smash it. You've worked so hard. Cheers, love. It’s a bit terrifying, though. Proper competitive. Need to start thinking about what to wear and prepare some answers. Do you think I should research more about the lecturers?

Ugh, this pizza is actually pretty grim, isn’t it? Like, seriously, they could at least  try  a bit more. Tell me about it! I was hoping for something vaguely edible after that lecture. "The wheels on the bus go round and round! Round and round! Round and round!" That’s lovely, Cian! Keep it up, boyo. You’re a proper star. He's having a right time tonight, isn't he? Bless him. Honestly, I can’t believe he’s still asleep. In his pants. He looked so comfortable, though. Like a little, rumpled bear. And it was chilly last night! Good job you got him an extra blanket. Perhaps we should start a savings jar… Good idea! We could even call it… the “Extension Fund.” Corny, I know. It’s perfect. It’s so bad, it’s good. Hey, shush! They’re stirring. Daddy! Pants! Oh, you are a menace! Yes, darling, Daddy was wearing pants. Very important pants. Now, who wants breakfast? And don't you dare ask for pancakes again! Last time was a disaster… Don’t tempt him. Let’s stick to toast and jam today. And maybe another blanket for the little bear still sleeping soundly. Pancakes! Jam! Alright, alright. Just… quietly, please! The architect is waiting for my feedback on those plans… after breakfast, of course. And after convincing little ones to stay dressed.

This coffee is…adequate. Not quite the robust Italian blend I’m used to, you know? Ah, you’re missing the proper espresso, eh? Tredegar coffee doesn't quite cut it for a man of Cairo. Though, I must say, it’s better than what we had last week. Remember that swill? Don’t remind me! It tasted like dishwater. Speaking of things that need improvement, I’m wrestling with the kitchen. Decided to finally re-tile. Absolute nightmare. Tiling, eh? You’ll need a very steady hand. My daughter attempted her bathroom last year – looked like a toddler had been at it with a trowel. Precisely! I’m considering hiring someone. Though, the quotes I’m getting are exorbitant. Do you know anyone reputable? I might. My cousin Gareth – he’s a builder, does a good job, bit of a character though. We'll have to see. More pressing, though, have you heard anything about the funding for the quantum entanglement project? Not a peep. I submitted the proposal weeks ago. It’s vital, you know. Without it, the Hadron collider portion is essentially dead. Another example of bureaucratic inertia, I suppose. Aye, it’s always like that. They hold onto your money, then wonder why research stagnates. Did you include the water modelling projections? That’s your strength, isn’t it? Showing how entanglement can improve hydrological predictions? Of course! I thought it was a compelling argument. They’re also asking for more ethical justifications, apparently. As if understanding the fundamental nature of the universe is inherently unethical. Ha! You’re right, it's absurd. They're trying to apply risk assessment to a realm that’s beyond comprehension. It’s like asking a badger how to build a spaceship. Exactly! Anyway, back to the kitchen…I’m contemplating a Tuscan style theme, you know? Cream tiles, terracotta accents. Something to remind me of a proper holiday in Italy. Tuscany, nice choice. My wife and I went there a few years back. Stunning countryside. The water there was fantastic too, so pure. It’s a stark contrast to what we get here now, isn’t it? Thames Water is an absolute disgrace. Don’t get me started on water companies! They’re charging a fortune for a service that’s openly failing. It's criminal, really. Should be nationalised. I agree completely. They seem to bleed the country dry then claim they can't afford to fix the leaking pipes.

Right, operation Lego sort is a go. Leo, stop building a dinosaur-unicorn hybrid, please. It’s not structurally sound. But it’s awesome, Mummy! It breathes fire  and  sparkles! I'm sure it is, darling, but we need to sort them into colours, remember? Red, blue, yellow, green… Green like Hulk! Exactly! Green like the Hulk. See, Elsie? Hulk is green Lego. Now, Leo, can you put all the red bricks in this bowl? But I need red for the dragon’s wings! The dragon can wait, sweetie. We need to get this sorted so we can actually  build  something properly. Maybe you can build a cool spaceship after? A spaceship! Cool! Can it have lasers? Of course, it can have lasers! Elsie, darling, are you finding any blue pieces? Blue for Michelangelo! Yes! Brilliant! Michelangelo needs blue for his mask. You’re a superhero identifier! Do you know which turtle is red? Raphael! He’s grumpy. He is a bit grumpy, isn’t he? Just like Bart Simpson sometimes. Oh, speaking of Simpsons, we need to watch an episode this weekend. Can we watch Tower of Terror? The one with the scary elevator? We can definitely watch that! Maybe after we finish sorting the Lego. Although, are you sure you don't want to put some red on your dinosaur-unicorn? Just a little. Maybe… but just a tiny bit. He needs a fire breath effect. A tiny bit. Right. Now, Elsie, have you seen any yellow? We're building a golden snitch later, remember? For Harry Potter. Yellow like Pikachu! Exactly! Pikachu and the Golden Snitch both have yellow. You're so clever. We should totally go to the cinema to see the new Wonka film. Can we get chocolate? Lots and lots of chocolate! We can get chocolate. It's almost Easter, after all. Granny's been saving some of the nice ones, you know, the ones with the caramel inside. Granny's is the best! Can we go see her soon? She needs help with her garden. We definitely will. We'll go next weekend and help her get the roses pruned and maybe even start on the shed renovation. Do you want to help me sort through her old photos? There might be some interesting ones. Photos! With people! Yes with people. And maybe some Lego boxes, who knows? Now, let's focus on this pile of bricks, superheroes and wizards need a well-organised base of operations.

God, it’s good to be back. This flat feels…normal again. Welcome back! You look knackered. How was Greece? Seriously, spill. Intense, amazing, exhausting… all of the above. The beaches were incredible, obviously. Picture postcard stuff. But it was so hot! Like, genuinely uncomfortably hot. I think I spent most of my time just lying on a sunbed, trying to remember how to breathe. Sounds idyllic, if a bit melting. Did you manage to do any exploring? Beyond the beach, I mean. A bit, yeah. We went to some ancient ruins, which were predictably impressive, but absolutely swarming with tourists. And we took a boat trip to this tiny island… it was gorgeous, completely unspoilt. But the taverna we ate at… honestly, the food was questionable. Questionable how? Like, actively dodgy questionable, or just… bland? More bland. Like, they'd clearly never heard of seasoning. I think I ate a whole plate of grilled vegetables without tasting a single thing. Oh no! That’s a tragedy. Well, you’re back now. I made a massive batch of lentil soup yesterday. It’s warming up nicely. You’re an absolute saint. I’m starving. Did you miss me at all? Of course, I did! It was weirdly quiet without your constant humming. And I had to deal with Leo’s questionable music taste all by myself. Oh god, don't remind me. What’s he been listening to? More of that obscure Norwegian techno? Worse. 80s power ballads. Seriously, I wanted to throw the speakers out the window. Classic Leo. Speaking of people... how was Sarah and Mark's wedding? You went before I did. It was lovely! Really beautiful ceremony. Sarah looked stunning, obviously. Mark looked…well, relieved, mostly. They seemed genuinely happy though. Did you see his mum? Briefly. Managed to avoid any intense conversation with her. Remember last Christmas when she tried to set me up with her nephew? Oh god, yes! The one who worked in accounting and collected stamps. Absolutely terrifying. Exactly! So I made a strategic retreat to the kitchen. Anyway, I have to tell you about Tom… Tom?  Tom  Tom? As in, your Tom? Yes,  that  Tom. I ran into him at the airport. No! Seriously? What happened? Don’t leave me hanging! It was…awkward. Really awkward. He was with someone. A very… polished woman. Definitely not my type, but he seemed quite smitten.

Right then, lads. Tea's nearly on. John’s put the fire on proper this time, didn’t he, John? Don’t want you shivering away, Mum and Dad. Aye, he did a good job, our John. Nice and warm in here now. Much better than that draughty house we used to live in. Aye, remember that wind tunnel, Mary? Blew the washing straight off the line. Grandad, you’re telling that story again. You tell that story every time we come round! Leave him be, love. It’s a good story. Besides, John's been working hard getting this place tidy for you two. He’s a good lad. He is that, Mary. Always willing to lend a hand. You brought the rhubarb crumble did you love? I did indeed. Fresh from the oven. Though the rhubarb was a bit stringy this year, weren't it? Think the weather’s got to it. Stringy rhubarb, eh? Means it needs more sugar. Always did when your father was about. He'd put half a bag in! Grandparents are always telling stories about Grandad. He was a character, your grandad, he was. Remember that time he tried to fix the telly with a spoon? Oh, aye! And blamed the electricians afterwards! Said they'd done a terrible job! Aye, he did. Stubborn as an ox, that man. But we loved him. So, Mum, what about getting that fence sorted out? It’s looking a bit dodgy, isn’t it? Aye, I’ve been thinking about that. I’ve got a few quotes from builders, but nothing concrete yet. John says he could have a go at it, but he’s got that presentation at work next week… You’re busy enough as it is, lad. Don’t go taking on too much. Yeah, John. Focus on that presentation. Mum, maybe we could get some of those panels you see at B&Q, you know, the ones that slot together? Might be easier. That’s a thought, love. I’ll have a look. Keeps the foxes out too, doesn't it? That's important. They've been sniffing around the bird feeders again. Foxes! Naughty creatures. Used to steal my hen's eggs, they did! Dreadful bother. Aye, they are. Clever things, though, in their own way. Grandad, do you want another biscuit? There’s ginger snaps and shortbread. Shortbread, please, lad. Nice and buttery.

Right, so I was reading up a bit more about Great Ormond Street this evening. It's just… incredible, isn’t it? All they do for those children. Mummy, is Tinkerbell a real fairy? That’s a very good question, sweetheart. In the films, she's a very special, magical fairy, isn't she? Like in Peter Pan? Peter Pan flies! And he has pirates! He does indeed! Brave Peter Pan. But fairies aren’t really real in the way that Peter Pan and pirates aren’t, darling. It’s a story, a wonderful story. But the people at Great Ormond Street,  they  do real magic, helping real children. Like Tinkerbell? In a way, yes. They help children get better, just like Tinkerbell helps Peter Pan. They have amazing doctors and nurses and scientists. They do amazing work. We should definitely pick something to donate, shouldn’t we, both of you? Can we pick the sparkly stuff? Like Tinkerbell has! We’ll see what we can find, little man. We’ll see. Do you know why I was thinking about all this, though? Why, Mummy? Well, we were talking about Peter Pan and Pan, weren’t we? And how much you both loved the Tinkerbell films? I liked the one where she saved the lost boys! You did! That was a very brave thing for Tinkerbell to do. And it made me think, that feeling of believing in something magical, something that helps people… That’s a really important feeling, isn’t it? It encourages us to be kind and do good things. Like donating? Exactly! Like donating to Great Ormond Street. So, what scene from the Peter Pan films is your favourite? When Peter Pan fights Captain Hook! He’s got a sword! A very impressive sword! And what about you, darling? Your favourite part? When Tinkerbell shines! And all the fairies fly! It’s so pretty! It  is  beautiful. And you know what? Thinking about all that sparkly magic is a good reminder to be kind, like Tinkerbell. Shall we watch one of the films again tonight? Yes! Please! With popcorn? Of course! Popcorn and a magical film. Perfect. Now, who wants to help me look for something sparkly to donate? Both of you? Me! Me! It has to be pink! Like Tinkerbell! And it needs to be big! So it can make lots of children better! ` That’s a very thoughtful idea, sweetheart.

Right, well, that’s us then. Another airport drop-off done. Feels a bit… quiet, doesn't it? Used to the chatter, the maps, the endless debate about directions. It does. Bit surreal. I feel like I should be arguing with you about whether to take the A361 or not, just for old times’ sake. Don't even start, darling. Remember that time we got completely lost trying to find that little farm shop near Bridport? Ended up on a muddy track with a herd of cows staring us down. Oh, good grief, yes! That was an adventure, wasn’t it? I'm still not sure how we managed to reverse all the way back out of there. This journey, though, relatively smooth. Considering. Relatively! You nearly missed the turning for the M5 again. I had to practically wrestle the wheel. A slight miscalculation, that's all! It’s a long drive, you know. My internal clock is still trying to adjust to this… early rising business. Hard when you're used to a leisurely start. Tell me about it! All this rushing around hasn’t done wonders for my sleep. I’ve been waking up at four for the past week, just staring at the ceiling. Teaching young people the importance of a good night's sleep when you can't even manage it yourself ironically. It's that pre-airport anxiety. You're thinking about everything that could go wrong. Flights, security, lost luggage... the whole shebang. Speaking of homes, it's amazing how many places we’ve all lived in Devon and Somerset, isn’t it? Remember that tiny cottage near Seaton? The one with the wonky floors? Oh, the Seaton cottage! We had the washing line strung between two apple trees. Was idyllic, really. And then there was that house in Taunton, with the enormous garden… didn’t need half of it. And don't forget the one near Crediton. Those views! Absolutely breathtaking. But far too isolated for my liking. I missed being closer to shops and amenities. I wonder if we’ll ever settle down properly anywhere. Feels like we're always moving, always exploring. We’re a restless bunch, aren’t we? Moving house is practically a family tradition. So, Christmas… any plans solidified yet? Not really. Just hoping we can all manage to be together. It’s been so hectic lately. Definitely need to nail down Christmas.

Dreadful work, isn’t it? All this track laying. My knees aren’t what they used to be, you know. Though I suppose none of us are as young as we were. Aye, it is a bit o’ a grind, that’s for sure. Back's playin’ up a bit myself today. Should've got a Swedish massage before I came out, should’ve. Heard good things about 'em. Loosen ya right up. Oh, Swedish massage! I've considered it. My daughter, Penelope, has been going on about them. Says it’s the only thing that eases her shoulder trouble. She's a social worker, you see, all that sitting and hunching over paperwork. Social worker, eh? Good deed, that is. My niece, Sarah, she works at the hospice down in Bristol. Now,  that’s  a proper job. Helping folk at the end. Bit heavy, mind you. Heavens, yes. My dear husband, Arthur, was… cared for… in a hospice for his final months. So, so important to have good nurses and a compassionate setting. Though, sometimes, I think they’re too quick with the… well, you know. Making it all rather tidy, rather swift. Proper grieving needs time, doesn't it? Aye, it does. Need a good weep, don't we? My wife, Doreen, she… well, it was a shock when she went. Sudden like. Never really got over it, to be honest. Still keep her photo on the mantelpiece. I understand entirely. It’s a rather selfish thing, isn’t it, how much we cling to those photographs and reminders? Penelope’s got a little boy, Thomas - he's just started nursery. Absolutely adorable, but all that early education… I worry, sometimes. Is it right to push them so hard, so young? Nursery's important, mind. Gets 'em used to being with other kids. Doreen always said a good start's half the battle. Course, back in her day… she worked in a factory, you know? Before she married me. Said women were treated no better than the machines. Not a lot of female equality back then. No, definitely not. Things have improved, of course, but there’s still a long way to go. The terminology they use, sometimes, is just dreadful. 'Caregiver' instead of 'nurse,’ for instance. It diminishes the profession. Aye, that's a poor thing to say. So, you here for the ME event next year then?

Right, so I was looking at flights again, Mum. And EasyJet have got a really good deal to Malaga for mid-September. Malaga, lovely! Haven't been there in years. Is that where you wanted to go? You were thinking somewhere sunny, weren’t you? Yeah, definitely. I'm desperate for some sunshine, and Malaga seems to have a nice mix of beaches and culture. Plus, it's straightforward to get to. EasyJet’s alright, as long as you pack light. Remember that time you went to Barcelona and had to pay for luggage? Nearly bankrupted you! Don't remind me! I’ve learned my lesson. Hand luggage only this time, promise. What about you, are you free to come? Oh, absolutely! I’ve cleared my calendar. It would be wonderful to get away for a week. When were you thinking of going, exactly? I was looking at flying out on the 15th and coming back on the 22nd. That gives us a full seven days. Sounds perfect. And what about accommodation? Have you booked anything yet? Not yet. I was thinking maybe an Airbnb? Somewhere with a little kitchen so we can do some of our own cooking. It’s always cheaper, isn’t it? It can be, yes. Just be careful and read the reviews thoroughly. You don’t want to end up with a dodgy landlord. Good point. I’ve been checking Booking.com as well, just to compare prices. There's a really cute little apartment near the beach that got great reviews. It’s a bit more than the Airbnb, but it has a pool. A pool? That does sound tempting! Especially in September, when it might still be quite warm. Exactly! I was thinking we could spend a few days just lounging by the pool, then maybe do some exploring. I saw there’s a lovely old Moorish castle just outside of Malaga. Oh, that sounds wonderful! I've always wanted to see one of those. And the food in Spain...oh my! I know! Tapas, paella...I'm already drooling! I was also looking at some day trips. Ronda is supposed to be amazing. Have you ever been? Ronda? No, I haven’t. But it sounds like a good idea. High on a cliff, isn't it? Very picturesque. Yes! And they have a famous bridge. I think we should definitely try to fit it in.

Right, so, my bank statement just came through. Seems like I ordered that new kit for Uni – the coding one. Bit pricey, but should make things easier, yeah? Coding kit, eh? Good investment. You on a tight budget, son. Don't be worrying about it. Anything else popping up? Just the usual, really. Groceries, petrol. Oh, and that ridiculous subscription to "Retro Gaming Monthly." Mum’s going to kill me when she sees that. Retro gaming, you say? You still stuck on those old consoles? You know, back in Barbados, we didn't have anything like that. We played football in the street until the streetlights came on. That was our entertainment. Yeah, I know, Dad. It’s just… I like the nostalgia. And the retro games are often technically more interesting than the modern ones, you know? Like, the limitations force the programmers to be so clever. Cleverness is cleverness, wherever it’s found. Speaking of cleverness, how’s work going? Still managing all those… what do you call them? Digital marketing things? Yeah, it’s alright. Busy, as always. They’ve got me working on a new campaign for a sportswear company. Pretty standard stuff, targeting young athletes. Lots of Instagram influencers, you know the drill. Influencers… hmm. Seems like a strange way to sell things. Back in my day, you’d just have a picture of the product and clever description. Simple. It’s different now, Dad. People trust recommendations from people they perceive as relatable. It’s all about authenticity, even if it’s manufactured. Manufactured authenticity… that's a new one. Heard about that footballer, Rashford, used to play for Man U? Yeah, what about him? Apparently, he's started a foundation to help children with food and housing. That's what I call real influence. Not these youngsters on Instagram showing off fancy trainers. Fair point. He’s doing good work. Have you heard anything from Auntie Marlene lately? I texted her last week, but haven’t had a reply. She's been a bit under the weather, I think. Your cousin, Marcus – he was saying she's had trouble with her knee again. She's fussing over it, as usual. Says she might need another operation. Oh, that’s a shame. I’ll give her a call then. Maybe offer to pop over and help with the groceries or something. She’d appreciate that.

You know, I was trying to Skype with young Emily earlier, but the connection was dreadful. Kept cutting out. Oh dear, that’s frustrating. Poor girl. Is she alright? She’s fine, just busy with her studies, you know. Says they’re doing a project on the world, all the different countries. Showed me a picture of a globe she’d made. A globe, eh? That's good. Reminds you of when I had to do that sort of thing. Though we used those awful inflatable ones, didn’t we? Burst one halfway through. Inflatable! Fancy that. I remember when a proper globe was a real luxury. Cost a fortune. Used to be able to get them cheap at Woolworths, back in the day. Shame that’s gone. Remember those holidays we had, Peter? Always wanted to see the world. Yorkshire… that was lovely, wasn’t it? The Dales, you could just wander for hours. Should’ve gone to that youth hostel, like we planned. Proper walking country up there. I took my class on a field trip to the Peak District once. Some of them were moaning about the hills, but they loved exploring the caves and learning about the rocks. Children today, eh? Everything has to be handed to them on a plate. Remember when we used to hop on the underground, no complaints, just getting about. Oh, the tube. Got so busy these days, packed like sardines. I don't think I could manage it now. Not with this blasted leg. Doc says it’s arthritis. Sorry to hear that, Peter. Does it hinder you much? It's a bother, yes. Makes gardening a right chore. Used to love pottering about, growing tomatoes, roses… You had a beautiful garden, Peter. Such lovely colours. I always admired your roses. Thank you, Maureen. It’s not what it was, though. Can't bend down as easy as I used to. You should get one of those raised beds, Peter. Easier on the back and the knees. Aye, that’s a thought. So, Maureen, how are things with your daughter? Has she settled in alright with the new fella? Oh, it's complicated. They get on well enough, but you know how it is. Relationships... they're tricky things. She's quite happy, I think. They always seem tricky, don't they? Glad to hear your daughter's generally happy though.

Right, so EasyJet’s showing up as the cheapest to get us back to Leeds for the weekend. What do you reckon, Liv? About £70 each return. Could be worse. Seventy quid, huh? Bit steep, isn't it? I was hoping for under sixty. But honestly, after this week, anything to get me out of Cambridge sounds good. Tell me about it. This conference was relentless. Seriously, three days non-stop of powerpoints and networking. I’m knackered. Did you manage to actually get any work done this week, then? Not really. Been firefighting, mostly. Supply chain issues all over the place. Honestly, it’s like trying to herd cats. Keeps me busy, though. At least I'm not stuck staring at pie charts like you. Pie charts are my nemesis. Though, to be fair, at least I got to sample the catering. This pasta’s alright, innit? Your mum’s cooking is always banging. Glad you like it! She went a bit mad with the garlic, though, didn’t she? Hope we don’t smell too much when we get on the plane. I’ll bring some breath mints then. Listen, so flights are booked, then? Should I just do it now and sort the payment? Yeah, go for it. My card’s playing up again. It's a right pain. Honestly, everything’s a drama with my finances. Don't remind me. Don't worry about it. I’ll sort it. Are you watching that new documentary on Netflix? The one about space exploration? Oh, is that the one everyone’s been raving about? No, I haven’t had a chance. Been buried under paperwork all week. We should watch it tomorrow night. Definitely. I watched the first two episodes. It’s proper mind-blowing. Makes you feel pretty insignificant, doesn't it? Everything does these days, really. Especially when you're dealing with container ships stuck in the Suez Canal. Honestly, it's enough to make you want to move to a desert island. You and me both. Speaking of islands, Mum sent me a picture of the beach in Margate. Proper grey and drizzly, as always. Typical. Never sunshine in Margate. Still, at least you’ve got the sea air. Yeah, but I'd swap it for a bit of Yorkshire sunshine any day. Right, payment’s sorted. You’re in. Flights booked. Now, should we put on something a bit less intense than documentaries and just... chill?

Right then, let’s have a look at these statements. Seems a bit steep, doesn't it? Especially this electricity bill. It is a bit much, Dad. Everything’s gone up, hasn’t it? Even the pasta at Sainsbury’s. I noticed that last week. Tell me about it! I went to Aldi, trying to save a few bob, but even their prices are creeping up. Remember when you could get a whole bag of potatoes for a pound? Don’t I. Back in my day… Anyway, never mind. I’m just trying to keep on top of things. This banking app is a nightmare. Keeps asking for two-factor authentication. Oh, I know! It’s so annoying. They want to make it as difficult as possible, don't they? It's like they're actively trying to confuse older people. It's a scam, that’s what it is. Trying to get at your money. Should just stick to writing cheques, really. I tried sticking to cheques once. Nearly had my arm broken by the postman for overload! He said he'd never seen so many cheques in his life. Oh, Dad! He probably just needed a holiday. Still, you’ve got to be careful. Heard on the news last night about that phishing scam, very clever. They were pretending to be from the police. The police! What for? They were trying to get people’s bank details, pretending there was fraudulent activity on their accounts. Terrible. They're getting more sophisticated, aren’t they. My neighbour nearly fell for it. Luckily, her daughter warned her. The justice system needs to get a grip on these chaps. Absolutely. It's a disgrace. The police are stretched thin anyway, chasing after wildlife disturbances and lost cats. Seems like that’s all they do these days. Well, they have got to do  something , Dad. Remember that fox that was causing havoc last spring? Oh, yes! Eating all the bins over. We had to call the council. Eventually someone came, but it took weeks. Council. Don't get me started on the council. Can’t complain about anything without getting the runaround. It’s just… frustrating. I know. I had a nightmare trying to sort out my mobile phone recently. Changing providers. Absolute nightmare. The customer service was appalling. Oh, you’re lucky if you get anyone who understands you! Last time I called, the woman kept repeating the same thing, over and over.

Right, so we’re doing favourite things, yeah? This is gonna be good. First one - favourite animal. Mine’s gotta be a penguin. They’re just so wobbly and proper little chaps. Penguins are brilliant! Mine's a Golden Retriever. So much fluff, and they’re always smiling. Proper happy dogs. You know, like, endlessly optimistic. Ah, a Golden Retriever is a good choice. Mine has to be a red panda. They’re like little foxes, but softer and…redder. And they eat bamboo! It’s very aesthetically pleasing. Red pandas are lovely. I've always loved a cat, though. Specifically a big, fluffy Maine Coon. They look like little lions, don’t they? So dignified. Ooh, lions! I like cats too, but I’m a sucker for a husky. Big, blue eyes, can pull a sled, y’know? Proper hardy. Alright, alright, good animal choices! Okay, next up: favourite food. This is important. So many contenders. But I think it has to be a really good Sunday roast. All the trimmings, crispy Yorkshire puddings… it’s just comfort food, innit? Definitely comfort food. For me, it's my Granny's potato farls. Fresh out of the pan, with a bit of butter… pure heaven. My grandma makes the best bara brith. Raisin bread, soaked in tea, the perfect sweetness. It's like a hug in a loaf. Ooh, bara brith sounds good. Mine is plain: chips! Proper, thick-cut chips, with loads of salt and vinegar. Can’t beat ‘em. Chips? Seriously? You’re missing out on so much! My favourite has to be a good poke bowl. Loads of vibrant bits and bobs, fresh fish… feels really healthy, even though it probably isn’t. Poke bowls are good, yeah. Bit pricey though, aren't they? Aye, they are a bit of a treat. Farles are much more economical! My mum makes a fantastic welsh rarebit. Melted cheese on toast - simple but beautiful! You guys are all fancy with your food choices! I’m sticking with chips. Simple pleasures, eh? What's your favourite holiday destination? Oh, holiday! I’ve always wanted to go to South Korea. The culture seems so interesting, and the food… street food, ramyeon… South Korea! Wow, ambitious! I’d love to go to Greece. Sunshine, beaches, history… Greece is lovely. I’d pick Ireland, though. Back to where I come from! Just wander around the countryside, listen to the music… Home for me too!

Honestly, thinking about being, like, really old is terrifying. Like, what if I end up in one of those places where they just… watch daytime telly all day? You'd probably be running the art club in there, teaching everyone how to make willow sculptures. You know, Southwest Cornwall artisan vibes. Ugh, no. No willow sculptures. Maybe painting landscapes. But definitely no daytime TV. Although, Strictly does look pretty good sometimes… See? You'd adapt. Everyone does. Though I’m terrified of forgetting things. Like, forgetting what my grandkids look like. That’s the worst, isn't it? I think that’s why I like looking at old photos. Kind of a… a preventative measure. Reminds me that people change, but memories are still there. Makes sense. Have you started that essay on Hockney yet? The one that's due like, next week? Don't even. I've stared at it for three hours. Three hours of just blinking at a computer screen. I’m pretty sure Hockney is judging my lack of progress. He probably is. Seriously though, is there anything specific you’re struggling with? Maybe bouncing ideas off someone would help? It's just... he's so prolific. And his style has changed so much. Where do I even  begin  to wrap my head around it all? It's overwhelming. Break it down. Pick one period, one piece, and just really analyse  that . Then build outwards. Don't try to conquer the whole Hockney universe in one go. Right. Logical. You’re like my essay-writing Yoda. I try. What about you? How’s that Chaucer paper going? You seemed proper stressed about it last week. It’s…existing. I’ve got a decent thesis, I think, but finding the quotes… it's like searching for buried treasure in a medieval manuscript. Just keep at it. And maybe have some chocolate. Comfort eating is a valid research strategy. Absolutely. Speaking of comfort… want to play some Animal Crossing later? I just got a new update and need to spend hours organising my villagers' houses. Actually, yes! I’ve been needing an excuse to escape reality for a bit. I need to catch Isabelle up with all the latest fashion trends. She’s been wearing the same floral dress for  weeks . Cruel! Total fashion faux pas. You know, maybe old age won’t be so bad after all. If I can still play Animal Crossing and design interiors.

Honestly, I’m starving. This day has been brutal. Mr. Henderson kept asking for updates every ten minutes. Ten! Sounds like a Henderson day, then. You know, you could just tell him you'll email him at 5, and then ignore him until 5. I tried that. He followed me to the printer. Literally. Just stood there, staring. Oh my god. You're kidding. Did he say anything? Just… stared. It was intensely unsettling. Anyway, pasta’s the plan? I grabbed that pesto from the supermarket. Perfect. I’m making a quick tomato sauce to go alongside. Balancing flavours, you know? Always the chef. Did you hear back from Liam? About Saturday? Not yet. He said he was going to check with Ben. You know how it is. He always needs Ben's approval for everything. It’s ridiculous. They’ve been friends since they were five. Why does Ben need to sign off on weekend plans? I know! It's so… codependent. I’m starting to think he’s deliberately dragging his feet. Why would he be? Is he still seeing Chloe? I don’t know. He’s being incredibly vague. He just says he’s “busy.” And then posts pictures on Instagram of him and Ben playing pool. Suspicious. Trust your gut. It’s usually right. Remember when you thought Sarah was lying about her dog being sick? Don’t remind me! Poor Winston had a fabulous weekend at the groomers while I was panicking about vet bills. Exactly! So, Liam. He's either got a secret girlfriend, or he’s afraid of commitment. Either way, not a good sign. You’re probably right. I’m just… I like him, you know? We’ve been getting along really well lately. I know you do. And you deserve someone who can make up their mind about a Saturday night. Are you still cycling to work every day? You looked exhausted the other day. Yeah, still cycling. It's cheaper than the train, and I need the exercise. But I’m definitely getting fitter. I can almost reach the top of Primrose Hill without stopping now. That’s progress! I should probably dust off my bike. I'm turning into a potato. I can't move after sitting at a desk all day. You should! We could go for a ride next weekend. Once Liam’s sorted himself out, obviously. Sounds good.

Right then, let’s run through this speaker consent form again just to be absolutely sure we're all covered. It’s a new thing the uni’s brought in, apparently after that incident with the student recordings last year. Seems a bit heavy-handed, doesn’t it? A bit, yes. But needs must, I suppose. We don't want any trouble. Have you signed yours, Margaret? Of course. All done. And you, Eleanor? Aye, signed and sealed. Can’t be too careful. Though I still think it’s a bit daft, expecting attendees to read through the small print about GDPR and data protection. Most of them won’t. True. But at least we’re ticking the boxes. Now, let's move on to the seminar itself. I’ve had a look at the outline, and I think the flow is generally good. But I'm a little concerned about the section on Hofstede's Cultural Dimensions. It feels a bit…dry. I agree. It’s a foundational element, definitely, but we need to make it engaging. Perhaps we could interweave some real-world case studies? Something to illustrate the practical implications? I think that’s a brilliant idea, Caroline. I’ve got a good one from my time working with a Japanese trading company. They had a huge misunderstanding over email communication, entirely due to differing levels of directness. Oh, that's perfect, Eleanor! We absolutely need that. It’s vital to ground everything in examples. I think we should split the presentation; you could handle the cultural dimensions, Eleanor, then I could follow with the negotiation strategies, and Caroline can wrap up with the non-verbal communication aspect. Sound fair? That works for me. You're strongest on negotiation, Margaret, and Eleanor’s expertise on cultural theory is undeniable. I’m happy with that. So, Hofstede, then negotiation, then non-verbal… What about the time allocation per section? We've got an hour and fifteen minutes, haven't we? Yes, an hour and fifteen. I was thinking twenty minutes for cultural dimensions, twenty-five for negotiation, and twenty for non-verbal, leaving fifteen for Q&A. Does that seem sensible? It does. Though we might need to be a bit ruthless with the Q&A – students sometimes go off on tangents. Aye, they do. Especially if there's a particularly keen one in the audience. I'll keep an eye on things and gently steer them back on track if necessary.

Honestly, that seminar was brutal today. I’m still trying to process half of what Zhao said. Tell me about it. I thought my brain was going to leak out of my ears. Did you manage to salvage anything from the discussion afterward? A few nuggets, yeah. But mostly it was just a lot of circular reasoning about Neo-Confucianism and the impact on urban planning. I swear, if I hear the words "harmonious society" one more time… I know the feeling. My lecture on post-colonial literature felt like a complete flop. Half the students were clearly just doodling in their notebooks. Students are always like that sometimes. It's the heat, isn't it? It saps all their energy. Anyway, speaking of energy, I’m exhausted. This walk home feels longer every day. It does. I keep thinking we need to find a closer apartment, you know? Something within walking distance of campus at least. Less opportunity for the scooter mafia to fleece us. I know, I know. But the prices… they're insane. And then finding something decent, with a bit of space… It feels impossible. Remember that tiny studio we looked at last month? Don’t remind me. It was smaller than my office, and smelled faintly of damp dumplings. No, thank you. Exactly. I was thinking maybe we should look at those new developments a bit further out, near the river? They seem to have a bit more space, and the views are supposed to be nice. The ones with the gated communities and the 24-hour security guards? The ones where they try and sell you premium purified water and exercise classes?
