Well, they do seem to offer more for the price, to be fair. And maybe a bit more peace and quiet. You’ve been complaining about the noise from the karaoke bar down the street. True. It’s just… it feels so… sterile. I’d rather have slightly dodgy plumbing and the occasional drunken singing than live in a show flat, wouldn't you? I get it. But the plumbing in this place  is  dodgy. Remember last week’s shower incident? Let's not. And the leaky roof. It's just a constant stream of little problems, isn’t it? Keeps us busy. Keeps the landlord busy, more like. He’s been promising to fix the roof for six months now. I swear, I’m going to write him a strongly worded letter.

This lentil soup is actually really good, isn't it? I was worried it'd be bland. Yeah, it is. You've outdone yourself. Seriously, I've been craving something proper like this. It's a million miles away from the microwave meals I've been living on. Well, I did make a big batch. I’m trying to be better about minimizing food waste, you know? It feels almost criminal sometimes how much we chuck away. Absolutely. Remember Grandma's house though? Not a crumb ever got wasted. Everything went into the stock pot, or got pickled, or transformed into something else. God, yes. And the sheer volume of jars in her pantry! It was like a laboratory of preserved fruits and vegetables. She'd have had a field day with all this modern obsession with "zero waste" living. She  was  zero waste. She was. Though, I remember moaning about having to peel potatoes for hours. Of course you did. You always did! We've been watching that new documentary on Netflix, haven't we? The one about industrialization and how it’s impacted… everything. 'Concrete Jungle'? Yeah, it’s pretty bleak. Makes you think about these urban farming initiatives. Imagine if every rooftop was a garden. It’s a nice thought. Although, I wonder if it’s really viable on a large scale. And even if it was, would it be sustainable? All that water… True. There are so many layers to it. Speaking of sustainability, did you see they’re considering bringing back the plastic bag charge for smaller bags. Honestly, it’s about time. People just hoard them anyway. I'm more concerned about the packaging on everything, though. It’s ridiculous. Tell me about it. It's all going to end up as microplastics eventually, isn’t it? What do you reckon about all these advancements in robotics and automation and how it will effect our jobs? It’s scary and exciting at the same time. I worry about young people, especially. We need to be better at careers advice in schools. It’s not just about telling them to go to university. It's about showing them pathways into closed industries, into engineering, things like that. Absolutely. They’re so focused on the “creative” industries, thinking they need to become influencers. It's hard to break into these more traditional fields without the right connections or experience.

Right, so the initial results from the study are… concerning, to say the least. The anxiety levels are significantly higher than projected, especially amongst the younger demographic. Higher than projected, huh? Give me the specifics. Are we talking about something directly linked to the pandemic, or is there something else bubbling under the surface? It’s a layered thing, definitely. The pandemic exacerbated pre-existing anxieties, of course – job security, future prospects… the usual suspects. But there’s also this… persistent unease about social media, about constant comparison. They feel pressured to project this perfect image, and the disconnect between that and reality is causing a lot of distress. That resonates, doesn’t it? Even I find myself scrolling mindlessly sometimes, feeling… inadequate. Though I try and keep a lid on it. Do they articulate that, explicitly? Some do. It's horrifying, actually, how commonplace it’s become to admit to feeling ‘constantly on edge’ because of Instagram. One participant said, and I quote, "It's like everyone else is living their best life except me." Awful. It's insidious, isn't it? They’re bombarded with curated perfection. Honestly, I'm glad Lily isn't really on it yet. We’re trying to hold off as long as possible. Smart move. It’s just… you can’t completely shield them, can you? The world's evolving so fast. Speaking of Lily, how was her nursery today? Did she enjoy her painting session? She did! Apparently, she painted a rather abstract representation of a dinosaur. Lots of green and purple. The teacher said it was "very expressive." I think it's just chaotic finger painting, but I played along. Of course you did. You always do. You’re brilliant at that. I wish I could be more… present, you know? This study is consuming me. I feel like I’m living on coffee and stress. Don’t say that. You’re doing important work, genuinely. But you need to carve out time for yourself too. Remember what we talked about? Mindfulness? Even just ten minutes a day can make a difference. Easier said than done when I'm staring at graphs showing escalating anxiety rates. They're reimbursing expenses for a gym membership though… That’s a start. Look, I'm making your favourite – Bolognese. You need proper sustenance to tackle those graphs. And tonight, we’re having a screen-free evening.

Just can’t seem to shake this feeling, can I? Like a lead weight in me chest. Now, now, Arthur. Don’t go on like that. We’re here, aren’t we? We’re all here. And you’ve got family. You were saying something earlier about the sea, Arthur? You seemed a bit down about that. It just…it reminds me of things, you know? Sunny days, Elsie laughing, the kids building sandcastles… simpler times. And now… the council’s trying to increase the charges for the car park down at Cromer again. Makes it impossible to get down there properly. It’s all just getting a bit much, really. They're the worst, those councils. Always wanting more. Remember when we used to go down to Southwold? Used to be proper cheap. Aye. Those were the days. Elsie loved Southwold. So many pebbles. Said they were like little worries you could pick up and throw into the sea. That’s lovely, Arthur. Really lovely. Listen, about feeling down… have you been talking to anyone? About the… well, you know. Not really. Don’t like to burden people. Nonsense! We’re your family, Arthur. That's what we're here for. Don't be silly. It's okay to need a friend to talk to, mate. There’s that volunteer group at the community centre, remember? They run a listening service. Might be worth a shot. A listening service? Sounds a bit… formal, don't you think? It doesn't have to be. It's just someone to chat with, Arthur. Someone who'll listen without judging. Exactly. And there’s this new fella started volunteering there, young chap. Called Ben. Seems alright. Apparently, he's got a bit of a thing for birds. Birds? What sort of thing? Little blue tits, apparently! He was saying someone put up a bird feeder in the park, and they were all flocking to it. Said it was brilliant. Little bit of joy in the world. Ben sounds like a lovely young man. So, you’ll think about it, Arthur? Give it a go? I don’t know. It's just...the house, too. Always worrying about the bills. Never enough coming in, you know? You know, I was thinking about that flat they’re building down on Mill Road. Small, but might be an option for you eventually? Modern, low maintenance. Less to worry about.

Honestly, I’ve been obsessed with this serum lately. You absolutely  have  to try it. Oh really? What is it? You know I’m always looking for something new. My skin's been so dull lately. It's called "Radiant Bloom" – you can get it online, or at Boots. It's a bit pricey, I won't lie, but it's worth every penny. Boots, you say? I might have to have a look. How does it work? Is it like retinol or something intense? I’m really scared of those, they always make me peel. No, it's gentler than retinol. It has hyaluronic acid, so it’s really hydrating, and some sort of Vitamin C derivative. It just… plumps everything up. Makes my skin look so dewy. Look!  Tilts her head to the side and shows her face  Wow, you do look good. Seriously! Your skin's just glowing. I’ve been trying to get into a skincare routine, but I just end up overwhelmed with all the options. I know, right? It's a minefield! Remember when we were teenagers and we all used that St. Ives scrub? Murdered our faces! Oh god, don’t remind me! My sister still uses it. I try to tell her it's awful, but she's convinced it's working wonders. Exactly! And my nails... I finally found a decent red! What are you wearing at the moment? Just a boring nude. I can’t be bothered with anything too flashy for work, you know? It’s all about efficiency at the post office. No room for glittery nails when you’re processing returns. Fair enough. Though a little sparkle never hurt anyone! Any beauty news from Chloe? Have you heard from her? She was raving about that new highlighter last time we spoke. No, not recently. She’s been really busy with the new job, I think. I keep meaning to text her, but then I get distracted by something else. It's always something. Did you go shopping this weekend then? I did! Went to Primark actually, you know how I love a good bargain. Found some amazing leggings and a really cute top. We should have gone together. Oh, that's a shame. I was thinking of popping in after work, maybe tomorrow. They had some really nice necklaces online, I was eyeing them up. I need to treat myself, honestly.

Right, so the Tate’s doing that Hockney exhibition, yeah? Worth a look? I’ve been meaning to go, but parking round there’s always a nightmare. Hockney's good, yeah. I went last month with Sarah. It’s proper rammed, mind, but the stuff's brilliant. Parking… honestly, I just got a taxi. Saved me the hassle. Worth it, I reckon. See, that's the thing, isn't it? Can’t be faffing about trying to find a space. Last time I went, I circled for twenty minutes. Ended up walking ages. You’re mental. Anyway, how's the teaching going? Still dealing with teenagers wanting to be TikTok stars? Don't even get me started. Little Liam tried to explain the rules of a dance challenge to me today. I just nodded and smiled. They're a different breed, aren’t they? What about you? Still wading through child protection cases? Yep. This week’s been… intense. Got a referral involving a seriously dodgy situation. Proper draining, it is. Makes you question everything sometimes. Proper tough. I hate that you have to deal with that. You need a holiday. Fancy going to that new place in Magaluf? Nah, I'm good. Too much hassle. Thinking about heading up to Scotland actually, sometime next year. Might even look at buying a wee place up there. Scotland! Seriously? Whereabouts? You’d be a world away from the city. Somewhere near Inverness, maybe. I’ve always fancied living somewhere a bit quieter. Less…noise. What about you? Still planning on moving? Trying to, yeah. Found a couple of places in South Liverpool, but the prices are ridiculous. Trying to save every penny I can. Which is annoying, because Christmas is looming. Don't remind me. Mum's already planning what presents she's getting everyone. The woman's obsessed. Mine too! She’s been dropping not-so-subtle hints about what I  should  get her. Expecting a designer handbag no doubt. You're kidding. You're not getting her a designer handbag! How much would that even cost? Exactly! Plus, you know, Masters fees to pay for, yeah? How’s the interview going? Actually, how many people are you interviewing against? Apparently, quite a few. They said it’s a competitive field. So, you know, pressure’s on. I’m trying not to think about it too much, just focusing on prepping what I’m going to say.

Honestly, it’s exhausting, isn’t it? Just… constantly navigating everyone’s feelings. Tell me about it. Leo's been having a proper meltdown today. Something about wanting blue crayons and only blue crayons. It’s a tiny thing, but it feels monumental at the time, you know? Absolutely. And trying to be… reasonable. Not just to him, but to Mark, who's all, "Just give him a red one and tell him it's blue!" It’s like, well, Mark, that’s not really helping, is it? Classic. It’s the well-meaning but ultimately unhelpful advice, isn't it? I get that all the time from my mum. "Just ignore it, he’ll get over it." Like ignoring a toddler tantrum somehow makes it disappear. Precisely! It's about validating their feelings, even if it’s just over a Crayola. Speaking of, Matthew’s been having his own little dramas with Chloe’s mum, Sarah. Oh, no. Not again. What’s this one about? Apparently, Sarah is convinced Matthew is deliberately trying to undermine her relationship with Chloe. Says he’s subtly suggesting Chloe needs more "stability" and “routine." Which is just... ridiculous. Matthew is the most stable person I know. Sarah is exhausting. It’s always someone else’s fault, isn't it? It’s never her having difficulty adapting. Exactly! And Chloe's caught in the middle, as usual. She just wants them all to be happy. Matthew’s trying his best to be neutral, but it’s clearly stressing him out. You know, I always worry about Matthew. He’s such a genuinely kind person, he tries so hard to please everyone, sometimes I think he forgets to look after himself. I do too. He's a pushover sometimes, bless him. I've told him to just… tell her bluntly if he’s uncomfortable. But you know how he is – he'll beat around the bush for ages before saying anything remotely direct. It’s a hard balance, isn't it? You want him to be respectful and considerate, but you don’t want him being walked all over. Totally. And then there's the whole step-parenting dynamic. It's like, how much are you supposed to get involved? Where's the line? Chloe’s mum seems to think Matthew should be taking on more responsibility for Chloe, like he’s her dad. Oh, that’s rough.

Right, so Liam sent me his Pinterest board for his birthday. It’s…intense. Intense how? Full-on woodland creatures and artisanal beard oil again? Worse, actually. It's a meticulously curated collection of vintage campervans and mid-century modern furniture. Like, he’s planning an entire aesthetic getaway. Sounds intensely Liam. Did he actually  get  you anything though? He did! Which is lovely, but added to the Pinterest madness. He got me that ridiculous constellation projector I mentioned. The one that makes the stars on your ceiling. The one you said looked like a Christmas decoration? Exactly! But it is quite nice, actually. Makes the bedroom feel a bit…cosy. Less like a research manager’s cave. So, are you regretting that horrifying documentary we watched last night now? About competitive cheese rolling? Don’t remind me! Honestly, who gets that excited about a wheel of cheese hurtling down a hill? My poor mum would have a heart attack. Speaking of mum, did she manage to book that table at the Italian she wanted for her birthday? Yeah, she did. Friday night. She’s already planning the outfit, apparently. Something with sequins. Of course she is. It's a birthday, it wouldn’t be a birthday without sequins. Did you hear from Chloe and Mark? Are they sticking around for the weekend? They're definitely here. They were saying they’re going to check out that new exhibit at the Fitzwilliam tomorrow. Apparently, it’s got some seriously impressive Byzantine mosaics. Oh, fancy! Always loved Byzantine stuff. Their taste is impeccable, isn't it? Sometimes I feel a bit…ordinary in comparison. All my Pins are just cat photos and recipes for sourdough. Ordinary? You just published a paper that's going to shake up the whole field of urban planning! Don’t sell yourself short. You always know what to say. Still, I feel like I should be curating a mood board of Tuscan villas and handmade ceramics. Stick to the cats and sourdough. It’s more authentic. Besides, someone has to keep things grounded while Liam’s plotting his van-life empire. True. Speaking of empires, did you manage to finish that chapter on 18th-century agricultural practices? It sounded brutal.  Brutal  is an understatement. Seriously, the amount of human misery involved in farming turnips is…a lot. It’s giving me nightmares. Oh dear. You need a pint.

Right, so this one's got a good review rate. Seven hundred and eighty-five people have bought it, and it's got 4.8 stars. Feels a bit… matchy-matchy though, doesn’t it? A bit, yeah. Too much brushed brass. Remember what you said about the kitchen needing a bit of… edge? Exactly. We don’t want it to feel like a hotel lobby. Okay, let’s filter by ‘black’ then. And… matte black. Don’t want anything too shiny. Good thinking. Let’s see… that’s promising. Industrial style, says. £45. And the dimensions are good. Not too enormous. Right, put that in the ‘favourites’ folder, just in case. Okay, house hunting now. I found three new ones in the catchment area for the school. Oh really? Let's have a look. Where are they located? Two are just off Elm Road, a bit further out than we ideally wanted, but they’re bigger gardens. And one's on Primrose Avenue - remember we said we liked that street? Primrose Avenue is lovely. Let's start with that one. Click, click... Oh, that’s… surprisingly small. Yeah, the photos are slightly misleading. Look at that kitchen though. It's been completely renovated. It has, hasn't it? But the lounge… it’s tiny. And the garden is practically non-existent. £380,000, though. That's a bit more reasonable than some of the others we’ve looked at. True. And remember, we’re not looking for a  forever  home, just somewhere decent for the kids to finish school. Don’t want anything too ambitious. Right. Okay, let's look at the one off Elm Road now. This one looks… promising. Four bedrooms. Pretty decent sized garden. Blimey. The kitchen's enormous. Though it looks like it needs updating. And the bathrooms… oh dear. Yeah, the decor’s a bit… dated. But you could definitely do something with it. That’s a big plus. How much is that one? £450,000. Bit steep, but the garden is a real selling point. Plus, the school's practically on the doorstep. Let's check the train links. And… not great, actually. It’s a twenty-minute walk to the station. Okay, that's something to consider. Right, last one. This is the one that's been on the market the longest, apparently. Always a warning sign. Let's see... Oh. This is... rather unusual.

Honestly, the shift rotas at the ward are getting ridiculous. I swear they’re deliberately trying to break us. Tell me about it! It’s been like that everywhere, hasn’t it? Even at Willowbrook, things are stretched thin. Where’s Amy today? Is she in? Hey everyone! Sorry I’m late, Pip decided he needed a ‘very important’ sniff of every single bush on the way here. This little guy rules the roost, you know. Pip’s always been a character. Good to see you, love. How are things going at the agency? Still hopping from place to place? Yeah, still. It's alright, you know? Keeps me busy. Had a lovely lady in Sevenoaks this week, really sweet. Though, the husband was a bit... intense about the biscuit crumbs. Men and crumbs! It's a universal thing. You’d think they'd have bigger things to worry about. I had a client last week, bless him, thought I was a housekeeper as well as a carer. Kept asking me to polish his silver! Oh, goodness. You’ve got to love them, though, haven't you? They appreciate the little things. Speaking of appreciating, I need to tell you both, I think I'm finally going to put my foot down with Mr. Henderson. Mr. Henderson? What’s he done now? Well, he keeps complaining about the temperature of his tea. I’ve told him a hundred times I’ve got it exactly right. And then he insists I reheat it, even though it’s stone cold by the time I get back to him. Oh, bless him! Some people just like to have a moan, don't they? Exactly! So, I’m having a little chat with his daughter. Gently, of course, but I need to make it clear I can’t be constantly running back and forth with a cup of tea. Good for you! Assertiveness is a lost art these days. Remember when I applied for that senior care assistant role at St. Jude’s? Oh yeah! The one you were so excited about? I was! But they offered it to Sarah from down the road. Apparently, she has ‘more experience with complex needs.’ Honestly, I've dealt with more complex needs than Sarah’s ever seen! It’s infuriating, isn't it? They always seem to find something. You’re brilliant, Sarah’s perfectly capable… It’s just who they like.

You know, I was reading this fascinating article this morning about sleep. Apparently, consistent exposure to blue light – phones, laptops, the whole shebang – is far more disruptive than we thought. They’re saying even dim exposure right before bed messes with melatonin production. Tell me something I don't know. I feel like I've been battling that for years. My students are glued to their screens until the last possible minute. It’s a wonder any of them function. Exactly. The research suggested a specific type of amber light filter is surprisingly effective. Apparently, it’s not just about reducing the brightness, it’s about shifting the spectrum away from the blue wavelengths. Might have to invest in some glasses. Good idea. We should definitely look into those. Thinking about sleep… remember that disastrous camping trip we took last summer in the Lake District? How could I forget? Torrential rain, soggy tents, and you insisting on navigating with that horrifyingly inaccurate map. Hey, it  looked  like a good route! I thought I had us heading toward Grasmere, but we ended up completely lost somewhere near Keswick. Seriously, the sheep were giving us pitying looks. Pitying looks from sheep! That’s a new one. We were driving around in circles for hours. I think I aged about ten years. At least the view was pretty. When it wasn't obscured by rain, that is. It’s funny, isn’t it? You can be utterly hopeless in your own city, but the moment you step outside your postcode, you’re completely directionally challenged. I still have no idea how to get into Bristol without ending up on some ridiculously narrow country lane. Agreed. I'm hopeless navigating big cities. I rely entirely on those map apps. Speaking of navigation, I was listening to a podcast about pilots the other day. Apparently, there’s this pilot, Captain Davies, who is just… remarkable. Oh really? What makes him so remarkable? His spatial awareness is apparently off the charts. They were explaining how he can factor in wind speed, air pressure, even subtle shifts in the aircraft's balance, almost instinctively. He practically anticipates turbulence before it arrives. It’s not just about skill, it's something... innate. That  is  fascinating. It’s like he’s got a three-dimensional map permanently etched in his brain. Makes you realise how much we take for granted.

Right, so, picture this. Pip – my hamster – he's gone completely mental. Oh no! What’s he been up to? Did he escape again? Nah, not escaped. He’s… redecorating. Apparently. He’s dragging bedding everywhere and piling it up into these massive little towers. It looks like a miniature construction site in his cage. Aye, hamsters are right wee characters, aren’t they? My gran had a hamster once, called Winston. He used to hoard sunflower seeds under his bedding and then forget where he put them. Proper comedian, Winston, sounds like. Pip’s just showing off then, is he? Building a tiny empire. Exactly! And he’s got this one sunflower seed, like, his prized possession. He just sits with it, rotating it, sniffing it… It’s hilarious. Sounds like he needs a bigger cage. Or maybe he’s just bored? I thought of that. I’m thinking about getting him one of those little hamster wheels with tunnels and stuff. They love those. My grandmam’s hamster went mental for a cardboard tube one. Just zoomed round and round all day. Does that mean you’re turning into a hamster expert then, Clare? I suppose I am, a little bit! What about you lot? Anything exciting happening? Well, I was thinking about going to that new vintage market in town next weekend. Fancy coming? Ooh, yeah! I'm in. Anything retro is proper good. I’m always up for a market. Especially if there's a decent coffee shop nearby. Definitely. And we need to talk about this ginger guy… Oh, tell me everything! Is he… cute? He’s… interesting. Let's just say he has a very specific opinion on marmalade. A very specific opinion on marmalade? What's wrong with marmalade? Oh, this is gonna be good! Spill the tea, Clare. What did his opinion involve? Honestly, you wouldn't believe it. He said… he said Seville oranges are  overrated . The audacity! He’s kidding, right? That's a crime against breakfast, that is! I’m siding with you on this one, Clare. Dump him. I'm tempted! But he did have a very nice laugh. So… we’ll see. Marmalade aside, you girls up to anything else today? I'm thinking we could hit the shops later. Sounds like a plan! Let’s grab some lunch first. My treat. Alright, let's go then!

Right, so I’m declaring Australia. Officially. You’re not getting it, Dad. It's strategically vital. Strategically vital? It's a bloody desert with a few kangaroos, son. You’re being far too serious about this. Remember, it’s just a game. He gets far too serious about  everything , doesn't he, darling? Remember that time he tried to negotiate the price of a box of chocolates at the petrol station? They were outrageously overpriced! It’s about principle, Mum. Besides, Australia’s got resources. And South America’s looking a bit shaky for you tonight, David. Shaky? I’ve got Brazil and Argentina! You’re the one who spread your forces too thin across Africa. Honestly, you look like you’re trying to conquer the whole world single-handedly. Well, someone has to have ambition! And I’m fairly certain I remembered to reinforce North Africa this turn. Oh, is that your Turkish Delight, David? You know, I always found that smell calming. Bit like Christmas, really. Remember those Orange Slice chocolates we used to have? Yes, and you’d always steal the ones with the most orange peel. Trying to use your skills, were you? Honestly, you'd have been a formidable negotiator on the world stage. Speaking of skills, you're letting me take Asia, aren’t you? It’s practically yours for the taking. Because I'm feeling generous, yes. Don't think I’m letting you off lightly. You’ll pay for this. Oh look, there's a map on the table. Right next to the Risk board. Irony, isn't it? It’s called strategic planning, Mum. Now, let's see… I need to reinforce Indonesia. But I'm worried about a Russian push. You and Aaron need to watch out. Aaron's off playing video games, as usual. Never had a head for strategy, that boy. Softened by all those computer systems. No hardship. no grit. Back in my day... Dad, please. Not the “back in my day” speech again. We’re playing Risk, not reliving your youth. He just worries, love. He's been thinking about Aaron's future a lot lately. Concerned about the world he’s growing up in. All these updates to everything constantly, it's tiring to keep up with, isn’t it? And the child policies. Shocking really, in some countries. Don’t even go there, Margaret.

Ugh, I just... I don't know, Liv. I'm having a proper moment. A moment? What kind of moment? You look like you’re about to cry into that bracelet. I am, a little bit. Uni’s just… harder than I thought it would be. Everyone else seems to have it figured out – their course, their career, their whole lives mapped out. I just feel… lost. Lost like, “what am I doing with my life” lost, or "this essay is going to be the death of me" lost? Both, actually. The History module is brutal. And I keep thinking, am I even doing the right thing? Like, should I have gone to art college? Should I be making pottery instead of writing essays about the Tudors? You and your pottery. You'd probably end up making novelty Tudor-themed mugs. Maybe! But seriously, I’m worried I’ve made a mistake. What if I’m not cut out for this? Listen, everyone feels that sometimes, yeah? Honestly. Even me, and I’m basically Miss Organized. But everyone has days where they question everything. You’re brilliant, Stell. You’re amazing at art, and you’re really good at history, even if you hate it right now. Don't let a bad essay derail you. Easy for you to say, you’re practically a genius at Law. You were basically born knowing the legal system. Don’t exaggerate. It's just... I  like  it. You’ve got a passion for art. Remember that exhibition you did back home? It was incredible. Yeah, but that was just… fun. This is supposed to be my  future . It doesn’t have to be locked down forever! You can change your mind. You can do a different major next year. Plenty of people do. And you’re only first year. True. Speaking of futures... did you see what happened with Harry Styles? Honestly? No! Spill. He's got a baby! Rumour has it anyway. Apparently, it’s with a supermodel. No way! A baby?! Harry Styles? That's wild. Imagine a miniature Harry running around. Tiny velvet suits everywhere. Exactly! And it makes me feel even more confused. Like, everyone’s achieving grand things with their lives – babies, careers, famous boyfriends. And I’m here stressing about a footnote. Right, okay, let’s reel it in. Harry Styles is an outlier, not the norm. And you’re doing great.

So, Mr. Harrison’s really pushing this project, isn’t he? Like, ten percent of our grade. Ten percent! Tell me about it. I’m still trying to figure out what my angle even  is . He said we need to look at a social issue and… how do you even pick one? Right? There are so many. I was thinking maybe something about the cost of living crisis. It’s everywhere, you know? Gas prices, food… my mum’s been stressed about bills something awful. Yeah, that's massive. But everyone will do that, won’t they? It'll be like, fifty essays all saying the same thing. True. What about… I don't know... the impact of social media on mental health? That feels a bit done, too. Yeah. It's just... everything feels done. It's like, what hasn’t been analysed to death? Remember when Mrs. Davies made us do that project about the impact of fast fashion? Ugh, that was boring. Totally. But it's interesting, though, isn't it? How much we consume. I was reading this article about how we’re already using way more resources than the planet can actually provide. Crazy stuff. My dad was ranting about that the other day, actually. He's been watching a lot of these documentaries on YouTube about the climate. Says we're all doomed. Classic dad. My dad just complains about politicians, mostly. He was going on yesterday about Starmer and how he "has no backbone." It’s exhausting. Politics is a mess, isn't it? It's hard to even know who to trust. My mum's always saying, "They're all the same." She's probably right. Sometimes I think it would be easier if everyone just…stopped trying. What are you reading at the moment? Anything good? Just finished ‘Saga’ number forty-two. Seriously, it’s blowing my mind. The scope of that story is insane. Everything's interwoven somehow. It makes you think about… well, about everything, really. 'Saga's' mental. My brother’s into that. He’s obsessed. I’m more of a ‘Batman’ guy, y’know? Classic. Fair enough. Batman’s alright. I just think 'Saga’ gets deeper, you know? Like, it kind of examines how poverty shapes people, how it makes them desperate... See that? That shop's been boarded up forever. Used to be a proper bakery. Yeah. It’s just sad, isn’t it?

Honestly, darling, the recording was absolute chaos. I thought I was going to lose my mind. Recording what? Your new course? Yes! The online one on Elizabethan literature. I’m so pleased with the content, but the technical aspects… they were a nightmare. Mic kept cutting out, the lighting was all wonky… and my cat, Beatrice, decided it was the perfect time for a nap  on  the keyboard. Oh no! Poor you. It sounds stressful. It was. But I got there in the end. It's finished now, proofed, and uploaded. I’m absolutely exhausted, but relieved. How are things with you? Anything exciting happening? Not much, really. Still… job hunting, you know. It's… disheartening. I know, sweetie. It’s a tough market. But you have so much to offer. Have you looked at those voluntary roles at the library again? I know you love books. I did, but they said they’re not taking on any new volunteers at the moment. That’s a shame. Well, don't give up. You'll find something. Speaking of things that are tough, my poor shoulders are playing up again. Had to cancel my Pilates class. Oh, no! Your physiotherapy isn’t helping? It’s a little, but it’s those wretched joints. They just ache constantly, especially with the damp weather we've been having. Mrs. Henderson next door keeps offering me cod liver oil. Says it did wonders for her arthritis. Oh, she’s a character. She is! Absolute character. Keeps an eye on the place, though. Actually, she told me she saw a delivery van parked outside yesterday, looking suspicious. Thought they might be burglars. Oh, that’s worrying. Did she call the police? No, just started shouting at them from her window! Apparently, it was just the new neighbours moving in. They’re a young couple with a rather large dog. A Great Dane, I think. A Great Dane! Wow. They'll take up a lot of space. They will. I hope they're house-trained. Anyway, back to miserable topics... I’ve put on another stone, I think. This winter has been brutal for my willpower. All I want to do is eat comfort food. I know exactly how you feel. It’s so hard to resist things. I’ve been trying to cut back on biscuits. It's an epic battle. Biscuits are the devil’s work!

Right, I think the pasta's nearly al dente. Just a minute more. Smells alright though, doesn’t it? It does! Honestly, you’ve outdone yourself. Much better than that curry you tried to make last time. Remember that? The one that tasted like sadness? Don't remind me! I thought I’d be a culinary genius. Turns out I’m better at organising events than recreating Indian cuisine. This pesto’s banging though, isn't it? Seriously amazing. Did you make it from scratch? Yep! Got some lovely basil from that farmers’ market in town the other day. It makes all the difference, doesn't it? Fresh basil is a game-changer. It absolutely is. So, what are we watching tonight? You promised me a ridiculous rom-com. Right! I've got "27 Dresses" queued up. Prepare for maximum cheesiness. It's just the thing after a long week of dealing with demanding speakers and dodgy AV equipment. Perfect. Anything exciting happening at work at the moment? Besides the usual chaos, I mean. Not really. We've got a big pharmaceutical conference coming up next month, which means months of stress and spreadsheets. But it’s a good one, so should be worth it. How's the production side of things? Still keeping the factory running smoothly? It’s…fine. It's always a juggling act, isn’t it? Suppliers having issues, machines breaking down, someone forgetting to order the right component… the list is endless. And my boss is breathing down my neck about efficiency targets. Ugh, sounds intense. At least you're good at it, right? You're a production wizard. I try! It’s just... sometimes I wonder if it’s all worth it. All the late nights and the stress. You know? I do. But you’re really good at what you do. And the money's not bad, is it? You’re saving up for that trip to Japan, aren't you? I am! That’s keeping me motivated. Cherry blossoms and ramen... it's the dream. You should come with! Oh, I wish! But I'd be too busy organising someone else’s wedding or corporate away day. Maybe someday. Right, pasta's ready! Let's dig in. Then, ridiculous rom-com time! Deal! Oh, one more thing - did you ever hear back from that pottery class you were looking at? I did! It starts next Tuesday.

Okay, so we’re actually agreeing on something for once! “Everything Everywhere All at Once” – brilliant, right? Seriously! It was mental, but in the best way possible. I was stressed out for like, half the film, trying to keep up with what was happening. Aye, it was good. A wee bit confusing at first, though, to be fair. All the universes colliding and stuff. Took me a minute to get my head around it. I loved the whole multiverse concept. It made you think, you know? Like, what if you'd made different choices? Would your life be completely different? It was okay. A little bit… loud. Yeah, it  was  a lot. But the humour was amazing, especially the googly eyes bit. I nearly choked on my popcorn. Oh my god, the googly eyes! Classic. And Michelle Yeoh was incredible. Absolutely. She carried the whole thing, honestly. That scene with her and her dad… I got a bit emotional. Aye, that was a good bit. Proper tug at the heartstrings. It’s not just all hyperactive fighting, is it? Nah, there’s loads of heart in it. It's about family, and regret, and finding meaning in the chaos. Deep stuff. I liked the bit with the rocks. The talking rocks. Oh yeah! That was random! But hilarious. It makes sense in the context of the whole thing, though. Everything's connected. So, agreed. “Everything Everywhere All at Once” - 10/10. What else has anyone seen recently? Liam, you’re awfully quiet. What about you? I saw "The Banshees of Inisherin" recently. Different vibe entirely, right? Ooh, that one’s on my list! Is it good? It’s brilliant. Really well acted, beautiful scenery. A bit bleak and sad, mind, but really moving. I've heard good things! It's all everyone was talking about for ages. It’s got Colin Farrell in it, hasn’t it? He’s good in everything. I’ve been re-watching "Paddington 2." Solid choice. Can't go wrong with Paddington. You can’t! It’s the perfect comfort film. Aye, can't argue with that. Paddington's a legend. Maybe we should have a film night next week? Everyone pick a film. I’m in! We could make it a themed night, or something. Ooh, themed night sounds good! Like, 80s movies or something? Can I pick Paddington? Of course, you can pick Paddington! It’s a classic.

Honestly, Mum, Paris was  wild . I’m exhausted. Wild how? Did you get into any trouble? You know your father would have kittens. No trouble, just… a lot. We walked miles, saw so much, ate so much. My feet are screaming. And I think I’ve pulled something in my ankle. Oof, you look like you’ve been through it. Paris, eh? Sounds good. Let me guess, Claire dragged you both to every single patisserie in the city? Pretty much! She has a  serious  sweet tooth. I’m regretting the entire thing now, looking at these macarons – so many! But they were incredible, honestly. Well, you needed a holiday. You've been working like a dog with that project. Is it all sorted now then, darling? Almost. Just a few final bits to tie up. It's been such a stressful few weeks, though. The client was being a nightmare – constantly changing their minds. Story of my life. I swear, some patients think I have a magic wand and can fix everything with a smile and a cup of tea. Exactly! It’s like, "I'm a mental health nurse, not a miracle worker!" You’ll get used to it, love. It’s just part of the job. So, tell me, what else did you do? See the Eiffel Tower, I presume? Of course! Saw the Louvre, wandered along the Seine... Claire tried to convince me to climb Notre Dame, but I politely declined. With my ankle, that would have been a disaster. You’re sensible! I almost twisted my ankle yesterday just walking the dog. It’s ridiculous. I need to get it looked at. I know the feeling. Foot troubles are the worst. Did you go anywhere nice today, Jess? Just popped to the shops. Needed to stock up on essentials. And I’m making a big batch of chilli tonight. It's the only thing that’ll revive me after dealing with a particularly difficult patient today. Oh, good! I'm starving. That sounds lovely. So you walked around all day with your ankle, dear? You should have rested more. Did you remember to take your evening primrose oil? It’s really good for inflammation. Yes, Mum, I took the oil. And trying to rest when Claire was bouncing off the walls was impossible! It was like being trapped with a hyperactive puppy. Sounds about right for Claire.

Hey Chloe! Fancy seeing you here before the morning classes start. How was your weekend? Hey Mark! It was alright, pretty chilled actually. Did a bit of shopping in Brighton, nothing too exciting. What about you? Did you manage to escape Bedford? I did! Went to Chichester, actually. First time. Really beautiful, isn't it? All those Roman ruins. Oh, I've been! It’s lovely. Did you see the cathedral? It's stunning. My mum loves Chichester, we go every few months. She’s really into antiques. I didn't have time to see the cathedral, but I walked along the harbour – the weather was gorgeous, perfect for a wander. Reminded me a bit of Greece, actually – you ever been? Not yet, sadly. It’s on the list though! I’m saving up. Right now, I’m just trying to get through this shift. Being a supervisor is… demanding, let's just say. I can imagine! At least you’re moving up, though. It's good to see you aiming for something higher. Want a coffee? The cafe’s just down the hall. My treat. That would be amazing, thank you! I’m definitely in need of a caffeine boost. Trying to budget this month, though. Payday feels ages away, doesn't it? These tuition fees are a killer still, even after all these years. Tell me about it! Student loans haunt you forever. How’s your brother doing? Last I heard he was still looking for work? Yeah, he’s still struggling a bit. He’s got that creative writing thing going, though, which is nice. Keep telling him to publish something! You, as an English instructor, should be his biggest cheerleader! I try to! I keep telling my students to embrace the passives, though, and half of them just glaze over. It's a constant battle. Speaking of linguistics… Did you see that fascinating article about the Malaysian dialect the other day? Actually, no! I missed it. Was it about phonology? I did a little bit on sociolinguistics during my undergraduate degree, but I always found phonology a bit overwhelming. My sister's studying it now, though – she’s doing a Master’s at Warwick. I’ll have to send you the link. It was really interesting, how many grammatical structures are borrowed from other languages. It really puts our own erratic grammar into perspective, doesn’t it?

Right, so how much rice do I need? Like, for two people? Okay, let’s see… for you and me, a cup should be plenty. Actually, maybe a cup and a half. You like a good portion, don't you? Yeah, definitely. And what about the water? It says like, double the rice, right? Nearly. Two cups of water for every cup of rice. That’s the general rule. Though I find if your cooker's a bit ropey, you might need a  tiny  bit more. Do you remember what happened last time? Ugh, the rice-pudding incident? Don't remind me. It was like, cement. Exactly! So monitor it. Once the water’s bubbling away, put the lid on and leave it alone. Don't peek! Right. No peeking. Easy. What are we having with it? You said curry? Yeah, I made a big pot earlier. It’s got chicken, loads of veggies… I’ll check the salt levels, though. I sometimes get carried away with it. Want some jalapenos? Maybe just a few. Don’t want it setting my mouth on fire. Last time… You were practically crying! Honestly. Look, while that’s simmering, can you grab the mushrooms out of the fridge? I need to chop them for the stir-fry that's going to be on the side. Sure. Are we still using those vouchers we got for that place in town? The Indian restaurant? I was thinking that! We could go next Saturday. Provided we use these vouchers before they expire, of course. Shame about the meat though. It smells a bit dodgy, doesn't it? Yeah, I think that ground beef has gone off. Maybe we should just stick to chicken and veggies tonight then? Good shout. Less risk of dodgy tummy. Speaking of dodgy… did you see that documentary about facial deformities? Yeah, that was… intense. Poor kids. It was, wasn't it? I felt awful. It makes you appreciate what you've got. You know, I read an article the other day about how even things like jelly fish contain a surprising amount of fat and protein. Jellyfish?! Why would anyone eat jellyfish?!? Apparently, it's eaten in some Asian countries. They drain out all the water and then deep fry it. Sounds disgusting, doesn't it? All that oil…and the salt, probably loads of salt. Everything's got too much salt these days.

This is alright, I suppose. Bit bland though, isn’t it? Honestly, Liam, you complain about everything. Mum put in a lot of effort. I'm not sayin' she didn't, love. Just a bit more seasoning, that's all. You know, a bit of pepper never hurt anyone. You’re just missing your Mum’s cooking, aren’t you? Aye, maybe I am. It’s just… different, being away from home. Even if I were working, the routine would be different. It  is  weird not having Mum’s Sunday dinners. I miss the Yorkshires, properly crispy ones. These are a bit…sad. Don't start, Elodie. They're fine. And you’re just being picky. How’s school going, anyway? Still drowning in history essays? Don't remind me. Mr. Davies is piling it on. He's got it in for me, I swear. All this about the Tudors. It’s so boring. He just wants you to work hard, Elodie. You’ve got the potential. Easy for you to say, you’re already done with school! Doing brilliant things. I’m just a support worker, not brilliant! It's good work though, I like it. Helps to know I'm making a difference, even a little one. It’s a steady job, that’s what matters. I wish I could find something steady. Keep sendin’ out applications, do you? Every day? Of course, Liam. Mum’s been helping you look, haven’t you got anything back? A few bits and bobs. Mostly just rejections. One interview, got all the way through the first round, then nothing. Feels like a right waste of time. Try volunteering somewhere. It looks good on a CV, loads of people do it. Aye, I’ve thought about that. Just… hard to motivate yourself when you’re lookin' at the same four walls all day. Well, you could come with Sarah and me on Saturday to that charity shop in town. They’re always looking for volunteers. Maybe. It’s a thought. Did you see that new show on Netflix? The one with the detectives?  Crimson Shadows , yeah! I binged it all last weekend. Absolutely brilliant. Who’s your favourite character? Definitely Detective Miller. He’s so moody and mysterious. I thought Detective Carter was better, she was much more resourceful. I just liked the rain. All the rain in that show. Reminded me of home.

This shepherd's pie is really good, Annie. You’ve outdone yourself. Cheers, Ben! Glad you like it. It's a recipe my Grandma used to make, thought I’d give it a go. It's a bit of Yorkshire comfort food, even here in Cambridge. It certainly brings a bit of home to mind. You seem to be keeping busy with work, then? You mentioned something about a big conference? Oh, it's mental. This conference is huge. International speakers, hundreds of attendees… it’s all a bit overwhelming, really. I’m coordinating everything from venue bookings to speaker travel, dietary requirements, the works. Sounds stressful. Still, a good challenge, I suppose. Keeps you on your toes. Must be a far cry from that little stationery shop you used to work in. It is! A  lot  more responsibility. And the hours are killer. I’ve barely seen daylight this past few weeks. I keep telling myself it'll be worth it when it’s all over, but right now… I'm just running on coffee and adrenaline. Well, you're doing brilliantly, from what you tell me. You always were a grafter. You’re putting all that Yorkshire grit to good use. Thanks, Ben. Means a lot. It's just... sometimes I feel like I'm forgetting how to relax. I haven't been to the gym in ages. Remember how we used to go together? Vaguely. My knees aren’t what they used to be, you know. I stick to walks now. Nice gentle strolls in the park, that’s about it. But you should definitely make time for yourself, Annie. All that working will catch up with you. I know, I know. It's just hard to squeeze it in. Everyone keeps asking for something – a last-minute change to the seating plan, a speaker needs a special tea… it's non-stop. People always want something. It's just the way of the world. You’ve got to learn to manage expectations. Don't go offering yourself up for every little thing. Easier said than done! I’m a bit of a people-pleaser, I suppose. I always want to make sure everyone’s happy. That’s a good quality, but don’t let it burn you out. Have you kept in touch with Sarah and Emily? From school? Sarah, yeah, we chat online occasionally. She’s doing really well in London, turned into a proper barrister.

Right, boys, plates in the dishwasher, please. And someone needs to clear the table. I'm still full, Mum. You always are, Liam. Ethan, you helping out? Yeah, Dad. Just finishing this level on my game. Ethan, put the game down. It'll still be there in five minutes. A little bit of help goes a long way. Fine, fine. Did you see Novak Djokovic? He’s smashed it at Wimbledon. He is playing brilliantly. That serve is just clinical. I read an article earlier about how his training regime is… intense. It has to be, doesn't it? You don’t get to that level without dedicating everything. Speaking of dedication, have you two been doing your French homework like I asked? Yeah, mostly. Got stuck on the subjunctive mood though. That’s just ridiculous. Why does it even  exist ? The subjunctive is a source of much consternation even for native French speakers, son. It expresses doubt or possibility. Think “I wish…” Sounds boring. It isn't boring, Ethan. It’s important. Anyway, I was reading something really interesting the other day… about how Hitler had a surprisingly well-groomed moustache. All those photos just make him look even more… sinister, you know? What? Why are we talking about Hitler? It's just an interesting historical detail, Liam. It highlights how even the most monstrous figures could take pride in appearances. Actually, facial hair has made a comeback. Look at Tom Holland, he’s got a proper beard now. He does! He looks quite different, doesn’t he? Brings a whole new vibe to Spiderman. Yeah, he looks older. Are you still seeing Chloe, Ethan? Yeah, she’s good. Has she seen your Instagram? You've been posting some decent stuff lately. That picture of the sunset over Cannock Chase was really nice. Yeah, she liked it. She’s got a new filter she’s been using – makes everything look really golden. Honestly, those filters. Sometimes, it's better to just appreciate things as they are. Nature doesn't need Instagram. You sound like a grumpy old man, Dad. Someone has to be the voice of reason. Now, table clear  please , before I start refereeing this entire conversation. Liam, you’re on dishwasher duty, Ethan, you’re clearing the table. Honestly, sometimes I feel like a hotel manager. Can I go back to my game after? Yes, but finish your homework first.

Right, nearly home now. Just gotta navigate this roundabout, eh, love? Yeah, easy peasy. So, about that sofa... Have you looked at any more online? Mum was saying the one you showed her was a bit…beige. Beige is a colour, love! It’s calming. And yes, I’ve had a proper trawl. Found a lovely grey one, corduroy. Bit different. Think Nan would hate it. Corduroy? Oh, goodness. It’ll collect every crumb and hair. I’m still finding fluff from that old velvet armchair I had. Ended up in the tip, that did. A right wrestle getting it out the door. We could take all this to the tip next weekend, couldn't we? That old armchair, that chipped side table... finally get rid. Definitely. Speaking of getting rid of things, have you heard anything more about Emily’s friend’s family? The one from uni? Oh, Sarah’s friend, Chloe? Yeah, apparently her dad's got some sort of dodgy building project going on. Heavily into these conversions. Wanting all the permits and whatnot. Seems a bit underhand. People and their schemes. Honestly, it's a wonder anything gets done properly these days. Remember when Mr. Henderson used to do all the repairs around here? Proper craftsman he was. He was. Nowadays, you're lucky if they can even tighten a screw! And don’t even get me started on people washing your clothes at the launderette. I swear, someone put a red sock in with my whites last week! Ruined my favourite blouse. Mum, you were ranting about that for a week! It’s just a blouse. Easy for you to say! It was a nice blouse! Anyway, it's all connected, isn’t it? Reminds me of your Auntie Brenda trying to sell us that hideous ceramic cat for Christmas one year. Oh, the cat! Dreadful thing. Absolutely dreadful. Never could understand why she thought it was a present. It was so dusty. It sat on the mantlepiece for ages, covered in dust. Grandma used to hide it behind a plant. She did! Poor Grandma. She’d spend ages trying to disguise it. We all feel for the Grandparents don't we, They trying. It’s hard, isn’t it? Seeing them get older. Fred’s memory's going now, you know. Little bits, like names. Dementia, the doctor says. It’s… worrying. I know, Nan.

Right, so I was thinking, Friday night, we could definitely do that new Italian place, you know, the one near the theatre? Oh, yes! That sounds lovely, darling. I saw a review of it actually. Apparently, their pasta is to die for. Are you still going to the gym after work on Thursday? Yeah, trying to! It’s been a bit hectic with work, though. Honestly, Mum, I’m stressed about this project. It’s got a huge deadline, and Brenda’s being completely unhelpful again. Brenda? Still? Honestly, that woman… You know, I always thought she’d have been made redundant years ago. Speaking of which… have you heard anything more about those cuts at school? Just rumours, mostly. Apparently, they’re looking at some redundancies again. Can you imagine? After all those years. It's a shame, isn't it? Poor Mrs. Hawthorne. She's been there forever. Though, the exams are busier than ever - Ofsted put a lot of pressure on them. Still, it’s unsettling. Tell me about it. Makes you think, doesn’t it? About the future and all that. I was looking at houses online again, actually. Just daydreaming. Oh, still thinking about the extension? Yeah, well, we need the space, don't we? And the garden is getting ridiculous. Though, the quotes are terrifying! We'd practically be remortgaging the whole house. Don't rush into anything, love. And get a few quotes before you commit. Remember Uncle George's disastrous extension? Nearly bankrupted him! Oh, God, yes! That was a disaster. He put in those fancy bi-fold doors and they kept jamming. He swore blind it was the wind's fault. He always blamed something else, didn’t he? Anyway, have you been eating properly? You sound tired. I’m trying! I had a salad for lunch, at least. It's hard when I'm dashing around all day. I’ve started taking a packed lunch again. That’s good, darling. You need to look after yourself. Your Grandad was asking after you the other day. He said to give you a big hug. Oh, tell him I said hello, please. I need to ring him soon. Actually, I promised him I'd go visit him on Saturday. Good, good. He’ll love to see you. So, Saturday then - you'll come round for a roast, won't you? I'm making that one with the apples and sage.

So, what are we doing tomorrow then? Like, actually doing? Not just sitting around. Well, we could try and get out, couldn't we? Little Finn’s getting a bit stir-crazy, isn’t he? He’s wanting to see Mick again, I think. Mick’s good. But we’ve watched him like, ten times today. I know, I know. But it’s something to do, isn't it? And the weather’s supposed to be decent. Maybe we could go to the pool? Swimming’s good! But it’s always rammed, innit? And Finn’s still not that great at swimming. He mostly just splashes. He’s learning. And it's good exercise. We could pack a picnic? Yeah, that would be good. What about going to see Liam? He said he’s got his new guitar. Oh, that’s a lovely idea! Remind me to text him. Has Finn been getting on with Liam? They didn’t seem to be getting on great last time. He was a bit grumpy. He was tired, I think. He does that, you know? Just gets all melty. Oh, my sweetie. What’s wrong, love? Are you hungry? Maybe we should just have a chilled day. I’ve got that pile of washing to do, and the garden is a mess. The garden  is  a mess. You know, I could do some weeding? It’d be good to do something useful. Really? Would you? That would be amazing. Honestly, I’ve been putting it off. But I don’t know my weeds from flowers, and I’m worried I'll pull up something nice. I’ll look up a guide online. And I can do it in the afternoon. What are you doing tonight then? Just… trying to figure out what Finn’s saying. I swear he's trying to tell me something important. He keeps saying "Baa-roo-to!" Sounds like Japanese. Are you learning Japanese again? I was. Briefly. I got a Duolingo owl shrieking at me to do my lessons, and I abandoned it. Honestly, the pressure! Do you want spaghetti for dinner? It’s easy enough. Yeah, spaghetti sounds good. Maybe Liam could come round for spaghetti too, and we could all try learning some Japanese? Now you’re being silly. But we could definitely invite Liam. It’d be good to see him. And you doing the weeding would be brilliant, honestly.

Right, this bit’s getting proper mental, innit? Mental's the word for it. Proper bleak. Still, I'm glad we chose this one. Needed a bit of dark, ya know? After all that sunshine in Majorca. Majorca was brilliant, though. Proper relaxin’. Didn’t realise how much I needed a week of just… nothin’. Except maybe scoffing pastries. You were scoffing pastries, alright. Nearly put on a stone. Remember that bakery near the cathedral? Don't remind me! Worth it, though. Absolutely worth it. Speaking of scoffing, I need to book a dentist appointment. Me gums are playing up something fierce. Dentist, eh? You’re brave. I had a filling last year and I nearly fainted. Proper traumatizing. You always faint. It's a proper thing now, isn’t it? Like a party trick. It is a bit, isn’t it? The dentist just expects it now. He keeps a little spray ready. "Here you go, Liam, just in case." Proper. Anyway, this film… seriously, the cinematography is bonkers. Makes you think, doesn't it? About, like, how much we all overthink things. Definitely. Reminds me of that Murakami book you lent me, 'Kafka on the Shore'. All that weird, symbolic stuff. Brilliant, though. Yeah, Murakami's amazing. Should have brought that out again, actually. Been meaning to re-read it for ages. Keeps feeding into the writing, you know? Right, right. You always say that. Still plugging away at that novel, then? Yeah, slowly but surely. Just battling with a particularly tricky chapter at the moment. The dialogue feels clunky. Need to sort it out. You’ll get there. You always do. Just gotta keep chipping away. Hey, saw The La’s tribute band down at the Cavern last week. No way! Really? How were they? Proper good, actually. Sounded pretty spot-on. Crowd was buzzing. It’s mental, isn’t it? How much that band means to this city. Absolutely. Proper legends. Should be goin’ to more gigs. Been neglecting me music fix lately. We need to remedy that. There’s that new indie band playing at the Arts Club next month. Heard good things. Right, put it in the diary. You know, I was thinkin’ the other day, Liverpool’s just… thriving, innit? There's always something going on. Proper thriving. And the Citibikes are a game-changer. Makes getting around so much easier. Although I did nearly wipe out trying to use one in the rain last week.

So, tell me all about this new job, love. Really tell me. How’s it going? It’s… lovely, actually. Really lovely. Completely different from my placement, you know? Much more responsibility, but in a good way. That’s what you wanted, wasn't it? A bit more independence? Definitely. At the placement, it felt like I was just… shadowing. Now I’m actually  doing  things. Planning lessons, marking work, working really closely with the kids… And the kids are alright? Any little terrors? There are a few, of course! Cheeky little monkeys. But mostly they're brilliant. So engaged and eager to learn. Little Leo, in Year 2, he just  loves  phonics. It's adorable. That’s lovely to hear. It’s such a rewarding job, teaching. You must feel like you're making a difference. I do. It's not always easy, obviously. There’s a lot of paperwork and long days, but… seeing their faces when they finally ‘get’ something… it makes it all worthwhile. Absolutely. So, any plans for Easter? I was thinking of finally tackling that recipe for those lemon and poppyseed cakes. Remember Nana’s? Oh, yes! Those were amazing. I’d love to try and recreate them! We could bake them together? I’d love that. I've got all the tins out and everything ready. It's just a matter of finding the time. Speaking of time… have you heard anything more about the Christening date? Auntie Carol's still dithering about the venue. She is, isn’t she? She messaged me yesterday. Apparently, the village hall is booked solid for miles around. She’s looking at renting out the community centre in Lichfield. Oh, that's a bit of a trek for some people. Especially Uncle Dave. I know. She’s trying to find somewhere palatable though. Wants it to be nice for little Emily. I think Emily will be more interested in the cake than the venue, if I’m honest! Probably true! What about your parents? Are they coming up for Easter? Yes, Mum and Dad will be here. Dad's already promised to bring his infamous Easter egg hunt kit. Oh, bless him. It’ll be chaos. Remember that one year when he hid the eggs in the flowerbeds? And little Tom spent the whole afternoon covered in mud! Good memories though, aren’t they? Speaking of good memories, have you booked that holiday yet?

Oh, that journey was a nightmare! Birmingham traffic is truly something else. Thanks for having me over, though, it's lovely to see you. Don't mention it, love! It's been too long. You look tired though, work been hectic? Absolutely! The new GCSE syllabus has landed, which means endless marking and prepping. Honestly, I spend more time making sure the kids understand the subjunctive than I do actually teaching the language! Oh, I know that feeling well. Even after all these years, new syllabuses feel like a fresh wave of paperwork. How are your little ones managing? Still obsessed with Pokémon? They have moved on to Minecraft, sadly. It’s far less colourful, and equally consuming. Leo is trying to build a replica of Hogwarts, which is...ambitious. Maisie's into those beauty vlogger things, you know, eyeshadow palettes and contouring. Oh, goodness. My niece is the same. She spends hours watching those tutorials. It's fascinating, isn't it? Where do they even  get  all those brushes? I have no idea! It’s a whole industry. Anyway, how are things with you? Still loving your job at the primary school? Yes, still there. Honestly, it's the best thing I ever did. The kids keep you young, you know? And even better, I’ve got a little helper now. Oh really? Yes, my granddaughter, Daisy. Her mum’s having a bit of a tough time, so Daisy’s come to live with us. That’s lovely! How old is she? She’s five. A little whirlwind, she is. Always running around, asking questions. And she’s absolutely obsessed with our cat, Winston. He's been a bit put out, to be honest. Used to be king of the castle, and now he’s got a tiny human trying to dress him in doll’s clothes. Oh, that’s hilarious! Winston will adjust. Cats are resilient creatures. I remember when we got Leo a hamster, Mr. Nibbles, he looked as though we’d invited a swarm of bees into the house! That’s exactly it! Anyway, enough about Winston and his hissy fits. Have you heard anything about Mrs. Peterson’s son’s new business? Apparently, he’s doing really well with his online handmade soaps. I did! Someone mentioned it on Facebook. Apparently, they’re selling out within hours. I’m surprised, though, he always seemed so…reserved.

Right, okay, so, Grandma, you’re telling me you actually  tried  to smuggle Ortolan into France? Oh, don’t you start, Daniel. It was years ago! Before all these ludicrous restrictions. And you have to understand, darling, the flavour! It was a once-in-a-lifetime thing. A real culinary adventure. Culinary adventure that could have landed you in serious trouble, Nana. Honestly. Though I have to admit, the concept sounds… intriguing. Intriguing illegal bird, more like. You’re a mad woman, Patricia. Nonsense, Edward! It was a vintage year. And I knew a man… a  very  important man... who could arrange it. This is incredible. I can't believe you're telling this story, especially with the Seder going on. This is… historically inappropriate. Relax, Daniel. It’s a good story. Besides, we're talking about Jewish food aspirations, and Nana has plenty of those. Want to hear about my matzah ball recipe, everyone? It’s a little tweak on my great-aunt’s, vegan, of course. Vegan matzah balls? Seriously? Honestly, they're amazing! You'd never know. It's all about the vital wheat gluten. Vital wheat gluten? Good heavens. My mother would roll over in her grave. A proper matzah ball needs schmaltz, Leo! Schmaltz! Absolutely. There’s no substitute. That richness... Perfect with a good charoset. Speaking of which, Chloe, yours last year was phenomenal – proper apple and walnut balance. Thanks, Edward! I’m trying a new date and fig version this year. I’m hoping it’ll be even better. I’ve also been experimenting with saffron. Saffron in charoset? Bold move, Chloe. Really bold. It’ll be far too overpowering. Honestly, these young people and their… innovations. You mustn't mess with tradition! But isn’t tradition about evolving? My grandfather used to put a single olive in his Seder plate, completely against custom. Said it represented peace. Okay, that's actually pretty cool. A little subversive even. See, Nana? It’s not all about rigidity. Although, I do agree, good gefilte fish is sacrosanct. I’ve been trying to perfect my own – it’s been a mission. Gefilte fish! Now,  that ’s a subject. My cousin Miriam in New York makes the best. She sends us a jar every Chanukah. It's flown across the Atlantic! New York? You should go visit her, Grandma! I'm planning a trip to New York in the autumn – Broadway and bagels, obviously.

Right, so, who's ready to absolutely demolish "The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo"? I'm buzzing to hear everyone’s thoughts. Oh, absolutely! I finished it last night and… wow. I need to talk about it. Seriously, the ending! I’ve been easing myself into it this week. Work has been a nightmare, you know, end-of-quarter stuff never stops. But I’m about halfway through now. Are we going to spoil it, or will we build up to it? Let's build up! I think the really interesting thing is the structure, isn’t it? The way it jumps around in time, slowly revealing bits and pieces. It keeps you so hooked. Totally! The interviews, the way Evelyn chooses what to share... it's so clever. And the glamour! I felt like I was transported back to old Hollywood. I'm enjoying the glamour too. Though, I must admit, I initially found the constant shifting back and forth a little jarring. It took me a chapter or two to settle in. Reminds me of that one series, “This is Us”, you know? Same kind of structure. Oh, definitely! Similar feel. Speaking of television, did anyone watch that new detective series on ITV? “The Long Shadow”? I tried, but it was a bit too intense for me. I'm still recovering from the last true crime doc I watched! I need something lighter, more escapist, I think. Like… croquet and a cup of tea! You and your croquet! I'm trying to get back into knitting. I started a chunky scarf for my niece. Are you still crocheting, Emily? Oh yes! I’m doing a blanket for my nephew. It’s a right beast to manage, but he’ll love it. He's more interested in cars than books at the moment, the little rascal. My little Oliver is obsessed with anything dinosaur-related. Footloose in the house. It's exhausting. Though, I've been trying to read more with him – actually reading  to  him, not just snippets before bed. It's so important to read aloud, isn’t it? Though I do struggle with those illustrated children's books... all those words on each page! I prefer a good, solid novel. I've been trying to embrace eBooks more. Much easier for travel, you know? But I still love the smell and feel of a physical book. It’s a proper experience.

Right then, initial impressions. Bit smaller than I thought, innit? Feels good in the hand though. Proper premium, this. Yeah, it’s nice. The screen’s gorgeous. Though, I’m a bit intimidated already. You know I'm not exactly tech-savvy, Dad. Don't be daft, love. It’s Nokia. They practically invented this stuff. Remember the 3310? Unbreakable. This is a step up, obviously, but the principles are sound. Think of it as a slightly more glamorous brick. Right, a glamorous brick. First thing I need to do is sort out the data. I’m going to be glued to the internet researching all day. Can you remember how to set up a roaming thingy? I can never get my head around that stuff. Absolutely. Let’s have a look. Right, settings...mobile network...data roaming. You want to enable that, but be mindful. Roaming charges can be eye-watering. So, only use Wi-Fi whenever you can. Good point. I’m always forgetting that. And what about the language? It defaulted to Finnish, obviously. Aye, ‘course it did! Let's switch that back. Settings...language…English. Sorted. See? Easy peasy. Nokia’s always been good for user-friendliness. Even back when I was doing my thesis, the demos showed how the clever software was intuitive for everyone rather than just the tech heads. It’s a shame, really. Nokia used to be  the  phone, didn't they? And now… Well, they’re back, I suppose. It's brilliant though, proper feel-good story. It is, isn't it? A bit of a phoenix rising from the ashes. And the quality is still there. You can feel it. Remember Gran used to say, "German engineering, built to last." This feels like that. Made with pride, not just slapped together. Definitely feels different from my old one. Right, next problem. Contacts. I’ve got about a million on my phone, and I need to make sure they all transfer across. It's a nightmare, always. That’s the tricky bit. Let’s see… Okay, there’s a SIM card transfer option. We'll need to take the SIM card out of your old phone and pop it in this one. You know, it’s remarkable how reliant we’ve become on these little gadgets. I mean, remember life before mobile phones? Actually communicating with people, face to face. You sound like you’re about to give a lecture on the sociological impact of mobile telephony, Dad.

Right, so we need to sort out this birthday party for Finn, don’t we? He’s turning seven next month – can you believe it? Yeah, it’ll be good. Should we do it at home or like, book a place? I think at home will be easier, won't it? Less to worry about, cheaper… and Finn loves having his friends here. We could set up the garden, weather permitting. Yeah, that's good. What about a theme? I was thinking maybe animals? Finn's absolutely obsessed at the moment. Animals are cool. What kind of animals though? Like, dinosaurs? He's a bit past dinosaurs now, I think. He's really into Red Pandas at the moment. Remember he was drawing them for ages? Oh yeah! They’re really fluffy. Do you think we can get like, decorations with Red Pandas on them? We could! Or even just a big poster. What about you? What’s  your  favorite animal? Still the Malamooche? Always! They’re the best dogs ever. Such big fluffy faces and they drool everywhere. Yes, darling, a very good boy. He likes big, fluffy dogs. Honestly, your brother loves those dogs. I don’t know why. They’re just… awesome. Remember that one we saw in that park last year? The one that was the size of a small pony? Oh my goodness, yes! It was enormous. We need to send Finn a picture. He’d love that. What about presents? Have you thought about what you want to get Leo for his birthday? Hmm… maybe a new iPad cover? His is all sticky from juice. Good idea. Or maybe he’d like a new board game? We haven't played those in a while. Yeah! We could get one of those strategy ones. The one where you build cities. We'll have to look. We also need to think about holidays. Remember we talked about going to Japan? Yeah! I’d really like to see some Japanese films. Me too! And we could teach Finn a little bit of Japanese – just basic words. What about your gymnastics lessons? Are you enjoying those? They're pretty good. I’m trying to learn a new trick – a cartwheel onto a beam. It’s really hard. I'm sure you'll get it! You’re really good at gymnastics. We’ll get the decorations sorted, the cake ordered, and plan all the games, okay?

Honestly, nan you’d think being from London, you’d be used to proper snow. You’re going on about drifts like it’s a national crisis! Well, Bognor Regis isn't exactly known for its Siberian winters, is it? A bit of frost, a few flakes if we're lucky. Nothing like what you lot get up north, eh? True, true. But I do remember this one Christmas, when I was a kid, back in Manila… it was properly chaotic. My Lola – that’s grandma – insisted on making Pastel de Leche from scratch, which takes forever and involves like, ten different kinds of milk. Ooh, Pastel de Leche! Is that the custard cake? I remember reading about it. Must be lovely. It is, it is. But the kitchen ended up looking like a war zone. Flour everywhere, spilled milk… my aunties were arguing about how long to bake it. And then my cousin, he was about five, decided to 'help' and ended up smearing custard all over himself! Classic. My Christmas usually involves my mam slating my uncle’s choice of crackers – he always buys the cheap ones. Typical. My wife, bless her, insists on having a real Christmas tree, even though it sheds needles everywhere. I’ve vacuumed up more pine needles than carpet this December. We always had an artificial tree. My Arthur – that was my late husband – wouldn’t have it any other way. Said real trees were a fire hazard. Sensible man, he was. Though I do miss the smell… It’s a smell, innit? Like pine and… orange peel? My nan always had orange peel on the tree. It smells proper Christmassy. We’d always have a star on top, made of – get this – tin foil. My Lola was a big believer in resourceful decorations. And karaoke, oh lord, the karaoke. Every Christmas Eve, after dinner and the star of tin foil, we'd all belt out Filipino Christmas carols. Karaoke? Good heavens! I’m not sure my ears could handle that. We had a recorder. My wife and I would play Christmas carols on it. Simple pleasures. We have the same. We both used to play. Sounds a bit dull, grandad. You need to spice things up! My friends and I always end up playing silly drinking games on Christmas Eve. Never anything too wild, mind you. Just enough to loosen up the mood.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is amazing, Sarah. You’ve outdone yourself. It really is fantastic, Anne. Best I’ve tasted in ages. Though I’m starting to regret that second helping… Don’t be silly, David. A little extra never hurt anyone. Anne, you really know your way around a kitchen. It’s a far cry from my attempts at comfort food - mostly involves frozen pizza these days. Writer’s life, eh? Fuelled by caffeine and convenience. Precisely. Though I did try a lentil shepherd's pie last week. A disaster. It tasted like disappointment and regret. I can imagine. So, Anne, how's the transcribing going? Still battling endless legal jargon? You have no idea. This one’s about a disputed property line. It's drier than the Sahara, I swear. But the money's decent, so I can't complain too much. I’m just glad I finished the last one – a hundred hours of interviews with a beekeeper. A beekeeper! Now  that  sounds fascinating. Is there a book in that? You never know. It’s surprisingly complex, the world of bees. Proper passion project for him. Anyway, what have you been up to, Eleanor? Finished that new manuscript yet? Almost. The final edits are brutal, you know how it is. I'm trying to get it to my agent by the end of next week. I'm thinking of treating myself to a new Kindle cover to celebrate – something bright and cheerful, rather than the dreary grey one I've had for years. You should! I got a Kindle Paperwhite for Christmas. Absolutely brilliant - so easy on the eyes. Have you considered one? I’ve been thinking about it. My eyes aren’t what they used to be, and lugging around massive hardbacks when I travel is getting tiresome. It's a game-changer, Anne. You’ll love it. You can carry your entire library in your handbag. Tempting, very tempting. What are you reading on it, David? Just finished a real corker of a detective series. "The Holloway Murders." Have you heard of it? Ooh, sounds intriguing. Scottish, isn't it? I love a good detective novel. Agatha Christie is always a safe bet, of course. It is, yeah. Set in Edinburgh. Really atmospheric, dark and twisty. Proper page-turner. I’m thinking of diving back into "Sherlock" – maybe rewatch the whole series. Oh, I love “Sherlock”!

Right then, Doris, you’ve been mulling over that solicitor’s letter, haven't you? Don’t keep chewing your lip like that, it'll give you wrinkles. I have, Arthur. It’s just… all this about the will. It’s a bit unsettling, isn't it? Especially after all these years. I’ve never really given much thought to such things. It’s sensible to be organized, Margaret. Particularly at our age. And well done to Michael for being proactive. He’s a good lad, always thinking ahead. Michael’s a bright spark, that one. Got his head screwed on. Unlike some, eh, Doris?  chuckles  Don't you start, Arthur. It's not about having my head screwed on or off. It’s about… feelings. Knowing things are changing. Feeling is natural, Margaret. But don't let sentiment cloud the practicality of it. This solicitor, Mr. Davies, he’s reputable. He’ll have explained everything clearly. Davies is a good chap. Used to handle old Mrs. Henderson’s affairs down the street. Never a bother. Always straightforward. He did explain, yes. It's just... he suggested I write down my wishes too. Regarding… well, my belongings. And it feels so… final. Like I’m putting labels on everything. It's not about labelling, Margaret. It’s about ensuring things go where you want them to. Minimizing the potential for disagreements later. Remember what happened with your Aunt Elsie and her antique tea set? The family nearly came to blows! Elsie and that blasted tea set! Never could understand why she fussed over it so. Just bits of chipped china, really. It was a family heirloom, Arthur! It had been passed down for generations. Anyway, that’s exactly what I’m worried about. Squabbles amongst my grandchildren. I don’t want them arguing over my collection of porcelain dolls. Then be specific, Margaret. Write down exactly who gets what. Be clear. That’s the key. And don’t feel you  have  to include everything. Just the items with sentimental value, the ones people might be likely to dispute. Doris, listen to Geoffrey. Practical advice. It's like that time I tried to leave everything to chance with the allotment produce. Chaos reigned! Carrots disappearing, beans being swapped for rhubarb... absolute pandemonium. Oh, Arthur. Always with the allotment stories. Alright, alright, I’ll try. But where do I even start? All these forms… Mr. Davies will provide you with the forms, Margaret.

Okay, here's a conversation based on the provided context, aiming for a natural flow and incorporating the diverse dialects. It's roughly 450 words long.
