Conversation:   Maisie: Right, so the pub's booked for Friday then? The Old Red Lion, yeah? Eleanor: Yep! I’ve confirmed it. Seven o'clock. I put a note on Slack about dietary requirements - anyone got anything I missed? Chloe: I'm good, veggie as always, but all sorted, I reckon. It’s just… I’m still buzzing about what happened earlier. Ugh, I’m so ready for the weekend. This week has been brutal. Tell me about it! Mrs. Davies is piling on the homework in history. I swear, I've been researching Roman aqueducts for three hours straight. Seriously? I thought Mr. Harrison was the homework tyrant, but she’s giving him a run for his money. Did you even finish the essay on the Tudors? Nearly. I got stuck on the bit about Henry VIII’s wives. It’s just… so much to remember. Anne Boleyn, Jane Seymour, Anne of Cleves, Catherine Howard, Catherine Parr… my brain is melting. Right? It’s a minefield of historical wives! I did finish mine though. I actually quite liked it, once I stopped procrastinating and Googling “what did Tudor peasants eat?” Oh god, that's a rabbit hole. I tried that, ended up looking at pictures of medieval turnips. Not exactly inspiring essay material. No way. What about science? Did you understand any of that quantum physics stuff Mr. Patel was on about? Absolutely not. I think he was trying to confuse us on purpose. All those diagrams and equations… I just scribbled down notes that looked vaguely important. Same. I was staring blankly at the whiteboard, pretending to concentrate. At least Liam wasn't asking questions this time. Liam’s a menace! He just loves winding Mr. Patel up. Remember last week when he asked if electrons have feelings? Oh my gosh, I’d completely forgotten! Mr. Patel’s face was priceless. He just stammered and went all red. It was brilliant. Anyway, did you hear about Chloe getting into the school orchestra? No! That's amazing! She's been practicing her violin for ages. So proud of her. What instrument is she playing? Cello, apparently. She got the first cello spot. It’s such a competitive thing. Wow, even more impressive! I’m so bummed I didn’t try out for the drama club this year. I was too nervous. You should have! You're brilliant at acting. Remember that time you did that impression of Mrs. Davies? Don’t remind me. I almost got detention for that one. But seriously, I'm thinking about trying out next term. Maybe. You definitely should! You’d be fantastic. Come on, we’ll work on some lines together. Let's pretend we're Shakespeare! Okay, okay, but if Mrs. Davies hears us, I’m blaming you.

This risotto is absolutely gorgeous, Mum. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Aye, well, I’ve been practice’n, lass. Seein’ as you’re always moanin' about restaurant risotto bein' dry, thought I’d give it a go meself. It’s really good, honestly. I'm not usually a risotto fan, but this... this is something else. Creamy, but not heavy, you know? Exactly! And the mushrooms are cooked perfectly. Can I have some more bread, please? Aye, of course, love. I’ll get ye some. This reminds me of that time your grandad tried to make it… absolute disaster, it were. Burnt rice all over the kitchen. Oh God, did he really? You always tell that story. I can just imagine. Poor Grandad. So, Mum, how was work today? Anything exciting happening at the store? Same as always, really. Mrs. Henderson complaining about the price of the towels again. Honestly, some folk… You’d think a nice fluffy towel was rocket science! People are always complaining about something, aren't they? I had a ridiculous meeting this afternoon. Spent an hour going over a Gantt chart for a project that’s already finished. Pointless. Ugh, sounds frustrating. That’s exactly what I hate about my job sometimes – all the admin that doesn’t actually… do anything. Well, at least you're busy, eh? Keeps you out of mischief. Your dad reckons I should be doin' more volunteering, that kind of thing. Dad always has some idea, doesn't he? Keep you on your toes. He just wants you to be happy, Mum. You’re brilliant at what you do – you always put a smile on people’s faces. Aye, well, it's a job at the end of the day and I need something to do. I miss you both at home though. It’s quiet without you clatterin’ about. We miss you too! That’s why we wanted to come for dinner and properly catch up. Definitely. So, I was thinking… have you managed to book that weekend away yet? We talked about going to the Lakes. I’ve been lookin’, aye. Prices are a bit steep, to be honest. But there's a nice little cottage not too far from Keswick, not right in the centre, but close enough. Comfy lookin’. Send me a link! We can have a look. When are you thinking of going? Sometime next month, ideally.

Honestly, Sarah, I'm just knackered. This week has been relentless. Accounts are a nightmare this quarter, and the pressure is just building. Tell me about it! Cleaning's been busy too, you know. People seem to think now's the time to do a deep clean when the weather's nice, bless ‘em. It’s non-stop. But I’m glad to see you, love. It’s been ages. How's everything  really ? Well, the operation went pretty well, I think. They said it was successful, but the recovery… it’s a slower process than I anticipated. Still getting a bit tired, and the pain meds make me feel a bit fuzzy. Oh, sweetheart, I'm so sorry to hear that. It sounds rough. Are you taking it easy? You always push yourself too hard. Trying to. It’s hard though, especially with everything happening at work. And the kids, of course. What with them? Is everything alright with Maisie and Liam? Maisie's being a typical teenager, moody and glued to her phone. Liam's the worry, actually. He’s getting into trouble at school. Detention last week for disrupting class. I’m having words with him, but… Oh dear. Is it just bad behaviour, or something more going on? Sometimes they bottle things up, you know. I think it’s attention-seeking, partly. He feels overshadowed by Maisie, I think. She’s clever and gets all the praise, and Liam… well, he just acts out. I’m going to have a proper chat with his form tutor this week, see if she has any insight. That’s a good idea. Don’t be afraid to chase it up. Schools can be rubbish at communicating sometimes. I had a right old battle to get them to address Tom’s bullying a few years back. I remember that. You were brilliant. Speaking of Tom, we should try and visit soon. It feels like forever since we popped over to see them. We should! I’ll give them a ring this week. It's been too long. And we need to do that weekend away we talked about. Somewhere quiet, just us two. Absolutely. I need it desperately. I've been trying to plan ahead a bit with work to give myself some breathing space. Actually, I was thinking about changing banks. The fees they're charging are ridiculous. Oh, really?

Honestly, I’m never getting any studying done with this constant thinking about work. Tell me about it! I’ve got three essays to write and all I can think about is whether or not I’m going to get any shifts at the coffee shop this weekend. My student loan isn’t exactly stretching, you know? No way, it never does. Bartending’s alright though, innit? At least you get decent tips sometimes. Though last Saturday was brutal – stag do gone wrong, spilled drinks everywhere… Oof, sounds rough. I’ve only worked behind the counter a few times, helping out during busy periods. It’s always chaotic. The latte art’s harder than it looks, too. I ended up accidentally drawing a… well, let's just say it wasn’t a swan. Oh god! What was it? I’ll spare you the details. Let's just say it involved a very confused customer and a hastily withdrawn coffee. Classic. I had a bloke last week try and pay for his pint with a crisp packet. Said he was “saving up.” Seriously? Some people are wild. How do you deal with it? I’d probably just burst into tears. Years of practice, love. Years. You learn to just roll with it and try not to take anything personally. Although, sometimes, you just have to give 'em a bit of Yorkshire grit. I bet. So, are you still looking to move on from The Stag's Head eventually? Yeah, that’s the plan. It's alright, good money, but it's not exactly intellectually stimulating, is it? I’d love to find something that uses my degree a bit more. Maybe something in publishing? That would be brilliant! You’d be amazing at that. You’re so good with people. What about that internship you mentioned a couple of weeks ago? Did you hear back? Not yet. They said they'd be in touch by the end of last week. I’m trying not to get my hopes up too much. It’s all just a bit stressful, you know? Feels like every job application I send out just disappears into the void. I know the feeling! I need to start looking for summer work soon, too. Any ideas? I’m not sure I fancy being a barista all summer again. It gets pretty draining. Hmm. There's that event management company in town.

Right, so, anyone managed to actually book anything for the summer yet? I’m starting to feel the pressure. Oh, you and me both, Liam. I've been looking, but prices are just ridiculous, aren't they? Proper daylight robbery. I was thinking of Skegness, just to be honest. Cheap and cheerful, you know? Skegness? Ach, darling, you’d be better off staying here! The rain’s just as bad, and you can still get a decent cuppa. I’ve been thinking of heading back to County Down for a few weeks. Just to see the family. County Down, Moira? Lovely part of the world. Been a while since I've been over to Ireland. Used to go as a kid, you know, with my grandmother. Always remember the smell of turf fires… Sounds nice, Moira. Much better than battling for a sunbed in Majorca. I was tempted by Greece, but then I saw the flights…eye-watering. Greece is always tempting though, isn’t it? I had a friend who went to Crete last year. Said it was gorgeous, but she ended up with a dodgy stomach and didn’t stop complaining! Ah, that's always the risk, isn't it? Foreign food. Always something. My cousin went to Spain and ended up with a bad case of sunstroke and a fondness for sangria. Took her weeks to recover! Well, you can’t have everything. I’m considering a bit of Cornwall this year. Bit of a drive, but the scenery’s always good. Plus, there are some fantastic gardens down there. Cornwall, that's a good shout, David. I've always wanted to go to the Eden Project. Though, knowing my luck, it'll be raining cats and dogs. It always is in Cornwall, love. You're better off embracing it. Grab a pasty, put on a waterproof, and enjoy the scenery. Speaking of rain, I remember one holiday in Blackpool... absolute downpour the entire week! Ended up spending most of it in the arcades. Blackpool! Now there's a throwback. My dad used to take us every year. The lights were... impressive. In a slightly overwhelming sort of way. It's funny, isn't it? You plan and you budget, and then you end up remembering the weirdest details. Blackpool arcades, turf fires, dodgy stomachs… Exactly! Memories are made of the unexpected, aren’t they? As long as I get a bit of sunshine, I’ll be happy.

Oh, come on! That was a clear foul! Honestly, the ref is having a shocker tonight. You're always saying that, love. Every game. It’s your default reaction, isn't it? No, but genuinely! Look at the replay! He tripped him right up! It was blatant. And it’s costing us! Yeah, alright. Could’ve been a free kick, I suppose. But they're still holding the ball well. Just need to be a bit more clinical in the final third. Clinical? They’re like a herd of elephants trying to get through a needle's eye! Honestly. Remember when we used to go to the Stadium of Light and it was buzzing? Now... Progress, love. It's progress. They’re building a new squad, it takes time. You're expecting miracles. I’m expecting them to score a goal! It's the 85th minute! We’re still nil-nil. I’m starving. Fancy getting something? What are you thinking? Pizza? There’s that new place we saw last week. Apparently, their garlic bread is amazing. Ooh, yeah! But like… proper, dripping-in-garlic-and-cheese garlic bread. Not that pale imitation stuff. I know, right? I checked the reviews. Apparently, they don’t skimp on the garlic. It’s a risk, though. Might set off the smoke alarm. Worth it. I’m craving comfort food something greasy. All this tension and drama... I need something to soak it up. Maybe some chips too? Chips it is then. Large portion. You're always hungry when we watch the football. It's a sport requiring intense concentration! I burn calories worrying about every decision the manager makes. Right, of course. Intense concentration. So, pizza and chips then? I'll order. What toppings do you want? Pepperoni definitely. And maybe some mushrooms. And if they actually score a goal before the final whistle, I'm getting extra cheese. Don't let them down! Don't pressure the lads, love. Just play the game. And I’m getting a veggie option. Trying to be healthy, you know. "Healthy" while simultaneously ordering a large portion of chips. You are a contradiction. But alright. Go for it. Just make sure there’s plenty of garlic bread for me. Deal. Let me just put this order in and then maybe we can stream that documentary you wanted to see...after the match of course. Yeah, after the match.

Right, that’s lovely, Mum. Proper brew. Grandma, you're spoiling us. Always do, lad. Always want you all nice and cozy. It's a bit chilly today, isn't it? Though, I don’t remember it ever being  that  chilly in July. Times are changing, that's all. It  is  a bit nippy, isn't it? Good job you’ve got the heating on, Gran. So, Mark, how's that project going at work? The one with the, what was it… the logistics firm? It’s… well, it's a challenge. You know how it is. Supply chains are still a nightmare. We’re trying to optimise routes, get deliveries out quicker, use more eco-friendly transport. All that good stuff. Eco-friendly, eh? Remember when a car was just a car? No thinking about fuel efficiency. My David had a Morris Minor back in the day. Bright red, it was. Drove it everywhere. I can imagine. Dad used to talk about his old Ford Anglia. Said it was “characterful.” Meaning unreliable. Your dad loved his cars, didn’t he? Remember that blue Vauxhall he had? The one that always smelled of petrol? Oh god, yes! The Astra. A classic. You know, I was watching  Top Gear  the other day – the old Clarkson, Hammond, May days – and it got me thinking about how much cars have changed.  Top Gear ? Never watched it. Too noisy. Give me a good old movie any day. Remember when they showed  Brief Encounter  at the Paramount? Went with David three times! Made me cry every time. Still does, if I think about it. Oh,  Brief Encounter ! Such a classic. I saw that at the cinema when I was a teenager. It’s funny, isn’t it? The films they made then were so… restrained. Exactly. Now everything’s explosions and superheroes. Not quite the same depth. Though, I did enjoy the new  Barbie  film. Bit of a culture shock, but actually quite clever.  Barbie ? Really? I've heard it's all rather… flamboyant. It is, but it's got a message. It's a commentary on society and consumerism. All this modern nonsense. Give me a good black and white film any day. Something with a bit of class. And a proper love story. No explosions. You and your love stories, Mum. Anyway, I was thinking about making a lemon drizzle cake this weekend. Would you like one, Mark?

Honestly, you two. It’s Pancake Day! How many pancakes did you  eat ? Just one. It was yucky. I don't like it. It's too…flappy. Flappy? It’s a pancake, Leo! And Willow, it's not yucky, you just said it was your favourite thing yesterday! What’s happened? I don't like it anymore. Right. Well, at least try to eat a little bit. We talked about all the children at school who don’t always have enough to eat. Remember Mrs. Davies told us about Liam? Liam only has pasta sometimes. Exactly. So even if you don't  love  pancakes, just a few bites would be good, okay? Okay. Can we go to the Science Museum this weekend? Possibly! We need to check the tickets. Remember how cool the space exhibit was last time? Yes! Rockets! And the giant dinosaur bones! Yes, all that. But first, hands! Wash those little hands. We’re having washing-up time after this. And then, you know, brushing teeth. But Mummy! No buts! Healthy teeth, healthy kids. Speaking of healthy, did you enjoy your assembly today, Leo? Mrs. Peterson was reading that Green Knowe story again. The one about the Old Magic? It’s spooky! It is, isn't it? I loved those books when I was little. Maybe we should get them out again. Though, I was thinking, perhaps we could take a trip to Paris next year? Paris! With the Eiffel Tower! Can we see the Louvre? And eat croissants? Croissants are definitely on the list. Although, first we need to get through this plate of pancakes. I saw a review of a performance at the Festival Hall too, maybe something for us adults if the kids are busy drawing afterwards. Can I draw rockets? You absolutely can draw rockets. And spiders, and dinosaurs, and anything else your imagination conjures up. Now, finish those pancakes! Mummy, Millie in my class says her dad is taking her to the beach next week. Oh, that's lovely! We’ll have to plan a beach trip soon. Maybe to Cornwall? Cornwall has sand castles! It does indeed. Just one more bite, sweethearts. One more bite for Liam, and one more bite for your mummy who is trying to get you to eat something. And after that, we'll all brush our teeth and think about sand castles and rockets. Deal? Deal. Deal.

This noodles are unbelievably good. Seriously, best Chinese I’ve had in ages. Yeah, this is a good choice. Glad we didn't get that dodgy place again. Remember last time? The spring rolls were basically just damp pastry. Oh god, yes. And the chicken tasted vaguely of…fish? You’re being dramatic. It wasn't  that  bad. It was questionable. Right, so, has anyone heard about Aunt Brenda? Apparently, the funeral’s next week. Oh, really? Didn’t realise she’d… I mean, she’d been poorly for a while, hadn’t she? Feel bad for Mum, that’s rough. She was always fond of Brenda. Yeah, it's sad. I wonder if we should organise something for afterwards? Maybe just a simple get-together at someone's place? Good idea. Keeps it a bit more…lighthearted, you know? Less formal. I’m happy to host. My flat’s big enough. We can order pizza, put on some terrible movies… Perfect! Although, no more Chinese after this feast. My stomach is protesting already. Speaking of terrible movies, did anyone see that new Liam Neeson action film? Absolutely ridiculous. Yeah, the plot holes were bigger than the Grand Canyon. Though, I did enjoy the explosions. I wouldn’t touch it with a barge pole. Give me a classic Disney film any day. Bob the Builder marathon, anyone? Please no. My childhood trauma is real. Oh, remember when we all used to build Lego Death Stars? Those were the days. Classic. I still have a few boxes stashed away somewhere. Might need to resurrect them. So, anyone got any weekend plans? Besides mourning Aunt Brenda, of course. Thinking of going to a cricket match on Saturday. They're playing the Yorkshire side. Interested? Cricket? Hmm, I’d rather watch paint dry. But I’ll come for the social aspect. And the food stalls, obviously. I’m heading up to see my dad. He’s been dealing with some issues on the farm. Drought’s hitting pretty hard this year, apparently. That’s awful. Hope he's okay. Did you see that article about the language models getting surprisingly good at imitating accents? Apparently, they're using the National Corpus to train them. Mental. Seriously? Like, they can replicate a Scouse accent perfectly? Apparently. It's a bit scary, honestly. All these AI advancements... Just imagine a Bob the Builder AI. “Can we fix it?

So, you were telling me about Mrs. Higgins next door when you were a child, Dad? The one with the champion roses? Ah, Mrs. Higgins. A formidable woman, she was. Fierce about those roses, she was. Wouldn’t let a soul near ‘em, except for her grandson, little Arthur. He was a sweet boy, always chasing butterflies amongst the petals. Did she ever win any prizes for them? Prizes? Land sakes, she won more prizes than you could shake a stick at! At the Wolverhampton Flower Show, the Horticultural Society… she was the queen of the roses, she was. Everyone reckoned she fed them secret ingredients. Probably something scandalous, knowing her. Scandalous rose food! What sort of things did people whisper about? Well, there were rumours, of course. One was she’d talk to them. Really talk, mind you. Like they were people. My mother used to say she’d heard her arguing with a particularly stubborn bloom. Oh, that's brilliant! My mum used to do the same with her tomatoes. Said it helped them ripen. It’s funny how we pick up these little habits. It reminds me of Grandma Elsie and her insistence on polishing the silverware every Tuesday, without fail, even if we were having beans on toast for dinner! Elsie was a character, that one. Always complaining about the rise in insurance premiums. Remember how she used to haggle with the postman over the price of a stamp? Oh yes, that was Elsie to a tee! Always trying to get a bargain. What about Uncle George and his obsession with driverless cars? He’s convinced they’re the future. He is! He was going on about them for ages, saying they’d revolutionise travel. Though he’s still terrified of flying, ironically. Always has been. Said he’d rather travel by bicycle. Though considering his age… Yes, I don't think he’s on many long journeys these days. Speaking of which, I saw a fascinating article about Google’s tax deal with HMRC. It's all a bit complicated. It is, isn't it? All these big corporations finding loopholes. Honestly, it's infuriating. I was just in the supermarket, trying out their Scan As You Go system. A complete disaster. Took me twice as long. Really? I thought it seemed quite convenient. Although, I do miss just browsing the shelves. Do you remember when supermarkets were smaller, more local?

Right, Operation Chinese New Year is officially underway! Who wants to draw a dragon? Me! Me! Can I use glitter? Of course, you can use glitter, darling. Loads of it! But remember, dragons breathe fire, so we need to draw some flames too, okay? Do I have to? Dragons are scary. They're not scary, Leo! They’re powerful and lucky! They bring good fortune. This year is the Year of the Dragon, remember? Look, Mummy! It’s a sparkly dragon! Oh, it's wonderful, Willow! Very sparkly indeed! See, Leo? Isn't it amazing? It's got too many colours. Well, dragons come in all sorts of colours, silly! Just like the planets. Did you know Jupiter has a giant red spot? Jupiter! Like in school? We learned about Jupiter! Is it far away? Very far away, sweetheart. Much further than even your Grandma’s house! It takes a very long time to get there in a rocket. Can we eat noodles now? Almost, little one! Let's finish our dragons first. Speaking of noodles, I'm thinking sweet and sour chicken and egg fried rice tonight. What do you say? Yay! Can we have fortune cookies? Absolutely! And maybe some spring rolls too, if we're lucky. Are you excited about school this week? Any fun things happening? We're doing fractions. Fractions, eh? That can be tricky. Remember, it's just about sharing things equally. Like sharing the noodles! I have piano lessons on Wednesday! Miss Emily says I’m getting really good at Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star. That’s brilliant, darling! I’m so proud of you. And Leo, how are your drum lessons going? Are you banging away like a little rockstar? It’s okay. Daniel keeps stealing my sticks. Daniel! That’s not very nice, is it? We’ll have a chat with him about sharing. Speaking of being active, how was your aerial hoop class on Saturday? Did you learn anything new? I did a spin! A wobbly spin, but still a spin! That’s fantastic! You're getting so brave! And did you watch ‘Barbie and the Great Adventure’ over the weekend? It was on the telly! It was boring. Oh, you’re just saying that! You love Barbie! What about when we finish these dragons, we’ll have a proper Chinese feast, and  then  we can watch it again? Yes! And I'll show you my dragon sparkly drawing!

Cheers, everyone! Seriously, this place is unreal. Didn’t expect Rome to be  this  quiet though, you know? It is pretty relaxed. I’m kinda loving it. Beats the usual tourist mayhem. Though, that Airbnb was a bit of a nightmare to find, wasn't it, Liam? Tell me about it. Google Maps led us on a wild goose chase through some seriously dodgy backstreets. Thought we were going to get mugged. You two always find the drama. Mine was fine, near the Pantheon. Practically a tourist attraction myself, walking past it every day! Yeah, navigate in this city is a nightmare. Even for me, and I’m used to driving on the wrong side of the road. These cobblestone streets are trying to kill me! Seriously! Right, so, dinner tonight. What are we thinking? I saw a place earlier that looked amazing – apparently their pasta carbonara is legendary. Ooh, I'm in for carbonara. I’ve been craving it all week. So, what's the verdict – Liam and Chloe's trek worthy? Absolutely. Consider it a pilgrimage. Although, I’m still slightly traumatized by those backstreets... Anyone else feeling the heat? It’s like a sauna out here, even now. Fair dinkum, it is hot! I'm gonna need another Aperol Spritz to survive. Seriously, though, Rome is pretty incredible. Got that timeless thing going on, you know? Definitely. It feels bigger than I expected, in a good way. I’m trying to pick up a few phrases – “Grazie,” “Prego,” that’s about it so far. My Italian's a bit… patchy. My mum tried to teach me when I was a kid, but I mostly just remember how to order pizza. Classic Chloe. I'm attempting a slightly broader vocabulary. My nan was from Birmingham originally, but her family had links to Italy, so I’ve been trying to dust off a few family phrases. It's a bit embarrassing actually, my pronunciation is atrocious. You’d think you’d be good at accents, though, with all the people you meet at the café! It’s different, you know? Learning to understand different accents, not  speaking  them. Though, I did recently have a very intense conversation with an American tourist about the best way to brew coffee... Sounds about right. Americans and their coffee. Tell you what, you should hear the arguments blokes have back home about the perfect flat white.

Ugh, I’m so stressed about Chloe’s hen do. It’s meant to be next month, and I still haven’t figured out any games. Chloe's hen do? Don't worry too much! It'll be fine. Remember Sarah's? We just ended up gossiping and eating cake. It was brilliant. Yeah, Sarah's was a vibe. Seriously, low-key is the way to go. Stressing over games just makes it feel…forced. I agree. Last year, someone tried to organise a murder mystery for Jess’s hen. It was a disaster. People just wanted to chat and have a drink. I know, but Chloe's really into Pinterest. She's got this whole vision of fairy lights and flower crowns and a scavenger hunt… Sounds like a craft project, not a hen do! You could embrace the Pinterest thing, actually! Like, a crafting station. Everyone could decorate their own tote bags or make friendship bracelets. Ooh, that’s a good idea! Little kits with pre-cut fabric and beads and stuff. We could get loads in from Hobbycraft. Hmm, a crafting station… I hadn’t thought of that. That could actually work. It would give people something to do if they get bored. I’m still worried about the venue though. Rosie and Ali Bonds is booked, but it’s a bit small, isn’t it? It is a bit cosy, but that's part of the charm! And it's got that cute little garden. We could do a picnic in the garden if the weather’s nice. Perfect! We could bake some cupcakes or brownies for the picnic. I’m attempting a Victoria sponge this weekend. Wish me luck! Oh, please share! I’m hopeless at baking. My last attempt resulted in a rock-solid lemon drizzle. I can help with the baking! I made a really good red velvet cake last week. It was actually quite impressive, even I said so. See? You’ve got this! Just relax and enjoy it. Chloe's going to love it no matter what. She's just excited. Speaking of excited, did anyone see Maya’s Instagram story? She’s starting her trip to Bali! No! Show me! Oh wow, it looks amazing! White sand, turquoise water… I’m so jealous. She looks so relaxed. I wish I could escape to a beach for a week. You need a holiday!

Right, so, the chicken’s defrosting, yeah? Think this is enough? We're only doing two, aren't we? Feels about right. Though, you know, I was thinking, maybe curry? Curry? With chicken? Sounds good, actually. But, ugh, I'm still feeling a bit rough, to be honest. This bug’s really hung on. Still? Thought you were getting better. You were complaining about stomach cramps for like, a week. I  was  getting better, then it came back with a vengeance yesterday. Just… drained. And the slightest smell makes me feel nauseous. That’s awful. Shouldn't you have seen someone? Mum said it’s probably just a virus and needs to run its course. Honestly, she's insistent about those things. Reminds me of that holiday in Greece when I had food poisoning, and she told me to 'just drink more water'. Classic Mum. Remember that hotel too? The one with the… questionable pool? Don't remind me. So many tiles missing, and that weird green algae. I swear, I had a rash for a month after that. And the breakfast buffet? It was like a battlefield. True, true. Trying to avoid anything that looked remotely dodgy was a full-time job. So, curry then? I’ve got some decent korma paste. And rice, obviously. Yeah, curry sounds amazing. Less chopping for me too, which is a bonus given the whole feeling-like-death thing. You make the rice, I'll get the chicken sorted and maybe, if I feel up to it, chop some peppers. Perfect. While you're doing that, I’ll pre-heat the oven. What about naan? Any point ordering some? Definitely need naan. And poppadoms. Although, ordering is a pain. Deliveroo's always got a massive service charge. Yeah, rip-off. Though, honestly, after last week’s cooking disaster, I'm glad to let someone else handle it. Remember that attempt at paella? Don’t. Just… don't. Burnt rice, rubbery prawns... it was a tragedy. We ended up ordering pizza. A culinary catastrophe. Right, rice on, oven's on. You feeling okay to stand at the cooker for a bit or should I handle the chicken too? I think I can manage for a bit. Just promise me you’ll keep an eye on me. And a glass of water within easy reach. Deal. And if you start looking green, you’re sitting down.

Right then, let’s get this shopping list sorted. I’m going to Morrisons tomorrow. What do you need, Jean? Oh, just the basics really, Penelope. Milk, bread, a couple of apples. And do you think they’ll have those calendar fobs in? You know, the ones with the little pictures? I like to start putting them on the calendars in November. I think they will, yes. They usually do. Though the selection’s never as good as it used to be. Remember when they had proper selection boxes? Mountains of them! Oh, goodness, yes! And the art and craft at school, remember? The craft fairs we used to put on. Not the organised affairs they are now. We used to make all sorts of things. Remember Mrs. Plumley insisting we all made felt mice? Oh, the felt mice! They were monstrous. All lopsided and with wonky eyes. I vividly recall trying to glue on googly eyes that just kept falling off. And you saving every scrap of felt, convinced you could make something magnificent. Remember David's hockey boots? Heavens, he kicked them all over the playing field! They were a disaster! He always needed new ones. Speaking of school days, I was thinking about what we studied at university… it feels like a lifetime ago. It does. Your sound recording course, wasn’t that fascinating? I always admired you for pursuing something so technical. I stayed with history, of course. It was, but terribly slow-moving technology at the time. It was all tape recorders and reel-to-reel. Imagine! Now it's all digital. And that module on social history... I still think about some of those lectures. The impact of industrialisation on working-class families... it stays with you. Absolutely. Then all those changes with computers. Remember when computers were the size of rooms? And the punch cards? How could I forget? I was working with those at the University and I was amazed. It's mind-boggling how drastically they’ve changed. I was thinking about it the other day, I wonder if we should donate some of my old computer equipment to that Computing Museum up in Manchester? That’s a wonderful idea, Penelope! They'd have all sorts of wonderful things to display. So much better than gathering dust in your spare room. Honestly, you were ahead of the curve with all that technology.

So, honestly, the neighbours have been absolutely lovely, haven't they? We had a welcome basket delivered yesterday. Did you? What was in it? Homemade jam, scones…some lovely local honey. And a card signed by half the street, wishing us well. That’s just lovely, isn't it? Wellington always had a terrible sense of community. People kept themselves to themselves. Southend was the same, really. Though you did get the odd character. Remember Mrs. Higgins and her peacocks? Oh, don't remind me! The squawking woke me up every morning! So, the jam – was it good? Delicious! We had it on the scones this morning. Right, needs some cream though. Can’t have a scone without clotted cream. You'll have to introduce me, then. I'm still getting my bearings here. Trying to figure out where the nearest decent hardware store is. This DIY is a nightmare. There's one just down the road in Lifton, about a ten-minute drive. A little pricey, but they’ve got everything. I got all the decking screws there. And apparently, the local pub, The Forest Inn, is supposed to be excellent. Heard the food is really good. Yes, I’ve already been! Had the fish and chips. Very good indeed, you should try it. It's amazing that they have vegetarian options. Right, that’s going on the list. I rather fancy a pint, to be honest. Settling in properly needs to involve a pub, doesn't it? Absolutely. Though you'll have to drive, John. I’m sticking to tea. After all the wine I had at Christmas... Speaking of Christmas, are you thinking about putting up decorations yet? Feeling festive? Trying to! But I'm still unpacking boxes. Feels like I’m living in a cardboard box village. It'll all come together. You're doing brilliantly, darling. It’s a big move. And the walking groups are great. Did you sign up for the one that goes around Dartmoor? Yes, I did! Apparently, they’re lovely, and such a good way to meet people. Honestly, everyone's been so welcoming. Even the treasurer of the local garden club waved to me when I was trying to get the roses planted. Roses, eh? What variety did you go for? David Austin. 'Gertrude Jekyll'. Apparently, they're really reliable here. Very good choice. And you're just in time for pruning season, too.

Ugh, this is ridiculous. Another rejection email. Let me guess, another retail job? They're all asking for experience, aren't they? It's a vicious cycle. Tell me about it. “Proven track record of customer service” – I’ve never even  had  a job! How am I supposed to have a proven track record? I know, it’s daft. You'd think they’d at least consider someone with a decent degree. You were top of the class in History, remember? Doesn't seem to matter much does it? I saw a job advertised at JD Sports, thought I'd give it a shot. The online application was longer than my dissertation. JD Sports? Seriously? You'd be surrounded by trainers all day. Better than being surrounded by nothing, eh? Speaking of which, did you order that new phone case from Amazon yet? The one with the floral design? Not yet. Right, so I was thinking about the Semiotics module, and I’m struggling a bit with how to frame the Baudrillard section for this year's cohort. They’re really resistant to the hyperreality concept. Honestly, the state of things… I was reading an article this morning about the latest by-election results. Utter chaos. Chaos is a strong word, Margaret. A bit dramatic, even for you. Though I’ll grant you, Welsh politics is currently a delightful mess. First Minister changing like the seasons. It's just... confusing, isn't it? Seems like everyone’s arguing about everything. Exactly, Rhys! It’s not just Wales either. The whole country feels fractured. And the debates are so… aggressive. No nuance, no attempt at understanding the other side. Well, that's the nature of contemporary politics, isn’t it? Soundbites and shouting matches. Remember the miners' strike? There was passion then, a sense of purpose. This just feels…performative. Oh, don’t remind me of the miners' strike. Your father… he was so involved, wasn't he? All those meetings, the picket lines… It must have been a difficult time. Aye, it was. A lot of hardship, a lot of anger. But there was a solidarity, a sense of community that’s hard to find these days. My grandfather, too, he worked in the pits. Proper hard graft, that was. Dust in your lungs from the moment you woke up until you went to sleep. Did he ever talk about it much, Dad? Not really. Welsh men, we weren’t great at talking about feelings back then, were we? It was a man’s job, he’d say. Just got on with it. But I heard the stories, you know? From my mother, from the neighbours. Life was hard, but they had each other. It’s fascinating, isn’t it, how much history shapes us? My own family, on my mother’s side, were all involved in the suffrage movement. Quite radical for women in London at the time. My grandmother used to tell me stories about marching, getting arrested… Strong women, your side of the family. We’ve got our share of strong women in Wales too, of course. Bronwen Morgan, Mary Evans… Women who fought for their rights, their communities. Are we nearly there yet? My legs are starting to ache. Almost, Rhys. Just another hour or so. Are you still thinking about that essay on post-colonial literature? Yeah, but I’m stuck on this one point about representation. It's so tricky. Tricky indeed. Representation is always tricky, isn’t it? Whose voices are heard?

Right, so, the dragons have escaped the castle, but they’re not breathing fire this time. They’re… they’re knitting! Knitting dragons! Why are they knitting? Hmm, good question! Maybe they're knitting scarves for all the knights, because it’s suddenly gotten very, very chilly. And they're grumpy about it because using dragon scales for yarn is  scratchy . Dragon scales are pointy. Exactly! Very pointy. And that’s why the dragons are cross. Do you think they need special knitting needles? Big ones! Like trees! Ooh, yes! Giant tree needles, perfect! See, you’re a brilliant storyteller, sweetheart. What do you think should happen next? The princess… she helps them? The princess helps them! That's a lovely idea. Why does she want to help the grumpy, scratchy-yarn-using dragons? Because she likes knitting too! And she’s got lots of fluffy wool. So clever! The princess arrives with a huge pile of fluffy, pink wool. And the dragons are very surprised because it’s so much softer than scales. And they stop being grumpy? Yes! They stop being grumpy and start knitting the warmest, pinkest scarves ever! What do you think we should do this weekend? The Linton Book Festival is on, remember? Can we go? Can we go and hear stories? We can! I was thinking about going to see Helen Moss. Remember, we have her books? The ones with the funny animals! Yes! The ones with the funny animals. She’s doing a talk and a workshop – maybe we can all go together? We could even invent a story together, inspired by her. Maybe about a badger who knits tiny hats for squirrels? A badger in a hat! Yes! And the squirrels wear them on their heads when it’s raining! That's brilliant! See? You’re already inspiring stories. Maybe we can knit little hats for the badger and squirrels too, when we get back! Can we have pink wool? Like the dragons! Absolutely! We’ll get a whole basket of pink wool. Now, who wants some toast? And then we'll finish our story about the knitting dragons... perhaps they'll open a shop! "Dragon's Scales & Scarves - Scratchy No More!" What do you think? Is that a good name? Yes! Very good! With sparkly signs! Can I draw the signs? Of course, you can! You're the best sign-maker I know.

Right, so I’m thinking lentil shepherd's pie. Feel like comfort food tonight after that shift. Sounds good, Maisie. But are you sure about the lentils? I was thinking maybe chickpeas, a bit more… sassy. Sassy lentils? Is that even a thing, Elara? Honestly. I'm just trying to prevent this curry from becoming a total disaster. It's either bland or it’s nuclear. There’s no in-between. Chickpeas would be alright. But I’m trying to cut back on gas, you know? Lentils are… gentler. And I need to remember those B12 tablets – Doc said I was borderline deficient. Seriously? Still? I keep telling you, a proper veggie diet isn't  automatically  deficient. You need to be mindful. It's just, like, proper planning. Don't start the lecture, Elara. Some of us have lives, you know? Like, preventing this curry from triggering a full-scale kitchen fire. Alright, alright. No lectures. Just… remembering. It's easy to forget, isn’t it? Anyway, the bigger conversation is – did you guys see that article about cultured meat? The… shmeat? Oh my god, yes! It’s incredible, isn’t it? Like, theoretically, we could completely eliminate factory farming. No more animal suffering. No more massive environmental impact. It's mental. But also… a bit creepy? Like, eating something grown in a lab? It feels… unnatural. But isn’t that a weird arbitrary line, though? We’re all eating stuff that's been massively altered from its natural state. Think about selective breeding, genetically modified crops… Exactly! And think about the scale of the cruelty and the pollution of current meat production. It’s oppressive on so many levels. Animals, the environment, people working in abattoirs… it’s all linked. I get that. It's just… a fox hunting comparison came to mind. You know? Taking something from a natural environment and putting it in a lab, just as a product for consumption. Feels a bit… dystopian. Fair point. But hunting is entirely different. It's targeted violence. This is trying to solve a systemic problem. And at least with cultured meat, you’re removing the suffering  from  the equation. Absolutely. Although… I did read something about the energy requirements being quite high. So, it's not  necessarily  a huge environmental win just yet. Speaking of environmental wins, this curry is definitely saving the planet. Okay, now it’s dangerously spicy.

Right, nearly ready then. Just putting the oven on. How was your day, David? Busy, love, very busy. Had a right kerfuffle with Graham in accounts. Apparently, my spreadsheet wasn’t ‘intuitive’ enough. Honestly. Oh, Graham. Bless him. Always the drama. Did you manage to explain it to him? Eventually. Took a lot of deep breaths and explaining the basics. Felt like I was teaching a five-year-old. Maisie, darling, are you starving? Not starving, Dad, just peckish. This day has been a disaster. Client completely changed their minds about the campaign at the last minute. So much wasted effort. Oh, sweetheart, that’s awful! Some clients are just impossible. Don't let it wind you up too much. Dinner will make it all better. Tell me about it. At least the washing machine's behaving itself today. Last week, it decided to just stop mid-cycle and flood half the utility room. Oh, don't remind me. Remember when your Auntie Brenda tried to fix it herself and nearly electrocuted herself? Oh my god, yes! She swore off DIY for life after that. She certainly did. Said she’d rather wrestle a badger than touch another appliance. Speaking of, did you see Carol’s photos from the wedding last weekend? Yes! Gorgeous, weren’t they? The flowers were just stunning. And poor Liam, bless him, kept tripping over the carpet! He looked so stressed throughout the whole thing. It was rather endearing, actually. Are they back from honeymoon yet? Just got back yesterday, apparently. They’re in the Lake District. Said it's beautiful, but the rain was relentless. Typical British weather, isn’t it? Right, potatoes are on. You two wouldn’t mind helping me set the table, would you? Sure. Dad, have you seen the cat? I thought I heard him meowing earlier. Last I saw, he was trying to climb the curtains again. Honestly, that cat. It's like he's deliberately trying to give me grey hairs. He’s just being a cat, darling. A very mischievous cat. Speaking of mischief, you’re never going to believe what happened to your cousin, Emily. Let me guess, she left her phone on the bus again? Worse! She accidentally sent a very… passionate text to her boss! No! Oh, Emily! What did she do? Apparently, she deleted it immediately, but he’d already seen it. She’s mortified, of course.

Right, so supper’s nearly ready. I’ve got chicken and veg, who wants some mash? Mash would be good, yeah. Please! Loads of gravy though. Loads of gravy it is. Oh, look at these forks! Where did these come from? What? The butterfly forks? Gran sent them. For Remembrance Day. Oh, right! How silly of me. They’re quite beautiful, aren't they? Very… poignant. They look weird. Well, they’re meant to symbolise someone returning home. Do you remember we did two minutes silence today at school? Yeah, it was boring. It wasn't boring, it was important. It was for all the people who died in the wars. I know, I know. Just felt really long. It is a long time to stand still and be quiet. But it's important to remember. Your Grandad always used to say... Mum, can we talk about birthdays later? I’m kind of stressed about Liam’s party. Of course, love. What are you stressed about? I’m excited about Liam’s party! It’s just… finding a DJ, and making sure the music’s okay, and… I don’t want anyone to get into trouble. Well, you're being a very responsible party planner. It's good to be thinking ahead. I'm sure it will be fine. And I’m happy to have a look at playlists with you. Can we have cake at Liam's party? Of course you'll have cake. Anything else you want? Maybe a bouncy castle? Yes! A bouncy castle! Let's not get carried away with the bouncy castle. Your dad would have something to say about that. He probably would. Although… I wonder if he's seen what's happening with Russia and Ukraine? It’s all over the news again. It is. It's awful. I was reading something earlier about how the sanctions aren’t really working, and it just feels like it’s dragging on forever. Is it like a war? Kind of. It's complicated. It’s incredibly complex, darling. There’s a lot of history and politics involved. It's not something easy to explain. But essentially, Russia is invading Ukraine. Why? That's the big question, isn't it? There are lots of reasons, some of them old, some of them… well, rather unpleasant. It’s very sad for everyone involved. Makes you appreciate things, doesn’t it?

Right, so Cornwall it is then! I’ve just been looking at campsites, and there are some really lovely ones near Polzeath. Loads of space for the kids to run around. Polzeath! Can we build a sandcastle bigger than last time, Mummy? Absolutely, sweetheart! We'll build a whole sandcastle kingdom. And maybe even find some crabs. Crabs! Can we keep one? Please, Mummy? We can’t keep a crab, darling. They need to live in the sea. But we can look for them, and maybe take some pictures. Okay! And can we go to Adventure Island? Well, we’ll need to factor that in. Adventure Island’s brilliant, but it's a bit of a detour, isn’t it? We could do it on the way back, maybe? Adventure Island! The roller coaster! Yes, you love the roller coaster. Though, you might be a bit taller by then to go on all the rides. Mummy, are we going to see the sparkly thing at the museum? You mean the V&A exhibition? Yes, darling! We can definitely make time for that. I'm really looking forward to it, actually. It's all about textiles and it's supposed to be amazing. Textiles? What's textiles? It's… it's like all the lovely fabrics and threads and things that make clothes and blankets, and rugs! See, like your favourite teddy bear is made of textiles. Oh! Like my sparkly dress! Exactly! Speaking of which, remind me to check if you've outgrown it. We might need a bigger suitcase. Oh, and we should probably look at what we can eat – remember last time with the dairy? My tummy hurt! I know, sweetheart. We’ll be extra careful this time. Lots of dairy-free ice cream, and I’ll pack plenty of snacks you can have. I'll look up some good Cornish pasties that are gluten-free too. Can we have pasties everyday? Maybe not  every  day. But definitely a few! So, campsites near Polzeath, Adventure Island on the way back, V&A exhibition, and dairy-free everything. Anything else you two want to do? Go swimming! In the sea! Absolutely! We’ll be in the sea as much as possible. Right, I’m going to start making a detailed list. It’s going to be a brilliant holiday. And after this, I can finally get back to marking those dreaded exams.

Seriously, Mr. Davies is grilling us on Shakespeare again. Like, we get it, Romeo and Juliet is tragic. Can’t he move on? Tell me about it! I spent the whole lesson trying not to yawn. He just drones on and on. And his eyebrows! He raises one like he’s discovered a new planet every time someone asks a question. It’s so distracting. I was staring at his eyebrow the entire time. Did you finish the history coursework? Almost. Just need to do the conclusion. I’m dreading it though. I’m really not feeling history at the moment. I’d rather be out biking. Me too. Remember that trail we found near Langley last weekend? That was epic. Should we go again next Saturday? Definitely. Except… remember Liam’s allergies? He couldn’t stop sneezing the entire time. Yeah, poor dude. He said something about pollen affecting him. Maybe we should pick a different route? Somewhere with less… everything. Good point. Anyway, are you going to Jake's party next Friday? Of course! It's supposed to be massive. Everyone's going. Are you bringing anyone? Yeah, I’m trying to convince Maya to come. She’s being all shy about it. Says she doesn’t like crowds. Maya’s cool. She just has a different vibe, you know? She'd probably have a better time than she thinks. Did you hear about what happened with Ben and Mrs. Peterson? No! What? Apparently, he threw a paper airplane in class and it landed right on her head. She went ballistic. Seriously? Ben? He’s usually so quiet. I wonder if he'll get in trouble with the prefects. Probably. Those prefects are buzzing around like bees lately. Mr. Thompson seems to be riding their backs. Trying to be all strict. He always was a bit of a goody-two-shoes. Remember when he reported us for kicking that football near the sports hall? Ugh, don’t remind me. I still feel bad about that. Hey, did you see the new trailer for "Cosmic Crusaders 7"? No! Is it as good as the last one? They’ve got that new actress, right? The one who was in that sci-fi show last year. Apparently, she’s fantastic! Everyone’s saying it’s the best one yet. We have to go see it as soon as it comes out. Agreed!

Honestly, this road is a nightmare. Every single lane seems to be doing its own thing. Tell me about it. Birmingham traffic is a beast. Glad we left when we did, though. At least we’re moving. Still, I'd rather be on the A1, honest. Straight as a dye, that road. You can practically set your watch by it. Not like this roundabout mayhem. You always were a fan of the A1. Remember that time we drove up to Edinburgh and you insisted we take it the whole way? Aye, because why not? Straight, predictable. Unlike this. Speaking of predictable though, did you catch any of the cricket yesterday? A bit. England were looking shaky, weren't they? Root's form is concerning. Aye, a right pickle. Shame, really. I was hoping for a decent showing. Though, to be fair, watching England cricket is usually a recipe for disappointment. True enough. Still, good to have something to follow. You still cycling much? Trying to. The weather hasn’t exactly been cooperating lately. Want to go for a proper ride next weekend, if we get a bit of sunshine? Maybe head out towards the Cotswolds? Cotswolds sounds lovely, actually. Bit hilly, though. Are you sure you’re up for it after lugging around all those linguistic data files all week? Don't remind me. My back feels like I’ve been wrestling a particularly stubborn rhyming dictionary. But fresh air's the best medicine, isn't it? Better than any physiotherapy. Definitely. And you’ll have to show me those new bike trails you mentioned. The ones they’ve built around the canal. Aye, proper good. Should be a bit gentler for a change. Though, I might have to invest in a new bike basket. The one I've got is… well, it’s seen better days. You could get one of those panniers instead. More practical, especially if you're carrying anything heavy. Hmm, you might be right. Always thought they looked a bit…cycling posh, though. Cycling posh? Come on. They're just useful. Well, you’re the engineer, you’d know best. You and your practicality. Still, I'll think about it. Reckon it would be worth a look. Just don't tell my friends from back home I'm turning into a cycling posh. They'll never let me hear the end of it. Your secret's safe with me.

Right, Chinese tonight? I'm absolutely starving. Yeah, sounds good! What are we thinking? Usual place? Let's branch out! I saw that new place, Golden Dragon, down on the high street. Reviews look decent. Golden Dragon... hmm. I’m a creature of habit, to be honest. I love Happy Wok. Their sweet and sour pork is  chef's kiss . Happy Wok is a safe bet. But we always go there. Let's live a little, Elara! I’m with Ben. Plus, I’m craving something a bit more…fancy. Less MSG, maybe? Golden Dragon has got loads of pictures of the chef in the window – looks legit. Legit doesn't always equal delicious. Remember that time we tried that 'authentic' Korean place? Oh god, yeah. The kimchi was…an experience. Okay, fair point. But still, let's at least  look  at the menu online. Is there a website? Let me see… yep, GoldenDragonPeterborough.com. Seriously, the website looks like it was made in 1998. Oh, brilliant. That's a good sign, isn’t it? Not really, Ben! Okay, scrolling... they’ve got everything. Duck, lobster, all sorts of things we don’t normally get. Lobster? Seriously? That’s like, double the price of Happy Wok. Come on, treat ourselves! It's Friday. We deserve it. Okay, I'm tempted. But let's see the prices first. Right, scroll, scroll... Wow, okay, the duck is surprisingly affordable. And they've got these amazing-looking vegetable spring rolls. Spring rolls are always a good decision. But I'm worried it won't be as…comforting. You know? Happy Wok is just…familiar. Like a warm hug. You're being ridiculous. It's Chinese food! It’s all delicious! Alright, alright. Let's do this – I’ll build a basket online. We can all take a look and add what we want. Does that sound good? Okay, fine. But if it’s dodgy, I’m blaming you both. And I’m ordering extra sweet and sour pork from Happy Wok next time. Deal. Elara, you pick the starters. Ben, you grab the drinks. I’ll tackle the mains. Let’s do this! Okay, first up – vegetable spring rolls! Definitely. And... crispy seaweed? Yes! Crispy seaweed is essential. Right, I’m going for the Kung Pao Chicken. Always a winner. What are you having, Elara? I’m thinking the…lemon chicken? Is that too boring?

So, the kids are all quiet then? Been a bit hectic this afternoon, I imagine. Yeah, relatively peaceful. Little Liam was a bit tearful about a grazed knee, but nothing major. You? How was your lecture? Oh, it was…fine. Trying to explain the nuances of Romantic poetry to twenty-year-olds who'd rather be on TikTok. It's a challenge, let me tell you! They look at me like I’m speaking Martian sometimes. Tell me about it! Trying to explain the intricacies of sepsis to patients who just want a quick fix…it's a different kind of disconnect, but a disconnect nonetheless. The NHS is just… stretched, isn't it? Utterly stretched. And the bureaucracy! Don't even get me started. You're facing it on the front lines, but we see it from the back end too. Funding cuts, increased workloads… it’s disheartening. You’re telling me! It feels like we’re just constantly firefighting. I saw a consultant the other day, looking absolutely worn out. Said he was contemplating early retirement. Can you imagine? Losing that kind of experience. Absolutely terrifying. Speaking of things that are unsettling, have you noticed anything odd with Mrs. Higgins next door? Mrs. Higgins? The one with the prize-winning roses? She's been a bit… peculiar, hasn’t she? I saw her out late last night, gardening in her pyjamas. And the curtains have been drawn all day. Exactly! And the bins haven't been put out for collection. That’s completely out of character. She’s usually so meticulous. I was thinking about popping round later, but I didn't want to intrude. I was thinking the same. Maybe a quick knock to see if she’s alright? I used to have a neighbour like that, kept herself to herself. Turned out she'd fallen and hurt her hip, and was too proud to ask for help. That’s what I was worried about. Maybe we should both check in later this evening? Strength in numbers, eh? Definitely. I’m finishing a last shift tomorrow, so no excuses then. Are you still planning that trip to Finland? You mentioned it ages ago. Yes, still on the cards! Hoping to see the Northern Lights. It's been a lifelong dream. My daughter's actually quite interested in going too, so I'm trying to make it a family affair.

Awful gales we’re having, eh, Arthur? Proper rattling the windows. Aye, lad. Like the Mersey's tryin’ to swallow the whole city. Reminds me of '61, the floods. Worse though, that was, worse by far. I’ve never experienced anything like it, living in Germany most of my life. It’s... dramatic. Dramatic? You’ll see dramatic when the water’s swirling past your doorstep. Still, can’t complain too much, eh? At least the telly’s still working. True. Been watching a fair bit of news lately. Bit worrying, what's going on with those immigration policies, eh? Aye, the usual. Blame the foreigners for everything. When I were a lad, we needed help in the docks. Now they’re saying we’re being flooded. Same story, different faces. It’s a complex issue, though. Some are genuinely seeking asylum, fleeing persecution. Aye, and some are chancers, lookin' for an easy life. Always been that way, hasn't it? Never stopped a rogue, though. Still gotta treat everyone with some decency, wouldn’t you say? Absolutely. Though, the police seem to be cracking down a bit harder, haven’t you noticed? More patrols around. Aye, seen 'em. Right busy, eh? Little bit too busy for my taste. Remember when you could leave your door unlocked? Not that I do anymore. Too many dodgy things going on these days. It’s a shame, isn't it? Used to be a real sense of community around here. It's fading, lad, fading. Young 'uns don’t know their neighbours anymore. Stuck noses in their phones. What's a good word for that? Foot and mouth disease of the mind. That's what it is! Quite a vivid analogy. I liked that. Got a bit of wit left in me yet, eh? My sister says I'm turning into a miserable old sod. Don’t listen to her. You’re full of stories. Remind me, what did your dad do? Oh, he were a docker. Hard graft, that was. Never did well out of it, mind. Barely scraped by, same as most of us. He used to tell the best jokes though. He’d say, "Why don't scientists trust atoms? Because they make up everything!" That's terrible! But in a good way. Aye, that’s my dad for ya. Always had a way of cheeri-ing you up, even when the world was falling apart.

Okay, here's a conversation based on the provided context. I've aimed for a natural feel, keeping in mind the diverse backgrounds and occupations of the speakers.   Location:   Cambridge University Press Printing House, lunch break in the staff canteen.   Speakers:       Elara :   From Sunderland, Corpus Administrator.     Phoebe :   From Aylesbury, Language Research Coordinator.     Maisie :   From Lincoln, Language Research Administrator.     Morgan :   From Pennsylvania, Senior ELT Research Manager.     Zara :   From Leeds, Publishing.        Phoebe:   …and honestly, the corpus data on ‘quite’ is just  wild . You wouldn’t believe the range of uses people are finding for it now. It's not just "rather" like it used to be.   Elara:   Aye, I’ve noticed that too. It’s popping up in some pretty unexpected contexts in the Sunderland corpus. It’s brilliant, really. Makes you question all your assumptions about word meaning.   Maisie:   Speaking of unexpected, did anyone see that article about the resurgence of regional dialect usage in social media? Apparently, it's a conscious choice for some people.   Morgan:   I did! Fascinating, isn’t it? It’s likely that the digital landscape has allowed for more regional expressions to flourish than ever before. It makes my work researching ELF even more complicated, though. It's like, how do you define ‘correct’ usage when there’s this constant evolution and diversification?   Zara:   Totally. And it's not just about dialect - think about the slang. It’s changing so rapidly. Trying to keep track of it for the publishing side is a nightmare. I spent half an hour yesterday trying to figure out if ‘rizz’ was still a thing.   Elara:   Rizz? Is that… like, charisma?   Zara:   Yeah, pretty much. It's like… having game. It started online, apparently. Everything does these days.   Phoebe:   Oh dear. I feel old. I have to ask my younger brother if these things are still relevant.   Maisie:   That’s what I did last week, with ‘slay!’ I asked my little cousin, she looked at me like I was mad.   Morgan:   It’s the price we pay for studying language, I suppose. Always chasing the evolving tail of the beast. Do you guys ever think about how our backgrounds shape the way we understand these trends? Like, being from the North, Elara, do you notice dialect influences differently compared to, say, someone from Buckinghamshire, Phoebe?   Elara:   Definitely. It's ingrained, isn’t it? It's not something you actively  think  about, but you hear it in everything.

So, you were saying about the documentary on BBC Four last night? The one about Basque culture? Yeah, ‘Basque: Europe’s Forgotten People’. Absolutely fascinating. Their language is completely isolated, right? No known relation to any other language in Europe. Mind-blowing, isn't it? It makes you wonder about the migrations and shifts in population we never properly piece together. Reminds me a bit of Cornish, actually, in a way – a struggling language fiercely guarded by those who still use it. Exactly! I’ve been dabbling a bit in Cornish myself, just the basics. It’s surprisingly difficult though, isn't it? All those mutations… Tell me about it. I tried to pick up Welsh once, and ended up just mumbling sounds that vaguely resembled a greeting. My tutor nearly threw his textbook across the room. Oh, that’s brilliant! I reckon everyone’s had a similar humbling experience. Learning languages is just… humbling. It really highlights how much we take for granted with English. Absolutely. And the internet's made it easier, certainly, but it's also created this weird homogenized culture. Everything feels so…global now. It’s almost harder to stumble across something truly unique. I agree. And the algorithms! Don’t even get me started on the algorithms. They’re just feeding you more of what you already like, trapping you in these echo chambers. It's amazing how little people seem to notice. Precisely! My sister was telling me she only watches reality TV now. Apparently, "Love Island" is all anyone in her friendship group talks about. Oh dear. I tried watching it once. Couldn't get through five minutes. It’s just…performative. All manufactured drama. It is, isn't it? Though, I do find myself strangely drawn to those Japanese game shows… the ones with the absurd challenges and the incredibly enthusiastic commentary. Oh, yeah! Those are brilliant! I love the ones where they have to eat weird things. Remember that show where they had to eat a giant octopus leg? Oh, please! I try not to. It's a masterclass in controlled chaos. It’s probably culturally specific, that level of frenetic energy. Probably. Though, I think some people just enjoy the spectacle. It's escapism, I suppose. Speaking of teaching, I'm thinking of running a short workshop on Basque language basics at the Uni. Would you be interested in helping out?

Right then, love, tea's brewed. Elsie, Arthur, come on in, sit yersels down. It’s lovely to see you both. Aye, Margaret. Always good to get out of that little flat, you know. Gets a bit much sometimes, doesn’t it, Arthur? Aye, lass. Good to be here. Smell of baking’s lovely. Grandma, Grandpa, it’s brilliant to see you! I finished my history essay, finally. Mr. Davies was being a right pain with the feedback. Oh, bless ya, lad. History. Always liked that myself. You get a good mark? Not bad. A B+. I reckon I could've got a better one if he hadn't spent half the lesson droning on about the War of the Roses again. Well, can't fault him for sticking to his subject, can ya? Now, I've been trying to get this blasted curtain rail sorted. It's wobbling something fierce. I think the screws are stripped. Stripped, you say? Happens all the time, lass. Back in my day, we used to use matchsticks and glue. Held just fine. Matchsticks and glue, Grandma? Seriously? Aye! Don’t you be scoffing. Made do with what we had. Times were different then. Used to do it with a bit of wood and a bit of putty, I did. Trustworthy as anything. That's a good idea actually. I’ve got some dowel. I might give that a go. Your dad, Robert, he’s promised to pop round tomorrow to take a look at the guttering. Says it's leaking again. Gutters again? That’s the third time this year! He’s always promising to fix ‘em. I know, love. He’s a busy man. But I've told him, if it's not sorted by next week, I'm getting a proper tradesman in. Regardless. Good for you, lass. Don't let him ride you roughshod. He’s just a bit forgetful, Margaret. Always has been. Forgetful or just doesn’t want to get his hands dirty? Here, Arthur, you remember that time you fell off the roof trying to fix the chimney? Oh, don’t remind me! Nearly broke my neck. Your mother was furious, she was. Called the fire brigade, she did. Seriously? Grandma wasn’t telling me that! Oh, it's true, lad. Your grandpa was a fearless – and foolish – man. Fearless and a bit clumsy! Now, you got any of those biscuits left, Margaret?

Look at this, Liam! Remember Sarah and Ben's wedding? Vaguely. It was lovely, wasn’t it? Sunny, good food… all a bit of a blur, if I’m honest. So many weddings, so little sleep. That's so true. But look at this photo of them dancing. They look so happy. And look, there's Emily hiding behind the flower arrangement, trying to avoid being spotted. Classic Emily. Always the mischievous one. I wonder how they're getting on over there. Did you ever send them that link to the Sichuan cooking class? I did, a few weeks ago. Don't think they replied. They're probably busy with the little ones. It’s a world away from Norfolk, isn't it? Absolutely. Different culture, different pace of life. It's amazing they settled so quickly. Makes you wonder if we’ll ever get round to properly exploring Yunnan. We will. We just need to…prioritise. The kids seem to be keeping us busy enough at the moment. Though they’d love it, wouldn’t they? Imagine them running through rice paddies. They’d probably try to eat the rice paddies. Remember their phase with the mud pies? Don’t remind me! I spent hours scrubbing that out of their hair. Speaking of travel, did you see that blog post from Chloe? She's in Iceland. No! Iceland. I’m so jealous. The Northern Lights… I've always wanted to see them. She sent me a message saying it’s breathtaking. Apparently, she's meeting up with Mark – you know, Mark from the History department? – for the weekend. Really? Small world, isn’t it? I always thought Chloe had a thing for him. Quiet sort, but seems lovely. She mentioned it last Christmas, she said he’d been showing her some really interesting historical sites. I hope she’s being careful though, it’s freezing there. Of course. I always worry. You know, I was looking through the old photos from that trip to Italy, the one before we had the kids… Oh! The one where we got hopelessly lost in Venice? That's the one. Remember that little trattoria we found? The best pasta I’ve ever had. I do. It felt like we were the only two people in the world. It was magical. We need to go back. We will. Someday. When the little ones are old enough to appreciate good pasta and getting hopelessly lost.

Honestly, last night was  wild . I’m still recovering. Tell me about it! My head feels like it's going to explode. Whose brilliant idea was it to go to Fabric again? Don't look at me! It was Chloe's. She insisted it was the only place to celebrate Liam getting that internship. Liam? Seriously? That guy just stares at his shoes all night. Zero vibe. I know, right? But his cousin knows the promoter, so free entry. Can’t argue with that. Though I think my bank account  can  argue with the overpriced cocktails. Oh, don't even start me on the drinks. I think I spent more on those neon-green things than I do on my weekly grocery shop. And they tasted like cough syrup. They did! Ugh, I’m definitely sticking to beer from now on. Did you see Sarah trying to take a selfie? Oh God, yes! She was contorting herself into the weirdest position, trying to get the perfect angle with the strobe lights. Looked like a confused flamingo. Classic Sarah. She spent the whole night obsessing over her Instagram story. Honestly, it’s exhausting. Tell me about it. I deleted all mine before I even left the club. I couldn’t even remember half of what happened. Like, I’m pretty sure I tried to teach a guy how to dab. No way! You? Dabbing? I have no idea why! I was just feeling… spirited. Also, I think someone spiked my water. Seriously? That’s awful! You should have told someone. Nah, I just figured I’d had a bit too much. Anyway, speaking of spirits... did you see Tom flirting with Anya near the bar? Ooh, yes! He was trying to be all subtle and casual, but she clearly wasn’t having it. She just kept giving him these icy looks. She's way out of his league. Honestly, I think he’s got a thing for any girl who doesn’t immediately roll her eyes when he opens his mouth. True. I saw mum's friend's daughter was there too, she's actually really cute. Oh yeah? What’s she like? Is she one of those girls who's always on her phone? No, not really. She was talking to Chloe for a bit about some film project. So, kind of interesting. Maybe a chance for Tom then? Although, knowing Tom, he’d probably just ask her if she likes football.

Right, so we’re all agreed about Gran’s visit next week then? Tuesday’s the best, I think. She’d be tired otherwise. Tuesday’s perfect. I can definitely be there by lunchtime. Just need to double-check my transcription schedule. Bit of a rush on with that client at the moment, they're wanting everything by Friday. Aye, Tuesday works for me. Should be a good chance to catch up properly, hasn't been easy with her feeling a bit under the weather lately. Exactly. It’ll be lovely to see her. And I’ve already started a list of things she might enjoy doing while she’s here. A walk by the lake, perhaps a visit to that little garden centre… Oh, the one with all the quirky gnomes? She'd love that. Remember when she bought that ridiculous one for Auntie Maureen's birthday? How could I forget? The one with the fishing rod and the slightly alarming grin. She insisted Maureen needed a bit of character in her garden. She has a good eye for character, doesn’t she? Speaking of entertainment, did you see that game last night? The Liverpool versus Man U one? I caught a bit of it. It was a nail-biter, wasn't it? Think Liverpool should've been awarded a penalty though, clear as day. Aye, well, referee’s clearly got a soft spot for Man U. Always has. Don't start, John. Remember what happened last time you started arguing about football over dinner? The gravy pot nearly got thrown. Just making an observation, love. Football's full of questionable decisions. Just like life, really. That's a bit deep for Tuesday night peas and chips, isn't it? Though, I suppose there’s culpability in everything. Like, who's responsible for the mess in the kitchen after dinner? Always him. He claims to be "helping" but… I was! I was clearing the plates! Someone has to do it. Fair enough. But clearing the plates doesn't involve leaving chips scattered across the floor. Oh, John. You’re incorrigible. It's good to have you here, though. These peas are lovely, by the way. Best I've made in ages. They are cracking, Margaret. Proper posh chips too, not those frozen ones you sometimes get. They are. It's nice to have a proper family dinner. Makes a change from eating at my desk.

Right, well, that was lovely. Thanks so much for coming down. Bit of a whirlwind visit, wasn't it? Definitely! It was so nice to see you both, though. And Sussex is beautiful. I wished we'd had more time to walk around Brighton properly. It is, isn't it? Though all those pebbles! My feet were aching by the end of yesterday. Reminds me of Margate, back in the day. You and your memories, Arthur! It was lovely to see you, darling. And it was lovely to see you too, [Speaker_1’s name]. Such a nice flat you've got here. Thanks, Mum. Glad you like it. It’s… lived in, shall we say? Especially after accidentally dropping my laptop yesterday. Oh no! Are you alright? The laptop is… not. The screen's cracked. Send help. But I'm fine. Funny thing is, I was just thinking about how I need to sort out that voice recognition software too. Could have used that to apologize to the laptop. Voice recognition, eh? Fancy that. Back in my day, you just typed. Slowly, mind you. No shortcuts. Speaking of shortcuts, did you ever manage to get that blackberry phone set up, Arthur? Oh, that contraption! Still haven't a clue. [Speaker_1’s name] tried to show me, bless him, but it’s all just buttons and a tiny screen. Give me a good old telephone any day. It's a shame, really. It has some good features. It's so bizarre how much technology has changed. Remember when finding your glasses was the biggest tech challenge? Absolutely! Now it's troubleshooting broken laptops and confusing blackberries. Don't forget the bin strikes! Such a mess down the road. Everyone’s just leaving their rubbish out. Awful. Speaking of mess and things… Are you drinking that still water, [Speaker_2’s Name]? Yes? It's just bottled. Bottled water! Honestly. Paying for water. The water companies… highway robbery, I tell you. You can get perfectly good tap water. Dad, you’re on a roll! Though, Mum’s been pretty insistent about the Brita filter. Apparently, the taste of tap water here is horrific. It is a bit dodgy, isn’t it? It has that chlorine taste. So, you’re all going to be alright now you've said goodbye? Yeah, just tidying up. Should probably put something on for dinner tonight, just for us.

Right, let’s see… Manchester United lost. Again. Honestly, what are they playing at? Yeah, didn’t catch much of it, but saw the score flash up. Shocking really. You’d think they’d at least put up a fight. How about Liverpool? They drew. Not much better, is it? Though at least it wasn’t a defeat. You know, this weather… it’s properly grey. Makes you feel a bit…down. Tell me about it. I’m starting to feel that SAD creeping in. It’s not quite as bad as when I was back in Bury in January, but… Poland in November isn’t exactly sunshine and roses, is it? This coffee's helping though. It’s actually really good here, isn’t it? It is! Best I’ve had since…well, since Cambridge. Funny isn't it, finding the best coffee in a small Polish town. What’s Mark up to? Did you get a message from him? Yeah, just now. He’s complaining about the pre-exam stress with his students. They're freaking out about the FCE next month. It’s a lot to manage, especially when you want them to feel confident, not pressured. I know the feeling. Being responsible for someone's future… it weighs on you, doesn't it? Even if you're just teaching them grammar. Absolutely. Speaking of which, I think I need to have a final proofread of their practice tests tonight. It's just… relentless. I was thinking about applying for that summer program on the farm, you know, the one near Krakow? Working with the sheep? To completely switch off. A farm? You? That’s a bit of a change from teaching English! I know, right? But a bit of fresh air and hard work might do me good. And my dog, Elsie, would love it. She’d go crazy chasing sheep. Elsie's a little terror, isn't she? Remember when she stole that sausage off Mr. Henderson last summer? Don't remind me! He wasn’t too pleased. Have you been reading anything good lately? I saw a review of that new Sally Rooney. Not really. Been watching a lot of documentaries on Attenborough. Actually, I saw one about starlings the other day. Fascinating creatures. They do those murmurations, don’t they? It's like a swirling grey cloud. Oh yeah, I’ve seen those! It’s incredible.

Right, so this should feed an army, shouldn’t it? You two managed to demolish half a bag of crisps already. We were hungry! Long day, you know. Cement doesn't shift itself. Tell me about it. Production line is a nightmare this week. We’re behind schedule on everything. I swear, Dave from logistics is deliberately making things difficult. Dave always is, isn't he? He’s got a personal vendetta against everyone. You’ll win in the end, though. Yorkshire grit, remember? Speaking of grit… how’s the conference going, Liv? Still organising the tech billionaires’ weekend away? Oh, you have no idea. It’s been chaos. One of them wants a specific type of artisanal cheese flown in from France. Artisanal. Cheese. Like that’s a reasonable request. Seriously? People are mental. That’s why I stick to spreadsheets and logistics. Much more predictable. You're lucky. Although, even spreadsheets can throw curveballs. Anyway, what about you, Sam? Any exciting dating developments? You’ve been awfully quiet. Not really. Went on a date last week. He spent the entire time talking about his Warhammer collection. Oh, bless. Did he at least offer you a miniature warrior? No, just hours of detailed backstory. I think I made my excuses after the dessert. That’s a hard pass. I’m starting to think I’ll be single forever. Don't say that! You're gorgeous, intelligent, and you make a killer pasta. Any man would be lucky. What are you looking for anyway? A prince? I don’t know! Someone who can hold a conversation that doesn’t revolve around… things with tiny swords, I suppose. Fair enough. Oh! Speaking of things I'm bringing… Anyone fancy a browse through my sale haul? I went mad at ASOS yesterday. Ooh, tell me about it! Let me guess, a sparkly dress you didn't need? Guilty. But look! It was only £15! And it's perfect for… something. It's… very pink. That’s the point! I need more colour in my life. Plus, I thought you might want to borrow it. Me? In pink sequins? I think not.
