I’m more of a minimalist black turtleneck kind of girl. Suit yourself. What about you, Sam? Any new pieces you’re loving? Actually, yeah! I impulsively bought this amazing oversized blazer from Depop. It’s vintage, from the 90s. So good with everything.

This is a lovely square, isn’t it? Always quite a tranquil spot, even in London. I rather like the layout – not overly formal, but a good sense of space. And the lime trees, of course. Beautiful in the spring. It is nice. I was just thinking about how they’ve done a decent job with the landscaping. Much better than some of the other green spaces around here. Though, I’m still trying to figure out where all the pigeons go in winter. Good point. There was a little boy earlier, practically sprinting to catch one. Quite the chase! Made me think of those panda enclosures in Chengdu. Remember when we went? Of course! The sheer number of pandas was overwhelming. Though, I still think the bears in Yunnan province, in their natural habitat, are infinitely more impressive. That landscape… just extraordinary. Absolutely. China is breathtaking. Such a diverse range of landscapes, and the wildlife… utterly remarkable. Reminds me, I was chatting to some Chinese guests the other day, asking about their favourite parts of travelling. One of them was raving about the Qinghai-Tibet Railway. Oh, yeah, heard good things. Bit touristy, I imagine, though? Speaking of tourists, Paris is absolutely rammed at the moment, apparently. My sister's over there. Said she queued for an hour just to see the Mona Lisa. Dreadful, isn't it? Though, I suppose it's a testament to the painting's power. Anyway, back to work – I’m slightly stressed about having to assess my colleague's teaching observations. He's really struggling with the pronunciation of certain sounds. That's always tricky. Difficult to give constructive criticism without hurting someone’s feelings. How's your supervision going, by the way? Any breakthroughs with the dissertation? Slow progress, to be honest. The supervisor's being a bit… elusive. I need to push him a bit more on the methodology, I think. Right, coffee and cake sounds good. Fancy a slice of that coconut cake over there? Definitely. And some decent coffee. I’m dreading the thought of those watery brews some places serve. Actually, I saw one of those “chuggers” earlier. Nasty business, eh? The worst! Always try to avoid eye contact. Although, thinking of travel, I was considering Devon for a few days’ break. Somewhere rural, with quiet lanes, nice walks… Ooh, sounds lovely. Though, driving in rural Devon is a nightmare!

Right, so are you absolutely sure you’ve got the postcode? I don’t want to end up in Middlesborough again. Relax, Beth. I’ve double-checked. It’s SG18 afterward. Harpenden, remember? Not Middlesborough. Completely different hemisphere. Hemisphere's a bit dramatic, isn't it? It’s just… I still get flashbacks from that time. The seagulls. The confusion. It wasn’t  that  bad. And you were the one who insisted on navigating using a paper map. It felt bad at the time! Anyway, this is important. Grandma’s expecting us for tea. And she specifically asked for those shortbreads from Greggs – the ones with the little sugar crystals. Right, mission critical. Shortbread acquisition is priority number one. Did you grab the flowers I asked for? Yep, they’re in the back. Lilies, like she wanted. Though the florist looked at me a bit funny when I said specifically lilies. She's got good taste, your Grandma. Lilies always brighten the place up. So, how’s the project going at work? Still wrestling with those verb tenses? Tell me about it. Professor Davies is on the warpath if any of the annotations are even slightly off. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I'm losing my mind trying to categorize every single nuance of usage. Sounds… intense. Need a proper break when you finish. Maybe finally take that trip you talked about? Somewhere hot, with a beach and absolutely zero corpus linguistics. That sounds amazing. Honestly, that’s all I can think about. Though Mom keeps hinting I need to start looking at apartments closer to the university. Don’t rush into anything. You’re doing brilliantly where you are. Plus, commuting back for Sunday dinners is a vital part of the family ecosystem. You're right. Mom just worries. Speaking of which, should I call her to let her know we're on track? Yeah, good idea. She'll be pacing the floor if she doesn't hear from us soon. And tell her I said hello. Remind her about that leaky tap she's been meaning to fix. Will do. Though she'll probably deflect and start lecturing me about my diet. Classic Mom move. Just brush it off. We're nearly there. Just a few more minutes. Fingers crossed we don’t encounter any rogue seagulls along the way. Don't even joke about it! Okay, I think I see the turning.

Honestly, I'm still knackered from that conference last week. Three days of back-to-back meetings, arranging everything, making sure everyone's happy… It’s exhausting. Yeah, sounds intense. What was it for anyway? A tech firm, launching their new software. Loads of suits, very serious. I swear, half of them just wanted the free biscuits. Classic. So, how's your cold, Liam? You sounded ropey on the phone. Not great, to be honest. Sore throat, proper head cold. Mum reckons it's just a bug, but I feel like I’ve been run over by a bus. Get some proper rest, then. Don't go trying to be a hero. It only makes it worse. I did that once, tried to power through a flu and ended up in bed for a week. Definitely. My flatmate caught something last week – apparently, it’s going around. Poor thing’s been tucked up for days. Reminded me of when I had that awful stomach bug in uni. Oh god, those are the worst. Remember that time we all got one on that student trip to Brighton? Don't remind me! Ruined the whole weekend. Urgent trips to the loo became the main activity. Seriously! Anyway, aside from crippling illnesses, how are things with Mark? You seemed a bit… guarded last time we spoke. It’s complicated. He's been working crazy hours, and we barely see each other. When we do, he’s just tired and grumpy. I feel like I'm living with a ghost sometimes. That's rough. Has he said anything about it? Maybe he’s under pressure at work. He says he’s fine, that it’ll all settle down. But it's been like this for months. I miss him, you know? The normal him. Have you tried talking to him properly about it? Like, really laying it all out there? I’ve tried. He just gets defensive. Says I'm being clingy. Men, eh? Can’t ever just say things. Tell me about it. Sarah's been having drama with Ben. He kept going on about how he's always right, even when he’s clearly not. Oh, the classic move. So frustrating. Maybe you need to give him some space? Sometimes, a bit of distance can make them realise what they’re missing. I’ve thought about it. Maybe a weekend apart? Force him to miss me?

Honestly, I'm knackered. This project is just… relentless. Tell me about it. I'm completely drained too. Double shift tomorrow. Lovely. At least you’re doing something genuinely helpful. I feel like I’m mostly just… shuffling spreadsheets. Though, Sarah from accounts did make a proper mess of the budget projections this week. It was a nightmare to sort out. Oh, Sarah. Bless her. She means well. Did you have to have 'the talk' with her again? Basically. I tried to be diplomatic, but honestly, it was like pulling teeth. She insisted she’d done everything “by the book.” The book that’s clearly outdated and needs rewriting, apparently. Ugh, those conversations are the worst. So, anything else dramatic happening at the office? Well, Mark finally left. Mark? From sales? Wow, really? I didn’t realise he was that unhappy. I thought he was quite keen on that new assistant, Chloe. He was, but apparently, the director kept micromanaging him. He said it was suffocating. He’s going to try freelance marketing. Brave move, I suppose. Good for him, taking a risk. Need a change, clearly. Are you going to his leaving do? Yeah, next Friday. I’m dreading it, to be honest. Forced socializing after a week like this… It'll be the last thing I want to do. What about you? Anything exciting happening in the world of mental health nursing? Actually, yes. Bit of a bombshell, really. Liam finally broke up with Chloe. Liam? No way! I thought they were pretty solid. Apparently not. He says she was getting clingy and demanding. He needed space. Typical bloke, saying that after three years. Poor Liam. He’s always been a bit of a softie. Did he tell you the details? Not really. Said it was amicable, but you could tell he was hurting. I had to hold it together during handover - some of the patients noticed I was a bit off. Poor you, juggling patients and heartbroken friends. You're a superstar. Listen, I'm going to order some Thai. My brain needs carbs and minimal effort. You in? Absolutely. And maybe a large glass of wine. Tonight calls for it. You deserve it after wrestling with Sarah’s spreadsheets. And me, after Liam’s drama. It's been a week. Sounds like a plan. Let me see what’s on Deliveroo... Should we tell Beth and Maya?

Right, so, the big question is, are dragons  always  evil? No! Sparkle is good! She helps people! Sparkle’s a very good dragon, yes. But in most stories, aren’t they guarding gold and breathing fire and, you know, generally being a bit grumpy? But knights are good! They fight the dragons! That's right, knights are usually good. But sometimes knights are a bit…bossy, aren't they? Thinking they know best? Think of Sir Lancelot. Who's Sir Lancelot? He's a knight from the Arthurian legends. A really famous knight. And he had a secret, a bit of a naughty secret. Sometimes knights aren't as good as they seem. So even knights can be naughty? Absolutely. Everyone can be naughty sometimes. It's about what you  do  after you're naughty, isn't it? Do you try to make things right? So, trolls are  always  bad? Hmmm, trolls. Now that's a tricky one. Some trolls are definitely mean, living under bridges and demanding payment to let you pass. But others… well, the Welsh tell stories of friendly trolls who help people lost in the mountains. They’re just misunderstood sometimes because they’re different. Like monsters? Are monsters always bad? That’s a really good question, clever clogs! Think about the story of the Beast. He looked scary, didn't he? But he was just lonely and hurt. And underneath all that fur, he had a good heart. So, it’s what's  inside  that matters? Exactly! It’s not about how you look or what you do sometimes, it’s about what’s in your heart. Goodness and badness, it’s rarely black and white, is it? It's all shades of grey, like a really misty morning. I liked the bit about the trolls being lost! Me too. It’s nice to think about even the scariest monsters just wanting a friend. Now, have you two finished your breakfast? We need to get ready for Grandma’s. Can I take Sparkle to Grandma’s? Of course you can. She can help Grandma fight any grumpy goblins that might be lurking! Goblins aren't good! No, you're absolutely right. Goblins are definitely on the naughty list! Now, let’s go! Grandma's waiting. Do you want me to continue with more of this conversation? Maybe focusing on a specific legend or folk tale? \ Let me know how you'd like me to proceed.  \ I can also add more speakers if you wish.

Right, so the school's filming trip to Cambridge...did you see the emails about it, Sarah? Briefly, yeah. Something about filming at King’s College, right? Sounds lovely for them. Is Lily excited? Absolutely buzzing. She’s been talking about it non-stop. Apparently, they're making a short film about the history of the colleges. King’s! That’s right, sweetie. King’s! You’ll be famous on the screen! Film? That’s brilliant, Ben. Your sister will be a star! How’s her leg doing, by the way? She was limping a bit yesterday. It's still a bit sore. She says it clicks when she walks a lot. I’ve told her to take it easy. She's worried about missing out, though. Being on the sidelines isn’t her thing. I know that feeling. Poor thing. I hope it’s nothing serious. Maybe some rest and ice will do the trick? That’s the plan. I’m trying to be a stern parent and tell her to chill out, but she’s already plotting how she can still participate. True to form! Listen, I booked myself a slot at the gym this evening. Fancy joining me? Need to shake off some of this…domesticity. Tempting, but I need to supervise the filming trip prep. Lily’s determined to bring a massive bag of snacks, apparently. Oh, the glamour! What are you thinking of letting her have? She’s asking for doughnuts. Seriously! Doughnuts! Well, moderation is key, isn’t it? Maybe just one little one. That's what I'm trying to say! But you know how she gets. Doughnut! He wants one too, does he? Seems so! Well, I might sneak him a small one after Lily's headmaster’s lecture about balanced nutrition. Fair enough. I’m thinking of hitting the treadmill tonight. It's been ages since I've really pushed myself. Are you actually running or just walking briskly with a determined expression? A bit of both, I'll admit. The running machines are surprisingly demoralising, aren’t they? You look like you’re going somewhere, but you’re just…spinning. Exactly! It's the ultimate metaphor for modern life. Absolutely! Still, beats doing nothing. And it's getting warmer, isn’t it? It is, thankfully. Last week, I was freezing at night. I had to put another blanket on. Me too.

This Earl Grey's quite pleasant, isn't it, David? Much better than that dreadful stuff they serve at the school canteen. It is rather nice, yes. A bit pricey for a Tuesday lunch though, wouldn’t you say? Still, good to get out. How's the teaching going? Still battling teenage apathy? You know it. They’re glued to their screens, David. It's a constant struggle to get them engaged. I tried a debate about the Green Party's policies yesterday, thinking it might spark something. Oh? And? Did they show any interest? The Green Party are making quite the noise at the moment. Minimal, to put it mildly. One boy actually mumbled something about "tree-huggers" under his breath. Honestly! They need to understand the urgency of the climate crisis. Kids these days. No sense of perspective. I was reading in the paper about that new eco-village they're building just outside Lewes. Seems a bit idealistic, doesn’t it? It does, but at least someone’s trying something. Speaking of which, how’s the antique shop doing? Still battling with online marketplaces and those dreadful impulse buyers? Always a challenge, Michael. The online stuff's eating into my profits, I’ll admit that. But I had a good day last Saturday at that boot sale up in Henfield. Picked up a lovely set of vintage teacups - think they’ll fetch a decent price. Boot sales… Now there's a nostalgic pursuit. Haven’t been to one of those in years. Used to go with my mum religiously. It’s a treasure hunt, really. You just have to be prepared to sift through a lot of rubbish. I’m always amazed at what people are willing to part with. Found a first edition Agatha Christie for a fiver last month! You and your bargains. You’ve always had a knack for finding things. It’s a good thing, mind you. Keeps you busy. How’s Margaret doing? Still complaining about her arthritis? She's… managing. It's getting tougher, especially in the damp weather. We're trying to keep her active, get her out for walks in the park when we can. It’s hard to watch her slow down, you know? I can only imagine. It's the same with my sister, Eleanor. Her eyesight's failing. She's terrified of losing her independence. It’s a terrible thing.

Honestly, the ficus is thriving. Absolutely thriving. I swear, I’ve got a green thumb, despite what my Nan always said. A green thumb? You once killed a cactus, didn’t you? A very  specific  cactus, and it was unfairly shaded! A circumstantial death, not a lack of horticultural skill. Anyway, this ficus is doing brilliantly. Bright, glossy leaves, new shoots. It’s a mood booster. Well, Cambridge needs a mood booster, doesn’t it? All this doom and gloom in the news… Speaking of which, did you see Trump's latest outburst? Absolutely bonkers. Tell me about it. I had to switch off. My brain couldn’t handle another hour of that. Honestly, sometimes I think the world is actively trying to induce a panic attack. Right? It’s exhausting. I was just reading an article about the impact of political polarisation on mental health. Pretty bleak stuff. Should probably steer away from that topic after a long week of research. Definitely. So, pasties. I’m craving a proper pasty. A proper, Cornish pasty. Not one of those pastry monstrosities you get around here. Oh, you're serious? You're willing to go on a quest for a decent pasty over a pint in a Cambridge pub? It’s a matter of principle! There’s a whole world of pastry-based deliciousness out there, and we're being denied it. I miss Greggs proper. Not that chain that’s here now. I understand. It's like the difference between a proper Midlands bacon bap and… well, whatever vaguely bacon-adjacent thing they’re trying to sell here. It's just not the same. Speaking of things that aren’t the same… my bank balance is looking significantly lighter than it was last week. Postgrad life, innit? Tell me about it. I'm starting to seriously question my spending habits. I saw a dress the other day… a silk dress. Absolutely gorgeous. I nearly bought it. Nearly. Nearly? You know you have three other dresses hanging in your wardrobe that are practically identical. That’s beside the point. This one was  silk . It was a statement. Actually, I probably shouldn't even be talking about dresses. I should be sorting out my pension. Which is a terrifying thought. Don't remind me. I’m clinging to the idea that someone else will solve that problem for me. Probably robots. Robots with a penchant for ficus plants and proper pasties.

Your mum really has embraced the "maximalist" look, hasn't she? It's… a lot. A lot is an understatement. It’s a testament to a lifetime of collecting. Remember when she tried to convince us we  needed  a porcelain pug collection? How could I forget? I still have nightmares. Actually, speaking of needing things, I've been battling with the uni about funding for the art history module. Apparently, 'experiential learning’ doesn't translate to 'lots of bus fare to the Sainsbury Centre'. Tell me about it. They’re always squeezing budgets. You’d think with all the tuition fees they charge… Anyway, what art are you covering? Anything exciting? Mostly modern British sculpture. We’re doing a whole section on Henry Moore. It's fascinating, but trying to get them to appreciate something that looks like a giant, rusty potato? It’s a challenge. I can imagine! You need to hook them with something. Did you show them that video of the killer whales in Johnstone Strait? The one where they teach their young to beach themselves to catch seals? Oh my goodness, yes! I totally forgot about that. They were mesmerized. They said it was the most incredible thing they'd ever seen. Made Moore's sculptures seem a bit… less extreme, actually. Right? Demonstrates clever problem-solving, innovative adaptation… Very Henry Moore. You know, it's weird, I was watching something the other night about the amount of violence on TV. It’s insane. Like, glorifying it, desensitizing people… Completely. It's a societal problem, isn’t it? My dad was ranting to me the other day about some show he was watching. Apparently, there was a scene where someone punched a vicar. Oh, lovely. You know, my student the other day was going on about squatting. Apparently, he's considering it. Said it’s a form of protest. Seriously? Wow. That’s… ambitious. And probably quite illegal. What’s he protesting? Housing costs, mainly. Said something about "reclaiming urban spaces." You get a certain type. You do. Remember when we were kids, and we all obsessed over Blue Peter badges? I'm pretty sure that’s where a lot of these social activist tendencies started. Absolutely! Making things out of junk and feeling like you were contributing something. Now we’re protesting by… squatting. Progress, I guess? To progress! And to your mum’s astonishing collection of ceramic cats.

Right then, you wouldn't believe the state of that hostel they're trying to run up in Norwich. Absolute shambles, it is. Kids just running wild, and no one in charge. Oh dear, really? That’s a shame. Remember Elsie from down the road used to run a little guesthouse? Kept it spotless, she did. Always a pot of tea on the go and a biscuit. Elsie sounds like a saint. These hostels, though... they need proper management. It’s not just about providing a bed and a roof. It’s about… well, guidance, isn’t it? Exactly! And they’re expecting the poor girl running it to do it all on her own. No support. It’s just… well, typical. Remember my old man, running his butcher shop in Costessey? He worked from dawn till dusk. Seven days a week. No handouts, just honest graft. Your father was a marvel, Arthur. Such a hardworking man. Mine too, you know. He had a little hardware store in Harrow. Always tinkering with something, fixing things. He’d even sharpen your knives for you, if you asked nicely. My mum and dad were similar, really. Mum ran the school canteen – endlessly peeling potatoes and making sure everyone got a decent meal. Dad was a head of the science department. Always on about atoms and molecules and the wonders of engineering. Science! Always thought that was a bit of a faff. Give me a good engine any day. Remember that Morris Minor I had? Now  that  was a proper car. Used to be able to fix anything on it. Not like these modern things, all computers and electrics. Can’t even open the bonnet without a degree. Oh, Arthur, you and your cars. You’d spend all your money on them, wouldn't you? I remember you taking that thing all the way to Skegness once. Best holiday I ever had! Speaking of holidays… did you see that photo album Margaret brought round? The one with the pictures of the family at Great Yarmouth? Vaguely. Something about a donkey ride, wasn’t there? Speaking of Great Yarmouth… remember the smell from the abattoir back then? Used to hang in the air something awful. Oh goodness, yes! Dreadful, it was. You’d be craving a good roast dinner just to try to counteract it. Though, frankly, anything seemed preferable to those school dinners. Remember them?

So, you were a recruiter, right? Before you came to Cambridge? That’s quite a switch from academia. Yeah, a pretty big one! Spent five years in recruitment, mostly tech roles. It was... intense. Constant pressure, lots of networking, long hours. Not what I envisioned doing forever, though. I can imagine. It sounds incredibly different from what we do here. I always wonder if people underestimate how much of a skill it is - selling people, essentially. It absolutely is. You have to be a performer, really. You’re representing both the candidate and the company, trying to align their needs and sell them on each other. It’s exhausting but surprisingly useful for public speaking now, actually. Really? How so? Well, you learn to quickly read a room, gauge people’s reactions, tailor your message. You develop a sort of… persuasive shorthand. It's been helpful when presenting, definitely. Though I tend to avoid any talk of candidate pipelines now! Understandable. I was just looking at the feedback for that academic literacy module I’m running for lecturers. It’s…mixed. Oh yeah? Anything particularly troubling? It’s not  bad  exactly, but there's a real disparity in the levels. Some lecturers write beautifully, effortlessly. Others... well, they clearly struggle with structuring an argument, evidence, even basic grammar. It's surprising, really, considering their experience. It wouldn't surprise me, honestly. I think there's a misconception that because someone is a skilled lecturer, they're automatically a skilled writer. Teaching and writing are different skillsets, aren’t they? Exactly! One of the comments said, and I quote, “I can explain this to my students perfectly well, so why do I need to write it down?” Oh, that’s gold. Sounds like a classic. It’s the whole “thinking out loud” versus “thinking on paper” thing, isn’t it? Precisely. It’s about clarity, concision, and rigorous argumentation. I’m trying to emphasize that academic writing isn’t just about sounding intelligent; it’s about being  persuasive  with evidence. And making sure your logic holds up under scrutiny, right? I remember when I was doing my postgraduate – so many papers rejected just because of a flaw in the reasoning, even if the writing was technically sound. Yes! I'm trying to get them to focus on that process of critical evaluation. One lecturer wrote, “I found the task quite patronizing, as if I didn’t already  know  how to write.”

Hi! Is this seat free? Yeah, go for it. Plenty of room. Cheers. I’m Jess, by the way. Studying History. Proper headache trying to get my head around the Reformation at the mo’. Hey Jess! I’m Chloe. English Literature. The Victorian poets are slowly draining my soul. Hello. I'm Priya. Biomedical Science. Oh, Biomedical Science! That sounds fascinating. I’m terrible at anything science-y, I’d probably set the lab on fire if I tried. Don't we all feel like that sometimes? I'm Liam, by the way. Business Management. Trying to learn how to talk about profit margins without falling asleep. Business Management, that’s good money, isn’t it? My parents keep asking when I’m going to get a "real job." Like, writing essays about Keats isn't a real job apparently. My family is similar. They wanted me to be a doctor, so Biomedical Science is already a compromise. It's a lot of pressure. Tell me about it. My grandad keeps asking when I'm going to "get a proper job" too. He thinks History is just looking at dusty old things. I tried to explain it's a lot more than that, but he just blinked at me. Liam: My nan asks if I'm going to make loads of money. I tell her I’ll buy her a new electric kettle. That usually shuts her up. Brilliant! That’s the move. You gotta deflect with something practical. Speaking of practical, anyone know where the coffee machine is? This Victorian poetry is sucking the life out of me. I think it’s down that corridor, on the left. But be warned, the queue is usually massive. Thanks, Priya! I’m starving. I might brave it. Actually, what brought you here, Priya? Are you studying here too? I am. I’m only in my first year. It's a bit overwhelming, to be honest. Lots of new people, lots of new things... It’s a big change from home. Liam: Yeah, first year's always a bit of a shock to the system. Everyone feels a bit lost. Happens every year. Totally. Remember that time I accidentally walked into a lecture on Quantum Physics? Thought I was going to the poetry seminar. Walked out after five minutes, feeling incredibly stupid. Oh wow! That’s brilliant! I once got locked in the library overnight.

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed after that week. Absolutely mental. Tell me about it. What was so bad? Another disastrous speaker drop-out? Worse. The entire AV system decided to stage a rebellion fifteen minutes before the keynote. Fifteen. Minutes. Managed to salvage it with a frantically borrowed projector, but it was stressful. You wouldn't believe the faces of the senior managers. Oh god. Sounds like a nightmare. At least you got fed afterwards, right? This pasta  is  amazing. Yeah, the catering guy felt bad. Though I’m pretty sure he was secretly laughing at my misfortune. Did you ever think about joining the reserves, like your cousin Liam? Briefly, yeah. After uni, actually. The skills training seemed cool, all that technical stuff. But then I realised I’d rather just  know  how to use a computer than actually fix one in, you know, a potentially exploding situation. Plus, Liam’s horrifying stories of endless admin… He  does  complain a lot. Still, earning a pension that early has gotta be tempting. It is. But the thought of marching around in camouflage… not really my vibe. Speaking of vibes, did you see that new  Kinfolk  magazine? The one with the photography of the old farmhouses? Ooh, yeah! Gorgeous. I’m trying to get into that kind of aesthetic for the conference styling, you know, more rustic and natural. Less generic hotel ballroom. Good shout. It’s a clever look. Have you seen  Everything Everywhere All at Once  yet? I finally got around to it last night. Oh my god, yes! Absolutely blew my mind. The bagel! The hot dog fingers! I’m still thinking about it. Right? The sheer absurdity of it all, but also, genuinely moving. Michelle Yeoh was incredible. You know, it made me think about how we try to control things, fix problems… and how sometimes the best thing to do is just… embrace the chaos. Deep, Rach! Deep. Maybe I should channel that energy when the AV system inevitably breaks down again. You should. I saw on Twitter that they’re finally updating the operating system on some of those ancient computers at the conference centre. Apparently, it was still running Windows XP. Seriously?! That’s… prehistoric. They’re going to crash even  more  regularly. Apparently, they’ve been putting it off because nobody knew how to actually do it. So, naturally, they called in the most expensive IT consultants.

Honestly, the ref was dreadful tonight. Utterly dreadful. Three missed calls against Liam, three! Tell me about it. I was shouting myself hoarse. Though, to be fair, that might just be my usual volume. You always shout, Finn. It's part of your charm, apparently. Right, right. Charm. I’ll take it. Anyway, anyone else notice how Dave from London kept subtly flexing the entire game? Showing off his new gym membership. Oh my god, yes! It was excruciating. Like, we get it, you can lift weights. We're here to play basketball, not admire your biceps. And the whole "I work in finance, you wouldn't understand" vibe he was giving off whenever someone questioned his plays? So patronising. Honestly, Londoners. It’s a stereotype for a reason. Typical. Coming up here thinking they're superior. You know, it's just the same with dating, isn’t it? So many guys from down south, convinced they're ten times more desirable than anyone here. Seriously! It’s exhausting. I went on a date last week – didn’t even make it to dessert. He spent the whole time talking about his internship at a law firm. Like, I appreciate ambition, but spare me the details, please. Ugh, the worst. Men who are just… resume-reading. Exactly! It’s like they’ve forgotten how to actually, you know, connect with another human being. I'm starting to think I'll just end up with the cats. They’re much better conversationalists. Speaking of connections… Did you hear about Sarah’s cousin visiting from London next month? Apparently, he's a documentary filmmaker. No way! That’s brilliant for Sarah. What’s he filming? Something about social inequality in the housing market. Apparently, it got quite heated at the last screening – lots of shouting. Sounds right up Sarah’s street, actually. She's been so passionate about the housing crisis lately. Yeah, she's practically single-handedly trying to overhaul the local council's planning policies. She's something else. Speaking of political upheaval... Did you see what’s happening with that new bill? The one about… ugh, I can't even remember the specifics. It's all so confusing. It’s the one that basically allows developers to bypass planning regulations, isn't it? Gutting local communities for profit. Typical. It's ridiculous. It’s just the rich getting richer while everyone else struggles to find somewhere affordable to live.

Blimey, it's a bit…compact, isn’t it? Yours and ANON’s flat. It is a little snug, yes. But it's got character! And lovely light. I think it’s cozy! Much better than my student halls, definitely. Glad you think so! It took a while to get everything organized. Where would you like to sit? Anywhere’s fine. Just used to a bit more space, you see. Living in that little bedsit for years…you get used to it. Did you get the utility bills sorted, ANON? Yeah, Dad. Just got them. They're…a bit higher than I expected, actually. Everything’s going up, love. Everything's gone up. Especially the price of a packet of nuts. Remember when you could get a big bag of Brazil nuts for a few pennies? You wouldn’t know it now! I bought some walnuts the other day - outrageous. You should try that spice shop down by the pier. Proper little treasure trove, that place. So many smells. Want to go sometime? We could! I need to stock up on some cumin. Been craving it. Speaking of cravings... I’ve made cream teas. Proper Cornish scones, with clotted cream and jam. Oh, lovely! I hope you said 'scone' right, dear. It’s ‘scone’ like 'gone’, not 'scone' like 'bone’. I know, Mum! I've been practicing. Brighton locals are very particular about it. It's a national crisis if you say it wrong! All this fuss about a bit of bread and cream. Back in my day... We know, dear. Back in your day, things were different. How's your cholesterol, by the way? Remember the doctor said… Don't you start, Maureen! It’s fine. I just watch the cream a bit. I’m hardly going to suddenly get diverticulitis in my old age. It runs in the family you know. You're a picture of health, Dad. Just need to kick that habit of betting on the horses! It’s just a bit of harmless fun! Keeps me entertained. Besides, I nearly had a win last week. Almost. Almost doesn't pay the bills, does it? So, , how's the care work going? Still enjoying it? It’s rewarding, but tiring. Lots of paperwork. And it’s the little things, you know? Like the constant stream of plastic bags they use. It’s disheartening. I know what you mean.

Honestly, the state of Twitter today. It's just… relentless. Relentless how? Is something particularly awful kicking off? Just the usual. People yelling at each other about absolutely nothing. And everyone's suddenly an expert on Ukrainian politics. It's exhausting. I need a digital detox, proper. I can appreciate that. I've been battling spreadsheet fatigue all morning. This project on the new bridge design is… intense. Structural integrity, water flow calculations, pleasing the council… it’s a lot. Tell me about it. Corpus admin isn't exactly glamorous, but dealing with linguistic data all day can be weirdly draining. You're constantly spotting subtle biases and patterns nobody else even notices. Did you see that article about AI language models perpetuating gender stereotypes? Vaguely, yeah. It's a tricky one, isn’t it? Technology reflecting and amplifying existing societal issues. Speaking of which, did you catch that piece about the proposed housing development on the edge of town? The prices are absolutely ludicrous. Ludicrous is an understatement! I was looking at flats the other week – just because I was bored – and even the smallest ones were pushing £400,000! How is anyone supposed to get on the property ladder these days? Especially in Cambridge. It’s ridiculous. My parents are still talking about buying their house for £30,000 in the eighties. Madness. Maybe I should stick to bridges, less competition. You’d be brilliant at it, anyway. You’re all about the precision and the detail. I’m a bit more… chaotic. You’re organized chaos. Like a very well-documented mess. What are you having for dinner tonight? Need any inspiration? I was thinking of trying that Moroccan tagine recipe I found online. Ooh, that sounds amazing! I was just going to order a takeaway, but that actually sounds a lot better. I’m terrible at cooking, though. Everything I make ends up… questionable. Remember that attempt at a Victoria sponge last year? How could I forget? It looked like a geological specimen! But you tried. And that's what matters. Easy for you to say – you’re basically a structural engineer, precision is in your blood! Hey, have you heard anything about the weather forecast for the weekend? I was hoping to get out for a walk on Saturday. Apparently, it’s going to be quite grey and drizzly. Classic British summer, eh? Although, I did hear some bloke on the news saying the jet stream is doing some weird thing… might be sunshine eventually.

Right, so, the day's been absolutely manic. Honestly, I don’t know how I'm even standing. Tell me about it! Freelance life is feast or famine, isn't it? I've been glued to my laptop all day trying to finish this campaign copy. Client's being a nightmare, keeps changing his mind. Oh, I know that feeling. My lot at the home were all having a right moan this morning. Mrs. Peterson decided she absolutely  needed  gooseberries for breakfast. Gooseberries! In November. Gooseberries? Seriously? Seriously! And then when we told her they weren’t on the menu, she got all upset. You wouldn’t believe the palaver. Sounds familiar. I had Mr. Henderson demanding a full English Breakfast at 10 pm last night. Bless him, he just gets confused. How's your mum, Sarah? She's good, thanks. Bit lonely, I think. Keep trying to get her to come to that pottery class I told you about. She's convinced she’s useless at it. My nan’s been asking about her. She remembers her pottery days. Tell her to give it a go! It's just a bit of fun. Anyway, back to the chaos. We had a locum doctor in today, fresh out of med school. Kept calling me "ma'am" every five seconds. Honestly, I felt like his grandmother. Oh, that's brilliant! I had a new agency worker last week, bless her. Spent half an hour trying to feed Mr. Davies pureed food through a straw! He's got perfectly good teeth, you know. Oh no! Did he realise? Eventually. He just shook his head and said, "I’m not a baby, love.” Made the whole room laugh. You can't beat that. You know, I’m thinking about trying to organize a little Christmas get-together. Just a few of us, a bit of festive cheer… Oh, that would be lovely! I'm definitely in. What did you have in mind? Nothing fancy, just some nibbles, mulled wine, Christmas music…maybe a white elephant gift exchange? A white elephant? What’s that? It's where you bring a silly present, something you don't want anymore, and everyone draws a number to pick it. It’s always hilarious. That sounds fun! I'm in too, although I don’t know what I’d bring. Probably a slightly chipped teapot. Perfect! Then we’ll sort out a date.
